sanskrit: svavījena svanāmāntair vibhaktānyaṅganāmabhiḥ // yuktāni hṛdayādīni dvādaśāntāni pañcataḥ / ārabhya kalpayitvā tu japet siddhyanurūpataḥ //
english: One has to repeat according to his accomplishment the mystic formula divided into the mystic basic syllable and their ending names along with the names of limbs, after having resolved the yoked twelve limbs beginning with the heart etc.

sanskrit: hṛdayañca śiraścūḍā kavacaṃ netramastrakaṃ / ṣaḍaṅgāni tu vījānāṃ mūlasya dvādaśāṅgakaṃ //
english: The heart, head, tuft, armour, eye, weapons are the six limbs of the mystic basic syllables of the basic mystic formula constituting twelve parts.

sanskrit: hṛcchiraś ca śikhā varma cāstranetrāntayodaraṃ / praṣṭabāhūrujānūṃś ca jaṅghā pādau kramānnyaset //
english: One should then assign in order to the limbsthe heart, head, tuft, hands, eyes, belly, back, arms, thighs, knees, shank, and feet, the following syllables and gods.

sanskrit: kaṃ ṭaṃ paṃ śaṃ vainateyaḥ khaṃ ṭhaṃ phaṃ ghaṃ gadāmanuḥ /
english: The letters kam, ṭam, pam, śam are for Vainateya. The letters kham, ṭham, pham, ṣam are for the brother of macebearer Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: gaṃ ḍaṃ baṃ saṃ puṣṭhimanto ghaṃ ḍhaṃ bhaṃ haṃ śriyai namaḥ //
english: The letters gam, ḍam, vam, sam form the mystic formula for the nourishment. Gham, ḍham, bham, ham salutations to Śrī Goddess of wealth.

sanskrit: vaṃ śaṃ maṃ kṣaṃ pāñcajanyaṃ chaṃ taṃ paṃ kaustubhāya ca / jaṃ khaṃ vaṃ sudarśanāya śrīvatsāya saṃ vaṃ daṃ caṃ laṃ //
english: One has to worship Pāñcajanya, with the mystic letters vam, śam, mam, kṣam. The mystic letters cham, tam, pam are for the worship of Kaustubha gem worn by Viṣṇu on his head, jam, kham, vam for the Sudarśana the disc in the hands of Viṣṇu, sam, vam, dam, cam, lam for Śrīvatsa the mark on the chest of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: oṃ dhaṃ vaṃ vanamālāyai mahānantāya vai namaḥ / nirvījapadamantrāṇāṃ padair aṅgāni kalpayet //
english: Om, dham, vam salutations to the garland of wild flowers worn by Viṣṇu and to the great Ananta. The limbs are set forth with the words of the mystic formula consisting of words without the mystic letters.

sanskrit: jātyantair nāmasaṃyukterhṛdayādīni pañcadhā / praṇavaṃ hṛdayādīni tataḥ proktāni pañcadhā //
english: Along with the names ending with the caste names, the heart and other limbs are set forth. The praṇava letter Om is repeated five times. Then the heart and other limbs are mentioned five times. .

sanskrit: praṇavaṃ hṛdayaṃ pūrvaṃ parāyeti śiraḥ śikhā / nāmnātmanā tu kavacaṃ astraṃ nāmāntakaṃ bhavet //
english: With the praṇava one should adore the heart first. With the word ‘for the supreme’, the head and the tuft and with one’s name, the armour are adored. The end of the name would be to worship the weapon.

sanskrit: oṃ parāstrādisvanāmātmā caturthyanto namontakaḥ /
english: Om, the supreme weapon is the first. Then one’s own name ending in the fourth case is to be said.

sanskrit: ekavyūhādiṣaḍviṃśavyūhāttasyātmano manuḥ //
english: This consists of one to twentysix parts.

sanskrit: kaniṣṭādikarāgreṣu prakṛtiṃ dehakercayet /
english: One should worship prakṛti nature at the tips of the little and other fingers of the arms in one’s body.

sanskrit: parāya puruṣātmā syāt prakṛtyātmā dvirūpakaḥ //
english: That one consisting of prakṛti nature is the second form of the supreme being consisting of puruṣa soul.

sanskrit: oṃ parayāmnyātmane caiva vāyvarkau ca dvirūpakaḥ /
english: Om salutation to the supreme being, the foremost or the first soul. The air and the sun are his two forms.

sanskrit: agniṃ trimūrtau vinyasya vyāpakaṃ karadehayoḥ // vāyvarkau karaśākhāsu savyetarakaradvaye / hṛdi mūrto tanāveṣa trivyūhe turyarūpake //
english: The fire the third form having been assigned to pervade hands and the body, wind and the sun in the fingers of hand, this is embodied in the three parts in the two arms, left and the other arm, in the heart, in the body forming the fourth state.

sanskrit: ṛgvedaṃ vyāpakaṃ haste aṅgulīṣu yajurnyaset /
english: The Ṛgveda is made to pervade hand. The Yajus Yajurveda is assigned to fingers.

sanskrit: taladvayetharvarūpaṃ śirohṛccaraṇāntakaḥ //
english: The form of Atharva is assigned to two palms.

sanskrit: ākāśaṃ vyāpakaṃ nyasya kare dehe tu pūrvavat / aṅgulīṣu ca vāyvādi śirohṛdguhyapādake //
english: As before having assigned the extensive sky to his arm and body, wind and other elements, to fingers, head, heart, generative organ and the feet.

sanskrit: vāyurjyotirjalaṃ pṛthvī pañcavyūhaḥ samīritaḥ /
english: The wind, fire, water, earth and sky or ether are spoken as his five forms.

sanskrit: manaḥ śrotrantvagdṛgjihvā ghrāṇaṃ ṣaḍvyūha īritaḥ // vyāpakaṃ mānasaṃ nyasya tatoṅguṣṭāditaḥ kramāt /
english: The mind, ear, skin, eye, tongue and nose are said to be the six forms. The extensive mind is assigned from the thumb onwards to the head, mouth, generative organ and the organ of excretion.

sanskrit: mūrdhāsyahṛdguhyapatsu kathitaḥ karuṇātmakaḥ //
english: The prime form is said to be consisting of compassion.

sanskrit: ādimūrtistu sarvatra vyāpako jīvasañjñitaḥ /
english: It is known as the jīva life which is all pervasive.

sanskrit: bhūrbhuvaḥ svarmaharjanastapaḥ styañca saptadhā // kare dehe nyasedādyamaṅguṣṭādikrameṇa tu / talasaṃsthaḥ saptamaś ca lokeśo dehake kramāt //
english: The seven words, earth, ether, heaven, mahas, jana, tapa and satya are assigned duly to hands and the body beginning with thumb. The Lord of the world, the seventh one and existing in the palm is taken gradually to the body, head, forehead, mouth, heart, generative organ and feet.

sanskrit: agniṣṭhomastathokthastu ṣoḍaśī vājapeyakaḥ //
english: This is said to be the Agniṣṭoma. Next follows the description of the Vājapeya and the Ṣoḍaśī rites.

sanskrit: atirātrāptoryāmañca yajñātmā saptarūpakaḥ /
english: Atirātra and Aptoryāma rites will also be described.

sanskrit: dhīrahaṃ manaḥ śabdaś ca sparśarūparasāstataḥ // gandho buddhirvyāpakaṃ tu kare dehe nyaset kramāt /
english: The soul of the sacrifice which has seven forms extending to the intellect, ego, mind, sound, touch, colour, taste, smell, comprehension, should be assigned duly to the fingers and the body.

sanskrit: nyasedantyai ca talayoḥ ke lalāṭe mukhe hṛdi // nābhau guhye ca pāde ca aṣṭavyūhaḥ pumān smṛtaḥ /
english: A person has to assign it to the teeth, palms, head, forehead, face, heart, navel, the generative organ and the feet. These are remembered as the eight Vyūhas parts.

sanskrit: vījo buddhirahaṅkāro manaḥ śabdo guṇonilaḥ // rūpaṃ raso navātmāyaṃ jīva aṅguṣṭhakadvaye /
english: The life which consists of nine partslife, intellect, ego, mind, sound, quality, wind, colour, and taste, is assigned to two thumbs.

sanskrit: dehe śirolalāṭāsyahṛnnābhiguhyajānuṣu /
english: They are placed in order on the left hand by means of the forefinger and other fingers.

sanskrit: pādayoś ca daśātmāyaṃ indro vyāpī samāsthitaḥ // aṅguṣṭhakadvaye vahnistarjanyādau pareṣu ca /
english: Indra remains pervading the ten limbs consisting of body, head, forehead, mouth, heart, navel, the generative organ, two knees and feet. The fire is assigned to two thumbs.

sanskrit: pādayorekadaśātmā manaḥ śrotraṃ tvageva ca / cakṣurjihvā tathā ghrāṇaṃ vākpāṇyaṅghriś ca pāyukaḥ //
english: Mind consisting of eleven partsear, skin, eye, tongue, smell, speech, hand, foot, anus is assigned to head, forehead, face, heart, navel, the generative organ, two knees and feet with the forefinger.

sanskrit: upasthaṃ mānaso vyāpī śrotramaṅguṣṭhakadvaye /
english: The mind is made to pervade the male organ. The two thumbs are made to pervade the ear.

sanskrit: tarjanyādikramādaṣṭau atiriktaṃ taladvaye // uttamāṅgulalalāṭāsyahṛnnābhāvatha guhyake / uruyugme tathā jaṅghe gulphapādeṣu ca kramāt //
english: Commencing with the forefinger in order, the eight fingers are assigned. The two fingers left over are assigned to palm. The head, forehead, month, heart, navel are assigned in order to generative organ, two thighs, shanks, ankles and feet.

sanskrit: viṣṇurmadhuharaś caiva trivikramakavāmanau / śrīdharotha hṛṣīkeśaḥ padmanābhastathaiva ca //
english: Viṣṇu, Madhuhara killer of the demon Madhu, Trivikrama, Vāmana, Śrīdhara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha, Dāmodara, Keśava, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, Govinda are the names of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: mādhavaścātha govindo viṣṇuṃ vai vyāpakaṃ nyaset //
english: Viṣṇu is made to pervade.

sanskrit: aṅguṣṭhādau tale dvau ca pāde jānuni vai kaṭau / śiraḥśikharakaṭyāñca jānupādādiṣu nyaset //
english: The thumb and other fingers, palms, feet, two knees, waist are assigned to head, crown of head, waist, knees. and feet.

sanskrit: dvādaśātmā pañcaviṃśaḥ ṣaḍviṃśavyūhakas tathā / puruṣo dhīrahaṅkāro manaścittañca śabdakaḥ //
english: There are twelve, twentyfive or twentysix partsthe supreme being, intellect, ego, mind, thinking, touch, taste, colour, smell, ears, skin, eyes, tongue, nose, speech, hand, feet,.

sanskrit: upastho bhūrjalantejo vāyurākāśameva ca /
english: anus, generative organ, earth, water, light, wind and sky.

sanskrit: śeṣān hastatale nyasya śirasyatha lalāṭake /
english: The pervasive Supreme Being is assigned and then in the thumbs and other fingers.

sanskrit: mukhahṛnnābhiguhyorujānvaṅghrau karaṇodgatau // pāde jānvorupasthe ca hṛdaye mūrdhni ca kramāt /
english: The remnant are assigned in the palm, head, or forehead and then face, heart, navel, generative organ, thigh, knee, and feet are assigned to feet, knee, thing, generative organ, heart and head in order.

sanskrit: paraś ca puruṣātmādau ṣaḍviṃśe pūrvavatparaṃ // sañcintya maṇḍalaike tu prakṛtiṃ pūjayedbudhaḥ /
english: A wise man has to meditate upon the great soul of the Supreme Being in these twentysix things as before and then the nature has to be worshipped in a circular altar.

sanskrit: pūrvayāmyāpyasaumyeṣu hṛdayādīni pūjayet //
english: The heart and other limbs have to be worshipped in the east, south, west and north.

sanskrit: astramagnyādikoṇeṣu vainateyādi pūrvavat /
english: As before the weapons of Viṣṇu, Vainateya the vehicle bird of Viṣṇu are adored in the corners of southeast etc.

sanskrit: dikpālāṃś ca vidhistvanyaḥ trivyūhegniś ca madhyataḥ //
english: One should adore the guardian deities of the quarters also. In the worship of three parts, the fire will be at the centre.

sanskrit: pūrvādidigbalāvasorājyādibhiralaṅkṛtaḥ /
english: The directions east etc. are decorated with the strength, abode and kingdom.

sanskrit: viśvarūpaṃ sarvasthityai yajedrājyajayāya ca / sarvavyūhaiḥ samāyuktamaṅgair api ca pañcabhiḥ // garuḍādyaistathendrādyaiḥ sarvān kāmānavāpnuyāt /
english: The omnipresent form of Viṣṇu, endowed with all parts and the five constituents Garuḍa etc. as well as Indra and others, should be adored by one for conquering kingdoms and for firmness of all objects. One may get all desires fulfilled.

sanskrit: viśvaksenaṃ yajennāmnā vai vījaṃ vyomasaṃsthitaṃ //
english: Viṣvaksena an epithet of Viṣṇu is worshipped by his name, the mystic letter being placed in the ether.

sanskrit: mudrāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye sānnidhyādiprakārakaṃ / añjaliḥ prathamā mudrā vandanī hṛdayānugā //
english: now describe the characteristic of the different positions of fingers mudrā which bring the worshipper nearer to the object of worship. Añjali folding of hands is the first mudrā.

sanskrit: ūrdhvāṅguṣṭho vāmamuṣṭirdakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhabandhanaṃ / savyasya tasya cāṅguṣṭho yasya cordhve prakīrtitaḥ //
english: The second is the Vandanī fingers interlocked to be placed near the heart. With the left fist folded and the thumb erect, the right thumb interwoven with the erect left thumb is said to be the third one.

sanskrit: tisraḥ sādharaṇā vyūhe athāsādharaṇā imāḥ /
english: These are the three common formations. The following are not common.

sanskrit: kaniṣṭhādivimokena aṣṭo mudrā yathākramaṃ //
english: By the unyoking of the smallest and other fingers eight positions are formed in order.

sanskrit: aṣṭānāṃ pūrvavījānāṃ kramaśastvavadhārayet /
english: The first eight basic syllables are repeated in order.

sanskrit: aṅguṣṭhena kaniṣṭāntaṃ namayitvāṅgulitrayaṃ //
english: One has to bend the three fingers commencing with the little finger, with the thumb.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ kṛtvā sammukhañca vījāya navamāya vai /
english: One has to raise up the hand to the face for the ninth mystic syllable.

sanskrit: varāhasya smṛtā mudrā aṅganāñca kramādimāḥ / ekaikāṃ mocayedbaddhvā vāmamuṣṭo tathāgulīṃ //
english: Then the left hand is raised up and bent half slowly. These are the mudrās of the limbs of Varāha in order. Then the left fist having been kept closed, the fingers are released one by one.

sanskrit: ākuñcayet pūrvamudrāṃ dakṣiṇepyevameva ca /
english: The same position is held by the right hand also and the previous position is bent down.

sanskrit: ūrdhvāṅguṣṭho vāmamuṣṭhirmudrāsiddhistato bhavet //
english: If the two palms are placed together so as to form a cavity it represents the Varāha Mudrā.

sanskrit: vakṣye dīkṣāṃ sarvadāñca maṇḍalebje hariṃ yajet /
english: shall describe the initiation rite, which yields everything. Hari should be worshipped in the lotus in a circle.

sanskrit: daśamyāmupasaṃhṛtya yāgadravyaṃ samastakaṃ // vinyasya nārasiṃhena sammantrya śatavārakaṃ / sarṣapāṃstu phaḍantena rakṣoghnān sarvataḥ kṣipet //
english: Having gathered the articles required for the sacrifice on the tenth lunar day, assigning and consecrating hundred times with the basic syllables of the manlion Narasiṃha form, one should scatter on all sides the mustard seeds, destructive of demons, ending the act with the syllable phaṭ.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ sarvātmakāṃ tatra nyaset prāsādarūpiṇīṃ /
english: The female energy, contained in every being, in the form of grace is assigned there.

sanskrit: sarvauṣadhiṃ samāhṛtya vikirānabhimantrayet //
english: Having collected all the herbs and spread, they are consecrated.

sanskrit: śatavāraṃ śubhe pātre vāsudevena sādhakaḥ / saṃsādhya paṇjagavyantu pañcabhirmūlamūrtibhiḥ //
english: A worshipper has to accomplish the five products of the cow hundred times in pure vessels by means of the five basic forms.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇāntaiḥ samprokṣya kuśāgraistena tāṃ bhuvaṃ/ vikirānvāsudevena kṣipeduttānapāṇinā //
english: Having sprinkled the earth with the basic syllable ending with the word Nārāyaṇa, with the tips of kuśa grass, those scattered things are thrown with the raised hand with the basic syllable of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: tridhā pūrvamukhastiṣṭhan dhyāyet viṣṇuṃ tathā hṛdi /
english: Then standing with the face facing the east one has to meditate on Viṣṇu in the heart.

sanskrit: vardhanyā sahite kumbhe sāṅgaṃ viṣṇuṃ prapūjayet //
english: One has to worship Viṣṇu in the waterpot along with the vardhanī.

sanskrit: śatavāraṃ mantrayitvā tvastreṇaiva ca vardhanīṃ / acchinnadhārayā siñcan īśānāntaṃ nayecca taṃ //
english: Having recited hundred times the sacred syllables for the weapon and having sprinkled the Vardhanī vessel with a continuous shower of water it should be taken to the northeast quarter.

sanskrit: kalasaṃ pṛṣṭhato nītvā sthāpayedvikiropari /
english: Taking the jar on his back one has to place it on the scattered mustard seeds.

sanskrit: saṃhṛtya vikirān darbhaiḥ kumbheśaṃ karkarīṃ yajet //
english: Then having gathered them by means. of the Kuśa grass one has to adore the presiding deity of the jar and the karkarī.

sanskrit: savastraṃ pañcaratnāḍhyaṃ khaṇḍile pūjayeddhariṃ / agnāvapi samabhyarcya mantrān sañjapya pūrvavat //
english: One has to worship Hari adorned with clothes and five jewels, on a piece of ground made ready, offering oblations to fire for his sake and reciting the sacred syllables, as before.

sanskrit: prakṣālya puṇḍarīkena vilipyāntaḥ sugandhinā / ukhāmājyena saṃpūrya gokṣīreṇa tu sādhakaḥ // ālokya vāsudevena tataḥ saṅkarṣaṇena ca /
english: Sprinkling with a lotus and anointing with unguents the worshipper has to fill the boiling vessel with clarified butter and cow’s milk. Having looked at it with the Vāsudeva and the Saṅgharṣaṇa basic syllables, rice mixed with clarified butter should be thrown into milk wellcooked.

sanskrit: taṇḍulānājyasaṃsṛṣṭān kṣipet kṣīre susaṃskṛte // pradyumnena smāloḍya darvyā saṅghaṭṭayecchanaiḥ / pakvamuttārayet paścādaniruddhena deśikaḥ // prakṣālyālipya tat kuryādūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ tu bhasmanā /
english: After stirring it with the basic syllable of Pradyumna the worshipper has to mix it slowly with the ladle and then the cooked food is lifted with the basic syllable of Aniruddha. Having washed him and besmearing with sandals, the vertical mark is made on the forehead with the ashes.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇena pārśveṣu carumevaṃ susaṃskṛtaṃ //
english: The food thus prepared well is placed by the side with the basic syllable of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: bhāgamekaṃ tu devāya kalaśāya dvitīyakaṃ / tṛtīyena tu bhāgena pradadyādāhutitrayaṃ //
english: A part of it has to be offered to the deity, the second part to the jar, and with the third part he should offer three oblations.

sanskrit: śiṣyaiḥ saha caturthaṃ tu gururadyādviśuddhaye /
english: The preceptor has to partake of the fourth part in the company of his disciples for the sake of purification.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇena sammantrya saptadhā kṣīravṛkṣajam // dantakāṣṭhaṃ bhakṣayitvā tyaktvā jñātvāsvapātakaṃ / aindrāgnyuttarakeśānīmukhaṃ patitamuttamaṃ // śubhaṃ siṃhaśataṃ hutvā ācamyātha praviśya ca / pūjāgāraṃ nyasenmantrī prācyāṃ viṣṇuṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ //
english: Having consecrated seven times the stick got from the milky tree, the piece of wood for cleaning the tree being made use of and discarded and being conscious of one’s sins and having offered oblations to the hundred auspicious and most excellent lions lying in the north, northeast, east and southeast, having done the ācamana and having entered the chamber of worship, the knower of the mystic syllables should assign ViṣṇU in the east and do circumambulation.

sanskrit: saṃsārārṇavamagnānāṃ paśūnāṃ pāśamuktaye / tvameva śaraṇaṃ deva sadā tvaṃ bhaktavatsala //
english: You are, alone, O Lord! the refuge of the beings immersed in the ocean of mundane existence, for the release from the fetters. You are always kind towards your worshippers.

sanskrit: devadevānujānīhi prākṛtaiḥ pāśabandhanaiḥ /
english: “O Lord of Lords! you permit me.

sanskrit: pāśitānmocayiṣyāmi tvatprasādāt paśūnimān //
english: will free these beings by your grace from their earlier fetters by which they are bound”.

sanskrit: iti vijñāpya deveśaṃ sampraviśya paśūṃstataḥ / dhāraṇābhistu saṃśodhya pūrvajjvalanādinā // saṃskṛtya mūrtyā saṃyojya netre baddhvā pradarśayet /
english: Having submitted thus to the lord of the celestials and having made the animals enter the place, they have to be purified then by holding them as before and to be consecrated with the fire. Having yoked them with the deity their eyes should be closed. Their eyes are covered.

sanskrit: puṣpapūrṇāñjalīṃstatra kṣipettannāma yojayet //
english: Handful of flowers are offered there and their names are added.

sanskrit: amantramarcanaṃ tatra pūrvavat kārayet kramāt /
english: Worship is made duly as before without reciting any basic syllable mantra.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ mūrtau patet puṣpaṃ tasya tannāma nirdiśet //
english: That particular name of the idol on which the flower falls that is pointed out.

sanskrit: śikhāntasammitaṃ sūtraṃ pādāṅguṣṭhādi ṣaḍguṇaṃ / kanyāsu kartitaṃ raktaṃ punastattriguṇīkṛtam //
english: One should then take up a red thread spun by a maiden and measure it six times from the tuft of the hair to the toe and again multiply it three times.

sanskrit: prakṛtiṃ prakriyābhedaiḥ saṃsthitāṃ tatra cintayet //
english: Then one should meditate on the Prakṛti in which the universe lies and from which the universe is born, as being present there,.

sanskrit: tena prākṛtikān pāśān grathitvā tattvasaṅkhyayā / kṛtvā śarāve tat sūtraṃ kuṇḍapārśve nidhāya tu //
english: Having tied the nooses of Prakṛti proportional to the number of principles, that thread is placed on an earthen vessel near the pit.

sanskrit: tatastattvāni sarvāṇi dhyātvā śiṣyatanau nyaset / sṛṣṭikramāt prakṛtyādipṛthivyantāni deśikaḥ //
english: Then having meditated upon the principles commencing with the Prakṛti to the earth, following the order of creation, the spiritual teacher should assign them to the body of the disciple.

sanskrit: tatraikadhā paṇcadhā syāddaśadvādaśadhāpi vā /
english: Those principles, one, five, ten or twelve may be tied individually and given by those who devote their thought on the principles.

sanskrit: aṅgaiḥ pañcabhiradhvānaṃ nikhilaṃ vikṛtikramāt /
english: With the five organs of action one has to create the entire universe in the order of evolution.

sanskrit: tanmātrātmani saṃhṛtya māyāsūtre paśostanau // prakṛtirliṅgaśaktiś ca kartā buddhis tathā manaḥ / pañcatanmātrabuddhyākhyaṃ karmākhyaṃ bhūtapañcakaṃ //
english: Having drawn the subtle principles into one’s self and having placed the rope of illusion on the animal, the nature is taken as the creative power, the intellect or the mind as the agent, the five subtle principles as born of intellect and the five elements from the organs of action.

sanskrit: dhyāyecca dvādaśātmānaṃ sūtre dehe tathecchayā /
english: One has to meditate on these twelve principles in the rope as well as in the body according to his desire.

sanskrit: hutvā sampātavidhinā sṛṣṭeḥ sṛṣṭikrameṇa tu // ekaikaṃ śatahomena dattvā pūrṇāhutiṃ tataḥ / śarāve sampuṭīkṛtya kumbheśāya nivedayet //
english: Having made oblations with the residue of offerings according to the order of creation, and hundred oblations to each and every principle and then the final oblation, the earthen vessel is covered and is dedicated to the presiding deity of the pot.

sanskrit: adhivāsya yathā nyāyaṃ bhaktaṃ śiṣyaṃ tu dīkṣayet /
english: Having duly performed the initial consecration, the devoted disciple is initiated.

sanskrit: karaṇīṃ kartarīṃ vāpi rajāṃsi khaṭikāmapi // anyadapyupayogi syāt sarvaṃ tadvāyugocare / saṃsthāpya mūlamantreṇa parāmṛśyādhivādhivāsayet //
english: Then in a place where the wind blows, an arrow of a particular shape and a knife made either of silver or iron as well as all necessary materials are placed and touched with the principal mystic syllable he should perform the initial consecration ceremony.

sanskrit: namo bhūtebhyaś ca baliḥ kuśe śete smaran hariṃ / maṇḍapaṃ bhūṣayitvātha vitānaghaṭalaḍḍukaiḥ //
english: He should then say “Salutations, offer the food to the goblins on the kuśa grass”. Then having contemplated upon Hari, the sacrificial yard is adorned with multitudes of vessels of sweet meats.

sanskrit: maṇḍaletha yajedviṣṇuṃ tataḥ santarpya pāvakaṃ /
english: Viṣṇu is then worshipped in a circular altar.

sanskrit: āhūya dīkṣayecchiṣyān baddhapadmāsanasthitān //
english: Then after offering oblations to the fire, the pupils who are seated in the Padmāsana posture are called upon and are initiated.

sanskrit: sammokṣya viṣṇuṃ hastena mūrdhānaṃ spṛśya vai kramāt / prakṛtyādivikṛtyantāṃ sādhibhūtādhidaivatāṃ // sṛṣṭimādhyātmikīṃ kṛtvā hṛdi tāṃ saṃharet kramāt /
english: Having sprinkled water on Viṣṇu, and touching the head gradually, all the principles from the primordial down to the transformations as well as their presiding deities, the entire divine creation is conceived in the heart and all the subtle principles which have become one with the soul are absorbed gradually.

sanskrit: tataḥ samprārthya kambheśaṃ sūtraṃ saṃhṛtya deśikaḥ /
english: Then the preceptor has to pray the presiding deity of the pitcher and draw the thread.

sanskrit: mūlamantreṇa sṛṣṭīśamāhutīnāṃ śatena taṃ / udāsīnamathāsādya pūrṇāhutyā ca deśikaḥ // śuklaṃ rajaḥ samādāya mūlena śatamantritaṃ / santāḍya hṛdayantena huṃphaṭkārāntasaṃyutaiḥ //
english: Then having come near the fire and placing it the thread by the side of the fire, he should offer hundred oblations to the passive Lord of creation with the principal mystic syllable. Then the preceptor having reached him, and having offered the final oblation, has to collect the white dust and strike the heart with that sanctified by the basic mystic syllable and ending with the syllables huṃ and phaṭ.

sanskrit: viyogapadasaṃyuktair vījaiḥ padādibhiḥ kramāt / pṛthivyādīni tattvāni viśliṣya juhuyāttataḥ //
english: Then oblations are separately offered in order to the earth and other principles with mystic syllables made up by subtracting syllables.

sanskrit: vahnāvakhilatattvānāmālaye vyāhṛte harau /
english: Separating by means of beating and collecting them one has to remain quiet.

sanskrit: tāḍanena viyojyaivaṃ ādāyāpādya śāmyatāṃ / prakṛtyāhṛtya juhuyādyathokte jātavedasi // garbhādhānaṃ jātakarma bhogañcaiva layantathā /
english: Then after collecting by the Primordial, an offering is made into the fire as instructed. After offering eight oblations each in favour of Garbādhāna, Jātakarma, enjoyment and dissolution, he should offer them for purification.

sanskrit: śuddhaṃ tattvaṃ samuddhṛtya pūrṇāhutyā tu deśikaḥ / sannayeddvipare tattve yāvadavyāhṛtaṃ kramāt //
english: The preceptor should take up pure materials and bring together the two excellent principles in order in such a way they are not broken.

sanskrit: tat paraṃ jñānayogena vilāpya paramātmani / vimuktabandhanaṃ jīvaṃ parasminnavyaye pade // nivṛttaṃ paramānande śuddhe buddhe smaredbudhaḥ /
english: Then the soul, freed from fetters is immersed in the supreme soul in the supreme undecaying position. A learned person has to think of the peaceful, supreme, blissful, pure intellect and offer the completing oblation. Thus ends the rite of initiation.

sanskrit: dadyāt pūrṇāhutiṃ paścādevaṃ dīkṣā samāpyate // prayogamantrān vakṣyāmi yair dīkṣā homasaṃlayaḥ /
english: shall describe the mystic syllables for the application with which the oblation relating to the initiation is closely associated Oṃ, Yaṃ, the goblins, the pure huṃ, phaṭ.

sanskrit: anena tāḍanaṃ kuryādviyojanamiha dvayaṃ //
english: By this one should strike and separate the two. Oṃ, Yaṃ, destroy the goblins.

sanskrit: ādānaṃ kṛtvā cānena prakṛtyā yojanaṃ śṛṇu /
english: After having seized this syllable you hear the mode of yoking it with the nature.

sanskrit: homamantraṃ pravakṣyāmi tataḥ pūrṇāhutermanuṃ //
english: shall describe the mystic syllable for the oblation as well as the final oblation. Oṃ, destroy the goblins oblations.

sanskrit: pūrṇāhutyanantare tu tadvai śiṣyantu sādhayet /
english: After the final oblation the disciple has to be accomplished.

sanskrit: evaṃ tattvāni sarvāṇi kramātsaṃśodhayed budhaḥ //
english: In this way the wise man has to purify the principles.

sanskrit: namontena svavījena tāḍanādipuraḥsaram / yaṃ vījena samānantu tāḍanādiprayogakam //
english: Oṃ, suṃ, to the principle of smell, separate, huṃ, phaṭ. Oṃ, protect, hā. Oṃ, svam, svam, unite with the primordial. Oṃ, suṃ, huṃ, to the principle of smell, destroy oblations.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrṇāhutiś caivamuttareṣu prayujyate /
english: Then the final oblation is to be applied in the northern direction as follows Oṃ, rāṃ, to the principle of taste.

sanskrit: ekamūrtāvayaṃ prokto dīkṣāyogaḥ samāsataḥ /
english: This method of initiation has been described in brief in the case of the deity of a single form.

sanskrit: evameva prayogastu navavyūhādike smṛtaḥ //
english: The procedure for the ninevyūhas etc. are also remembered to be of the same kind.

sanskrit: dagdhāparasmin sandadhyānnirvāṇe prakṛtinnaraḥ /
english: A person after having consumed all the things should consign the primordial thing to eternal bliss.

sanskrit: avikāre samādadhyādīśvare prakṛtinnaraḥ //
english: Then a person has to consign the primordial thing to the Lord devoid of transformation.

sanskrit: śodhayitvātha bhutāni karmāṅgāni viśodhayet / buddhyākhyānyatha tanmātramanojñānamahaṅkṛtiṃ //
english: Then having purified the elements, one has to purify the instruments of action, the intellect, the principles, mind, knowledge and egoism.

sanskrit: liṅgātmānaṃ viśodhyānte prakṛtiṃ śodhāyet punaḥ /
english: After having purified the soul of the body, he should again purify the primordial principle at the end.

sanskrit: puruṣaṃ prākṛtaṃ śuddhamīśvare dhāmni saṃsthitaṃ // svagocarīkṛtāśeṣabhogamuktau kṛtāspadaṃ / dhyāyan pūrṇāhutiṃ dadyāddīkṣeyaṃ tvadhikāriṇī //
english: The supreme being and the pure primordial principle stationed in the Lord which is held under control and has been rendered an abode after being freed from bondage is contemplated upon and the final oblation is offered. This is the mode of initiation for a person who is fit.

sanskrit: aṅgair ārādhya mantrasya nītvā tattvagaṇaṃ samaṃ / kramādevaṃ viśodhyānte sarvasiddhisamanvitaṃ // dhyāyan pūrṇāhitiṃ dadyātdīkṣeyaṃ sādhake smṛtā /
english: Having worshipped with the constituents of the mystic syllables, the principles are uniformly carried and gradually purified. Having meditated on the Lord endowed with all accomplishments, the final oblation is made.

sanskrit: dravyasya vā na sampattiraśaktirvātmano yadi //
english: This is the mode of initiation for an aspirant in case if there is no abundance of articles and no capacity for a person.

sanskrit: iṣṭvā devaṃ yathā pūrvaṃ sarvopakaraṇānvitaṃ / sadyodhivāsya dvādaśyāṃ dīkṣayeddeśikottamaḥ //
english: Having worshipped the lord as before endowed with all the materials, the excellent preceptor has to initiate the disciple on the dvādaśī the th day from the beginning of the rite.

sanskrit: bhakto vinītaḥ śārīrair guṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvitaḥ /
english: The disciple must be devoted, humble, endowed with all physical qualities, not very rich.

sanskrit: adhvānaṃ nikhilaṃ daivaṃ bhautaṃ vādhyātmikī kṛtaṃ / sṛṣṭikrameṇa śiṣyasya dehe dhyātvā tu deśikaḥ // aṣṭāṣṭāhutibhiḥ pūrvaṃ kramāt santarpya sṛṣṭimān / svamantrair vāsudevādīn jananādīn visarjayet //
english: Such a person is initiated.after the worship of the deity in the altar. Having contemplated the entire path, divine, pertaining to the elements or to the self, in the order of their creation in the body of the disciple, the preceptor, desirous of creation, having offered first sixteen oblations to Vāsudeva and other gods who are radiant, with their respective mystic syllables, they are allowed to go.

sanskrit: homena śodhayet paścātsaṃhārakramayogataḥ /
english: Then purification is made by oblation in the order of destruction.

sanskrit: yonisūtrāṇi baddhāni muktvā karmāṇi deśikaḥ // śiṣyadehātsamāhṛtya kramāttattvāni śodhayet /
english: Having released all the fetters of deeds, the preceptor, has to purify the principles, having drawn them in order from the body of the disciple.

sanskrit: agnau prākṛtike viṣṇau layaṃ nītvādhidaivake // śuddhaṃ tattvamaśuddhena pūrṇāhutyā tu sādhayet /
english: Having dissolved in the fire, the primordial Viṣṇu and the Supreme Spirit, the pure principle is accomplished by offering final oblation with impure prin•ciple.

sanskrit: śiṣye prakṛtimāpanne dagdhvā prākṛtikān guṇān //
english: After the disciple had attained his natural state, he has to consume all the qualities of the primordial being.

sanskrit: maucayedadhikāre vā niyuñjyāddeśikaḥ śiśūn / athānyān śaktidīkṣāṃ vā kuryāt bhāve sthito guruḥ //
english: The preceptor has to release or bind the children. Or the preceptor remaining in his natural state has to perform a different kind of initiation called Śaktidīkṣā.

sanskrit: bhaktyā samprātipannānāṃ yatīnāṃ nirdhanasya ca / sampūjya sthaṇḍile viṣṇuṃ pārśvasthaṃ sthāpya putrakaṃ // devatābhimukhaḥ śiṣyastiryagāsyaḥ svayaṃ sthitaḥ / adhvānaṃ nikhilaṃ dhyātvā parvabhiḥ svair vikalpitaṃ //
english: Having worshipped Viṣṇu placed nearby with the lad in an altar and who is being adored with the devotion of ascetics and mendicants, the pupil remains facing the deity, the self preceptor facing obliquely. After having contemplated upon the entire course which has been resolved by him the preceptor according to the phases of the moon, the preceptor has to think deeply with contemplation on the Lord, the supreme spirit, stationed in the body of the disciple.

sanskrit: dhyānayogena sañcintya pūrvavattāḍanādinā //
english: As before all the principles have to be purified gradually by beating etc.

sanskrit: kramāttattvāni sarvāṇi śodhayet sthaṇḍile harau / tāḍanena viyojyātha gṛhītvātmani tatparaḥ //
english: on the altar of Hari. Then he who is bent on the inquiry of the self has to set them aside after having taken them, and beating.

sanskrit: deve saṃyojya saṃśodhya gṛhītvā tat svabhāvataḥ / ānīya śuddhabhāvena sandhayitvā krameṇa tu //
english: He should purify them befitting their nature and unite them with the deity. They are then collected with pure mental disposition and yoked in order.

sanskrit: śodhayeddhyānayogena sarvato jñānamudrayā /
english: By means of contemplative mood and the pose of knowledge jñānamudrā they are all purified.

sanskrit: śuddheṣu sarvatattveṣu pradhāne ceśvare sthite //
english: When all the principles have been thus purified and the Supreme lord remains.

sanskrit: dagdhvā nirvāpayecchiṣyān pade caiśe niyojayet / ninayet siddhimārge vā sādhakaṃ deśikottamaḥ //
english: as the main, the principles have to be burnt and the fire extinguished and the disciples have to be engaged in the service of the Lord. Then the excellent preceptor should conduct the aspirant on the path of accomplishment.

sanskrit: evamevādhikārastho gṛhī karmaṇyatandritaḥ /
english: In the same manner, a householder becomes qualified by remaining vigilant in the performance of the rites.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ śodhayaṃstiṣṭhed yāvadrāgakṣayo bhavet //
english: One has to remain purifying his self until there is dissipation of anger.

sanskrit: kṣīṇarāgamathātmānaṃ jñātvā saṃśuddhikilviṣaḥ / āropya putre śiṣye vā hy adhikārantu saṃyamī // dagdhvā māyāmayaṃ pāśaṃ pravrajya svātmani sthitaḥ /
english: After having known himself as shorn of anger and purified from sins, a selfcontrolled person should confer the right on his son or the disciple. After having burnt the noose composed of illusion, renouncing and remaining in the contemplation of the self, he, who possesses the unmanifest form, should remain waiting for the decay of his body.

sanskrit: śarīrapātamākāṅkṣannāsītāvyaktaliṅgavān //
english: Sitting with crossed legs, the feet placed over the thigh of the opposite leg.

sanskrit: abhiṣekaṃ pravakṣyāmi yathācāryastu putrakaḥ / siddhibhāk sādhako yena rogī rogādvimucyate // rājyaṃ rājā sutaṃ strīñca prāpnuyānmalanāśanaṃ /
english: shall describe the anointment of the preceptor as the son would do and by which an aspirant would become accomplished and a diseased would get rid of the disease, the king would get his kingdoṃ, a woman would get a child and also. destruction of impurity.

sanskrit: mūrtikumbhān suratnāḍhyānmadhyapūrvādito nyaset //
english: Pictures made of earth and endowed with gems are to be placed in the middle, the east etc.

sanskrit: sahasrāvartitān kuryādathavā śatavartitān / maṇḍape maṇḍale viṣṇuṃ prācyaiśānyāñca pīṭhike //
english: Thousands or hundreds of them are placed in a circular form and Viṣṇu in the east and northeast at an elevated place in an altar.

sanskrit: niveśya śakalīkṛtya putrakaṃ sādhakādikaṃ /
english: Having placed all of them the aspirant should assign his son in parts.

sanskrit: abhiṣekaṃ samabhyarcya kuryādgītādipūrvakaṃ //
english: After having worshipped well the anointment should be performed preceded by songs etc.

sanskrit: dadyācca yogapīṭhādīṃstvanugrāhyāstvayā narāḥ / guruś ca samayān brūyādguptaḥ śiṣyotha sarvabhāk //
english: Men should offer yogic seats etc. requesting his favour. The preceptor also should announce the terms and the pupil initiated into the secrets then becomes the recipient of all that he wants.

sanskrit: sādhakaḥ sādhayenmantraṃ devatāyatanādike / śuddhabhūmau gṛhe prārcya maṇḍale harimīśvaraṃ //
english: The aspirant has to accomplish the mystic syllable in the temple of the deity after having worshipped the Lord Hari in a circular figure in a purified ground.

sanskrit: caturastrīkṛte kṣetre maṇḍalādīni vai likhet /
english: One has to draw circles etc.

sanskrit: rasavāṇākṣikoṣṭheṣu sarvatobhadramālikhet //
english: in a square piece of ground, the Sarvatobhadra is drawn in the compartments of rasa, bāṇa and akṣi.

sanskrit: ṣaṭtriṃśatkoṣṭhakaiḥ padmaṃ pīṭhaṃ paṅktyā vahirbhavet /
english: A lotus seat containing thirtysix apartments should be outside in a row.

sanskrit: dvābhyāntu vīthikā tasmād dvābhyāṃ dvārāṇi dikṣu ca //
english: Among these two squares are set apart for the pathway and two for the doors in the quarters.

sanskrit: vartulaṃ bhrāmayitvā tu padmakṣetraṃ puroditam /
english: A lotus figure is drawn in front outside and a circle is drawn around it.

sanskrit: padmārdhe bhāmayitvā tu bhāgaṃ dvādaśamaṃ vahiḥ //
english: Half of the lotus is divided into twelve compartments.

sanskrit: vibhajya bhrāmayeccheṣaṃ catuḥkṣetrantu vartulaṃ /
english: Having thus divided it one should draw four circles, one around the other.

sanskrit: prathamaṃ karṇikākṣetraṃ keśarāṇāṃ dvitīyakam //
english: The first one is that of the pericarp and the second, that of the filaments.

sanskrit: tṛtīyaṃ dalasandhīnāṃ dalāgrāṇāṃ caturthakam /
english: The third is that of the joints of the petals and the fourth, that of the tips of the petals.

sanskrit: prasārya koṇasūtrāṇi koṇadiṅmadhyamantataḥ // nidhāya keśarāgre tu dalasandhīṃstu lāñchayet /
english: The joints of the petals are marked by stretching the threads from the angular points upto the middle of the side facing the angle and placing them on the tips of the filaments.

sanskrit: pātayitvātha sūtrāṇi tatra patrāṣṭakaṃ likhet //
english: Then the threads are made to lie fall and then an eightpetalled lotus is drawn.

sanskrit: dalasandhyantarālantu mānaṃ madhye nidhāya tu / dalāgraṃ bhrāmayettena tadagraṃ tadanantaraṃ // tadantarālaṃ tatpārśve kṛtvā vāhyakrameṇa ca / keśare tu likheddvau dvau dalamadhye tataḥ punaḥ //
english: Having allowed a measure equal to the space between the joints of the petals, the tops of the petals are drawn in front of it and afterwards. Having allowed in the middle a measure of space equal to that of the interstices between the petals, two filaments are drawn in between every two petals.

sanskrit: padmalakṣmaitat sāmānyaṃ dviṣaṭkadalamucyate /
english: This is the ordinary lotus circle said to be of twelve petals.

sanskrit: karṇikārdhena mānena prāksaṃsthaṃ bhrāmayet kramāt //
english: Circles are drawn in order in the east of the measure of half the pericarp.

sanskrit: tatpārśve bhramayogena kuṇḍalyaḥ ṣaḍ bhavanti hi /
english: By this drawing there will be six circles on its side.

sanskrit: evaṃ dvādaśa matsyāḥ syurdviṣaṭkadalakañca taiḥ //
english: In this way there will be twelve fish and twelve petals.

sanskrit: pañcapatrābhisiddhyarthaṃ matsyaṃ kṛtvaivamabjakam / vyomarekhāvahiḥ pīṭhantatra koṣṭāni mārjayet //
english: Having drawn a fish with five petals of a lotus for the sake of success, the skyline is made outside the seat altar. The compartments are cleanly swept.

sanskrit: trīṇi koṇeṣu pādārthaṃ dvidvikānyaparāṇi tu / caturdikṣu viliptāni gātrakāṇi bhavantyuta //
english: Four other places for the feet are made ready in the angular points. Besmeared vessels are kept in the four quarters. Two rows are marked in the quarters for the sake of pathway.

sanskrit: dvārāṇyāśāsu kurvīta catvāri catasṛṣvapi //
english: Doors are made in all the four quarters.

sanskrit: dvārāṇāṃ pārśvataḥ śobhā aṣṭau kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ /
english: A wise man has to make eight ornaments of graceful expressions by the side of the doors.

sanskrit: tatpārśva upaśobhāstu tāvatyaḥ parikīrtitāḥ // samīpa upaśobhānāṃ koṇāstu parikīrtitāḥ /
english: An equal number of ornaments are also to be made by their side. Then corners of ornaments should be made.

sanskrit: caturdikṣu tato dve dve cintayenmadhyakoṣṭhakaiḥ //
english: In each one of the middle compartments in all the four directions, two figures are drawn.

sanskrit: catvāri vāhyato mṛjyādekaikaṃ pārśvayorapi /
english: The four outer compartments are cleansed, as well as one on each side.

sanskrit: śobhārthaṃ pārśvayostrīṇi trīṇi lumpaddalasya tu // tadvadviparyaye kuryādupaśobhāṃ tataḥ param / koṇasyāntarvahistrīṇi cintayeddvirvibhedataḥ //
english: Three figures are drawn on each side of the petal for beautifying it. Similarly, three ornaments are to be drawn on the opposite direction inside the angular point as well as outside without any difference between the two.

sanskrit: evaṃ ṣoḍaśakoṣṭhaṃ syādevamanyattu maṇḍalam /
english: In this way, sixteen compartments are formed and in the same manner another circle is formed.

sanskrit: dviṣaṭkabhāge ṣaṭtriṃśatpadaṃ padmantu vīthikā //
english: In the figure having twelve compartments a lotus figure with thirtysix petals is drawn.

sanskrit: ekā paṅktiḥ prābhyāṃ tu dvāraśobhādi pūrvavat /
english: As before one line is drawn at each door for beautification.

sanskrit: dvādaśāṅgulibhiḥ padmamekahaste tu maṇḍale //
english: In the circular altar of one cubit a lotus should be drawn having twelve fingerbreadth.

sanskrit: dvihaste hastamātraṃ syādvṛddhyā dvāreṇa vācaret /
english: A door should be drawn of the measure of two cubits by one cubit.

sanskrit: apīṭhañcaturasraṃ syādvikarañcakrapaṅkajam //
english: The altar should be a square.

sanskrit: padmārdhaṃ navabhiḥ proktaṃ nābhistu tisṛbhiḥ smṛtā / aṣṭābhirdvārakān kuryānnemintu caturaṅgulaiḥ //
english: Half the lotus is drawn with nine finger breadth, the navel with three, the radius with eight breadth, the circumference with four.

sanskrit: tridhā vibhajya ca kṣetramantardvābhyāmathāṅkayet /
english: Having divided the ground into three parts, an inner figure is marked with two breadth.

sanskrit: pañcāntasvarasiddhyarthaṃ teṣvasphālya likhedarān //
english: For the sake of accomplishing one’s object one has to mark the five vowels inside and the radii.

sanskrit: indīvaradalākārānathavā mātulāṅgavat / padmapatrāyatānvāpi likhedicchānurūpataḥ //
english: Then according to his desire, one has to draw figures of the petals of lotus or citron leaves or of the shape of lotus leaves.

sanskrit: bhrāmayitvā vahir nemāvarasandhyantare sthitaḥ / bhrāmayedaramūlantu sandhimadhye vyavasthitaḥ // aramadhye sthito madhamaraṇiṃ bhrāmayet samam /
english: Having fixed at the junction of the radius and having moved around the outer circumference and having stationed in the middle link line one has to move upto the root of the radius. The middle fireproducing stick is moved equally stationing in the middle of the radius.

sanskrit: evaṃ siddhyantarāḥ samyak mātulāṅganibhāḥ samāḥ //
english: Some more figures resembling citron leaves are drawn in this way for the sake of accomplishment.

sanskrit: vibhajya saptadhā kṣetraṃ caturdaśakaraṃ samam /
english: Then the ground should be divided into seven parts each of them measuring equally of fourteen cubits.

sanskrit: dvidhā kṛte śataṃ hy atra ṣaṇnavatyadhikāni tu //
english: There should be two hundred and ninetysix apartments.

sanskrit: koṣṭakāni caturbhistair madhye bhadraṃ samālikhet /
english: The word Bhadra welfare is written in four compartments in the middle.

sanskrit: parito visṛjedvīthyai tathā dikṣu samālikhet //
english: All around that space is set apart for pathway.

sanskrit: kamalāni punarvīthyai paritaḥ parimṛjya tu / dve dve madhyamakoṣṭhe tu grīvārthaṃ dikṣu lopayet //
english: Then lotus figures. are drawn in all directions. Having swept clean around the pathway, four central quarters in all directions are set apart for providing the neck.

sanskrit: catvāri vāhyataḥ paścāttrīṇi trīṇi tu lopayet /
english: Four apartments are set apart outside and then three in each row.

sanskrit: grīvāpārśve vahistvekā śobhā sā parikīrtitā //
english: By the side of the neck there should be an apartment outside known as the ornament.

sanskrit: vimṛjya vāhyakoṇeṣu saptāntastrīṇi mārjayet /
english: Among the outer angles leaving off seven, the rest and three inside are sprinkled with water.

sanskrit: maṇḍalaṃ navabhāgaṃ syānnavavyūhaṃ hariṃ yajet // pañcaviṃśatikavyūhaṃ maṇḍalaṃ viśvarūpagaṃ /
english: An altar of nine divisions is formed in this way consisting of nine parts. This is the circular altar of twentyfive compartments in which the universal form of Hari is worshipped.

sanskrit: dvātriṃśaddhastakaṃ kṣetraṃ bhaktaṃ dvātriṃśatā samaṃ //
english: Thirtytwo cubits of ground should be equally divided into thirtytwo compartments.

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛte caturviṃśatyadhikantu sahasrakaṃ /
english: When it is done in this way, there would be one thousand and twentyfour compartments.

sanskrit: koṣṭhakānāṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ madhye śoḍaśakoṣṭhakaiḥ // bhadrakaṃ parilikhyātha pārśve paṅktiṃ vimṛjya tu / tataḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ koṣṭair dikṣu bhadrāṣṭakaṃ likhet //
english: Having written the word bhadraka welfare in the sixteen middle squares and having sprinkled water on the adjacent rows of compartments, the eight bhadrakas are written in sixteen apartments in all directions.

sanskrit: tatopi paṅktiṃ sammṛjya tadvat ṣoḍaśabhadrakaṃ / likhitvā paritaḥ paṅktiṃ vimṛjyātha prakalpayet //
english: Then having sprinkled the rows of compartments and writing sixteen bhadrakas the rows all around are sprinkled. and allotment is made.

sanskrit: dvāradvādaśakaṃ dikṣu trīṇi trīṇi yathākramaṃ /
english: Twelve doors are drawn in the usual order in each quarter.

sanskrit: catvāryantarvahirdve tu śobhārthaṃ parimṛjya tu / upadvārasiddhyarthaṃ trīṇyantaḥ pañca vāhyataḥ // parimṛjya tathā śobhāṃ pūrvavat parikalpayet /
english: Having omitted the six compartments inside and having sprinkled for beautification the four at the centre, the four on the sides and two inside and outside, and having cleansed three inside and five outside for accomplishing additional doors, as before beautification is made.

sanskrit: vahiḥ koṇeṣu saptāntastrīṇi koṣṭhāni mārjayet //
english: Seven of the corners outside and three apartments inside are cleansed.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśatikavyūhe paraṃ brahma yajet kaje /
english: The supreme brahman is to be worshipped in the auspicious twentyfive compartment formation.

sanskrit: madhye pūrvāditaḥ padme vāsudevādayaḥ kramāt //
english: Then in the lotus drawn in the middle commencing with east, Vāsudeva and other deities are worshipped in order.

sanskrit: varāhaṃ pūjayitvā ca pūrvapadme tataḥ kramāt / vyūhān sampūjayettāvat yāvat ṣaḍviṃśamo bhavet //
english: Having worshipped the boarform in the lotus in the east the formation is worshipped in order until the thirtysix forms are finished.

sanskrit: yathoktaṃ vyūhamakhilamekasmin paṅkaje kramāt / yaṣṭavyamiti yatnena pracetā manyate 'dhvaraṃ //
english: With the effort that it has to be worshipped, one has to worship all formations in the order in the single lotus as described. The progenitor is regarded as the sacrifice.

sanskrit: satpantu mūrtibhedena vibhaktaṃ manyate 'cyutaṃ /
english: Acyuta divided into many forms is regarded as ‘truth’.

sanskrit: catvāriṃśat karaṃ kṣetraṃ hy uttaraṃ vibhajet kramāt //
english: Forty cubits of the ground in the north has to be divided in order.

sanskrit: ekaikaṃ saptadhā bhūyastathaivaikaṃ dvidhā punaḥ /
english: Each one of these divisions are again first divided into seven parts and then into two.

sanskrit: catuḥṣaṣṭyuttaraṃ saptaśatānyekaṃ sahasrakaṃ // koṣṭhakānāṃ bhadrakañca madhye ṣoḍaśakoṣṭhakaiḥ /
english: Then of one thousand seven hundred and sixtyfour apartments we will have a bhadraka figure formed by the central sixteen apartments.

sanskrit: pārśve vīthīṃ tataścāṣṭabhadrāṇyatha ca vīthikā //
english: There will be a pathway on the side, then eight bhadra apartments and a pathway.

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśābjānyatho vīthī caturviṃśatipaṅkajaṃ / vīthīpadmāni dvātriṃśat paṅktivīthikajānyatha // catvāriṃśattato vīthī śeṣapaṅktitrayeṇa ca /
english: Then sixteen figures of lotuses and twentyfour lotuses for the rows and thirtytwo for the pathway and forty rows and a passage with the remaining three rows are drawn.

sanskrit: dvāraśobhopaśobhāḥ syurdikṣu madhye vilopya ca //
english: The doors are provided with ornaments and minor beautifications in the directions, omitting the centre.

sanskrit: dvicatuḥṣaḍdvārasiddhyai caturdikṣu vilopayet / pañca trīṇyekakaṃ vāhye śobhopadvārasiddhaye //
english: For accomplishing, two, four and six doors space is cut off in the four directions and five, three and one outside are set apart for accomplishing the adornment of the doors.

sanskrit: dvārāṇāṃ pārśvayorantaḥ ṣaḍ vā catvāri madhyataḥ /
english: In the same manner, six or four compartments are omitted outside the door and four inside.

sanskrit: dve dve lumpedevameva ṣaḍ bhavantyupaśobhikāḥ //
english: There will be six minor adornments. 0.

sanskrit: ekaikasyāṃ diśi trīṇi dvārāṇyapi bhavantyuta /
english: There should be four doors on one side or three doors specifically in each direction.

sanskrit: pañca pañca tu koṇeṣu paṅktau paṅktau kramāt mṛjet /
english: One has to draw five apartments at the angular points as well as in the rows in order.

sanskrit: koṣṭakāni bhavedevaṃ martyeṣṭyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ śubhaṃ //
english: An auspicious altar dear to a mortal has to be drawn in this manner.

sanskrit: madhye padme yajedbrahma sāṅgaṃ pūrvebjanābhakaṃ / āgneyebje ca prakṛtiṃ yāmyebje puruṣaṃ yajet //
english: One has to worship Brahmā in the lotus at the centre, the lotusnavelled Viṣṇu with all his retinue in the east, the nature primordial matter in the lotus in the southeast and the supreme spirit in the lotus in the south.

sanskrit: puruṣāddakṣiṇe ca vahniṃ nairṛte vāruṇenilaṃ / ādityamaindave padme ṛgyajuś caiśapadmake //
english: One has to worship the firegod in the lotus at the south of the supreme spirit, the windgod in the southwest and west, the sun in the lotus of the moon, the ṚgVedaand YajurVeda in the lotus of the lord.

sanskrit: indrādīṃś ca dvitīyāyāṃ padme ṣoḍaśake tathā / sāmātharvāṇamākāśaṃ vāyuṃ tejas tathā jalaṃ //
english: Indra and other gods are to be worshipped in the sixteen lotuses in the second row then, along with the Sāmaveda, Atharva veda, sky, wind, lustre, water, earth, mind, ear, skin, and eye.

sanskrit: rasanāñca tathā ghrāṇaṃ bhūrbhuvaś caiva ṣoḍaśaṃ //
english: One should also worship the tongue, nose, the worlds Bhū, and Bhuva.

sanskrit: maharjanastapaḥ satyaṃ tathāgniṣṭomameva ca / atyagniṣṭomakaṃ cokthaṃ ṣoḍaśīṃ vājapeyakaṃ // atirātrañca sampūjya tathāptoryāmamarcayet / mano buddhimahaṅkāraṃ śabdaṃ sparśañca rūpakaṃ // rasaṃ gandhañca padmeṣu caturviṃśatiṣu kramāt /
english: Having worshipped the worlds Mahas, Janas, Tapas and Satya and also the sacrifices Agniṣṭoma, Atyagniṣṭoma, Uktha, Ṣoḍaṣī, Vājapeya, Atirātra, one has to worship Aptoryāma, mind, intellect, ego, sound, touch, colour, taste, and smell in order in twentyfour lotuses.

sanskrit: jīvaṃ manodhipañcāhaṃ prakṛtiṃ śabdamātrakaṃ //
english: One has to worship the soul, ego, the lord of the mind, and the sound principle of the primordial matter.

sanskrit: vāsudevādimūrtīñca tathā caiva daśatmakaṃ / manaḥ śrotraṃ tvacaṃ prārcya cakṣuś ca rasanaṃ tathā //
english: One should then worship the images of Vāsudeva and others, having worshipped the following tenthe soul, mind, ear, skin, eye, tongue, nose, speech, hand, and foot in thirtytwo lotuses.

sanskrit: caturthāvaraṇe pūjyāḥ sāṅgāḥ saparivārakāḥ //
english: One has to worship these in the fourth enclosure along with their attendants and retinue.

sanskrit: pāyūpasthau ca sampūjya māsānāṃ dvādaśādhipān / puruṣottamādiṣaḍviṃśān vāhyāvaraṇake yajet //
english: Having worshipped the anus and penis one has to worship the lords of the twelve months as well as the twentysix forms commencing with Puruṣottama in the external enclosure.

sanskrit: cakrābje teṣu sampūjyā māsānāṃ patayaḥ kramāt /
english: Among these the Lords of the months are to be worshipped in the lotus of the disc.

sanskrit: aṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ ṣaḍvā pañcātha caturo 'pare //
english: Then the eight, six, five or four total twentythree principles of the primordial matter are to be worshipped in another lotus.

sanskrit: rajaḥ pātaṃ tataḥ kuryāllikhite maṇḍale śṛṇu /
english: Then one has to dust in a drawn circular altar. You hear.

sanskrit: karṇikā pītavarṇā syādrekhāḥ sarvāḥ sitāḥ samāḥ //
english: The pericarp should be of yellow colour, and all the lines equal and white.

sanskrit: dvihaste 'ṅguṣṭamātrāḥ syurhaste cārdhasamāḥ sitāḥ /
english: They should be two cubits long and one thumb in breadth. Half the length are white.

sanskrit: padmaṃ śuklena sandhīṃstu kṛṣṇena śyāmatothavā // keśarā raktapītāḥ syuḥ koṇān raktena pūrayet /
english: The joints should be coloured white, black or darkblue. The filaments should be red and yellowcoloured. The corners should be filled with red.

sanskrit: bhūṣayedyogapīṭhantu yatheṣṭaṃ sārvavarṇikaiḥ //
english: The yogic seat should be bedecked with any of the colours according to one’s own desire.

sanskrit: latāvitānapatrādyair vīthikāmupaśobhayet / pīṭhadvāre tu śuklena śobhāraktena pītataḥ // upaśobhāñca nīlena koṇaśaṅkhyāṃś ca vai sitān /
english: The pathway is decorated with canopy of creepers and leaves. The entrance to the altar should be painted white, brightred and yellow. Ornamentation of all the white corners is done with blue colour.

sanskrit: bhadrake pūraṇaṃ proktamevamanyeṣu pūraṇaṃ //
english: It has been said that the altar bhadraka should be filled with the colours and in this way the other altars are filled.

sanskrit: trikoṇaṃ sitaraktena kṛṣṇena ca vibhūṣayet / dvikoṇaṃ raktapītābhyāṃ nābhiṃ kṛṣṇena cakrake // arakān pītaraktābhiḥ śyāmān nemintu raktataḥ /
english: The three corners should be decorated with pale, red and black, the two corners with red and yellow and the centre of the circle by black. The black coloured radii should be decorated by yellow and red, the circumference with red, the lines outside being drawn in white, brown, red, black and yellow.

sanskrit: śālipiṣṭādi śuklaṃ syādraktaṃ kausumbhakādikam /
english: The powder of rice is white. The dust of saffron is red. It becomes yellow with turmeric.

sanskrit: haridrayā ca hāridraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ syāddagdhadhānyataḥ //
english: From burnt grains we get black colour.

sanskrit: śamīpatrādikaiḥ śyāmaṃ vījānāṃ lakṣajāpyataḥ /
english: It becomes black with śami leaves and other leaves.

sanskrit: caturlakṣaistu mantrāṇāṃ vidyānāṃ lakṣasādhanam // ayutaṃ buddhividyānāṃ stotrāṇāñca sahasrakam /
english: By the repetition of the basic mystic letters lakh times and of the basic syllables four lakh times, a lakh of mystic learning is accomplished. Ten thousand times of the science of intellect and thousand times of the hymns are repeated.

sanskrit: pūrvamevātha lakṣeṇa mantraśuddhis tathātmanaḥ //
english: The purification of the self by means of a lakh of the basic syllables is done prior to this.

sanskrit: tathāpareṇa lakṣeṇa mantraḥ kṣetrīkṛto bhavet /
english: Then with another lakh, the basic syllable would get established.

sanskrit: pūrvamevāsamo homo vījānāṃ samprakīrtitaḥ //
english: It has been well advocated that oblation of the mystic letters is similar to the prior service.

sanskrit: pūrvasevā daśāṃśena mantrādīnāṃ prakīrtitā /
english: The prior service has been advocated to be performed with a tenth part of the mystic syllables.

sanskrit: paraś carye tu mantre tu māsikaṃ vratamācaret //
english: The monthly austerity has to be performed with the preparatory mystic syllable.

sanskrit: bhuvi nyasedvāmapādaṃ na gṛhṇīyāt pratigraham /
english: The left foot should be placed on the ground and the donation should not be accepted.

sanskrit: evaṃ dvitriguṇenaiva madhyamottamasiddhayaḥ //
english: In this way by the repetition, twice or thrice one gets mediocre and excellent accomplishments.

sanskrit: mantradhyānaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena syānmantrajaṃ phalam /
english: shall describe the mode of contemplation of the mystic syllable, by which one gets the benefits got from the basic syllable.

sanskrit: sthūlaṃ śabdamayaṃ rūpaṃ vigrahaṃ vāhyamiṣyate //
english: The gross form is composed of sound and is laid down as the outward deity.

sanskrit: sukṣmāṃ jyotirmayaṃ rūpaṃ hārdaṃ cintāmayaṃ bhavet /
english: The subtle form composed of lustre becomes the mental figure made up of thoughts in the heart.

sanskrit: cintayā rahitaṃ yattu tat paraṃ prakīrtitam //
english: That form which is beyond thinking, is declared as the supreme.

sanskrit: varāhasiṃhaśaktīnāṃ sthūlarūpaṃ pradhānataḥ /
english: The potential of the bear, lion and other forms are principally gross.

sanskrit: cintayā rahitaṃ rūpaṃ vāsudevasya kīrtitam //
english: The form of Vāsudeva is declared as that beyond the reach of thought.

sanskrit: itareṣāṃ smṛtaṃ rūpaṃ hārdaṃ cintāmayaṃ sadā /
english: The other forms are remembered always as existing in the thoughts of the heart.

sanskrit: sthūlaṃ vairājamākhyātaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vai liṅgitaṃ bhavet //
english: The gross form is said to be vairāja belonging to Brahman and the subtle form would be marked.

sanskrit: cintayā rahitaṃ rūpamaiśvaraṃ parikīrtitam /
english: The form beyond thought is declared as that of Īsvara the lord.

sanskrit: hṛtpuṇḍarīkanilayañcaitanyaṃ jyotiravyayam // vījaṃ vījātmakaṃ dhyāyet kadambakusumākṛtiṃ /
english: One has to contemplate on the lustrous, undecaying consciousness residing in the lotus of the heart, namely the basic letter, the soul of the basic letter of the shape of a kadamba flower.

sanskrit: kumbhāntaragato dīpo niruddhaprasavo yathā // saṃhataḥ kevalastiṣṭhedevaṃ mantreśvaro hṛdi /
english: Just a lamp lies obstructed inside the pitcher, so also the lord of the mystic syllable lies restrained in the heart.

sanskrit: anekaśuṣire kumbhe tāvanmātrā gabhastayaḥ // prasaranti vahistadvannāḍībhirvījaraśmayaḥ /
english: There are many holes in the pitcher. The beams of the light come out through them. In the same way the beams of the mystic letters come out through the tubular organs.

sanskrit: athāvabhāsato daivīmātmīkṛtya tanuṃ sthitāḥ //
english: Then uniting themselves with the power of the deity they exist in the body.

sanskrit: hṛdayāt prasthitā nāḍyo darśanendriyagocarāḥ /
english: The tubular organs, having come out from the heart, come within the ken of the sense of sight.

sanskrit: agnīṣomātmake tāsāṃ nāḍyau nāsāgrasaṃsthite //
english: Among those tubular organs the two tubular organs Agni and Soma are those which remain at the tip of the nose.

sanskrit: samyagguhyena yogena jitvā dehasamīraṇam / japadhyānarato mantrī mantralakṣaṇamaśnute //
english: Then having conquered the wind in the body the reciter of the basic syllable engaged in the repetition and contemplation enjoys the benefits of the basic syllable.

sanskrit: saṃśuddhabhūtatanmātraḥ sakāmo yogamabhyasan / aṇimādimavāpnoti viraktaḥ pravilaṅghya ca / devātmake bhūtamātrānmucyate cendriyagrahāt //
english: With the gross elements and subtle principles purified, contented and practising yoga, one gets aṇimā etc. Remaining detached and depending on the lord of the soul one gets free from the gross elements and subtle principles and seizure of the organs.

sanskrit: rakṣāṃ svasya pareṣāñca vakṣye tāṃ mārjanāhvayāṃ / yayā vimucyate duḥkhaiḥ sukhañca prāpnuyānnaraḥ //
english: will now describe the rite known as the cleansing for the protection of one’s self and others, by which a man would become freed of miseries and get happiness.

sanskrit: oṃ namaḥ paramārthāya puruṣāya mahātmane / arūpabahurūpāya vyāpine paramātmane // niṣkalmaṣāya śuddhāya dhyānayogaratāya ca /
english: Oṃ, salutations to the greatest object, the soul, the great soul, the formless and manyformed, the allpervading, supreme soul, blemishless, pure and person engaged in meditative contemplation.

sanskrit: namaskṛtya pravakṣyāmi yat tatsidhyatu me vacaḥ //
english: Having saluted shall expound. May my words prove true.

sanskrit: varāhāya nṛsiṃhāya vāmanāya mahāmune /
english: Salutations to the Boar, Manlion and Dwarf forms of Viṣṇu, the great sage.

sanskrit: namaskṛtya pravakṣyāmi yattatsidhyatu me vacaḥ //
english: Having saluted shall expound. May my words prove true.

sanskrit: trivikramāya rāmāya vaikuṇṭhāya narāya ca /
english: Salutations to Trivikrama a form of Viṣṇu, as he measured the three steps and removed the pride of the demon Bali, Rāma, Vaikuṇṭha abode ofViṣṇu, the Supreme man.

sanskrit: namaskṛtya pravakṣyāmi yattat sidhyatu me vacaḥ //
english: Having saluted shall expound. May my words become true.

sanskrit: varāha narasiṃheśa vāmaneśa trivikrama / haragrīveśa sarveśa hṛṣīkeśa harāśubham //
english: O Boar, Lord as Manlion, Lord as Dwarf, Trivikrama, Hayagrīveśa Lord as Horsenecked, Lord of all beings, Hṛṣīkeśa Viṣṇu the Lord of all senses destroy my impurity.

sanskrit: aparājitacakrādyaiś caturbhiḥ paramāyudhaiḥ / akhaṇḍitānubhāvaistvaṃ sarvaduṣṭaharo bhava //
english: With these four most excellent weapons, the ever victorious disc and others of unbroken power, you become destroyer of all wicked things.

sanskrit: harāmukasya duritaṃ sarvañca kuśalaṃ kuru / mṛtyubandhārtabhayadaṃ duritasya ca yat phalam //
english: You remove the calamity of such a person and do him all good and also remove the fear of distress due to fetters of death which is the fruit of sins.

sanskrit: parābhidhyānasahitaiḥ prayuktañcābhicārakam / gadasparśamahārogaprayogaṃ jarayā jara //
english: You destroy the magical incantations set up by others with meditation for working evils, causing diseases and decrepitude.

sanskrit: oṃ namo vāsudevāya namaḥ kṛṣṇāya khaḍgine /
english: Oṃ, salutations to Vāsudeva, Kṛṣṇa, bearer of sword.

sanskrit: namaḥ puṣkaranetrāya keśavāyādicakriṇe //
english: Salutations to lotuseyed, Keśava and the first holder of the disc.

sanskrit: namaḥ kamalakiñjalkapītanirmalavāsase / mahāhararipuskandhasṛṣṭacakrāya cakriṇe //
english: Salutations to the wearer of clean dress made yellow by the filaments of lotuses and the disc of Viṣṇu hurled on the shoulders of the enemies at the great battle, and the wielder of the same.

sanskrit: dṃṣṭroddhṛtakṣitibhṛte trayīmūrtimate namaḥ / mahāyajñavarāhāya śeṣabhogāṅkaśāyine //
english: Salutations to the one who lifted the earth on his tusk, who has the three forms embodied in him, the great Yajñavarāha, and the one who reclines on the hood of the serpent Śeṣa.

sanskrit: taptahāṭakakeśāgrajvalatpāvakalocana / vajrādhikanakhasparśaṃ divyasiṃha namostu te //
english: Salutations to you, the divine lion having manes of the hue of molten gold, eyes bright like the burning fire, and claws harder than thunderbolt to touch.

sanskrit: kāśyapāyātihrasvāya ṛgyajuḥsāmabhūṣita / tubhyaṃ vāmanarūpāyākramate gāṃ namo namaḥ //
english: Salutations again and again to you, Kāśyapa, the shortest statured, adorned with the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma veda and the Dwarf form which covered the earth.

sanskrit: varāhāśeṣaduṣṭāni sarvapāpaphalāni vai / marda marda mahādaṃṣṭra marda marda ca tatphalam //
english: O Boar, One with huge tusks, you crush all evils completely, their effects and also the effects of sins.

sanskrit: narasiṃha karālākhya dantaprāntānalojjvala / bhañja bhañja ninādena duṣṭānyasyārtināśana //
english: O Manlion, having a dreadful face and the burning fire in between the teeth, the destroyer of distress, you breakdown all evils by your cry.

sanskrit: ṛgyajuḥsāmagarbhābhirvāgbhirvāmanarūpadhṛk / praśamaṃ sarvaduḥkhāni nayattvasya janārdanaḥ //
english: May Janārdana Viṣṇu, the one who assumed the form of a Dwarf, dispel all grief of this person by words embedded with the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma veda.

sanskrit: aikāhikaṃ dvyāhikañca tathā tridivasaṃ jvaram / cāturthakantathātyugrantathaiva satatajvaram // doṣotthaṃ sannipātotthaṃ tathaivāgantukaṃ jvaram /
english: Destroy feversquotidian occurring on alternate days, tertian, quartan and also the terrible satata, those arising out of derangement of humours, the sannipāta caused by the derangement of three humours, as well as accidental.

sanskrit: gudaghrāṇāṅghrirogāṃś ca kuṣṭharogāṃs tathā kṣayaṃ / kāmalādīṃs tathā rogān pramehāṃścātidāruṇān // bhagandarātisārāṃś ca mukharogāṃś ca valgulīm / aśmarīṃ mūtrakṛcchrāṃś ca rogānanyāṃś ca dāruṇān // ye vātaprabhavā rogā ye ca pittasamudbhavāḥ /
english: The diseases of the eye, the afflictions of the head, diseases pertaining to the stomach, difficulty in breathing in, excessive breathing, burning sensation in the body along with trembling, diseases in the anus, nose, feet, leprosy as well as consumption, and diseases like jaundice and very dreadful urinary disease, fistula, all kinds of dysentry, diseases of the mouth, chest diseases, stone in the bladder, strangury, and other dreadful diseases, diseases caused by wind, biles and phlegm and others like sannipāta, accidentally afflicting diseases, poison due to spiders and boils etc.

sanskrit: vilayaṃ yāntu te sarve viṣṇoruccāraṇena ca /
english: May all these be destroyed by the recitation of the name of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: kṣayaṃ gachhantu cāśeṣāste cakrābhihatā hareḥ //
english: Being struck down by the disc of Hari, may all these ailments be completely destroyed.

sanskrit: acyutānantagovindanāmoccāraṇabhīṣitāḥ /
english: Being scared by the recitation of the names Acyuta undecaying, Ananta unending,.

sanskrit: naśyanti sakalā rogāḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham //
english: Govinda cowherd all are synonyms of Viṣṇu, all the diseases are destroyed.

sanskrit: sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ vāpi kṛtrimaṃ cāpi yadviṣam / dantodbhavaṃ nakhabhavamākāśaprabhavaṃ viṣam // lūtādiprabhavaṃ yacca viṣamanyattu duḥkhadaṃ / śamaṃ nayatu tat sarvaṃ kīrtitosya janārdanaḥ //
english: On his name being recited, may Janārdana destroy the poisons of animate and inanimate objects, as well as artificially made, those caused by teeth, by nails and those arising from the sky as well as those caused by insects like spider and others which cause grief. May the life of boyhood of Viṣṇu Kṛṣṇa destroy the evil forces which afflict mothers and children,.

sanskrit: grahān pretagrahāṃścāpi tathā vai ḍākinīgrahān / vetālāṃś ca piśācāṃś ca gandharvān yakṣarākṣasān // śakunīpūtanādyāṃś ca tathā vaināyakān grahān /
english: such as, planets, evil spirits, female goblins, vampires, ghosts, gandharvas, yakṣas, demons, the impeding forces such as Śakuni, Pūtanā and others, the female forces such as Mukhamaṇḍī, Revatī and the terrible Vṛddharevatī, and the fierce forces known as Vṛddhaka.

sanskrit: vṛddhāś ca ye grahāḥ kecidye ca bālagrahāḥ kvacit / narasiṃhasya te dṛṣṭyā dagdhā ye cāpi yauvane //
english: May these evil forces which afflict at the old age, and the children and the youth be scorched by the looks of the Manlion.

sanskrit: sadā karālavadano narasiṃho mahābalaḥ / grahānaśeṣānniḥśeṣān karotu jagato hitaḥ //
english: May the dreadful face of the Manlion of enormous strength destroy these evil forces completely for the welfare of the world.

sanskrit: narasiṃha mahāsiṃha jvālāmālojjvalānana / grahānaśeṣān sarveśa khāda khādāgnilocana //
english: O Manlion, O Great lion, possessor of garland of flames, Fierymouthed, Possessor of fiery eyes, Lord of all, devour the evil forces completely.

sanskrit: ye rogā ye mahotpātā yadviṣaṃ ye mahāgrahāḥ / yāni ca krūrabhṛtāni grahapīḍāś ca dāruṇāḥ // śastrakṣateṣu ye doṣā jvālāgardabhakādayaḥ / tāni sarvāṇi sarvātmā paramātmā janārdanaḥ // kiñcidrūpaṃ samāsyāya vāsudevāsya nāśaya //37//
english: May the Lord of all beings, Supreme Lord, Janārdana destroy diseases, great portents, poisons, great evil forces, the fierce beings, the afflictions due to the planets whichever is cruel, the injuries caused by weapons, and jvālāgardabhaka etc., assuming any one of the forms of Vāsudeva and hurling the Sudarśana disc which is dreadful like a garland of fire..

sanskrit: sarvaduṣṭopaśamanaṃ kuru devavarācyuta //
english: O Acyuta, the foremost among gods you destroy the evil. forces.

sanskrit: sudarśana mahājvāla cchindhi cchindhi mahārava /
english: O Sudarśana, the huge fire and great sound you destroy all evils.

sanskrit: sarvaduṣṭāni rakṣāṃsi kṣayaṃ yāntu vibhīṣaṇa //
english: O Vibhīṣaṇa one who frightens! may all the evil demons get destroyed.

sanskrit: prācyāṃ pratīcyāṃ ca diśi dakṣiṇottaratas tathā / rakṣāṅkarotu sarvātmā narasiṃhaḥ sugarjitaḥ //
english: May the Manlion deity, the soul ofall beings, possessing terrific roars protect me in the east, west, south and north.

sanskrit: divi bhuvyantarīkṣe ca pṛṣṭhataḥ pārśvatogrataḥ / rakṣāṅkarotu bhagavān bahurūpī janārdanaḥ //
english: May Lord Janārdana of manifold forms protect me in heavens, on the earth, in the sky, behind me, on the sides and in front of me.

sanskrit: yathā viṣṇurjagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣaṃ / tena satyena duṣṭāni śamamasya vrajantu vai //
english: As Viṣṇu protects the entire universe consisting of the celestials, demons and mortals, may the evils of this person be put down by that truth.

sanskrit: yathā viṣṇau smṛte sadyaḥ saṅkṣayaṃ yānti pātakāḥ / satyena tena sakalaṃ duṣṭamasya praśāmyatu //
english: As the sins get destroyed at once by the remembrance of Viṣṇu, may all evil of this person get destroyed by that truth.

sanskrit: paramātmā yathā viṣṇurvedānteṣu ca gīyate / tena satyena sakalaṃ duṣṭamasya praśāmyatu //
english: As the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu has been extolled in the vedānta the philosophical inquiry is known as it forms the concluding portion of the Vedas may all the evils of this person get destroyed by that truth.

sanskrit: yathā yajñeśvaro viṣṇurdeveṣvapi hi gīyate / satyena tena sakalaṃ yanmayoktaṃ tathāstu tat //
english: As Viṣṇu, the lord of sacrifices is exolled among the celestials, may what all has been uttered by me become so by that truth.

sanskrit: śāntirastu śivañcāstu duṣṭamasya praśāmyatu / vāsudevaśarīrotthaiḥ kuśair nirmathitaṃ mayā //
english: May there be peace. May there be good. May the evil of this man get destroyed, being agitated by me with the kuśa grass originating from the body of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: apamārjatu govindo naro nārāyaṇas tathā /
english: May Govinda, the NaraNārāyaṇa cleanse me.

sanskrit: tathāstu sarvaduḥkhānāṃ praśamo japanāddhareḥ //
english: May there be remo, of all miseries by the chant of the names of Hari in the same manner.

sanskrit: apamārjanakaṃ śastraṃ sarvarogādivāraṇam /
english: This is the weapon which cleans and which wards off all diseases.

sanskrit: ayaṃ hariḥ kuśo viṣṇurhatā rogā mayā tava //
english: am Hari. The kuśa grass is Viṣṇu. Your diseases have been destroyed by me.

sanskrit: nirvāṇādiṣu dīkṣāsu cattvāriṃśattathāṣṭa ca /
english: . . An intelligent man has to do fortyeight purificatory rites among the initiatory rites for attaining liberation.

sanskrit: saṃskārān kārayeddhīmān śṛṇutānyaiḥ suro bhavet //
english: You hear them, by which one may become a celestial.

sanskrit: garbhādhānantu yonyāṃ vai tataḥ puṃsavanañcaret / sīmantonnayanañcaiva jātakarma ca nāma ca //
english: One has to perform garbhādhāna as soon as the conception takes place, then the puṃsavana rite, the simantonnayana, the jātakarma, and the naming ceremony.

sanskrit: annāśanaṃ tataścūḍā brahmacaryavratāni ca / catvāri vaiṣṇavī pārthī bhautikī śrotrikī tathā //
english: One has to perform the four ritesthe vaiṣṇavī, pārthī, bhautikī and śrautī, and making a gift of cows, entering the life of a householder after completing one’s vedic studies.

sanskrit: aṣṭakā pārvaṇaśrāddhaṃ śrāvaṇyagrāyaṇīti ca // caitrī cāśvayujī sapta haviryajñāṃś ca tān śṛṇu /
english: The seven kinds of Pākayajñas are aṣṭakā, pārvaṇaśrāddha, śrāvaṇī, āgrayaṇī, caitrī and āśvayujī. The Haviryajñas are seven. You hear them.

sanskrit: ādhānañcāgnihotrañca darśo vai paurṇamāsakaḥ //
english: They are agni ādhāna, agnihotra, darśapūrṇamāsa, cāturmāsya, paśubandha, and sautrāmaṇi.

sanskrit: somasaṃsthāḥ sapta śṛṇu agniṣṭomaḥ kratūttamaḥ // atyagniṣṭoma ukthaś ca ṣoḍaśo vājapeyakaḥ /
english: You hear the seven kinds of Somasaṃsthās agniṣṭoma the excellent sacrifice atyagniṣṭoma, uktha, ṣoḍaśī, vājapeya, atirātra and aptoryāma.

sanskrit: atirātrāptoryāmaś ca sahasreśāḥ savā ime //
english: These are of thousand kinds.

sanskrit: hiraṇyapāṇirhemākṣo hemāṅgo hemasūtrakaḥ // hiraṇyāsyo hiraṇyāṅgo hemajihvo hiraṇyavān /
english: They are hiraṇyāṅghri, hiraṇyākṣa, hiraṇyamitra, hiraṇyapāṇi, hemākṣa, hemāṅga, hemasūtraka, hiraṇyāsya, hiraṇyāṅga, hemajihva, and hiraṇyavat.

sanskrit: aśvamedho hi sarveśo guṇāścāṣṭātha tān śṛṇu //
english: The aśvamedha is the excellent among them. Now you hear the eight virtues.

sanskrit: dayā ca sarvabhūteṣu kṣāntiś caiva tathārjavam / śaucaṃ caivamanāyāso maṅgalaṃ cāparo guṇaḥ //
english: They arecompassion towards all beings, forbearance, sincerity, purity, ease, wishing the welfare of all, liberality and freedom from avarice.

sanskrit: akārpaṇyañcāspṛhā ca mūlena juhuyācchatam /
english: A hundred oblations are to be offered with the basic mystic syllable.

sanskrit: sauraśākteyaviṣṇvīśadīkṣāstvete samāḥ smṛtāḥ //
english: The same procedure is to be followed in the initiation ceremony related to Saura, Śakti the female deity and Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaś caitair bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
english: Being purified by these purificatory rites, one may get enjoyment, release from bondage.

sanskrit: sarvarogādvinirmukto devavadvartate naraḥ /
english: Such a man becoming free from diseases remains like a god.

sanskrit: japyāddhomātpūjanācca dhyānāddevasya ceṣṭabhāk //
english: The rite of parting the hair performed on the fourth, sixth and eighth month of pregnancy.

sanskrit: pavitrārohaṇaṃ vakṣye varṣapūjākalaṃ hareḥ / āṣāḍhādau kārtikānte pratipadvanadā tithiḥ //
english: shall describe the mode of installation of Hari and the benefits of worship for a year. The first day of the lunar fortnight at the commencement of the month of āṣāḍha and the concluding part of the month of Kārttika yields riches.

sanskrit: śriyā gauryā gaṇeśasya sarasvatyā guhasya ca / mārtaṇḍamātṛdurgāṇāṃ nāgarṣiharimanmathaiḥ // śivasya brahmaṇastadvaddvitīyādititheḥ kramāt /
english: Commencing with the second day of the lunar fortnight the installation of Śrī, Gaurī, Gaṇeśa, Sarasvatī, Guha son of Śiva, Mārtaṇḍa Sun, the divine mothers, Durgā, Śiva and Brahmā are performed in order.

sanskrit: yasya devasya yo bhaktaḥ pavitrā tasya sā tithiḥ //
english: To which deity one is devoted, the lunar day of that deity is sacred to him.

sanskrit: ārohaṇe tulyavidhiḥ pṛthak mantrādikaṃ yadi /
english: Only the sacred syllables are different.

sanskrit: sauvarṇe rājataṃ tāmraṃ netrakārpāsikādikaṃ // brāhmaṇyā kartitaṃ sūtraṃ tadalābhe tu saṃskṛtaṃ /
english: A thread spun by a brahmin woman made of gold, silver, copper, silk or cotton etc. or in its absence a purified one is made into nine folds.

sanskrit: triguṇaṃ triguṇīkṛtya tena kuryāt pavitrakaṃ //
english: The investiture is done with that.

sanskrit: aṣtottaraśatādūrdhvaṃ tadardhaṃ cottamādikaṃ /
english: It is excellent if it is longer than one hundred and eight fingerlength or half of it.

sanskrit: kriyālopāvighātārthaṃ yattvayābhihitaṃ prabho // mayā tat kriyate deva yathā yatra pāvitrakaṃ /
english: “Whatever has been prescribed by you, O Lord, for the warding off of the discontinuance of the rite, that is being done by me O Lord.

sanskrit: avighnaṃ tu bhavedatra kuru nātha jayāvyaya //
english: May there be no impediment here in the pavitraka rite.

sanskrit: prārthya tanmaṇḍalāyādau gāyatryā bandhayennaraḥ / oṃ nārāyaṇāya vidmahe vāsudevāya dhīmahi // tanno viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt devadevānurūpataḥ /
english: O Lord of undiminishing success! Grant me this”. Having prayed in this way, one has to tie it to the circular altar at first with the Gāyatrī Oṃ nārāyaṇāya vidmahe vāsudevāya dhīmahi tanno viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt.

sanskrit: jānūrunābhināmāntaṃ pratimāsu pavitrakaṃ // pādāntā vanamālā syādaṣṭottrasahasrataḥ / mālā tu kalpasādhyaṃ vā dviguṇaṃ ṣoḍaśāṅgulāt //
english: A garland made of one thousand and eight woodflowers is consecrated to the Lord of lords extending upto the feet and the pavitraka sacred thread upto the knees, thighs, and navel of the idol befitting him. The garland should be made thirtytwo fingers length.

sanskrit: karṇikā keśaraṃ patraṃ mantrādyaṃ maṇḍalāntakaṃ / maṇḍalāṅgulamātraikacakrābjādyau pavitrakaṃ //
english: In the circular lotus of one finger breadth the pericarp, filament, leaf, the first basic syllable and the outer circumference of the circle are consecrated.

sanskrit: ācāryāṇāṃ ca sūtrāṇi pitṛmātrādipustake //
english: By the measure of one’s fingers the threads for the preceptors are consecrated on the models of the parents on the ground.

sanskrit: nābhyantaṃ dvādaśagranthiṃ tathā gandhapavitrake /
english: Twelve knots made fragrant are consecrated to the end of the navel.

sanskrit: dvyaṅgulāt kalpanādau dvirmālā cāṣṭottaraṃ śataṃ // athavārkacaturviṃśaṣaḍtriṃśanmālikā dvijaḥ /
english: Then two garlands are made ready at first containing one hundred and eight flowers. O twice born one! Otherwise twentyfour or thirtysix garlands should be consecrated to the sun with the ring and middle fingers by those who desire for a daughter.

sanskrit: kaniṣṭādau dvādaśa vā granthayaḥ syuḥ pavitrake / raveḥ kumbhahutāśādeḥ sambhave viṣṇuvanmatam //
english: There may be twelve knots in the sacred thread for the pot of the Sun, and the fire as in the case of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: pīṭhasya pīṭhamānaṃ syānmekhalānte ca kuṇḍakaṃ / yathāśakti sūtragranthiparicāretha vaiṣṇave //
english: According to one’s ability the knots of the sacred thread should be placed in the midst of the articles for the worship of Viṣṇu on the altar in the pit encircled by a girdle.

sanskrit: sūtrāṇi vā saptadaśa sūtreṇa trivibhaktake / rocanāgurukarpūraharidrākuṅkumādibhiḥ // rañjayeccandanādyair vā snānasandhyādikṛnnaraḥ /
english: One who has bathed and performed the twilight worship should dye the seventeen strings divided into three parts, with rocanā yellow pigment, agallochuṃ, camphor, turmeric, saffron or sandal.

sanskrit: ekādaśyāṃ yāgagṛhe bhagavantaṃ hariṃ jayet //
english: Then one has to worship Hari on the eleventh lunar day at the sacrificial yard.

sanskrit: samastaparivārāya baliṃ pīṭhe samarcayet /
english: One has to offer food to all the subordinate deities at the altar.

sanskrit: kṣyauṃ kṣetrapālāya dvārānte dvāropari tathā śriyaṃ //
english: Kṣaum, to the guardian deity at the end of the door. And one should then worship Śrī on the garland.

sanskrit: dhātre dakṣe vidhātre ca gaṅgāñca yamunāṃ tathā /
english: Adorations to Dhātā, Vidhātā names of Brahmā, the rivers Ganges, Yamunā.

sanskrit: śaṅkhapadmanidhī pūjya madhye vāstvapasāraṇaṃ //
english: And after having worshipped the two nidhis śaṅkha and padma at the middle, the vāstu is removed.

sanskrit: sāraṅgāyeti bhūtānāṃ bhūtaśuddhiṃ sthitaś caret //
english: Then one has to perform the purificatory rites for the elements remaining standing.

sanskrit: pañcodghātair gandhatanmātrarūpaṃ bhūmimaṇḍalaṃ /
english: Oṃ, hrūm, haḥ, phaṭ, hrūṃ, absorb the subtle principle of smell.

sanskrit: jānunābhimadhyagataṃ śvetaṃ vai padmalāñchitaṃ /
english: Salutations.

sanskrit: dvirudghātair dhūmravarṇaṃ dhyāyecchuddhendulāñchitam / sparśamātraṃ śabdamātraiḥ saṃhareddhyānayogataḥ //
english: Oṃ, hrūṃ, haḥ, phaṭ, hrūṃ. absorb the subtle principle of taste. Salutations. Oṃ, hrūṃ, haḥ, phaṭ, hrūṃ absorb the subtle principle of touch.

sanskrit: ekodghātena cākāśaṃ śuddhasphaṭikasannibham / nāsāpuṭaśikhāntasthamākāśamupasaṃharet //
english: Salutations, with the single incantation one has to. absorb the etherial space of the colour of pure crystal and pervading the space in between the nose and tuft.

sanskrit: śoṣaṇādyair dehaśuddhiṃ kuryādevam kramāttataḥ /
english: One has to perform purification of the body by desiccation etc.

sanskrit: śuṣkaṃ kalevaraṃ dhyāyet pādādyañca śikhāntakam //
