english: Then the dry body from the foot to the tuft has to be meditated upon.

sanskrit: yaṃ vījena vaṃ vījena jvālāmālāsamāyutam / dehaṃ ramityanenaiva brahmarandhrādvinirgatam // vindundhyātvā cāmṛtasya tena bhasmakalevaram /
english: After having meditated upon the drop which has come out of the cavity of brain with the syllable raṃ and on the body covered by a garland of flames with the syllables yaṃ and vaṃ, one has to besmear the body with the ambrosia of ashes.

sanskrit: samplāvayellamityasmāt dehaṃ sampādya divyakam //
english: Then with the syllable laṃ, it should be converted into a sacred body.

sanskrit: nyāsaṃ kṛtvā kare dehe mānasaṃ yāgamācaret /
english: Having made the nyāsa on the hand and body one has to do mental worship.

sanskrit: viṣṇuṃ sāṅgaṃ hṛdi padme mānasaiḥ kusumādibhiḥ // mūlamantreṇa deveśamprārcayedbhuktimuktidam /
english: Viṣṇu is adored with his retinue in the heartlotus with mental flowers. The lord of lords who yields enjoyment and liberation has to be worshipped with the principal mystic syllable.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ devadeveśa sannidhau bhava keśava //
english: “O lord of gods, welcome to you. O Keśava! be present here.”

sanskrit: gṛhāṇa mānasīṃ pūjāṃ yathārthaṃ paribhāvitām / ādhāraśaktiḥ kūrmātha pūjyonanto mahī tataḥ //
english: “Accept my excellent mental adoration properly.” Then the Tortoise, the supporting power, then Ananta and then the earth have to be worshipped.

sanskrit: madhyegnyādau ca dharmādyā adharmādīndramukhyagam / sattvādi madhye padmañca māyāvidyākhyatattvake // kālatattvañca sūryādimaṇḍalaṃ pakṣirājakaḥ /
english: The righteousness, unrighteousness etc. have to be worshipped in the middle of fire etc., the lotus in the middle of sattva goodness etc., the principle of time, the solar and other regions and the king of birds, in māyā illusion and avidyā ignorance.

sanskrit: madhye tataś ca vāyavyādīśāntā gurupaṅktikāḥ //
english: Then the deities of the quarters commencing with northwest and ending with northeast as well as the line of preceptors.

sanskrit: gaṇaḥ sarasvatī pūjyā nārado nalakūvaraḥ / gururgurupādukā ca paro guruś ca pādukā //
english: The attendant gods, Sarasvatī, Nārada sage, Nalakūbara son of Kubera, the preceptor, the sandals of the preceptor’s preceptor and of the preceptor have to be worshipped.

sanskrit: pūrvasiddhāḥ parasiddhāḥ keśareṣu ca śaktayaḥ / lakṣmīḥ sarasvatī prītiḥ kīrtiḥ śāntiś ca kāntikā //
english: The perfections already accomplished and the later perfections, the female energiesLakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Prīti, Kīrti, Śānti, Kānti, Puṣṭi, Tuṣṭi, Mahendrā etc.

sanskrit: puṣṭistuṣṭirmahendrādyā madhye vācāhito hariḥ / dhṛtiḥ śrīratikāntyādyā mūlena sthāpito 'cyutaḥ //
english: have to be worshipped in the middle. Hari, Dhṛti, Śrī, Rati, and Krānti etc. have to be invoked in the middle. Acyuta is established with the principal mystic syllable.

sanskrit: oṃ abhimukho bhaveti prārthya sannihito bhava / vinyasyārghyādikaṃ datvā gandhādyair mūlato yajet //
english: Having prayed by saying “Oṃ, have your face towards me and come near me,” and having placed the articles of worship and offered scents etc. one has to worship with the principal mystic syllable.

sanskrit: oṃ bhīṣaya bhīṣaya hṛt śirastrāsaya vai punaḥ /
english: Oṃ you frighten, you frighten. Again terrorise the heart and head.

sanskrit: mardaya mardaya śikhā agnyādau śastratostrakaṃ //
english: You pound the tuft, commencing with the flames and from the śastra to the astra.

sanskrit: rakṣa rakṣa pradhvaṃsaya pradhvaṃsaya kavacāya namastataḥ /
english: You protect.

sanskrit: oṃ hrūṃ phaṭ astrāya namo mūlavījena cāṅgakaṃ //
english: Salutations to the armour. Oṃ, hrūṃ, phaṭ. Salutations to the missile.

sanskrit: pūrvadakṣāpyasaumyeṣu mūrtyāvaraṇamarcayet /
english: At first one should worship different forms of idols in the east, south, west and north.

sanskrit: vāsudevaḥ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ pradyumnaścāniruddhakaḥ // agnyādau śrīdhṛtiratikāntayo mūrtayo hareḥ /
english: Vāsudeva, Saṅkaṛṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Agni, Śrī, Dhṛti, Rati and Kānti are the forms of Hari.

sanskrit: śaṅkhacakragadāpadmamagnyādau pūrvakādikaṃ // śārṅgañca muṣalaṃ khaḍgaṃ vanamālāñca tadvahiḥ /
english: The conch, disc, mace, lotus and Agni should be worshipped in the east. The bow, club, sword, and garland of wild flowers should be worshipped outside it.

sanskrit: indrādyāś ca tayānanto nairṛtyāṃ varuṇastataḥ //
english: Indra and others as well as Ananta, and Varuṇa should be worshipped in the southwest.

sanskrit: brahmendreśānayormadhye astrāvaraṇakaṃ vahiḥ /
english: Brahmā and Indra should be worshipped in the northeast and their hosts of weapons on the outside.

sanskrit: airāvatastataśchāgo mahiṣo vānaro jhaṣaḥ // mṛgaḥ śaśo 'tha vṛṣabhaḥ kūrmo haṃsastato vahiḥ /
english: The Airāvata the elephant of Indra, goat, buffalo, monkey, fish, deer, hare, bull, tortoise, and haṃsa should be worshipped and Kṛṣṇa on the outside.

sanskrit: pṛśnigarbhaḥ kumudādyā dvārapālā dvayaṃ dvayaṃ //
english: The gatekeepers Kumuda and others should be worshipped in pairs from the east to the north.

sanskrit: pūrvādyuttaradvārāntaṃ hariṃ natvā baliṃ vahiḥ /
english: After saluting Hari, the food is offered outside.

sanskrit: viṣṇupārṣadebhyo namo balipīṭhe baliṃ dadet // viśvāya viśvaksenātmane īśānake yajet /
english: Salutations to the attendants of Viṣṇu. The offering should be made on the altar. One should worship the Universal Being, the Allpervading on the northeast.

sanskrit: devasya dakṣiṇe haste rakṣāsūtrañca bandhayet //
english: The protective thread should be tied on the right arm of the lord.

sanskrit: saṃvatsarakṛtācāryāḥ sampūrṇaphaladāyine / pavitrārohaṇāyedaṃ kautukaṃ dhāraya oṃ namaḥ //
english: One should say, “Oṃ salutations to the one who confers full benefits of worship done through the whole year. You wear this thread for the purpose of installation.”

sanskrit: upavāsādiniyamaṃ kuryādvai devasannidhau / upavāsādiniyato devaṃ santoṣayāmyaham //
english: One should observe the vow of fasting etc. in the presence of the deity saying, “ am pleasing the deity by observing fasting etc.”

sanskrit: kāmakrodhādayaḥ sarve mā me tiṣṭhantu sarvathā /
english: “May not lust, anger, and all other qualities reside in me ever.

sanskrit: adyaprabhṛti deveśa yāvadvaiśeṣikaṃ dinam //
english: O lord of gods from this day onwards it is the last of them.”

sanskrit: yajamāno hy aśaktaścet kuryānnaktādikaṃ vratī / hutvā visarjayet stutvā śrīkarannityapūjanam //
english: If the worshipper is unable to do as described, he should observe the vow eating only in the night. Having made oblations, the visarjana dismissal is done, after laudation.

sanskrit: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śrīdharāya trailokyamohanāya namaḥ //
english: Oṃ, hrīṃ, śrīm, salutations to Śrīdhara the enchanter of the three worlds.

sanskrit: viśedanena mantreṇa yāgasthānañca bhūṣayet /
english: The assignment of fingers on the different parts of the body by touching them.

sanskrit: namo brahmaṇyadevāya śrīdharāyāvyayātmane // ṛgyajuḥsāmarūpāya śabdadehāya /
english: “Salutations to the brahman, the lord, Śrīdhara and undecaying self, the form of Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma veda, possessing a body composed of sound and Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: vilikhya maṇḍalaṃ sāyaṃ yāgadravyādi cāharet //
english: Having drawn the circular altar in the evening, one has to bring materials for the sacrifice.

sanskrit: prakṣālitakarāṅghriḥ san vinyasyārghyakaro naraḥ / arghyādibhistu śiraḥ prokṣya dvāradeśādikaṃ yathā // ārabhed dvārayāgañca toraṇeśān prapūjayet /
english: Having washed hands and feet and made assignment, and taken the arghya respectful offering in the hands one should sprinkle the arghya on the head and the gateway. He should then begin sacrifice at the gateway. He should worship the presiding deity of the arch.

sanskrit: aśvatthodumbaravaṭaprakṣāḥ pūrvādigā nagāḥ //
english: The aśvattha, udumbara, vaṭa and plakṣa are the trees of the east.

sanskrit: ṛgindraśobhanaṃ prāsyāṃ yujuryamasubhadrakam /
english: The Ṛg veda is the ornament of Indra on the west. The Yajur veda is auspicious for Yama.

sanskrit: sāmāpaś ca sudhanvākhyaṃ somātharvasuhotrakam //
english: The Sāma veda is of the watergod and is known as Sudhanvan. The Atharva veda is of Soma and is called Suhotraka.

sanskrit: toraṇāntaḥ patākāś ca kumudādyā ghaṭadvayam / dvāri dvāri svanāmnārcyāḥ pūrve pūrṇaś ca puṣkaraḥ //
english: The edges of the gate, flags, gatekeepers Kumuda etc. and two pitchers should be adored at every door by their respective names, as well as a pitcher full of water in the east.

sanskrit: ānandanandanau dakṣe vīrasenaḥ suṣeṇakaḥ / sambhavaprabhavau saumye dvārapāṃś caiva pūjayet //
english: Then one should worship the guards of the doorsĀnanda, Nandana, Dakṣa, Vīrasena, Suṣeṇaka, Sambhava and Prabhava in the north Saumya.

sanskrit: astrajaptapuṣpakṣepādvighnānutsārya saṃviśet /
english: One should enter after having removed obstacles by throwing flowers and the repetition of names of weapons.

sanskrit: bhūtaśuddhiṃ vidhāyātha vinyasya kṛtamudravaḥ //
english: Having performed purificatory rites of the elements and the assignment of limbs one should show the posture of hands.

sanskrit: phaṭkārāntāṃ śikhāṃ japtvā sarṣapān dikṣu nikṣipet /
english: Having recited the mystic syllable ending with phaṭ. one should scatter mustard seeds in different directions.

sanskrit: vāsudevena gomūtraṃ saṅkarṣaṇena gomayam // pradyumnena payastajjāt dadhi nārāyaṇād ghṛtam /
english: One should sanctify the cow’s urine with Vāsudeva, cow’s dung with Saṅkarṣaṇa, the milk with Pradyumna and the curd. got from it with Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: ekadvitryādivārāṇi ghṛtādvai bhāgatodhikam // ghṛtapātre tadekatra pañcagavyamudāhṛtam /
english: The ghee should be one part and the others respectively one part more. When these are mixed in a vessel of ghee it is known as the pañcagavya the five products got from a cow.

sanskrit: maṇḍapaprokṣaṇāyaikañcāparamprāśanāya ca //
english: A part of it is for the sprinkling of the temple building and the other for eating.

sanskrit: ānīya daśakumbheṣu indrādyān lokapān yajet /
english: One should worship Indra and other guardian deities of the world in ten pitchers which have been brought.

sanskrit: pūjyājñāṃ śrāvayettāṃś ca sthātavyaṃ cājñayā hareḥ //
english: Having worshipped them one has to make them hear command. They must be installed by the command of Hari.

sanskrit: yāgadravyādi saṃrakṣya vikirān vikirettataḥ /
english: Having kept the articles of sacrifice wellprotected, one must scatter those which must be scattered.

sanskrit: mūlāṣṭaśatasañjaptān kuśakūrcān hareś ca tān //
english: the basic mystic syllable eight hundred times one should take kuśa grass.

sanskrit: aiśānyāṃ diśi tatrasthaṃ sthāpyaṃ kumbhañca vardhanīṃ /
english: Then one should place there a pitcher and the vessel vardhanī at the northeast.

sanskrit: kumbhe sāṅgaṃ hariṃ prārcya vardhanyāmastramarcayet // pradakṣiṇaṃ yāgagṛhaṃ vardhanyācchinnadhārayā /
english: Having worshipped Hari along with the attendant gods in the pitcher one should worship weapons in the vessel vardhanī. Having made a circumambulation of the sacrificial place, water is sprinkled in broken streams by the vardhanī.

sanskrit: siñcannayettataḥ kumbhaṃ pūjayecca sthirāsane //
english: Then the pitcher should be taken and worshipped at a fixed place.

sanskrit: sapañcaratnavastrāḍhyakumbhe gandhādibhirharim / vardhanyāṃ hemagarbhāyāṃ yajedastrañca vāmataḥ //
english: Hari should be worshipped with perfumes etc. in the pitcher adorned with five gems and cloth and the weapons should be worshipped at the left in the Vardhanī in which gold has been placed.

sanskrit: tatsamīpe vāstulakṣmīṃ bhūvināyakamarcayet / srapanaṃ kalpayedviṣṇoḥ saṅkrāntyādau tathaiva ca //
english: In the same way, one should arrange for the consecration of Viṣṇu on the days of movement of the sun from one stellar place to another, and other days of importance.

sanskrit: pūrṇakumbhān nava sthāpya navakoṇeṣu nirbraṇān //
english: Nine dentless jars full of water should be placed in the nine corners.

sanskrit: pūrvādikalasegnyādau pañcāmṛtajalādikam /
english: The five sweet things, water etc. are placed in the east, northeast etc.

sanskrit: dadhi kṣīraṃ madhūṣṇīdaṃ pādyaṃ syāccaturaṅgakam //
english: The curd, milk, honey and hot water are the four constituents for the worship of the feet.

sanskrit: padmaśyāmākadūrvāś ca viṣṇupatnī ca pādyakam /
english: The lotus, śyāmāka a kind of grain, dūrvā grass and the consort of Viṣṇu are for the worship of the feet.

sanskrit: tathāṣṭāṅgārghyamākhyātaṃ yavagandhaphalākṣatam //
english: Together with barley seeds, perfumes, fruits and unbroken rice, this is spoken as constituting the eight articles for the worship of the feet.

sanskrit: kuśāḥ siddhārthapuṣpāni tilā dravyāṇi cārhaṇam /
english: The kuśa grass, flowers of white mustard, sesamum are the articles used for adoration.

sanskrit: lavaṅgakakkolayute dadyādācamanīyakam //
english: One should offer waters for rinsing the mouth together with cloves and kaṅkola berries.

sanskrit: snāpayenmūlamantreṇa devaṃ pañcāmṛtair api / śuddhodaṃ madhyakumbhena devamūrdhni viniḥkṣipet //
english: One should bathe the deity with the five sweet materials along with the recitation of the principal mystic syllable. One should pour pure water on the head of the deity from the central pot.

sanskrit: kalaśānniḥsṛtaṃ toyaṃ kūrcāgraṃ saṃspṛśennaraḥ / śuddhodakena pādyañca arghyamācamanandadet //
english: The worshipper should touch water poured from the pitcher and the tip of the kūrcha bunch of kuśa grass. One should offer pure water for washing the feet and arghya for sipping.

sanskrit: parimṛjya paṭenāṅgaṃ savastraṃ maṇḍalaṃ nayet /
english: After having wiped the body with a cloth, the deity adorned with a cloth should be taken to the altar.

sanskrit: tatrābhyarcyācareddhomaṃ kuṇḍādau prāṇasaṃyamī //
english: Having worshipped him there, one should offer oblations in the sacrificial pit after having controlled breath.

sanskrit: prakṣālya hastau rekhāś ca tisraḥ pūrvāgragāminīḥ / dakṣiṇāduttarāś ca tisraś caivaottarāgragāḥ //
english: Having washed hands, three lines running towards the east from the south to the north and three running towards the north are drawn.

sanskrit: arghyodakena samprokṣya yonimudrāmpradarśayet / dhyātvāgnirūpañcāgnintu yonyāṃ kuṇḍe kṣipennaraḥ //
english: Having sprinkled them with the waters of arghya, one has to show yonimudrā. Having meditated on the fire of the form of the self in the yoni one should throw it in the pit.

sanskrit: pātrāṇyāsādayet paścāddarbhaśrukśruvakādibhiḥ / bāhumātrāḥ paridhaya idhmavraś canameva ca // praṇītā prokṣaṇīpātramājyasthālī ghṛtādikam /
english: Then one should place vessels together with darbha grass and wooden ladles. The twigs and saw should be at arm’s distance. Then one must bring vessels praṇītā, prokṣaṇī and sthālī for holding the clarified butter and offering ghee etc.

sanskrit: prasthadvayaṃ taṇḍulānāṃ yugmaṃ yugmamadhomukham //
english: Two prasthas of rice are spread evenly with face downwards.

sanskrit: praṇītāprokṣaṇīpātre nyaset prāgagragaṃ kuśam /
english: The kuśa grass with its tip facing eastwards should be placed in the praṇītā and prokṣaṇī vessels.

sanskrit: adbhiḥ pūryapraṇītāntu dhyātvā devaṃ prapūjya ca // praṇītāṃ sthāpayedagre dravyāṇāñcaiva madhyataḥ /
english: Having filled praṇītā vessel with water and having meditated on the deity and worshipping, the praṇītā vessel should be placed in the midst of materials in front.

sanskrit: prokṣaṇīmadbhiḥ sampūrya prārcya dakṣe tu vinyaset //
english: Having filled the prokṣaṇī vessel with water and worshipping it, it should be placed on the right side.

sanskrit: caruñca śrapayedagnau brahmāṇaṃ dakṣiṇe nyaset /
english: The oblation should be consigned to the fire. Brahmā should be assigned to the south.

sanskrit: kuśānāstīrya pūrvādau paridhīn sthāpayettataḥ //
english: Having spread the kuśa grass in the east etc. the line of enclosure should be drawn.

sanskrit: vaiṣṇavīkaraṇaṃ kuryād garbhādhānādinā naraḥ /
english: Rites relating to Viṣṇu should be done with the rites such as garbhādhāna etc.

sanskrit: garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmantonnayanañjaniḥ //
english: The garbhādhāna, puṃsavana, sīmantonnayana, and the rite performed after the birth are the rites.

sanskrit: nāmādisamāvartanāntaṃ juhuyādaṣṭa cāhutīḥ / pūrṇāhutīḥ pratikarma śrucā sruvasuyuktayā //
english: Eight offerings to the fire are made commencing with naming ceremony and ending with samāvarta rite performed on the completion of one’s studies. The final oblation is made with the sacrificial ladles for each act.

sanskrit: kuṇḍamadhye ṛtumatīṃ lakṣmīṃ sañcintya homayet /
english: The oblation is made after having meditated on the lustrous goddess Lakṣmī at the middle of the pit.

sanskrit: kuṇḍalakṣmīḥ samākhyātā prakṛtistriguṇātmakā //
english: She is known as Kuṇḍalakṣmī Lakṣmī of the sacrificial pit, the source of the material world composed of the three qualities.

sanskrit: sā yoniḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vidyāmantragaṇasya ca /
english: She is the source of all beings as well as mystic learning and collection of mystic syllables.

sanskrit: vimukteḥ kāraṇaṃ vahniḥ paramātmā ca muktidaḥ //
english: The fire is the cause of liberation. The supreme soul Viṣṇu is the conferer of emancipation.

sanskrit: prācyāṃ śiraḥ samākhyātaṃ bāhū koṇe vyavasthitau / īśānāgneyakoṇe tu jaṅghe vāyavyanairṛte // udaraṃ kuṇḍamityuktaṃ yoniryonirvidhīyate /
english: His head is spoken as at the east, the two arms are situated at the corners northeast and southeast, the two thighs at the northwestern and southwestern corners. The belly is called the sacrificial pit. The organ of generation is said to be the source.

sanskrit: guṇatrayaṃ mekhalāḥ syurdhyātvaivaṃ samidho daśa //
english: The three qualities are the girdle.

sanskrit: pañcādhikāṃstu juhuyāt praṇavānmuṣṭimudrayā / punarāghārau juhuyādvāyvagnyantaṃ tataḥ śrapet //
english: Having meditated thus fifteen twigs should be placed in the fire after reciting Oṃ by showing muṣṭimudrā. Oblations should be made again to the vessels and worship is offered to the vessels on the northwest to southeast.

sanskrit: īśāntaṃ mūlamantreṇa ājyabhāgau tu homayet /
english: Parts of oblations are offered for the directions upto the northeast with the basic mystic syllable.

sanskrit: uttare dvādaśāntena dakṣiṇe tena madhyataḥ //
english: Oblations are made in the north with the syllables forming the end of the twelve syllables and with the middle of the mystic syllable in the south.

sanskrit: vyāhṛtyā padmamadhyasthaṃ dhyāyedvahnintu saṃskṛtam / vaiṣṇavaṃ saptajihvaṃ ca sūryakoṭisamaprabham // candravaktrañca sūryākṣaṃ juhuyācchatamaṣṭa ca /
english: The consecrated fire of Viṣṇu, possessing seven tongues and having the radiance of crores of sums and having the moon as its face and sun as the eye and situated in the middle of the lotus should be meditated upon with the vyāhṛtis. Then one should offer one hundred and eight oblations to this form.

sanskrit: tadardhañcāṣṭa mūlena aṅgānāñca daśāṃśataḥ //
english: Then fiftyeight oblations should be offered and a tenth of it for the limbs.

sanskrit: sampātāhutināsicya pavitrāṇyadhivāsayet / nṛsiṃhamantrajaptāni guptānyastreṇa tāni tu //
english: The basic syllables forming part of the Gāyatrīmantra. Having sprinkled with the residual offering one should perform consecration of the sacred, subtle, and chanted mystic formulae of the manlion.

sanskrit: vastrasaṃveṣṭitānyeva pātrasthānyabhimantrayet / vilvādyadbhiḥ prokṣitāni mantreṇa caikadhā dvidhā //
english: Consecration of the vessels covered by the clothes should be done with mystic syllables. The vessels on which water is sprinkled once or twice with bel leaves, should be placed near the pitcher.

sanskrit: kumbhapārśve tu saṃsthāpya rakṣāṃ vijñāpya deśikaḥ / dantakāṣṭhañcāmarakaṃ pūrve saṅkarṣaṇena tu //
english: Having pronounced the protective spell the priest should place stick for cleansing the teeth and myrabolan on the east with the recitation of syllable for Saṅkarṣaṇa.

sanskrit: pradyumnena bhasmatilān dakṣe gomayamṛttikāṃ / vāruṇena cāniruddhena saumye nārāyaṇena ca // darbhodakañcātha hṛdā agnau kuṅkumarocanaṃ / aiśānyāṃ śirasā dhūpaṃ śikhayā nairṛtepyatha //
english: The ashes, sesamum, and cowdungmixed earth should be consecratedon the south with syllable for Pradyumna, in the west with that of Aniruddha and in the north with that of Nārāyaṇa. Then the waters along with the kuśa grass should be assigned to the southeast with the heart, the saffron and pigment on the northeast with the head, the incense on the southwest with the tuft.

sanskrit: mūlapuṣpāṇi divyāni kavacenātha vāyave / candanāmbvakṣatadadhidūrvāś ca puṭikāsthitāḥ //
english: Then the principal beautiful flowers should be assigned to the northwest with the armour. The sandal, water, unbroken rice, curd, and dūrvā grass are placed in small cups made of leaves.

sanskrit: gṛhaṃ trisūtreṇāveṣṭya punaḥ siddhārthakān kṣipet /
english: The chamber having been encircled by three threads,. the articles kept ready should be thrown again.

sanskrit: dadyātpūjākrameṇātha svaiḥ svair gandhapavitrakaṃ // mantrair vai dvārapādibhyo viṣṇukumbhe tvanena ca /
english: own order of adoration one should offer perfumes and other articles, at the foot of the gate or at the pitcher of Viṣṇu with sacred syllables.

sanskrit: viṣṇutejobhavaṃ ramyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanaṃ //
english: One should then worship the radiant, beautiful form of Viṣṇu capable of destroying all sins.

sanskrit: sarvakāmapradaṃ devaṃ tavāṅge dhārayāmyahaṃ /
english: “ conceive on thy limbs, the deity who grants all coveted things”.

sanskrit: sampūjya dhūpadīpādyair vrajeddvārasamīpataḥ // gandhapuṣpākṣatopetaṃ pavitrañcākhilerpayet /
english: After having worshipped him by showing the incense, lamp etc., one should approach the gateway. One should offer pavitra along with perfumes, flowers and unbroken grains.

sanskrit: pavitraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tejo mahāpātakanāśanaṃ //
english: The radiant pavitra ofViṣṇu is capable of destroying all sins.

sanskrit: dharmakāmārthasiddhyarthaṃ svakeṅge dhārayāmyahaṃ /
english: hold on my limbs the pavitra for the accomplishment of virtue, desire and worldly benefits.

sanskrit: āsane parivārādau gurau dadyāt pavitrakaṃ // gandhādibhiḥ samabhyarcya gandhapuṣpākṣatādimat /
english: The pavitra isoffered to the other attendant deities and to the preceptor seated on a seat. After having worshipped well with perfumes, one has. to offer to Hari along with perfumes, flowers etc.

sanskrit: viṣṇutejobhavetyādimūlena harayerpayet //
english: and saying, “May these become the energy of Viṣṇu”.

sanskrit: vahnisthāya tato datvā devaṃ samprārthayettataḥ / kṣīrodadhimahānāgaśayyāvasthitavigrahaḥ //
english: Having offered to the deity stationed in the fire one should pray to the deity saying, “O lord couched on the great serpent in the milky ocean.

sanskrit: prātastvāṃ pūjayiṣyāmi sannidhau bhava keśava / indrādibhastato datvā viṣṇupārṣadake baliṃ //
english: shall worship you in the morning. You please be present here O Keśava.” Then having offered offerings to Indra and others one should dedicate them to the attendants of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tato devāgrataḥ kumbhaṃ vāsoyugasamanvitaṃ / rocanācandrakāśmīragandhādyudakasaṃyutaṃ //
english: Then one should place a pitcher covered by two cloths and filled with water mixed with perfumes, rocanā, camphor and saffron in front of the deity.

sanskrit: gandhapuṣpādinābhūṣya mūlamantreṇa pūjayet /
english: Having adorned the deity with perfumes and flowers, one should worship him with the mystic formula.

sanskrit: pañcagavyañcarundantakāṣṭhañcaiva kramādbhavet / purāṇaśravaṇaṃ stotraṃ paṭhan jāgaraṇaṃ niśi // parapreṣakabālānāṃ strīṇāṃ bhogabhujāṃ tathā /
english: Having come out of the hall one should place in three circular enclosures the five products obtained from the cow, the sacrificial offering caru and wood for cleansing the teeth. One should read purāṇas and recite hymns and along with servants, a women and children remain awake.

sanskrit: sadyodhivāsanaṃ kuryādvinā gandhapavitrakaṃ //
english: Then the consecration rite should be performed immediately without sacred perfumes.

sanskrit: prātaḥ snānaṃ kṛtvā dvārapālān prapūjya ca / praviśya gupte deśe ca samākṛṣyātha dhārayet //
english: Having bathed in the morning and worshipping the guardian deities, the worshipper should enter the secret chamber and gather articles and place.

sanskrit: pūrvādhivāsitaṃ dravyaṃ vastrābharaṇagandhakaṃ /
english: The articles are the dress, ornaments and perfumes which were offered in the consecration ceremony earlier.

sanskrit: nirasya sarvanirmālyaṃ devaṃ saṃsthāpya pūjayet //
english: Having discarded the remnants of articles for worship, the deity should be wellinstalled and worshipped.

sanskrit: pañcāmṛtaiḥ kaṣāyaiś ca śuddhagandhodakaistataḥ / pūrvādhivāsitaṃ dadyādvastraṃ gandhaṃ ca puṣpakaṃ //
english: One should offer the pañcāmṛta five sweet articles, the unguents, pure and perfumed waters as well as dress, perfumes.and flowers.

sanskrit: agnau hutvā nityavacca devaṃ samprārthayennamet /
english: Having offered unto the fire as done everyday one should pray to the deity and bow down.

sanskrit: samarpya karma devāya pūjāṃ naimittikīṃ caret //
english: Having submitted one’s actions to the deity one should perform the naimittika periodical ceremony.

sanskrit: dvārapālaviṣṇukumbhavardhanīḥ prārthayeddhariṃ /
english: One should worship the gatekeeper, the pitcher ofViṣṇu and the varddhanī vessel and Hari.

sanskrit: ato deveti mantreṇa mūlamantreṇa kumbhake //
english: The pitcher should be consecrated with the sacred syllable ‘ato deva’ and the following.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa namastubhyaṃ gṛhṇīṣvedaṃ pavitrakaṃ /
english: “O Kṛṣṇa! Salutations to you.

sanskrit: pavitrīkaraṇārthāya varṣapūjāphalapradaṃ //
english: You accept this sacred thread for the sake of purifying all and which yields fruits of a year’s worship.

sanskrit: pavitrakaṃ kurudhvādya yanmayā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ /
english: You purify sins that had been committed by me.

sanskrit: śuddho bhavāmyahaṃ deva tvatprasādāt sureśvara //
english: O God! the lord of celestials will be purified by your grace.”

sanskrit: pavitrañca hṛdādyaistu ātmānamabhiṣicya ca / viṣṇukumbhañca samprokṣya vrajeddevasamīpataḥ //
english: Having sprinkled mentally the sacred thread and the self, and having sprinkled the pitcher of Viṣṇu, one should go near the deity.

sanskrit: pavitramātmane dadyādrakṣābandhaṃ visṛjya ca /
english: One should offer a sacred thread to the self, after having discarded the protective thread tied on the hand.

sanskrit: gṛhāṇa brahmasūtrañca yanmayā kalpitaṃ prabho // karmaṇāṃ pūraṇārthāya yathā doṣo na me bhavet /
english: O Lord! Accept the sacred thread that has been made ready by me, for the sake of accomplishing rites so that there may not be any fault on me.

sanskrit: dvārapālāsanagurumukhyānāñca pavitrakam // kaniṣṭādi ca devāya vanamālāñca mūlataḥ / hṛdādiviśvaksenānte pavitrāṇi samarpayet //
english: The sacred thread should be offered to the gatekeepers, the seat and to the chief preceptors. The garlands of forest flowers should be offered to the gods of inferior order with the basic formula. The articles should be offered to the heart etc.

sanskrit: vahnau hutvāgnivartibhyo viṣṇvādibhyaḥ pavitrakam / prārcya pūrṇāhutiṃ dadyāt prāyaścittāya mūlataḥ //
english: and ending with Viṣvaksena an epithet of Viṣṇu. Having offered to the fire the oblations placed near the fire for Viṣṇu and other gods, and having worshipped, the final oblation should then be made with the basic formula for the expiation of one’s sins.

sanskrit: aṣṭottaraśataṃ vāpi pañcopaniṣadaistataḥ / maṇividrumamālābhirmandārakusumādibhiḥ // iyaṃ sāṃvatsarī pūjā tavāstu garuḍadhvaja /
english: O Lord! having Garuḍa as your emblem! Let this be your annual adoration with one hundred and eight or five Upaniṣads and with garlands of gems and corals, the flowers mandāra and others.

sanskrit: vanamālā yathā deva kaustubhaṃ satataṃ hṛdi // tadvat pavitratantūṃś ca pūjāṃ ca hṛdaye vaha /
english: “O Lord! Just as the garland of wild flowers and the kaustubha gem are worn always on the chest, so also bear the sacred thread and the worship on the chest.

sanskrit: kāmato 'kāmato vāpi yatkṛtaṃ niyamārcane // vidhinā vighnalopena paripūrṇaṃ tadastu me / prārthya natvā kṣamāpyātha pavitraṃ mastake 'rpayet //
english: Whatever has been done wantonly or unwantonly in the regulations of the worship let it become complete by the rite shorn of impediments.” Having worshipped, bowing down, and requesting them the purified article should be placed on one’s own head.

sanskrit: datvā baliṃ dakṣiṇābhirvaiṣṇavantoṣayedguruṃ /
english: Having made offering to Viṣṇu the preceptor should be satisfied by giving the fees.

sanskrit: viprān bhojanavastrādyair divasaṃ pakṣameva vā //
english: The brahmins should be satisfied by giving food, clothes and other things either for a day or for a fortnight.

sanskrit: pavitraṃ snānakāle ca avatārya samarpayet /
english: At the time of bathing, having gone down into the waters, the sacred thread should be offered.

sanskrit: anivāritamannādyaṃ dadyādbhuṅktetha ca svayaṃ //
english: Without any restriction, food and other things should be given to others and then one has to eat.

sanskrit: visarjane 'hni sampūjya pavitrāṇi visarjayet /
english: Having worshipped fire at the rite of dismissal the threads are removed.

sanskrit: sāṃvatsarīmimāṃ pūjāṃ sampādya vidhivanmama // vraja pavitrakedānīṃ viṣṇulokaṃ visarjitaḥ /
english: One should then say “Having thus duly accomplished my annual adoration O thread! you now go to the world of Viṣṇu having been permitted by me.

sanskrit: madhye someśayoḥ prārcya viṣvaksenaṃ hi tasya ca // pavitrāṇi samabhyarcya brāhmaṇāya samarpayet /
english: Having worshipped Someśa and Viṣvaksena at the centre and having worshipped the sacred threads one should dedicate them to thebrahmins.

sanskrit: yāvantastantavastasmin pavitre parikalpitāḥ // tāvadyugasahasrāṇi viṣṇuloke mahīyate /
english: As many knots as there are in that thread one will live gloriously for so many thousands of years in the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: kulānāṃ śatamuddhṛtya daśa pūrvān daśāparān / viṣṇulokaṃ tu saṃsthāpya svayaṃ muktimavāpnuyāt //
english: One will get release from bondage after having redeemed hundreds of his ancestors the ten preceding and the ten succeeding and having established them in the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: saṅkṣepāt sarvadevānāṃ pavitrārohaṇaṃ śṛṇu /
english: Listen to the description of the mode of investiture for all deities.

sanskrit: pavitra sarvalakṣma syāt svarasānalagaṃ tvapi //
english: The thread is the primary characteristic as. well as its yellow orpiment.

sanskrit: jagadyone samāgaccha parivāragaṇaiḥ saha /
english: O the cause of the universe! come here along witḥ the attendant gods.

sanskrit: nimantrayāmyahaṃ prātardadyāntubhyaṃ pavitrakaṃ ///
english: invite you in the morning and offer this sacred thread.

sanskrit: jagatsṛje namastubhyaṃ gṛhṇīṣvedaṃ pavitrakaṃ /
english: O the creator of the universe.

sanskrit: pavitrīkaraṇārthāya varṣapūjāphalapradaṃ // śivadeva namastubhyaṃ gṛhṇīṣvedaṃ pavitrakaṃ / maṇividrumamālābhirmandārakusumādibhiḥ //
english: Salutations to you! Accept this sacred thread for the sake of purification and which conveys the fruits of the annual worship. O God Śiva! Salutations to you! Accept this sacred thread along with garlands of gems and corals and mandāra flowers.

sanskrit: iyaṃ sāṃvatsarī pūjā tavāstu vedavitpate /
english: O lord of the learned in the Vedas! Let this be your annual worship.

sanskrit: sāṃvatsarīmimāṃ pūjāṃ sampādya vidhimanmama // vraja pavitrakedānīṃ svargalokaṃ visarjitaḥ /
english: After having accomplished this annual worship of mine according to the rules, O articles of worship! go to heavens after being discarded by me.

sanskrit: sūryadeva namastubhyaṃ gṛhṇīṣvedaṃ pavitrakaṃ //
english: O lord Sun! Salutations to you.

sanskrit: śivadeva namastubhyaṃ gṛhṇīṣvedaṃ pavitrakaṃ //
english: Accept this article of worship. O Lord Śiva! Salutations to you.

sanskrit: pavitrīkaraṇārthāya varṣapūjāphalapradaṃ /
english: Accept this.article of worship which is capable of yielding fruits of annual worship for the sake of purification.

sanskrit: vāṇeśvara namastubhyaṃ gṛhṇīṣvedaṃ pavitrakaṃ //
english: O lord of gaṇas! Salutations to you.

sanskrit: pavitrīkaraṇārthāya varṣapūjāphalapradaṃ /
english: Accept this.article of worship which is capable of yielding fruits of annual worship for the sake of purification.

sanskrit: śaktideva namastubhyaṃ gṛhṇīṣvedaṃ pavitrakaṃ //
english: O goddess Śakti! Salutations to you.

sanskrit: pavitrīkaraṇārthāya varṣapūjāphalapradaṃ /
english: Accept this.article of worship which is capable of yielding fruits of annual worship for the sake of purification.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇamayaṃ sūtramaniruddhamayaṃ varaṃ // dhanadhānyāyurārogyapradaṃ sampradadāmi te /
english: dedicate unto you this excellent thread verily the same as lord Nārāyaṇa and lord Aniruddha and which is capable of yielding fruits of annual worship for the sake of purification and which yields wealth, grains and health.

sanskrit: kāmadevamayaṃ sūtraṃ saṅkarṣaṇamayaṃ varaṃ // vidyāsantatisaubhāgyapradaṃ sampradadāmi te /
english: dedicate unto you this excellent thread verily the same as Kāmadeva and Saṅkarṣaṇa, which yields learning, progeny and welfare.

sanskrit: vāsudevamayaṃ sūtraṃ dharmakāmārthamokṣadaṃ // saṃsārasāgarottārakāraṇaṃ pradadāmi te /
english: dedicate unto you this thread verily the same as Vāsudeva, which yields dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa and which is the cause for transport over the ocean of mundane existence.

sanskrit: viśvarūpamayaṃ sūtraṃ sarvadaṃ pāpanāśanaṃ // atītānāgatakulasamuddhāraṃ dadāmi te /
english: This thread verily the universal form is the donor of all things, the destroyer of sins and elevates past and future lineage.

sanskrit: kaniṣṭhādīni catvāri manubhistu kramāddade //
english: offer in order to the four younger deities with the mystic syllables.

sanskrit: vāsudevādyālayasya kṛtau vakṣye phalādikaṃ /
english: wil now describe the benefits of erecting the temples of Vāsudeva and others.

sanskrit: cikīrṣordevadhāmādi sahasrajanipāpanut // manasā sadmakartṝṇāṃ śatajanmāghanāśanaṃ /
english: One who is desirous of constructing the temples of gods gets freed from sins incurred in thousand births. Those who conceive of building a temple get the sins accrued in hundreds of births destroyed.

sanskrit: yenumodanti kṛṣṇasya kriyamāṇaṃ narā gṛhaṃ // tepi pāpair vinirmuktāḥ prayāntyacyutalokatāṃ /
english: Those who approve the building of a temple for lord Kṛṣṇa, also become free from their sins and go to the world of Acyuta Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: samatītaṃ bhaviṣyañca kulānāmayutaṃ naraḥ // viṣṇulokaṃ nayatyāśu kārayitvā harergṛhaṃ /
english: Having built a temple for Hari, a man immediately conveys a lakh of his ancestors both past and future to the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: vasanti pitaro dṛṣṭvā viṣṇuloke hy alaṅkṛtāḥ // vimuktā nārakair duḥkhaiḥ kartuḥ kṛṣṇasya mandiraṃ /
english: The manes of a person who builds a temple for Viṣṇu having seen it remain in the world of Viṣṇu wellhonoured and relieved of their sufferings in hells.

sanskrit: brahmahatyādipāpaughaghātakaṃ devatālayaṃ //
english: The erection of the abode for the deity destroys sins such as the killing of a brahmin.

sanskrit: phalaṃ yannāpyate yajñair dhāma kṛtvā tadāpyate / devāgāre kṛte sarvatīrthasnānaphalaṃ labhet //
english: Whichever benefit could not be obtained by doing sacrificial rites, could be got by the erection of an abode for the god. He who erects an abode for the god reaps fruits of bathing in all holy waters.

sanskrit: devādyarthe hatānāñca raṇe yattatphalādikaṃ / śāṭhyena pāṃśunā vāpi kṛtaṃ dhāma ca nākadaṃ //
english: Even the making of a temple by perfidy with dust one would reach heaven. It gets more benefits than those got being slain in the battle.

sanskrit: ekāyatanakṛt svargī tryagārī brahmalokabhāk /
english: One who builds one temple goes to heaven. One who builds three temples goes to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: pañcāgārī śambhulokamaṣṭāgārāddharau sthitiḥ //
english: The builder of five abodes reaches the world of Śambhu Śiva. By building eight abodes one remains in the world of Hari.

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśālayakārī tu bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
english: One who builds sixteen abodes gets enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: kaniṣṭhaṃ madhyamaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kārayitvā harergṛhaṃ // svargaṃ ca vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ mokṣamāpnoti ca kramāt /
english: Having built a small, medium or excellent temple for Hari one gets heaven or the world of Viṣṇu or emancipation respectively in order.

sanskrit: śreṣṭhamāyatanaṃ viṣṇoḥ kṛtvā yaddhanavān labhet // kaniṣṭhenaiva tat puṇyaṃ prāpnotyadhanavānnaraḥ /
english: Which merits a rich man would get by erecting an excellent temple of Viṣṇu, a poor man would get by erecting a small temple itself.

sanskrit: samutpādya dhanaṃ kṛtyā svalpenāpi surālayaṃ // kārayitvā hareḥ puṇyaṃ samprāpnotyadhikaṃ varaṃ /
english: Having acquired riches and built a temple for Hari even with a small portion of it one would get excellent and enormous merits.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇātha sahasreṇa śatenārdhena vā hareḥ // kārayan bhavanaṃ yāti yatrāste garuḍadhvajaḥ /
english: By erecting a temple of Hari with a lakh or thousand or hundred or fifty units of money one would reach the place of that person who has the eagle in his banner.

sanskrit: bālye tu krīḍamāṇā ye pāṃśubhirbhavanaṃ hareḥ // vāsudevasya kurvanti tepi tallokagāminaḥ /
english: Those who play in their childhood with the building of abodes of Hari with earth also go to the world of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: tīrthe cāyatane puṇye saddhakṣetre tathāṣṭame // karturāyatanaṃ viṣṇoryathoktāttriguṇaṃ phalaṃ /
english: The building of temples of Viṣṇu at holy places, within temples, accomplished place or hermitage yields threefold benefit than those already described.

sanskrit: bandhūkapuṣpavinyāsaiḥ sudhāpaṅkena vaiṣṇavaṃ // ye vilimpanti bhavanaṃ te yānti bhagavatpuraṃ /
english: Those who decorate the temple ofViṣṇu with the bandhūka flowers and an oint with fragrant paste, also reach the place of the lord.

sanskrit: samuddhṛtya harerdhāma prāpnoti dviguṇaṃ phalaṃ /
english: Having erected the temple of Hari, a person obtains twofold merits after having elevated the fallen, the falling and halffallen.

sanskrit: patitasya tu yaḥ kartā patitasya ca rakṣitā //
english: He who brings about the fall of a man is the protector of one fallen.

sanskrit: iṣṭakānicayastiṣṭhed yāvadāyatane hareḥ // sakulastasya vai kartā viṣṇuloke mahīyate /
english: By erecting a temple of Viṣṇu one reaches his region. As long as the bricks remain in the temple of Hari, the founder of that family is honoured in the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: sa eva puṇyavān pūjya iha loke paratra ca //
english: He becomes pious and adorable in this world as well as the next.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇasya vāsudevasya yaḥ kārayati ketanaṃ / jātaḥ sa eva sukṛtī kulantenaiva pāvitaṃ //
english: He who builds a temple for Kṛṣṇa, the son of Vasudeva is born as a man of good deeds and his family gets purified.

sanskrit: viṣṇurudrārkadevyādergṛhakartā sa kīrtibhāk /
english: He who builds an abode for Viṣṇu, Rudra, Sun or the goddess etc.

sanskrit: kiṃ tasya vittanicayair mūḍhasya parirakṣitaḥ //
english: What is the use of the hoarded riches for an ignorant person?

sanskrit: duḥkhārjitair yaḥ kṛṣṇasya na kārayati ketanaṃ / nopabhogyaṃ dhanaṃ yasya pitṛvipradivaukasāṃ // nopabhogāya bandhūnāṃ vyarthastasya dhanāgamaḥ /
english: If one does not cause an abode for Kṛṣṇa to be built with wealth acquired by hard work and if one’s wealth could not be enjoyed by manes, brahmins, celestials and relatives, his acquisition of wealth is useless.

sanskrit: yathā dhruvo nṛṇāṃ mṛtyurvittanāśas tathā dhruvaḥ //
english: As death is certain for a man so also the destruction of wealth.

sanskrit: mūḍhastatrānubadhnāti jīvitetha cale ghane / yadā vittaṃ na dānāya nopabhogāya dehināṃ // nāpi kīrtyai na dharmāthaṃ tasya svāmyetha ko guṇaḥ /
english: One who does not spend his riches for charities or for enjoyments is stupid and is being bound even while alive, while the riches are flickery. Is there any merit in being the lord of wealth acquired either accidentally or by one’s effort, if it is not spent for acquiring fame or for philanthropy?

sanskrit: dadyāt samyag dvijāgryebhyaḥ kīrtanāni ca kārayet /
english: One may give to the foremost brahmins and also do such acts which would glorify him.

sanskrit: dānebhyaścādhikaṃ yasmāt kīrtanebhyo varaṃ yataḥ // atastatkārayeddhīmān viṣṇvādermandirādikaṃ /
english: More than the charities and more than the acts which would glorify him, one has to build the temples of Viṣṇu and other gods.

sanskrit: viniveśya harerdhāma bhaktimadbhir narottamaiḥ // niveśitaṃ bhavet kṛtsnaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaraṃ /
english: The temple of Hari being set up by devoted great men, the three worlds, the movable and immovable things and the entire objects get established.

sanskrit: bhūtaṃ bhavayam bhaviṣyañca sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tathetarat // ābrāhmastambaparyantaṃ sarvaṃ viṣṇoḥ samudbhavaṃ /
english: All the things beginning with Brahmā to the Pillar, that has already born, that is being born, that is to be born, the gross, the minute and the other things are born of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tasya devādidevasya sarvagasya mahātmanaḥ // niveśya bhavanaṃ viṣṇor na bhūyo bhuvi jāyate /
english: Having set up an abode for that lord of lords, the omnipresent, the great Viṣṇu, one is not born again in this world.

sanskrit: yathā viṣṇordhāmakṛtau phalaṃ tadvaddivaukasāṃ // śivabrahmārkavighneśacaṇḍīlakṣmyādikātmanāṃ /
english: By building temples for the celestials, Śiva, Brahmā, Sun, Vighneśa lord of impediments, Caṇḍī Pārvatī, Lakṣmī and others a man reaps the same benefit as he would get for building an abode for Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: devālayakṛteḥ puṇyaṃ pratimākaraṇedhikaṃ //
english: Greater merit is acquired by installing images of gods.

sanskrit: pratimāsthāpane yāge phalasyānto na vidyate /
english: In the rites relating to installation of an idol there is no limit for the fruits gained.

sanskrit: mṛṇmayāddāruje puṇyaṃ dārujādiṣṭkābhave // iṣṭakotthācchailaje syāddhemāderadhikaṃ phalaṃ /
english: One made of bricks yields greater merit than that made of wood. One made of stones gives greater merit than that made of bricks. Images made of gold and other metals yield more benefits.

sanskrit: saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ prārambhādeva naśyati //
english: Sins committed in seven births get destroyed even at the very commencement of installation.

sanskrit: devālayasya svargī syānnarakaṃ na sa gacchati /
english: One who builds a temple goes to heaven and never goes to hell.

sanskrit: kulānāṃ śatamuddhṛtya viṣṇulokaṃ nayennaraḥ //
english: Having elevated a hundred of his ancestors he conveys them to the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: yamo yamabhaṭānāha devamandirakāriṇaḥ /
english: Yama god of death said to his emissaries

sanskrit: pratimāpūjādikṛto nāneyā narakaṃ narāḥ // devālayādyakartāra āneyāste tu gocare /
english: “Those men who build temples of gods and adore the idols are not to be brought to hell. Bring them to my view who have not built temples and other things.

sanskrit: visāradhvaṃ yathānyāyanniyogo mama pālyatāṃ //
english: Move around in the befitting way and execute my directive.

sanskrit: nājñābhaṅgaṃ kariṣyanti bhavatāṃ jantavaḥ kvacit / kevalaṃ te jagattātamanantaṃ samupāśritāḥ //
english: Except those who have resorted to Ananta, the father of the universe, no other beings would at any time disregard the command.

sanskrit: bhavadbhiḥ parihartavyāsteṣāṃ nātrāsti saṃsthitiḥ /
english: Those who are devotees of Viṣṇu and have their mind fixed on him have to be avoided by you. They are not to live here.

sanskrit: pūjayanti sadā viṣṇuṃ te vastyājyāḥ sudūrataḥ /
english: Those who always adore Viṣṇu should be avoided by you from a distance.

sanskrit: yastiṣṭhan prasvapan gacchannuttiṣṭhan skhalite sthite // saṅkīrtayanti govindaṃ te vastyājyāḥ sudūrataḥ /
english: Those who sing the glories of Govinda while standing or sleeping or walking or standing behind or stumbling or remaining at a place are to be avoided by you from a distance.

sanskrit: nityanaimittikair devaṃ ye yajanti janārdanam //
english: Those who worship Janārdana with obligatory and occasional rites are not to be beheld by you.

sanskrit: nāvalokyā bhavadbhiste tadgatā yānti tadgatim /
english: Those who follow this course attain good position.

sanskrit: ye puṣpadhūpavāsobhirbhūṣaṇaiścātivallabhaiḥ // arcayanti na te grāhyā narāḥ kṛṣṇālaye gatāḥ /
english: Those who worship the god with flowers, incense, raiments, favourite ornaments, and those who have gone to the abode of Kṣṣṇa are not to be seized by you.

sanskrit: upalepanakartāraḥ sammārjanaparāś ca ye // kṛṣṇālaye parityajyāsteṣāṃ putrās tathā kulam /
english: Those who besmear with unguents, and those who are engaged in sprinkling his body, their children and their descendants should be left in the temple of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: yena cāyatanaṃ viṣṇoḥ kāritaṃ tatkulodbhavam // puṃsāṃ śataṃ nāvalokyaṃ bhavadbhirduṣṭacetasā /
english: Hundreds of men born in the family of one who has built the temple of Viṣṇu should not be seen by you with evil mind.

sanskrit: yastu devālayaṃ viṣṇordāruśailamayaṃ tathā // kārayen mṛṇmayaṃ vāpi sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate /
english: Whoever builds a temple of Viṣṇu with wood or stone or earth gets free from all sins.

sanskrit: ahanyahani yajñena yajato yan mahāphalam // prāpnoti tat phalaṃ viṣṇoryaḥ kārayati ketanaṃ /
english: One who builds the temple of Viṣṇu gets that great benefit which one would acquire by doing sacrificial rites everyday.

sanskrit: kulānāṃ śatamāgāmi samatītaṃ tathā śataṃ // kārayan bhagavaddhāma nayatyacyutalokatāṃ /
english: By building a temple for Viṣṇu one conveys hundreds of his discendants and hundreds of his ancestors to the world of Acyuta.

sanskrit: saptalokamayo viṣṇustasya yaḥ kurute gṛhaṃ //
english: Viṣṇu is identical with the seven worlds.

sanskrit: tārayatyakṣayāṃllokānakṣayān pratipadyate /
english: One who builds a house for him saves the endless worlds and also obtains endlessness.

sanskrit: iṣṭakācayavinyāso yāvantyabdāni tiṣṭhati // tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi tatkarturdivi saṃsthitiḥ /
english: One who builds a temple for him, lives for so many years in heaven as the number of years the set up bricks would remain.

sanskrit: pratimākṛdviṣṇulokaṃ sthāpako līyate harau / devasadmapratikṛtipratiṣṭhākṛttu gocare //
english: The maker of the idol would reach the world of Viṣṇu. One who consecrates it would get absorbed in Hari. One who builds a temple, makes an idol and installs it goes within his range.

sanskrit: yamoktā nānayaṃstetha pratiṣṭhādikṛtaṃ hareḥ /
english: “ have not brought one who has installed Hari as told by Yama”.

sanskrit: hayaśīrṣaḥ pratiṣṭhārthaṃ devānāṃ brahmaṇe 'bravīt //
english: Hayaśiras told Brahmā for the installation of gods.

sanskrit: viṣṇvādīnāṃ pratiṣṭhādi vakṣye brahman śṛṇuṣva me /
english: O Brahman! Listen to me speaking about the installation of images of Viṣṇu and others.

sanskrit: proktāni pañcarātarāṇi saptarātrāṇi vai mayā //
english: The principles of Pañcarātra and Saptarātra have already been described by me.

sanskrit: vyastāni munibhirloke pañcaviṃśatisaṅkhyayā /
english: They have been divided by the sages into twentyfive books in this world.

sanskrit: hayaśīrṣaṃ tantramādyaṃ tantraṃ trailokyamohanaṃ //
english: Hayaśīrṣa tantra is the first one.

sanskrit: nāradīyañca sampraśnaṃ śāṇḍilyaṃ vaiśvakaṃ tathā // satyoktaṃ śaunakaṃ tantraṃ vāsiṣṭhaṃ jñānasāgaraṃ / svāyambhuvaṃ kapilañca tārkṣaṃ nārāyaṇīyakaṃ // ātreyaṃ nārasiṃhākhyamānandākhyaṃ tathāruṇaṃ /
english: Trailokyamohana, Vaibhava, Pauṣkara, Prahlāda, Gārgya, Gālava, Nāradīya, Śrīpraśna, Śāṇḍilya, Aiśvara, spoken by Satya, Śaunaka, Vāsiṣṭha, Jñānasāgara, Svāyambhuva, Kāpila, Tārkṣya, Nārāyaṇīyaka, Ātreya, Nārasiṃha, Ānanda, Aruṇa, Baudhāyana, and the one spoken by Viśva as the quintessence of that the preceding, having eight parts or the other books.

sanskrit: pratiṣṭhāṃ hi dvijaḥ kuryānmadhyadeśādisambhavaḥ /
english: A brahmin born in the middle country may perform installation rite.

sanskrit: nakacchadeśasambhūtaḥ kāverīkoṅkaṇodgataḥ // kāmarūpakaliṅgoptyaḥ kāñcīkāśmīrakośalaḥ /
english: Those who were born in Kaccha Cutch, in the regions of the river Kāverī, Koṅkaṇa, Kāmarūpa, Kaliṅga, Kāñcī, Kāśmīra, Kosala should not do installation.

sanskrit: ākāśavāyutejombu bhūretāḥ pañca rātrayaḥ //
english: The sky, wind, radiance, water, and earth are the pañcarātra.

sanskrit: acaitanyāstamodriktāḥ pañcarātravivarjitaṃ /
english: Those other than the pañcarātra are inanimate and engulfed in darkness.

sanskrit: brahmāhaṃ viṣṇuramala iti vidyātsa deśikaḥ //
english: He is the preceptor who has the knowledge “ am brahman and stainless Viṣṇu”.

sanskrit: sarvalakṣaṇahīṇopi sa gurustantrapāragaḥ /
english: Even though deficient in all characteristics he who is a. master of the tantras is to be looked upon as the preceptor.

sanskrit: nagarābhimukhāḥ sthāpyā devā na ca parāṅmukhāḥ //
english: The image of the deity should be placed facing the city and never turned backwards.

sanskrit: kurukṣetre gayādau ca nadīnāntu samīpataḥ / brahmā madhye tu nagare pūrve śakrasya śobhanaṃ //
english: At Kurukṣetra, Gayā and other places and near the rivers, the image of Brahmā at the centre of the city and the image of Indra on the east are auspicious.

sanskrit: agnāvagneś ca mātṝṇāṃ bhūtānāñca yamasya ca / dakṣiṇe caṇḍikāyāś ca pitṛdaityādikasya ca //
english: The images of Agni, mothers, goblins, and Yama should be placed in the southeast. The images of Caṇḍikā should be placed in the south and those of the manes and demons in the southwest.

sanskrit: vairṛte mandiraṃ kuryāt varuṇādadeś ca vāruṇe /
english: The temples ofVaruṇa and others should be built in the west.

sanskrit: vāyor nāgasya vāyavye saumye yakṣaguhasya ca //
english: The images of Vāyu and Nāga serpent should be on the northwest and those of Yakṣa and Guha Kārttikeya on the north.

sanskrit: caṇḍīśasya maheśasya aiśe viṣṇoś ca sarvaśaḥ /
english: Those of Caṇḍīśa the lord of Caṇḍī, the great lord and Viṣṇu are always placed in the northeast.

sanskrit: samaṃ vāpyadhikaṃ vāpi na kartavyaṃ vijānatā / ubhayordviguṇāṃ sīmāṃ tyaktvā cocchrayasammitāṃ // prāsādaṃ kārayedanyaṃ nobhayaṃ pīḍayedbudhaḥ /
english: One should not knowingly construct a temple of a reduced size or equal in size or bigger in size than another temple already constructed so as to encroach upon it. A wiseman would leave between them a space measuring twice the elevation and erect a new temple without affecting both the temples.

sanskrit: prākārasīmāparyantaṃ tato bhutabaliṃ haret /
english: After having examined the ground one has to take possession of it.

sanskrit: māṣaṃ haridrācūrṇantu salājaṃ dadhisaktubhiḥ // aṣṭākṣareṇa saktūṃś ca pātāyitvāṣṭadikṣu ca /
english: The offerings to the presiding goblins should be offered upto the outer enclosing wall with a mixture of black gram, turmeric powder, fried grains, curd and flour.

sanskrit: rākṣasāś ca piśācāś ca yesmiṃstiṣṭhanti bhūtale // sarve te vyapagacchantu sthānaṃ kuryāmahaṃ hareḥ /
english: Having dropped the flour in all directions along with the recitation of eight syllables one has to say, “The demons and goblins who remain on this ground may go away.

sanskrit: halena vāhayitvā gāṃ gobhiś caivāvadārayet //
english: am making a place for Hari.” Having cleaved the earth with the plough one should cleave it with oxen.

sanskrit: pramāṇvaṣṭakenaiva trasareṇuḥ prakīrtyate //19//
english: Eight Paramāṇus make one rathāṇu. Eight rathāṇus are said to make one trasareṇu.

sanskrit: tair aṣṭabhistu bālāgraṃ likhyā tair aṣṭabhirmatā /
english: Eight times that makes one bālāgra and eight times that is known as likhyā.

sanskrit: tābhiryūkāṣṭabhiḥ khyātā tāścāṣṭau yavamadhyamaḥ //
english: Eight times that is known as yūka. Eight times that is a yavamadhyama.

sanskrit: yavāṣṭakair aṅgulaṃ syāccaturviṃśāṅgulaḥ karaḥ /
english: Eight times yava makes one aṅgula. Twentyfour aṅgulas make one kara.

sanskrit: caturaṅgulasaṃyuktaḥ sa hastaḥ padmahastakaḥ //
english: Four aṅgulas make one padmahastaka.

sanskrit: pūrvamāsit mahadbhūtaṃ sarvabhūtabhayaṅkaraṃ /
english: In days of yore that material principle was dreadful among all principles.

sanskrit: taddevair nihitaṃ bhumau sa vāstupuruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: It being placed on the earth it was known to be the lord of that place.

sanskrit: catuḥṣaṣṭipade kṣetre īśaṃ koṇārdhasaṃsthitaṃ / ghṛtākṣataistarpayettaṃ parjanyaṃ padagataṃ tataḥ //
english: At a place divided into sixtyfour compartments Īśa occupying a half of the corner square is worshipped with ghee and unbroken rice. Then the god Parjanya the rain god occupying a square is worshipped.

sanskrit: utpalādibhirjayantañca dvipadasthaṃ patākayā / mahendrañcaikakoṣṭhasthaṃ sarvaraktaiḥ pade raviṃ //
english: The god Jayanta, who occupies two squares is worshipped with lotus flowers and water, and the lord Mahendra, who remains in one square is worshipped with a banner.

sanskrit: vitānenārdhapadagaṃ satyaṃ pade bhṛśaṃ ghṛtaiḥ /
english: The god of truth occupying half a square at the bottom is worshipped with canopy and profuse offering of ghee.

sanskrit: vyoma śākunamāṃsena koṇārdhapadasaṃsthitaṃ //
english: The lord of the sky occupying half the aṅgular square is propitiated with the bird’s flesh.

sanskrit: srucā cārdhapade vahniṃ pūṣāṇaṃ lājayaikataḥ / svarṇena vitathaṃ dviṣṭhaṃ mathanena gṛhākṣataṃ //
english: The firegod in half a square is worshipped with the sacrificial ladle and the god Pūṣan in a square with fried grains, the lord of untruth in two squares with gold, churning rod and unbroken rice in the house.

sanskrit: māṃsaudanena dharmeśamekaikasmin sthitaṃ dvayaṃ / gandharvaṃ dvipadaṃ gandhair bhṛśaṃ śākunajihvayā //
english: The lord Dharmeśa stationed in two squares is worshipped with meat and cooked food, the Gandharva in two squares with incense and the tongue of a bird.

sanskrit: ekasthamūrdhvasaṃsthañca mṛgaṃ nīlapaṭais tathā /
english: Mṛga occupying one upper square is then worshipped with blue cloth.

sanskrit: pitṝn kṛśarayārdhasthaṃ dantakāṣṭhaiḥ padasthitaṃ //
english: The manes are worshipped with a dish composed of milk, sesamum and rice in half a square and sticks of toothbrush in another square.

sanskrit: dauvārikaṃ dvisaṃsthañca sugrīvaṃ yāvakena tu / puṣpadantaṃ kuśastambaiḥ padmair varuṇamekataḥ //
english: The two doorkeepers Sugrīva and Puṣpadanta occupying two squares are worshipped with barley grains and a clump of grass respectively, and Varuṇa with lotus flowers in a square.

sanskrit: asuraṃ surayā dviṣṭhaṃ pade śeṣaṃ ghṛtāmbhasā / yavaiḥ pāpaṃ padārdhasthaṃ rogamardhe ca maṇḍakaiḥ //
english: The asura demon in two squares is propitiated with wine, the serpent Śeṣa in a square with ghee and water, the sin in half a square with barley grains, the disease in half a square with maṇḍaka a kind of baked flour.

sanskrit: nāgapuṣpaiḥ pade nāgaṃ mukhyaṃ bhakṣyair dvisaṃsthitaṃ / mudgaudanena bhallāṭaṃ pade somaṃ pade tathā //
english: The Nāga serpent is worshipped in a square with the nāga flowers and the chief serpent in two squares with edibles The Bhallāṭa a kind of superhuman being is worshipped in a single square with rice mixed with kidneybean, and the moon with the same offering in the next square.

sanskrit: madhunā pāyasenātha śālūkena ṛṣiṃ dvaye / pade ditiṃ lopikābhirardhe ditimathāparaṃ //
english: The sage placed in two squares is worshipped with honey, sweat gruel and nutmeg, Diti in a square with anointments and Aditi in one and a half squares.

sanskrit: pūrikābhistataścāpamīśādhaḥ payasā pade / tatodhaścāpavatsantu dadhnā caikapade sthitaṃ //
english: Āpas is propitiated in a square below in the northeast with milk and cake and then Apavatsa remaining in a square below with curd.

sanskrit: laḍḍukaiś ca marīcintu pūrvakoṣṭhacatuṣṭaye / savitre raktapuṣpāṇi brahmādhaḥkoṇakoṣṭhake //
english: Marīci is propitiated in four squares in the east with balls of sweetmeat and for the god Savitṛ, the red flowers are placed in the lower aṅgular square.

sanskrit: tadadhaḥkoṣṭhake dadyāt sāvitryai ca kuśodakaṃ / vivaste 'ruṇaṃ dadyāccandanañcaturaṅghriṣu //
english: In the square below that, water along with kuśa grass is offered to Savitṛ, red sandal paste is offered to Aruṇa in four squares.

sanskrit: rakṣodhaḥkoṇakoṣṭhe tu indrāyānnaṃ niśānvitaṃ / indrajayāya tasyādho ghṛtānnaṃ koṇakoṣṭhake //
english: Respectful offering along with turmeric is made to Indra in the lower square in the southwest and rice mixed with ghee is offered in the corner square below Indrajaya.

sanskrit: catuṣpadeṣu dātavyamindrāya guḍapāyasaṃ / vāyvadhaḥkoṇadeśe tu rudrāya pakvamāṃsakaṃ //
english: Sweet gruel mixed with jaggery is offered to Indra in four squares and cooked meat is offered to Rudra in the corner square in the northwest.

sanskrit: tadadhaḥkoṇakoṣṭhe tu yakṣāyārdraṃ phalantathā / mahīdharāya māṃsānnaṃ māghañca caturaṅghriṣu //
english: In the corner square below that wet fruit is offered to Yakṣa, rice meat and blackgram are offered to Mahidhara in four squares.

sanskrit: madhye catuṣpade sthāpyā brahmaṇe tilataṇḍulāḥ /
english: Rice and sesamum should be placed in the central square for Brahmā.

sanskrit: carakīṃ māṣasarpibhyāṃ skandaṃ kṛśarayāsṛjā // raktapadmair vidārīñca kandarpañca palodanaiḥ / pūtanāṃ palapittābhyāṃ māṃsāsṛgbhyāñca jambhakaṃ //
english: Carakī is worshipped with blackgram and clarified butter and Skanda with a dish composed of milk, sesamum and rice and a garland. Vidārī a demoness is worshipped with red lotuses, Kandarpa god of love with cooked rice and meat, Pūtanā a demoness with meat and bile and Jambaka a demon with meat and blood.

sanskrit: pittāsṛgasthibhiḥ pāpāṃ pilipiñjaṃ srajāsṛjā /
english: The Iśa is appeased with bile, blood and bones, Pilipiñja a demon with a garland and blood.

sanskrit: rakṣomātṛgaṇebhyaś ca piśācādibhya eva ca / pitṛbhyaḥ kṣetrapālebhyo balīn dadyāt prakāmataḥ //
english: Other deities are worshipped with blood and meat and in their absence with unbroken rice. Sacrificial offerings are made to demons, divine mothers, manes and guardian deities of the ground in due order.

sanskrit: āhutvaitānasantarpya prāsādādīnna kārayet /
english: One should not build temples and other things. without offering to these deities or appeasing them.

sanskrit: brahamasthāne hariṃ lakṣmīṃ gaṇaṃ paścāt samarcayet //
english: Hari, Lakṣmī, Gaṇa the attendant deity of Śiva should be worshipped at the place set apart for Brahmā.

sanskrit: mahīśvaraṃ vāstumayaṃ vardhanyā sahitaṃ ghaṭaṃ / brahmāṇaṃ madhyataḥ kumbhe brahmādīṃś ca digīśvarān //
english: The final offering is then made to Brahmā in the central pitcher and to Brahmā and other deities as well as Maheśvara, the presiding deity of the ground with a pitcher together with a small vessel.

sanskrit: dadyāt pūrṇāhutiṃ paścāt svasti vācya praṇamya ca / pragṛhya karkarīṃ samyak maṇḍalantu pradakṣiṇaṃ //
english: After having made benediction, and holding well the waterjar with small holes at the bottom an auspicious circumambulation is made.

sanskrit: sūtramārdeṇa he brahmaṃstoyadhārāñca bhrāmayet /
english: O Brahman! the drop of water is rotated to fall in a line.

sanskrit: pūrvavattena mārgeṇa sapta vījāni vāpayet //
english: As before in the same line seven kinds of seeds are sown.

sanskrit: prārambhaṃ tena mārgeṇa tasya khātasya kārayet /
english: The excavation should begin in the same way.

sanskrit: tato gartaṃ khanenmadhye hastamātraṃ pramāṇataḥ //
english: Then a hole of the measure of a hand should be dug at the centre.

sanskrit: caturaṅgulakaṃ cādhaścopalipyārcayettataḥ / dhyātvā caturbhujaṃ viṣṇumarghyaṃ dadyāttu kumbhataḥ //
english: Then having made the pit smooth to a depth of four fingers’ breadth and having contemplated on the fourarmed Viṣṇu waters of adoration should be offered from the pitcher.

sanskrit: karkaryā pūrayet śvabhraṃ śuklapuṣpāṇi ca nyaset /
english: Then the hole is filled with water from the waterjar having holes at the bottOṃ, white flowers are placed.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāvartakaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bījair mṛddbhiś ca pūrayet //
english: The excellent conchshell known as the Dakṣiṇāvarta curved to the right has to be filled with seeds and earth.

sanskrit: arghyādānaṃ viniṣpādya govastrādīndadedgurau / kālajñāya sthapataye vaiṣṇavādibhya arcayet //
english: After having performed the offering of water, one should present the preceptor of cows, clothes and other things and honour the sculptor, and the vaiṣṇavas who know the proper time.

sanskrit: tatastu khānayedyatnajjalāntaṃ yāvadeva tu /
english: One should then dig carefully till water is found.

sanskrit: puruṣādhaḥsthitaṃ śalyaṃ na gṛhe doṣadaṃ bhavet // asthiśalye vidyate vai bhittirvai gṛhiṇo 'sukhaṃ /
english: The substance lying below the presiding deity under the building would not have any beneful influence. The bone or substance below if broken, the broken thing forebodes baneful influence for the inmate.

sanskrit: yannāmaśabdaṃ śṛṇuyāttatra śalyaṃ tadudbhavaṃ //
english: Whatever kind of sound one would hear, it is to be known as due to the substance lying below.

sanskrit: pādapratiṣṭhāṃ vakṣāmi śilāvinyāsalakṣaṇaṃ /
english: shall narrate the mode of consecration of the foundation and the rites relating to the laying down of the foundation stone.

sanskrit: agrato maṇḍapaḥ kāryaḥ kuṇḍalānāntu catuṣṭayaṃ //
english: A shed is erected at first and four sacrificial pits are made.

sanskrit: kumbhanyāseṣṭakānyāso dvārastambhocchrayaṃ śubhaṃ /
english: The placing of pitchers of water and bricks, the erection of the doors and pillars are finished.

sanskrit: pādonaṃ pūrayet khātaṃ tatra vāstuṃ yajet same //
english: The dug up pit is filled to a quarter of its depth and the presiding deity is worshipped at the same time.

sanskrit: iṣṭakāś ca supakvāḥ syurdvādaśāṅgulasammitāḥ /
english: The bricks should be of twelve fingers in length, with a breadth and width of four fingers respectively, and wellburnt.

sanskrit: savistāratribhāgena vaipulyena samanvitāḥ //
karapramāṇā śreṣṭhā syācchilāpyatha śilāmaye / nava kumbhāṃstāmramayān sthāpayediṣṭakāghaṭān //
english: Stones measuring a cubit in length would be best in the case of stone slabs. Nine copper pitchers and bricks should be placed.

sanskrit: adbhiḥ pañcakaṣāyeṇa sarvauṣadhijalena ca /
english: The pitchers should be filled with water, substance known as pañcakaṣāya, waters of all herbs and fragrant waters.

sanskrit: hiraṇyavrīhisaṃyuktair gandhacandanacarcitaiḥ / āpo hi ṣṭheti tisṛbhiḥ śanno devīti cāpyatha // tarat samandīriti ca pāvamānībhireva ca / uduttamaṃ varuṇamiti kathānaś ca tathaiva ca // varuṇasyeti mantreṇa haṃsaḥ śuciṣadityapi /
english: Then with the pitchers filled well with waters and containing gold and rice and anointed by fragrant sandal, and having placed the stones along with the recitation of the mystic syllablesthe threefooted āpo hi ṣṭhā, śanno devī, tarat sa mandīḥ, pāvamānī, uduttamaṃ varuṇa, kayā naḥ, varuṇasya, haṃsaḥ śuciṣat, śrīsūkta.

sanskrit: śayyāyāṃ maṇḍape prācyāṃ maṇḍale harimarcayet /
english: Hari should be worshipped in a bed in the shed in the eastern part of the drawn diagram.

sanskrit: juhuyājjanayitvāgniṃ samidho dvādaśīstataḥ //
english: Then having kindled the fire twelve twigs should be offered as oblation.

sanskrit: āghārāvājyabhāgau tu praṇavenaiva kārayet /
english: The primary offering and the offering with clarified butter should be done with the syllable oṃ.

sanskrit: aṣṭāhutīs tathāṣṭāntair ājyaṃ vyāhṛtibhiḥ kramāt //
english: Then subsequently eight offerings and again eight offerings with clarified butter should be offered with the syllables known as vyāhṛtis duly.

sanskrit: lokeśānāmagnaye vai somāyāvagraheṣu ca /
english: After that offer oblation in the fire to the gods, Agni, Soma and Puruṣottama separately with vyāhṛtis.

sanskrit: prāyaścittaṃ tataḥ pūrṇāṃ mūrtimāṃsaghṛtāṃstilān / vedādyair dvādaśāntena kumbheṣu ca pṛthak pṛthak // prāṅmukhastu guruḥ kuryādaṣṭadikṣu vilipya ca / madhye caikāṃ śilāṃ kumbhaṃ nyasedetān surān kramāt //
english: The preceptor officiating at the rite should do the expiatory rite facing the eastern quarter offering to the image, meat, and sesamum along with ghee separately in the pitchers with the vedic syllables or the mystic formula of twelve syllables. Having scattered sesamum in the eight directions a stone and a pitcher should be placed at the centre and the following divinities should be invoked in order.

sanskrit: padmaṃ caiva mahāpadmaṃ makaraṃ kacchapaṃ tathā / kumudañca tathā nandaṃ padmaṃ śaṅkhañca padminīṃ //
english: Padma, mahāpadma, makara, kacchapa, kumuda, nanda, padma, śaṅkha and padminī are the divinities.

sanskrit: kumbhānna cālayetteṣu iṣṭakānāntu devatāḥ /
english: The pitchers should not be moved.

sanskrit: īśānāntāś ca pūrvādāviṣṭakāṃ prathamaṃ nyaset //
english: Eight bricks should be placed in them duly beginning with the eastern direction and ending with the northeast.

sanskrit: śaktayo vimalādyāstu iṣṭakānāntu devatāḥ / nyasanīyā yathā yogaṃ madhye nyasyā tvanugrahā // avyaṅge cākṣata pūrṇaṃ muneraṅgirasaḥ sute /
english: The female energies Vimalā and others, the presiding deities of these bricks, should be invoked in their proper pitchers. The energy Anugraha should be invoked at the central pitcher. “O perfect, unbroken, fullbodied brick, the daughter of the sage Aṅgiras, am establishing you.

sanskrit: iṣṭake tvaṃ prayaccheṣṭaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ kārayāmyahaṃ //
english: You grant me the desired thing.”

sanskrit: garbhādhānaṃ tataḥ kuryānmadhyasthāne samāhitaḥ //
english: The preceptor, having placed the brick with this mystic syllable should do garbhādhāna.

sanskrit: kumbhopariṣṭhādeveśaṃ padminīṃ nyasya devatāṃ / mṛttikāś caiva puṣpāṇi dhātavo ratnameva ca // lauhāni dikpaterastraṃ yajedvai garbhabhājane / dvādaśāṅgulavistāre caturaṅgulakocchraye //
english: Having invoked the goddess Padminī at the central pitcher, earth, flowers, minerals, gems, and iron pieces as well as the weapons of deities of quarters should be placed in the hole of twelve fingers’ width and four fingers’ depth.

sanskrit: padmākāre tāmramaye bhājane pṛthivīṃ yajet /
english: The goddess earth should be worshipped in a copper vessel of the shape of a lotus.

sanskrit: ekānte sarvabhūteśe parvatāsanamaṇḍite // samudraparivāre tvaṃ devi garbhaṃ samāśraya /
english: “O the exclusive mistress of all beings, abound with the summits of mountains as the seats, one surrounded by oceans, O goddess! You resort to this hole.

sanskrit: nande nandaya vāsiṣṭhe vasubhiḥ prajayā saha //
english: O rejoicer! born of sage Vasiṣṭha! you rejoice with the Vasus and the progeny.

sanskrit: jaye bhārgavadāyāde prajānāṃ vijayāvahe / pūrṇeṅgirasadāyāde pūrṇakāmaṃ kuruṣva māṃ //
english: O Victorious! related to Bhārgava Paraśurāma Maker of thine subjects victorious! the perfect! the relative of Aṅgiras! fulfil all my desires.

sanskrit: bhadre kāśyapadāyāde kuru bhadrāṃ matiṃ mama /
english: O Auspicious one! Heir of sage Kāśyapa! Make my mind good.

sanskrit: sarvavījasamāyukte sarvaratnauṣadhīvṛte //
english: One who is accomplished with all seeds! One who possesses all gems and herbs!

sanskrit: jaye surucire nande vāsiṣṭhe ramyatāmiha / prajāpatisute devi caturasre mahīyasi //
english: May you be victorious! O beautiful one! O rejoicer! Related to Vasiṣṭha! The daughter of the creator! O Goddess! O handsome one! Stay on here in blissO majestic one!

sanskrit: subhage suprabhe bhadre gṛhe kāśyapi ramyatāṃ / pūjite paramāś carye gandhamālyair alaṅkṛte //
english: Stay thou in this house! O beautiful and brilliant one! the daughter of Kaśyapa! The honoured, most wonderful and bedecked with scents and garlands!

sanskrit: bhavabhūtikarī devi gṛhe bhārgavi ramyatāṃ / deśasvāmipurasvāmigṛhasvāmiparigrahe //
english: O Goddess! Stay in bliss in this room! O Bhārgavi daughter of Śukra! Bestower of worldly prosperities! Possessed by the gods, kings, and masters of the house!

sanskrit: manuṣyādikatuṣṭyarthaṃ paśuvṛddhikarī bhava /
english: May you become the multiplier of animals for the happiness of men and others.

sanskrit: evamuktvā tataḥ khātaṃ gomūtreṇa tu secayet // kṛtvā nidhāpayedgarbhaṃ garbhādhānaṃ bhavenniśi /
english: Having said in this way one should then sprinkle cow’s urine on the pit. Having done so, one should place in the pit such that the impregnation would take place in the night.

sanskrit: govastrādi pradadyācca guravenyeṣu bhojanaṃ //
english: One should give away cows and clothes to the preceptor the officiating priest, and food to other people.

sanskrit: garbhaṃ nyasyeṣṭakā nyasya tato garbhaṃ prapūrayet / pīṭhabandhamataḥ kuryānmitaprāsādamānataḥ //
english: Having filled the hole and placing the bricks in the hole, the hole is completely filled. Then one should construct the base of the deity proportionate to the edifice of the deity.

sanskrit: pīṭhottamañcocchrayeṇa prāsādasyārdhavistarāt / padahīnaṃ madhyamaṃ syāt kaniṣṭhaṃ cottamārdhataḥ //
english: An excellent base is that where it is more than half the breadth of the edifice, while a quarter lesser than that would be mediocre and that which is half of the excellent base aforesaid would be the lowest in merit.

sanskrit: pīṭhabandhopariṣṭhāttu vāstuyāgaṃ punaryajet /
english: After completing the base, the rite for the presiding deity of the ground should be done again.

sanskrit: pādapratiṣṭhākārī tu niṣpāpo divi modate //
english: One who performs the consecration of the base would enjoy in heavens free from sin.

sanskrit: devāgāraṃ karomīti manasā yastu cintayet / tasya kāyagataṃ pāpaṃ tadahnā hi praṇaśyati //
english: One who would mentally think that “ am going to build a temple”, the sins which had stuck to his body would get destroyed that day itself.

sanskrit: aṣṭeṣṭakasamāyuktaṃ yaḥ kuryāddevatālayaṃ // na tasya phalasampattirvaktuṃ śakyeta kenacit /
english: No need to speak about the merits of one who has built a temple in the prescribed manner. It is impossible for anyone to describe the merits one would accrue by building a temple with eight bricks alone.

sanskrit: anenaivānumeyaṃ hi phalaṃ prāsādavistarāt //
english: One should indeed infer from this the proportionate fruits accrued from the building of temples of greater dimensions.

sanskrit: grāmamadhye ca pūrve ca pratyagdvāraṃ prakalpayet / vidiśāsu ca sarvāsu grāme pratyaṅmukho bhavet / dakṣiṇe cottare caiva paścime prāṅmukho bhavet //
english: The door of the temple at the centre of the village or on the eastern part should face the west, while in other directions the door should be facing the west and in the southern, northern and western parts the door should face the east.

sanskrit: prāsādaṃ sampravakṣyāmi sarvasādhāraṇaṃ śṛṇu /
english: Listen to me describing the construction of a temple in general.

sanskrit: caturasrīkṛtaṃ kṣetraṃ bhajet ṣoḍaśadhā budhaḥ //
english: A wise man should divide a square ground into sixteen parts.

sanskrit: madhye tasya caturbhistu kuryādāyasamanvitaṃ /
english: One should make the four central squares endowed with.

sanskrit: dvadaśaiva tu bhāgāni bhittyarthaṃ parikalpayet //
english: wealth. The other sixteen parts are left for the walls.

sanskrit: jaṅghocchrāyantu kartavyaṃ caturbhāgeṇa cāyataṃ /
english: The pedestal should extend over four squares.

sanskrit: jaṅghāyāṃ dviguṇocchrāyaṃ mañjaryāḥ kalpayed budhaḥ //
english: The length of the cornice should be double that of the pedestal.

sanskrit: turyabhāgena mañjaryāḥ kāryaḥ samyak pradakṣiṇaḥ /
english: The path of circumambulation should be a quarter of the length of the cornice.

sanskrit: tanmānanirgamaṃ kāryamubhayoḥ pārśvayoḥ samaṃ //
english: Two equal openings having the same width as the latter, should be left on the two sides for projections

sanskrit: dviguṇenāpi kartavyaṃ yathāśobhānurūpataḥ // vistārānmaṇḍapasyāgre garbhasūtradvayena tu /
english: The extent of the ground should be made at first equal to the length of the tower or twice that such as it may be beautiful.

sanskrit: dairghyātpādādhikaṃ kuryānmadhyastambhair vibhūṣitaṃ // prāsādagarbhamānaṃ vā kurvīta mukhamaṇḍapaṃ / ekāśītipadair vyāstuṃ paścāt maṇḍapamārabhet //
english: One should construct the pavilion in front of the sanctum on the lines running parallel through the sides of its inner chamber, adorned with pillars and being of the same length or longer than the principal temple sanctorum by a quarter of its length. The antichamber should then be constructed at steps.

sanskrit: śukān prāgdvāravinyāse pādāntaḥsthān yajet surān /
english: The deities at the end of the base should be worshipped before placing the parrots at the front door.

sanskrit: tathā prākāravinyāse yajed dvātriṃśadantagān //
english: In the same manner the thirtytwo gods at the end should be worshipped when the outer wall is raised.

sanskrit: sarvasādhāraṇaṃ caitat prāsādasya ca lakṣaṇaṃ /
english: This is the characteristic of a temple in general.

sanskrit: mānena pratimāyā vā prāsādamaparaṃ śṛṇu //
english: Listen to the description of raising a temple proportionate to the size of the image.

sanskrit: pratimāyāḥ pramāṇana kartavyā piṇḍikā śubhā /
english: The base of the deity should be of the same size as the image.

sanskrit: garbhastu piṇḍikārdhena garbhamānāstu bhittayaḥ // bhitterāyāmamānena utsedhantu prakalpayet /
english: The adytum of the temple should be half the size of the base and the walls proportionate to the adytum. The height of the walls should be equal to the length of the walls.

sanskrit: bhittyucchrāyāttu dviguṇaṃ śikharaṃ kalpayed budhaḥ //
english: The pinnacle should be made equal to twice the height of the wall.

sanskrit: śikharasya tu turyeṇa bhramaṇaṃ parikalpayet / śikharasya caturthena vyagrato mukhamaṇḍapaṃ //
english: The path around the temple should be a quarter of the extent of the pinnacle. The entrance chamber in the front should be a quarter of the extent of the pinnacle.

sanskrit: aṣṭamāṃsena garbhasya rathakānāntu nirgamaḥ /
english: The projections of the arches should be oneeighth of the extent of the adytum.

sanskrit: paridherguṇabhāgena rathakāṃstatra kalpayet //
english: The arches should be made proportionate to the circumference.

sanskrit: tattṛtīyeṇa vā kuryādrathakānāntu nirgamaṃ /
english: The projections of arches should otherwise be made as onethird of it.

sanskrit: vāmatrayaṃ sthāpanīyaṃ rathakatritaye sadā //
english: Always there should be three projections on the left on the three arches.

sanskrit: śikharārthaṃ hi sūtrāṇi catvāri vinipātayet /
english: Four upward lines should be marked for the construction of the pinnacle.

sanskrit: śikharasyārdhabhāgasthaṃ siṃhaṃ tatra tu kārayet / śukanāsāṃ sthirīkṛtya madhyasandhau nidhāpayet //
english: A downward line is marked to fall above the keystone which is located at the middle part of the pinnacle. A lion is built at the middle part of the pinnacle in a line with the keystone.

sanskrit: apare ca tathā pārśvaṃ tadvat sūtraṃ nidhāpayet /
english: Two such lines should be marked on the sides.

sanskrit: tadūrdhvantu bhavedvedī sakaṇṭā manasārakaṃ //
english: There should be a small platform above that.

sanskrit: skandhabhagnaṃ na kartavyaṃ vikarālaṃ tathaiva ca / ūrdhvaṃ ca vedikāmānāt kalaśaṃ parikalpayet //
english: The lion should not be in a dropping posture or fiercelooking. The conical shaped structure is placed above, proportional to the small platform.

sanskrit: vistārāddviguṇaṃ dvāraṃ kartavyaṃ tu suśobhanaṃ /
english: A beautiful opening should be made twice the length of the platform.

sanskrit: udumbarau tadūrdhvañca nyasecchākhāṃ sumaṅgalaiḥ //
english: Two globes should be placed above that with beautiful ornamental branches.

sanskrit: dvārasya tu caturthāṃśe kāryau caṇḍapracaṇdakau / viśvaksenavatsadaṇḍau śikhordhvoḍumbare śriyaṃ // diggajaiḥ snāpyamānāntāṃ ghaṭeḥ sābjāṃ surūpikāṃ /
english: Forms of Caṇḍa and Pracaṇḍa should be carved on the doorframe occupying a fourth of its space, possessing a staff like that of Viṣvaksena Viṣṇu and at the threshhold of the branch beautiful Goddess Śrī Lakṣmī should be carved as being bathed by the elephants of the quarters with waters from the pitchers.

sanskrit: prāsādasya caturthāṃśaiḥ prākārasyocchrayo bhavet // prāsādāt pādahīnastu gopurasyocchrayo bhavet /
english: The height of enclosing wall should be onefourth of that of the temple. The height of the tower should be a quarter lesser than that of the temple.

sanskrit: pañcahastasya devasya ekahastā tu pīṭhikā //
english: The pedestal of the image of the deity of five cubits should be of a cubit.

sanskrit: gāruḍaṃ maṇḍapañcāgre ekaṃ bhaumādidhāma ca /
english: A shed known as the Garuḍamaṇḍapa and shed for Bhauma Mars and other planets should be made.

sanskrit: kuryāddhi pratimāyāntu dikṣu cāṣṭamāsu copari //
english: In the eight directions above the chamber housing one should make the images as follows

sanskrit: pūrve varāhaṃ dakṣe ca nṛsiṃhaṃ śrīdharaṃ jale / uttare tu hayagrīvanāgneyyāṃ jāmadagnyakaṃ // nairṛtyāṃ rāmakaṃ vāyau vāmanaṃ vāsudevakaṃ / īśe prāsādaracanā deyā vasvarkakādibhiḥ /
english: The images of Varāha boar in the east, Nṛsiṃha manlion in the south, Śrīdhara a form of Viṣṇu in the west, Hayagrīva horsenecked form of Viṣṇu in the north, Jāmadagnyaka Paraśurāma, a manifestation of Viṣṇu in the southeast, Rāma in the southwest, Vāmana the shortstatured manifestation ofViṣṇu in the northwest and Vāsudeva in the northeast.

sanskrit: dvārasya cāṣṭamādyaṃśaṃ tyatkā bedho na doṣabhāk //
english: The temple should be decorated with gems all around. Leaving out oneeighth of the door if that is done, it is not defective.

sanskrit: prāsāde devatāḥ sthāpyā vakṣye brahman śṛṇuṣva me /
english: O Brahman! Listen to my description of the mode of installation of images of deities in the temples.

sanskrit: pañcāyatamadhye tu vāsudevaṃ niveśayet //
english: Image of Vāsudeva should be placed at the middle of the five divine edifices.

sanskrit: vāmanaṃ nṛhariñcāśvaśīrṣaṃ tadvañca śūkaraṃ / āgneye nairṛte caiva vāyavye ceśagocare //
english: The images of the dwarfform, manlion form, horseheaded form, and boar form of Viṣṇu should be placed in the southeast, southwest, northwest and northeast respectively.

sanskrit: atha nārāyaṇaṃ madhye āgneyyāmambikāṃ nyaset /
english: The image of Nārāyaṇa should be placed in the middle.

sanskrit: nairṛtyāṃ bhāskaraṃ vāyau brahmāṇaṃ liṅgamīśake // athavā rudrarūpantu athavā navadhāmasu /
english: The images of the goddess, sun, Brahmā and the liṅga symbolic representation of Śiva or of Rudra Śiva should be placed in the southeast, southwest, northwest and northeast respectively.

sanskrit: vāsudevaṃ nyasenmadhye pūrvādau vāmavāmakān // indrādīn lokapālāṃś ca athavā navadhāmasu /
english: Otherwise, image of Vāsudeva should be placed at the centre of the nine chambers and beautiful images of Indra and the guardian deities of the world should be placed in the east and other directions.

sanskrit: pañcāyatanakaṃ kuryāt madhye tu puruṣottamaṃ //
english: Otherwise, one should make five chambers and worship Puruṣottama Viṣṇu in the centre..

sanskrit: lakṣmīvaiśravaṇau pūrvaṃ dakṣe mātṛgaṇaṃ nyaset / skandaṃ gaṇeśamīśānaṃ sūryādīn paścime grahān //
