english: The images of Lakṣmī and Vaiśravaṇī Kubera should be placed in the east, the divine mothers in the south, Skanda, Gaṇeśa, Īśāna a form of Śiva and the sun and other planets in the west.

sanskrit: uttare daśa matsyādīnāgneyyāṃ caṇḍikāṃ tathā / nairṛtyāmambikāṃ sthāpya vāyavye tu sarasvatīṃ // padmāmaiśe vāsudevaṃ madhye nārāyaṇañca vā /
english: Otherwise, having installed the images of the manifestations of Viṣṇu such as the Fish etc., in the north, Caṇḍikā a form of Goddess Pārvatī in the southeast, Ambikā in the southwest, Sarasvatī in the northwest, Padmā Lakṣmī in the northeast and Vāsudeva or also Nārāyaṇa in the centre.

sanskrit: trayodaśālaye madhye viśvarūpaṃ nyaseddhariṃ //
english: The omnipresent form of Hari should be placed in the centre in the construction of the thirteen chambers.

sanskrit: pūrvādau keśavādīn vā anyadhāmasvayaṃ hariṃ /
english: Images of Keśava and others should be placed in the east and other directions or the images of Hari himself in all chambers.

sanskrit: mṛṇmayī dārughaṭitā lohajā ratnajā tathā // śailajā gandhajā caiva kausumī saptadhā smṛtā /
english: The images are of seven kindsearthen, wooden, metallic, made of gems, made of stones, made of sandal and made of flowers.

sanskrit: tatkālapūjitāś caitāḥ sarvakāmaphalapradāḥ /
english: The images made of flowers, sandal and earth yield all desired fruits when they are worshipped at that moment.

sanskrit: atha śailamayīṃ vakṣye śilā yatra ca gṛhyate // parvatānāmabhāve ca gṛhṇīyādbhūgatāṃ śilāṃ /
english: shall describe the stone image where such practice prevails. In the absence of hills, the stone lying buried in the earth should be taken out.

sanskrit: pāṇḍarā hy aruṇā pītā kṛṣṇā śastā tu vairṇināṃ //
english: Among the colours, white, red, yellow, and black are extolled.

sanskrit: na yadā labhyate samyag varṇināṃ varṇataḥ śilā / varṇādyāpādānaṃ tatra juhyāt siṃhavidyayā //
english: When stones of the abovementioned colours are not available the desired colour is brought about by the ceremony known as siṃhavidyā.

sanskrit: śilāyāṃ śuklarekhāgryā kṛṣṇāgryā siṃhahomataḥ / kāṃsyaghaṇṭāninādā syāt puṃliṅgā visphuliṅgikā //
english: After the performance of the siṃhahoma a piece of stone which becomes tinged with white colour or black colour or produces sound like a bellmetal or emits sparks of fire is deemed as male.

sanskrit: tanmandalakṣaṇā strī syādrūpābhāvānnapuṃsakā /
english: The female one is that in which these characteristics are present in a lesser degree. If they are devoid of colours they are neuter.

sanskrit: dṛśyate maṇḍalaṃ yasyāṃ sagarbhāṃ tāṃ vivarjayet //
english: The stones in which the sign of a circle is found are to be taken as impregnated and should be rejected.

sanskrit: pratimārthaṃ vanaṃ gatvā vrajayāgaṃ samācaret /
english: One should go to the forest and perform the forest rites for the sake of an image.

sanskrit: tatra khātvopalipyātha maṇḍape tu hariṃ yajet //
english: After having bathed and plastering a shed Hari should be worshipped there.

sanskrit: baliṃ datvā karmaśastraṃ ṭaṅkādikamathārcayet /
english: After having made the offering of the victim, the stonecutter’s chisel used for the work should be worshipped.

sanskrit: hutvātha śālitoyena astreṇa prokṣayecchilāṃ // rakṣāṃ kṛtvā nṛsiṃhena mūlamantreṇa pūjayet /
english: Having made the protective spell it should be worshipped with basic sacred syllable of lord Nṛsiṃha. After having made the offering to fire the final oblation should be made.

sanskrit: hutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ dadyāttato bhūtabaliṃ guruḥ // atra ye saṃsthitāḥ sattvā yātudhānāś ca guhyakāḥ / siddhādayo vā ye cānye tān sampūjya kṣamāpayet //
english: Then offerings to the goblins should be given by the preceptor. Having worshipped the good spirits, the demons, guhyakas a class of attendantgods of Kubera, and accomplished souls and others who may be residing there, should be requested to forgive. They should be addressed as follows.

sanskrit: viṣṇubimbārthamasmākaṃ yātraiṣā keśavājñayā /
english: “This journey has been undertaken by us for the image of Viṣṇu by the command of Keśava.

sanskrit: viṣṇvarthaṃ yadbhavet kāryaṃ yuṣmākamapi tadbhavet //
english: Any work done for the sake of Viṣṇu, should also be your concern.”

sanskrit: anena balidānena prītā bhavata sarvathā / kṣameṇa gacchatānyatra muktvā sthānamidaṃ tvarāt //
english: “Being always pleased with this offering you repair quickly to some other place quitting this place for good”.

sanskrit: evaṃ prabodhitāḥ sattvā yānti tṛptā yathāsukhaṃ /
english: Being informed thus these beings go to another place in good cheer and satisfied.

sanskrit: śilpibhiś ca caruṃ prāśya svapnamantraṃ japenniśi //
english: Having eaten the sacrificial porridge along with the sculptors, he should repeat in the night the following sacred syllables inducing sleep.

sanskrit: oṃ namaḥ sakalalokāya viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave / viśvāya viśvarūpāya svapnādhipataye namaḥ //
english: “Oṃ! salutations to Lord Viṣṇu, the omnipresent, Prabhaviṣṇu Viṣṇu strong, the universe, and Salutations to the lord of dreams.”

sanskrit: ācakṣva devadeveśa prasuptosmi tavāntikaṃ /
english: “O Lord of lords! have slept by your side.

sanskrit: svapne sarvāṇi kāryāṇi hṛdisthāni tu yāni me //
english: Instruct me in my dreams how to execute all the works have in my mind.”

sanskrit: śubhe svapne śubhaṃ sarvaṃ hy aśubhe siṃhahomataḥ /
english: “Oṃ Oṃ! hrūṃ phaṭ viṣṇave svāhā! When the dream is good, everything will also be good. If it is bad, it becomes good by the performance of the siṃhahoma.

sanskrit: prātararghyaṃ śilāyāṃ tu datvāstreṇāstrakaṃ yajet //
english: Having offered reverential waters to the stone in the morning, the implements should be worshipped with the sacred syllables for the worship of implements.

sanskrit: kuddālaṭaṅkaśastrādyaṃ madhvānyāktamukhañcaret /
english: The spades and chisels should have their edges besmeared with honey and clarified butter.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ cintayedviṣṇuṃ śilpinaṃ viśvakarmakaṃ //
english: The priest should think himself as Viṣṇu and the sculptor as Viśvakarman the divine architect.

sanskrit: śastraṃ viṣṇvātmakaṃ dadyāt mukhapṛṣṭhādi darśayet /
english: The implement which is of the form of Viṣṇu should be given to the sculptor and its face and back should be shown.

sanskrit: jitendriyaḥ ṭaṅkahastaḥ śilpī tu caturasrakāṃ // śilāṃ kṛtvā piṇḍikārthaṃ kiñcinnyūnāntu kalpayet /
english: Having cut a square block of the stone with controlled senses and holding a chisel, the sculptor should make a smaller one for the purpose of the pedestal.

sanskrit: rathe sthāpya samānīya savastrāṃ kāruveśmani / pūjayitvātha ghaṭayet pratimāṃ sa tu karmakṛt //
english: Having placed them in a chariot and brought to the workspot together with the cloth one who makes the image after having worshipped the form conceived, is a sculptor.

sanskrit: vāsudevādipratimālakṣaṇaṃ pravadāmi te /
english: shall describe to you the characteristics of the image of Vāsudeva and other gods.

sanskrit: prāsādasyottare pūrvamukhīṃ vā cottarānanāṃ // saṃsthāpya pūjya ca baliṃ datvātho madhyasūcakaṃ / śilāṃ śilpī tu navadhā vibhajya navame 'ṃśake //
english: Having placed the stone to the north of the temple facing either the east or the north and worshipped it, the sculptor should divide the stone into nine parts along the central line after making the offering.

sanskrit: sūrpabhaktaiḥ śilāyāṃ tu bhāgaṃ svāṅgulamucyate / dvyaṅgulaṃ golakaṃ nāmnā kālanetraṃ taducyate //
english: In the twelve divisions of the line a division is said to be an aṅgula a finger breadth. Two aṅgulas are known to be a golaka. It is also said to be a kālanetra.

sanskrit: bhāgamekaṃ tridhā bhaktvā pārṣṇibhāgaṃ prakalpayet /
english: Having divided one of the nine divisions into three, with one part the region of the calves should be made.

sanskrit: bhāgamekaṃ tathā jānau grīvāyāṃ bhāgameva ca //
english: In the same way a part is to be used for the knees and part for the neck.

sanskrit: mukuṭaṃ tālamātraṃ syāttālamātraṃ tayā mukhaṃ / tālenaikena kaṇṭhantu tālena hṛdayaṃ tathā //
english: The crown should be of a measure of a tāla aṅgulas. In the same way the face should be of the measure of a tāla. The neck and heart should also be a tāla each.

sanskrit: nābhimeḍhrāntarantālaṃ dvitālāvūrukau tathā /
english: The length of the thighs should be two tālas. The length of the part from the ankle to the knee should be two tālas.

sanskrit: tāladvayena jaṅghā syāt sūtrāṇi śṛṇu sāmprataṃ //
english: Listen now to the description of the drawing of lines on the body.

sanskrit: kāryaṃ sūtradvayaṃ pāde jaṅghāmadhye tathāparaṃ / jānau sūtradvayaṃ kāryamūrūmadhye tathāparaṃ // meḍhre tathāparaṃ kāryaṃ kaṭyāṃ sūtrantathāparaṃ /
english: Two lines should be drawn on the foot, and two more in between the calves and knees. Two lines about the kneesand two more in between the thighs and the knees should be drawn. One line should be drawn over the genital part, and one more about the waist.

sanskrit: hṛdaye ca tathā kāryaṃ kaṇṭhe sūtradvayaṃ tathā / lalāte cāparaṃ kāryaṃ mastake ca tathāparaṃ //
english: Then a line should be drawn on the heart and two lines on the neck. One such line should be drawn on the forehead and one more on the head. One more line should be drawn on the crown by the learned.

sanskrit: sūtrāṇyūrdhvaṃ pradeyāni saptaiva kamalodbhava //
english: O Brahman! seven vertical lines should be drawn.

sanskrit: kakṣātrikāntareṇaiva ghaṭ sūtrāṇi pradāpayet /
english: Six lines should be laid in between the armpits and the lower part of the spine.

sanskrit: madhyasūtraṃ tu santyajya sūtrāṇyeva nivedayet //
english: These lines alone should be marked clearly omitting the central line.

sanskrit: lalāṭaṃ nāsikāvaktraṃ kartavyañcaturaṅgulaṃ / grīvākarṇau tu kartavyau āyāmāccaturaṅgulau //
english: The forehead, the nose and the mouth should be made to measure four aṅgulas. The neck and the two ears should be made to measure four aṅgulas long.

sanskrit: dvyaṅgule hanuke kārye vistārāccibukantathā /
english: The cheeks so also the chin should be made to measure two aṅgulas broad.

sanskrit: aṣṭāṅgulaṃ lalāṭantu vistāreṇa prakīrtitam //
english: The forehead is said to be eight aṅgulas broad.

sanskrit: pareṇa dvyaṅgulau śaṅkhau kartavyāvalakānvitau /
english: Over that the temples sides of the forehead should be made two aṅgulas endowed with curbs.

sanskrit: caturaṅgulamākhyātamantaraṃ karṇanetrayoḥ //
english: The intervening space between the eyes and ears is said to be four aṅgulas.

sanskrit: dvyaṅgulau pṛthukau karṇau karṇāpāṅgārdhapañcame /
english: The ears should be two aṅgulas wide. The interspace between the ears and the ends of eyelashes should be two and a half units.

sanskrit: bhrūsamena tu sūtreṇa karṇaśrotraṃ prakīrtitam //
english: The cavity in the ear is spoken to be in the same line as the eyebrows.

sanskrit: viddhaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulaṃ karṇamaviddhañcaturaṅgulam /
english: A pierced ear should be six aṅgulas and an unpierced ear should be four aṅgulas equal to the chin.

sanskrit: civukena samaṃ viddhamaviddhaṃ vā ṣaḍaṅgulam //
english: Or it should be six aṅgulas whether it is pierced or not pierced.

sanskrit: gandhapātraṃ tathāvartaṃ śaṣkulīṃ kalpayettathā /
english: Then the external auditory passage with its membranes etc. should be made.

sanskrit: dvyaṅgulenādharaḥ kāryastasyārdhenottarādharaḥ //
english: The lower lip should be of two aṅgulas and the upper lip should be half of it.

sanskrit: ardhāṅgulaṃ tathā netraṃ vaktrantu caturaṅgulam /
english: Then the breadth of an eye should be half an aṅgula and the mouth should be four aṅgulas.

sanskrit: āyāmena tu vaipulyāt sārdhamaṅgulamucyate //
english: The measurement of its depth is spoken to be one and a half aṅgulas.

sanskrit: avyāttamevaṃ syādvaktraṃ vyāttaṃ tryaṅgulamiṣyate /
english: The unopened mouth should be in this way. The opened mouth should be three aṅgulas.

sanskrit: nāsāvaṃśasamucchrāyaṃ mūle tvekāṅgulaṃ matam //
english: The base of the bridge of the nose should be one aṅgula high.

sanskrit: ucchrāyā dvyaṅgulaṃ cāgre karavīropamāḥ smṛtāḥ /
english: From its tip it should be two aṅgulas similar to the karavīra flower oleander.

sanskrit: antaraṃ cakṣuṣoḥ kāryaṃ caturaṅgulamānataḥ //
english: The intervening space between the two eyes should be made to measure four aṅgulas.

sanskrit: dvyaṅgulaṃ cākṣikoṇaṃ ca dvyaṅgulaṃ cāntaraṃ tayoḥ /
english: The corners of the eyes should be two aṅgulas. The space between them should be two aṅgulas.

sanskrit: tārā netratribhāgeṇa dṛktārā pañcamāṃśikā //
english: The pupil should be one third of the eye and the iris should be one fifth of it.

sanskrit: tryaṅgulaṃ netravistāraṃ droṇī cārdhāṅgulā matā /
english: The breadth of the eye should be three aṅgulas. The cavity of the eye is considered to be half an aṅgula.

sanskrit: tatsamāṇā bhruvorlekhā bhruvau caiva same mate //
english: The lengths of the eyebrows are considered to be equal and are proportional to the eyebrows.

sanskrit: bhrūmadhyaṃ dvyaṅgulaṃ kāryaṃ bhrūdairghyaṃ caturāṅgulam /
english: The middle of the eyebrow should be two aṅgulas and its length should be four aṅgulas.

sanskrit: ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulāyāmammastakasya tu veṣṭanam //
english: The measure round the head should be thirtysix aṅgulas.

sanskrit: mūrtīnāṃ keśavādīnāṃ dvātriṃśadveṣṭanaṃ bhavet /
english: The measurement around the heads of the images of Keśava and other gods should be thirtysix aṅgulas.

sanskrit: triguṇantu bhavedūrdhvaṃ vistṛtāṣṭāṅgulaṃ punaḥ / grīvātriguṇamāyāmaṃ grīvāvakṣontaraṃ bhavet // skandhāvaṣṭāṅgulau kāryau trikalāvaṃśakau śubhau /
english: The interspace between the neck and the chest should be three times the length of the neck and should be thrice as much broad plus eight aṅgulas. The shoulders should be made to measure eight aṅgulas and the two beautiful shoulder regions should be three times those.

sanskrit: saptanetrau smṛtau bāhū prabāhū ṣoḍaśāṅgulau //
english: The arms should measure seven times the length of the eyes. The fore arms should be sixteen aṅgulas.

sanskrit: trikalau vistṛtau bāhū prabāhū cāpi tatsamau /
english: The arms should be three kalās in breadth and the forearms should also be equal to that.

sanskrit: bāhudaṇḍordhvato jñeyaḥ pariṇāhaḥ kalā nava //
english: The upper arm should have a circumference of nine kalās.

sanskrit: saptadaśāṅgulo madhye kūrpārordhe ca ṣoḍaśa /
english: It should be seventeen aṅgulas at the middle and sixteen aṅgulas above the elbowjoint.

sanskrit: kūrpārasya bhavennāhaḥ triguṇaḥ kamalodbhava //
english: O Brahman! the circumference of elbow should be three times that.

sanskrit: nāhaḥ prabāhumadhye tu ṣoḍaśāṅgula ucyate /
english: The circumference of the middle of the forearm is said to be sixteen aṅgulas.

sanskrit: agrahaste parīṇāho dvādaśāṅgula ucyate //
english: The circumference of the forepart of the arm is said to be twelve aṅgulas.

sanskrit: vistareṇa karatalaṃ kīrtitaṃ tu ṣaḍaṅgulam /
english: The palm of the hand is said to be six aṅgulas in breadth.

sanskrit: dairghyaṃ saptāṅgulaṃ kāryaṃ madhyā pajcāṅgulā matā //
english: The length should be seven aṅgulas. The middle finger should be five aṅgulas long.

sanskrit: tarjanyanāmikā caiva tasmādardhāṅgulaṃ vinā /
english: The index finger and the ring finger should be half an aṅgula less than that.

sanskrit: kaniṣṭhāṅguṣṭhakau kāryau caturaṅgulasammitau //
english: The little finger and the thumb should be made to measure four aṅgulas each.

sanskrit: dviparvoṅguṣṭhakaḥ kāryaḥ śeṣāgulyastriparvikāḥ / sarvāsāṃ parvaṇordhena nakhamānaṃ vidhīyate //
english: The thumb should be made to have two parvans joints. The other fingers should have three joints. The measure of the nail is laid down as half the size of the joints on the respective fingers.

sanskrit: vakṣaso yat pramāṇantu jaṭharaṃ tatpramāṇataḥ /
english: The extent of the belly is same as that of the chest.

sanskrit: aṅgulaikaṃ bhavennābhī vedhena ca pramāṇataḥ // tato meḍhrāntaraṃ kāryaṃ tālamātraṃ pramāṇataḥ /
english: Thenavel should be an aṅgula in breadth and proportionally deep. Then the interspace between the generative organ and the intestines should be made to measure a tāla.

sanskrit: nābhimadhye prīṇāho dvicatvāriṃśadaṅgulaiḥ //
english: The girth around the navel should be fortytwo aṅgulas.

sanskrit: antaraṃ stanayoḥ kāryaṃ tālamātraṃ pramāṇataḥ /
english: The interspace between the breasts should be made to measure a tāla in breadth.

sanskrit: civukau yavamānau tu maṇḍalaṃ dvipadaṃ bhavet //
english: The circular space around them should be two pādas two feet.

sanskrit: catuḥṣaṣṭyaṅgulaṃ kāryaṃ veṣṭanaṃ vakṣasaḥ sphuṭam / caturmukhañca tadadhoveṣṭanaṃ parikīrtitam //
english: The circumference of the chest should be made sixtyfour aṅgulas clearly. The girth of the lower portion of the chest is said to be four mukhas one tāla.

sanskrit: pariṇāhas tathā kaṭyā catuḥpañcāśadaṅgulaiḥ /
english: The circumference of the waist should be fiftyfour aṅgulas.

sanskrit: vistāraścorumūle tu procyate dvādaśaṅgulaḥ //
english: The breadth of the base of the thigh is said to be twelve aṅgulas.

sanskrit: tasmādabhyadhikaṃ madhye tato nimnataraṃ kramāt /
english: It is somewhat greater at the middle of the thigh and gradually less broad below.

sanskrit: vistṛtāṣṭāṅgulaṃ jānutriguṇā pariṇāhataḥ //
english: The kneejoint should be eight aṅgulas in breadth and thrice that in its girth.

sanskrit: jaṅghāmadhye tu vistāraḥ saptāṅgula udāhṛtaḥ /
english: The middle of the leg from the ankle to the knee is said to be seven aṅgulas broad.

sanskrit: triguṇā paridhiścāsya jaṅghāgraṃ pañcavistarāt //
english: The girth of it should be three times that. The top of the leg should be five aṅgulas broad.

sanskrit: triguṇā paridhiścāsya pādau tālapramāṇakau /
english: The girth of that the leg should be thrice its breadth. The feet should measure a tāla.

sanskrit: āyāmādutthitau pādau caturaṅgulameva ca //
english: The extent of elevation of the feet should be four aṅgulas.

sanskrit: gulphāt pūrvaṃ tu kartavyaṃ pramāṇāccaturaṅgulam / trikalaṃ vistṛtau pādau tryaṅgulo guhyakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: The front part of the ankles should be four aṅgulas The extent of the feet should be three kalās. The generative organ should be three aṅgulas.

sanskrit: pañcāṅgulastu nāhosya dīrghā tadvat pradeśinī /
english: Its girth should be five aṅgulas. The forefinger should be of same length.

sanskrit: aṣṭamāṣṭāṃśatonyūnaḥ śeṣāṅgulyaḥ krameṇa tu //
english: The other fingers are duly lesser by one part of eighth. The height of the toe is said to be one and a half aṅgulas.

sanskrit: yavonamaṅgulaṃ kāryamaṅguṣṭhasya nakhaṃ tathā // ardhāṅgulaṃ tathānyāsāṃ kramān nyūnaṃ tu kārayet /
english: The nail of the two should be made twice that. Those of other fingers should be gradually made half aṅgula less than the previous.

sanskrit: aṅgulau vṛṣaṇau kāryau meḍhraṃ tu caturaṅgulam // pariṇāhotra koṣāgraṃ kartavyañcaturaṅgulam /
english: The scrotum should be three aṅgulas long. The generative organ should be four fingers long. The girth of the upper part of the pouch should be made to be four aṅgulas.

sanskrit: ṣaḍaṅgulaparīṇāhau vṛṣaṇau parikīrtitau //
english: The girth of the scrotum is said to be six aṅgulas. The image should be adorned with ornaments.

sanskrit: anayaiva diśā kāryaṃ loke dṛṣṭvā tu lakṣaṇam //
english: This is the exact description of details. The features of the deities should be made in this world, as described.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇe tu kare cakramadhastāt padmameva ca / vāme śaṅkhaṃ gadādhastādvāsudevasya lakṣaṇāt //
english: A disc on the upper right hand, and a lotus on the lower right hand, the conch on the upper left hand, the mace on the lower left hand are to be placed according to the characteristic of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: śrīpuṣṭau vāpi kartavye padmavīṇākarānvite / ūrumātrocchitāyāme mālāvidyādharau tathā //
english: The images of Śrī and Puṣṭi should be made carrying a lotus and a harp respectively in their hands, their images reaching upto the thighs of that of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: prabhāmaṇḍalasaṃsthau tau prabhā hastyādibhūṣaṇā / padmābhaṃ pādapīṭhantu pratimāsvevamācaret //
english: The halo should also be decked with the images of celestial elephants. The pedestal should be radiant like a lotus on which the images should be worshipped as follows.

sanskrit: piṇḍikālakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye dairghyeṇa pratimāsamā / ucchrāyaṃ pratimārdhantu catuḥṣaṣṭipuṭāṃ ca tām //
english: Also called Golaka. One eighth of an aṅgula. Seems to be a corrupt form for mukhya equal to one tāla or twelve aṅgulas. shall describe the characteristics of the pedestal.

sanskrit: tyaktvā paṅktidvayaṃ cādhastadūrdhvaṃ yattu koṣṭhakam /
english: The length is the same as that of the image. The height should be half of it.

sanskrit: samantādubhayoḥ pārśve antasthaṃ parimārjayet // ūrdhvaṃ paṅgktidvayaṃ tyaktvā adhastād yattu koṣṭhakam / antaḥ sammārjayet yatnāt pārśvayorubhayoḥ samam //
english: Leaving two rows at the bottOṃ, the other parts should be polished on either side as also inside. Leaving two rows at the top, the other parts are polished evenly on either side and inside. The rectaṅgular space in between these should then be polished.

sanskrit: caturdhā bhājayitvā tu ūrdhvapaṅktidvayaṃ budhaḥ //
english: The first two rows should be divided into four parts by a wise man.

sanskrit: mekhalā bhāgamātrā syāt khātaṃ tasyārdhamānataḥ /
english: The girdle should be equal to one such part. The indent should be half that.

sanskrit: bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ parityajya pārśvayorubhayoḥ samaṃ // datvā caikaṃ padaṃ vāhye pramāṇaṃ kārayed budhaḥ /
english: Leaving one such part evenly on either side a wise man should leave on the exterior a breadth of a foot.

sanskrit: tribhāgeṇa ca bhāgasyāgre syāttoyavinirgamaḥ //
english: The water drains should be at the top of each one of the threeparts.

sanskrit: nānāprakārabhedena bhadreyaṃ piṇḍikā śubhā /
english: This auspicious and excellent pedestal has been described relating to its manifold ways of construction.

sanskrit: aṣṭatālā tu kartavyā devī lakṣmīstayā striyaḥ //
english: The images of thegoddess Lakṣmī and other feminine forms should be made to measure eight tālas in length.

sanskrit: bhruvau yavādhike kārye yavahīnā tu nāsikā / golakenādhikaṃ vaktramūrdhvaṃ tiryagvivarjitaṃ //
english: The eye brows should be more than a yava in length. The nose should be less than a yava in length. The mouth should measure more than a small ball well distributed above and below.

sanskrit: āyate nayane kārye tribhāgonair yavaistribhiḥ /
english: The eye should be made long measuring three parts of a yava less than three yavas.

sanskrit: tadardhena tu vaipulyaṃ netrayoḥ parikalpayet //
english: Then the two shoulders should be made sloping by less than a kalā.

sanskrit: namraṃ kalāvihīnantu kuryādaṃśadvayaṃ tathā //
english: The neck should be one and a half kalās long and made beautiful by a proportionate width.

sanskrit: netraṃ vinā tu vistārau ūrū jānū ca piṇḍikā // aṅghripṛṣṭhau sphicau kaṭyāṃ yathābhāgaṃ prakalpayet /
english: The thighs, kneejoints, the pedestal, should be broad. The feet, the hinder part, the bullocks and the hips should be made as prescribed.

sanskrit: saptāṃśonās tathāṅgulyo dīrghaṃ viṣkambhanāhataṃ //
english: The fingers should measure less than the seventh part of the above and should be long and not crooked.

sanskrit: netraikavarjitāyāmā jaṅghorū ca tathā kaṭiḥ /
english: The shank, thigh and the hip would be one netra less in length.

sanskrit: madhyapārśvaṃ ca tadvṛttaṃ ghanaṃ pīnaṃ kucadvayaṃ //
english: The middle part and the sides should have the same roundness. The two breasts should be fully developed and plump.

sanskrit: tālamātrau stanau karyau kaṭiḥ sārdhakalādhikā /
english: The beasts should be made to measure a tāla. The waist should be one and a half kalās.

sanskrit: lakṣma śeṣaṃ purāvatsyāt dakṣiṇe cāmubujaṃ kare //
english: A lotus should be placed on the right hand and a bilva fruit on the left hand.

sanskrit: vāme vittvaṃ striyau pārśve śubhe cāmarahastake /
english: There should be two maidens on the sides holding chowries in their hands.

sanskrit: dīrghaghoṇastu garuḍaś cakrāṅgādyānatho vade //
english: The image of Garuḍa should have a long nose. shall then describe those which bear the marks of a disc.

sanskrit: śālagrāmādimūrteś ca vakṣyehaṃ bhuktimuktidāḥ /
english: shall describe the characteristics of the śālagrāma mūrti the different gods represented by different kinds of śālagrāma stones which yield enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: vāsudevo 'sito dvāre śālagrāmadvicakrakaḥ //
english: The stone called Vāsudeva is black coloured around its mouth and has marks of two discs on it.

sanskrit: jñeyaḥ saṅkarṣaṇo lagnadvicakro rakta uttamaḥ / sūkṣmacakro bahucchidraḥ pradyumno nīladīghavaḥ //
english: The Saṅkarṣaṇa stone is red in colour and has marks The Aniruddha stone is yellow in colour and has the mark of a lotus.

sanskrit: pīto niruddhaḥ padmāṅgo vartulo dvitrirekhavān /
english: It is circular in shape and has two or three rays.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇo nārāyaṇo nābhyunnataḥ śuṣiradīrghavān //
english: The Nārāyaṇa stone is black in colour with an elevated, and deep hole.

sanskrit: parameṣṭho sābjacakraḥ pṛṣṭhacchidrakaś ca vindumān /
english: The Parameṣṭi stone has the marks of the lotus and. disc. It is perforated at the back and has dots on the surface.

sanskrit: sthūlacakro 'sito viṣṇurmadhye rekhā gadākṛtiḥ //
english: The Viṣṇu stone has a big disc mark. It is black in colour. It has a line in the middle part.

sanskrit: nṛsiṃhaḥ kapikaḥ sthūlavakraḥ syāt pañcavindukaḥ / varāhaḥ śaktiliṅgaḥ syāt taccakrau viṣamau sṛtau //
english: It is of the shape of a mace. The Nṛsiṃha stone is tawny. It has the mark of a big disc and five dots. The Varāha stone is of the shape of the female divinity.

sanskrit: indranīlanibhaḥ sthūlastrirekhālāñchitaḥ śubhaḥ / kūrmastathonnataḥ pṛṣṭhe vartulāvartako 'sitaḥ //
english: It has unequal discs. It is of the colour of sapphire. It is large with the marks of three lines and is good. The Kūrma stone has an elevated hinder part with circular lines.

sanskrit: hayagrīvoṅkuśāvārarekho nīlaḥ savindukaḥ / vaikuṇṭhaḥ ekacakro 'bjī maṇibhiḥ puccharekhakaḥ //
english: The Hayagrīva stone has a line of the shape of a good. It is blue coloured and is dotted. The Vaikuṇṭha stone has the mark of a disc and lotus. It has the radiance of a gem.

sanskrit: matsyo dīrghastrivinduḥ syāt kācavarṇastu pūritaḥ /
english: The Matsya stone is long and has three dots. It is crystallinecoloured and is well formed.

sanskrit: śrīdharo vanamālāṅkaḥ pañjarekhastu vartulaḥ //
english: The Srīdhara stone has a garland of wild flowers and five lines and is circular.

sanskrit: vāmano vartulaścātihrasvo nīlaḥ savindukaḥ /
english: The Vāmana stone is circular and is very short. It is. blue coloured and has a dot.

sanskrit: śyāmastrivikramo dakṣarekho vāmena vindukaḥ //
english: The Trivikrama stone is black coloured. It has a line on the right and a dot on the left side.

sanskrit: ananto nāgabhogāṅgo naikābho naikamūrtimān /
english: The Ananta stone has the mark of the hood of a serpent, it has variegated colours and manifold forms.

sanskrit: sthūlo dāmodaro madhyacakro dvāḥsūkṣmavindukaḥ //
english: The Dāmodara stone is big and has a disc in the middle part with two minute dots.

sanskrit: sudarśanastvekacakro lakṣmīnārāyaṇo dvayāt /
english: The Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa stone is that which has the marks of two discs.

sanskrit: tricakraścācyuto devastricakrako vā trivikramaḥ //
english: The Acyuta stone has the marks of three discs. Or the Trivikrama stone may have the marks of three discs.

sanskrit: janārdanaś catuś cakro vāsudevaś ca pañcabhiḥ /
english: The Janārdana stone has the marks of four discs. The Vāsudeva stone has the marks of five discs.

sanskrit: ṣaṭvakraś caiva pradyumnaḥ saṅkarṣaṇañca saptabhiḥ //
english: The Pradyumna stone has the marks of six discs. The Saṅkarṣaṇa. stone has the marks of seven discs.

sanskrit: puruṣottamoṣṭacakro navavyūho navāṅkitaḥ /
english: The Puruṣottama stone has the marks of eight discs. The Navavyūha form has the marks of nine discs.

sanskrit: daśāvatāro daśabhirdaśaikenāniruddhakaḥ /
english: The stone representing the ten manifestations of Viṣṇu is marked with ten discs.

sanskrit: dvādaśātmā dvādaśabhirata ūrdhvamanantakaḥ //
english: The Dvādaśātman class of śālagrāma is marked by twelve discs.

sanskrit: śālagrāmādicakrāṅkapūjāḥ siddhyai vadāmi te /
english: shall describe the mode of worshipping the śālagrāma marked with discs for the sake of accomplishment.

sanskrit: trividhā syāddhareḥ pūjā kāmyākāmyobhayātmikā //
english: The worship of Hari in the śālagrāma is of three kinds i kāmyā performed for gaining particular benefit

sanskrit: mīnādīnāntu pañcānāṃ kāmyātho vobhayātmikā / varāhasya nṛsiṃhasya vāmanasya ca muktaye //
english: The worship of the five manifestations of Viṣṇu such as the Fish etc., is, either kāmyā or ubhayātmikā The worship of the manifestations of the Boar Manlion and Dwarf forms of Viṣṇu is for emancipation.

sanskrit: cakrādīnāṃ trayāṇāntu śālagrāmārcanaṃ śṛṇu /
english: Listen to the threefold worship of the śālagrāma endowed with discs.

sanskrit: uttamā niṣphalā pūjā kaniṣṭhā saphalārcanā //
english: The excellent worship is that performed without desiring for the fruits.

sanskrit: madhyamā mūrtipūjā syāccakrābje caturasrake / praṇavaṃ hṛdi vinyasya ṣaḍaṅgaṅkaradehayoḥ // kṛtamudrātrayaś cakrād vahiḥ pūve guruṃ yajet /
english: The worship of an image is mediocre. In a circular lotus placed on a rectaṅgular seat, having assigned the praṇava the syllable Oṃ to the heart and having assigned the sacred syllables to the parts of the body and having shown three mudrās positions of fingers in the practice of worship, the preceptor should be worshipped outside the circle.

sanskrit: āpye gaṇaṃ vāyave ca dhātāraṃ nairṛte yajet //
english: The attendant gods gaṇas should be worshipped on the west.

sanskrit: vidhātārañca kartāraṃ hartāraṃ dakṣasaumyayoḥ / viśvaksenaṃ yajedīśe āgneye kṣetrapālakam //
english: Dhātṛ on the northwest, Vidhātṛ on the southwest, the Kartā and Hartā on the south and north, Viṣvaksena Viṣṇushould be worshipped in the northeast, and Kṣetrapālaka the guardian deity on the southeast.

sanskrit: ṛgādivedān prāgādau ādhārānantakaṃ bhuvaṃ /
english: The Vedas, Ṛgveda etc. should be worshipped in the east etc.

sanskrit: pīṭhaṃ padmaṃ cārkacandravahnyākhyaṃ maṇḍalatrayaṃ //
english: The serpent Ananta which is the support of the earth, the seat of worship, the lotus, the three orbssun, moon and fires should be worshipped.

sanskrit: āsanaṃ dvādaśārṇena tatra sthāpya śilāṃ yajet / astena ca samastena svavījena yajet kramāt //
english: The seat should consist of twelve letters forming the mystic formula of the God. Having placed the God there, the stone should be worshipped with the individual syllables and the whole of the sacred syllable in order.

sanskrit: pūrvādāvatha vedādyair gāyatrībhyāṃ jitādinā / praṇavenārcayet pañcānmudrāstisraḥ pradarśayet //
english: Then one should worship with the vedic sacred syllables accomplished by the syllables such as the gāyatrī, etc. and praṇava on the east and other directions.

sanskrit: viśvaksenasya cakrasya kṣetrapālasya darśayet /
english: Then the three mudrās of the Viṣvaksena Viṣṇu, the disc and the Kṣetrapāla should be shown.

sanskrit: śālagrāmasya prathamā pūjārtho niṣphalocyate //
english: This is the first variety of the worship of śālagrāma.

sanskrit: pūrvavat ṣoḍaśārañca sapadmaṃ maṇḍalaṃ likhet /
english: One should draw a circle as before with sixteen radii and with a lotus.

sanskrit: śaṅkhacakragadākhaḍgair gurvādyaṃ pūrvavadyajet // pūrve saumye dhanurvāṇān vedādyair āsanaṃ dadet /
english: One should then worship the preceptor and others with a conch, disc, mace and sword. The bow and the arrows should be placed in the east and the north. The seat should be placed with the vedic syllables.

sanskrit: śilāṃ nyased dvādaśārṇaistṛtīyaṃ pūjanaṃ śṛṇu //
english: The stone should be placed with the sacred twelve syllables of the lord. Listen to the third variety of worship.

sanskrit: aṣṭāramabjaṃ vilikhet gurvādyaṃ pūrvavadyajayet / aṣṭārṇenāsanaṃ datvā tenaiva ca śilāṃ nyaset /
english: One should draw a lotus having eight radii and worship the preceptor and others as before. Having offered the seat with the eight sacred letters one should place the stone with the same formula.

sanskrit: pūjayeddaśadhā tena gāyatrībhyāṃ jitaṃ tathā //
english: One should worship ten times with that formula. It is then accomplished by gāyatrī etc.

sanskrit: oṃrūpaḥ keśavaḥ padmaśaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ /
english: Keśava of the form of syllable Oṃ bears the lotus, conch, disc and mace.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇaḥ śaṅkhapadmagadācakrī pradakṣiṇaṃ //
english: Nārāyaṇa bears the conch, lotus, mace and disc.

sanskrit: tato gado mādhavoriśaṅkhapadmī namāmi taṃ / cakrakaumodakīpadmaśaṅkhī govinda ūrjitaḥ //
english: Circumambulation to Him. Then salute Madhava, who bears the mace, disc, conch and lotus. Govinda wields the disc, the Kaumodakī name of a mace, lotus and conch.

sanskrit: bhokṣadaḥ śrīgadī padmī śaṅkhī viṣṇuś ca cakradhṛk /
english: Viṣṇu, the bearer of the disc, the mace, lotus and conch is the bestower of emancipation.

sanskrit: śaṅkhacakrābjagadinaṃ madhusūdanamāname //
english: salute Madhusūdana, who bears the conch, disc, lotus and mace.

sanskrit: bhaktyā trivikramaḥ padmagadī cakrī ca śaṅkhyapi /
english: prostrate with devotion at the feet of Trivikrama who bears the lotus, mace, disc and conch.

sanskrit: śaṅkhacakragadāpadmī vāmanaḥ pātu māṃ sadā //
english: May Vāmana, the bearer of the conch, disc, mace and lotus protect me always.

sanskrit: gaditaḥ śrīdharaḥ padmī cakraśārṅgī ca śaṅkhyapi /
english: Śrīdhara who holds a lotus, disc, bow and also the conch yields emancipation.

sanskrit: hṛṣīkeśo gadācakrī padmī cakraśaṅkhī ca pātu naḥ //
english: Hṛṣīkeśa wields the mace, disc, lotus and conch. May He protect us.

sanskrit: varadaḥ padmanābhastu śaṅkhābjārigadādharaḥ / dāmodaraḥ padmaśaṅkhagadācakrī namāmi taṃ //
english: And Padmanābha is one who yields boons and who holds the conch, lotus, disc and mace, salute him. Dāmodara is one who holds a lotus, conch, mace and disc.

sanskrit: tene gadī śaṅkhacakrī vāsudevobjabhṛjjagat / saṅkarṣaṇo gadī śaṅkhī padmī cakrī ca pātu vaḥ //
english: May Vāsudeva, who wields a mace, conch, disc and lotus protect the universe. May Saṅkarṣaṇa, who holds a mace, conch, lotus and disc protect us.

sanskrit: gadī cakrī śaṅkhagadī pradyumnaḥ padmabhṛt prabhuḥ /
english: Lord Pradyumna is one who holds a mace, disc, conch and mace as well as a lotus.

sanskrit: aniruddhaś cakragadī śaṅkhī padmī ca pātu naḥ //
english: May Aniruddha, who wields the disc, mace, conch and lotus protect us.

sanskrit: adhokṣajaḥ padmagadī śaṅkhī cakrī ca pātu vaḥ //
english: May Adhokṣaja who wields lotus, mace, conch and disc protect you.

sanskrit: devo nṛsiṃhaś cakrābjagadāśaṅkhī namāmi tam /
english: salute that Lord Nṛsiṃha, who wields disc, lotus, mace and conch.

sanskrit: acyutaḥ śrīgadī padmī cakrī śaṅkhī ca pātu vaḥ // bālarūpī śaṅkhagadī upendraś cakrapadmyapi /
english: May Acyuta, who holds mace, lotus, disc and conch, protect you all. So also may Upendra, who is of the form of a child and who holds the disc and lotus, protect you.

sanskrit: janārdanaḥ padmacakrī śaṅkhadhārī gadādharaḥ //
english: And may Janārdana, who wields lotus, disc, conch and mace protect you.

sanskrit: śaṅkhī padmī ca cakrī ca hariḥ kaumodakīdharaḥ / kṛṣṇaḥ śaṅkhī gadī padmī cakrī me bhuktimuktidaḥ //
english: May Hari, who holds conch, lotus, disc as well as mace kaumodakī yield me enjoyment and emancipation. May Kṛṣṇa, who holds conch, mace, lotus and disc give enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: ādimūttirvāsudevastasmāt saṅkarṣaṇobhavat /
english: The first manifestation was that of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: saṅkarṣaṇācca pradyumnaḥ pradyumnādaniruddhakaḥ //
english: Pradyumna manifested from Saṅkarṣaṇa. Aniruddha appeared from Pradyumna.

sanskrit: keśavādiprabhedena aikaikasya tridhā kramāt /
english: Each one of the above forms was divided into three forms such as Keśava and others.

sanskrit: dvādaśākṣarakaṃ stotraṃ caturviṃśatimūrtimat / yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi nirmalaḥ sarvamāpnuyāt //
english: One who reads or hears this hymn consisting of twelve letters on the twentyfour forms gets free from impurity and gets all things.

sanskrit: daśāvatāraṃ matsyādilakṣaṇaṃ pravadāmi te /
english: shall describe to you the characteristics of the ten manifestations of Viṣṇu beginning with the Fish.

sanskrit: matsyākārastu matsyaḥ syāt kūrmaḥ kārmākṛlirbhavet //
english: The Fish form of Viṣṇu should resemble a fish. The Tortoise form should resemble a tortoise.

sanskrit: narāṅgo vātha kartavyo bhūvarāho gadādibhṛt / dakṣiṇe vāmake śaṅkhaṃ lakṣmīrvā padmameva vā // śrīvāmakūrparasthā tu kṣmānantau caraṇānugau /
english: The terrestrial boar manifestation should have a human body and as carrying a mace and other weapons in the right hand, and the conch, the goddess Lakṣmī or a lotus in the left. Or the goddess is represented as resting on the left elbow and the earth and the serpent Ananta at the feet.

sanskrit: varāhasthāpanādrājyaṃ bhavābdhitaraṇaṃ bhavet // narasiṃho vivṛttāsyo vāmorukṣatadānavaḥ / tadvakṣo dārayanmālī sphuraccakragadādharaḥ //
english: The installation of the figure secures for a person a kingdom and such a person gets across the ocean of mundane existence. The Manlion image should be represented as having a wide open mouth and having the killed demon Hiraṇyakaśipu on the left thigh.

sanskrit: chatrī daṇḍī vāmanaḥ syādathavā syāccaturbhujaḥ /
english: His chest should wear a garland and his arms should hold disc and mace. The Dwarfform may hold an umbrella and a stick or have four arms.

sanskrit: rāmaścāpī śarī khaḍgī śaṅkhī vā dvibhujaḥ smṛtaḥ / gadālāṅgaladhārī ca rāmo vātha caturbhujaḥ //
english: The figure of Paraśurāma may hold the bow and arrow, a sword and an axe. The figure of Rama should have the bow, arrow, sword, conch or two hands or may have four arms holding a mace and. plough.

sanskrit: vāmordhve lāṅgalaṃ dadyādadhaḥ śaṅkhaṃ suśobhanaṃ / muṣalaṃ dakṣiṇordhve tu cakrañcādhaḥ suśobhanaṃ //
english: The plough may be provided on the left half upper arm and the auspicious conch on the lower arm. The mace may be provided on the right half upper arm and the auspicious disc on the lower arm.

sanskrit: śāntātmā lambakarṇaś ca gaurāṅgaścāmbarāvṛtaḥ / ūrdhvapadmasthito buddho varadābhayadāyakaḥ //
english: The figure of Buddha should be made as calm, having long ears, white complexion, wearing a cloth, and seated on a lotus with its petals upwards and as conferring favour and protection.

sanskrit: dhanustūṇānvitaḥ kalkī mlecchotsādakaro dvijaḥ /
english: The figure of Kalki is to be represented as a twiceborn endowed with a bow and quiver and as destroying the foreigners.

sanskrit: athavāśvasthitaḥ khaḍgī śaṅkhacakraśarānvitaḥ //
english: Or he should be represented as seated on the horse and endowed with a sword, conch, disc and arrow.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇaṃ vāsudevādinavakasya vadāmi te /
english: shall describe the characteristics of nine forms of Viṣṇu commencing with Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇordhve gadā vāme vāmordhve cakramuttamaṃ //
english: The mace is placed on the right half upper arm and the excellent disc on the left half upper arm.

sanskrit: brahmeśau pārśvagau nityaṃ vāsudevosti pūrvavat / śaṅkhī sa varado vātha dvibhujo vā caturbhujaḥ //
english: The image of Vāsudeva may be made as before or as having four hands or two hands, one holding a conch and the other as conferring boons and having Brahmā and Īśa Śiva always on either side.

sanskrit: lāṅgalī muṣalī rāmo gadāpadmadharaḥ smṛtaḥ /
english: The figure of Balarāma is represented as holding a plough, mace, club and lotus.

sanskrit: pradyumno dakṣiṇe vajraṃ śaṅkhaṃ vāme dhanuḥ kare //
english: The image of Pradyumna is represented as having thunderbolt and conch on the right arm and the bow in the left arm.

sanskrit: gadānābhyāvṛtaḥ pītyā pradyumno vā dhanuḥśarī /
english: Or Pradyumna is represented as having the mace resting on the navel with pleasure or holding the bow and arrow.

sanskrit: caturbhujo niruddhaḥ syāttathā nārāyaṇo vibhuḥ //
english: Aniruddha may be represented as having four arms. In the same way Lord Nārāyaṇa may also be represented.

sanskrit: caturmukhaś caturbāhurvṛhajjaṭharamaṇḍalaḥ / lambakūrco jaṭāyukto vrahmā haṃsāgravāhanaḥ //
english: The image of Brahmā is represented as having four faces, four hands, big belly, long beards, matted hair, and having swan as the vehicle in front of him.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇe cākṣasūtrañca sruvo vāme tu kuṇḍikā /
english: There should be a rosary and a ladle on the right hand and a waterpot and vessel to hold the sacrificial clarified butter.

sanskrit: ājyasthālī sarasvatī sāvitrī vāmadakṣiṇe //
english: Sarasvatī and Sāvitrī consorts of Brahmā should be placed on the left and right sides.

sanskrit: viṣṇuraṣṭabhujastārkṣe kare khaḍgastu dakṣiṇe / gadāśaraś ca varado vāme kārmukakheṭake //
english: The image of Viṣṇu is represented as having eight hands, Garuḍa the vehicle, holding a sword, mace, and arrow in the right hand and as conferring gifts and holding the bow and mace in the left hand.

sanskrit: cakraśaṅkhau caturbāhur narasiṃhaś caturbhujaḥ / śaṅkhacakradharo vāpi vidāritamahāsuraḥ // acaturbāhurvarāhastu śeṣaḥ pāṇitale dhṛtaḥ / dhārayan bāhunā pṛthvīṃ vāmnena kamalādharaḥ //
english: The figure of Narasiṃha is represented as having four hands holding the conch and disc and piercing the body of the mighty demon Hiraṇyakaśipu. The figure of Varāha is endowed with four arms holding the serpent Śeṣa in one of the hands and the earth in the left hand and his consort Kamalā Lakṣmī.

sanskrit: pādalagnā dharā kāryā padā lakṣmīrvyavasthitā /
english: The earth should be made as resting at the feet and goddess Lakṣmī as seated at the feet.

sanskrit: trailokyamohanastārkṣye aṣṭabāhustu dakṣiṇe // cakraṃ khaḍgaṃ ca muṣalaṃ aṅkuśaṃ vāmake kare / śaṅkhaśārṅgagadāpāśān padmavīṇāsamanvite //
english: Trailokyamohana one who stupefies the three worlds should be represented as riding the Tārkhya the eaglevehicle and possess eight hands, holding the sword, mace and goad in the right hand and the conch, bow, mace and the noose in the left hand.

sanskrit: lakṣmīḥ sarasvatī kārye viśvarūpo 'tha dakṣiṇe /
english: Images of Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī should be endowed with lotus and lute respectively.

sanskrit: mudgaraṃ ca tathā pāśaṃ śaktiśūlaṃ śaraṃ kare // vāme śaṅkhañca śārṅgañca gadāṃ pāśaṃ ca tomaraṃ / lāṅgalaṃ paraśuṃ daṇḍaṃ churikāṃ carmakṣepakaṃ // viṃśadbāhuś caturvaktro dakṣiṇasthotha vāmake /
english: Then the form of Viśvarūpa of Viṣṇu should be endowed with the club, noose, spear and arrow in the right hand and conch, bow, mace, noose, tomara javelin, plough, axe, staff, sword and leather sling in the left hand. The Harihara Śiva and Viṣṇu form of Viṣṇu should be placed on the right or left side, being endowed with twenty hands, four faces and three eyes.

sanskrit: trinetre vāmapārśve na śayito jalaśāyyapi //
english: He should either be lying on his left or reclining on the water.

sanskrit: śriyā dhṛtaikacaraṇo vimalādyābhirīḍitaḥ /
english: He should also be shown as being attended to by the female divinities Vimalā and others.

sanskrit: nābhipadmacaturvaktro hariśaṅkarako hariḥ // śūlarṣṭidhārī dakṣe ca gadācakradharo pade / rudrakeśavalakṣmāṅgo gaurīlakṣmīsamanvitaḥ //
english: He should also have the fourfaced Brahmā in the navellotus. The form of Viṣṇu bearing the marks of Rudra and Keśava should hold a spear and sword in the right hand and the mace and disc in the other and be in the company of Gaurī and Lakṣmī the consorts of Śiva and Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: śaṅkhacakragadāvedapāṇiścāśvaśirā hariḥ / vāmapādo dhṛtaḥ śeṣe dakṣiṇaḥ kūrmapṛṣṭhagaḥ //
english: The Hayaśiras horseheaded form of Viṣṇu should be represented as holding the conch, disc, mace and the Vedas. The left foot should rest on the serpent Śeṣa and the right on the back of tortoise.

sanskrit: dattātreyo dvibāhuḥ syādvāmotsaṅge śriyā saha /
english: The form of Dattātreya may have two arms, the goddess Śrī Lakṣmī being seated on the left lap.

sanskrit: viśvaksenaś cakragadī halī śaṅkhī harergaṇaḥ // caṇḍī viṃśatibāhuḥ syādbibhratī dakṣiṇaiḥ karaḥ / śūlāsiśakticakrāṇi pāśaṃ kheṭāyudhābhayaṃ // ḍamaruṃ śaktikāṃ vāmair nāgapāśañca kheṭakaṃ /
english: The Viṣvaksena form of Viṣṇu may hold a disc, mace, plough and conch. The image of Caṇḍī may have twenty hands and may hold the spear, sword, dart, disc, noose, club, ḍamaru a small drum and spike in the left hands and also show protective posture and the snake as the noose, club, axe, goad, bow, bell, banner, mace, mirror, and iron mace in the right hands..

sanskrit: kuṭhāṅkuśacāpāṃś ca ghaṇṭādhvajagadāṃs tathā // ādarśamudgarān hastaiś caṇḍī vā daśabāhukā / tadadho mahiṣaśchinnamūrdhā patitamastakaḥ //
english: Or the figure of Caṇḍī is made to have ten hands, with the buffalo placed below with its head fully severed and the demon as issuing forth from its neck with rage and brandishing his weapon, holding spike in the hand, vomitting blood, his hairs.

sanskrit: śastrodyatakaraḥ kruddhastadgrīvāsambhavaḥ pumān / śūlahasto vamadrakto raktasraṅmūrdhajekṣaṇaḥ //
english: stained with blood and blood dripping out from the eyes. forming a garland on the chest, being devoured by the lion and wellbound by the noose in the neck.

sanskrit: siṃhenāsvādyamānastu pāśabaddho gale bhṛśaṃ / yāmyāṅghyrākrāntasiṃhā ca savyāṅghrirnīcagāsure //
english: The goddess is represented as resting her right foot on the lion and the left foot on. the demon underneath. This form of Caṇḍikā, the destroyer of enemies.

sanskrit: caṇḍikeyaṃ trinetrā ca saśastrā ripumardanī /
english: is made as having three eyes and endowed with weapons.

sanskrit: navapadmātmake sthāne pūjyā durgā svamūrtitaḥ // ādau madhye tathendrādau navātattvātmabhiḥ kramāt /
english: This Durgā is to be worshipped with the nine elements in order in a diagram of nine lotuses from her own form at the beginning, centre and the eastern and other directions.

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśabhujaikā tu dakṣe muṇḍaṃ ca kheṭakaṃ // ādarśatarjanīcāpaṃ dhvajaṃ ḍamarukaṃ tathā /
english: The image should be made as possessing eighteen arms carrying a human head, club, mirror, tarjanī a kind of weapon, bow, banner and.

sanskrit: vajrakhaḍgāṅkuśaśarān cakrandevī śalākayā /
english: a little drum in the right hand and the noose, spear, mace, trident, thunderbolt, sword, goad and dart in the left hand.

sanskrit: etair evāyudhair yuktā śeṣāḥ ṣoḍaśabahukāḥ // ḍamaruṃ tarjanīṃ tyaktvā rudracaṇḍādayo nava /
english: The others Rudracaṇḍā and other goddesses should be endowed with the same weapons in their sixteen hands except the little drum and tarjanī a kind of weapon.

sanskrit: rudracaṇḍā pracaṇḍā ca caṇḍogrā caṇḍanāyikā // caṇḍā caṇdavatī caiva caṇḍarūpāticaṇḍikā /
english: The nine goddesses commencing with Rudracaṇḍā are Rudracaṇḍā, Pracaṇḍā, Caṇḍogrā, Caṇḍanāyikā, Caṇḍā, Caṇḍavatī, Caṇḍarūpā, Aticaṇḍikā and Ugracaṇḍā stationed at the centre.

sanskrit: ugracaṇḍā ca madhyasthā rocanābhāruṇāsitā //
english: They are made to be coloured as the rocanā.

sanskrit: nīlā śuklā dhūmrikā ca pītā śvetā ca siṃhagāḥ /
english: yellow pigment, red, black, blue, white, purple, yellow and white and as riding the lion.

sanskrit: mahiṣotha pumān śastrī tatkacagrahamuṣṭikāḥ // ālīḍhā nava durgāḥ syuḥ sthāpyāḥ putrādivṛddhaye /
english: Then the buffalo as a human form should be held by the hair by the nine forms of Durgā holding weapons. They are in the ālīḍha posture.

sanskrit: tathā gaurī ca caṇḍikādyā kuṇḍyakṣararadāgnidhṛk //
english: They have to be established for the increase of progeny as also the forms Gaurī, Caṇḍikā and others as well as the forms Kuṇḍi, Akṣararadā and Agnidhṛk.

sanskrit: saiva rambhā vane siddhāgnihīnā lalitā tathā /
english: She is the same as Rambhā. She is accomplished and devoid of fire. She is also Lalitā.

sanskrit: skandhamūrdhakarā vāme dvitīye dhṛtadarpaṇā //
english: She holds the severed head along with the neck in the left hand and a mirror in the second hand.

sanskrit: yāmye phalāñjalihastā saubhāgyā tatra cordhvikā / lakṣmīryāmyakarāmbhojā vāme śrīphalasaṃyutā //
english: The image of Saubhāgyā is made as holding fruits in the folded palms on the right side. The image of Lakṣmī holds the lotus in the right hand and the śrīphala bilva fruit in the left.

sanskrit: pustākṣamālikāhastā vīṇāhastā sarasvatī /
english: The image of Sarasvatī should be made as holding a book, rosary and lute in the hands.

sanskrit: kumbhābjahastā śvetābhā makaropari jāhnavī // kūrmagā yamunā kumbhakarā śyāmā ca pūjyate /
english: The image of Jahnavī the river Ganges is represented as holding a pot and flower in the hand and standing on the crocodile and of white complexion. The image of the river Yamunā is worshipped as mounted on the tortoise and as holding a pot in the hand and of dark complexion.

sanskrit: savīṇastumburuḥ śuklaḥ śūlī mātragrato vṛṣe //
english: The image of Tumburu is represented as white in colour, holding a lute and trident and riding a bull.

sanskrit: gaurī caturmukhī brāhmī akṣamālāsurānvitā / kuṇḍakṣapātriṇī vāme haṃsagā śāṅkarī sitā // śaracāpau dakṣiṇe 'syā vāme cakraṃ dhanurvṛṣe /
english: The fourfaced Brāhmī the femaleenergy of Brahmā is represented as of fair complexion, riding a swan and as carrying a rosary, different vessels such as surā and kuṇḍa in the left hand. Śāṅkarī is represented as white, seated on a bull holding the bow and arrow in the right hand and the disc and the bow in the left hand.

sanskrit: kaumārī śikhigā raktā śaktihastā dvibāhukā // cakraśaṅkhadharā savye vāme lakṣmīrgadābjadhṛk /
english: Kaumārī is represented as red in colour, riding the peacock and having two arms, holding the spears. The form of Lakṣmī should hold the disc, and conch in the right hand and the mace and lotus in the left hand.

sanskrit: daṇḍaśaṅkhāsi gadayā vārāho mahiṣasthitā //
english: The form of Vārāhī should be mounted on the buffalo and hold the stick, conch, sword and goad.

sanskrit: aindrī vāme vajrahastā sahasrākṣī tu siddhaye /
english: The image of Aindrī conferring success should be represented as having thousand eyes and holding the thunderbolt in the left hand.

sanskrit: cāmuṇḍā koṭarāghnī syānnirmāṃsā tu trilocanā // nirmāṃsā asthisārā vā ūrdhvakeśī kṛśodarī / dvīpacarmadharā vāme kapālaṃ paṭṭiśaṅkare //
english: Cāmuṇḍā may have three eyes deeply sunken, a skeleton form devoid of flesh, erectly standing hair, emaciated belly, clad in tigerskin and holding a skull and spear in the left hand and a trident and scissor in the right standing on the dead body of a man and wearing a garland of bones.

sanskrit: vināyako narākāro vṛhatkukṣirgajānanaḥ //
english: The image of Vināyaka should have a human body, big belly, elephant face, big trunk and sacred thread.

sanskrit: kalā dvādaśa nāḍī tu grīvā sārdhakalocchritā / ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaṃ kaṇṭhaṃ guhyamadhyardhamaṅgulaṃ //
english: The mouth measuring kalās in breadth while the trunk should measure fingerbreadths in length. The neck should be kalās in girth and 0 kalās in height. The throatregion should be finger in length.

sanskrit: nābhirūrū dvādaśañca jaṅghe pāde tu dakṣiṇe /
english: The region of the navel and thigh should be of twelve fingers as also the leg from the ankle to the knee and the feet.

sanskrit: svadantaṃ paraśuṃ vāme laḍḍukañcotpalaṃ śaye //
english: He should be represented as holding his own tusk made into an axe in the right hand and the laḍḍuka a ball of sweet and lotus flower in the left.

sanskrit: sumukhī ca viḍālākṣī pārśve skando mayūragaḥ / svāmī śākho viśākhaś ca dvibhujo bālarūpadhṛk //
english: The image of Skanda, the lord of the universe also known as Śākha and Viśākha, is represented as a boy possessing two arms and riding a peacock with the images of Sumukhī and Viḍālākṣī.

sanskrit: dakṣe śaktiḥ kukkuṭotha ekavaktrotha ṣaṇmukhaḥ / ṣaḍbhujo vā dvādaśabhirgrāmeraṇye dvibāhukaḥ //
english: The god may be represented as having a single face or six faces, six hands or twelve hands carrying the spear and a cock in the right hand. In the village or the forest it should have two arms.

sanskrit: śaktīṣupāśanistriṃśatotradostarjanīyutaḥ / śaktyā dākṣiṇahasteṣu ṣaṭsu vāme kare tathā //
english: He should bear the spear, arrow, noose, nistriṃśa sword, goad and tarjanī a kind of weapon in the six right hands and the spear in the left hand.

sanskrit: śikhipicchandhanuḥ kheṭaṃ patākābhayakukkuṭe / kapālakartarīśūlapāśabhṛdyāmyasaumyayoḥ // gajacarmabhṛdūrdhvāsyapādā syāt rudracarcikā / saiva cāṣṭabhujā devī śiroḍamarukānvitā //
english: The image of Rudracarcikā the manifestation of the goddess may have a bow adorned by the plume of peacock, club, banner, protective posture, cock, skull, scissors, trident and noose in the right and left hands. She should also be clad in the elephant hide, with her leg raised up and the little drum placed on the head.

sanskrit: tena sā rudracāmuṇḍā nāṭeśvaryatha nṛtyatī /
english: Hence she is known as Rudracāmuṇḍā, the goddess of dancing and one who is dancing.

sanskrit: iyameva mahālakṣmīrupaviṣṭā caturmukhī //
english: This goddess herself, having four faces and in the sitting posture is known as Mahālakṣmī.

sanskrit: daśabāhustrinetrā ca śastrāsiḍamarutrikaṃ // bibhratī dakṣiṇe haste vāme ghaṇṭāṃ ca kheṭakaṃ / khaṭvāṅgaṃ ca triśūlañca siddhacāmuṇḍakāhvayā //
english: The goddess having ten hands and three eyes holding different weapons, sword and ḍamaru little drum in the right hand and the bell, club, staff with a skull at one end and trident in the left hand and eating men, horses, buffaloes and elephants held in the hand is called Siddhacāmuṇḍā.

sanskrit: siddhayogeśvarī devī sarvasiddhapradāyikā /
english: That goddess accomplishes everything and is known as Siddhayogeśvarī.

sanskrit: etadrūpā bhavedanyā pāśāṅkuśayutāruṇā //
english: She is also represented in another form endowed with the noose and goad and red in complexion.

sanskrit: bhairavī rūpavidyā tu bhujair dvādaśabhiryutā /
english: The goddess Bhairavī who has an embodiment of beauty is endowed with twelve arms.

sanskrit: etāḥ śmaśānajā raudrā ambāṣṭakamidaṃ smṛtaṃ //
english: These are all spoken as fierce forms arising from the cremation ground. The above are remembered as the eight forms of the goddess.

sanskrit: kṣamā śivāvṛtā vṛddhā dvibhujā vivṛtānanā / danturā kṣemakarī syādbhūmau jānukarā sthitā // yakṣiṇyastabdhadīrghākṣāḥ śākinyo vakradṛṣṭayaḥ /
english: The goddess Kṣamā Forbearance should be surrounded by jackals, old, having two arms, and widely opened mouth. The goddess Kṣemaṅkarī Benevolent may have protruding teeth and be resting her knees on the ground. The wives of semigods should be made to have long and motionless eyes.

sanskrit: piṅgākṣāḥ syurmahāramyā rūpiṇyopsarasaḥ sadā //
english: The Mahāramyas should have yellow eyes. The images of nymphs should always be made beautiful.

sanskrit: sākṣamālī triśūlī ca nandīśo dvārapālakaḥ / mahākālosimuṇḍī syācchūlakhaṭakavāṃs tathā //
english: The form of Nandīśa the bull, the doorkeeper of the goddess, should carry a rosary and a trident. The image of Mahākāla a form of Śiva as the destroyer may have a sword, human skull, trident and club.

sanskrit: kṛśo bhaṅgī ca nṛtyan vai kuṣmāṇḍasthūlakharvavān /
english: Kuṣmāṇḍa another attendant of Śiva should have a stout and dwarf form dancing.

sanskrit: gajagokarṇavaktrādyā vīrabhadrādayo gaṇāḥ //
english: Vīrabhadra and other attendants of Śiva should have ears and faces of elephants, cows, etc.

sanskrit: ghaṇṭākarṇoṣṭadaśadoḥ pāparogaṃ vidārayan / vajrāsidaṇḍacakreṣumuṣalāṅkuśamudgarān // dakṣiṇe tarjanīṃ kheṭaṃ śaktiṃ muṇḍañca pāśakaṃ / cāpaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ kuṭhārañca dvābhyāñcaiva triśūlakaṃ /
english: Ghaṇṭākarṇa an attendant of Śiva form should have eighteen hands crushing the accrued sin, holding weapons thunderbolt, sword, club, disc, arrow, mace, goad and hammer in the right hand and tarjanī a weapon, club, dart, human skull, noose, bow, bell and axe on the left and a trident in the remaining two hands and wearing a garland of bells and crushing the eruptive diseases.

sanskrit: ghaṇṭāmālākulo devo visphoṭakavimardanaḥ //
english: The consorts of Skanda.

sanskrit: sasaptāśve saikacakre rathe sūryo dvipadmadhṛk /
english: The image of the Sun should be made to ride a chariot having one wheel and seven horses.

sanskrit: masībhājanalekhanyau bibhratkuṇḍī tu dakṣiṇe // vāme tu piṅgalo dvāri daṇḍabhṛt sa ravergaṇaḥ / bālavyajanadhāriṇyau pārśve rājñī ca niṣprabhā //
english: He must hold two lotuses, inkstand, pen and a staff in his right hand. Piṅgala, an attendant and gatekeeper of the Sun should be placed on the left with the mace in his hand. Sungod should have female attendants bearing chowries flyflappers and the palelooking consort by his side.

sanskrit: athavāśvārūḍhaḥ kārya ekastu bhāskaraḥ /
english: Or the image of the Sun should be made as riding a horse alone.

sanskrit: varadā dvyabjanaḥ sarve dikpālāstrakarāḥ kramāt //
english: The guardian deities of different quarters should duly be endowed with weapons, holding two lotuses in hands and bestowing boons.

sanskrit: mudgaraśūlacakrābjabhṛtognyādividiksthitāḥ /
english: The images of Agni and other gods bearing the club, trident, disc and lotus should be placed in different directions around.

sanskrit: sūryāryamādirakṣontāś caturhastā dviṣaḍdale //
english: The images of the forms of Sun, commencing with Aryamā are represented as possessing four arms and placed in a diagram of twelve petals.

sanskrit: varuṇaḥ sūryanāmā ca sahasrāṃśus tathāparaḥ / dhātā tapanasañjñaś ca savitātha gabhastikaḥ // raviś caivātha parjanyastvaṣṭā mitrotha viṣṇukaḥ / meṣādirāśisaṃsthāś ca mārgādikārttikāntakāḥ //
english: Varuṇa, Sūrya, Sahasrāṃśu one who has thousand rays, Dhātṛ, Tapana, Sāvitṛ, Gabhastika, Ravi, Parjanya, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra and Viṣṇu are his different names as he moves over the zodiacal signs commencing with the Aries in the course of months commencing with Mārgaśīrṣa and ending with Kārttika.

sanskrit: dhūmro nīlaḥ kramādvarṇāḥ śaktayaḥ keśarāgragāḥ / iḍā suṣumnā viśvārcirindusañjñā pramardinī // praharṣiṇī mahākālī kapilā ca prabodhanī / nīlāmbarā ghanāntasthā amṛtākhyā ca śaktayaḥ //
english: Their female energies known by the namesIḍā, Suṣmnā, Viśvārcis, Indu, Pramardinī, Praharṣaṇī, Mahākālī, Kapilā, Prabodhanī, Nīlāmbarā, Ghanāntasthā and Amṛtā, and placed at the ends of petals are of black, red, pale red, yellow, pale yellow, white, brown, yellow, green, white, grey and blue.

sanskrit: varuṇādeś ca tadvarṇāḥ keśarāgreṣu vinyaset /
english: Similar colours are given to Varuṇa and others placed at the tips of petals.

sanskrit: tejaś caṇḍo mahāvakro dvibhujaḥ padmakhadgabhṛt //
english: The form of Tejas effulgence should be represented as fierce, extremely crooked, possessing two arms holding a lotus and sword.

sanskrit: kuṇḍikājapyāmālīnduḥ kujaḥ śaktyakṣamālikaḥ / budhaścāpākṣapāṇiḥ syājjīvaḥ kuṇḍyakṣamālikaḥ //
english: The figure of Mercury should be holding the bow and rosary in his hands. The form of Jupiter should be holding the sacrificial pitcher and rosary. The image of Venus may be holding the sacrificial pitcher and rosary.

sanskrit: śukraḥ kuṇḍyakṣamālī syāt kiṇkiṇīsūtravāñchaniḥ / ardhacandradharo rāhuḥ ketuḥ khaḍgī ca dīpabhṛt //
english: That of Saturn should be endowed with a girdle of bells. While that of Rāhu the ascending node of the moon considered as a planet is represented as holding half of the lunar disc, that of Ketu the descending node of the moon considered as a planet is represented as holding the sword and lamp.

sanskrit: anantastakṣakaḥ karkaḥ padmo mahābjaḥ śaṅkhakaḥ / kulikaḥ sūtriṇaḥ sarve phaṇavaktrā mahāprabhāḥ //
english: The serpents Ananta, Takṣaka, Karka, Padma, Mahābja and Śaṅkha are all represented as having hooded heads with great radiance.

sanskrit: indro vajrī gajārūḍhaśchāgagogniś ca śaktimān / yamo daṇḍī ca mahiṣe nairṛtaḥ khaḍgavān kare //
english: The image of Indra is endowed with thunderbolt and as seated on an elephant, that of Agni as riding a goat and holding a spear, that of Yama as on a buffalo and carrying a club and that of Nirṛti as holding a sword.

sanskrit: makare varuṇaḥ pāśī vāyurdhvajadharo mṛge / gadī kuvero meṣastha īśānaś ca jaṭī vṛṣe //
english: The image of Varuṇa ocean god is made as seated on a crocodile and as holding a noose, that of Vāyu wind god as riding an antelope and holding a banner, that of Kubera god of wealth as seated on a sheep and bearing a mace, and that of Īśāna as seated on a bull and having a matted hair.

sanskrit: dvibāhavo lokapālā viśvakarmākṣasūtrabhṛt /
english: The images of the guardian deities of the quarters of the world are endowed with two arms.

sanskrit: hanūmān vajrahastaḥ syāt padbhyāṃ sampīḍitāśrayaḥ //
english: The figure of Hanūmat monkey, devoted to Rāma may be holding the thunderbolt in his hand and pounding the earth with his feet.

sanskrit: vīṇāhastāḥ kinnarāḥ syurmālāvidyādharāś ca khe /
english: The semidivine beings Kinnaras may be represented as holding lutes in their arms and the Vidyādharas semidivine beings as having garlands and moving in the sky.

sanskrit: durbalāṅgāḥ piśācāḥ syurvetālā vikṛtānanāḥ / kṣetrapālāḥ śūlavantaḥ pretā mahodarāḥ kṛśāḥ //
english: The goblins may be represented as having emaciated bodies and the vampires as deformed faces, the Guardians of the sites as having the tridents and the spirits of the dead people as lean and bigbellied.

sanskrit: yoginyaṣṭāṣṭakaṃ vakṣye aindrādīśāntataḥ kramāt /
english: shall describe the characteristics of the eight Yoginis female attendants on Durgā respectively residents of the eight quarters east to northeast.

sanskrit: akṣobhyā rūkṣakarṇo ca rākṣasī kṛpaṇākṣayā //
english: The Yoginīs Akṣobhyā, Rūkṣakarṇī, Rākṣasi, Kṛpaṇā and Akṣayā reside in the east.

sanskrit: piṅgākṣī ca kṣayā kṣemā ilā līlālayā tathā / lolā laktā balākeśī lālasā vimalā punaḥ //
english: The Yoginīs Piṅgākṣī, Kṣayā, Kṣemā, Ilā, Līlā, Layā, Laktā, Balākeśī, Lālasā and Vimalā dwell in the southeast.

sanskrit: hutāśā ca viśālākṣī huṅkārā vaḍavāmukhī / mahākrūrā krodhanā tu bhayaṅkarī mahānanā //
english: The Yoginīs Hutāśā, Viśālākṣī, Huṅkārā, Vaḍavāmukhī, Mahākrūrā, Krodhanā, Bhayaṅkarī and Mahānanā are the residents of the south.

sanskrit: sarvajñā taralā tārā ṛgvedā tu hayānanā / sārākhyā rudraśaṅgrāhī sambarā tālajaṅghikā //
english: The Yoginīs Sarvajñā, Taralā, Tārā, Ṛgvedā, Hayānanā, Sārā Sārākhyā, Rudrasaṅgrāhī, Śambarā and Tālajaṅghikā occupy the south west.

sanskrit: raktākṣī suprasiddhā tu vidyujjihvā karaṅkiṇī / meghanādā pracaṇḍogrā kālakarṇī varapradā //
english: Raktākṣī, Suprasiddhā, Vidyujjihvā, Karaṅkiṇī, Meghanādā, Pracaṇḍogrā, Kālakarṇī and Varapradā are the inmates of the west.

sanskrit: candrā candrāvalī caiva prapañcā pralayāntikā / śiśuvaktrā piśācī ca piśitāśā ca lolupā //
english: Candrā, Candrāvalī, Prapañcā, Pralayāntikā, Śiśuvaktrā, Piśācī, Piśitāśā and Lolupā dwell in the northwest.

sanskrit: dhamanī tāpanī caiva rāgiṇī vikṛtānanā / vāyuvegā vṛhatkukṣirvikṛtā viśvarūpikā //
english: Dhamanī, Tāpanī, Rāgiṇī, Vikṛtānanā, Vāyuvegā, Bṛhatkukṣi, Vikṛtā and Viśvarūpikā govern the north.

sanskrit: yamajihvā jayantī ca durjayā ca jayāntikā / viḍālī revatī caiva pūtanā vijayāntikā //
english: Yamajihvā, Jayanti, Durjayā, Jayantikā, Viḍālā, Revatī, Pūtanā and Vijayāntikā hold sway over the northeast.

sanskrit: aṣṭahastāś caturhastā icchāstrāḥ sarvasiddhidāḥ /
english: These Yoginīs should be represented as having eight arms or four arms, wielding weapons of their choice and yielding all benefits on their votaries.

sanskrit: bhairavaścārkahastaḥ syāt kūrparāsyo jaṭendubhṛt // khaḍgāṅkuśakuṭhāreṣuviśvabhayabhṛdekataḥ / cāpatriśūlakhaṭvāṅgapāśakārdhavarodyataḥ // gajacarmadharo dvābhyāṃ kṛttivāsohibhūṣataḥ /
english: Lord Bhairava may hold the arka plant Calotropis gigantee in the hand and have the face like the knee or elbow bearing the matted hair and the Moon. Kṛttivāsas should be represented as holding on one side the sword, goad, axe and arrow and offering protection to the universe and a bow, trident, club with a skull at the top and noose on the other.

sanskrit: pretāśano mātṛmadhye pūjyaḥ pañcānanothavā //
english: Or he shall be having five faces and be wearing the elephant’s hide and adorned by the serpents.

sanskrit: avilomāgniparyantaṃ dīrghāṣṭakaikabheditaṃ / tatṣaḍaṅgāni jātyantair anvitaṃ ca kramād yajet //
english: One has to worship him being endowed with the letters of the alphabet upto the letter ‘ra’ and with his mantra having six constituents and the eight long vowel mantras.

sanskrit: mandirāgnidalārūḍhaṃ suvarṇarasakānvitaṃ / nādavindvandusaṃyuktaṃ mātṛnāthāṅgadīpitaṃ //
english: He is also to be contemplated upon as established in the wicks of the flame in the house as endowed with golden ornaments and the nāda, bindu and indu and making the body of the divine mother and the lord radiant.

sanskrit: vīrabhadro vṛṣārūḍho mātragre sa caturmukhaḥ /
english: Vīrabhadra attendant of Śiva is represented as having four faces, seated on a bull in front of the mother goddesses.

sanskrit: gaurīṃ tu dvibhujā tryakṣā śūlinī darpaṇānvitā //
english: Goddess Gauri consort of Śiva is represented as having two arms and three eyes as endowed with a spear and mirror.

sanskrit: śūlaṃ galantikā kuṇḍī varadā ca caturbhujā / abjasthā lalitā skandagaṇādarśaśalākayā //
english: Goddess Lalitā a form of Durgā should be represented as having tour arms holding a spear, a small pitcher, and another pitcher in the hands and showing boonconferring hands.

sanskrit: caṇḍikā saśahastā syāt khaḍgaśūlāriśaktidhṛk / dakṣe vāme nāgapāśaṃ carmāgkuśakuṭhārakaṃ /
english: She should also be endowed with a mirror, a small stick for applying collyrium and Skanda and Gaṇa Gaṇeśa. Goddess Caṇḍikā may be represented as having ten hands having a sword, spear, disc and dart in the right hand and the magical noose, shield, pike, axe, and bow in the left hand.

sanskrit: dhanuḥ siṃhe ca mahiṣaḥ śūlena prahatogrataḥ //
english: She must be riding a lion with the buffalo demon having been slain with her spear in front of her.

sanskrit: liṅgādilakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye kamalodbhava tacchṛṇu /
english: O Lotusborn Brahman shall describe to you the characteristics of the liṅga and other things.

sanskrit: dairghyārdhaṃ vasubhirbhaktvā tyaktvā bhāgatrayaṃ tataḥ // viṣkambhaṃ bhūtabhāgaistu caturasrantu kārayet / āyāmaṃ mūrtibhirbhaktvā ekadvitrikramān nyaset //
english: Havingmarked a rectangular block of stone as divided into two parts lengthwise, the lower part again being divided into eight parts and three parts of these divisions being left out, the remaining block formed by five parts should be divided breadthwise into three parts and the three gods should be assigned therein.

sanskrit: brahmaviṣṇuśivāṃśeṣu vardhamānoyamucyate /
english: This is spoken as representing the forms of Brahman, Viṣṇu and Śiva among which the last one is larger than the other two parts.

sanskrit: caturasresya varṇārdhaṃ guhyakoṇeṣu lāñchayet //
english: Half of the figure is marked at the angular points in the square.

sanskrit: aṣṭāgraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ bhāgaṃ sidhyatyeva na saṃśayaḥ /
english: An octagonal block known as the part of Viṣṇu is certainly obtained thus.

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśāsraṃ tataḥ kuryāddvātriṃśāsraṃ tataḥ punaḥ //
english: Then a polygon of sixteen sides is made and then a polygon of thirtytwo sides.

sanskrit: catuḥṣaṣṭyasrakaṃ kṛtvā vartulaṃ sādhayettataḥ / kartayedatha liṅgasya śiro vai deśikottamaḥ //
english: Having made a polygon of sixtyfour sides, the circular shape is accomplished. Then the excellent spiritual teacher should chisel the head portion of the emblem.

sanskrit: vistāramatha liṅgasya aṣṭadhā saṃvibhājayet / bhāgārdhārdhantu santyajya cchatrākāraṃ śiro bhavet //
english: The breadth of the liṅga may be divided into eight parts. An umbrellashaped top portion of the liṅga is got by discarding half of this length.

sanskrit: triṣu bhāgeṣu sadṛśamāyāmaṃ yasya cistaraḥ / tadvibhāgasamaṃ liṅgaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradaṃ //
english: A liṅga which has a breadth equal to threefourth of its length bestows all the desired benefits.

sanskrit: dairghyasya tu caturthena viṣkambhaṃ devapūjite /
english: The pillar part of the emblem should be a quarter of the length of the emblem in the case of those worshipped by the celestials.

sanskrit: sarveṣāmeva liṅgānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ śṛṇu sāmprataṃ //
english: Listen now the narration of the characteristics of all liṅgas.

sanskrit: madhyasūtraṃ samāsādya brahmarudrāntikaṃ budhaḥ / ṣoḍaśāṅgulaliṅgasya ṣaḍbhāgair bhājito yathā //
english: The wiseman should divide the liṅga measuring aṅgulas into parts through the central line upto the Brahman and Rudra parts.

sanskrit: tadvaiyamanasūtrābhyāṃ mānamantaramucyate / yavāṣṭamuttare kāryaṃ śeṣāṇāṃ yavahānitaḥ //
english: The spaces in between two such lines of division should measure eight yavas each in the first two cases, each latter measuring a yava less than the preceding one.

sanskrit: adhobhāgaṃ tridhā kṛtvā tvardhamekaṃ parityajet /
english: Having divided the lower part into three parts, one part should be left out.

sanskrit: aṣṭadhā taddvayaṃ kṛtvā ūrdhvabhāgatryaṃ tyajet //
english: Having divided the remaining two parts into eight parts, the three upper ones of these divisions should be left aside.

sanskrit: ūrdhvañca pañcamādbhāgād bhrāmya rekhāṃ pralambayet /
english: Those three sections above the five divisions should be rotated and the markings lengthened.

sanskrit: bhāgamekaṃ parityajya saṅgaṃ kārayettayoḥ //
english: Having left out one part their union should be brought about.

sanskrit: etat sādhāraṇaṃ proktaṃ liṅgānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ mayā / sarvasādhāraṇaṃ vakṣye piṇḍikāntānnibodha me //
english: These are the general characteristics of the liṅga described by me. shall now describe the most general characteristics of the pedestals.

sanskrit: brahmabhāgapraveśañca jñātvā liṅgasya cocchrayaṃ / nyased brahmaśilāṃ vidvān samyakkarmaśilopari //
english: After having known the commencing portion of the liṅga and height, the part belonging to Brahman should be well placed by the learned person on the stone pedestal.

sanskrit: tathā sumucchrayaṃ jñātvā piṇḍikāṃ pravibhājayet /
english: Then having known the height of the liṅga the different dimensions of the pedestal should be made.

sanskrit: dvibhāgamucchritaṃ pīṭhaṃ vistāraṃ liṅgasammitam //
english: The base of the liṅga should be twice the height and length commensurate with that of the liṅga.

sanskrit: tribhāgaṃ madhyataḥ khātaṃ kṛtvā pīṭhaṃ vibhājayet /
english: The central part of the pedestal should be hewn and divided into three parts.

sanskrit: svamānārdhatribhāgeṇa bāhulyaṃ parikalpayet //
english: Its breadth should be onesixth part of its length.

sanskrit: bāhulyasya tribhāgeṇa mekhalāmatha kalpayet / khātaṃ syānmekhalātulyaṃ kramānnimnantu kārayet //
english: The girth should measure onethird part of its breadth, and the depth of cavity should be equal to that of the girth. It should be sloping gradually.

sanskrit: mekhalāṣoḍaśāṃśena khātaṃ vā tatpramāṇajñaḥ /
english: Or the depth of the cavity should be one sixteenth part of that of the girth.

sanskrit: ucchrāyaṃ tasya pīṭhasya vikārāṅgaṃ tu kārayet // bhūmau praviṣṭamekaṃ tu bhāgaikena piṇḍikā /
english: The height of the base should be deviated. One part of the base should remain imbedded in the ground. One part of it will be the height of the stool proper.

sanskrit: kaṇṭhaṃ bhāgaistribhiḥ kāryaṃ bhāgenaikena paṭṭikā //
english: Three such parts will be the height of the neck portion.

sanskrit: dyaṃgena cordhvapaṭṭantu ekāṃśāḥ śeṣapaṭṭikā / bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ praviṣṭantu yāvat kaṇṭhaṃ tataḥ punaḥ //
english: The first step should be one such part. The second step should be of two such parts in height while the remaining steps should have a height of such a single part until one reaches the neck portion step by step.

sanskrit: nirgamaṃ bhāgamekaṃ tu yāvadvai śeṣapaṭṭikā /
english: Outlets to the breadth of such a part should be set apart on each one of the steps till the last one.

sanskrit: praṇālasya tribhāgena nirgamastu tribhāgataḥ //
english: They should be cut into three parts by the three outlets.

sanskrit: mūleṅgulyagravistāramagre tryaṃśena cārdhataḥ /
english: It should measure a tip of the finger in breadth at the base and onesixth of a finger at their ends.

sanskrit: īṣannimnantu kurvīta khātaṃ taccottareṇa vai /
english: Their beds should be a little inclined towards the eastern side.

sanskrit: piṇḍikāsahitaṃ liṅgametat sādhāraṇaṃ smṛtam //
english: These are considered to be the general characteristics of the liṅga along with the pedestal.

sanskrit: vakṣyāmyanyaprakāreṇa liṅgamānādikaṃ śṛṇu /
english: shall describe the measurement of the liṅga in a different way. Listen.

sanskrit: vakṣye lavaṇajaṃ liṅgaṃ ghṛtajaṃ buddhivardhanam // bhūtaye vastraliṅgantu liṅgantātkālikaṃ viduḥ /
english: shall now speak about the liṅgas made of salt, and ghee which when worshipped increases one’s intellect. A liṅga made of cloth is worshipped for the sake of wealth. It is known as temporal.

sanskrit: pakvāpakvaṃ mṛṇmayaṃ syādapakvāt pakvajaṃ varaṃ //
english: The one made of earth is either burnt or half burnt of which the former is better.

sanskrit: tato dārumayaṃ puṇyaṃ dārujāt śailajaṃ varaṃ / śailādvaraṃ tu muktājaṃ tato lauhaṃ suvarṇajaṃ //
english: Then, one made of wood is meritorious. One made of stone is more meritorious than that made of wood. The liṅga made of pearl is more meritorious than that of stone. Then relatively meritworthy are the liṅgas made of iron, and gold.

sanskrit: rājataṃ kīrtitaṃ tāmraṃ paittalaṃ bhuktimuktidaṃ / raṅgajaṃ rasaliṅgañca bhuktimuktipradaṃ varaṃ //
english: The liṅgas made of silver, copper and brass yield enjoyment and release from bondage. The liṅgas made of red lead and mercury are excellent and confer enjoyment and release from bondage.

sanskrit: rasajaṃ rasalohādiratnagarbhantu vardhayet / mānādi neṣṭaṃ siddhādi sthāpitetha svayambhuvi //
english: The installation of a liṅga on the earth made of mercury and iron etc or studded with gems increases one’s glory and grants success as desired.

sanskrit: vāme ca svecchayā teṣāṃ pīṭhaprāsādakalpanā /
english: If desired one can build temples and bases to these emblems on the left side.

sanskrit: pūjayet sūryavimbasthaṃ darpaṇe prativimbitaṃ //
english: One may worship the image of the sun cast on the mirror.

sanskrit: pūjye harastu sarvatra liṅge pūrṇārcanaṃ bhavet /
english: Hara should be worshipped everywhere. The worship gets completed only by the worship of the liṅga.

sanskrit: hastottaravidhaṃ śailaṃ dārujaṃ tadvadeva hi //
english: A liṅga made of stone or wood should be of a cubit length.

sanskrit: calamaṅgulamānena dvāragarbhakaraiḥ sthitam / aṅgulād gṛhaliṅgaṃ syādyāvat pañcaśāṅgulaṃ //
english: The movable liṅga should be of the size of a finger and encircled by the adytum. The liṅga worshipped in the house should be of the size of one to fifteen fingers.

sanskrit: dvāramānāt trisaṅkhyākaṃ navadhā garbhamānataḥ / navadhā garbhamānena liṅgandhāmni ca pūjayet //
english: The liṅgas are classified into three groups according to the measure of the doorway or into nine groups according to the measure of the adytum. These liṅgas should be worshipped in one’s residence.

sanskrit: evaṃ liṅgāni ṣaṭtriṃśat jñeyāni jyeṣṭhamānataḥ / madhyamānena ṣaṭtriṃśat ṣaṭtriṃśadadhamena ca //
english: Thus there are thirtysix liṅgas in the first class, thirtysix in the second class and thirtysix in the third class.

sanskrit: itthamaikyena liṅgānāṃ śatamaṣṭottaraṃ bhavet /
english: Thus totally there would be one hundred and eight liṅgas.

sanskrit: ekāṅgulādipañcāntaṃ kanyasañcalamucyate //
english: The liṅgas measuring one to five fingers known as the short are said to be movable.

sanskrit: ṣadvādidaśaparyantañcalaṃ liṅgañca madhyamaṃ /
english: The movable liṅgas measuring six to ten fingers are known as middle.

sanskrit: ekādaśāṅgulādi syāt jyeṣṭhaṃ pañcadaśāntakam //
english: Those measuring eleven to fifteen fingers are known as the best.

sanskrit: ṣaḍaṅgulaṃ mahāratnai ratnair anyair navāṅgulam /
english: Those made of excellent gems should measure six fingers. Those made of other gems should measure nine fingers.

sanskrit: ravibhirhemabhārotthaṃ liṅgaṃ śeṣaistripañcabhiḥ //
english: The rest of the liṅgas should be fifteen fingers.

sanskrit: dvātriṃśatṣoḍaśāṃśāṃś ca koṇayostu vilopayet // caturniveśanāt kaṇṭho viṃśatistriyugais tathā /
english: The four sets of corners from the top should be successively cut into four or sixteen equal sides, and those again into thirtytwo and sixtyfour in turn so as to make it a polygon of sixtyfour equal sides.

sanskrit: pārśvābhyāṃ tu viluptābhyāṃ calaliṅgaṃ bhavedvaraṃ //
english: The two sides being thus lopped off, the neck of a solid liṅga should be twentysix parts from the rectangular space at its foot.

sanskrit: dhāmno yugartunāgāṃśair dvāraṃ hīnāditaḥ kramāt / liṅgadvārocchrayādarvāg bhavet pādonataḥ kramāt // garbhārdhenādhamaṃ liṅgaṃ bhūtāṃśaiḥ syāt tribhirvaraṃ /
english: The face of the liṅga should gradually be decreasing by four, six and eight parts from its base and similarly the middle part of the liṅga should be gradually less than the height at its beginning by a foot. That which is equal to half the size of the adytum is said to be the lowest variety of liṅga.

sanskrit: tayormadhye ca sūtrāṇi sapta sampātayet samaṃ //
english: Seven equal lines should be drawn in the central portion of these liṅgas.

sanskrit: evaṃ syurnava sūtrāṇi bhūtasūtraiś ca madhyamaṃ /
english: In this way there would be nine lines. The middle variety of liṅga would have five lines.

sanskrit: dvyantaro vāmavāmañca liṅgānāṃ dīrghatā nava // hastādvivardhate hasto yāvatsyur nava pāṇayaḥ /
english: The length of the liṅgas should be nine fingers. The opposite side should be separated by two intermediate links. The liṅga is measured out cubit by cubit till it would be nine hands length.

sanskrit: hīnamadhyottamaṃ liṅgaṃ trividhaṃ trividhātmakam //
english: The liṅga is of three kindsinferior, mediocre and superior.

sanskrit: ekaikaliṅgamadhyeṣu trīṇi trīṇi ca pādaśaḥ / liṅgāni ghaṭayeddhīmān ṣaṭsu cāṣṭottareṣu ca // sthiradīrghaprameyāttu dvāragarbhakarātmikā /
english: A wiseman should mark three liṅgas at the centre of every liṅga foot by foot at fourteen places by a fixed measure of length of the door or the adytum.

sanskrit: catvāri liṅgarūpāṇi viṣkambheṇa tu lakṣayet /
english: Four liṅgas representing Śiva, Viṣṇu, Bṛhaspati proportionately should be marked by the breadth.

sanskrit: dīrghamāyānvitaṃ kṛtvā liṅgaṃ kuryāt trirūpakaṃ //
english: The liṅga should be shaped long to represent the three forms.

sanskrit: caturaṣṭāṣṭavṛttañca tattvatrayaguṇātmakaṃ /
english: The liṅga should have a circumference of four, eight, eight inches representing the three qualities.

sanskrit: liṅgānāmīpsitaṃ dairghyaṃ tena kṛtvāṅgulāni vai // dhvajādyāyaiḥ surair bhūtaiḥ śikhibhirvā haret kṛtiṃ /
english: One should make the liṅgas of such lengths as one desires. One should divide the figure marked by the banners, celestial gods, elements or cocks.

sanskrit: tānyaṅgulāni yaccheṣaṃ lakṣayecca śubhāśubhaṃ //
english: One should know the good or bad from the inches left over.

sanskrit: dhvajādyā dhvajasiṃhebhavṛṣāḥ jyeṣṭhāḥ pare śubhāḥ / svareṣu ṣaḍjagāndhārapañcamāḥ śubhadāyakāḥ //
