english: The orb of wind principle should be conceived as marked with six dots. It should be meditated as composed of tranquility, black in colour and endowed with the principal syllable of hrīṃ and purified by two stretches of retention of breath.

sanskrit: sañcityodghātayugmena pṛthvībhūtaṃ viśodhayet //
english: The principle of earth should be purified.

sanskrit: nabhovindumayaṃ vṛttaṃ vinduśaktivibhūṣitaṃ / vyomākāraṃ suvṛttañca śuddhasphaṭikanirmalaṃ //
english: It should be contemplated as filled in with ether, as of the form of the speck of ether, uniformly circular, spotless like the pure crystal and adorned by the energy of bindu.

sanskrit: hauṅkāreṇa phaḍantena śāntyatītakalāmayaṃ / dhyātvaikodghātayogena suviśuddhaṃ vibhāvayet //
english: After having contemplated on the form of the digit that is beyond tranquility by means of the mantra hauṃ ending with phaṭ, one should contemplate the pure thing by one stretch of retention of breath..

sanskrit: āpyāyayettataḥ sarvaṃ mūlenāmṛtavarṣiṇā / ādhārākhyāmanantañca dharmajñānādipaṅkajaṃ //
english: One should then permeate the lotus or circles such as ādhāra base, ananta endless, dharma righteousness and jñāna knowledge with the shower of ambrosia with the principal mantra.

sanskrit: hṛdāsanamidaṃ dhyātvā mūrtimāvāhayettataḥ / sṛṣṭyā śivamayaṃ tasyāmātmānaṃ dvādaśāntataḥ //
english: After having contemplated this seat of the heart, one should then invoke the form of essence of Śiva placed inside that lotus with twelve petals.

sanskrit: atha tāṃ śaktimantreṇa vauṣaḍantena sarvataḥ / divyāmṛtena samplāvya kurvīta sakalīkṛtaṃ //
english: Then that form should be permeated everywhere with the divine ambrosia with the mantra of the energy ending with vauṣaṭ and the sakalīkaraṇa accomplishing rite should be performed.

sanskrit: hṛdayādikarānteṣu kaniṣṭhādyaṅgulīṣu ca / hṛdādimantravinyāsaḥ sakalīkaraṇaṃ mataṃ //
english: The sakalīkaraṇa is that by which the mantras for the heart etc. are placed in the different parts of the body such as the heart, arms, and the little fingers of the hand.

sanskrit: astreṇa rakṣya prākāraṃ tanmantreṇātha tadvahiḥ / śaktijālamadhaścordhvaṃ mahāmudrāṃ pradarśayet //
english: Having protected the enclosure with the weapon and the outer place with its mantra the mahāmudrā consisting of the energy should be shown below and above that.

sanskrit: āpadamastakaṃ yāvad bhāvapuṣpaiḥ śivaṃ hṛdi / padme yajet pūrakeṇa ākṛṣṭāmṛtasadghṛtaiḥ // śivamantrair nābhikuṇḍe tarpayeta śivānalaṃ /
english: One should worship Śiva in the lotus in the heart from head to foot with the retention of breath and with the flowers of one’s own feeling. One should then offer the clarified butter of ambrosia to the fire of Śiva in the sacred pit of the navel with the mantras of Śiva.

sanskrit: lalāṭe vindurūpañca cintayecchubhavigrahaṃ //
english: One should contemplate the white figure of the form of bindu on the forehead.

sanskrit: ekaṃ svarṇādipātrāṇāṃ pātramastrāmbuśodhitaṃ / vinduprasūtapīyūṣarūpatoyākṣatādinā //
english: One of the vessels among the golden pitchers, should be purified by water of nectar got from the speck and by unbroken rice.

sanskrit: hṛdāpūrya ṣaḍaṅgena pūjayitvābhimantrayet /
english: Having filled the vessel with the six constituents and after having worshipped it, it should be consecrated.

sanskrit: saṃrakṣya heti mantreṇa kavacena viguṇṭhayet //
english: After having protected it with the mantra hā one should cover it with the armour.

sanskrit: racayitvārghyamaṣṭāṅgaṃ secayeddhenumudrayā / abhiṣiñcedathātmānaṃ mūrdhni tattoyavindunā //
english: After having made ready the water of offering, one should sprinkle the eight constituents with water by showing the dhenumudrā a particular form of intertwining the fingers representing the cow.

sanskrit: tatrasthaṃ yāgasambhāraṃ prokṣayedastravāriṇā / abhimantrya hṛdā piṇḍaistanutrāṇena veṣṭayet //
english: One should sprinkle water of the weapon on the materials of worship kept there. One should then encircle them with the armour of piṇḍa with the hṛt mantra.

sanskrit: darśayitvāmṛtāṃ mudrāṃ puṣpaṃ datvā nijāsane / vidhāya tilakaṃ mūrdhni puṣpaṃ mūlena yojayet // snāne devārcane home bhojane yāgayogayoḥ / āvaśyake jape dhīraḥ sadā vācaṃyamo bhavet //
english: After having shown the amṛtā mudrā formation with fingers denoting nondecay and putting flower on its seat and a mark on the forehead consecrated by the principal mantra of the god a bold man should remain perfectly silent at the time of bathing, worship of the god, offering oblation unto fire, eating, practising yoga and repetition of necessary mantras.

sanskrit: nādāntoccāraṇānmantraṃ śodhayitvā susaṃskṛtaṃ / pūjane 'bhyarcya gāyatryā sāmānyārghyamupāharet //
english: The mantra should be purified by pronouncing the nāda oṃ at the end. That purified mantra should then be used in the worship along with the gāyatrī mantra and the general water of oblation should be offered.

sanskrit: brahmapañcakamāvartya mālyamādāya liṅgataḥ / aiśānyāndiśi caṇḍāya hṛdayena nivedayet // prakṣālya piṇdikāliṅge astratoye tato hṛdā / arghyapātrāmbunā siñcediti liṅgaviśodhanaṃ //
english: After having repeated the brahmapañcaka, the worshipper should collect the garland from the liṅga and offer it to Caṇḍa in the northeastern direction. The purification of the liṅga consists in the washing of the pedestal and the liṅga with the water consecrated by the mantra of weapon and hṛdmantra and sprinkle with the water for washing from the vessel of arghya.

sanskrit: ātamadravyamantraliṅgaśuddhau sarvān surānyajet /
english: All the celestials should be worshipped for the purification of the self, the materials, the mantra and the liṅga.

sanskrit: vāyavye gaṇapataye hāṃ gurubhyo 'rcayecchive //
english: Hāṃ, Salutations to God Gaṇapati in the northwestern direction. One should pay obeisance to the preceptor in the northeast.

sanskrit: ādhāraśaktimaṅkuranibhāṃ kūrmaśilāsthitāṃ / yajed brahmaśilārūḍhaṃ śivasyānantamāsanaṃ // vicitrakeśaprakhyānamanyonyaṃ pṛṣṭadarśinaḥ / kṛtatretādirūpeṇa śivasyāsanapādukāṃ //
english: One should worship the goddess of the seat of the god in the kūmaśilā the tortoise form on the stone as possessing complexion of the tender shoots and the seat of Śiva known as ananta endless should be worshipped as seated on the brahmaśilā along with the attendants of the god such as Vicitrakeśa, Kṛta and Tretā who form the seat and shoes as they were of divinity.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ jñānañca vairāgyamaiśvaryañcāgnidiṅmukhān / kūrpārakuṅkumasvarṇakajjalābhān yajet kramāt //
english: Then the worshipper should worship righteousness, knowledge, detachment and prosperity, towards the southeast as possessing the hues of camphor, saffron, gold and collyrium respectively.

sanskrit: padmañca karṇikāmadhye pūrvādau madhyato nava /
english: At the centre of the lotusshaped diagram and in its petals in the east etc.

sanskrit: varadābhayahastāś ca śaktayo dhṛtacāmarāḥ // vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrī ca kālī kalavikāriṇī / balavikaraṇī pūjyā balapramathanī kramāt //
english: one should worship the energy goddessesVāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, Kālī, Kālavikariṇī, Balavikaraṇī and Balapramathanī in order as holding the chowries and as conferring boons and offering protection.

sanskrit: hāṃ sarvabhūtadamanī keśarāgre manonmanī / kṣittyādi śuddhavidyāntu tattvavyāpakamāsanaṃ //
english: One should worship the goddessesHāṃ, salutations to Sarvabhūtadamanī, salutations to Manonmanī, to Kṣiti, to Śuddhavidyā at the extremities of the petals of the lotus diagram as also the seat as spread over the component parts of the universe.

sanskrit: nyaset siṃhāsane devaṃ śuklaṃ pañcamukhaṃ vibhuṃ / daśabāhuṃ ca khaṇḍenduṃ dadhānandakṣiṇaiḥ karaiḥ // śaktyṛṣṭiśūlakhaṭvāṅgavaradaṃ vāmakaiḥ karaiḥ /
english: The lord of white complexion, possessing five faces and ten arms, allpervasive, bearing the crescent moon and carrying weaponsspear, sword, lance, and staff in the right hands and a drum, citron, blue lotus, a string and a waterlily in the left hands should be located on the lionseat.

sanskrit: dvātriṃśallakṣaṇopetāṃ śaivīṃ mūrtintu madhyataḥ /
english: The image of Śiva possessing thirtytwo characteristics should be installed at the centre.

sanskrit: hāṃ haṃ hāṃ śivamūrtaye svaprakāśaṃ śivaṃ smaran // brahmādikāraṇatyāgānmantraṃ nītvā śivāspadaṃ /
english: Hāṃ, haṃ, hāṃ salutations to the image of Śiva. After having meditated upon the selfluminant Śiva, the mantra should be led to the spot sacred to Śiva after leaving below the place sacred to Brahmā.

sanskrit: tato lalātamadhyasthaṃ sphurattārāpatiprabhaṃ // ṣaḍaṅgena samākīrṇaṃ vindurūpaṃ paraṃ śivaṃ / puṣpāñjaligataṃ dhyātvā lakṣmīmūrtau niveśayet //
english: Then the worshipper having meditated upon that Supreme form of Śiva, effulgent with the splendour of the moon, as a luminous point at the middle of the forehead and being invested with the six constituents, with flowers in folded palms, should deposit those flowers on the form of Goddess Lakṣmī.

sanskrit: oṃ hāṃ hauṃ śivāya nama āvāhanyā hṛddā tataḥ /
english: Oṃ, hāṃ, hauṃ salutations to Śiva. The deity should be invoked with the invoking hṛd mantra.

sanskrit: āvāhya sthāpya sthāpanyā sannidhāyāntikaṃ śivaṃ // nirodhayenniṣṭhurayā kālakāntyā phaḍantataḥ / vighnānutsārya viṣṭhyātha liṅgamudrāṃ namaskṛtiṃ //
english: Having established Śiva with the sthāpanī mudrā, and placed near that should be checked with Niṣṭhurā and Kālakāntī concluding with phaṭ. After having removed obstructions by sending them away and making obeisance by showing the liṅgamudrā, it should be covered with the hṛd mantra.

sanskrit: hṛdāvaguṇṭhayet paścādāvāhaḥ sammukhī tataḥ /
english: The invocation should follow it. Then standing in front of the image heshould repeat.

sanskrit: niveśanaṃ sthāpanaṃ syātsannidhānaṃ tavāsmi bhoḥ //
english: “Let you be located and firmly established. O lord! am in your presence.”

sanskrit: ākarmakāṇḍaparyantaṃ sannedheyoparikṣayaḥ / svabhakteś ca prakāśoyastadbhavedavaguṇṭhanaṃ //
english: The rite of avaguṇṭhana signifies the presence and supervision of the God and the exhibition of one’s devotion to the God from the commencement to the end of the act.

sanskrit: sakalīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā mantraiḥ ṣaḍbhirathaikatāṃ / aṅgānāmaṅginā sārdhaṃ vidadhyādamṛtīkṛtaṃ //
english: After having done the accomplishing act with the six mantras, the rite of amṛtīkaraṇa should be performed by mentioning different parts of the body along with the body.

sanskrit: cicchaktihṛdayaṃ śambhoḥ śiva aiśvaryamaṣṭadhā / śikhāvaśitvaṃ cābhedyaṃ tejaḥ kavacamaiśvaraṃ //
english: The worshipper should permeate his heart with the energy of consciousness of Śambhu Śiva. Similarly, he should. contemplate the tuft of hair of Śiva as formed of the eightfold glories.

sanskrit: pratāpo duḥsahaścāstramantarāyāpahārakaṃ / namaḥ svadhā ca svāhā ca vauṣaṭ ceti yathākramaṃ //
english: The worshipper should contemplate the invincible energy of God as forming his armour, the unbearable prowess of God which removes all impediments and the words salutations, svadhā, svāhā and vauṣaṭ should be appended in.

sanskrit: hṛtpuraḥsaramuccārya pādyādīni nivedayet /
english: order. The water for washing the feet should be offered preceded by the recitation of the hṛd mantra.

sanskrit: pādyaṃ pādāmbujadvandve vaktreṣvācamanīyakaṃ // arghyaṃ śirasi devasya dūrvāpuṣpākṣatāni ca /
english: The water should be offered at the lotus feet and the water for the rinsing of the mouth at the face of the image, the respectful offering at the head of the lord along with the dūrvā grass, flowers and unbroken rice.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃskṛtya saṃskārair daśabhiḥ parameśvaraṃ // yajet pañcopacāreṇa vidhinā kusumādibhiḥ /
english: Having purified the supreme lord with the ten purifications thus, one should worship with the five kinds of services such as the flowers etc. as laid down in the code books.

sanskrit: arghyodavindupuṣpādyair gaḍḍūkaiḥ snāpayecchanaiḥ / payodadhighṛtakṣaudraśarkarādyair anukramāt //
english: Having sprinkled and rubbed the image with salt, mustard seed etc., it should be slowly bathed with drops of water, flowers, perfumes, milk, curd, ghee, honey and sugar successively.

sanskrit: īśādimantritardravyair arcya teṣāṃ viparyayaḥ /
english: The defects in the above materials should be rectified by worshipping with materials along with the recitation of Īśa mantras.

sanskrit: toyadhūpāntaraiḥ sarvair mūlena snapayecchivaṃ // virūkṣya yavacūrṇena yatheṣṭaṃ śītalair jalaiḥ / svaśaktyā gandhatoyena saṃsnāpya śucivāsasā //
english: Lord Śiva should be bathed with water and fragrance with the principal mantra. Having applied the paste of barley, it should be bathed copiously with cold water and also with fragrant water according to one’s ability.

sanskrit: nirmārjyārghyaṃ pradadyācca nopari bhrāmayet karaṃ / na śūnyamastakaṃ liṅgaṃ puṣpaiḥ kuryāttato dadet //
english: Having wiped it dry with a clean cloth, the preliminary offering of water should be given. The hand should not be moved over the head of the image. The liṅga should never be left without any flower on its head.

sanskrit: candanādyaiḥ samālabhya puṣpaiḥ prārcya śivāṇunā / dhūpabhājanamastreṇa prokṣyābhyarcya śivāṇunā // astreṇa pūjitāṃ ghaṇṭāṃ cādāya guggulaṃ dadet /
english: Having smeared it with sandal etc. and worshipped with flowers with the mantras of Śiva, the vessel for holding the perfumes should be consecrated with the weapons mantra and worshipped with the mantras of Śiva. The bell consecrated by the weapon mantra should be taken and the incense should be offered.

sanskrit: dadyādācamanaṃ paścāt svadhāntaṃ hṛdayāṇunā // ārātrikaṃ samuttārya tathaivācāmayet punaḥ /
english: The water for rinsing should be given then with the repetition of svadhā at the end and with the hṛd mantra. Having shown light for the idol in the night, then water for rinsing should be offered.

sanskrit: praṇamyādāya devājñāṃ bhogāṅgāni prapūjayet //
english: After having made obeisance to god and taking his permission, eatables and other articles of enjoyment should be offered.

sanskrit: hṛdagnau candrabhaṃ caiśe śivaṃ cāmīkaraprabhaṃ / śikhāṃ raktāñca nairṛtye kṛṣṇaṃ varma ca vāyave //
english: The heart should be worshipped in the southeast, the moon on the northeast, the goldencoloured Śiva together with the tuft and blood on the southwest, Kṛṣṇa and armour on the northwest.

sanskrit: caturvaktraṃ caturbāhuṃ dalasthān pūjayedimān /
english: These gods having four faces and four arms should be worshipped in the petals in the east etc.

sanskrit: daṃṣṭrākarālamapyastraṃ pūrvādau vajrasannibhaṃ //
english: along with the divine weapon similar to thunder and fierce teeth.

sanskrit: mūle hauṃ śivāya namaḥ oṃ hāṃ hūṃ hīṃ hoṃ śiraś ca / hṛṃ śikhāyai haiṃ varma haścāstraṃ parivārayutāya ca //
english: Hauṃ salutations to Śiva at the base, Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ hīṃ hoṃ in the head, hṛṃ to the tuft, haiṃ to the armour, haḥ to the weapons and to one with the attendants.

sanskrit: śivāya dadyāt pādyañca ācāmañcārghyameva ca / gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpadīpaṃ naivedyācamanīyakaṃ //
english: Waters for washing the feet, for rinsing the mouth and respectful offering, perfumes, flowers, incense, lamp, food offerings and water for rinsing again, should be given to lord Śiva.

sanskrit: karodvartanatāmbūlaṃ mukhavāsañca darpaṇaṃ / śirasyāropya devasya dūrvākṣatapavitrakaṃ //
english: Intertwined blades of kuśa and unbroken rice should be placed on the head of the image of the lord. Perfumes, betel, piece of cloth for wiping the face and a mirror should also be offered to the deity.

sanskrit: mūlamaṣṭaśataṃ japtvā hṛdayenābhimantritaṃ / carmaṇāveṣṭitaṃ khaḍgaṃ rakṣitaṃ kuśapuṣpakaiḥ // akṣatair mudrāyā yuktaṃ śivamudbhavasañjñayā / guhyātiguhyaguptyarthaṃ gṛhāṇāsmatkṛtaṃ japaṃ //
english: After having repeated the principal mantra eight hundred times, the sword of the lord covered by the sheath, protected by the kuśa and flowers and consecrated by hṛd mantra along with the unbroken rice and with the udbhava mudrā a formation made with the fingers indicating generation. O most mysterious! Accept this repetition of mantra for our welfare.

sanskrit: siddhirbhavatu me yena tvatprasādāttvayi sthite /
english: “May there be success for me by this by your presence here”.

sanskrit: bhogī ślokaṃ paṭhitvādyaṃ dakṣahastena śambhave // mūlāṇunārghyatoyena varahaste nivedayet /
english: Having recited this verse at first, the worshipper should offer to Śambhu Śiva the waters of respect with the right hand with the repetition of the principal mantra.

sanskrit: yatkiñcit kurmahe deva sadā sukṛtaduskṛtaṃ //
english: Whatever good or bad that may do O lord! let it be cast off from me who am in the region of Śiva.

sanskrit: tanme śivapadasthasya hūṃ kṣaḥ kṣepaya śaṅkara / śivo dātā śivo bhoktā śivaḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat //
english: Hūṃ kṣaḥ O Śaṅkara, Śiva is the giver, Śiva is the enjoyer, Śiva is all this universe.

sanskrit: śivo jayati sarvatra yaḥ śivaḥ sohameva ca /
english: Śiva is victorious everywhere. am identical with Śiva.

sanskrit: ślokadvayamadhītyaivaṃ japaṃ devāya cārpayet //
english: After having repeated these two verses, the japa should be dedicated to the lord.

sanskrit: śivāṅgānāṃ daśāṃśañca datvārghyaṃ stutimācaret / pradakṣiṇīkṛtya nameccāṣṭāṅgañcāṣṭamūrtaye /
english: Having offered the waters of respect, one should adore the deity. After circumambulating the deity, one should bow to the eightformed representing the five elements, sun, moon and yajamāna deity by prostrating the eight limbs touching the ground.

sanskrit: natvā dhyānādibhiś caiva yajeccitre 'nalādiṣu //
english: After salutation the deity should be worshipped in a picture or in the fire by meditation etc.

sanskrit: arghapātrakaro yāyādagnyāgāraṃ susaṃvṛtaḥ / yāgopakaraṇaṃ sarvaṃ divyadṛṣṭyā ca kalpayet //
english: The worshipper should enter another room unseen with the vessel containing water for offering in his hand and should look to the arrangements of the materials essential in the performance of a sacrifice, as it were, with a divine eyesight.

sanskrit: udaṅmukhaḥ kuṇḍamīkṣet praokṣaṇaṃ tāḍanaṃ kuśaiḥ / vidadhyādastramantreṇa varmaṇābhyukṣaṇaṃ mataṃ // khaḍgena khātamuddhāraṃ pūraṇaṃ samatāmapi / kurvīta varmaṇā sekaṃ kuṭṭanantu śarātmanā //
english: The sprinkling and beating the water with the kuśa should be done by repeating the mantra of the weapon and the consecration should be done with the mantra of the armour. The digging out a piece of earth, filling and levelling with the sword should be done with the mantra of the armour and bathing and division into parts should be done with the mantra of the arrow.

sanskrit: sammārjanaṃ samālepaṃ kalārūpaprakalpanaṃ /
english: The rites of cleansing, anointing, fixing the crescent.

sanskrit: trisūtrīparidhānaṃ ca varmaṇābhyarcanaṃ sadā //
english: form, investiture of the sacred thread and worship should be done always by the mantra of the armour.

sanskrit: rekhātrayamudak kuryādekāṃ pūrvānanāmadhaḥ /
english: Three lines should be drawn in the north and one below them should be drawn so as to face the east.

sanskrit: kuśena ca śivāstreṇa yadvā tāsāṃ viparyayaḥ //
english: Whatever defects, in them may be made good by touching them with the kuśa and the astramantra of Śiva.

sanskrit: vajrīkaraṇamantreṇa hṛdā darbhaiś catuṣpathaṃ / akṣapātrantatanutreṇa vinyasedviṣṭaraṃ hṛdā //
english: A quadrilateral figure should be. drawn with the kuśa by the mantras of vajrīkaraṇa establishing.firmly and hṛd. The vessel for the rosaries should be laid with the mantra of the armour.

sanskrit: hṛdā vāgīśvarīṃ tatra īśāmāvāhya pūjayet /
english: The Goddess of speech along with the God should be invoked therein and worshipped.

sanskrit: vahniṃ sadāśrayānītaṃ śuddhapātroparisthitaṃ // kravyādāṃśaṃ parityajya vīkṣaṇādiviśodhitaṃ / audaryaṃ caindavaṃ bhautaṃ ekīkṛtyānalatrayaṃ //
english: The consecrated fire brought from a holy place and placed in a pure receptacle, after leaving aside its parts presided over by the demons and purified by the divine look etc., the three fires audārya, aindava and bhauta should be made into one.

sanskrit: oṃ hūṃ vahnicaitanyāya vahnivījena vinyaset /
english: Oṃ hūṃ salutations to god of fire. The deity should be established with the principal mantra of the fire.

sanskrit: saṃhitāmantritaṃ vahniṃ dhenumudrāmṛtīkṛtaṃ // rakṣitaṃ hetimantreṇa kavacenāvaguṇṭhitaṃ /
english: The fire which has been invoked with the vedic hymns and made immortal by showing the dhenumudrā formation with the fingers representing a cow, and protected by mantras of weapons should be covered by the armour.

sanskrit: pūjitantriḥ paribhrāmya kuṇḍasyordhvaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ //
english: It should be worshipped by waving over the pit thrice and circumambulation.

sanskrit: śivavījamiti dhyātvā vāgīśāgarbhagocare / vāgīśvareṇa devena kṣipyamānaṃ vibhāvayet //
english: Having meditated upon the fire as an element of Lord Śiva, the worshipper should contemplate it as lying dormant in the womb of Goddess of speech and cast by the Lord of speech.

sanskrit: bhūmiṣṭhajānukko mantrī hṛdātmasammukhaṃ kṣipet /
english: The worshipper should have his knees resting on the ground and put the fire in his front with the hṛd mantra.

sanskrit: tato 'ntasthitavījasya nābhideśe samūhanaṃ //
english: Then the seeds of fire in the vicinity should be gathered at the centre.

sanskrit: sambhṛtiṃ paridhānasya śaucamācamanaṃ hṛdā / garbhāgneḥ pūjanaṃ kṛtvā tadrakṣārthaṃ śarāṇunā //
english: The collection of clothes, purification and offering of water for rinsing the mouth should be done with the hṛd mantra. Having worshipped the dormant fire , it should be protected by the recitation of the mantra of the shaft.

sanskrit: badhnīyādgarbhajaṃ devyāḥ kakaṅkaṇaṃ pāṇipallave /
english: The embryo fire should be contemplated as tied around the wrist of the goddess as a bracelet.

sanskrit: garbhādhānāya sampūjya sadyojātena pāvakaṃ //
english: The fire should be worshipped with the sadyojāta mantra for the impregnation.

sanskrit: tato hṛdayamantreṇa juhuyādāhutitrayaṃ /
english: Three oblations to the fire should then be offered with hṛdayamantra.

sanskrit: puṃsavanāya vāmena tṛtīye yāsi pūjayet // āhutitritayaṃ dadyācchirasāmbukaṇānvitaṃ /
english: For the puṃsavana rite for the determination of the sex of the foetus generally performed in the third month it should be worshipped on the left side. Three oblations containing drops of water should be offered with the head.

sanskrit: sīmantonnayanaṃ ṣaṣṭhe māsi sampūjya rūpiṇā //
english: The sīmantonnayana rite parting of the hair on the head performed in the sixth month should be done after having worshipped the fire.

sanskrit: juhuyādāhutīstisraḥ śikhayā śikhayaiva tu / vaktrāṅgakalpanāṃ kuryādvaktrodghāṭananiṣkṛtī // jātakarmanṛkarmabhyāṃ daśame māsi pūrvavat /
english: As before the jātakarma the purificatory rite on the birth of a child and ṛtukarma the rite after the first menses usually performed in the tenth month should be performed by kindling the fire with darbha etc.

sanskrit: vahniṃ sandhukṣya darbhādyaiḥ snānaṃ garbhamalāpahaṃ //
english: Mental bathing should be done to remove tḥe impurities of the pregnancy.

sanskrit: suvarṇabandhanaṃ devyā kṛtaṃ dhyātvā hṛdārcayet /
english: After having mentally contemplated the golden bracelet of the goddess one should worship with the hṛd mantra.

sanskrit: sadyaḥsūtakanāśāya prokṣayedastravāriṇā // kumbhantu vahirastreṇa tāḍayedvarmaṇokṣayet / astreṇottarapūrvāgrānmekhalāsu vahiḥ kuśān // āsthāpya sthāpayetteṣu hṛdā paridhivistaraṃ /
english: The ends of the kuśa which form the boundary of the sacrificial pit and placed on the north and east should be washed with water with the mantra of the weapon. The periphery of a circle around the fire should be determined with the kuśa, previously consecrated with the weapon and hṛd mantra and then the cushions inscribed within it should be spread out by reciting the weapon mantra.

sanskrit: samidhiḥ pañca hotavyāḥ prānte mūle ghṛtaplutāḥ /
english: Five sacrificial sticks dipped in clarified butter should be offered into the fire with the repetition of the principal mantra.

sanskrit: brahmāṇaṃ śaṅkaraṃ viṣṇumanantañca hṛdārcayet //
english: Brahmā, Śaṅkara, Viṣṇu and Ananta should be worshipped with the hṛd mantra.

sanskrit: dūrvākṣataiś ca paryantaṃ paridhisthānanukramāt /
english: The gods located in the periphery of that circle should be worshipped in turn with unbroken rice.

sanskrit: indrādīśānaparyantāntānviṣṭarasthānanukramāt // agnerabhimukhībhūtān nijadikṣu hṛdārcayet / nivārya vighnasaṅghātaṃ vālakaṃ pālayiṣyatha //
english: The gods Indra to Īśāna who are directly facing the fire and are having their places inside the circle should be worshipped in their own regions with the hṛd mantra “Protect this child fire by removing all obstacles, that might befall it.”

sanskrit: śaivīmājñābhimānteṣāṃ śrāvayettadanantaraṃ /
english: One should then make them hear this command of Śiva.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā sruksruvāvūrdhvavadanādhomukhaiḥ kramāt // pratāpyāgnau tridhā darbhamūlamadhyāgrakaiḥ spṛśet /
english: He should then take the sacrificial spoon and the ladle, heat them on the fire and touch them with the base, middle and tips of the darbha with face downwards.

sanskrit: kuśaspṛṣṭapradeśe tu ātmavidyāśivātmakaṃ // kramāttattvatrayaṃ nyasya hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ saṃ ravaiḥ kramāt /
english: In the place touched by the kuśa the three principles relating to the soul, knowledge and Śiva should be located duly with the sounds hāṃ, hrīṃ, hūṃ and saṃ.

sanskrit: sruvi śaktiṃ sruve śambhuṃ vinyasya hṛdayāṇunā // trisūtrīveṣṭitagrīvo pūjitau kusumādibhiḥ / kuśānāmupariṣṭāttau sthāpayitvā svadakṣiṇe //
english: Having located the goddess in the sacrificial spoon and Śambhu Śiva in the sacrificial ladle with the hṛdaya mantra, their necks being girdled with three strings of thread and worshipped with flowers etc., kuśas should be placed on them and they should be placed on the right side.

sanskrit: gavyamājyaṃ samādāya vīkṣaṇādiviśodhitaṃ / svakāṃ brahmamayīṃ mūrtiṃ sañcintyādāya tadghṛtaṃ //
english: Having gathered the clarified butter of the cow that has been purified by looking at it and after having contemplated one’s own Brahma form and carrying that clarified butter, one should wave it over the pit and move it round and round in the southeast.

sanskrit: kuṇḍasyordhvaṃ hṛdāvartya bhrāmayitvāgnigocare / punarviṣṇumayīṃ dhyātvā ghṛtamīśānagocare // dhṛtvādāya kuśāgreṇa svāhāntaṃ śirasāṇunā /
english: Again having contemplated the Viṣṇu form, one should hold the clarified butter and carry it towards the northeast, it should be offered to Viṣṇu into the fire with the tips of the kuśa and with the mantra of the head ending with svāhā.

sanskrit: juhuyādviṣṇave vinduṃ rudrarūpamanantaraṃ //
english: Similarly, one should conceive the form of Rudra Śiva as a point in one’s own navel and meditate.

sanskrit: prādeśamātradarbhābhyāmaṅguṣṭānāmikāgrakaiḥ // dhṛtābhyāṃ sammukhaṃ vahnerastreṇāplavamācaret /
english: One should sprinkle water over that with two kuśas of the length of a span and held with the ring finger and thumb. Water should be sprinkled over the fire in front of the worshipper with the two kuśas held as above accompanied by the mantra of the weapon.

sanskrit: hṛdātmasammukhaṃ tadvat kuryāt samplavanantataḥ //
english: Similarly, the worshipper should again sprinkle water over the fire in front of him with the hṛd mantra.

sanskrit: hṛdālabdhadagdhadarbhaṃ śastrakṣepāt pavitayet / dīptenāparadarbheṇa nivāhyānena dīpayet //
english: The burnt ashes of darbha collected with the hṛd mantra should be purified by striking with the implements and with the other lighted darbha it should be taken out and lighted.

sanskrit: astramantreṇa nirdagdhaṃ vahnau darbhaṃ punaḥ kṣipet /
english: The darbha burnt by the mantra of the weapon should again be thrown into the fire.

sanskrit: kṣiptvā ghṛte kṛtagranthikuśaṃ prādeśasammitaṃ // pakṣadvayamiḍādīnāṃ trayaṃ cājye vibhāvayet / krāmādbhāgatrayādājyaṃ sruveṇādāya homayet //
english: Having put the knotted darbha of the length of a span in the clarified butter, one should contemplate the two for nights, the three arteries iḍā etc. in the clarified butter and offer the clarified butter divided into three parts as oblation unto fire with the sacrificial ladle in order with the syllable sva and hā.

sanskrit: svetyagnau hā ghṛte bhāgaṃ śeṣamājyaṃ kṣipet kramāt / udghāṭanāya netrāṇāṃ agnernetratraye mukhe //
english: Oṃ hāṃ oblation to the gods Agni and Soma. The above oblations should be offered into the fire for the purpose of opening as it were the three eyes of the fire god in his face.

sanskrit: sruveṇa ghṛtapūrṇena caturthīmāhutiṃ yajet /
english: The fourth oblation should be offered with the sacrificial ladle filled with clarified butter.

sanskrit: abhimantrya ṣaḍaṅgena bodhayeddhenumudrayā // avaguṇṭhya tanutreṇa rakṣedājyaṃ śarāṇunā / hṛdājyavinduvikṣepāt kuryādabhyukṣya śodhanaṃ //
english: After having consecrated in the six parts of one’s body, the fire god should be invoked with the dhenumudrā posture with the fingers representing a cow. Having covered it with the armour, the clarified butter should be protected by the mantra of the shaft.

sanskrit: vaktrābhighārasandhānāṃ vaktraikīkaraṇaṃ tathā / ityekaikaghṛtāhutyā kuryādvaktrābhighārakaṃ //
english: Thus with oblations to one by one, one should do the union of the different faces. Oṃ hāṃ oblations to Sadyojāta and Vāmadeva. Oṃ hāṃ oblations to Vāmadeva and Aghora.

sanskrit: itivaktrānusandhānaṃ mantrair ebhiḥ kramāccaret /
english: Thus the union is done in order with the recitation of these mantras.

sanskrit: agrito gatayā vāyuṃ nirṛtādiśivāntayā // vaktrāṇāmekatāṃ kuryāt sruveṇa ghṛtaghārayā /
english: With the flow of ghee from the sacrificial ladle taking it from the fire through the angular points such as northwest, southwest, and ending with northeast, one should unite the faces.

sanskrit: oṃ hāṃ sadyojātavāmadevāghoratatpuruṣeśānebhyaḥ svāhā //
english: Oṃ hāṃ oblations to Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa and Īśāna.

sanskrit: itīṣṭavaktre vaktrāṇāmantarbhāvastadākṛtiḥ //
english: Thus its form and other faces should be contemplated in the face of one’s liking.

sanskrit: īśena vahnimabhyarcya datvāstreṇāhutitrayaṃ / kuryāt sarvātmanā nāma śivāgnistvaṃ hutāśana //
english: Having worshipped the fire in the northeast and offering three oblations with the mantra of the weapon, the worshipper with his entire soul should contemplate“O FireGod! you are the divine essence of Śiva.”

sanskrit: hṛdārcitau visṛṣṭāgnau pitarau vidhipūraṇīṃ / mūlena vauṣaḍantena dadyāt pūrṇāṃ yathāvidhi //
english: Having worshipped the parents with the hṛd mantra and left them aside, the final oblation which concludes the rite should be offered as laid down with the principal mantra ending with vauṣaṭ.

sanskrit: tato hṛdambuje sāṅgaṃ sasenaṃ bhāsuraṃ paraṃ / yajet pūrvavadāvāhya prārthyājñāntarpayecchivaṃ //
english: Then one should worship the resplendent, Supreme God attended upon by the attendants and retinue, after having invoked him in the lotus of his heart as before.

sanskrit: yāgāgniśivayoḥ kṛtvā nāḍīsandhānamātmanā /
english: He should offer waters of oblation to Śiva after having requested his permission.

sanskrit: śaktyā mūlāṇunā homaṃ kuryādaṅgair daśāṃśataḥ // ghṛtasya kārṣiko homaḥ kṣīrasya madhunas tathā /
english: A kārṣika a particular weight of the clarified butter, milk and honey and a śukti twice that of kārṣika of the curd and a handful of sweet porridge should be offered.

sanskrit: śaktimātrāhutirdadhnaḥ prasṛtiḥ pāyasyatu // yathāvat sarvabhakṣāṇāṃ lājānāṃ muṣṭisammitaṃ /
english: The worshipper should offer as deemed fit the oblation with all the eatables, a handful of fried grains, three pieces of roots and an equal number of fruits.

sanskrit: grāsārdhamātramannānāṃ sūkṣmāṇi pañca homayet / ikṣorāparvikaṃ mānaṃ latānāmaṅguladvayaṃ //
english: Five halfmouthfuls of cooked rice, bits of sugarcane of the length of a span and stems of sacrificial creepers measuring two fingers in length should be offered into the fire.

sanskrit: puṣpaṃ patraṃ svamānena samidhāṃ tu daśāṅgulaṃ /
english: The oblations of flowers and leaves should be according to their own measure. The sacrificial twigs should measure ten fingers in length.

sanskrit: candracandanakāśmīrakastūrīyakṣakardamān //
english: The camphor, sandal, saffron, musk and an ointment made of camphor, aggallochum and kakkola in equal parts should also be offered.

sanskrit: kalāyasammitānenān guggulaṃ vadarāsthivat / kandānāmaṣṭamaṃ bhāgaṃ juhuyādvidhivat paraṃ //
english: The worshipper should make an oblation of the kalāya a leguminous seed and guggulu a fragrant gumresin of the size of the kernel of the jujube fruit and eight parts of the roots as laid down.

sanskrit: homaṃ nirvartayedevaṃ brahmavījapadaistataḥ / ghṛtena sruci pūrṇāyāṃ nidhāyādhomukhaṃ sruvaṃ //
english: The oblation should thus be completed with the principal mantra brahmabīja oṃ with sacrificial ladles filled with clarified butter holding the ladle in such a way as to have its cup part downwards.

sanskrit: srugagre puṣpamāropya paścādvāmena pāṇinā / punaḥ savyena tau dhṛtvā śaṅkhasannibhamudrayā // samudgato ardhakāyaś ca samapādaḥ samitthitaḥ /
english: Having placed a flower at the head of the spoon and then holding it first with the left hand and then with the right band and showing the mudrā denoting the conch he should stand up half erect with feet evenly placed and eyes fixed upon the end of the ladle and holding the base of ladle pressed against his navel.

sanskrit: brahmādikāraṇātyāgādviniḥsṛtya suṣumṇayā / vāmastanāntamānīya tayormūlamatandritaḥ // mūlamantramavispaṣṭaṃ vauṣaḍantaṃ samuccaret /
english: Then one should rouse up the stream of his pure consciousness through the suṣumnā nerve centre below the spiral chord and carry it to the base of his left breast vigilantly and tell the principal mantra ending with the vauṣaṭ in a low tone.

sanskrit: tadagnau juhuyādājyaṃ yavasammitadhārayā //
english: The clarified butter should be offered having a flow of the measure of the barley.

sanskrit: ācāmaṃ candanaṃ datvā tāmbūlaprabhṛtīnapi /
english: Water for rinsing the mouth, sandal, betals etc. should be offered.

sanskrit: bhaktyā tadbhūtimāvandya vidadhyātpraṇatiṃ parāṃ //
english: The worshipper should meditate in his greatness with devotion and then offer salutation.

sanskrit: tato vahniṃ samabhyarcya paḍantāstreṇa saṃvarān / saṃhāramudrayāhṛtya kṣamasvetyabhidhāya ca // bhāsurān paridhīstāṃś ca pūrakeṇa hṛdāṇunā / śraddhayā parayātmīye sthāpayeta hṛdambuje //
english: After having worshipped the fire well with the mantra of the weapon ending with phaṭ and showing the saṃhāra mudrā the posture of the fingers conveying destruction and uttering Pardon me, the gods who reside in the periphery of the mystic circle should be placed in the lotus of the heart with extreme devotion with the hṛd mantra after taking a breath.

sanskrit: sarvapākāgramādāya kṛtvā maṇḍalakadvayaṃ /
english: All the edibles got ready for the worship should be taken and kept in two circular diagrams.

sanskrit: antarvahirbaliṃ dadyādāgneyyāṃ kuṇḍasannidhau //
english: Offerings should be done both inside and outside in the vicinity of sacrificial pit in the southeast.

sanskrit: oṃ hāṃ rudrebhyaḥ svāhā pūrve mātṛbhyo dakṣiṇe tathā /
english: Oṃ hāṃ oblations to Rudras in the east and in the same way to the mothers in the south.

sanskrit: vāruṇe hāṃ gaṇebhyaś ca svāhā tebhyastvayaṃ baliḥ //
english: Hāṃ, oblations to the gaṇas on the west. This offering is for them.

sanskrit: uttare hāñca yakṣebhya īśāne hāṃ grahebhya u / agnau hāmasurebhyaś ca rakṣobhyo nairṛte baliḥ //
english: And hāṃ to the yakṣas on the north, hāṃ to the planets on the northeast, hāṃ to the asuras on the southeast, hāṃ oblations to the rākṣasas in the southwest.

sanskrit: vāyavye hāñca nāgebhyo nakṣatrebhyaś ca madhyataḥ / hāṃ rāśibhyaḥ svāhā vahnau viśvebhyo nairṛte yathā //
english: And hāṃ to the nāgas on the northwest, and to the stars at the centre. Hāṃ oblations to the constellations in the southeast, and then to the Viśve Viśvedevas in the southwest.

sanskrit: vāruṇyāṃ kṣetrapālāya antarbalirudāhṛtaḥ /
english: It is said that the offering for the guardian of the ground is inside and outside in the west.

sanskrit: dvitīye maṇḍale vāhye indyāyāgniyamāya ca // nairṛtāya jaleśāya vāyave dhanarakṣiṇe /
english: Oblations should be made to Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera and Īśāna in the east etc. outside in the second maṇḍala.

sanskrit: īśānāya ca pūrvādau hīśāne brahmaṇe namaḥ //
english: Salutations to Brahmā on the northeast.

sanskrit: nairṛte viṣṇave svāhā vāyasādervahirbaliḥ /
english: Oblations to Viṣṇu in the southwest. The offerings for the crows etc. should be outside.

sanskrit: balidvayagatānmantrān saṃhāramudrayā.atmani //
english: The mantras for the two offerings in one’s soul should be by the saṃhāramudrā posture with fingers indicating destruction. l.

sanskrit: tataḥ śivāntikaṅgatvā pūjāhomādikaṃ mama / gṛhāṇa bhagavan puṇyaphalamityabhidhāya ca //
english: The worshipper should approach the image of Lord Śiva and address as follows “O Lord! accept the merits of the worship and the oblations offered by me.”

sanskrit: arghyodakena devāya mudrayodbhavasañjñayā / hṛdvījapūrvamūlena sthiracitto nivedayet //
english: We should convey these to the lord with a firm mind along with the respectful offering of water and uttering the principal mantra preceded by the hṛdbīja oṃ and the exhibition of the udbhava mudrā a posture of fingers representing generation.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrvavadabhyarcya stutvā stotraiḥ praṇamya ca / arghyaṃ parāṅmukhaṃ datvā kṣamasvetyabhidhāya ca //
english: Then having worshipped as before and praising with hymns and saluting, the worshipper should offer the respectful offering of water with his face turned away from the image and should say “Pardon me”.

sanskrit: nārācamudrayāstreṇa phaḍantenātmasañcayaṃ / saṃhṛtya divyayā liṅgaṃ mūrtimantreṇa yojayet // sthaṇḍile tvarcite deve mantrasaṅghātamātmani / niyojya vidhinoktena vidadhyāccaṇḍapūjanaṃ //
english: The liṅga should be discharged by uttering the mantra of the weapon ending with phaṭ coupled with the divine nārācamudrā formation with fingers representing an iron arrow, it should be merged with the mantra of the image. After having worshipped god on the platform and having merged in himself the collection of mantras as laid down, the worship of Caṇḍa should be made.

sanskrit: oṃ caṇḍeśānāya namo madhyataś caṇḍamūrtaye /
english: Oṃ salutations to Caṇḍeśāna. Salutations to the image of Caṇḍa at the centre.

sanskrit: oṃ dhūlicaṇḍeśvarāya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā tamāhṇayet //
english: Oṃ, huṃ phaṭ oblations to Dhūlicaṇḍeśvara. Thus he should be invoked.

sanskrit: caṇḍahṛdayāya hūṃ phaṭ oṃ caṇḍaśirase tathā / oṃ caṇḍaśikhāyai hūṃ phaṭ caṇḍāyuḥ kavacāya ca //
english: Hūṃ phaṭ to Caṇḍa at the heart. Then Oṃ to Caṇḍa on the head. Oṃ hūṃ phaṭ to Caṇḍa on the tuft, to Caṇḍa, the protector and armour. So also to Caṇḍa as the weapon hūṃ phaṭ.

sanskrit: caṇḍastrāya tathā hūṃ phaṭ caṇḍaṃ rudrāgnijaṃ smaret / śūlaṭaṅkadharaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sākṣasūtrakaṇḍaluṃ //
english: meditate on Caṇḍa, born of the fire of Rudra and as carrying the mace, axe, rosaries and the anchorite’s pitcher and as havinga dark complexion.

sanskrit: ṭaṅkākare 'rdhacandre vā caturvaktraṃ prapūjayet / yathāśakti japaṃ kuryādaṅgānāntu daśāṃśataḥ //
english: The fourfaced deity should be worshipped in the halfcrescent shaped axe weapon of Caṇḍa. One should repeat the mantra befitting one’s capacity, being onetenth of the principal worship.

sanskrit: gobhūhiraṇyavastrādimaṇihemādibhūṣaṇaṃ / vihāya śesanirmālyaṃ caṇḍeśāya nivedayet //
english: Except the offerings such as the cow, earth, gold, clothes, gems and ornaments, the remains of offerings should be offered to Caṇḍeśa.

sanskrit: lehyacoṣyādyanuvaraṃ tāmbūlaṃ sragvilepanaṃ / nirmālyaṃ bhojanaṃ tubhyaṃ pradattantu śivājñayā //
english: Being ordered by Śiva, have offered to you these articles of food and drink, betels, garlands and scented pastes, the ramnants of offering.

sanskrit: sarvametat kriyākāṇḍaṃ mayā caṇḍa tavājñayā /
english: O Caṇḍa! may all these acts of service undertaken by me by your order be agreeable to you.

sanskrit: nyūnādhikaṃ kṛtaṃ mohāt paripūrṇaṃ sadāstu me //
english: Any shortcoming or redundancy out of my ignorance may be made complete always.

sanskrit: iti vijñāpya deveśaṃ datvārghyaṃ tasya saṃsmaran / saṃhāramūrtimantreṇa śanaiḥ saṃhāramudrayā // pūrakānvitamūlena mantrānātmani yojayet / nirmālyāpanayasthānaṃ limpedgomayavāriṇā /
english: Having submitted to the lord thus and offered the respectful water and contemplated his form, the mantras should be merged with the self with the mantra of the destructive deity and showing slowly the saṃhāra mudrā formation with the fingers representing destruction along with the principal mantra and taking a breath. The offering such as flowers etc.

sanskrit: prokṣyārghyādi visṛjyātha ācānto 'nyatsamācaret //
english: After offering water respectfully one should conclude by rinsing one’s mouth and do any other worship.

sanskrit: kapilāpūjanaṃ vakṣye ebhirmantrair yajecca gāṃ / oṃ kapile nande namaḥ oṃ kapile bhadrike namaḥ //
english: shall describe to you the mode of worship of Kapilā the cow. The cow should be worshipped with these mantras. Oṃ salutations to you O Kapila, one makes us rejoice, the abode of bliss.

sanskrit: oṃ kapile suśīle namaḥ kapile surabhiprabhe /
english: Salutations to you. Oṃ salutations to you O Kapila of good disposition.

sanskrit: oṃ kapile sumanase namaḥ oṃ bhuktimuktiprade namaḥ //
english: Oṃ Kapila, the goodminded, salutations. Oṃ salutations to the bestower of enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: saurabheyi jaganmātardevānāmamṛtaprade / gṛhāṇa varade grāsamīpsitārthañca dehi me //
english: O Daughter of Surabhi! the Mother of the universe! Giver of ambrosia to the celestials! Granter of boons! Accept this morsel of food and grant me all my desires.

sanskrit: vanditāsi vasiṣṭhena viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā /
english: You had been worshipped by Vasiṣṭha and the learned Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: kapile hara me pāpaṃ yanmayā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ //
english: O Kapila! Take away my sins and the bad acts of mine.

sanskrit: gāvo mamāgrato nityaṃ gāvaḥ pṛṣṭhata eva ca /
english: Let there be cows always in front of me. Let there be cows behind me.

sanskrit: gāvo me hṛdaye cāpi gavāṃ madhye vasāmyahaṃ //
english: Let there be cows in my heart also. am dwelling in the midst of cows.

sanskrit: dattaṃ gṛhṇantu me grāsaṃ japtvā syāṃ nirmalaḥ śivaḥ /
english: May you accept the morsel of food offered by me. After repetition of the mantra let me be pure like Lord Śiva.

sanskrit: prārcya vidyāpustakāni gurupādau namennaraḥ //
english: After having worshipped the books of learning one should bow at the feet of the preceptor.

sanskrit: yajet snātvā tu madhyāhne aṣṭapuṣpikayā śivaṃ /
english: One should bathe again at noon and worship Lord Śiva with aṣṭapuṣpikā.

sanskrit: pīṭhamūrtiśivāṅgānāṃ pūjā syādaṣṭapuṣpikā //
english: The aṣṭapuṣpikā is the worship of the image, seat and the limbs of the image of Śiva.

sanskrit: madhyāhne bhojanāgāre sulipte pākamānayet /
english: The cooked food should be brought into the wellcleansed kitchen at midday.

sanskrit: tato mṛtyuñjayenaiva vauṣaḍantena saptadhā // japtaiḥ sadarbhaśaṅkhasthaiḥ siñcettaṃ vārivindubhiḥ /
english: Then after the recitation of the mṛtyuñjaya mantra that which conquers death seven times and ending with the vauṣaṭ, the food should be sprinkled with drops of water with the darbha and conch.

sanskrit: sarvapākāgramuddhṛtya śivāya vinivedayet //
english: The entire food should first be dedicated to Śiva after lifting them up.

sanskrit: athārdhaṃ cullikāhome vidhānāyopakalpayet /
english: Then half of the above should be set apart for oblation at the fireplace.

sanskrit: viśodhya vidhinā cullīṃ tadvahniṃ pūrakāhutiṃ //
english: After having purified the fireplace as per rules, the oblation should be done.

sanskrit: hutvā nābhyagninā caikaṃ tato recakavāyunā / vahnivījaṃ samādāya kādisthānagatikramāt // śivāgnistvamiti dhyātvā cullikāgnau niveśayet /
english: Having made the oblation once in the fire around one’s navel one should gather the seed of fire with the breath drawn in and after taking it through the places of the letters, one should meditate on it as “You are the fire of Lord Śiva” and it should be put at the fireplace.

sanskrit: oṃ hāṃ agnaye namo vai hāṃ somāya vai namaḥ //
english: Oṃ hāṃ obeisance to firegodas also hāṃ obeisance to Soma.

sanskrit: sūryāya vṛhaspataye prajānāṃ pataye namaḥ /
english: Obeisance to Sungod, to Jupiter, the lord of people.

sanskrit: sarvebhyaś caiva devebhyaḥ sarvaviśvebhya eva ca //
english: Obeisance to all gods and to all Viśvedevas.

sanskrit: hāmagnaye khiṣṭikṛte pūrvādāvarcayedimān / svāhāntāmāhutiṃ datvā kṣamayitvā visarjayet //
english: One should worship these in the east and other directions. After having made oblations ending with the word svāhā one should bid farewell after seeking forbearance.

sanskrit: cullyā dakṣiṇabāhau ca yajeddharmāya vai namaḥ / vāmabāhāvadharmāya kāñjikādikabhāṇḍake //
english: One should worship the god of righteousness on the righthand side of the fireplace. “Salutations to the god of righteousness. The lord of unrighteousness should be worshipped on the lefthandside in a vessel containing sour gruel.

sanskrit: rasaparivartamānāya varuṇāya jalāgnaye / vighnarājo gṛhadvāre peṣaṇyāṃ subhage namaḥ //
english: Lord Varuṇa should be worshipped as the transformer of the sap and as the lord of fire in the waters. Lord of obstacles Vināyaka should be worshipped at the entrance.

sanskrit: oṃ raudrike namo girike namaś caolūkhale yajet / balapriyāyāyudhāya namaste muṣale yajet //
english: Oṃ obeisance to Raudrikā and Girikā. Obeisance one should worship in the mortar. Obeisance to the pestle, the weapon dear to Bala rāma.

sanskrit: sammārjanyāṃ devatokte kāmāya śayanīyake /
english: The two gods mentioned should be worshipped in the broomstick and the god of love in the bed.

sanskrit: madhyastambhe ca skandāya datvā vāstubaliṃ tataḥ // bhuñjīta pātre sauvarṇe padminyādidalādike /
english: Having offered oblation to the trunk for the presiding deity of the ground at the middle stump one should eat from a golden vessel or in the petals of the lotus etc.

sanskrit: ācāryaḥ sādhakaḥputra samayī maunamāsthitaḥ //
english: The preceptor, the worshipper and the son should maintain silence at the time of this vow.

sanskrit: vaṭāśvatthārkavātāvisarjabhallātakāṃstyajet /
english: The leaves of the vaṭa, aśvattha, arka, vātāri, sāla and bhallātaka should be discarded.

sanskrit: apośānaṃ purādāya prāṇādyaiḥ praṇavānvitaiḥ // svāhāntenāhutīḥ pañca datvādīpyodarānalaṃ /
english: After having rinsed the mouth with water, five oblations should be offered with the five priiṇas winds in the body together with the praṇava oṃ ending with svāhā oblations.

sanskrit: nāgaḥ kūrmo 'tha kṛkaro devadatto dhanañjayaḥ //
english: With the secondary winds in one’s body viz., nāga, kūrma, kṛkara, devadatta and dhanañjaya, oblations should be made.

sanskrit: etebhya upavāyubhyaḥ svāhāpoṣānavāriṇā / bhaktādikaṃ nivedyāya piveccheṣodakaṃ naraḥ //
english: Having offered food with the waters of āpośāna prayer repeated before and after eating, one should drink the rest of the water.

sanskrit: amṛtopastaraṇamasi prāṇāhutīstato dadet /
english: You are an ambrosial seat.

sanskrit: prāṇāya svāhāpānāya samānāya tatas tathā // udānāya ca vyānāya bhuktvā cullakamācaret /
english: Oblations for the vital winds should be made as before. Oblations to the prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna. Having eaten food, water should be sipped.

sanskrit: amṛtāpiścānamasīti śarīre 'nnādivāyavaḥ //
english: The mantra for that is “you are the ambrosial covering.” Thus the food and the winds in the body are worshipped.

sanskrit: pavitrārohaṇaṃ vakṣye kriyārcādiṣu pūraṇaṃ /
english: shall describe the mode of investiture of the sacred thread for the deity which completes the acts of worship etc.

sanskrit: nityaṃ tannityamuddiṣṭaṃ naimittikamathāparaṃ //
english: It is of two kinds, the daily routine without any motive and the other being undertaken to be done with a motive.

sanskrit: āṣāḍhādicaturdaśyāmatha śrāvaṇabhādrayoḥ / sitāsitāsu kartavyaṃ caturdaśyaṣṭamīṣu tat //
english: It should be done on the eighth or fourteenth day of the bright or dark fortnights in the months of āṣāḍha JulyAugust or śrāvaṇa AugustSeptember or bhādrapada SeptemberOctober.

sanskrit: kuryādvā kārttikīṃ yāvattithau pratipādike / vahnibrahmāmbikebhāsyanāgaskandārkaśūlināṃ // durgāyamendragovindasmaraśambhusudhābhujāṃ /
english: Or it should be done on the first day of either fortnights during the above months upto kārttika OctoberNovember, for the images of the fire god, Brahmā, Ambikā, Ibhāsya Gaṇeśa, Nāga lord of serpents, Skanda, Arka Sun, Śūlin, Durgā, Yama, Indra, Govinda manifestation of Viṣṇu, Smara God of love, Śambhu Śiva and other gods.

sanskrit: sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ tāmraṃ kṛtādiṣu yathākramaṃ // kalau kārpāsajaṃ cāpi paṭṭapadmādisūtrakaṃ /
english: The threads should be made of gold, silver and copper in the kṛta first one among the four eras and other yugas eras. A cotton thread or silk thread or the one made of fibres of lotus should be used in the kali yuga the last.

sanskrit: praṇavaś candramā vahnirbrahmā nāgo guho hariḥ // sarveśaḥ sarvadevāḥ syuḥ krameṇa navatantuṣu /
english: The praṇava oṃ, moon, firegod, Brahmā, serpentgod, Guha son of Śiva, Hari Viṣṇu, Sarveśa and other gods would reside in the nine component strings of the thread.

sanskrit: aṣṭottaraśatānyardhaṃ tadardhaṃ cottamādikaṃ // ekāśītyāthavā sūtraistriṃśatāppaṣṭayuktayā /
english: The uttama excellent and other classes madhyama and adhama would be those which contain one hundred and eight strings or half of that or a quarter of that.

sanskrit: pañcāśatā vā kartavyaṃ tulyagranthyantarālakaṃ //
english: Or it should be made to contain eightyone or thirtyeight or fifty strings having binding knots at equal intervals.

sanskrit: dvādaśāṅgulamānāni vyāsādaṣṭāṅgulāni ca / liṅgavistāramānāni caturaṅgulakāni vā // tathaiva piṇḍikāsparśaṃ caturthaṃ sarvadaivataṃ /
english: The breadth of the thread should be twelve or eight or four finger lengths or else it should be equal to the breadth of the liṅga. In length it should be touching the pedestal of the image or should be equal to a quarter of the length of the deity as a whole.

sanskrit: gaṅgāvatārakaṃ kāryaṃ sujātena sudhautakaṃ // granthiṃ kuryācca vāmena aghoraṇātha śodhayet / rañjayet puruṣeṇaiva raktacandanakuṅkumaiḥ //
english: The descent of the Ganges should be accomplished by washing with pure water. The knots should be made with the mantra of Vāma deva, purified with that of Aghora, dyed with the paste of saffron, sandal, musk, yellow pigment, camphor, turmeric and red chalk etc.

sanskrit: granthayo daśa kartavyā athavā tantusaṅkhyayā // antaraṃ vā yathāśobhamekadvicaturaṅgulaṃ /
english: There should be ten knots or equal to the number of strings. The interspace between the knots should be one, two or four finger lengths in such a way as to make it elegant.

sanskrit: prakṛtiḥ pauruṣī vīrā caturthī tvaparājitā // jayānyā vijayā ṣaṣṭhī ajitā ca sadāśivā / manonmanī sarvamukhī granthayo 'bhyadhikāḥ śubhāḥ //
english: The knots are known as sadāśivā, manonmanī, prakṛti nature, pauruṣī relating to the puruṣa, vīrā valorous, aparājitā invincible, jayā victorious, vijayā victorious, ajitā unconquered, sadāśivā always auspicious, manonmanī expanding intellect, and sarvamukhi omniscient which confer good.

sanskrit: kāryā vā candravahnyarkapavitraṃ śivavaddhṛdi / ekaikaṃ nijamūrtau vā puptake guruke gaṇe //
english: The sacred thread for the moon, firegod and sun should be done similar to that for Śiva, in the heart, or in their own image or in a book or in that of the preceptor or the gaṇas.

sanskrit: syādekaikaṃ tathā dvāradikpālakalaśādiṣu /
english: In the same way there should be one in each one of the pitchers of the doorkeeper and the presiding deity of the directions etc.

sanskrit: hastādinavahastāntaṃ liṅgānāṃ syātpavitrakaṃ // aṣṭāviṃśatito yuddhaṃ daśabhirdaśabhiḥ kramāt / dvyaṅgulābhyantarāstatra kramādekāṅgulāntarāḥ //
english: The sacred thread for the liṅga should measure from one to nine cubits in length. The number of knots in a thread of the vṛddha class should be twentyeight, the number for other classes being eighteen and eight respectively, their breadth in all being proportionate with the breadth of the liṅga.

sanskrit: saptamyāṃ vā trayodaśyāṃ kṛtanityakriyaḥ śuciḥ //
english: On the seventh or thirteenth day of a fortnight one should become clean and do his daily rites.

sanskrit: bhūṣayet puṣpavastrādyaiḥ sāyāhne yāgamandiraṃ /
english: Then he should adorn the place of worship with flowers, cloth etc.

sanskrit: kṛtvā naimittikīṃ sandhyāṃ viśeṣeṇa ca tarpaṇaṃ //
english: in the evening and should perform the naimittika rites done with some motive, especially the waters of oblation.

sanskrit: parigṛhīte bhūbhāge pavitre sūryamarcayet /
english: After having taken possession of the sacred ground, the sungod should be worshipped.

sanskrit: ācamya sakalīkṛtya praṇavārghyakaro guruḥ // dvārāṇyastreṇa samprokṣya pūrvādikramato 'rcayet /
english: Water should be offered with respect with the praṇava the syllable oṃ. The threshold should be sprinkled with water with the mantra of the weapon and the worship should be duly commenced from the east.

sanskrit: hāṃ śāntikalādvārāya tathā vidyākalātmane // nivṛttikalādvārāya pratiṣṭhākhyakalātmane /
english: Ham obeisance to the entrance to the śāntikalā digit of peace obeisance to the vidyākalā digit of knowledge. Obeisance to the digit of nonaction, to the one digit known as existence.

sanskrit: tacchākhayoḥ pratidvāraṃ dvau dvau dvārādhipau yajet //
english: The warden of the god should be worshipped at the top sides of those doors, two at each as follows

sanskrit: nandine mahākālāya bhṛṅgiṇe 'tha gaṇāya ca / vṛṣabhāya ca skandāya devyai caṇḍāya ca kramāt //
english: Obeisance to Nandin, to Mahākāla, to Bhṛṅgin, to Gaṇa, to Vṛṣabha, to Skanda, to Devī and to Caṇḍa in order.

sanskrit: nityaṃ ca dvārapālādīn praviśya dvārapaścime / iṣṭvā vāstuṃ bhūtaśuddhiṃ viśeṣārghyakaraḥ śivaḥ //
english: In the case of worship being undertaken without any motive, the preceptor, having entered and worshipped the guardian deities at the western entrance, and after purification of materials, should offer water of respect.

sanskrit: prokṣaṇādyaṃ vidhāyātha yajñasambhārakṛnnaraḥ / mantrayeddarbhadūrvādyaiḥ puṣpādyaiś ca hṛdādibhiḥ //
english: After having done the sprinkling of water etc., and collected the materials for the rite, consecration with darbha, dūrvā and flowers should be made with the mantras like hṛd etc.

sanskrit: śivahastaṃ vidhāyetthaṃ svaśirasyadhiropayet /
english: After having permeated thus with the essence of Śiva, one should place it on his head.

sanskrit: śivo 'hamādiḥ sarvajño mama yajñapradhānatā //
english: am Śiva, the first being, omniscient and have the importance in the rites.

sanskrit: atyarthaṃ bhāvayeddevaṃ jñānakhadgakaro guruḥ /
english: The preceptor holding the sword of knowledge in his hand should deeply contemplate the lord.

sanskrit: nairṛtīṃ diśamāsādya prakṣipedudagānanaḥ //
english: Subsequently he should go to the southwestern direction and pour the washings etc. with his face turned towards the north.

sanskrit: arghyāmbu pañcagavyañca samastān makhamaṇḍape / catuṣpathāntasaṃskārair vīkṣaṇādyaiḥ susaṃskṛtaiḥ //
english: The respectful water offering, the pañcagavya the five things got from a cow and all other articles of worship which have been purified by means of rites at the end of crossroads and by divine look etc.

sanskrit: vikṣipya vikirāṃstatra kuśakūrcopasaṃharet / tānīśadiśi vardhanyāmāsanāyopakalpayet // nairṛte vāstugīrvāṇā dvāre lakṣmīṃ prapūjayet /
english: and put in the sacrificial pavilion, one should collect the bunch of kuśa lying scattered, place them over the little jar in the northeastern direction. The presiding deities of the place should be worshipped in the southwest and Goddess Lakṣmī at the entrance.

sanskrit: paścimābhimukhaṃ kumbhaṃ sarvadhānyopari sthitaṃ //
english: The pitcher is placed on all kinds of grains facing the west.

sanskrit: praṇavena vṛṣārūḍhaṃ siṃhasthāṃ vardhanīntataḥ / kumbhe sāṅgaṃ śivandevaṃ vardhanyāmarcayet //
english: Then the bullriding God and the pitcher varddhanī placed on the lion should be worshipped with the praṇava oṃ. Lord Śiva should be worshipped in the jar with his attendant gods and the weapons in the vardhanī.

sanskrit: dikṣu śakrādidikpālān viṣṇubrahmaśivādikān /
english: Indra and other guardian deities of directions, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva should be worshipped in the different directions.

sanskrit: vardhanīṃ samyagādāya ghaṭapṛṣṭānugāminīṃ // śivājñāṃ śrāvayenmantrī pūrvādīśānagocaraṃ /
english: Having taken the vardhanī in the hand behind the pitcher, the preceptor should read out the mandate of Lord Śiva in all directions commencing with the east and ending with the northeast.

sanskrit: avicchinnapayodhārāṃ mūlamantramudīrayet //
english: The entire ground should be made wet by an unbroken flow of water along with the recitation of principal mantra.

sanskrit: samantād bhrāmayedenāṃ rakṣārthaṃ śastrarūpiṇīṃ /
english: This should be moved around in all directions for the sake of protection as if it were the weapons.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ kalaśamāropya śastrārthantasya vāmataḥ // samagrāsanake kumbhe yajeddevaṃ sthirāsane /
english: Having placed the pitcher in the east, the lord should be worshipped in the pitcher placed foremost at the front firmly, while there should. be one for the weapons to the left of it.

sanskrit: vardhanyāṃ praṇavasthāyāmāyudhantadanu dvayoḥ //
english: The weapons located with the praṇava oṃ should be worshipped with the vardhanī.

sanskrit: bhagaliṅgasamāyogaṃ vidadhyālliṅgamudrayā / kumbhe nivedya bodhāsiṃ mūlamantrajapantathā //
english: Then the union of the two, the base and the liṅga should be accomplished by showing the liṅga mudrā posture of the fingers representing the liṅga. Then the sword of knowledge should be dedicated to the consecrated pitcher.

sanskrit: taddaśāṃśena vardhanyāṃ rakṣāṃ vijñāpayedapi /
english: Protection should be spelled out with a tenth of the mantra in the vardhanī.

sanskrit: gaṇeśaṃ vāyave 'bhyarcya haraṃ pañcāmṛtādibhiḥ // snāpayet pūrvavat prārcya kuṇḍe ca śivapāvakaṃ / vidhivacca caruṃ kṛtvā sampātāhutiśodhitaṃ //
english: lord of the gaṇas in the northwest and Lord Hara Viṣṇu with the five sweet things milk, sugar, ghee, curd and honey, the fire sacred to Śiva should be worshipped in the sacrificial pit as before and bathed after having made the sacrificial gruel duly purified by the sampāta residual oblation.

sanskrit: devāgryātmavibhedena darṣyā taṃ vibhajet tridhā / datvā bhāgau śivāgnibhyāṃ saṃrakṣedbhāgamātmani //
english: It should be divided with the kuśa into three parts respectively consecrated to the god, the firegod, and the soul, of which the former two should be offered to Lord Śiva and the firegod and the part consecrated to the soul should be kept apart.

sanskrit: śareṇa carmaṇā deyaṃ pūrvato dantadhāvanaṃ / tasmādghoraśikhābhyāṃ vā dakṣiṇe paścime mṛdaṃ //
english: The stick for cleansing the teeth should be offered on the east by repeating the mantras of the weapon and arrow, and a piece of earth on the west or south with the a ghora and śikhā mantras.

sanskrit: sādyojātena ca hṛdā cottare vāmanīkṛtaṃ / jalaṃ vāmena śirasā īśe gandhānvitaṃ jalaṃ //
english: Water reduced in quantity should be offeredon the north with the sadyojāta and the hṛd mantras. Perfumed water should be offered on the northeast with the vāma deva and śiras mantras.

sanskrit: pañcagavyaṃ palāśādipuṭakaṃ vai samantataḥ /
english: The five things got from a cow and flowers like palāśa and lotus should be cast all around.

sanskrit: aiśānyāṃ kusumaṃ dadyādāgneyyāṃ diśi rocanāṃ //
english: Flowers should be offered on the northeast and the yellow pigment on the southeast.

sanskrit: aguruṃ nirṛtāśāyāṃ vāyavyāṃ ca catuḥsamaṃ / homadravyāṇi sarvāṇi sadyojātaiḥ kuśaiḥ saha //
english: The agallochum should be offered on the southwestern direction and all the articles for oblation in four equal proportions on the northwest with the sadyojāta mantra and with the kuśa.

sanskrit: daṇḍākṣasūtrakaupīnabhikṣāpātrāṇi rūpiṇe / kajjalaṃ kuṅkumantailaṃ śalākāṃ keśaśodhanīṃ //
english: An anchorite’s stick, rosary, loincloth, alms bowl, collyrium, saffron, oil, a small stick for applying the collyrium, comb, betel leaf, and mirror should be offered to the image of the god.

sanskrit: tāmbūlaṃ darpaṇaṃ dadyāduttare rocanāmapi /
english: The yellow pigment should be offered on the north.

sanskrit: āsanaṃ pāduke pātraṃ yogapaṭṭātapatrakaṃ // aiśānyāmīśamantreṇa dadyādīśānatuṣṭaye /
english: He should offer a seat, a pair of sandals, a vessel, an upper cloth and an umbrella on the northeast with the mantra of the lord for the satisfaction of Īśāna one of the five forms of

sanskrit: pūrvasyāñcarukaṃ sājyaṃ dadyādgandhādikaṃ nave //
english: The sacrificial porridge together with the clarified butter and perfumes etc. should be offered on the east.

sanskrit: pūrvitrāṇi samādāya prokṣitānyarghyavāriṇā / saṃhitāmantrapūtāni nītvā pāvakasannidhiṃ //
english: Having gathered the sacred threads and sprinkled them with the waters offered as respect, they should be led to the presence of fire after purifying them with the saṃhitā mantras.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇājinādinā.acchādya smaran saṃvatsarātmakaṃ / sākṣiṇaṃ sarvakṛtyānāṃ goptāraṃ śivamavyayaṃ // sveti heti prayogeṇa mantrasaṃhitayā punaḥ /
english: After having covered them with the hide of the black antelope and remembering the eternal blissful one, the witness of all deeds, the protector, the one without any change, that Śiva, with the application of sva and ha mantras and saṃhitā mantras, the sacred threads should be purified.

sanskrit: śodhayecca pavitrāṇi vārāṇāmekaviṃśatiṃ //
english: Twentyone water vessels should be got ready. The room for worship etc. should be girdled by threads.

sanskrit: gṛhādi veṣṭayetsūtrair gandhādyaṃ ravaye dadet / pūjitāya samācamya kṛtanyāsaḥ kṛtārghyakaḥ //
english: should be offered to the sungod, who had already been worshipped. After having rinsed the mouth, and doing the assigning, the water should be offered with respect.

sanskrit: nandyādibhyo 'tha gandhākhyaṃ vāstoścātha praviśya ca / śastrebhyo lokapālebhyaḥ svanāmnā śivakumbhake //
english: along with the weapons, the guardians of the world, Nandin and others by mentioning the name of each in the pitcher of lord Śiva after adding perfumes.

sanskrit: vardhanyai vighnarājāya gurave hy ātmane yajet /
english: vardhanī, lord of obstacles, the preceptor should be worshipped.

sanskrit: atha sarvauṣadhīliptaṃ dhūpitaṃ puṣpadūrvayā // āmantrya ca pavitraṃ tat vidhāyāñjalimadhyagaṃ /
english: Then the sacred thread smeared with the paste of all herbs and perfumed with the flowers and dūrva and purified with the mantras should be held between the folded palms.

sanskrit: oṃ samastavidhicchidrapūraṇe ca vidhiṃ prati // prabhavamantrayāmi tvāṃ tvadicchāvāptikārikāṃ /
english: Oṃ! salutation to you the regulation for rectifying any omission in regulations. O lord! invoke you and that which yields the desired boon. O lord of entity and nonentity! You bless me,.

sanskrit: tatsiddhimanujānīhi yajataścidacitpate //
english: one who worships, with that success. .

sanskrit: sarvathā sarvadā śambho namaste 'stu prasīda me /
english: O Śambhu Śiva! Obeisance to you at all times. and by all means. Be pleased with me.

sanskrit: āmantrito 'si deveśa saha devyā gaṇeśvaraiḥ // mantreśair lokapālaiś ca sahitaḥ paricārakaiḥ /
english: O lord of celestials!. You have been invoked along with the goddess, lords of gaṇas, lords of mantras, guardians of the world and attendant gods invoke you.

sanskrit: nimantrayāmyahantubhyaṃ prabhāte tu pavitrakaṃ //
english: This sacred thread is for you in the early morning..

sanskrit: niyamañca kariṣyāmi parameśa tavājñayā /
english: O supreme lord! By your command shall do the prescribed routine.

sanskrit: ityevandevamāmantrya recakenāmṛtīkṛtaṃ // śivāntaṃ mūlamuccārya tacchivāya nivedayet / japaṃ stotraṃ pramāṇañca kṛtvā śambhuṃ kṣamāpayet //
english: Thus one should invoke the lord and do the amṛtīkaraṇa rite by drawing in the breath. Having recited the principal mantra for Śiva, it should be dedicated to lord Śiva. After completing the recitation of mantra, praises, and obeisance, lord Śambhu Śiva should be bid adieu.

sanskrit: hutvā carostṛtīyāṃśaṃ taddaddīta śivāgnaye / digvāsibhyo digīśebhyo bhūtamātṛgaṇebhya u // rudrebhyo kṣetrapādibhyo namaḥ svāhā balistvayaṃ /
english: Having made oblation with the third part of the gruel in the fire permeated with the essence of Śiva, oblation should be made for the residents in the quarters, the lords of the quarters, the spirits, the mothers, gaṇas, Rudras, guardians of the region. Obeisance.

sanskrit: diṅnāgādyaiś ca pūrvādau kṣetrāya cāgnaye baliḥ //
english: The oblation is made for the guardian elephants of the quarters east etc. and to the regions.

sanskrit: samācamya vidhicchidrapūrakaṃ homamācaret / pūrṇāṃ vyāhṛtihomañca kṛtvā rundhīta pāvakaṃ //
english: After having rinsed the mouth, the oblation should be done for the rectification of omissions in the observances. After doing the final oblation, the fire should be put out.

sanskrit: tata omagnaye svāhā svāhā somāya caiva hi /
english: Then Oṃ oblations to fire god, to Soma, Oṃ oblations to fire and Soma.

sanskrit: ityāhuticatuṣkantu datvā kuryāttu yojanāṃ / vahnikuṇḍārcitaṃ devaṃ maṇḍalābhyarcite śive //
english: So also to firegod, the accomplishes After having made four oblations, the union of the gods respectively worshipped in the sacrificial pit and the mystic circle of lord Śiva should be brought about.

sanskrit: nāḍīsandhānarūpeṇa vidhinā yojayettataḥ /
english: Then the union should be made by the method of assigning in the different parts of the body.

sanskrit: vaṃśādipātre vinyasya astrañca hṛdayantataḥ // adhiropya pavitrāṇi kalābhirvātha mantrayet /
english: Then the sacred threads should be placed in a vessel made of bamboo along with the mantras of weapons and armour and consecrated with the mantras of the digits.

sanskrit: ṣaḍaṅgaṃ brahmamūlair vā hṛddharmāstrañca yojayet //
english: The six articles of worship should be consecrated with the principal brahma mantra oṃ.

sanskrit: vidhāya sūtraiḥ saṃveṣṭya pūjayitvāṅgasambhavaiḥ / rakṣārthaṃ jagadīśāya bhaktinamraḥ samarpayet //
english: Having girdled the vessel with threads and worshipped it with the mantras of the parts of the body it should be offered to the lord of the universe with extreme devotion for the sake of protection.

sanskrit: pūjite puṣpadhūpādyair datvā siddhāntapustake /
english: After it has been worshipped with flowers, incense etc.

sanskrit: guroḥ pādāntikaṃ gatvā bhaktyā dadyāt pavitrakaṃ //
english: and two theological books have been submitted, one should go near the feet of the preceptor and offer the sacred thread with devotion.

sanskrit: nirgatya vahirācamya gomaye maṇḍalatraye / pañcagavyañcarundantadhāvanañca kramād yajet //
english: Having come out of the place and rinsed the mouth, one should worship five things got from a cow, the gruel and the stick for cleansing the teeth on three circles made with the cowdung.

sanskrit: ācānto mantrasambaddhaḥ kṛtasaṅgītajāgaraḥ / svapedantaḥ smarannīśaṃ bubhukṣurdarbhasaṃstare //
english: After rinsing the mouth again, one should remain awake singing songs and repeating hymns and should sleep at the end after fasting on a bed of darbha all the while contemplating on the lord.

sanskrit: anenaiva prakāreṇa mumukṣurapi saṃviśet /
english: Even one, who is desirous of cessation of births and deaths, should undertake in this way lying only on a bed of ashes, fasting and selfcontrolled.

sanskrit: kevalambhasmaśayyāyāṃ sopavāsaḥ samāhitaḥ // atha prātaḥ samutthāya kṛtasnānaḥ samāhitaḥ /
english: Having got up early in the morning, and finishing bathing the worshipper should enter the sacrificial shed after completing the twilight worship and remaining composed.

sanskrit: samādāya pavitrāṇi avisarjitadaivataḥ / aiśānyāṃ bhājane śuddhe sthāpayet kṛtamaṇḍale //
english: Having collected the sacred thread , and the deity not being given farewell, the sacred thread should be placed in a spotless vessel within a mystic diagram in the northeast.

sanskrit: tato visarjya deveśaṃ nirmālyamapanīya ca /
english: Then the lord of celestials should be bid farewell and the materials of worship should be removed from the body of the deity.

sanskrit: pūrvavad bhūtale śuddhekṛtvāhnikamatha dvayaṃ //
english: He should again perform the two rites as before on the cleaned ground.

sanskrit: ādityadvāradikpālakumbheśānau śive 'nale /
english: Then the godssun, the guardian deities of the entrance and of the directions the pitcher, Īśāna, Śiva and the firegod.

sanskrit: naimittikīṃ savistarāṃ kuryāt pūjāṃ viśeṣataḥ //
english: should specially be worshipped, as usually done in the naimittikī done with some motives rites, elaborately.

sanskrit: mantrāṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ prāyaścittahomaṃ śarātmanā / aṣṭottaraśataṃ kṛtvā dadyāt pūrṇāhutiṃ śanaiḥ //
english: Having done the tarpaṇa appeasing rite with the mantras and the oblation of expiation one hundred and eight times with the mantras of the arrows, the final oblation should be made slowly.

sanskrit: pavitraṃ bhānave datvā samācamya dadīta ca / dvāramālādidikpālakumbhavardhanikādiṣu //
english: Having offered the sacred thread to the sun god and rinsing the mouth, the worshipper should offer it to the guardian deities of the entrance and of the directions, the sacrificial pitcher and vardhanī etc.

sanskrit: sannidhāne tataḥ śambhorupaviśya nijāsane / pavitramātmane dadyādgaṇāya guruvahnaye //
english: Then having sat in his own seat in the presence of lord Śambhu Śiva, the worshipper should offer the sacred thread to one’s own self, the gaṇa, the priest and firegod.

sanskrit: oṃ kālātmanā tvayā deva yaddiṣṭaṃ māmake vidhau /
english: Oṃ O lord! soul of the time, whatever has been ordained by you in my observances that which has been done.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ kliṣṭaṃ samutsṛṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ guptañca yat kṛtaṃ // tadastu kliṣṭamakliṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ kliṣṭamasaṃskṛtaṃ / sarvātmanāmunā śambho pavitreṇa tvadicchayā //
english: contradictorily, and omitted, and that which has been done secretly O Śambhu let the contradictory thing become normal, the contradictory deed become refined, by this omniscient sacred thread and by your wish.

sanskrit: oṃ pūrayamakhavrataṃ niyameśvarāya svāhā / ātmatattve prakṛtyante pālite padmayoninā //
english: Oṃ! Complete this sacrificial observance! Oblations to the lord of regulations, the principle of the soul, that which underlines the natural principle that is protected by the lotusborn Brahmā.

sanskrit: mūlaṃ layāntamuccārya pavitreṇārcayecchivaṃ / vidyātattve ca vidyānte viṣṇukāraṇapālite // īśvarāntaṃ samuccārya pavitramadhiropayet /
english: Having recited the principal mantra upto the end, lord Śiva should be worshipped with the sacred thread . Again in the principle of knowledge which is the end of all the learning and which is governed by Viṣṇu, one should invest the sacred thread having recited the mantras of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: śivānte śivatattve ca rudrakāraṇapālite // śivāntaṃ mantramuccārya tasmai deyaṃ pavitrakaṃ /
english: Similarly, in the principle relating to Śiva, he should recite the mantras of Śiva and invest that deity with the sacred thread.

sanskrit: sarvakāraṇapāleṣu śivamuccārya suvrataḥ // mūlaṃ layāntamuccārya dadyādgaṅgāvatārakaṃ /
english: O man of good practices! In the case of those governed by all the deities one should recite the principal mantra upto the end after having recited the mantras of Śiva and the descent of the Ganges should be accomplished.

sanskrit: ātmavidyāśivaiḥ proktaṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ pavitrakaṃ // vinirdiṣṭaṃ bubhukṣūṇāṃ śivatattvātmabhiḥ kramāt /
english: In the case of those who desire to get release from the cycle of births it is said that the sacred thread should be invested with the mantras of Śiva relating to the knowledge of the soul. For those who desire to get enjoyment it has been pointed out that the sacred thread should be invested duly with the mantras of the principles ofŚiva.

sanskrit: svāhāntaṃ vā namo 'ntaṃ vā mantrameṣāmudīrayet //
english: The mantras should be uttered ending with ‘oblation’ or ‘obeisance’.

sanskrit: natvā gaṅgāvatārantu prārthayettaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ /
english: Having made obeisance to the descent of the Ganges, he should pray to it with folded palms.

sanskrit: tvaṅgatiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃsthitistvañcarācare //
english: “You are the refuge for all beings. You reside in the movable and immovable beings.”

sanskrit: antaścāreṇa bhūtānāṃ draṣṭā tvaṃ parameśvara /
english: “O Supreme lord! You are the witness of the acts of beings by pervading inside the beings.

sanskrit: karmaṇā manasā vācā tvatto nānyā gatirmama //
english: By deed or thought or words have no other being to resort to except you.”

sanskrit: mantrahīnaṃ kriyāhīnaṃ dravyahīnañca yat kṛtaṃ / japahomārcanair hīnaṃ kṛtaṃ nityaṃ mayā tava //
english: “O Great lord! Whatever has been done defective in the mantra or deeds or in the materials of worship or in the repetition and worship in the daily observances, may you complete them.

sanskrit: akṛtaṃ vākyahīnaṃ ca tat pūraya maheśvaraṃ /
english: O Supreme lord! You are wellpurified.

sanskrit: supūtastvaṃ pareśāna pavitraṃ pāpanāśanaṃ //
english: You are pure and destroyer of sins.

sanskrit: tvayā pavitritaṃ sarvaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamaṃ /
english: Every being in the universe, the immovable and movable have been purified by you.

sanskrit: khaṇḍitaṃ yanmayā deva vrataṃ vaikalpayogataḥ //
english: “O lord! Whatever has been made defectively by me in my observances let it be free from becoming useless.

sanskrit: ekībhavatu tat sarvaṃ tavājñāsūtragumphitaṃ / japaṃ nivedya devasya bhaktyā stotraṃ vidhāya ca // natvā tu guruṇādiṣṭaṃ gṛhṇīyānniyamannaraḥ /
english: By your mandate let all of them become united, being tied in a string.” Having conveyed the recitation of the mantras to the lord and praising him devotedly, one should take up the vow after saluting the preceptor and as directed by him.

sanskrit: caturmāsaṃ trimāsaṃ vā tryahamekāhameva ca //
english: It should be for four months, or three months, or three days or one day.

sanskrit: praṇamya kṣamayitveśaṃ gatvā kuṇḍāntikaṃ vratī / pāvakasthe śive 'pyevaṃ pavitrāṇāṃ catuṣṭayaṃ // samāropya samabhyarcya puṣpadhūpākṣatādibhiḥ /
english: After having saluted the lord and seeking excuse, the votary should go near the sacrificial pit and cast four sacred threads for Śiva located in the fire, and worship with flowers, incense, unbroken rice etc.

sanskrit: antarbaliṃ pavitrañca rudrādibhyo nivedayet //
english: The oblation and holy thread should be presented to the Rudras.

sanskrit: praviśyāntaḥ śivaṃ stutvā sapraṇāmaṃ kṣamāpayet /
english: Having entered inside and praising Śiva the lord should be bid adieu with salutations.

sanskrit: prāyaścittakṛtaṃ homaṃ kṛtvā hutvā ca pāyasaṃ // śanaiḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ datvā vahnisthaṃ visṛjecchivaṃ / homaṃ vyāhṛtibhiḥ kṛtvā rundhyānniṣṭhurayānalaṃ //
english: After having made the expiatory oblation and oblation of sweet porridge, the final oblation should be offered and lord Śiva located in the fire should be bid farewell. Having performed oblations with the vyāhṛtis the syllables Oṃ bhūḥ, Oṃ bhuvaḥ etc., the fire should be obstructed with niṣṭhurii scornful goddess.

sanskrit: agnyādibhyastato dadyādāhutīnāṃ catuṣṭayaṃ /
english: Then four oblations should be offered to the firegod and others.

sanskrit: dikpatibhyastato dadyāt sapavitraṃ vahirbaliṃ // siddhāntapustake dadyāt sapramāṇaṃ pavitrakaṃ /
english: Oblation should be given outside along with a sacred thread to the guardian deities of all directions. Two theological books and a sacred thread should be offered.

sanskrit: homaṃ vyāhṛtibhiḥ kṛtvā datvā.ahuticatuṣṭayaṃ //
english: After having done the oblations with the vyāhṛtis, four oblations should be made as follows. Oṃ, hāṃ oblations to the firegod.

sanskrit: guruṃ śivamivābhyarcya vastrabhūṣādivistaraiḥ /
english: The preceptor should be worshipped as lord Śiva with clothes, ornaments and bed.

sanskrit: samagraṃ saphalaṃ tasya kriyākāṇḍādi vārṣikaṃ //
english: All annual rites etc. of the performer become fruitful if the preceptor gets satisfied.

sanskrit: yasya tuṣṭo guruḥ samyagityāha parameśvaraḥ /
english: The Supreme lord had said so.

sanskrit: itthaṃ guroḥ samāropya hṛdālambipavitrakaṃ // dvijātīn bhojayitvā tu bhaktyā vastrādikaṃ dadet /
english: Mter having placed the thread on the body of the preceptor thus, the brahmins should be fed and offered clothes etc.

sanskrit: dānenānena deveśa prīyatāṃ me sadā śivaḥ //
english: with devotion. “O lord of celestials! May lord Śiva get pleased by this gift of mine.”

sanskrit: bhaktyā snānādikaṃ prātaḥ kṛtvā śambhoḥ samāharet / pavitrāṇyaṣṭapuṣpaistaṃ pūjayitvā visarjayet //
english: After having bathed in the morning the investor should perform his daily rites of prayer and worship and take leave of god Śiva after having worshipped him and the sacred threads with eight flowers.

sanskrit: nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kṛtvā vistareṇa yathā purā / pavitrāṇi samāropya praṇamyāgnau śivaṃ yajet //
english: After having performed the nitya and naimittika rites as before in full, the sacred threads should be placed and lord Śiva should be worshipped in the fire after obeisance.

sanskrit: prāyaścittaṃ tato 'streṇa hutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ yajet /
english: The final oblation should then be given.

sanskrit: bhuktikāmaḥ śivāyātha kuryāt karmasamarpaṇaṃ //
english: One who is desirous of enjoyment should then submit the fruitsof his acts to lord Śiva.

sanskrit: tvatprasādena karmedaṃ māstu phalasādhakaṃ / muktikāmastu karmedaṃ māstu me nātha bandhakaṃ //
english: “May this rite of mine become fruitful by your grace! One who is desirous of release from the cycle of births should do this act as follows O lord! May there be no bondage for me.”

sanskrit: vahnisthaṃ nāḍīyogena śivaṃ saṃyojayechive / hṛdi nyasyāgnisaṅghātaṃ pāvakaṃ ca visarjayet //
english: Lord Śiva located in the fire should be united with lord Śiva in the solar plexus of the investor by nāḍīyoga assignment on limbs.

sanskrit: samācamya praviśyāntaḥ kumbhānugatasaṃvarān / śive saṃyojya sākṣepaṃ kṣamasveti visarjayet //
english: After having rinsed the mouth well, he should enter inside the shed and permeate the water of the pitcher with the essence of Śiva and bid farewell after saying “Pardon me”.

sanskrit: visṛjya lokapālādīnādāyeśāt pavitrakaṃ / sati caṇḍeśvare pūjāṃ kṛtvā datvā pavitrakaṃ //
english: After having taken leave of the guardian deities of the world, the sacred thread should be taken from the lord and placed on the Caṇḍeśvara form of the lord after worship.

sanskrit: tannirmālyādikaṃ tasmai sapavitraṃ samarpayet /
english: The materials of worship along with the sacred thread should be submitted to him.

sanskrit: athavā sthaṇḍile caṇḍaṃ vidhinā pūrvavadyajet //
english: In the alternative lord Caṇḍa should be worshipped on the sacrificial ground in the prescribed manner as before.
