english: Being desirous of attaining the other world, shall pray to the son of Mitra, born in a different continent and most dear to the gods.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ candanaṃ pratigṛhyatāṃ /
english: Kindly accept the sandal that is the king among the trees.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ bhājanī pāpanāśanī // saubhāgyārogyalakṣmīdā puṣpamālā pragṛhyatāṃ /
english: May you accept the garland, that is the destroyer of sins, the vessel of piety, wealth, desire and liberation and that which confers fortune, health and prosperity.

sanskrit: dhūpo 'yaṃ gṛhyatāṃ deva bhaktiṃ me hy acalāṅkuru //
english: O Lord! Let the incense be accepted. You make my devotion steady.

sanskrit: īpsitaṃ me varaṃ dehi paratra ca śubhāṅgatiṃ / surāsurairmuniśreṣṭha sarvakāmaphalaprada // vastravrīhiphalairhemnā dattastvarghyo hy ayaṃ mayā /
english: You confer on me the desired boon and also auspicious position in the next place got by the celestials and demons. O Excellent among the sages! Conferer of all the desired fruits! This libation has been offered by me together with clothes, rice, fruits and gold.

sanskrit: agastyaṃ bodhayiṣyāmi yanmayā manasoddhṛtaṃ //
english: make known to sage Agastya that which have raised with my mind.

sanskrit: phalairarghyaṃ pradāsyāmi gṛhāṇārghyaṃ mahāmune / agastya evaṃ khanamānaḥ khanitraiḥ prajāmapatyaṃ balamīhamānaḥ /
english: offer libation with fruits. You accept libation, O Great Sage!” Agastya being thus excavated with the spades gave men the desired progeny and strength.

sanskrit: ubhau karṇāvṛṣirugratejāḥ pupoṣa satyā deveṣvāśiṣo jagāma //
english: The sage with fierce splendour along with his chaste wife nourished the two ears. He then conferred blessing on the celestials.

sanskrit: rājaputri namastubhyaṃ munipatnī mahāvrate / arghyaṃ gṛhṇīṣva deveśi lopāmudre yaśasvini //
english: “O Daughter of a king! Obeisance to you, the wife of the sage Agastya! One who is a great devotee! O Governess of the celestials! Accept libation. O Lopāmudrā! One who is famous!

sanskrit: pañcaratnasamāyuktaṃ hemarūpyasamanvitaṃ / saptadhānyavṛtaṃ pātraṃ dadhicandanasaṃyutaṃ //
english: Libation should be offered to Agastya together with a vessel containing five gems, gold and silver and enclosed by seven kinds of grains as well as curd and sandal.

sanskrit: arghyaṃ dadyādagastyāya strīśūdrāṇāmavaidikaṃ /
english: The above libation should be done by women and śūdras without the recitation of the sacred syllables.

sanskrit: agastya muniśārdūla tejorāśe ca sarvada //
english: “O Agastya! Foremost among the sages! A multitude of splendour! Bestower of all things!”

sanskrit: imāṃ mama kṛtāṃ pūjāṃ gṛhītvā vraja śāntaye /
english: After having accepted this worship of mine you retreat in peace.

sanskrit: tyajedagastryamuddiśya dhānyamekaṃ phalaṃ rasaṃ //
english: One has to forego a kind of grain, a variety of fruit and a kind of taste for the sake of Agastya.

sanskrit: tato 'nnaṃ bhojayedviprān ghṛtapāyasamodakān /
english: Then the brahmins should be given food as well as ghee, sweet gruel and sweet balls.

sanskrit: gāṃ vāsāṃsi suvarṇañca tebhyo dadyācca dakṣiṇāṃ //
english: Cows, clothes and gold should be given to them as fees.

sanskrit: ghṛtapāyasayuktena pātreṇācchāditānanaṃ / sahiraṇyañca taṃ kumbhaṃ brāhmaṇāyopakalpayet //
english: That pitcher should be given to a brahmin together with gold and its mouth being covered by another vessel containing ghee and sweet gruel.

sanskrit: saptavarṣāṇi datvārghyaṃ sarve sarvamavāpnuyuḥ /
english: All would get all things by offering libation for seven years.

sanskrit: nīrā putrāṃś ca saubhāgyaṃ patiṃ kanyā nṛpodbhavaṃ //
english: A woman would get children and fortune and a girl would get a husband born to a king.

sanskrit: kaumudākhyaṃ mayoktañca caredāśvayuje site /
english: The Kaumudavrata, which has been described by me, should be practised in the bright fortnight in āśvayuji.

sanskrit: hariṃ yajet māsamekamekādaśyāmupoṣitaḥ //
english: After fasting on the eleventh day, lord Hari should be worshipped for a month.

sanskrit: āśvine śuklapakṣehamekāhārī hariṃ japan / māsamekaṃ bhuktimuktyai kariṣye kaumudaṃ vrataṃ // upoṣya viṣṇuṃ dvādaśyāṃ yajeddevaṃ vilipya ca / candanāgurukāśmīraiḥ kamalotpalapuṣpakaiḥ //
english: One should resolve as follows “ shall practise the Kaumudavrata taking food only once dailyin the bright fortnight in āśvina after repeating the name of Hari for a month, for the sake of enjoyment and emancipation”. After fasting, he should worship lord Viṣṇu, after having besmeared the lord with sandals, agallochum and saffron with lotus, blue lotus flowers or white lotuses or mālatī flower.

sanskrit: kalhārairvātha mālatyā dīpaṃ tailena vāgyataḥ /
english: He should offer a lamp with oil silently.

sanskrit: ahorātraṃ ca naivedyaṃ pāyasāpūpamodakaiḥ //
english: Offering of sweet gruel, cakes and sweet balls should be made day and night.

sanskrit: oṃ namo vāsudevāya vijñāpyātha kṣamāpayet /
english: “Oṃ obeisance to Vāsudeva”. Having made the offering with this syllable the vow should be completed.

sanskrit: bhojanādi dvije dadyādyāvad devaḥ prabuddhyate //
english: Food and other things should be given to a brahmin. The fast for a month would continue until the lord wakes up.

sanskrit: tāvanmāsopavāsaḥ syādadhikaṃ phalamapyataḥ /
english: If it is continued beyond that it would get greater benefit.

sanskrit: vratadānāni sāmānyaṃ pravadāmi samāsataḥ /
english: . shall describe briefly the vows and gifts in general .

sanskrit: tithau pratipadādau ca sūryādau kṛttikāsu ca // viṣkambhādau ca meṣādau kāle ca grahaṇādike / yat kāle yad vrataṃ dānaṃ yad dravyaṃ niyamādi yat //
english: Whichever vow or whichever gift or whichever article or the routines in whichever time such as the first lunar day and other days, on days such as the Sunday, in asterisms such as the kṛttikā, in viṣkumba a particular combination etc., in the constellations aries etc.

sanskrit: tad dravyākhyañca kālākhyaṃ sarvaṃ vai viṣṇudaivataṃ /
english: and at the time of the eclipses, lord Viṣṇu is the governing deity for all these materials, and time.

sanskrit: ravīśabrahmalakṣmyādyāḥ sarve viṣṇorvibhūtayaḥ //
english: Sun, Īśa, Brahmā, Lakṣmī and all others are the manifestations of lord Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tamuddiśya vrataṃ dānaṃ pūjādi syāttu sarvadaṃ /
english: The vow, gift, worship and other acts done for him would yield all things.

sanskrit: jagatpate samāgaccha āsanaṃ pādyamarghyakaṃ //
english: “O lord of the universe! You come here.

sanskrit: madhuparkaṃ tathācāmaṃ snānaṃ vastañca gandhakaṃ / puṣpaṃ dhūpaś ca dīpaś ca naivedyādi namo 'stu te //
english: Here are seat, water for washing the feet, waters of libation, the sweet drink, water for sipping, bathing, clothes, perfumes, flower, incense, lamp and offerings.

sanskrit: iti pūjāvrate dāne dānavākyaṃ samaṃ śṛṇu /
english: Obeisance to you.” This is the common statement in worship, vow and giving gift. The statement for giving a gift is similar. Listen to me.

sanskrit: adyāmukasagotrāya viprāyāmukaśarmaṇe // etad dravyaṃ viṣṇudaivaṃ sarvapāpopaśāntaye/
english: “Today offer this article dedicated to Viṣṇu to such and such a brahmin belonging to such and such a gotra.

sanskrit: āyurārogyavṛddhyarthaṃ saubhāgyādivivṛddhaye // gotrasantativṛddhyarthaṃ vijayāya dhanāya ca / dharmāyaiśvaryakāmāya tatpāpaśamanāya ca //
english: offer this gift to you for the appeasement of all sins, for increasing the longevity and health, for increasing the fortune, for furthering the progeny in the gotra, for conquest, wealth, piety, desire for prosperity, the removal of that sin, and release from mundane existence.

sanskrit: etaddānapratiṣṭhārthaṃ tubhyametad dadāmyahaṃ //
english: For the sake of the accomplishment of this gift am giving to you only.

sanskrit: etena prīyatāṃ nityaṃ sarvalokapatiḥ prabhuḥ /
english: May the lord, the master of the world, get permanently pleased with this.

sanskrit: yajñadānavratapate vidyākīrtyādi dehi me //
english: O Lord of sacrifice, gift and vow! Give me knowledge, fame and other things.

sanskrit: dharmakāmārthamokṣāṃś ca dehi me manasepsitaṃ /
english: Give me piety, desire, wealth and emancipation, that which is wished by the mind”.

sanskrit: yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyānnityaṃ vratadānasamuccayaṃ // sa prāptakāmo vimalo bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
english: Whoever reads this collection of vow and gift daily, would get the desires fulfilled, would become pure and get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: tithivārarkṣasaṅkrāntiyogamanvādikaṃ vrataṃ // naikadhā vāsudevāderniyamāt pūjanādbhavet /
english: The vows which should be practised under the auspices of different lunar days, weekdays, casterisms, positions of the sun, astral combinations and Manu and the like should not be practised by worshipping god Vāsudeva in one and the same way.

sanskrit: dānadharmān pravakṣyāmi bhuktimuktidān śṛṇu /
english: Listen to me. shall describe the charities that would bestow enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: dānamiṣṭaṃ tathā pūrtaṃ dharmaṃ kurvan hi sarvabhāk //
english: One who does acts of charity such as digging wells etc. would get all things.

sanskrit: vāpīkūpataḍāgāni devatāyatanāni ca / annapradānamārāmāḥ pūrtaṃ dharmaṃ ca muktidaṃ //
english: Digging reservoirs, wells and tanks, constructing temples, giving food and establishing gardens are known to be pūrtadharma, that confers emancipation.

sanskrit: agnihotraṃ tapaḥ satyaṃ vedānāñcānupālanaṃ / ātithyaṃ vaiśvadevañca prāhuriṣṭañca nākadaṃ //
english: Performing agnihotra a kind of sacrifice, penance, truth, protecting scriptures, serving guests, doing vaiśvadeva an offering made to the gods Viśvedevas are said to be iṣṭa that take one to heaven.

sanskrit: grahoparāge yaddānaṃ sūryasaṅkramaṇeṣu ca / dvādaśyādau ca yaddānaṃ pūrtaṃ tadapi nākadaṃ //
english: The gift made at the time of the eclipse of planets and that offeredat the time of the entry of the Sun from one constellation to another, gift made on the twelfth lunar days etc.

sanskrit: deśe kāle ca pātre ca dānaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet / ayane viṣuve puṇye vyatīpāte dinakṣaye // yugādiṣu ca saṅkrāntau caturdaśyaṣṭamīṣu ca / sitapañcadaśīsarvadvādaśīṣvaṣṭakāsu ca // yajñotsavavibāheṣu tathā manvantarādiṣu /
english: A gift at the proper place, time and to a proper person would be of crore merits especially in the transit of the Sun on the tropics, on the equinox, at the time of vyatīpāta, at the waning of the day, at different days beginning the cycles of period, at the transit of the Sun from one constellation to another, on the fourteenth days, on the eighth days, on the fullmoon days, on the twelfth days, at the time of aṣṭakas a collection of three days beginning from the seventh day after the full moon, at the time of sacrifices, festivals and marriages, at the Manuperiods, at the vidhṛti yoga, on having had a bad dream and when a good brahmin has been got.

sanskrit: śraddhā vā yaddine tatra sadā vā dānamiṣyate /
english: Otherwise it is desired that a gift has to be bestowed always upon those on whom one has the faith to do.

sanskrit: ayane dve vipuve dve catasraḥ ṣaḍaśītayaḥ // catasro viṣṇupadyaś ca saṅkrātyo dvādaśottamāḥ /
english: Tropical periods are two, equinoxes are two making up four. The eightysix auspicious periods arethe four viṣṇupadīs, the twelve transits of the Sun from one constellation to another and the transit of the Sun in virgo, gemini, pisces and sagittarious.

sanskrit: ṣaḍaśītimukhāḥ proktāḥ ṣaḍaśītiguṇāḥ phalaiḥ /
english: The eightysix periods are said to have eightysix times merits than ordinary periods.

sanskrit: atītānāgate puṇye dve udagdakṣiṇāyane // triṃśat karkaṭake nāḍyo makare viṃśatiḥ smṛtāḥ /
english: The two summer and winter solstices are meritorious when it has come and when it ḥhas not come i.e., thirty nāḍīs in cancer and twenty in capricorn respectively.

sanskrit: vartamāne tulāmeṣe nāḍyāstubhayato daśa //
english: When the Sun stays in the libra or aries it would be ten nāḍīs in both.

sanskrit: ṣaḍaśītyāṃ vyatītāyāṃ ṣaṣṭiruktāstu nāḍikāḥ /
english: In the eightysix periods described already sixty nāḍikās are auspicious after the Sun’s entry.

sanskrit: puṇyākhyā viṣṇupādyāñca prākpaścādapi ṣoḍaśa //
english: Among the auspicious periods of viṣṇupadī sixteen nāḍīs before and after are auspicious.

sanskrit: śravaṇāśvidhaniṣṭhāsu nāgadaivatamastake / yadā syādravivāreṇa vyatīpātaḥ sa ucyate //
english: It is said to be the vyatīpāta if the Sunday morning occurs in the asterisms śravaṇa, aśvani, dhaniṣṭhā and āśleṣā.

sanskrit: navamyāṃ śuklapakṣasya kārttike niragāt kṛtaṃ / tretā sitatṛtīyāyāṃ vaiśākhe dvāparaṃ yugaṃ // darśe vai māghamāsasya trayodaśyāṃ nabhasyake /
english: The kṛta yuga began on the ninth day in the bright fortnight in kārttika, the tretā yuga on the third day in the bright fortnight in vaiśākha, the Dvāpara yuga on the newmoon day in the month of māgha and the kali yuga on the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight in nabhasyaka bhādrapada.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇe kaliṃ vijānīyāj jñeyā manvantarādayaḥ //
english: One has to know them thus. One should also know the periods of Manu and others thus.

sanskrit: aśvayukacchuklanavamī dvādaśī kārttike tathā / tṛtīyā caiva māghasya tathā bhādrapadasya ca // phālgunasyāpyamāvāsyā pauṣasyaikādaśī tathā / āṣāḍhasyāpi daśamī māghamāsasya saptamī // āvāṇe cāṣṭamī kṛṣṇā tathāṣāḍhe ca pūrṇimā /
english: Gifts made on the ninth day of the white fortnight in aśvayuk, the twelfth day in kārttika, the third day in māgha and bhādrapada, the newmoon day in phālguna, the eleventh day in pauṣa, the tenth day in āṣāḍha, the seventh day in the month of māgha, the eighth day of the dark fortnight in śrāvaṇa, the fullmoon day in āṣāḍha, and similarly fifteenth day of kārttika, phālguna and jyaiṣṭha, the three aṣṭakas in the later part of āgrahāyaṇī DecemberJanuary and the eighth day known as the aṣṭaka confer undecaying benefits.

sanskrit: gayāgaṅgāprayāgādau tīrthe devālayādiṣu /
english: In the same way one should give gifts in the auspicious periods at sacred places like Gayā, the river Gaṅgā and Prayāga and temples etc.

sanskrit: aprārthitāni dānāni vidyārthaṃ kanyakā na hi //
english: Gifts should be made without being requested. But knowledge, wealth and girls should not be given as gifts thus.

sanskrit: dadyāt pūrvamukho dānaṃ gṛhṇīyāduttarāmukhaḥ /
english: Gift should be made facing the east and the gift should be received facing the north.

sanskrit: āyurvivardhate dāturgrahītuḥ kṣīyate na tat //
english: By this the longevity of the giver increases and that of the recipient does not decrease.

sanskrit: nāma gotraṃ samuccārya sampradānasya cātmanaḥ /
english: In general the name of the gotra of the recipient and their own selves are repeated and the gift is made by the givers.

sanskrit: sampradeyaṃ prayacchanti kanyādāne punastrayaṃ // snātvābhyarcya vyāhṛtibhirdadyāddānantu sodakaṃ /
english: Gift should be given after bathing and worshipping the deity along with the recitation of the vyāhṛtis the syllables bhū etc. of the gāyatrī mantra together with water.

sanskrit: kanakāśvatilā nāgā dāsīrathamahīgṛhāḥ // kanyā ca kapilā dhenurmahādānāni vai daśa / śrutaśauryatapaḥkanyāyājyaśiṣyādupagataṃ //
english: Gold, horse, sesamum, elephant, servant, chariot, earth, house, girl and tawny, cow are the ten great gifts. The money got by one’s learning, valour, penance, means of a girl, by officiating as a priest and through the disciple is said to be śulka fees, or bride’sprice etc..

sanskrit: śulkaṃ dhanaṃ hi sakalaṃ śulkaṃ śilpānuvṛttitaḥ /
english: All the wealth acquired by following some trade or work is also known as śulka.

sanskrit: kuśīdakṛṣivāṇijyaprāptaṃ yadupakārataḥ // pāśakadyūtacauryādipratirūpakasāhasaiḥ /
english: All that which was got by usury, agriculture and trade and that obtained as a favour and the one got by gambling, dice, stealing etc. and similar heroic pursuits are said to be acquired by some device.

sanskrit: vyājenopāvarjitaṃ kṛtsnaṃ trividhaṃ trividhaṃ phalaṃ //
english: The three kinds of acquisition have three different kinds of fruits.

sanskrit: adhyagnyadhyāvāhanikaṃ dattañca prītikarmaṇi / bhrātṛmātṛpitṛprāptaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ strīdhanaṃ smṛtaṃ //
english: Woman’s property is said to be of six kindsadhyagni gift made to a woman at the time of marriage, adhyāvāhanika gift made to a woman at the time of leaving her father’s house for her husband’s house, gift made by the husband out of love or affection and gifts got from the brother, mother or father.

sanskrit: brahmakṣatraviśāṃ dravyaṃ śūdrasyaiṣāmanugrahāt /
english: Brahmins, warriors and tradesmen have their own wealth. But a śūdra will have by their favour.

sanskrit: bahubhyo na pradeyāni gaurgṛhaṃ śayanaṃ stryiyaḥ //
english: One should not give as gift cow, house, bed and women to many.

sanskrit: kulānāntu śataṃ hanyādaprayacchan pratiśrutaṃ /
english: If one promises to give a gift and does not give, it would kill hundred of generations.

sanskrit: devānāñca gurūṇāñca mātāpitrostathaiva ca // puṇyaṃ deyaṃ prayatnena yat puṇyañcārjitaṃ kvacit /
english: Whatever little merit one has acquired should be made to the gods, preceptors, mothers and fathers with one’s effort.

sanskrit: pratilābhecchayā dattaṃ yaddhanaṃ tadapārthakaṃ //
english: The wealth that has been given as a gift with a view to have something in return would be useless.

sanskrit: śraddhayā sādhyate dharmo dattaṃ vāryapi cākṣayaṃ /
english: Piety is accomplished by faith. Even water given to the thirsty gets undiminishing merit.

sanskrit: jñānaśīlaguṇopetaḥ parapīḍāvahiṣkṛtaḥ // ajñānāṃ pālanāttrāṇāttat pātraṃ paramaṃ smṛtaṃ /
english: One is said to be an excellent person to receive a gift if he is endowed with knowledge, good conduct and quality, avoids doing harm to others and protects and saves the ignorant.

sanskrit: mātuḥ śataguṇaṃ dānaṃ sahasraṃ piturucyate //
english: A gift made to the mother is hundred times meritorious than the others, and that to the father is thousand times meritorious.

sanskrit: anantaṃ duhiturdānaṃ sodarye dattamakṣayaṃ /
english: The gift given to the daughter gets endless merits and that to the sister gets undecaying merits.

sanskrit: amanuṣye samaṃ dānaṃ pāpe jñeyaṃ mahāphalaṃ //
english: A gift given to a creature is of equal merit and that given to a sinner is of great merit.

sanskrit: varṇasaṅkare dviguṇaṃ śūdre dānaṃ caturguṇaṃ / vaiśye cāṣṭaguṇaṃ kṣatre ṣoḍaśatvaṃ dvijavruve //
english: A gift to a person of the mixed caste is two times meritorious, a gift to a śūdra is four times meritorious, to a vaiśya iseight times meritorious and to a kṣatriya is sixteen times meritorious.

sanskrit: vedādhyāye śataguṇamantaṃ vedabodhake /
english: Gift made to one who has studied the scriptures is hundred times meritworthy, to one who imparts the scriptures is of endless merit.

sanskrit: purohite yājakādau dānamakṣayamucyate // śrīvihīneṣu yaddattaṃ tadanantaṃ ca yajavani /
english: It is said that gift given to the priest and the officiating priest is of undecaying merit. Gift given to those devoid of wealth and to a sacrificer would be of limitless merit.

sanskrit: atapasvyanadhīyānaḥ pratigraharucirdvijaḥ // ambhasyaśmaplavenaiva saha tenaiva majjati /
english: A brahmin who does not do penances and study and has desire to accept gift would get drowned along with that just like a practitioner together with the stone in the floods.

sanskrit: snātaḥ samyagupaspṛśya gṛhṇīyāt prayataḥ śuciḥ // pratigrahītā sāvitrīṃ sarvadaiva prakīrtayet /
english: After bathing and touching waters properly one should accept the gift after becoming pure and restraining senses. The recipient of the gift should always repeat the sāvitrī gāyatrī.

sanskrit: tatastu kīrtayetsārdhaṃ dravyeṇa saha daivataṃ //
english: Then the deity should be glorified together with the materials.

sanskrit: pratigrāhī paṭheduccaiḥ pratigṛhya dvijottamāt / mandaṃ paṭhet kṣatriyāttu upāṃśu ca tathā viśaḥ // manasā ca tathā śūdrāt svastivācanakaṃ tathā /
english: The recipient should utter the complimentary words loudly after having received from an excellent brahmin, in a soft voice after receiving from a kṣatriya warrior, in a low voice after receiving from a viśa tradesman and mentally after receiving from a śūdra.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ sarvadaivatyaṃ bhūmirvai viṣṇudevatā //
english: All the gods are the presiding deities for the gift of protection. Viṣṇu is the deity of the earth.

sanskrit: kanyā dāsas tathā dāsī prājāpatyāḥ prakirtitāḥ / prājāpatyo gajaḥ proktasturago yamadaivataḥ //
english: Girl, servant and female servant are said to be governed by Prajāpati. An elephant is also governed by Prajāpati. The deity for the horse is Yama god of Death.

sanskrit: tathā caikaśaphaṃ sarvaṃ yāmyaś ca mahiṣas tathā /
english: Similarly all the onehoofed animals and the buffalo are governed by the God of Death.

sanskrit: uṣṭraś ca nairṛto dhenū raudrī chāgo 'nalas tathā // āpyo meṣo hariḥ krīḍa āraṇyāḥ paśavo 'nilāḥ / jalāśayaṃ vāruṇaṃ syādvāridhānīghaṭādayaḥ //
english: Nirṛti is the presiding deity of the camel, Śiva is that of a cow, Firegod is that of a goat, Varuṇa is that of a ram, Hari is that of a boar, Windgod is that of forest animals, Varuṇa for the tank, Varuṇa for vessels of water such as the pot etc.

sanskrit: samudrajāni ratnāni hemalauhāni cānalaḥ / prājāpatyāni śasyāni pakvānnamapi sattama // gāndharvaṃ gandhamityāhurvastraṃ vārhaspataṃ smṛtaṃ / vāyavyāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ sarve vidyā brāhmī tathāṅgakaṃ //
english: and gems got from the ocean, Firegod for gold and iron, Prajāpati for food grains and cooked food, Gandharva for fragrant material, Bṛhaspati for dress, Windgod for all birds, Brahmā for knowledge and its accessories, Sarasvatī for books etc., Viśvakarmā for sculpture, Vanaspati for the trees etc.

sanskrit: vanaspatirdrumādīnāṃ dravyadevā harestanuḥ //
english: The deities of the materials make up the body of Hari.

sanskrit: chatraṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ śayyā ratha āsanameva ca / upānahau tathā yānamuttānāṅgira īritaṃ //
english: Aṅgiras is said to be the deity of umbrella, antelopeskins, bed, chariot, seat, sandals and vehicle.

sanskrit: raṇopakaraṇaṃ śastraṃ dhvajādyaṃ sarvadaivataṃ /
english: All ammunitions, weapons, banners etc. are governed by all the gods.

sanskrit: gṛhañca sarvadaivatyaṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣṇudevatā //
english: A house also is governed by all the gods. Lord Viṣṇu is the presiding deity of all things.

sanskrit: śivo vā na tato dravyaṃ vyatiriktaṃ yato 'sti hi /
english: Or Śiva may be the presiding deity because there is no other article besides the above.

sanskrit: dravyasya nāma gṛhṇīyāddadānīti tathā vadet //
english: One should mention the name of the material and say that “ giving”.

sanskrit: toyaṃ dadyāttato haste dāne vidhirayaṃ smṛtaḥ /
english: Then water should be given on the hand. This is known to be the procedure in all gifts.

sanskrit: viṣṇurdātā viṣṇurdravyaṃ pratigṛhṇāmi vai vadet //
english: The receiver should say “Lord Viṣṇu is the giver. Lord Viṣṇu is the materials.

sanskrit: svasti pratigrahaṃ dharmaṃ bhuktimuktī phaladvayaṃ /
english: am receiving.” Wishing the welfare of the giver is the duty of the recipient that confers the two fruits of enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: gurūn bhṛtyānna jihīrṣurarciṣyan devatāḥ pitṝn //
english: One may accept gift from all for protecting the preceptors and servants and also to propitiate gods and manes.

sanskrit: sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyānna tu tṛpyet svayantataḥ /
english: But he should not get satisfied with that.

sanskrit: śūdrīyanna tu yajñārthaṃ dhanaṃ śūdrasya tatphalaṃ //
english: Money should not be taken from a śūdra for the sake of sacrifice. The benefit of that would reach the śūdra.

sanskrit: guḍatakrarasādyāś ca śūdrādgrāhyā nivartinā /
english: Molasses, buttermilk and juices etc. may be accepted by an anchorite from a śūdra.

sanskrit: sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyādavṛtyākarṣito dvijaḥ //
english: A brahmin struggling for his existence may accept gift from all.

sanskrit: nādhyāpanādyājanādvā garhitādvā pratigrahāt / doṣo bhavati viprāṇāṃ jvalanārkasamā hi te //
english: If the brahmins are associated with fire and sun there cannot be any defect in teaching performing sacrifice or by accepting a gift from a prohibited person.

sanskrit: kṛte tu dīyate gatvā tretāsvānīya dīyate /
english: A gift is given in the kṛtayuga by approaching the person, is given in the tretāyuga after inviting the person concerned.

sanskrit: dvāpāre yācamānāya kalau tvanugamānvite //
english: A gift is made in the Dvāparayuga to one who seeks and in the kaliyuga to one who follows and begs.

sanskrit: manasā pātramuddiśya jalaṃ bhūmau vinikṣipet /
english: Water should be poured on the ground after mentally resolving to give to a suitable person.

sanskrit: vidyate sāgarasyānto nānto dānasya vidyate //
english: The ocean has its limit. But there is no limit for the gift .

sanskrit: adya somārkagrahaṇasaṅkrāntyādau ca kālake / gaṅgāgayāprayāgādau tīrthadeśe mahāguṇe // tathā cāmukagotrāya tathā cāmukaśarmaṇe / vedavedāṅgayuktāya pātrāya sumahātmane //
english: shall give to such and such a person belonging to such and such a gotra, who is a good soul, and a proper person who is learned in the Vedas and its accessories at the time of the eclipse of the Moon and Sun, at the entry of the Sun into a constellation, at the sacred places of great merit such as the Ganges, Gayā, Prayāga etc.

sanskrit: yathānāma mahādravyaṃ viṣṇurudrādidaivataṃ / putrapautragṛhaiśvaryapatnīdharmārthasadguṇā // kīttividyāmahākāmasaubhāgyārogyavṛddhaye / sarvapāpopaśāntyarthaṃ svargārthaṃ bhuktimuktaye //
english: “ make a gift of such and such an article for which Viṣṇu and Śiva and others, are the presiding deities for the sake of getting children, grand children, house, fortune, wife endowed with good qualities and for the increase of fame, learning, desire, fortune and health and for the destruction of all sins and for getting heaven, enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: etattubhyaṃ sampradade prīyatāṃ me hariḥ śivaḥ / divyāntarīkṣabhaumādisamutpātaughaghātakṛt //
english: give this to you. May lord Hari identical with Śiva, the destroyer of spate of evils belonging to the heaven, sky and earth be pleased.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmamokṣāptyai brahmalokaprado 'stu me /
english: May you be the conferer of the world of Brahmā on me for the sake of getting the piety, wealth and desire.

sanskrit: etaddānapratiṣṭhārthaṃ suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dade /
english: offer gold as fee to such and such a brahmin of such and, such a gotra for the sake of making this gift established”.

sanskrit: anena dānavākyena sarvadānāni vai dadet //
english: All gifts should be made with this sentence for giving a gift.

sanskrit: sarvadānāni vakṣyāmi mahādānāni ṣoḍaśa /
english: shall describe all the gifts. The great gifts are sixteen.

sanskrit: tulāpuruṣa ādyantu hiraṇyagarbhadānakaṃ // brahmāṇḍaṃ kalpavṛkṣaś ca gosahasrañca pañcamaṃ /
english: The gift known as the tulāpuruṣa is the first. The others are gift of hiraṇyagarbha, brahmāṇḍa kalpavṛkṣa celestial tree. The fifth one is the gift of thousand cows.

sanskrit: hiraṇyakāmadhenuś ca hiraṇyāśvaś ca saptamaṃ //
english: The gift of golden kāmadhenu the celestial cow is the sixth one. The seventh one is the gift of golden horse.

sanskrit: hiraṇyāśvarathastadvaddhemahastirathas tathā /
english: The other gifts are the golden horse and chariot and the golden elephant and horse.

sanskrit: pañcalāṅgalakantadvaddharādānaṃ tathaiva ca // viśvacakraṃ kalpalatā saptasāgarakaṃ paraṃ /
english: Then the remaining gifts are five ploughs and the gift of earth, viśvacakra, kalpalatā, the excellent seven oceans, ratnadhenu and mahābhūtaghaṭa.

sanskrit: ratnadhenurmahābhūtaghaṭaḥ śubhadine 'rpayet // maṇḍape maṇḍale dānaṃ devān prārcyārpayeddvije /
english: The gift should be given on an auspicious day. Gift should be given to a brahmin after having worshipped gods in a circle in a shed.

sanskrit: merudānāni puṇyāni meravo daśa tān śṛṇu //
english: Listen to me. shall describe ten gifts known as merudāna heaps of different things.

sanskrit: dhānyadroṇasahasreṇa uttamo 'rdhārdhataḥ parau /
english: The best gift is that of a thousand droṇas a measure of grains. The rest are successively half the quantity of the preceding ones.

sanskrit: uttamaḥ ṣoḍaśadroṇaḥ kartavyo lavaṇācalaḥ // daśabhārair guḍādriḥ syāduttamo 'rdhārdhataḥ parau /
english: An excellent gift of a mountain of salt should be given consisting of sixteen droṇas. An excellent gift of a mountain of molasses would be often bhāras a measure}.

sanskrit: uttamaḥ palasāhasraiḥ svarṇamerus tathā parau //
english: An excellent hill of gold would be of thousand palas a measure of weight and the rest as that described above.

sanskrit: daśadroṇaistilādriḥ syāt pañcabhiś ca tribhiḥ kramāt /
english: A hill of sesamum would be of ten droṇas the rest being duly five and three droṇas.

sanskrit: kārpāsaparvato viṃśabhāraiś ca daśapañcabhiḥ //
english: The hill of cotton would be twenty, ten and five bhāras respectively.

sanskrit: viṃśatyā ghṛhakumbhānāmuttamaḥ syād ghṛtācalaḥ /
english: An excellent hill of ghee would be twenty pots of ghee.

sanskrit: daśabhiḥ palasāhasrair uttamo rajatācalaḥ //
english: An excellent hill of silver would be ten thousand palas.

sanskrit: aṣṭabhāraiḥ śarkarādrirmadhyomando 'rdhato 'rdhataḥ /
english: An excellent hill of sugar would be eight bhāras and the medium would be half that and the inferior still half that.

sanskrit: daśa dhenūḥ pravakṣyāmi yā dattvā bhuktimuktibhāk //
english: shall describe the ten cows by giving which one would get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: prathamā guḍadhenuḥ syād ghṛtadhenus tathāparā /
english: The first one would be the cow of molasses and the next one would be the. cow of ghee.

sanskrit: tiladhenustṛtoyā ca caturthī jaladhenukā // kṣīradhenurmadhudhenuḥ śarkarādadhidhenuke /
english: The third one is the cow of sesamum and the fourth one cow of water. The others are cow of milk, cow of honey, cow of sugar, cow of curd and the cow of juices.

sanskrit: rasadhenuḥ svarūpeṇa daśamī vidhirucyate //
english: The tenth one is the cow in its natural form. This is said to be the rule governing the ten cows.

sanskrit: kumbhāḥ syurdravadhenūnāmitarāsāntu rāśayaḥ /
english: But they should be a heap in the case of other materials.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇājinañcaturhastaṃ prāggrīvaṃ vinyasedbhuvi // gomayenānuliptāyāṃ darbhānāstīrya sarvataḥ / laghvaiṇakājinaṃ tadvadvatsasya parikalpayet //
english: One should place a deer skin of four cubits length on the ground besmeared with cow dung with the neck part on the east. Darbha should be spread everywhere. Similarly a seat should be made for the calf with the tender skin of eṇaka a kind of black antelope.

sanskrit: prāṅmukhīṃ kalpayeddhenumudakpādāṃ savatsakāṃ / uttamā guḍadhenuḥ syāt sadā bhāracatuṣṭayāt //
english: The cow together with the calf should be arranged such as it faces the east and the feet point to the north. An excellent gift of cow of molasses would always be of four bhāras out of which the calf should be of one bhāra.

sanskrit: vatsaṃ bhāreṇa kurvīta bhārābhyāṃ madhyamā smṛtā /
english: The middle type is known to be of two Bhāras for the cow and half a bhāra for the calf.

sanskrit: ardhabhāreṇa vatsaḥ syāt kaniṣṭhā bhārakeṇa tu // caturthāṃśena vatsaḥ syād guḍavittānusārataḥ /
english: The last type should be one bhāra for the cow and a quarter bhāra for the calf. Otherwise the gift may be made according to the molasses and wealth one may have.

sanskrit: pañca kṛṣṇalakā māṣaste suvarnastu ṣoḍaśa //
english: One māṣa a measure is five kṛṣṇalakas seed of the guñja plant. One suvarṇa is equal to sixteen māṣas.

sanskrit: palaṃ suvarṇāś catvārastulā palaśataṃ smṛtaṃ /
english: One pala is equal to four suvarṇas. One tulā is known to be one hundred palas.

sanskrit: syādbhāro viṃśatitulā droṇastu caturāḍhakaḥ //
english: A bhāra would be twenty tulās. One droṇa is equal to four āḍhaka.

sanskrit: dhenuvatsau guḍasyobhau sitasūkṣmāmbarāvṛtau / śuktikarṇāvikṣupādau śucimuktāphalekṣaṇau //
english: The cow and the calf both made of the molasses should be covered by a thin white cloth. The ears should be made of pearl oyster, the feet of sugarcane and the eyes of pure pearls.

sanskrit: sitasūtraśirālau ca sitakambalakamvalau / tāmragaḍḍukapṛṣṭhau tau sitacāmararomakau // vidrumabhrūyugāvetau navanītastanānvitau / kṣaumapucchau kāṃsyadohāvindranīlakatārakau //
english: The veins should be made of white thread, the woollen blankets for spreading of white wool, the backside with copper vases, the hairs with white chowrie, the two eyebrows with coral, the breast with butter, the tail with silken cloth, the milk pails made of bronze and the pupils with sapphire.

sanskrit: suvarṇaśṛṅgābharaṇau rajatakṣurasaṃyutau /
english: The ornaments on the horns should be made of gold and the hoofs of silver.

sanskrit: nānāphalamayā dantā gandhaghrāṇaprakalpitau //
english: The teeth should be of different kinds of fruits and the nose of sandal.

sanskrit: racayitvā yajeddhenumimair mantrair dvijottama /
english: O Brahmin! After having made ready the cow, it should be worshipped with these sacred syllables.

sanskrit: yā lakṣmīḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yā ca deveṣvavasthitā // dhenurūpeṇa sā devī mama śāntiṃ prayacchatu /
english: “That goddess who is the fortune of all beings and who remains in the celestials may in the form of the cow give me peace.

sanskrit: dehasthā yā ca rudrāṇī śaṅkarasya sadā priyā // dhenurūpeṇa sā devī mama pāpaṃ vyapohatu /
english: The goddess Rudrāṇī is always dear to lord Śaṅkara and remains in the body, may that goddess in the form of the cow dispel my sin.

sanskrit: viṣṇuvakṣasi yā lakṣmīḥ svāhā yā ca vibhāvasoḥ // candrārkaṛkṣaśaktiryā dhenurūpāstu sā śriye / caturmukhasya yā lakṣmīryā lakṣmīrdhanadasya ca // lakṣmīryā lokapālānāṃ sa dhenurvaradāstu me /
english: That one who is on the chest of lord Viṣṇu and who is the Svāhā for the fire, who is the energy of the moon, sun and star, that is of the form of the cow O Goddess of Fortune! May that cow which is the fortune of the fourfaced one Brahmā, the god of wealth and the guardian deity of the world, be the conferer on me.

sanskrit: svadhā tvaṃ pitṛmukhyānāṃ svāhā yajñabhujāṃ yataḥ //
english: You are the svadhā oblation of food for all the manes and the svāhā for the partakers of sacrifices.

sanskrit: sarvapāpaharā dhenustasmācchāntiṃ prayaccha me /
english: Hence you are the cow that removes all sins. Hence you get me peace”.

sanskrit: evamāmantritāṃ dhenuṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet //
english: The cow that has been sanctified thus should be given to a brahmin.

sanskrit: samānaṃ sarvadhenūnāṃ vidhānaṃ caitadeva hi /
english: The same procedure holds good for the offerings of all kinds of cows mentioned already.

sanskrit: sarvayajñaphalaṃ prāpya nirmalo bhuktimuktibhāk //
english: After having obtained the benefits of all sacrifices one would become pure and get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: svarṇaśṛṅgo śaphai raupyaiḥ suśīlā vastrasaṃyutā / kāṃsyopadohā dātavyā kṣoriṇau gauḥ sadakṣiṇā //
english: One should give as a gift a cow having golden horns, silvery hoofs, of good conduct and having udders with bronze, with milk and decked with cloth together with the fees.

sanskrit: dātāsyāḥ svargamāpnoti vatsarān somasammitān / kapilā cettārayati bhūyaścāsaptamaṃ kulaṃ //
english: One who gives such a cow would stay in heaven for as many years as the number of hairs on its body. If it is a tawny cow it would again elevate seven generations of the giver.

sanskrit: svarṇaśṛṅgīṃ raupyakhurāṃ kāṃsyadohanakānvitāṃ / śaktito dakṣiṇāyuktāṃ dattvā syādbhuktimuktibhāk //
english: One who gives a cow having golden horns, silvery hoofs and bronze attached udders together with fees befitting one’s capacity would get enjoyment and emancipation after giving.

sanskrit: dattvā svargamavāpnoti pūrveṇa vidhinā dadet // āsannamṛtyunā deyā savatsā gaustu pūrvavat /
english: It should be given as laid down before. A cow and a calf should be given as a gift by one that is about to die as laid down before.

sanskrit: yamadvāre mahāvīre taptā vaitaraṇī nadī //
english: He should say “There is the dark Vaitaraṇī river at the dreadful entrance to the place of the God of Death.

sanskrit: tāntartuñca dadāmyenāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ vaitaraṇīñca gāṃ /
english: am giving this black cow in order to cross that Vaitaraṇī.”

sanskrit: ekāṅgāṃ daśagurdadyāddaśa dadyācca gośatī /
english: One who has ten cows should give one. One having hundred cows should give ten cows.

sanskrit: śataṃ sahasragurdadyāt sarve tulyaphalā hi te //
english: A person having a thousand cows should give hundred. All yield the same benefit.

sanskrit: prāsādā yatra sauvarṇā vasordhārā ca yatra sā / gandharvāpsaraso yatra tatra yānti sahasradāḥ //
english: Those who give thousand cows as gift would go to a place where the mansions are golden, there would be flow of wealth and the gandharvas and celestial nymphs dwell.

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatapradānena mucyate narakārṇavāt /
english: By giving hundred cows one becomes free from the ocean of hells.

sanskrit: dattvā vatsatarīṃ caiva svarhaloke mahīyate // godānādāyurārogyasaubhāgyasvargamāpnuyāt /
english: By giving a weaned calf one stays in comfort in the heaven. By the gift of a cow one would get longevity, health, fortune and heaven.

sanskrit: indrādilokapālānāṃ yā rājamahiṣī śubhā // mahiṣīdānamāhātmyādastu me sarvakāmadā /
english: She is the auspicious queen of the guardian deities such as Indra and the like may she be the bestower of all my desires by the greatness of the gift of the shebuffalo.

sanskrit: dharmarājasya sāhāyye yasyāḥ putraḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ // mahiṣāsurasya jananī yā sāstu varadā mama /
english: That mother of the demon in the form of buffalo the children of which woman are established by the assistance of the Lord of Dharma, may be the bestower of wealth on me.

sanskrit: mahiṣīdānācca saubhāgyaṃ vṛṣadānāddivaṃ vrajet //
english: One would get fortune by giving a shebuffalo and reach heaven by giving a bull.

sanskrit: saṃyuktahalapaṅktyākhyaṃ dānaṃ sarvaphalapradaṃ /
english: The gift known as saṃyuktahalapaṅkti attached with ten ploughs confers all fruits.

sanskrit: paṅktirdaśahalā proktā dārujā vṛṣasaṃyutā //
english: A collection of ten ploughs is said to be a paṅkti. They should be made of wood and yoked to bulls.

sanskrit: sauvarṇapaṭṭasannaddhāndattvā svarge mahīyate /
english: One would stay in heaven by giving them bound with golden strips.

sanskrit: daśānāṃ kapilānāṃ tu dattānāṃ jyeṣṭhapuṣkare // tat phalañcākṣayaṃ proktaṃ vṛṣabhasya tu mokṣaṇe /
english: The benefits of giving ten tawny cows at the Puṣkara a sacred place in the month of jyeṣṭhā is said to be undecaying. Similar benefit would accrue by releasing a bull.

sanskrit: dharmo 'sitvañcatuṣpādaś catasraste priyā imāḥ //
english: One should say “O Fourfooted one! You are the virtue. These four are dear to you.

sanskrit: namo brahmaṇyadeveśa pitṛbhūtarṣipoṣaka / tvayi mukte 'kṣayā lokā mama santu nirāmayāḥ //
english: O lord of Viṣṇu! One who nourishes the manes, beings and the sages! Let me have the worlds free blemishes and undecaying when you are released.

sanskrit: mā me ṛṇo 'stu daivatyo bhautaḥ paitro 'tha mānuṣaḥ /
english: May not have the debts due to the gods, beings, manes and mortals.

sanskrit: dharmastvaṃ tvatprapannasya yā gatiḥ sāstu me dhruvā //
english: You are the virtue. That fate which befalls one who resorts to you, let it be firm in me.”

sanskrit: aṅgayeccakraśūlābhyāṃ mantreṇānena cotsṛjet /
english: One should mark the bull with the circles and spears and let it go with these sacred syllables described above.

sanskrit: ekādaśāhe pretasya yasya cotsṛjyate vṛṣaḥ // mucyate pretalokāttu ṣaṇmāse cāvdikādiṣu /
english: If a bull is released on the eleventh day of a dead person he would be freed from the world of the dead. The same benefit would accrue if a bull is let loose at the time of sixmonthly ceremony and annual ceremony for the dead.

sanskrit: daśahastena kuṇḍena triṃśatkuṇḍānnivartanaṃ //
english: A nivarttana would be of thirty kuṇḍas, each kuṇḍa being ten cubits.

sanskrit: tānyeva daśavistārādgocarme tatprado 'ghabhit /
english: The ground extending to ten times the nivartana is jplpwṇ to be gocarma.

sanskrit: gobhūhiraṇyasaṃyuktaṃ kṛṣṇājinantu yo 'rpayet // sarvaduṣkṛtakarmāpi sāyujyaṃ brahmaṇo vrajet /
english: One who gives deer’s skin together with a cow, earth and gold would get united with lord Brahmā, even though he had done many sinful deeds.

sanskrit: bhājanantilasampūrṇaṃ madhunā pūrṇameva ca // dadyāt kṛṣṇatilānāñca prasthamekañca māgadhaṃ /
english: One may give vessels filled with sesamum, honey and black sesamum as well as a prastha a particular measure of long pepper.

sanskrit: śayyāṃ dattvā tu saguṇāṃ bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt //
english: Having given a bed of good quality one may get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: haimīṃ pratikṛtiṃ kṛtvā dattvā svargas tathātmanaḥ /
english: After having made a golden image of the self and given the same as a gift, the giver could reach heaven.

sanskrit: vipulantu gṛhaṃ kṛtvā dattvā syādbhuktimuktibhāk //
english: After having made a large house and giving it one would get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: gṛhaṃ maṭhaṃ sabhāṃ svargī dattvā syācca pratiśriyaṃ / dattvā kṛtvā gogṛhañca niṣpāpaḥ svargamāpnuyāt // yamamāhiṣadānāttu niṣpāpaḥ svargamāpnuyāt /
english: One would reach heaven by giving a house, a hut for an ascetic, hall and shelter. One who builds a cattleshed and gifts it would be free from sin and reach heaven. One who makes a gift of the buffalo the vehicle of the God of Death would be free from sin and would go to heaven.

sanskrit: brahmā haro harirdevair madhye ca yamadūtakaḥ // pāśī tasya śiraśchittvā taṃ dadyāt svargabhāgbhavet /
english: One who gives as a gift the images of gods Brahmā Hara Śiva, Hari with the celestials and the messenger of the God of Death in their middle and the god Pāśī Varuṇa as cutting the head of the latter would reach heaven.

sanskrit: trimukhākhyamidaṃ dānaṃ gṛhītvā tu dvijo 'ghabhāk //
english: A brahmin who accepts this gift known as the ‘threefaced’ would incur sin.

sanskrit: cakraṃ rūpyamayaṃ kṛtvā ke dhṛtvā tat pradāpayet / hemayuktaṃ dvijāyaitat kālacakramidammahat //
english: One should give to a brahmin a wheel made of silver together with gold after having placed it on his own lap. This is known as the ‘wheel of time’ of great merit.

sanskrit: ātmatulyantu yo lauhaṃ dadenna narakaṃ vrajet /
english: One who makes a gift of iron equal to one’s weight would not go to hell.

sanskrit: pañcāśatpalasaṃyuktaṃ lauhadaṇḍaṃ tu yo 'rpayet // vastreṇācchādya viprāya yamadaṇḍo na vidyate /
english: One who gives an iron rod of fifty palas covered by a cloth to a brahmin would not get the chastising rod of the God of Death.

sanskrit: mūlaṃ phalādi vā dravyaṃ saṃhataṃ vātha caikaśaḥ // mṛtyujjayaṃ samuddiśya dadyādāyurvivardhaye /
english: One should give the root or fruit or other material collectively or separately for the Conqueror of Death for the increase of one’s life.

sanskrit: pumān kṛṣṇatilaiḥ kāryo raupyadantaḥ suvarṇadṛk // khaḍgodyatakaro dīrgho javākusumamaṇḍalaḥ / raktāmvaradharaḥ sragvī śaṅkamālāvibhūṣitaḥ // upānadyugayuktāṅghriḥ kṛṣṇakambalapārśvakaḥ /
english: One should make a figure of a man with black sesamum, with the teeth made of silver, eye made of gold, wielding a sword in the hand, bedecked with japā flowers, wearing red cloth, adorned with a garland of conchshells, the feet having a pair of sandals, the sides covered by black wool and holding a ball of flesh in his left hand. He is known as the embodiment of time.

sanskrit: sampūjya tañca gandhādyaiḥ brāhmaṇāyopapādayet /
english: After having worshipped that image with perfumes and other things, it should be given to a brahmin.

sanskrit: maraṇavyādhihīnaḥ syādrājarājeśvaro bhavet //
english: Such a giver would be free from death and disease and become a monarch.

sanskrit: govṛṣau tu dvije dattvā bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
english: One who gives a gift of a, cow and a bull to a brahmin would get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: revantādhiṣṭhitañcāśvaṃ haimaṃ dattvā na mṛtybhāk //
english: One would not die by giving a golden hairy horse.

sanskrit: ghaṇṭādipūrṇamapyekaṃ dattvā syādbhuktimuktibhāk /
english: One who makes such a gift endowed with bells would also get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: sarvān kāmānavāpnoti yaḥ prayacchati kāñcanaṃ //
english: One who gives gold would get the desired things.

sanskrit: suvarṇe dīyamāne tu rajataṃ dakṣiṇeṣyate / anyeṣāmapi dānānāṃ suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇā smṛtā //
english: When gold is given as gift, silver should be given as remuneration. Gold is the remuneration even in the case of other gifts.

sanskrit: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ taṇḍulaṃ dhānyameva ca / nityaśrāddhaṃ devapūjā sarvametadadakṣiṇaṃ //
english: No remuneration should be given when gold, silver, copper, rice and other grains are given as gift or at the daily ceremony for the manes and at the worship of gods.

sanskrit: rajataṃ dakṣiṇā pitre dharmakāmārthasādhanaṃ /
english: Silver given as remuneration at the ceremony for the manes is a means to get piety, pleasure and material comfort.

sanskrit: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ maṇimuktāvasūni ca // sarvametanmahāprājño dadāti vasudhāndadat /
english: A wiseman who gives land as a gift should also give gold, silver, copper, gems, pearls, wealth and all other things.

sanskrit: pitṝṃś ca pitṛlokasthān devasthāne ca devatāḥ // santarpayati śāntātmā yo dadāti vasundharām /
english: One who makes a gift of land, that composed man satisfies the manes in their world and the gods in the world of gods.

sanskrit: kharvaṭaṃ kheṭakaṃ vāpi grāmaṃ vā śasyaśālinaṃ // nivartanaśataṃ vāpi tadardhaṃ vā gṛhādikaṃ /
english: One who gives as a gift a market town or small town or village or field abound with grains or hundred nivartana or half of that or a house etc.

sanskrit: api gocarmamātrāmbā dattvorvīṃ sarvabhāg bhavet //
english: or only gocarma extent of land would get all things.

sanskrit: tailavinduryathā cāpsu prasarped bhūgataṃ tathā / sarveṣāmevadānānamekajanmānugaṃ phalaṃ //
english: Just as a drop of oil spreads on the waters so also the fruit of all gifts would follow the mortal in the next birth.

sanskrit: hāṭakakṣitigaurīṇāṃ saptajanmānugaṃ phalaṃ /
english: The benefit of making a gift of gold, land and an eight year old girl would follow the giver in his seven births.

sanskrit: trisaptakulamuddhṛtya kanyādo brahmalokabhāk //
english: One who gives a girl in marriage would elevate twentyone generations of his family and attain the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: gajaṃ sadakṣiṇaṃ dattvā nirmalaḥ svargabhāg bhavet / aśvaṃ dattvāyurārogyasaubhāgyasvargamāpnuyāt //
english: Having given an elephant together with remuneration one becomes free from blemish and would attain heaven. Having given a horse one would get long and healthy life and fortune and ascend heaven.

sanskrit: dāsīṃ dattvā dvijendrāya apsarolokamāpnuyāt /
english: One who gives a maid servant to an excellent brahmin would reach the world of nymphs.

sanskrit: dattvā tāmramayīṃ sthālīṃ palānāṃ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ // ardhaistadardhair ardhair vā bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
english: Having given a copper plate weighing five hundred palas a measure of weight or half the weight or a quarter of that weight or oneeighth of the weight would get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: śakaṭaṃ vṛṣasaṃyuktaṃ dattvā yānena nākabhāk // vastradānāllabhedāyurārogyaṃ svargamakṣayaṃ /
english: By giving a cart together with a bull one would go to heaven by means of a cart. One who makes a gift of cloth would get longevity, health and undecaying heaven.

sanskrit: dhānyagodhūmakalamayavādīn svargabhāg dadat // āsanaṃ taijasaṃ pātraṃ lavaṇaṃ gandhacandanaṃ /
english: Having given as a gift a seat, metallic vessel, salt, fragrant sandal, incense, lamp, betel, iron, silver, gem and other rare materials, one would get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: tilāṃś ca tilapātrañca dattvā svargamavāpnuyāt //
english: One would ascend heaven by giving sesamum and a vessel for keeping sesamum.

sanskrit: annadānāt paraṃ nāsti na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati /
english: There is nothing superior to the gift of food. Neither there was nor there would be.

sanskrit: hastyaśvarathadānāni dāsīdāsagṛhāṇi ca // annadānasya sarvāṇi kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīṃ /
english: The merit of gift of an elephant, horse, chariot, maidservant, servant and house will not equal a sixteenth part of the merit of giving food.

sanskrit: kṛtvāpi sumahatpāpaṃ yaḥ paścādannado bhavet // sarvapāpavinirmukto lokānāpnoti cākṣayān /
english: One who gives food after committing a great sin would become free from all sins and attain undecaying worlds.

sanskrit: pānīyañca prapāndattvā bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt // agniṃ kāṣṭhañca mārgādau dattvā dīptyādimāpnuyāt /
english: One who sets up a place for distributing water for drinking would get enjoyment and emancipation. By giving fire and firewood for travellers on the way, one would get radiance etc.

sanskrit: devagandharvanārībhirvimāne sevyate divi //
english: and would be served in the celestialvehicle in heaven by the celestials, gandharvas and women.

sanskrit: ghṛtaṃ taikañca lavaṇaṃ dattvā sarvamavāpnuyāt /
english: One would get all things by giving ghee, oil and salt.

sanskrit: chatropānahakāṣṭhādi dattvā svarge sukhī vaset //
english: After having given umbrella, sandal and firewood etc. one would dwell in heaven happily.

sanskrit: pratipattithimukhyeṣu viṣkumbhādikayogake / caitrādau vatsarādau ca aśvinyādau hariṃ haraṃ // brahmāṇaṃ lokapālādīn prārcya dānaṃ mahāphalaṃ /
english: A gift made after worshipping lords Hari, Hara, Brahmā and the guardian deities on the important lunar days like the first etc., on the combinations known as viṣkamhha etc., in the months caitra and others, in the years and the asterisms aśvinī etc. is of great merit.

sanskrit: vṛkṣārāmān bhojanādīn mārgasaṃvāhanādikān // pādābhyaṅgādikaṃ dattvā bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
english: One would get enjoyment and emancipation by providing shady trees, feeding places, vehicles to carry burden and for anointing the feet.

sanskrit: trīṇi tulyaphalānīha gāvaḥ pṛthvī sarasvatī //
english: There are three things which are of equal merits. They arecows, land and imparting knowledge.

sanskrit: vrāhmīṃ sarasvatīndattvā nirmalo brahmalokabhāk / saptadvīpamahīdaḥ sa brahmajñānaṃ dadāti yaḥ //
english: By imparting knowledge one becomes blemishless and attains the world of Brahmā. One who imparts knowledge about the brahman, would be equal to one who gives earth consisting of seven continents.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo yo dadyāt sarvabhāṅ naraḥ /
english: One who gives refuge to all beings would get all things.

sanskrit: purāṇaṃ bhārataṃ vāpi rāmāyaṇamathāpi vā // likhitvā pustakaṃ dattvā bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
english: One who copies and gives the purāṇa or Bhārata or Rāmāyaṇa, would get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: vedaśāstraṃ nṛtyagītaṃ yo 'dhyāpayati nākabhāk //
english: One who teaches scriptures dancing and music would reach heaven.

sanskrit: vittaṃ dadyādupādhyāye chātrāṇāṃ bhojanādikaṃ /
english: Money should be given to the teacher and food etc. for the students.

sanskrit: kimadattaṃ bhavettena dharmakāmādidarśinā //
english: What more can be possibly given by one who does with a motive to acquire virtues and desires.

sanskrit: vājapeyasahasrasya samyagdattasya yat phalaṃ / tatphalaṃ sarvamāpnoti vidyādānanna saṃśayaḥ //
english: There is no doubt that one would get by imparting knowledge every benefit that he would get by performing a thousand Vājapeya sacrifices.

sanskrit: śivālaye viṣṇugṛhe sūryasya bhavane tathā / sarvadānapradaḥ sa syāt pustakaṃ vācayettu yaḥ //
english: One who reads a book would be the giver of all gifts at the temples of lords Śiva, Viṣṇu and the Sungod.

sanskrit: trailokye caturo varṇāś catvāraścāśramāḥ pṛthak / brahmādyā devatāḥ sarvā vidyādāne pratiṣṭhatāḥ //
english: All the castes and the four institutions of life separately and all the gods such as Brahmā and others are established on the gift of knowledge.

sanskrit: vidyā kāmadughā dhenurvidyā cakṣuranuttamaṃ /
english: Knowledge is the wishyielding cow. It is the unsurpassing eye.

sanskrit: upavedapradānena gandharvaiḥ saha modate // vedāṅgānāñca dānena svargalokamavāpnuyāt /
english: One rejoices with the Gandharvas by giving the Upavedas the secondary texts such as the Āyurveda. One would attain heaven by giving the accessory texts of scriptures.

sanskrit: dharmaśāstrapradānena dharmeṇa saha modate //
english: One would rejoice with piety by giving the religious law books.

sanskrit: vidyādānamavāpnoti pradānāt pustakasya tu //
english: One would reap the same benefit by giving a book as he would by imparting knowledge.

sanskrit: śāstrāṇi ca purāṇāni dattvā sarvamavāpnuyāt /
english: One would get everything by giving sacred religious texts and Purāṇas.

sanskrit: śiṣyāṃś ca śikṣayedyastu puṇḍalīkaphalaṃ labhet //
english: One would get the benefit of Puṇḍarīka by imparting knowledge to the disciples.

sanskrit: yena jīvati taddattvā phalasyānto na vidyate /
english: There is not known to be any limit for the benefit accrued by one who gives that by which he lives.

sanskrit: loke sreṣṭhatamaṃ sarvamātmanaścāpi yat priyaṃ // sarvaṃ pitṝṇāṃ dātavyaṃ teṣāmevākṣayārthinā /
english: That which is the most excellent in the world and that which is liked by one should be given to the manes by one who desires to have them without depletion.

sanskrit: viṣṇuṃ rudraṃ padmayoniṃ devīvighneśvarādikān // pūjayitvā pradadyādyaḥ pūjādravyaṃ sa sarvabhāk /
english: One who gives materials for worship after having worshipped lords Viṣṇu, Rudra Śiva, the Lotusborn Brahmā, Goddess, Vighneśvara lord of impediments and others would get everything.

sanskrit: devālayaṃ ca pratimāṃ kārayat sarvamāpnuyāt //
english: One who causes to construct a temple and to make an image would get all things.

sanskrit: sammārjanaṃ copalepaṃ kurvan syānnirmalaḥ pumān /
english: One would be free from blemishes by washing and cleaning the temple.

sanskrit: nānāmaṇḍalakāryagre maṇḍalādhipatirbhavet //
english: One who draws the mystic diagrams would become the ruler of a province subsequently.

sanskrit: gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpadīpaṃ naivedyañca pradakṣiṇaṃ / ghaṇṭādhvajavitānañca prekṣaṇaṃ vādyagautakaṃ // vastrādidattvādevāya bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
english: After having given perfumes, flowers, incense, lamp, food offering, circumambulation, bell, banner, canopy, arranged a show, musical instruments and music and clothes for the lord, one would get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: kastūrikāṃ śihlakañca śrīkhaṇḍamagurūntathā // karpūrañca tathāmustaṃ gugguluṃ vijayaṃ dadet /
english: One should give musk, benzoin, sandal wood, agallochum, camphor, musta a kind of grass, guggulu a fragrant resin and vijaya.

sanskrit: ghṛtaprasthena saṃsthāpya saṅkrāntyādau sa sarvabhāk //
english: One who establishes light at the time of solstice and others with a prastha a measure of ghee would get everything.

sanskrit: snānaṃ palaśataṃ jñeyamabhyaṅgaṃ pañcaviṃśatiḥ /
english: Bathing is known to be with hundred palas of materials, bathing with oil with twentyfive palas.

sanskrit: palānāntu sahasreṇa mahāsnānaṃ prakīrtitaṃ //
english: A great bathing is said to be with a thousand palas of materials.

sanskrit: daśāparādhāstoyena kṣīreṇa snāpanācchataṃ / sahasraṃ payasā dadhnā ghṛtenāyutamiṣyate //
english: By bathing with water ten sins are washed off, by bathṃg with thick milk hundred sins are washed off, by bathing with milk a thousand sins are washed off and ten thousand sins are washed off by bathing with ghee.

sanskrit: dāsīdāsamalaṅkāraṃ gobhūmyaśvagajādikaṃ / devāya dattvā saubhāgyaṃ dhanāyuṣmān vrajeddivaṃ //
english: One would get fortune and wealth and would go to heaven by giving a maidservant, servant, ornaments, cow, land, horse and elephant and other things for the deity.

sanskrit: kāmyadānāni vakṣyāmi sarvakāma pradāni te /
english: shall describe gifts that confer the desired benefits.

sanskrit: nityapūjāṃ māsi māsi kṛtvātho kāmyapūjanaṃ //
english: One should do daily worship each month and do the worship for the accomplishment of one’s desires.

sanskrit: vratārhaṇaṃ guroḥ pūjā vatsarānte mahārcanaṃ /
english: The undertaking of the vow, worship of the preceptor and the grand worship at the end of the year are the routines.

sanskrit: aśvaṃ vai mārgaśairṣe tu kamalaṃ piṣṭasambhavaṃ // śivāya pūjya yo dadyāt sūryaloke ciraṃ vaset /
english: One who gives a horse and a lotus made of flour to lord Śiva after worship in mārgaśīrṣa would live in the world of Sun for a long time.

sanskrit: gajaṃ pauṣe piṣṭamayaṃ trisaptakulamuddharet //
english: By giving an elephant made of flour in pauṣa, one would lift twentyone generations.

sanskrit: māghe cāśvarathaṃ paiṣṭhaṃ dattvā narakaṃ vrajet /
english: By giving a horse and a chariot made of flour in māgha, one would not go to hell.

sanskrit: phālgune tu vṛṣaṃ paiṣṭaṃ svargabhuk syānmahīpatiḥ //
english: One would become a monarch and would ascend heaven by giving a bull made of flour in phālguna.

sanskrit: caitre cekṣumayīṃ gāvandāsadāsīsamanvitāṃ / dattvā svarge ciraṃ sthitvā tadante syānmahīpatiḥ //
english: Having given a cow made of sugarcane together with a servant and a female servant in caitra, one would remain in heaven for a long time and would become a monarch at the end.

sanskrit: saptavrīhīṃś ca vaiśākhe dattvā śivamayo bhavet /
english: One would become verily lord Śiva himself by giving seven kinds of rice in vaiśākha.

sanskrit: balimaṇḍalakañcānnaiḥ kṛtvāṣāḍhe śivo bhavet //
english: One would become identical with lord Śiva by making a circular altar in the āṣāḍha.

sanskrit: vimānaṃ śrāvaṇe pauṣpaṃ dattvā svargī tato nṛpaḥ /
english: One would ascend heaven and also become a king by giving a vehicle made of flowers in śrāvaṇa.

sanskrit: śatadvayaṃ phalānāntu dattvoddhṛtya kulaṃ nṛpaḥ //
english: By giving two hundred fruits one would elevate his family and become a king.

sanskrit: guggulādi dahedbhādre svargī sa syāttato nṛpaḥ /
english: One would become a king after ascending heaven by giving guggulu gum resin etc. in bhādra.

sanskrit: kṣīrasarpirbhṛtaṃ pātramāśvine svargadambhavet // kārttike guḍakhaṇḍājyaṃ dattvā svargī tato nṛpaḥ /
english: Giving a vessel filled with milk and clarified butter in āśvina would convey one to heaven. Having given pieces of jaggery and clarified butter in the kārttika one would go to heaven and then be a king.

sanskrit: merudānaṃ dvādaśakaṃ vakṣye 'haṃ bhuktimuktidaṃ //
english: shall describe the twelve varieties of gifts known as merudāna heaps of things resembling the Meru mountain that confers enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: meruvrate tu kārttikyāṃ ratnamerundaded dvije /
english: In the meruvrata one should give a meru mountain of gems to a brahmin in kārttika.

sanskrit: sarveṣāñcaiva merūṇāṃ pramāṇaṃ kramaśaḥ śṛṇu //
english: Listen to me. shall describe the measure of things in all the gifts of Merus duly.

sanskrit: vajrapadmamahānīlanīlasphaṭikasañjñitaḥ / puṣpaṃ marakataṃ muktā prasthamātreṇa cottamaḥ //
english: Only a prastha a measure of diamond, ruby, mahānīla a kind of sapphire, sapphire, crystal, topaz, emerald and pearl are excellent.

sanskrit: madhyo 'rdhaḥ syāttadardho 'dho vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet /
english: Half of that measure would be medium and a quarter of that would be inferior.

sanskrit: kārṇikāyāṃ nyasenmeruṃ brahmaviṣṇvīśadaivataṃ //
english: The Meru should be located in the pericarps presided by the lords Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Īśa.

sanskrit: mālyavān pūrvataḥ pūjyastatpūrve bhadarasañjñitaḥ /
english: Mālyavān should be worshipped on the east and that is known as Bhadra still to its east.

sanskrit: aśvarakṣastataḥ prokto niṣadho merudakṣiṇe //
english: Aśvarakṣa is said to be the next.

sanskrit: hemakūṭo 'tha himavān trayaṃ saumye tathā trayaṃ /
english: The Niṣadha, Hemakūṭa and Himavān, the three, should be worshipped on the south of Meru.

sanskrit: nīlaḥ śvetaś ca śṛṅgī ca paścime gandhamādanaḥ //
english: The mountains Gandhamādana, Vaikaṅka and Ketumāla would be on the west.

sanskrit: vaikaṅkaḥ ketumālaḥ syānmerurdvādaśasaṃyutaḥ /
english: Thus the Meru would be associated with the twelve mountains.

sanskrit: sopavāso 'rcayedviṣṇuṃ śivaṃ vā snānapūrvakaṃ //
english: One should worship lord Viṣṇu or lord Śiva after fasting preceded by bathing.

sanskrit: devāgre cārcya meruñca mantrair viprāya vai dadet /
english: The Meru should be worshipped with the sacred syllables in front of the deity and given to a brahmin.

sanskrit: viprāyāmukagotrāya merundravyamayamparaṃ // bhuktyai muktyai nirmalatve viṣṇudaivaṃ dadāmi te / indraloke brahmaloke śivaloke hareḥ pure // kulamuddhṛtya krīḍeta vimāne devapūjitaḥ /
english: One should say “ give this excellent material of the shape of Meru belonging to god Viṣṇu to a brahmin of such and such a gotra to become sinless and for the sake of enjoyment and emancipation.” One who does so would be honoured by the celestials and would sport in the divine chariot in the worlds of Indra, Brahmā, Śiva and Viṣṇu after elevating his family.

sanskrit: anyeṣvapi ca kāleṣu saṅkrāntyādau pradāpayet //
english: One should make the gift even at other times such as the entry of the Sun from one constellation into another.

sanskrit: palānāntu sahasreṇa hemamerumprakalpayet /
english: One should offer the golden Meru of the weight of a thousand palas.

sanskrit: śṛṅgatrayasamāyuktaṃ brahmaviṣṇuharānvitaṃ //
english: It should have three peaks representing the lords Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara Śiva.

sanskrit: ekaikaṃ parvatantasya śataikaikena kārayet /
english: Each one of the mountains should be hundred palas.

sanskrit: meruṇā saha śailāstu khyātāstatra trayodaśa //
english: Together with the Meru, the mountains are known to be thirteen.

sanskrit: ayane grahaṇādau ca viṣṇvagre harimarcya ca / svarṇameruṃ dvijāyārpya viṣṇuloke ciraṃ vaset //
english: One who makes a gift of gold Meru to a brahmin at the time of solstices, eclipses etc., in the presence of lord Viṣṇu, after having worshipped lord Hari Viṣṇu, would live in the world of Viṣṇu for a long time.

sanskrit: paramāṇavo yāvanta iha rājā bhavecciraṃ /
english: One would be a king for such a long time as the infinitesimal particles of the gift.

sanskrit: raupyameruṃ dvādaśādriyutaṃ saṅkalpato dadet //
english: One should resolve and give a silver Meru having twelve mountains.

sanskrit: prāguktaṃ ca phalaṃ tasya viṣṇuṃ vipraṃprapūjya ca / bhūmimeruñca viṣayaṃ maṇḍalaṃ grāmameva ca //
english: It would have the aforesaid benefit. One should worship lord Viṣṇu and a brahmin and resolve to give bhūmimeru land in the form of Meru consisting of a circular orb or a village of oneeighth part.

sanskrit: parikalpyāṣṭamāṃśena śeṣāṃśāḥ pūrvavat phalaṃ /
english: The other parts carry the same benefit as before.

sanskrit: dvādaśādrisamāyuktaṃ hastimerusvarūpiṇaṃ // dadettripuruṣair yuktaṃ dattvānantaṃ phalaṃ labhet /
english: One who gives the Meru in the form of an elephant together with the twelve mountains and the three beings gods would get infinite benefit.

sanskrit: tripañcāśvair aśvameruṃ hayayadvādaśasaṃyutaṃ //
english: Meru in the form of a horse would be fifteen horses together with twelve horses.

sanskrit: viṣṇvādīn pūjya taṃ dattvā bhuktabhogo nṛpo bhavet /
english: Giving this as a gift after worshipping lords Viṣṇu and others one would enjoy comforts and become a king.

sanskrit: aśvasaṅkhyāpramāṇena gomeruṃ pūrvavaddadet //
english: One should give a Meru in the form of cow of the same number as the horse as before.

sanskrit: paṭṭavastrair bhāramātrair vastrameruś ca madhyataḥ / śailair dvādaśavastraiś ca dattvā tañcākṣayaṃ phalaṃ //
english: A gift of a Meru in the form of cloth would be a bhāra of silk cloth in the middle with the twelve cloth as mountains around. By giving this gift one will have undiminishing benefit.

sanskrit: ghṛtapañcasahasraiś ca palānāmājyaparvataḥ / śataiḥ pañcabhirekaikaḥ pārvate 'smin hariṃ yajet //
english: A mountain of clarified butter would be five thousand palas of ghee, each one of the mountains being five hundred. One should worship lord Hari in this mountain.

sanskrit: viṣṇvagre brāhmaṇāyārpya sarvaṃ prāpya hariṃ vrajet /
english: Having offered it to a brahmin in the presence of lord Viṣṇu, one would get everything and reach lord Hari.

sanskrit: evaṃ ca khaṇḍameruñca kṛtvā dattvāpnuyāt phalaṃ //
english: One would get the same fruit by making a Meru of sugarcandy and giving in the same way.

sanskrit: dhānyameruḥ pañcakhāro 'para ekaikakhārakāḥ /
english: The Meru of grains should be five khāri a measure equal to droṇas and the other mountains of one khāri each.

sanskrit: svarṇatriśṛṅgakāḥ sarve brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarān //
english: All should have golden peaks denoting lords Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara.

sanskrit: sarveṣu pūjya viṣṇuṃ vā viśeṣādakṣayaṃ phalaṃ /
english: One would acquire special benefit by worshipping lord Viṣṇu in all of them.

sanskrit: evaṃ daśāṃśamānena tilameruṃ prakalpayet //
english: One should set up a Meru of sesamum in the same way measuring ten parts.

sanskrit: śṛṅgāṇi pūrvavattasya tathaivānyanageṣu ca /
english: The peaks should be as before for that mountain and other mountains.

sanskrit: tilameruṃ pradāyātha bandhubhirviṣṇulokabhāk //
english: One who makes a gift of a Meru of sesamum would reach the world ofViṣṇu together with his relatives.

sanskrit: namo viṣṇusvarūpāya dharādharāya vai namaḥ /
english: “Obeisance to the form of Viṣṇu. Obeisance to the mountain Dharādhara.

sanskrit: brahmaviṣṇvīśaśṛṅgāya dharānābhisthitāya ca // nagadvādaśanāthāya sarvapāpāpahāriṇe / viṣṇubhaktāya śāntāya trāṇaṃ me kuru sarvathā //
english: Obeisance to one having lords Brahma, Viṣṇu and Īśa on the peaks, to one remaining at the navel of the earth, to the lord of twelve mountains, to the destroyer of all sins, to the devotee of lord Viṣṇu and to the calm person.

sanskrit: niṣpāpaḥ pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ viṣṇuṃ gacchāmi oṃ namaḥ /
english: You always protect me so that may reach lord Viṣṇu together with my forefathers becoming sinless. Oṃ, obeisance.

sanskrit: tvaṃ haristu hareragre ahaṃ viṣṇuś ca viṣṇave //
english: You are indeed lord Hari. am lord Viṣṇu in the front of lord Hari.

sanskrit: nivedayāmi bhaktyā tu bhuktimuktyarthahetave /
english: shall inform lord Viṣṇu with devotion for the sake of enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: pṛthvīdānaṃ pravakṣyāmi pṛthivī trividhā matā / śatakoṭiryojanānāṃ saptadvīpā sasāgarā //
english: shall describe the mode of making a gift of the earth . The earth is known to be of three kinds extending to hundred crores of yojanas containing seven continents and the oceans.

sanskrit: jambudvīpāvadhiḥ sā ca uttamā medinīritā /
english: That earth upto the continent of Jambū is spoken as excellent.

sanskrit: uttamāṃ pañcabhirbhāraiḥ kāñcanaiś ca prakalpayet //
english: One should make an excellent one with five bhāras measure of weight of gold.

sanskrit: tadardhāntarajaṃ kūrmaṃ tathā padmaṃ samādiśet /
english: The tortoise and lotus supporting that should be laid with half that measure.

sanskrit: uttamā kathitā pṛthvī dvyaṃśenaiva tu madhyamā //
english: The excellent earth is said to be of the full measure. The middle one is said to have two parts.

sanskrit: kanyasā ca tribhāgena trihānyā kūrmapaṅkaje /
english: The last one should be of onethird part. The tortoise and lotus will be onethird.

sanskrit: palānāntu sahasreṇa kalpayet kalpapādapaṃ //
english: The wishyielding celestial tree should be made to weigh a thousand palas.

sanskrit: mūladaṇḍaṃ sapatrañca phalapuṣpasamanvitaṃ / pañcaskandhantu saṅkalpya pañcānāndāpayet sudhīḥ //
english: The central stalk of the tree together with the leaves, fruits and flowers and having five branches should be got ready and the five should be given by a good man.

sanskrit: etaddātā brahmaloke pitṛbhirmodate ciraṃ /
english: One who makes this gift would rejoice in the world of Brahmā together with the manes for a long time.

sanskrit: viṣṇvagre kāmadhenuntu palānāṃ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ //
english: The celestial cow should be made with five hundred palas in front of lord Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: brahmaviṣṇumaheśādyā devā dhenau vyavasthitāḥ /
english: The gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa and others are settled in the cow.

sanskrit: dhenudānaṃ sarvadānaṃ sarvada brahmalokadaṃ //
english: The gift of a cow is the gift of all things. It gives all things and also the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: viṣṇvagre kapilāṃ dattvā tārayet sakalaṃ kulaṃ / alaṅkṛtya striyaṃ dadyādaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet //
english: Having given a tawny cow one would elevate all families. By giving a girl in marriage after decorating her, one would acquire the benefit of doing the horse sacrifice.

sanskrit: bhūmiṃ dattvā sarvabhāk syāt sarvaśasyaprarohiṇīm /
english: One who gives a land in which all grains grow would get everything.

sanskrit: grāmaṃ vātha puraṃ vāpi kheṭakañca dadt sukhī //
english: One who gives a village or a town or a hamlet would be comfortable.

sanskrit: kārttikyādau vṛṣotsargaṃ kurvaṃstārayate kulaṃ //10//
english: By setting free a bull in kārttika one would elevate the family.

sanskrit: nāḍīcakraṃ pravakṣyāmi yajjñānāj jñāyate hariḥ /
english: shall describe the system of veins by knowing which one would know lord Hari.

sanskrit: nābheradhastādyat kandamaṅkurāstatra nirgatāḥ //
english: Fibrelike things spread out from the bulbous root below the navel.

sanskrit: dvāsaptatisahasrāṇi nābhimadhye vyavasthitāḥ /
english: They are seventytwo thousand situated at the centre of the navel.

sanskrit: tiryagūrdhvamadhaś caiva vyāptantābhiḥ samantataḥ //
english: They spread out and occupy everywhere across, above and below. They are situated like a wheel.

sanskrit: iḍā ca piṅgalā caiva susumṇā ca tathaiva ca // gāndhārī hastijihvā ca pṛthā caiva yathā tathā /
english: Among these iḍā, piṅgalā, suṣumnā, gāndhārī, hastijihvā, pṛthā, yaśā, alambuṣā, huhu and śaṅkhinī are the ten principal veins.

sanskrit: daśa prāṇavahā hy etā nāḍayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ / prāṇo 'pānaḥ samānaś ca udāno vyāna eva ca // nāgaḥ kūrmo 'tha kṛkaro devadatto dhanañjayaḥ /
english: These veins are said to be carrying the ten life forcesprāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, vyāna, nāga, kūrma, kṛkara, devadatta and dhanañaya. Prāṇa is the chief wind and is the lord of the ten.

sanskrit: prāṇaḥ prāṇayate prāṇaṃ visargāt pūraṇaṃ prati /
english: The prāṇa makes the life living from exhalation after the inhalation.

sanskrit: nityamāpūrayatyeṣa prāṇināmurasi sthitaḥ //
english: Remaining in the chest of beings it fills up daily.

sanskrit: niḥśvāsocchvāsakāsaistu prāṇo jīvasamāśritaḥ / prayāṇaṃ kurute yasmāttasmāt prāṇaḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
english: The prāṇa gets united with life by exhalation, inhalation and coughing. Because it moves out from the life it is said to be prāṇa.

sanskrit: adho nayatyapānastu āhārañca nṛṇāmadhaḥ /
english: Apāna pushes down the food in men.

sanskrit: mūtraśukravaho vāyurapānastena kīrtitaḥ //
english: It is said to be apāna because it is the wind that carries the urine and semen.

sanskrit: pītabhakṣitamāghrātaṃ raktapittakaphānilaṃ / samannayati gātreṣu samāno nāma mārutaḥ // spandayatyadharaṃ vaktraṃ netrarāgaprakopanaṃ / udvejayati marmāṇi udāno nāma mārutaḥ //
english: The wind known as samāna equalises the blood, biles, phlegm and wind in the body caused by drinking, eating and smelling. The wind known as udāna agitates the vulnerable points and causes the quivering of lips, face and causes change in the complexion of the eye.

sanskrit: vyāno vināmayatyaṅgaṃ vyāno vyādhiprakopanaḥ /
english: The wind vyāna depresses the body and activates the disease.

sanskrit: pratidānaṃ tathā kaṇṭhādvyāpānādvyāna ucyate //
english: It is said to be vyāna because it returns from the throat and spreads out.

sanskrit: udgāre nāga ity uktaḥ kūrmaśconmīlane sthitaḥ /
english: The wind nāga is known to be in vomitting and kūrma remains in the opening.

sanskrit: kṛkaro bhakṣaṇe caiva devadatto vijṛmbhite //
english: The wind kṛkara is in eating, devadatta in yawning, dhanañjaya in raising loud sound.

sanskrit: dhanañjayaḥ sthito ghoṣe mṛtasyāpi na muñcati /
english: They do not abandon even the dead.

sanskrit: jīvaḥ prayāti daśadhā nāḍīcakraṃ hi tena tat //
english: Thus goes the life cycle with the ten activities. Hence it is the cycle of veins.

sanskrit: saṅkrāntirviṣuvañcaiva ahorātrāyanāni ca / adhimāsa ṛṇañcaiva ūnarātra dhanantathā //
english: The solstices, the equinoxes, day and night, the sun’s passage north and south of the equator, intercalary month, debt, the incomplete night and wealth are attributed to the different parts of the body and their functions.

sanskrit: ūnarātraṃ bhaveddhikkā adhimāso vijṛmbhikā / ṛṇañcātra bhavet kāso niśvāso dhanamucyate //
english: The incomplete night would be the hiccough and the intercalary mouth the yawning. The debt would be coughing. The exhalation is said to be wealth.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ dakṣiṇaṃ jñeyaṃ vāmaṃ dakṣiṇasañjñitaṃ /
english: The right side of the body is known to be the north and the left side is designated as the south.

sanskrit: madhye tu viṣuvaṃ proktaṃ puṭadvayaviniḥsmṛtaṃ // saṅkrāntiḥ punarasyaiva svasthānāt sthānayogataḥ /
english: The equinoctical points are said to be in the middle line passing through the two parts while the solstice is that passing from its own nervecentre to another centre.

sanskrit: susumṇā madhyame hy aṅge iḍā vāme pratiṣṭhitā // piṅgalā dakṣiṇe vipra ūrdhvaṃ prāṇo hy ahaḥ smṛtaṃ /
english: O Brahmin! Suṣumnā is established in the middle of the body, the iḍā on the left and the piṅgalā on the right. The prāṇa above is remembered to be the day.

sanskrit: apāno rātrirevaṃ syādeko vāyurdaśātmakaḥ //
english: In the same way apāna would be the night. One wind exists in ten forms.

sanskrit: āyāmo dehamadhyasthaḥ somagrahaṇamiṣyate / dehātitattvamāyāmaṃ ādityagrahaṇaṃ viduḥ //
english: The expanse in the middle of the body is said to be the lunar eclipse. The expanse between the principles of the body is known to be the solar eclipse.

sanskrit: udaraṃ pūrayettāvadvāyunā yāvadīpsitaṃ / prāṇāyāmī bhavedeṣa pūrakā dehapūrakaḥ //
english: Filling the abdomen with wind as much as one desires is known to be the prāṇāyāma known as the pūraka because it fills up.

sanskrit: pidhāya sarvadvārāṇi niśvāsocchvāsavarjitaḥ /
english: After covering all the holes, one should remain like a pot after filling the abdomen with air without exhalation and inhalation.

sanskrit: sampūraṇakumbhavattiṣṭhet prāṇāyāmaḥ sa kumbhakaḥ //
english: That is the kumbhaka variety of prāṇāyāma.

sanskrit: muñcedvāyuṃ tatastūrdhvaṃ śvāsenaikena mantravit / ucchvāsayogayuktaś ca vāyumūrdvaṃ virecayet //
english: One who knows the sacred syllable should push the wind upwards and let out in one breath. He should evacuate it upwards to the region of the brain.

sanskrit: uccarati svayaṃ yasmāt svadehāvasthitaḥ śivaḥ / tasmāt tattvavidāñcaiva sa eva japa uccyate //
english: Since lord Śiva residing in the body of beings himself utters that the letter ha, that is said to be the repetition for those who know the principles.

sanskrit: ayute dve sahasraikaṃ ṣaṭśatāni tathaiva ca / ahorātreṇa yogīndro japasaṅkhyāṃ karoti saḥ //
english: That master of yoga does the repetition twentyone thousand six hundred times in the course of a day and night.

sanskrit: ajapā nāma gāyatrī brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarī /
english: This gāyatrī known as the ajapā is of the form of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara.

sanskrit: ajapāṃ japate yastāṃ punarjanma na vidyate //
english: There is no rebirth for one that repeats this ajapā mantra.

sanskrit: candrāgniravisaṃyuktā ādyā kuṇḍalinī matā / hṛtpradeśe tu sā jñeyā aṅkurākārasaṃsthitā //
english: The foremost kuṇḍalinī the energy coiled in one of the psychometric centres is considered to be associated with the moon, fire and sun. It is known to remain in the heart in the form. of a sprout.

sanskrit: sṛṣṭinyāso bhavettatra sa vai sargāvalambanāt / sravantaṃ cintayettasminnamṛtaṃ sāttvikottamaḥ //
english: The location of the creation should be therein because of its suspension from that. The foremost worshipper should contemplate therein the flowing ambrosia.

sanskrit: dehasthaḥ sakalo jñeyo niṣphalo dehavarjitaḥ /
english: The sakala endowed with the parts is known to be remaining in the body and the niṣkala without the parts as devoid of the body.

sanskrit: haṃsahaṃseti yo brūyāddhaṃso devaḥ sadāśivaḥ //
english: That one who repeats haṃsa is the lord Sadāśiva ever auspicious.

sanskrit: tileṣu ca yathā tailaṃ puṣpe gandhaḥ samaśritaḥ / puruṣasya tathā dehe sa vāhyābhyantarāṃ sthitaḥ //
english: That person remains in the body of the man both outside and inside just as oil in the sesamum and fragrance in the flowers.

sanskrit: brahmaṇo hṛdaye sthānaṃ kaṇṭhe viṣṇuḥ samāśritaḥ /
english: Lord Brahmā has his place in the heart. Lord Viṣṇu remains at the throat.

sanskrit: tālumadhye sthito rudro lalāṭe tu maheśvaraḥ //
english: Lord Rudra is situated in the middle of the cheeks. Lord Maheśvara is at the forehead.

sanskrit: prāṇāgrantu śivaṃ vidyāttasyānte tu parāparaṃ /
english: Lord Śiva should be known as the tip of the vital principle and the higher ^d the lower as its end.

sanskrit: pañcadhā sakalaḥ prokto viparītastu niṣphalaḥ //
english: The sakala form is said to be of five kinds and niṣkala form as the contrary.

sanskrit: prāsādaṃ nādamutthāpya śatatantu japedyadi / ṣaṇmāsātsiddhimāpnoti yogayukto na saṃśayaḥ //
english: That person who produces the sound that is prāsāda propitious and repeats hundred times would no doubt get accomplished in six months endowed with yoga.

sanskrit: gamāgamasya jñānena sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet /
english: There will be destruction of all sins because of the knowledge of the past and future events.

sanskrit: aṇimādiguṇaiśvaryaṃ ṣaḍbhirmāsair avāpnuyāt //
english: One would get virtues such as aṇinā the power to become minute as an atom in six months.

sanskrit: sthūlaḥ sūkṣmaḥ paraśceti prāsādaḥ kathito mayā /
english: The prāsāda been described by me as three gross, subtle and foremost.

sanskrit: hrasvo dīrghaḥ plutaśceti prāsādaṃ lakṣayettridhā // hrasvo dahati pāpāni dīrgho mokṣaprado bhavet /
english: Prāsāda is of three kindsshort, long and protracted. The short one burns sins. The long one would confer emancipation. The elongated one is in accomplishing things.

sanskrit: āpyāyane plutaśceti mūrdhni vinduvibhūṣitaḥ // ādāvante ca hrasvasya phaṭkāro māraṇe hitaḥ /
english: It is adorned with a dot on its head. The syllable phaṭ is beneficial at the beginning and end of the short sound for the sake of destroying an enemy.

sanskrit: ādāvante ca hṛdayamākṛṣṭau samprakīrtitam //
english: The heart mantra at the beginning and end is stated to be useful in captivating others’ minds.

sanskrit: devasya dakṣiṇāṃ mūrtiṃ pañcalakṣaṃ sthito japet /
english: One should repeat the same five lakhs time standing facing the southern face of the deity.

sanskrit: japānte ghṛtahomastu daśasāhasriko bhavet //
english: After the repetition there should be oblation of ghee ten thousand times.

sanskrit: evamāpyāyito mantro vaśyoccāṭādi kārayet /
english: With the sacred syllable having been accomplished thus one should do the repetition for captivating etc.

sanskrit: ūrdhve śūnyamadhaḥ śūnyaṃ madhye śūnyaṃ nirāmayaṃ //
english: It is void above, void in the middle and void below. It is devoid of blemishes.

sanskrit: triśūnyaṃ yo vijānāti mucyate 'sau dhruvaṃ dvijaḥ /
english: Whichever brahmin knows the three voids would certainly be released from the mundane existence.
