sanskrit: prāsādaṃ yo na jānāti pañcamantramahātanuṃ // aṣṭatriṃśatkalāyuktaṃ na sa ācārya ucyate /
english: One is said to be not a preceptor if he does not know the prāsāda, made of the five sacred syllables, endowed with thirtyeight parts.

sanskrit: tathoṅkārañca gāyatrīṃ rudrādīn vettya.asau guruḥ //
english: So also the preceptor knows the syllable oṃ, the gāyatrī, lord Rudra and others.

sanskrit: oṅkāraṃ yo vijānāti sa yogī sa hariḥ pumān /
english: One who knows the syllable oṃ is verily a yogin and the lord Hari.

sanskrit: oṅkāramabhyasettasmānmṛnmantrasārantu sarvadaṃ //
english: Hence one should practise the syllable oṃ, that is the essence of all sacred syllables, and the giver of all things.

sanskrit: sarvamantraprayogeṣu praṇavaḥ prathamaḥ smṛtaḥ /
english: The praṇava oṃ is known to be the first in the application of all the sacred syllables.

sanskrit: tena samparipūrṇaṃ yattat pūrṇaṃ karma netarat //
english: Hence the act which becomes complete with that, will not get completed with any other syllable.

sanskrit: oṅkārapūrvikāstisro mahāvyāhṛtayo 'vyayāḥ /
english: There are three great unmutilating vyāhṛtis syllables which are preceded by the syllable oṃ.

sanskrit: tripadā caiva sāvitrī vijñeyaṃ brahmaṇī mukhaṃ //
english: The threefooted sāvitrī gāyatrī should be known as the face of lord Brahmā.

sanskrit: yo 'dhīte 'hanyahanyetāstrīṇi varṣāṇyatantritaḥ / sa brahmaparamabhyeti vāyubhūtaḥ khamūrtimān //
english: One who unweariedly repeats these everyday for three years, reaches the supreme brahman becoming the wind and embodying the sky.

sanskrit: ekākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma prāṇāyāmaparantapaḥ /
english: The one syllable is the supreme brahman and prāṇāyāma control of the birth in the supreme penance.

sanskrit: sāvitryāstu parannāsti maunāt satyaṃ viśiṣyate //
english: There is nothing greater than sāvitrī. Truthfulness excels silence.

sanskrit: saptāvartā pāpaharā daśabhiḥ prāpayeddivaṃ /
english: The repetition of gāyatrī seven times would destroy one’s sins and ten times would convey the person to heaven.

sanskrit: viṃśāvartā tu sā devī nayate hīśvarālayaṃ //
english: That goddess repeated twenty times would convey him to the abode of lord Īśvara Śiva.

sanskrit: aṣṭottaraśataṃ japtvā tīrṇaḥ saṃsārasāgarāt /
english: One would cross the ocean of mundane existence by repeating it hundred and eight times.

sanskrit: rudrakuṣmāṇḍajapyebhyo gāyatrī tu viśiṣyate //
english: The Gāyatrī excels the repetition of Rudra and Kūṣmāṇḍa mantras in its merit.

sanskrit: na gāyatryāḥ parañjapyaṃ na vyāhṛtisamaṃ hutaṃ /
english: There is nothing excelling Gāyatrī for repetition. There is nothing equal to vyāhṛtis for doing oblations.

sanskrit: gāyatryāḥ pādamapyardhamṛgardhamṛcameva vā // brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ suvarṇasteyameva ca / gurudārāgamaś caiva japyenaiva punāti sā //
english: A quarter of the hymn or a half of it or half the hymn or the whole hymn being repeated purifies one of the sins such as the killing of a brahmin, drinking of wine, stealing of gold and cohabiting the preceptor’s wife.

sanskrit: pāpe kṛte tilair homo gāyatrījapa īritaḥ /
english: On having committed a sin it is said that one should do oblations with sesamum repeating Gāyatrī.

sanskrit: japtvā sahasraṃ gāyatryā upavāsī sa pāpahā //
english: After repetition of Gāyatrī a thousand times and fasting one gets rid of his sin.

sanskrit: goghnaḥ pitṛghno mātṛghno brahmahā gurutalpagaḥ / brahmaghnaḥ svarṇahārī ca surāpo lakṣajapyataḥ //
english: The killer of a cow, the patricide, the matricide, the killer of a brahmin, the defiler of the bed of preceptor, the person who has stolen gold and the drunkard get purified after repetition of the mantra a lakh number of times.

sanskrit: śudhyate vātha vā snātvā śatamantarjale japet /
english: Otherwise one should bathe and repeat hundred times remaining in the water.

sanskrit: apaḥ śatena pītvā tu gāyatryāḥ pāpahā bhavet // śataṃ japtā tu gāyatrī pāpopaśamanī smṛtā /
english: One would get rid of his sin by drinking water consecrated by the repetition of Gāyatrī hundred times. The Gāyatrī repeated hundred times is remembered to destroy one’s sins.

sanskrit: sahasraṃ śaptā sā devī upapātakanāśinī // abhīṣṭadā koṭijapyā devatvaṃ rājatāmiyāt /
english: That goddess repeated a thousand times would destroy the minor offences. The repetition a crore times would yield the desired benefits and lead one to godhead and sovereignty.

sanskrit: oṅkāraṃ pūrvamuccārya bhūrbhuvaḥ svastathaiva ca // gāyatrī praṇavaścānte jape caivamudāhṛtaṃ /
english: After having uttered the syllable oṃ first and the syllables bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ and svaḥ the earth, sky and heaven then, and the praṇava oṃ and Gāyatrī at the end is said to be the mode for repetition.

sanskrit: viśvāmitra ṛṣicchando gāyatraṃ savitā tathā // devatopanaye japye viniyogo hute tathā /
english: Viśvāmitra is the sage, gāyatrī the metre and Savitā Sun the god for the mantra when it is used for appeasement of gods, for repetition and for offering oblation.

sanskrit: agnirvāyū ravirvidyut yamo jalapatirguruḥ // parjanya indro gandharvaḥ pūṣā ca tadanantaraṃ / mitro 'tha varuṇastvaṣṭā vasavo marutaḥ śaśī // aṅgirā viśvanāsatyau kas tathā sarvadevatāḥ / rudro brahmā ca viṣṇuś ca kramaśo 'kṣaradevatāḥ //
english: The gods who preside over different letters constituting the mantra are the Fire god, Wind god, Sun, Lightning, God of Death, lord of the water ocean, Jupiter, God of rain, Indra, Gandharva, Pūṣan, Mitra, Varuṇa, Tvaṣṭṛ, Vasus, Maruts, Moon, Aṅgiras, Viśve devas, Nāsatya Aśvins, Ka, Rudra, Brahmā and Viṣṇu respectively who are said to destroy sins at the time of repetition of Gāyatrī.

sanskrit: stanau ca hṛdayaṃ grīvā mukhantālu ca nāsike // cakṣuṣī ca bhruvormadhyaṃ lalāṭaṃ pūrvamānanaṃ / dakṣiṇottarapārśve dve śira āsyamanukramāt //
english: They respectively protect the toes, ankles, legs, knees, shanks, the male organ of generation, testicles, hip, navel, belly, breasts, heart, neck, face, cheek, nostrils, eyes, the centre of the eyebrows, forehead, front part of the face, the two sides on the right and left, head and the mouth in order.

sanskrit: sphāṭikasvarṇapāṇḍvābhāḥ padmarāgo 'khiladyutiḥ / hemadhūmraraktanīlaraktakṛṣṇasuvarṇabhāḥ // śuklakṛṣṇapālāśābhā gāyatryā varṇakāḥ kramāt /
english: Yellow, blue, tawny, green, colour of the fire, the golden colour of lightning, smoky, black, red, white, colour of the sapphire, crystal coloured, golden, white, red, all the lustre, golden, smoky, blood red, blue red, golden, white, dark green are the colours of Gāyatrī.

sanskrit: dhyānakāle pāpaharā hutaiṣā sarvakāmadā // gāyatryā tu tilair homaḥ sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ /
english: It destroys sins at the time of repetition and confers all desires when used to offer oblation. Oblations made with sesamum and Gāyatrī would destroy all sins.

sanskrit: śāntikāmo yavaiḥ kuryādāyuṣkāmo ghṛtena ca //
english: One who desires to appease should do with barley. One who desires life should do with ghee.

sanskrit: siddhārthakaiḥ karmasiddhyai payasā brahmavarcase / putrakāmas tathā dadhnā dhānyakāmastu śālibhiḥ //
english: For success in one’s work one should do with white mustard. One should do with milk for spiritual splendour, with curd if one wishes to have children, with sāli grains if one desires to get grains.

sanskrit: kṣīravṛkṣasamiddhistu grahapīḍopaśāntaye /
english: One should do oblation with twigs of kṣīri milky trees for the appeasement of affliction due to planets.

sanskrit: dhanakāmas tathā bilvaiḥ śrīkāmaḥ kamalais tathā //
english: Then one desiring for wealth should do with bilva a kind of tree and desiring for fortune should do with lotuses.

sanskrit: ārogyakāmo dūrvābhirgurūtpāte sa eva hi /
english: One should do with dūrvā a kind of grass if he desires for health and the same if portents are met with.

sanskrit: saubhāgyecchurguggulunā vidyārthī pāyasena ca //
english: One should do with guggulu gumresin aspiring for prosperity and with sweet porridge if seeking knowledge.

sanskrit: ayutenoktasiddhiḥ syāllakṣeṇa manasepsitaṃ /
english: There would be the indicated success with oblation done ten thousand times and the mentally desired benefit with a lakh times.

sanskrit: koṭyā brahmabadhān muktaḥ kuloddhārī harirbhavet //
english: One would be released from the sin accrued by killing a brahmin, be lord Hari and the elevator of the family with oblations done crore times.

sanskrit: grahayajñamukho vāpi homo 'yutamukho 'rthakṛt / āvāhanañca gāyatryāstata oṅkāramabhyaset //
english: One should invoke Gāyatrī at the commencement of oblations done for propitiating the planets or the one for ten thousand times or any other sacrifices.

sanskrit: smṛtvauṅkārantu gāyatryā nibadhnīyācchikhāntataḥ / punarācamya hṛḍayaṃ nābhiṃ skandhau ca saṃspṛśet //
english: After having remembered the syllable oṃ one should tie up the tuft with the Gāyatrī. Then after having sipped three drops of water one should touch the heart, navel and shoulders.

sanskrit: praṇavasya ṛṣirbrahmā gāyatrīcchanda eva ca / devo 'gniḥ paramātmā syādyogo vai sarvakarmasu //
english: The sage is Brahmā, the metre is gāyatrī and the god is the Fire god for the praṇava oṃ. It is the Supreme soul and it should be associated in all acts.

sanskrit: śuklā cāgnimukhī devyā kātyāyanasagotrajā / trailokyavaraṇā divyā pṛthivyādhārasaṃyutā // akṣarasūtradharā devī padmāsanagatā śubhā /
english: She should be contemplated as possessing white complexion, having fire as the mouth, divine, born in the gotra of Kātyāyana, encircling the three worlds, associated with the support of the earth, wearing the rosary, the goddess seated in the padmāsana posture of sitting with legs crossed and auspicious with the following words “Oṃ! You are the lustre, the sacrifice, the strength, one of the seven Suns, the abode of the gods, the universe, the life of the universe, all beings and the life of all beings.

sanskrit: āgaccha varade devi japye me sannidhau bhava //
english: O Goddess! Bestower of boon! You come! The one to be repeated! You be present before me!”

sanskrit: vyāhṛtīnāntu sarvāsāmṛṣireva prajāpatiḥ /
english: Prajāpati is the sage for all vyāhṛtis the syllables bhū etc..

sanskrit: vyastāś caiva samastāś ca brāhmamakṣaramomiti //
english: They are used separately and collectively with the letter oṃ of Brahmā.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro yamadagnirbharadvājo 'tha gotamaḥ / ṛṣiratrirvaśiṣṭhaś ca kāśyapaś ca yathākramaṃ //
english: The sages of the vyāhṛtis are Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, Bharadvāja, Gautama, Atri, Vasiṣṭha and Kaśyapa in order.

sanskrit: indro viṣṇurvyāhṛtīnāṃ daivatāni yathākramaṃ //
english: Fire god, Wind god, Sun, Jupiter, Varuṇa, Indra, Viṣṇu are the presiding deities of vyāhṛtis in order.

sanskrit: gāyatryaṣṭiganuṣṭup ca vṛhatī paṅktireva ca / triṣṭup ca jagatī ceti chandāṃsyāhuranuktāmāt //
english: Gāyatrī, Uṣṇik, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī are said to be metres of these respectively.

sanskrit: āpohiṣṭhetyṛcā cāpāndrupadādīti vā smṛtā // tathā hiraṇyavarṇābhiḥ pāvamānībhirantataḥ / vipruṣo 'ṣṭau kṣipedūrdhvamājanmakṛtapāpajit //
english: It is remembered that eight drops of water should be thrown upwards with the hymn āpo hi ṣṭhā or drupadāt or hiraṇyavarṇāṃ or pāvamānī at the end in the use of the vyāhṛtis, in the prāṇāyāma and in oblation.

sanskrit: antarjale ṛtañceti upettriraghamarṣaṇaṃ /
english: It destroys the sin done since the birth.

sanskrit: āpohiṣṭhetyṛco 'syāś ca sindhudvīpa ṛṣiḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: One should recite the hymn ṛtaṃ ca, the destroyer of sins, thrice in the water. Sindhudvīpa is the sage for the hymn āpo hi ṣṭhā.

sanskrit: brahmasnānāya chando 'sya gāyatrī devatā jalaṃ /
english: The metre is gāyatrī and deity water for this hymn for brahmasnāna bathing to get rid of sin.

sanskrit: mārjane viniyogasya hayāvabhṛthake kratoḥ // aghamarṣaṇasūktasya ṛṣirevāghamarṣaṇaṃ /
english: It should be used for sprinkling water on the body or at the time of bathing at the conclusion of a sacrifice. Aghamarṣaṇa is the sage for this aghamarṣaṇa hymn.

sanskrit: anuṣṭup ca bhavecchando bhāvavṛttastu daivataṃ //
english: Anuṣṭubh would be the metre. Bhāvavṛtta is the deity.

sanskrit: āpījyorīrasa iti gāyatryāstu śiraḥ smṛtaṃ / ṛṣiḥ prajāpatistasya chandohīnaṃ yajuryataḥ //
english: The mantra āpo jyotī raso is remembered to be the head of Gāyatrī. Prajāpati Brahmā is the sage for that because the yajur mantras are not metrical.

sanskrit: brahmāgnivāyusūryāś ca devatāḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
english: Brahmā, Fire god, Wind god and Sun are said to be deities.

sanskrit: prāṇarodhāttu vāyuḥ syādvāyoragniś ca jāyate //
english: The wind is generated from the suppression of breath. Fire is produced from wind.

sanskrit: agnerāpastataḥ śuddhistataścācamanañcaret /
english: Water is produced from fire and then purity.

sanskrit: antaś carati bhūteṣu guhāyāṃ viśvamūrtiṣu //
english: Then one should rinse. It moves within beings, cavity and universal gods.

sanskrit: tapoyajñavaṣaṭkāra āpo jyotī raso 'mṛtaṃ /
english: The syllable vaṣaṭ is the sacrifice in the form of penance. Water is the lustrous sap of nectar.

sanskrit: udutyaṃ jātavedasamṛṣiḥ praṣkanna ucyate // gāyatrīcchanda ākhyātaṃ sūryaś caiva tu daivatam /
english: The sage of the hymn udu tyam jātavedasaṃ is said to be Praskanna ? Gāyatrī is stated to be the metre and Sun the deity.

sanskrit: atirātre niyogaḥ syādagnīṣomo niyogakaḥ //
english: It is used in the atirātra sacrifice and the agniṣṭoma is the employer.

sanskrit: citraṃ deveti ṛcake ṛṣiḥ kautsa udāhṛtaḥ /
english: Kautsa is stated to be the sage for the hymn citraṃ devānām.

sanskrit: triṣṭup chando daivatañca sūryo 'syāḥ parikīrtitaṃ //
english: Triṣṭubh is said to be the metre for this hymn and Sun the deity. ṚV. ... AV. ...

sanskrit: evaṃ sandhyāvidhiṃ kṛtvā gāyatrīñca japet smaret /
english: ... After having performed the twilight worship thus, one should recite Gāyatrī.

sanskrit: gāyañcchiṣyān yatastrāyet bhāryāṃ prāṇāṃstathaiva ca //
english: It is known to be Gāyatrī because it saves disciples, wives and lives.

sanskrit: tataḥ smṛteyaṃ gāyatrī sāvitrīya tato yataḥ / prakāśanātsā saviturvāgrūpatvāt sarasvatī //
english: It is known as the Sāvitrī because it illumines the Sun. It is known as Sarasvatī because it is the form of speech.

sanskrit: taj jyotiḥ paramaṃ brahma bhargastejo yataḥ smṛtaṃ /
english: It is known to be the bharga, the lustre, because it is the effulgence of supreme brahman.

sanskrit: bhā dīptāviti rūpaṃ hi bhrasjaḥ pāke 'tha tat smṛtaṃ //
english: The root bhā denotes shining. It is also known that bhrasj denotes cooking.

sanskrit: oṣadhyādikaṃ pacati bhrājṛ dīptau tathā bhavet / bhargaḥ syād bhrājata iti bahulaṃ chanda īritaṃ //
english: It ripens the herbs etc. The root bhrājṛ would denote shining. The word Bharga would be denoting shining. In this sense it has been used in the scriptures many times.

sanskrit: vareṇyaṃ sarvatejobhyaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ vai paramaṃ padaṃ /
english: It is said to be most excellent because it has an exalted position than all the splendours.

sanskrit: svargāpavargakāmair vā varaṇīyaṃ sadaiva hi //
english: It is the one always desired by those who wish to attain heaven.

sanskrit: vṛṇotervaraṇārthatvājjāgratsvapnādivarjitaṃ / nityaśuddhabuddhamekaṃ satyantaddhīmahīśvaraṃ //
english: As the word vṛṇoti means covering, it signifies an eternal, absolutely pure conscious, absolutely real and great god that is beyond the states of waking, dreaming and deep sleep.

sanskrit: ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirdhyayemahi vimuktaye /
english: am that brahman, the supreme effulgence. contemplate on that for the emancipation.

sanskrit: taj jyotirbhagavān viṣṇurjagajjanmādikāraṇaṃ //
english: That effulgence is lord Viṣṇu that is the cause of origin of the universe.

sanskrit: śivaṃ kecit paṭhanti sma śaktirūpaṃ paṭhanti ca / kecit sūryaṅkecidagniṃ vedagā agnihotriṇaḥ //
english: Some read Śiva, some read a form of goddess, some Sun and some such as those learned in the scriptures and those propitiating fire, the fire god.

sanskrit: agnyādirūpo viṣṇurhi vedādau brahma gīyate /
english: Lord Viṣṇu of the form of fire etc. is praised in the scriptures as the brahman.

sanskrit: tat padaṃ paramaṃ viṣṇordevasya savituḥ smṛtaṃ //
english: That most exalted place of lord Viṣṇu is known to be that of lord Savitā Sun.

sanskrit: mahadājyaṃ sūyate hi svayaṃ jyotirhariḥ prabhuḥ /
english: That lord Hari, the self effulgent produces the libations of clarified butter.

sanskrit: parjanyo vāyurādityaḥ śītoṣṇādyaiś ca pācayet //
english: The same god as the god of rain, the god of wind and the Sun would nourish everything by means of cold, heat etc.

sanskrit: agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate /
english: Libations cast into the fire reach the Sun.

sanskrit: ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannantataḥ prajāḥ //
english: Rains are produced from the Sun. Food grains grow from rain and then the people.

sanskrit: dadhātervā dhīmahīti manasā dhārayemahi /
english: The word dhīmahi may be from the root dhā to hold. It means “May we retain in our minds”.

sanskrit: no 'smākaṃ yaś ca bhargaś ca sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ dhiyaḥ // codayāt prerayed buddhīrbhoktṝṇāṃ sarvakarmasu /
english: The word naḥ means ‘our’ May that Bharga who is in the intellects of all beings prompt the intellects of those who enjoy in all their acts and results seen and unseen.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭādṛṣṭavipākeṣu viṣṇusūryāgnirūpavān //
english: He is of the form ofViṣṇu, Sun and Fire.

sanskrit: īśvaraprerito gacchet svargaṃ vāśvabhrameva vā /
english: Being prompted by the lord one may reach heaven or the pit of mundane existence.

sanskrit: īśāvāsyamidaṃ sarvaṃ mahadādijagaddhariḥ //
english: Everything is an abode of the lord. Lord Hari is verily the worlds such as the mahat.

sanskrit: svargādyaiḥ krīḍate devo yo 'haṃ sa puruṣaḥ prabhuḥ /
english: “ am that lord who sports with the paradise and the like.

sanskrit: ādityāntargataṃ yacca bhargākhyaṃ vai mumukṣubhiḥ // janmamṛtyuvināśāya duḥkhasya trividhasya ca /
english: That lord the universal being known as Bharga inside the Sun should be contemplated by those desiring for emancipation for the destruction of birth and death and the three kinds of griefs.

sanskrit: dhyānena puruṣo 'yañca draṣṭavyaḥ sūryamaṇḍale //
english: This universal being should be beheld in the orb of the Sun. .

sanskrit: tattvaṃ sadasi cidbrahma viṣṇoryat paramaṃ padaṃ /
english: You are that Supreme Being, the conscious brahman which is the exalted position of lord Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: devasya saviturbhargo vareṇyaṃ hi turīyakaṃ // dehādijāgradābrahma ahaṃ brahmeti dhīmahi /
english: am Bharga, the most exalted fourth place of lord Sun. am the body and the like, the state of waking and that upto that brahman. deem myself as the brahman.

sanskrit: yo 'sāvādityapuruṣaḥ so 'sāvahamananta oṃ //
english: am that absolute spirit in the Sun. am the infinite. Oṃ.

sanskrit: jñānāni śubhakarmādīn pravartayati yaḥ sadā //19//
english: that one who always directs the knowledge in auspicious acts and the like.

sanskrit: liṅgamūrtiṃ śivaṃ stutvā gāyatryā yogamāptavān /
english: After having propitiated lord Śiva of the form of the liṅga with Gāyatrī, Vasiṣṭha obtained yoga.

sanskrit: nirvāṇaṃ paramaṃ brahma vasiṣṭho 'nyaś ca śaṅkarāt //
english: Moreover he got the exalted brahman and emancipation from lord Śaṅkara Śiva.

sanskrit: namaḥ kanakaliṅgāya vedaliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
english: Obeisance to the golden liṅga and the liṅga in the form of scriptures.

sanskrit: namaḥ paramaliṅgāya vyomaliṅgāya vai namaḥ //
english: Obeisance to the supreme liṅga and the liṅga in the form of the sky.

sanskrit: namaḥ sahasraliṅgāya vahniliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
english: Obeisance to the thousand liṅgas and the liṅga in the form of the fire.

sanskrit: namaḥ purāṇaliṅgāya śrutiliṅgāya vai namaḥ // namaḥ pātālaliṅgāya brahmaliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
english: Obeisance to the liṅga of the forms of the Purāṇa and the scriptures. Obeisance to the liṅga in the form of the nether worlds and the brahman.

sanskrit: namo rahasyaliṅgāya saptadvīpordhaliṅgine //
english: Obeisance to the mysterious liṅga and the liṅga above the seven continents.

sanskrit: namaḥ sarvātmaliṅgāya sarvalokāṅgaliṅgine /
english: Obeisance to the liṅga as the soul of all beings and to the liṅga that is the limb of all people.

sanskrit: namastvavyaktaliṅgāya buddhiliṅgāya vai namaḥ //
english: Obeisance to the unmanifest liṅga and the liṅga of the form of the intellect.

sanskrit: namo 'haṅkārakiṅgāya bhūtaliṅgāya vai namaḥ / nama indriyaliṅgāya namastanmātraliṅgine // namaḥ puruṣaliṅgāya bhāvaliṅgāya vai namaḥ /
english: Obeisance to the liṅga representing the ego and to the liṅga denoting the beings. Obeisance to the liṅga of the form of senses and the subtle principles. Obeisance to the liṅga denoting the Supreme spirit and the sentiments.

sanskrit: namo rajordhaliṅgāya sattvaliṅgāya vai namaḥ //
english: Obeisance to the liṅga above the principle of rajas and to the principle of sattva.

sanskrit: namstebhavaliṅgāya namastraiguṇyaliṅgine / namo 'nāgataliṅgāya tejoliṅgāya vai namaḥ //
english: Obeisance to the liṅga of the form of becoming and of the form of the three qualities. Obeisance to the liṅga denoting future and the form of lustre.

sanskrit: namo vāyūrdhvaliṅgāya śrutiliṅgāya vai namaḥ / namaste 'tharvaliṅgāya sāmaliṅgāya vai namaḥ //
english: Obeisance to the liṅga beyond the wind and of the form of the scriptures. Obeisance to the liṅga in the form of the hymns of Atharva veda and the Sāma veda.

sanskrit: namo yajñāṅgaliṅgāya yajñaliṅgāya vai namaḥ / namaste tattvaliṅgāya devānugataliṅgine //
english: Obeisance to the liṅga that is the limb of the sacrifice and of the form of the sacrifice. Obeisance to the liṅga of the form of principles and to the liṅga of the form of the companion of the lord.

sanskrit: diśa naḥ paramaṃ yogamapatyaṃ matsamantathā /
english: You impart me the excellent yoga.

sanskrit: brahma caivākṣayaṃ deva śamañcaiva paraṃ vibho //
english: O Lord! May attain the imperishable brahman. O Lord you also confer tranquillity.

sanskrit: akṣayantvañca vaṃśasya dharme ca matimakṣayāṃ /
english: May the progeny be without break and let them have an undiminishing interest in righteousness.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhena stutaḥ śambhustuṣṭaḥ śrīparvate purā // vasiṣṭhāya varaṃ dattvā tatraivāntaradhīyata //13//
english: Once after having been propitiated by Vasiṣṭha on the Śrīparvata mountain thus, Śambhu Śiva granted the boon to Vasiṣṭha and disappeared there itself.

sanskrit: puṣkareṇa ca rāmāya rājadharmaṃ hi pṛcchate / yathādau kathitaṃ tadvadvaśiṣṭa kathayāmi te //
english: O Vasiṣṭha! shall describe now the duties of a king as told by Puṣkara to Rāma as the latter asked him the same.

sanskrit: rājadharmaṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvasmāt rājadharmataḥ /
english: shall describe the duties of a king foremost among the host of other duties.

sanskrit: rājā bhavet śatruhantā prajāpālaḥ sudaṇḍavān //
english: The king should be the slayer of the enemy, protector of the subjects and administer justice properly.

sanskrit: pālayiṣyati vaḥ sarvān dharmasthān vratamācaret /
english: He would look after the welfare of all those who are on the righteous path.

sanskrit: saṃvatsaraṃ sa vṛṇuyāt purohitamatha dvijaṃ //
english: He should practise this vow.

sanskrit: mantriṇaścākhilātmajñānmahiṣīṃ dharmalakṣaṇāṃ /
english: He has to choose the astrologer, the brahmin priest, the ministers who had known the minds of the people and the queen endowed with righteous qualities.

sanskrit: saṃvatsaraṃ nṛpaḥ kāle sasambhāro 'bhiṣecanaṃ //
english: After having practised the vow for a year the king should have the anointment with all the regal paraphernalia at the proper moment.

sanskrit: kuryānmṛte nṛpe nātra kālasya niyamaḥ smṛtaḥ /
english: But there is no regulation about time for the same if the king has died and a new king is installed.

sanskrit: tilaiḥ siddhārthakaiḥ snānaṃ sāṃvatsarapurohitau // ghoṣayitvā jayaṃ rājño rājā bhadrāsane sthitaḥ / abhayaṃ ghoṣayed durgānmocayedrājyapālake //
english: He should be bathed with sesamum and mustard and the astrologer and the priest should hail victory for the king. Then the king seated on the throne should proclaim protection for all and throw open the gates of the fortress for the provincial governors.

sanskrit: purodhasābhiṣekāt prāk kāryaindrī śāntireva ca /
english: Before the anointment is done, the priest should do the rite to appease Indra.

sanskrit: upavāsyabhiṣekāhe vedyagnau juhuyānmanūn // vaiṣṇavānaindramantrāṃstu sāvitrīn vaiśvadaivatān / saumyān svastyayanaṃ śarmāyuṣyābhayadānmanūn //
english: After having fasted on the day of anointment, offerings should be made into the sacrificial fire for the Manus with the sacred syllables of lord Viṣṇu, Indra, Savitṛ Sun, and the Viśvedevas and the sacred syllables that are auspicious, beneficial, conferring longevity and protection.

sanskrit: aparājitāñca kalasaṃ vahnerdakṣiṇapārśvagaṃ / sampātavantaṃ haimañca pūjayedgandhapuṣpakaiḥ //
english: The golden pitcher known as aparājitā not defeated by anybody containing the remnants of the sacrifice should be worshipped with perfumes and flowers on the right side of the fire.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇāvartaśikhastaptajāmbūnadaprabhaḥ / rathaughameghanirghoṣo vidhūmaś ca hutāśanaḥ //
english: The sacrificial fire should have flames circling clockwise, having the colour of heated gold, should be like the moving chariot, be making sound like the cloud and without smoke.

sanskrit: anulomaḥ sugandhaś ca svastikākārasannibhaḥ / prasannārcirmahājvālaḥ sphuliṅgarahito hitaḥ //
english: The flames in their natural form, fragrant, resembling the figure of a svastika, with clear and high flames and without sparks are benevolent.

sanskrit: na vrajeyuś ca madhyena mārjāramṛgapakṣiṇaḥ /
english: Cats, deer and birds should not pass between the king and the sacrificial fire.

sanskrit: parvatāgramṛdā tāvanmūrdhānaṃ śodhayennṛpaḥ // valmīkāgramṛdā karṇau vadanaṃ keśavālayāt / indrālayamṛdā grīvāṃ hṛdayantu nṛpājirāt // karidantoddhṛtamṛdā dakṣiṇantu tathā bhujaṃ / vṛṣaśṛṅgoddhṛtamṛdā vāmañcaiva tathā bhujaṃ //
english: The king should cleanse his head with the mud obtained from the summit of a mountain, the ears with the mud from the top of an anthill, the face with that mud from the temple of lord Keśava, the neck with the mud from the temple of lord Indra, the heart breast with that got from the courtyard of the king king’s palace, the right arm with the mud dug up by the tusk of an elephant, the left arm with the mud dug up by the horns of a bull, the back with the mud from a tank, the abdomen with the mud from the confluence of rivers and the sides should be purified with the mud from both the banks of a river.

sanskrit: veśyādvāramṛdā rājñaḥ kaṭiśaucaṃ vidhīyate / yajñasthānāttathaivorū gosthānājjānunī tathā // aśvasthānāttathā jaṅghe rathacakramṛdāṅghrike /
english: It is laid down that the waist of a king should be cleansed with the mud obtained from the threshold of a courtesan, the thigh with mud got from the sacrificial place, the knees with mud obtained from the cowshed, the shanks with that got from the stable, the feet with the mud from the wheel of a chariot.

sanskrit: mūrdhānaṃ pañcagavyena bhadrāsanagataṃ nṛpaṃ //
english: The head of the king seated on the throne should be washed with the five things got from a cow.

sanskrit: abhiṣiñcedamātyānāṃ catuṣṭayamatho ghaṭaiḥ /
english: Four ministers of the king should anoint him with waters from the pitchers.

sanskrit: pūrvato hemakumbhena ghṛtapūrṇena brāhaṇaḥ // rūpyakumbhena yāmye ca kṣīrapūrṇena kṣatriyaḥ / dadhnā ca tāmrakumbhena vaiśyaḥ paścimagena ca //
english: A brahmin minister should anoint him with a golden pitcher filled with ghee from the east, a kṣatriya minister with a silver pitcher filled with milk from the south, a vaiśya minister with a copper pitcher filled with curd from the west and a śūdra minister with an earthen pot with water from the north.

sanskrit: mṛṇmayena jalenodak śūdrāmātyo 'bhiṣicayet / tato 'bhiṣekaṃ nṛpaterbahvṛcapravaro dvijaḥ //
english: Then a brahmin priest reciting the Ṛgveda should anoint the king with honey and a priest of the Sāmaveda with waters along with the kuśa.

sanskrit: sampātavantaṃ kalaśaṃ tathā gatvā purohitaḥ // vidhāya vahnirakṣāntu sadasyeṣu yathāvidhi / rājaśriyābhiṣeke ca ye mantrāḥ parikīrtitāḥ // taistu dadyānmahābhāga brāhmaṇānāṃ svanais tathā /
english: O Fortunate one! Then the royal priest should go towards the pitcher containing the residual offering, perform duly the protective amulet of the fire for the courtiers and give it to the king with those sacred syllables mentioned in connection with the coronation and with the recitations made by the brahmins.

sanskrit: tataḥ purohito gacchedvedimūlantadeva tu // śatacchidreṇa pātreṇa sauvarṇenābhiṣecayet /
english: Then the priest should go to the foot of the sacrificial platform and anoint the king with a golden vessel having hundred holes.

sanskrit: yā oṣadhītyoṣadhībhīrathetyuktveti gandhakaiḥ // puṣpaiḥ puṣpavatītyeva brāhmaṇeti ca vījakaiḥ / ratnair āśuḥ śiśānaś ca ye devāś ca kuśodakaiḥ // yajurvedyatharvavedī gandhadvāreti saṃspṛśet / śiraḥ kaṇṭhaṃ rocanayā sarvatīrthodakair dvijāḥ //
english: The head of the king should be touched with the herbs with the recitation of the sacred syllables yā oṣadhi, with perfumes, with flowers with the syllables puṣpavatī, with seeds with the syllables brāhmaṇa, with gems with the syllables āśuḥ śiśāṇaḥ, with kuśa dipped in water with the syllables ye devāḥ and a reciter of the Yajurveda or the Atharvaveda should touch the head and throat with rocanā with the recitation of the syllables gandhadvārā and other brahmins with all the sacred waters.

sanskrit: gītavādyādinirghoṣaiścāmaravyajanādibhiḥ / sarvauṣadhimayaṃ kumbhaṃ dhārayeyurnṛpāgrataḥ //
english: Then they should hold a pitcher filled with the herbs in front of the king to the accompaniment of singing and instrumental music and the waving of chowries and fans.

sanskrit: taṃ paśyeddarpaṇaṃ rājā ghṛtaṃ vai maṅgalādikaṃ /
english: The king also should see them as well as the auspicious things such as the mirror and ghee etc.

sanskrit: abhyarcya viṣṇuṃ brahmāṇamindrādīṃś ca graheśvarān // vyāghracarmottarāṃ śayyāmupaviṣṭaḥ purohitaḥ / madhuparkādikaṃ dattvā paṭṭabandhaṃ prakārayet //
english: Then the priest, seated on a bed covered with a tigerskin, should worship gods Viṣṇu, Brahmā, lndra and others and the lords of planets and place the turban after having given the respectful offering of mixture of honey.

sanskrit: rājñomukuṭabandhañca pañcacarmottaraṃ dadet /
english: The crown of the king should be fixed with the hides of five animals.

sanskrit: dhruvādyair iti ca viśed vṛṣajaṃ vṛṣadaṃśajaṃ // dvīpijaṃ siṃhajaṃ vyāghrajātañcarma tadāsane /
english: The king should place the hides of a bull, a cat, elephant, lion and tiger on that seat with the recitation of the sacred syllables dhruvā dyauḥ.

sanskrit: amātyasacivādīṃś ca pratīhāraḥ pradarśayet // gojāvigṛhadānādyaiḥ sāṃvatsarapurohitau /
english: Then the doorkeeper should present the ministers to the king. Then the king should give presents of cows, goats, sheep, houses and other gifts to the astrologers and priests.

sanskrit: pūjayitvā dvijān prārcya hy anyabhūgonnamukhyakaiḥ //
english: The other brahmins should be honoured by giving gifts of land, cows, food etc.

sanskrit: vahniṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya guruṃ natvātha pṛṣṭhataḥ / vṛṣamālabhya gāṃ vatsāṃ pūjayitvātha mantritaṃ //
english: Then the king should circumambulate the sacrificial fire and make obeisance to the preceptor. He should then move backwards, touch the bull and worship the cow and calf.

sanskrit: aśvamāruhya nāgañca pūjayettaṃ samāruhet / paribhramedrājamārge balayuktaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ //
english: Then he should ride the consecrated royal steed. Similarly, he should worship the royal elephant and mount it. He should then go round the royal path along with his army.

sanskrit: puraṃ viśecca dānādyaiḥ prārcya sarvān visarjayet //35//
english: Then he should enter the palace and send away all those gathered after pleasing them with gifts.

sanskrit: rājadevādyabhiṣekamantrānvakṣye 'ghamardanān /
english: ... . shall describe the sacred syllables for the anointment of a king or god which would destroy sins.

sanskrit: kumbhāt kuśodakaiḥ siñcettena sarvaṃ hi siddhyati //
english: One would accomplish everything by sprinkling water from the pot with the kuśa.

sanskrit: surāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ / vāsudevaḥ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ pradyumnaścāniruddhakaḥ //
english: The sacred syllables are as follows “May the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha install you.

sanskrit: bhavantu vijayāyaite indrādyā daśadiggatāḥ /
english: May the gods Indra and others occupying ten cardinal points confer victory on you.

sanskrit: rudro dharmo manurdakṣo ruciḥ śraddhā ca sarvadā // bhṛguratrirvasiṣṭhaś ca sanakaś ca sanandanaḥ / sanatkumāro 'ṅgirāś ca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ //
english: The lords of created beings such as Rudra, Dharma, Manu, Dakṣa, Ruci, Śraddhā, Bhṛgu, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatkumāra, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Marīci and Kaśyapa guard you always.

sanskrit: prabhāsurā vahirṣada agniṣvāttāś ca pāntu te // kravyādāścopahūtāś ca ājyapāś ca sukālinaḥ /
english: May the God of Death, lustrous celestials, the manes Barhiṣadas, Agniṣvāttas Kravyādas, Upahūtas, Ājyapas and Sukālins guard you.

sanskrit: agnibhiścābhiṣiñcantu lakṣmyādyā dharmavallabhāḥ //
english: May the goddesses Lakṣmī and others, the consorts of Dharma anoint you with fires.

sanskrit: ādityādyāḥ kaśyapasya bahuputrasya vallabhāḥ / kṛśāśvasyāgniputrasya bhāryāścāriṣṭhaneminaḥ // aśvinyādyāś ca candrasya pulahasya tathā priyāḥ / bhūtā ca kapiśā daṃṣṭrī surasā saramā danuḥ //
english: May the consorts of Ādityas anḍ others, the progeny of Kaśyapa, having many offspring, the wives of Kṛśāśva, the son of Agni, the wives of Ariṣṭanemi, Aśvinī and others, the wives of the Moon anḍ the wives of Pulaha, namely, Bhūtā, Kapīśā, Daṃṣṭrī, Surasā, Saramā, Danu, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Krauñcī, Dhṛtarāṣṭrī and Śukī install you.

sanskrit: śyenī bhāsī tathā krauñcī dhṛtarāṣṭrī śukī tathā / patnyastvāmabhiṣiñcantu aruṇaścārkasārathiḥ // āyatir niyatīrātrir nidrā lokasthitau sthitāḥ /
english: May Āyati future, Niyati fate, Rātri night and Nidrā sleep who stabilise the world and support it as well as the goddesses Umā, consort of Śiva, Menā wife of Himavān, Śacī wife of Indra guard you.

sanskrit: umā menā śacī pāntu dhūmor nānirṛtirjaye //
english: May Dhūmrā, Ūrṇā and Nirṛti confer victory.

sanskrit: gaurī śivā ca ṛddhiś ca velā caiva naḍvalā / aśiknī ca tathā jyotsnā devapatnyo vanaspatiḥ //
english: May the goddesses Gaurī, Śivā, Ṛddhi, Velā, Naḍvalā, Asiknī and Jyotsnā, the consorts of the celestials and the presiding deity of the forest confer victory.

sanskrit: mahākalpaś ca kalpaś ca manvantarayugāni ca / saṃvatsarāṇi varṣāṇi pāntu tvāmayanadvayaṃ //
english: May the mahākalpa greater cycle of time, kalpa smaller cycle of time, manvantara Manu periods, yugas a certain long period of time, saṃvatsara years, varṣas and the two half years based on the movement of the sun guard you.

sanskrit: ṛtavaś ca tathā māsā pakṣā rātryahanī tathā / sandhyātithimuhūrtācca kālasyāvayavākṛtiḥ //
english: May the seasons, months, fortnights, night, day, twilight, tithis lunar days, muhūrtas period of minutes, which are the constituents of the time personified guard you.

sanskrit: sūryādyāś ca grahāḥ pāntu manuḥ svāyambhuvādikaḥ /
english: May the planets such as the Sun as well as the fourteen Manus Svāyambhuva and other Manus guard you.

sanskrit: raivataścākṣuṣaḥ ṣaṣṭho vaivasvata iheritaḥ / sāvarṇo brahmaputraś ca dharmaputraś ca rudrajaḥ //
english: Svāyambhuva, Svārociṣa, Auttami, Tāmasa, Raivata, Cākṣuṣa the sixth, Vaivasvata, Sāvarṇi, Brahmaputra, Dharmaputra, Rudraja, Dakṣaja, Raucya and Bhautya are the fourteen Manus.

sanskrit: viśvabhuk ca vipaścicca sucittiś ca śikhī vibhuḥ // manojavastathaujasvī baliradbhutaśāntayaḥ / vṛṣaś ca ṛtadhāmā ca divaspṛk kavirindrakaḥ //
english: May the foremost celestials Viśvabhuk, Vipaścit, Sucitti, Śikhī, Vibhu, Manojava, Ojasvī, Bali, Adbhuta, Śānti, Vṛṣa, Ṛtadhāmā, Divaspṛk, Kavi, Indraka, Raivanta, Kumāra, Vatsaka, Vināyaka, Vīrabhadra, Nandī, Viśvakarmā and Purojava anoint you.

sanskrit: nāsatyau devabhiṣajau dhruvādyā vasavo 'ṣṭa ca // daśa cāṅgiraso vedāstvābhiṣiñcantu siddhaye /
english: May the celestial physicians Nāsatyā, the eight Vasus Dhruva and others, the ten Aṅgirasas and the scriptures anoint you for gaining perfection.

sanskrit: ātmā hy āyurmano dakṣo madaḥ prāṇastathaiva ca // haviṣmāṃś ca gariṣṭhaś ca ṛtaḥ satyaś ca pāntu vaḥ /
english: May the soul, duration of life, mind, mental power, egoism, lifebreath, possessed of oblation, the most important, divine law and truth guard you.

sanskrit: kraturdakṣo vasuḥ satyaḥ kālakāmo dhurirjaye //
english: May Kratu, Dakṣa, Vasu, Satya, Kālakāma and Dhuri lead you to victory.

sanskrit: purūravā mādravāś ca viśvedevāś ca rocanaḥ / aṅgārakādyāḥ sūryastvānnirṛtiś ca tathā yamaḥ // ajaikapādahirvradhro dhūmaketuś ca rudrajāḥ / bharataś ca tathā mṛtyuḥ kāpāliratha kiṅkiṇiḥ // bhavano bhāvanaḥ pāntu svajanyaḥ svajanas tathā /
english: May the Purūravas, Mādravas, Viśvedevas, Rocana, Aṅgāraka and others, Sūrya, Nirṛti and Yama, Ajaikapāt, Ahirbudhnya, Dhūmaketu, Rudrajas, Bharata, Mṛtyu, Kāpāli, Kiṅkiṇī, Bhavana and Bhāvana protect you with their children and wives, Kratuśravāḥ, Mūrddhā, Yājana, Abhyuśanāḥ, Prasava, Avyaya, Dakṣa, Bhṛgu, the celestials, Manaḥ Anumantā, Prāṇaḥ, Nava, Apāna, Vīryavān, Vītihotra, Naya, Sādhya, Haṃsa and Nārāyaṇa protect you.

sanskrit: vibhuś caiva prabhuś caiva devaśreṣṭhā jagaddhitāḥ // dhātā mitro 'ryamā pūṣā śakro 'tha varuṇo bhagaḥ / tvaṣṭā vivasvān savitā viṣṇurdvādaśa bhāskarāḥ // ekajyotiś ca dvijyotistriś caturjyotireva ca / ekaśakro dviśakraś ca triśakraś ca mahābalaḥ //
english: May the foremost among the celestials who are devoted to the welfare of universe such as Vibhu, Prabhu, and the twelve Suns Dhātā, Mitra, Aryamā, Pūṣā, Śakra, Varuṇa, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭā, Vivasvān, Savitā and Viṣṇu as well as Ekajyotis, Dvirjyotis, Trijyotis, Caturjyotis, Ekaśakra, Dviśakra, Triśakra, Mahābala and Indra command saying ‘do not’.

sanskrit: atimitro 'numitraś ca purumitro 'parājitaḥ // ṛtaś ca ṛtavāg dhātā vidhātā dhāraṇo dhruvaḥ / vidhāraṇo mahātejā vāsavasya paraḥ sakhā // īdṛkṣaścāpyadṛkṣaś ca etādṛgamitāśanaḥ / krīḍitaś ca sadṛkṣaś ca sarabhaś ca mahātapāḥ //
english: Then may Pratimākṛt, Mita, Sammita, Amita, Mahābala, Ṛtajit, Satyajit, Suṣeṇa, Senajit, Atimitra, Anumitra, Purumitra, Aparājita, Ṛta, Ṛtavāk, Dhātā, Vidhātā, Dhāraṇa, Dhruva and Vidhāraṇa, the mighty friend of Indra, Īdṛkṣa, Adṛkṣa, Etādṛk, Amitāśana, Krīḍita, Sadṛkṣa, Sarabha, Mahātapas, Dhartā, Dhurya, Dhuri, Bhīma, Abhimukta, Kṣapātsaha, Dhṛti, Vasu Anādhṛṣya, Rāma, Kāma, Jaya, Virāṭ, the fortynine wind gods protect you.

sanskrit: urṇāyurugrasenaś ca dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca nandakaḥ / hāhā hūhūrnāradaś ca viśvāvasuś ca tumburuḥ // ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu gandharvā vijayāya te /
english: May the GandharvasCitrāṅgada, Citraratha, Citrasena, Kali, Ūrṇāyu, Ugrasena, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Nandaka, Hāhā, Hūhū, Nārada, Viśvāvasu and Tumburu anoint you for your victory.

sanskrit: anavadyā sukeśī ca menakāḥ saha janyayā / kratusthalā ghṛtācī ca viśvācī puñjikasthalā // pramlocā corvaśī rambhā pañcacūḍā tilottamā / citralekhā lakṣmaṇā ca puṇḍarīkā ca vāruṇī //
english: May the foremost among the priests and the divine group of damsels Anavadyā, Sukeśī, Menakā, Sahajanyā, Kratusthalā, Ghṛtācī, Viśvācī, Puñjikasthalā, Pramlocā, Ūrvaśī, Rambhā, Pañcacūḍā, Tilottamā, Citralekhā, Lakṣmaṇā, Puṇḍarīkā and Vāruṇī guard you.

sanskrit: prahlādo virocano 'tha balirvāṇo 'tha tatsutāḥ / ete cānye 'bhiṣiñcantu dānavā rākṣasās tathā // hetiś caiva prahetiś ca vidyutsphurjathuragrakāḥ /
english: May the demons Prahlāda, Virocana, Bali and Bāṇa and their sons and other foremost demons Heti, Praheti, Vidyut, Sphūrjathu anoint you.

sanskrit: yakṣaḥ siddhārmakaḥ pātu māṇibhadraś ca nandanaḥ // piṅgākṣo dyutimāṃś caiva puṣpavanto jayāvahaḥ /
english: May the Yakṣa, the accomplished soulMaṇibhadra, Nandana, Piṅgākṣa, Dyutimān and Puṣpavanta bring forth victory.

sanskrit: śaṅkhaḥ padmaś ca makaraḥ kacchapaś ca nidhirjaye //
english: May the treasures śaṅkha conch, padma lotus, makara fish, kacchapa tortoise bring victory.

sanskrit: piśācā ūrdhvakeśādyā bhūtā bhūmyādivāsinaḥ / mahākālaṃ puraskṛtya narasiṃhañca mātaraḥ // guhaḥ skando viśākhastvānnaigameyo 'bhiṣiñcatu /
english: May the ghosts Ūrdhvakeśa and others, the goblins who dwell on the earth, the divine mothers led by Mahākāla form of Śiva at deluge and Narasiṃha manlion form of Viṣṇu, Guha son of Śiva, Skanda, Viśākha and Naigameya other names of Guha anoint you.

sanskrit: garuḍaścāruṇaḥ pāntu sampātipramukhāḥ khagāḥ / anantādyā mahānāgāḥ śeṣavāsukitakṣakāḥ //
english: May the female goblins and female attendants on God Śiva dwelling in the sky and on the earth and the principal birds such as the Garuḍa, Aruṇa and Sampāti guard you.

sanskrit: airāvato mahāpadmaḥ kambalāśvatarāvubhau / śaṅkhaḥ karkoṭakaś caiva dhṛtarāṣṭro dhanañjayaḥ // kumudair āvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadanto 'tha vāmanaḥ / supratīko 'ñjano nāgāḥ pāntu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā //
english: May the great serpents Ananta, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Airāvata, Mahāpadma, Kambala, Aśvatara, Śaṅkha, Karkoṭaka, Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Dhanañjaya, and the elephants Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, Vāmana, Supratīka and Añjana protect you always from all evils.

sanskrit: paitāmahas tathā haṃso vṛṣabhaḥ śaṅkarasya ca / durgāsiṃhaś ca pāntu tvāṃ yamasya mahiṣas tathā //
english: May the swan, the bull, the lion and the buffalo, respectively the vehicles of Brahmā, Śaṅkara, Durgā and God of Death guard you.

sanskrit: uccaiḥśravāścāśvapatis tathā dhanvantariḥ sadā / kaustubhaḥ śaṅkarājaś ca vajraṃ śūlañca cakrakaṃ //
english: May Uccaiḥśravas, the lord of the horses, lord Dhanvantari, Kaustubha, the foremost among the conches, always proect the mace, spear and the disc.

sanskrit: nandako 'strāṇi rakṣantu dharmaś ca vyavasāyakaḥ / citraguptaś ca daṇḍaś ca piṅgalo mṛtyukālakau //
english: May Nandaka, Dharma, the governor of conduct, Citragupta, the wielder of the punishing rod, Piṅgala, Mṛtyu death and Kālaka the regulator of time protect the weapons.

sanskrit: bālakhilyādimunayo vyāsavālmīkimukhyakāḥ / pṛthurdilīpo bharato duṣyantaḥ śakrajidvalī // mallaḥ kakutsthaścānena yuvanāśvo jayadrathaḥ / māndhātā mucukundaś ca pāntu tvāñca purūravāḥ //
english: May the sages Vālakhilyas and others and the foremost among the sages such as Vyāsa and Vālmīki, the foremost among the kings of the past Pṛthu, Dilīpa, Bharata, Duṣyanta, Śakrajit, Bali, Malla, Kakutstha, Anenas, Yuvanāśva, Jayadratha, Māndhātā, Mucukunda and Purūravas guard you.

sanskrit: vāstudevāḥ pañcaviṃśattattvāni vijayāya te /
english: May the presiding deities of the grounds and the twentyfive principles confer victory on you.

sanskrit: rukmabhaumaḥ śilābhaumaḥ patālo nīlamūrtikaḥ // pītaraktaḥ kṣitiś caiva śvetabhaumo rasātalaṃ /
english: May the golden earth, rocky soil, nether world, blue soil, yellowish red earth, white soil, Rasātala a nether world, the earth, the terrestrial region and the foremost among the continents Jambū etc.

sanskrit: bhūlloko 'tha bhuvarmukhyā jamvūdvīpādayaḥ śriye //
english: bring you fortune.

sanskrit: uttarāḥ kuravaḥ pāntu ramyā hiraṇyakas tathā / bhadrāśvaḥ ketumālaś ca varṣaś caiva valāhakaḥ // harivarṣaḥ kimpuruṣa indradvīpaḥ kaśerumān /
english: May the Uttarakurus and the continents Ramya, Hiraṇyaka, Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla, Balāhaka, Harivarṣa, Kimpuruṣa, Indradvīpa, Kaśerumān, Tāmravarṇa, Gabhastimān, Nāgadvīpa and Saumyaka guard you.

sanskrit: gandharvo varuṇo yaś ca navamaḥ pāntu rājyadāḥ /
english: Varuṇa, the ninth gandharva, the conferer of dominion protect you.

sanskrit: himavān hemakūṭaś ca niṣadho nīla eva ca // śvetaś ca śṛṅavān merurmālyavān gandhamādanaḥ / mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śaktimānṛkṣavān giriḥ //
english: The mountains Himavān. Hemakūṭa Niṣadha, Nīla, Śveta, Śṛṅgavān, Meru, Mālyavān, Gandhamādana, Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śūktimān, Ṛkṣavān, Vindhya and Pāriyātra bestow peace upon you.

sanskrit: vindhyaś ca pāripātraś ca girayaḥ śāntidāstu te / ṛgvedādyāḥ ṣaḍaṅgāni itihāsapurāṇakaṃ //
english: May the Ṛgveda and the other Vedas, the six accessory texts Itihāsa and Purāṇas, medical science, science of music and archery, the accessory Vedas protect you.

sanskrit: śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ jyotiṣāṅgatiḥ // chandogāni ca vedāś ca mīmāṃsā nyāyavistaraḥ / dharmaśāstraṃ purāṇañca vidyā hy etāś caturdaśa //
english: Phonetics, the texts laying down rules for sacrificial acts, grammar, etymology, astronomy and metrics, the four scriptural texts, mīmāṃsā, the science of logic, code of laws and Purāṇa are the fourteen branches of learning.

sanskrit: sāṅkhyaṃ yogaḥ pāśupataṃ vedā vai pañcarātrakaṃ /
english: The schools of philosophy such as the Sāṅkhya and Yoga, the Pāśupata, the Vedas and the Pāñcarātra are the five dogmas.

sanskrit: durgā vidyā ca gāndhārī pāntu tvāṃ śāntidāś ca te /
english: May the goddesses Gāyatrī, Śivā, Durgā, Vidyā and Gāndhārī protect you and confer peace on you.

sanskrit: lavaṇekṣusurāsarpidadhidugdhajalābdhayaḥ // catvāraḥ sāgarāḥ pāntu tīrthāni vividhāni ca /
english: May the four oceans of salt, sugarcane juice, liquor, clarified butter, curd, milk and water and the different sacred spots protect you.

sanskrit: puṣkaraś ca prayāgaś ca prabhāso naimiṣaḥ paraḥ // gayāśīrṣo brahmaśirastīrthamuttramānasaṃ / kālodako nandikuṇḍastīrthaṃ pañcanadas tathā // bhṛgutīrthaṃ prabhāsañca tathā cāmarakaṇṭakaṃ / jambumārgaś ca vimalaḥ kapilasya tathāśramaḥ //
english: They are Puṣkara, Prayāga, Prabhāsa, the excellent Naimiṣa, Gayāśīrṣa, Brahmaśira, Uttaramānasa, Kālodaka, Nandikuṇḍa, Pañcanadatīrtha, Bhṛgutīrtha, Prabhāsa, Amarakaṇṭaka, Jambūmārga, the spotless, the hermitage of Kapila, Gaṅgādvāra Haridvāra, Kuśāvarta, Vindhyaka, Nīlaparvata, Varāhaparvata, Kanakhala, Kālañjara, Kedāra, Rudrakoṭi, Vārāṇasī, the great spot Badarikāśrama, Dvārakā, Śrīgiri, Puruṣottoma Puri, Śālagrāma and Vārāha, the spots of confluence of the rivers with the ocean, Phalgutīrtha, Bindusara, Karavīrāśrama and the rivers Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Śatadru, Gaṇḍakī, Acchodā, Vipāśā, Vitastā, Devikā, Kāverī, Varuṇā, Niścirā, Gomatī, Pārā, Carmaṇvatī, Rūpā, Mandākinī, Mahānadī, Tāpī, Payoṣṇī, Veṇā, Gaurī, Vaitaraṇī, Godāvarī, Bhīmarathī, Tuṅgabhadrā, Araṇī and Candrabhāgā and the goddesses Śivā and Gaurī anoint and protect you.

sanskrit: gaṅgādvārakuśāvartau vindhyako nīlaparvataḥ /
english: Literally means helpful, denotes the Aśvinī kumāras, the celestial physicians.

sanskrit: kālañjaraś ca kedāro rudrakoṭistathaiva ca / vārāṇasī mahātīrthaṃ vadaryāśrama eva ca //
english: Phonetics, the texts laying down rules for sacrificial acts, grammar, etymology, metrics and astronomy. The texts dealing with the interpretation of vedic texts.

sanskrit: tāpī payoṣṇī veṇā ca gaurī vaitaraṇī tathā //
english: Śaivite philosophical texts. Vaiṣṇavite philosophical texts.

sanskrit: so 'bhiṣiktaḥ sahāmātyo jayecchatrūnnṛpottamaḥ /
english: A foremost king thus crowned along with his ministers should conquer the enemies.

sanskrit: rājñā senāpatiḥ kāryo brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo 'tha vā //
english: A brahmin or a kṣatriya should be appointed by the king as the commanderinchief.

sanskrit: kulīno nītiśāstrajñaḥ pratīhāraś ca nītivit / dūtaś ca priyavādī syādakṣīṇo 'tibalānvitaḥ //
english: He should also be a descendant of a noble family and wellversed in ethics. The doorkeeper should be learned in ethics. The emissary should be speaking sweet, strong and a matchless warrior.

sanskrit: tāmbūladhārī nā strī vā bhaktaḥ kleśasahapriyaḥ /
english: The betelbearer may be a man or a woman devoted to the king, capable of enduring fatigue and be affectionate.

sanskrit: sāndhivigrahikaḥ kāryaḥ ṣāḍguṇyādiviśāradaḥ //
english: One who is proficient in the six expedients of royal policy should be made the minister of foreign affairs.

sanskrit: khaḍgadhārī rakṣakaḥ syātdārathiḥ syādbalādivit / sūdādhyakṣo hito vijño mahānasagato hi saḥ //
english: A guard should bear the sword. A charioteer should know the strength of the hostile army. The chief cook should be a beneficiary, learned and one living in the royal kitchen.

sanskrit: sabhāsadastu dharmajñā lekhako 'kṣaraviddhitaḥ / āhvānakālavijñāḥ syurhitā dauvārikā janāḥ //
english: The courtiers should be wellversed in righteousness. The royal scribe should be well versed in the art of writing. The doorkeepers should know the appropriate time of call and be beneficial.

sanskrit: ratnādijño dhanādhyakṣaḥ anudvāre hito naraḥ /
english: The treasurer should be a man wellacquainted with the gems and be beneficial in the acquisition of wealth.

sanskrit: syādāyurvedavidvaidyo gajadhyakṣo 'tha hayādivit // jitaśramo gajāroho hayādhyakṣo hayādivat /
english: The superintendent of elephants should know the science of elephants. The rider of an elephant should be one who has conquered fatigue. The superintendent of horses should know equinology.

sanskrit: durgādhyakṣo hito dhīmān sthapatirvāstuvedavit //
english: The architects should be wellversed in the nature of the grounds.

sanskrit: yantramukte pāṇimukte amukte muktadhārite / astrācāryo niyuddhe ca kuśalo nṛpaterhitaḥ //
english: Persons employed to give instructions in the use of weapons, should be wellversed in the use of weapons projected by the machines or discharged by the hands or not discharged entirely or discharged and held back and fight with hands.

sanskrit: vṛddhaścāntaḥpurādhyakṣaḥ pañcāśadvārṣikāḥ striyaḥ / saptatyavdāstu puruṣāś careyuḥ sarvakarmasu //
english: The officer in the harem should be old, fifty years old if women and seventy years old if men. They should be engaged in all types of work. The man in charge of the arsenal should be wakeful.

sanskrit: jāgratsyādāyudhāgāre jñātvā vṛttirvidhīyate /
english: A person is employed in a task after knowing his ability.

sanskrit: jyecchuḥ pṛthivīṃ rājā sahāyānanayoddhitān // dharmiṣṭhān dharmakāyeṣu śūrān saṅgrāmakarmasu / nipuṇānarthakṛtyeṣu sarvatra ca tathā śucīn //
english: A king should employ foremost, medium and ordinary people after knowing the tasks as excellent, medium and ordinary. A king desirous of victory should bring beneficial accomplices. Righteous men should be engaged in righteous acts, valorous men in tasks like battle, clever men in acts yielding material gains and men of good conduct in all acts.

sanskrit: strīṣu ṣaṇḍānniyuñjīta tīkṣṇān dāruṇakarmasu /
english: Eunuchs should be employed in matters relating to women and cruelhearted men in cruel deeds.

sanskrit: yo yatra vidito rājñā śucitvena tu tannaraṃ // dharme cārthe ca kāme ca niyuñjītādhame 'dhamān /
english: Whomsoever the king knows to be of good conduct, that person should be employed by the kings in the acts of piety, acquisition of wealth and pleasure.

sanskrit: rājā yathārhaṃ kuryācca upādhābhiḥ parīkṣitān //
english: The king should employ in appropriate task those people whose fidelity has been tested.

sanskrit: samantro ca yathānyāyāt kuryāddhastivanecarān / tatpadānveṣaṇe yattānadhyakṣāṃstatra kārayet //
english: The minister should engage properly men of the same kind to find the evil doers just as an elephant is employed to control the wild ones. Experts should be employed in their own fields of specialization.

sanskrit: yasmin karmaṇi kauśalyaṃ yasya tasmin niyojayet / pitṛpaitāmahān bhṛtyān sarvakarmasu yojayet //
english: The servants who have been serving since the time of the grandfather and father of the king should be engaged to do all tasks except in matters which are to be done by the heirs.

sanskrit: vinā dāyādakṛtyeṣu tatra te hi samāgatāḥ /
english: In those acts, only those who have come in that line should be employed.

sanskrit: pararājagṛhāt prāptān janān saṃśrayakāmyayā // duṣṭānapyatha vāduṣṭān saṃśrayeta prayatnataḥ /
english: Men who have come from other kings and desiring protege should be given protection irrespective of the fact whether they are bad or good.

sanskrit: duṣṭaṃ jñātvā viśvasenna tadvṛttiṃ vartayedvaśe //
english: If one is known to be bad, the king should not trust him and keep his livelihood under his control.

sanskrit: deśāntarāgatān pārśve cāraijñātvā hi pūjayet /
english: Men who have come from a different country should be watched by engaging spies and then honoured if they are found to be good.

sanskrit: śatravo 'gnivarṣaṃ sarpo nistriṃśamapi caikataḥ // bhṛtyā vaśiṣṭaṃ vijñeyāḥ kubhṛṭyāś ca tathaikataḥ / cāracakṣurbhavedrājā niyuñjīta sadācarān //
english: The enemies, fire, poison, serpent and the sword on one side and the trustworthy, distinguished servants on the other side should be known as equal. So also the wicked servants on one side equal the loyal servants ? The king should have the spies as the eyes. He should always, employ the spies.

sanskrit: janasyāvihitān saumyāṃs tathājñātān parasparaṃ /
english: The spies should not be known to the people. They should be good and not known to each other.

sanskrit: vaṇijo mantrakuśalān sāṃvatsaracikitsakān // tathā pravrajitākārān balābalavivekinaḥ /
english: He should employ the spies in the guise of tradesmen, diplomats, astrologers, physicians and as ascetics knowing the strength and weakness of the people.

sanskrit: naikasya rājā śraddadhyācchraddadhyād bahuvākyataḥ //
english: The king should not trust the words of a single person. He should believe the words of many.

sanskrit: rāgāparāgau bhṛtyānāṃ janasya ca guṇāguṇān / śubhānāmaśubhānāñca jñānaṅkuryādvaśāya ca //
english: The king should make use of the likes, displeasures, merits and demerits of his servants and people, as well as the good and bad deeds done by them in order to control them.

sanskrit: anurāgakaraṃ karma carejjahmādvirāgajaṃ /
english: He should do only such acts which would attract them and desist from acts causing displeasure.

sanskrit: janānurāgayā lakṣmyā rājā syājjanarañjanāt //
english: The king would be adorned by the fortune of the pleasure of the people because of pleasing the people.

sanskrit: bhṛtyaḥ kuryāttu rājājñāṃ śiṣyavatsacchriyaḥ pateḥ /
english: The servant has to carry out the orders of the king , like a disciple, for the prosperity of the master.

sanskrit: na kṣipedvacanaṃ rājño anukūlaṃ priyaṃ vadet // rahogatasya vaktavyamapriyaṃ yaddhitaṃ bhavet /
english: He should not disobey the commands of the king. He should speak only that which is good and dear to him. If an unpleasant news is beneficial to the king, the servant should let him know in privacy.

sanskrit: na niyukto haredvittaṃ nopekṣettasya mānakaṃ //
english: When he has been employed in some work he should not swindle the money. He should not do anything that would affect his dignity.

sanskrit: rājñaś ca na tathākāryaṃ veśabhāṣāviceṣṭitaṃ /
english: He should not similarly put on the dress of the king and speak and act in the manner of the king.

sanskrit: antaḥpuracarādhyakṣo vairabhūtair nirākṛtaiḥ // saṃsargaṃ na vrajedbhṛtyo rājño guhyañca gopayet /
english: The superintendent of the attendants of the harem should not have any contact with those dismissed by the king and have become enemies. The servant should guard the secret of the king.

sanskrit: pradarśya kauśalaṃ kiñcidrājānantu viśeṣayet //
english: After having done some act of ingenuity, the servant should ascribe it to the king.

sanskrit: rājñā yacchrāvitaṃ guhyaṃ na talloke prakāśayet /
english: He should not give publicity to any of the secrets heard by him from the king.

sanskrit: ājñāpyamāne vānyasmin kiṅkaromīti vā vadet //
english: When some superior person orders him to disclose he should say, “what to do?”

sanskrit: vastraṃ ratnamalaṅkāraṃ rājñā dattaṃ ca dhārayet / nānirdiṣṭo dvāri viśennāyogye bhuvi rājadṛk //
english: He should wear the dress, gems and ornaments given by the king. He should not enter the royal chamber without being asked by the king. He should not see him at an improper place.

sanskrit: jṛmbhānniṣṭhīvanaṅkāsaṃ kopaṃ paryantikāśrayaṃ / bhṛkuṭīṃ vātamudgāraṃ tatsamīpe visarjayet //
english: He should avoid yawning, spitting, coughing, frowning based on depravity, raising the eyebrows and eructation near him.

sanskrit: svaguṇākhyāpane yuktyā parāneva prayojayet /
english: One should engage others cleverly by making the king know about his qualities.

sanskrit: śāṭhyaṃ laulyaṃ sapaiśūnyaṃ nāstikyaṃ kṣudratā tathā // cāpalyañca parityājyaṃ nityaṃ rājānujīvinā /
english: Perfidy, avarice slandering, atheism, meanness and ficklemindedness should always be avoided by one in the service of the king.

sanskrit: śrutena vidyāśilpaiś ca saṃyojyātmānamātmanā // rājasevāntataḥ kuryādbhūtaye bhūtivardhanaḥ /
english: A servant who thus associates his own self with the self by means of scriptural knowledge and manual work should then do the service to the king for the sake of the growth of fortune.

sanskrit: namaskāryāḥ sadā cāsya putravallabhamantriṇaḥ //
english: He should always bow down to the sons, favourites and ministers of that person the king.

sanskrit: sacivair nāsya viśvāso rājacittapriyañcaret /
english: He need not gain the confidence of the ministers.

sanskrit: tyajedviraktaṃ raktāttu vṛttimīheta rājavit // apṛṣṭaścāsya na brūyāt kāmaṃ kuryāttathāpadi /
english: He should do such acts which please the king. The servant should ignore those not liked by the king. One who knows the king should desire to earn his livelihood from those liked by the king.

sanskrit: prasanno vākyasaṅgrāhī rahasye na ca śaṅkate //
english: He should not speak anything when not asked by the king.

sanskrit: kuśalādiparipraśnaṃ samprayacchati cāsanaṃ /
english: The duty of the servant is to enquire about the health of the king and to make the seat ready for him.

sanskrit: tatkathāśravaṇāddhṛṣṭo apriyāṇyapi nandane // alpaṃ dattaṃ pragṛhṇāti smaret kathāntareṣvapi /
english: A servant rejoices to hear the exploits of the king. He rejoices even after hearing an unpleasant comment. He receives the small remuneration and remembers it on other occasion.

sanskrit: iti raktasya kartavyaṃ sevāmanyasya varjayet //
english: Only such a servant should be employed. The services of others should be avoided.

sanskrit: durgasampattimākhyāsye durgadeśe vasennṛpaḥ /
english: shall describe the excellent fortification.

sanskrit: vaiśyaśūdrajanaprāyo 'hyanāhāryas tathāparaiḥ //
english: It should abound with the traders and servants and sparsely with others.

sanskrit: kiñcidbrāhmaṇasaṃyukto bahukarmakaras tathā /
english: It should have few brahmins and plenty of artisans.

sanskrit: adevamātṛko bhaktajalo deśaḥ praśasyate //
english: A country not depending on rainwater and having plenty of water for cultivation is commended.

sanskrit: parair apīḍītaḥ puṣpaphaladhānyasanvitaḥ /
english: It should not be vulnerable for attack by others and should abound with flowers, fruits and grains.

sanskrit: agamyaḥ paracakrāṇāṃ vyālataskaravarjitaḥ //
english: It should be impassable by foreign army and should be free from rogues and thieves.

sanskrit: ṣaṇṇāmekatamaṃ durgaṃ tatra kṛtvā vasedbalī / dhanurdurgaṃ mahīdurgaṃ naradurgaṃ tathaiva ca // vārkṣañcaivāmbudurgañca giridurgañca bhārgava /
english: The mighty king should build one of the following types of forts and live there. O Bhārgava son of Bhṛgu Paraśurāma! Fort guarded by archers, land, men, forest, water and hill are the six kinds of forts. The excellent among these forts would be the fort protected by the hill.

sanskrit: purantatra ca haṭṭādyadevatāyatanādikaṃ /
english: Such a fort should have the market place, temple and other things.

sanskrit: anuyantrāyudhopetaṃ sodakaṃ durgamuttamaṃ //
english: A fort furnished with weapons and implements and surrounded by water is an excellent one.

sanskrit: rājarakṣāṃ pravakṣyāmi rakṣyo bhūpo viṣāditaḥ /
english: shall describe the means of protecting the king. The king has to be saved from poison.

sanskrit: pañcāṅgastu śirīṣaḥ syānmūtrapiṣṭo viṣārdanaḥ //
english: The śirīṣa well ground with cow’s urine, known as pañcāṅga destroys poison.

sanskrit: śatāvarī chinnaruhā viṣaghnī taṇḍulīyakaṃ / koṣātakī ca kalhārī brāhmī citrapaṭolikā // maṇḍūlaparṇī vārāhī dhātryānandakameva ca /
english: Śatāvarī, chinnaruhā, viṣaghnī, taṇḍulīyaka, kośātakī, kalhārī, brāhmī, citrapaṭolikā, maṇḍūkaparṇī, vārāhī, dhātrī, ānandakaṃ , unmādinī, somarājī and the gemstone destroying poison are the antidotes for poison.

sanskrit: vāstulakṣaṇasaṃyukte vasan durge surānyajet / prajāś ca pālayedduṣṭāñjayeddānāni dāpayet //
english: Residing in the fort possessing the characteristics of a dwelling place, the king should propitiate gods. He should protect the subjects, conquer the wicked and make gifts.

sanskrit: devadravyādiharaṇāt kalpantu narake vaset / devālayāni kurvīta devapūjārato nṛpaḥ //
english: The king who takes away the articles dedicated to the god would dwell in hell for a kalpa period. The king being devoted to the worship of gods should erect temples.

sanskrit: surālayāḥ pālanīyāḥ sthāpanīyāś ca devatāḥ /
english: The temples should be protected and images of deities should be installed.

sanskrit: mṛṇmayāddārujaṃ puṇyaṃ dārujādiṣṭakāmayaṃ // aiṣṭakācchailajaṃ puṇyaṃ śailajāt svarṇaratnajaṃ /
english: A wooden one is meritorious than the earthen one, one made of bricks than the wooden one. One made of stone is meritorious than that of the image made of brick. One made of gold and gems is meritorious than that of the stone one.

sanskrit: krīḍan suragṛhaṃ kurvan bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt //
english: Even by the construction of a temple sportively one would get enjoyment and emancipation.

sanskrit: citrakvad gītavādyādiprekṣaṇīyādidānakṛt / tailājyamadhudugdhādyaiḥ snāpya devaṃ divaṃ vrajet //
english: One who donates paintings, musical instruments and arranges for dramatic performances to be seen and who anoints the deity with oil, clarified butter, honey, milk and other things would go to heaven.

sanskrit: pūjayet pālayedviprān dvijasvanna harennṛpaḥ /
english: The king should worship and protect the brahmins.

sanskrit: suvarṇamekaṃ gāmekāṃ bhūmerapyekamaṅgulaṃ // harannarakamāpnoti yāvadāhūtasamplavaṃ /
english: The king would reach hell and remain there till the inundation of beings deluge by taking away a piece of gold, a cow or an aṅgula breadth of a thumb measure of land from a brahmin.

sanskrit: naivāsti brāhmaṇabadhāt pāpaṃ gurutaraṃ kvacit /
english: There is no other sin greater than the killing of a brahmin.

sanskrit: adaivaṃ daivataṃ kuryuḥ kuryurdaivamadaivataṃ //
english: The brahmins would make nondivine into divine and divine into nondivine.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā hi mahābhāgāstānnamasyetsadaiva tu /
english: Brahmins are the most fortunate ones.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇī rudatī hanti kulaṃ rājyaṃ prajās tathā //
english: A brahmin woman who weeps would destroy the family, kingdom and subjects of a king.

sanskrit: sādhvīstrīṇāṃ pālanañca rājā kuryācca dhārmikaḥ /
english: A righteous king should protect the chaste women.

sanskrit: striyā prahṛṣṭayā bhāvyaṃ gṛhakāryaikadakṣayā // susaṃskṛtopaskarayā vyaye cāmuktahastayā /
english: The women should engage happily and efficiently in the cores of household work. She should be decorating well the household articles and be frugal in her expenses.

sanskrit: yasmai dadyātpitā tvenāṃ śuśrūṣettaṃ patiṃ sadā //
english: She should always do service to her husband to whom her father has given her in marriage.

sanskrit: mṛte bhartari svaryāyāt brahmacarye sthitāṅganā /
english: The lady practising continence after the death of the husband goes to heaven.

sanskrit: paraveśmarucir nasyānna syāt kalahaśālinī // maṇḍanaṃ varjayennārī tathā proṣitabhartṛkā /
english: She should not have the desire to live in other’s house and should not be quarrelsome. A widow as well as the wife of a man who has gone abroad, should not decorate her person.

sanskrit: devatārādhanaparā tiṣṭhedbhartṛhite ratā //
english: She should always be bent on the worship of god and the welfare of the husband.

sanskrit: dhārayenmaṅgalārthāya kiñcidābharaṇantathā /
english: A woman whose husband has gone abroad should wear some ornaments for the welfare of the husband.

sanskrit: bhartrāgniṃ yā viśennārī sāpi svagamavāpnuyāt //
english: The woman widow who enters the funeral fire along with the dead husband would also reach heaven.

sanskrit: śriyaḥ sampūjanaṅkāryaṃ gṛhasammārjanādikaṃ /
english: A householder should worship the goddess of fortune and do the cleansing of the house etc.

sanskrit: dvādaśyāṃ kārttike viṣṇuṃ gāṃ savatsāṃ dadettathā //
english: He should worship lord Viṣṇu on the twelfth day of kārttika and then make a gift of a cow together with a calf.

sanskrit: sāvitryā rakṣito bhartā satyācāravratena ca /
english: Her husband was saved by Sāvitrī wife of Satyavān, king of Sālva by practising truthfulness and good conduct.

sanskrit: saptamyāṃ mārgaśīrṣe tu site 'bhyarcya divākaraṃ // putrānāpnoti ca strīha nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //26//
english: There need not be any doubt that a woman would have children by the worship of the Sun on the seventh day in the bright fortnight in the month of mārgaśīrṣa.

sanskrit: grāmasyādhipatiṃ kuryāddaśagrāmādhipaṃ nṛpaḥ /
english: A king should appoint a head for every village, for ten villages, for hundred villages, and then an overall head.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ bhogavibhāgaś ca bhavet karmānurūpataḥ /
english: Their salaries would be in conformity with their duties.

sanskrit: nityameva tathā kāryaṃ teṣāñcāraiḥ parīkṣaṇaṃ //
english: The king should watch them daily through his spies.

sanskrit: grāme doṣān samutpannān grāmeśaḥ prasamaṃ nayet / aśakto daśapālasya sa tu gatvā nivedayet //
english: Any irregularity that has arisen in the village should be controlled by the village head. If he is not able to set it right he should approach the head of ten villages and report him.

sanskrit: śrutvāpi daśapālo 'pi tatra yuktimupācaret /
english: The head of the ten villages also should take appropriate step after having heard the same.

sanskrit: vittādyāpnoti rājā vai viṣayāttu surakṣitāt //
english: The king would get wealth etc. by protecting the state.

sanskrit: dhanavāndharmamāpnoti dhanavān kāmamaśnute /
english: A wealthy man gets righteousness and enjoys the desires.

sanskrit: ucchidyante vinā hy arthaiḥ kriyā grīṣme saridyathā //
english: All actions without being supported by wealth would be ephemeral just as the river in the summer.

sanskrit: viśeṣo nāsti lokeṣe patitasyādhanasya ca /
english: There is no difference between the fallen and the poor in the world.

sanskrit: patitānna tu gṛhṇanti daridro na prayacchati //
english: No one would take from the fallen. A poor man would not give.

sanskrit: dhanahīnasya bhāryāpi naikā syādupavartinī /
english: Even the wife of the poor would not lend him support.

sanskrit: rāṣṭrapīḍākaro rājā narake vasate ciraṃ //
english: A king oppressing the country would dwell in hell for a long time.

sanskrit: nityaṃ rājñā tathā bhāvyaṃ garbhiṇī sahadharmiṇī / yahā svaṃ sukhamutsṛjya garbhasya sukhamāvahet //
english: A king should do in the same way as a pregnant woman who would abandon her comforts and would attend to the welfare of the child in the womb.

sanskrit: kiṃ yajñaistapasā tasya prajā yasya na rakṣitāḥ /
english: What use of the sacrifices or of the penance for a king whose subjects have not been protected.

sanskrit: surakṣitāḥ prajā yasya svargastasya gṛhopamaḥ //
english: One whose subjects have been well protected, his house would be equal to heaven.

sanskrit: arakṣitāḥ prajā yasya narakaṃ tasya mandiraṃ /
english: One whose subjects have not been protected, his house would be the hell.

sanskrit: rājā ṣaḍbhāgamādatte sukṛtādduṣkṛtādapi //
english: The king collects onesixth of the income of both the good and bad subjects.

sanskrit: dharmāgamo rakṣaṇācca pāpamāpnotyarakṣaṇāt /
english: The king would acquire virtue by protecting the subjects and sin by not protecting them.

sanskrit: subhagā viṭabhīteva rājavallabhataskaraiḥ // bhakṣyamāṇāḥ prajā rakṣyāḥ kāyasthaiś ca viśeṣataḥ /
english: The subjects should be protected by the king from the oppressions by thieves in the guise of the officers of the state, especially the writercaste, just as a virtuous woman afraid of a villain is protected.

sanskrit: rakṣitā tadbhayebhyastu rājño bhavati sā prajā
english: The subjects being protected from their fear by the king would be the subjects of the king.

sanskrit: arakṣitā sā bhavati teṣāmeveha bhojanaṃ /
english: If not protected they become an easy prey for them.

sanskrit: duṣṭasammardanaṃ kuryācchāstroktaṃ karamādadet // koṣe praveśayedardhaṃ nityañcārdhaṃ dvije dadet /
english: The wicked should be put down and the tax laid down in the codes should be taken. Half the amount collected should be kept in the treasury and the other half should be given to brahmins daily.

sanskrit: nidhiṃ dvijottamaḥ prāpya gṛhṇīyātsakalaṃ tathā //
english: Having found a treasure a brahmin should take it in entirety.

sanskrit: caturthamaṣṭamaṃ bhāgaṃ tathā ṣoḍaśamaṃ dvijaḥ / varṇakrameṇa dadyācca nidhiṃ pātre tu dharmataḥ //
english: The same having been found by a kṣatriya, a vaiśya or a śūdra it is enough if onefourth or oneeighth or onesixteenth part of the treasure is given to the king in order as per law.

sanskrit: anṛtantu vadan daṇḍyaḥ suvittasyāṃśamaṣṭamaṃ /
english: One who lies is punishable with a fine of oneeighth part of the treasure.

sanskrit: praṇaṣṭasvāmikamṛkthaṃ rājātryabdaṃ nidhāpayet // arvāk tryabdāddharet svāmī pareṇa nṛpatirharet / mamedamiti yo brūyāt so 'rthayukto yathāvidhi //
english: The king should keep an unclaimed property in his custody for three years. One who is able to establish his claim after three years by saying that ‘it is mine’ should be given the property as laid down. On the contrary the king would forfeit the wealth.

sanskrit: sampādya rūpasaṅkhyādīn svāmī tad dravyamarhati / bāladāyādikamṛkthaṃ tāvadrājānupālayet // yāvatsyātsa samāvṛtto yāvadvātītaśaiśavaḥ /
english: The owner of a property deserves to get that property after furnishing details about its nature, dimension etc. The king should manage the property belonging to a minor till he the minor completes his study or crosses the state of childhood.

sanskrit: bālaputrāsu caivaṃ syādrakṣaṇaṃ niṣkalāsu ca //
english: The same procedure should be followed in the case of the properties belonging to widows with children and those not having the guardians.

sanskrit: pativratāsu ca strīṣu vidhabāsvāturāsu ca / jīvantīnāntu tāsāṃ ye saṃhareyuḥ svavāndhavāḥ //
english: The righteous king should punish those relatives who seize the properties of faithful women who have become widows and weak, even as they are alive, with the punishment meted to the thief.

sanskrit: sāmānyato hṛtañcauraistadvai dadyāt svayaṃ nṛpaḥ // caurarakṣādhikāribhyo rājāpi hṛtamāpnuyāt /
english: In general the property stolen by a thief should be paid by the king himself. The king should obtain from thieves and the officers in charge of the protection, the property taken by them.

sanskrit: ahṛte yo hṛtaṃ brūyānniḥsāryo daṇḍya eva saḥ //
english: One who lies that he has been robbed when he has not been robbed should be punished and expelled from the country.

sanskrit: na tadrājñā pradātavyaṃ gṛhe yad gṛhagair hṛtaṃ /
english: The property that has been stolen by the inmates of the house need not be restored by the king.

sanskrit: svarāṣṭrapaṇyādādadyādrājā viṃśatimaṃ dvija //
english: O Brahmin! the king should take one twentieth of the value from the merchandise belonging to his country.

sanskrit: śulkāṃśaṃ paradeśācca kṣayavyayaprakāśakaṃ / jñātvā saṅkalpayecchulkaṃ lābhaṃ vaṇigyathāpnuyāt //
english: The fees to be levied on goods from foreign countries should be determined after knowing the cost, the wear and tear and the profit got by the trader.

sanskrit: viṃśāṃśaṃ lābhamādadyāddaṇḍanīyastato 'nyathā /
english: In this case one twentieth of the profit should be taken. If not paid the importer should be punished.

sanskrit: strīṇāṃ pravrajitānāñca taraśulkaṃ vivarjayet //
english: Freight should not be collected from women and mendicants.

sanskrit: tareṣu dāsadoṣeṇa naṣṭaṃ dāsāṃstu dāpayet /
english: The ferryman should be made to repay by the king that which has been lost in transit on account of the fault of the ferryman.

sanskrit: śūkadhānyeṣu ṣaḍbhāgaṃ śimbidhānye tathāṣṭamaṃ // rājā vanyārthamādadyāddeśakālānurūpakaṃ /
english: The king should take one sixth in the case of the grain śūka barley and one eighth in the case of the grain śimbi a kind of kidney bean as toll befitting the region and season.

sanskrit: pañcaṣaḍbhāgamādadyād rājā paśuhiraṇyayoḥ //
english: The king should take four and five parts respectively in the case of animals and gold.

sanskrit: gandhauṣadhirasānāñca puṣpamūlaphalasya ca / patraśākatṛṇānāñca vaṃśavaiṇavacarmaṇāṃ // vaidalānāñca bhāṇḍānāṃ sarvasyāśmamayasya ca / ṣaḍbhāgameva cādadyān madhumāṃsasya sarpiṣaḥ //
english: Only.a sixth part should be collected in the case of perfumes, herbs, cereals, flowers, roots, fruits, leaves, vegetables, straw, bamboos hides, wicker works and vessels made of stone and all other materials, honey, meat and clarified butter.

sanskrit: mriyannapi na cādadyād brāhmaṇebhyas tathā karaṃ /
english: The king should not levy tax on the brahmins even in emergency.

sanskrit: yasya rājñastu viṣaye śrotriyaḥ sīdati kṣudhā // tasya sīdati tadrāṣṭraṃ vyādhidurbhikṣataskaraiḥ /
english: The king in whose realm a brahmin, wellversed in the scriptures, perishes on account of hunger, his kingdom gets ruined on account of diseases, famine and thieves.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ vṛttantu vijñāya vṛttiṃ tasya prakalpayet //
english: The king should ascertain the attainments and provide him an occupation.

sanskrit: rakṣecca sarvatastvenaṃ pitā putramivaurasaṃ /
english: The king should always protect him just as the father would protect his son.

sanskrit: saṃrakṣyamaṇo rājñā yaḥ kurute dharmamanvahaṃ // tenāyurvardhate rājño draviṇaṃ rāṣṭrameva ca / karma kuryur narendrasya māsenaikañca śilpinaḥ //
english: The life of the king, the wealth and the kingdom would increase by the meritorious deeds of a person brahmin being protected by the king. The artisans of the king should work for a day in a month without any remuneration.

sanskrit: bhuktamātreṇa ye cānye svaśarīropajīyinaḥ //34//
english: The other workers under him should work without any remuneration by taking food only.

sanskrit: vakṣye 'ntaḥpuracintāṃ ca dharmādyāḥ puruṣārthakāḥ /
english: shall describe the duties of the king in the harem . Virtues etc. are the purpose of life for the king.

sanskrit: anyonyarakṣayā teṣāṃ sevā kāryā striyā nṛpaiḥ //
english: The kings should entertain them without mutual conflict in the company of the women.

sanskrit: dharmamūlo 'rthaviṭapas tathā karmaphalo mahān /
english: Virtue is the root, worldly prosperity the bough and action or deed the great fruit.

sanskrit: trivargapādapastatra rakṣayā phalabhāgaṃ bhavet //
english: One who fosters this tree of the three objects of worldly existence, would realise the fruits.

sanskrit: kāmādhīnāḥ striyo rāma tadarthaṃ ratnasaṅgrahaḥ /
english: O Rāma! Women are subject to desire. Hence the gems are gathered for their sake.

sanskrit: sevyāstā nātisevyāś ca bhūbhujā viṣayaiṣiṇā // āhāro maithunannidrā sevyā nāti hi rug bhavet /
english: They should be entertained and also not much entertained by the king who desires for wealth. One should not indulge excessively in eating, sexual pleasure and sleep.

sanskrit: mañcādhikāre kartavyāḥ striyaḥ sevyāḥ svarāmikāḥ //
english: The king should share his bed only with his beloved women.

sanskrit: aikyaṃ dviṣadbhirvrajati garvaṃ vahati coddhatā // cumbitā mārṣṭi vadanaṃ dattanna bahu manyate / svapityādau prasuptāpi tathā paścādvibudhyate // spṛṣṭā dhunoti gātrāṇi gātrañca viruṇaddhi yā / īṣacchṛṇoti vākyāni priyāṇyapi parāṅmukhī //
english: A woman behaving badly, not rejoicing in hearing his exploits, associating with the enemies of the king, feeling haughty and proud, wiping her face when kissed, not feeling grateful after accepting a present, sleeping before and getting up later after sleep, shaking the body when touched and preventing from touching the body on account of shyness, scarcely listening to pleasing words and keeping the face turned away, ignoring to look at things placed in front, concealing the loins, having a pale face when looked at, turning her face away from the friends, appearing as if a mediator in the affairs of other women loved by the king and not adorning her person even after knowing that it is time for adorning should be rejected.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭe vivarṇavadanā mitreṣvatha parāṅmukhī //
english: One who is disinterested should be rejected and one who is loving should be entertained.

sanskrit: tatkāmitāsu ca strīsu madhyastheva ca lakṣyate /
english: The characteristics of a loving woman are as follows.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva hṛṣṭā bhavati vīkṣite ca parāṅmukhī // dṛśyamanā tathānyatra dṛṣṭiṃ kṣipati cañcalāṃ /
english: She rejoices even at the sight of her husband. When looked at she casts her eyes down. Being looked at she places her shaking glances elsewhere.

sanskrit: tathāpyupāvartayituṃ naiva śaknotyaśeṣataḥ //
english: Yet she would not be able to turn aside her look completely.

sanskrit: vivṛṇīti tathāṅgāni svasyā guhyāni bhārgava / garhitañca tathaivāṅgaṃ prayatnena nigūhati //
english: O Bhārgava son of Bhṛgu, Paraśurāma! She exhibits her concealed parts of body and covers up with effort the organs prohibited from being displayed.

sanskrit: taddarśane ca kurute bālāliṅganacumbanaṃ /
english: She embraces and kisses him immediately after being seen.

sanskrit: ābhāṣyamāṇā bhavati satyavākyā tathaiva ca //
english: She always speaks only the truth.

sanskrit: spṛṣṭā pulakitair aṅgaiḥ svedenaiva ca bhujyate /
english: When being touched feels horripilation later manifesting as the sweatdrops on the body.

sanskrit: karoti ca tathā rāma sulabhadravyayācanaṃ //
english: O Rāma! She asks for easy and simple things from the husband.

sanskrit: tataḥ svalpamapi prāpya karoti paramāṃ mudaṃ /
english: She gets great rejoice after getting even a little.

sanskrit: nāmasaṅkīrtanādeva muditā bahu manyate //
english: She feels elated and favoured much by the mere pronunciation of her name.

sanskrit: karajāṅkāṅkitānyasya phalāni preṣayatyapi /
english: She sends fruits to her husband with the impressions of her nails.

sanskrit: tatpreṣitañca hṛdaye vinyasatyapi cādarāt // āliṅganaiś ca gātrāṇi limpatīvāmṛtena yā /
english: She holds those sent by her husband on the chest out of regard. She besmears the body as if with the ambrosia by her embraces.

sanskrit: supte svapityathādau ca tathā tasya vibudhyate // urū spṛśati cātyarthaṃ suptañcainaṃ vibudhyate /
english: She sleeps after the husband had slept and would get up before he gets up. She would wake him up from sleep by touching his thigh much.

sanskrit: kapitthacūrṇayogena tathā daghnaḥ srajā tathā // ghṛtaṃ sugandhi bhavati dugdhaiḥ kṣiptais tathā yavaiḥ /
english: O Sage! The clarified butter becomes fragrant by combination with the powders of kapittha and a column of curd as also with barley put in milk.

sanskrit: bhojyasya kalpanaivaṃ syādgandhamuktiḥ pradarśyate //
english: This is the way by which an eatable thing should be dressed. Now shall describe the mode of preparation of perfumes.
