sanskrit: śaucamācamanaṃ rāma tathaiva ca virecanaṃ / bhāvanā caiva pākaś ca bodhanaṃ dhūpanantathā // vāsanañcaiva nirdiṣṭaṃ karmāṣṭakamidaṃ smṛtaṃ /
english: O Rama! Cleansing, gargling, vomitting, adorning with flowers etc., heating, burning incense sticks fumigation and perfuming are indicated to be the eight acts.

sanskrit: kapitthabilvajamvāmrakaravīrakapallavaiḥ //
english: Purification of a thing is by washing it with water containing the leaves of Kapittha, bilva, mango and Karavīra.

sanskrit: teṣāmabhāve śaucantu mṛgadarpāmbhasā bhavet //
english: In the absence of these, purification should be done with water saturated with musk.

sanskrit: nakhaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ ghanaṃ māṃsī spṛkkaśaileyajaṃ jalaṃ / tathaiva kuṅkumaṃ lākṣā candanāgurunīradaṃ // saralaṃ devakāṣṭhañca karpūraṃ kāntayā saha / bālaḥ kundurukaś caiva gugguluḥ śrīnivāsakaḥ //
english: The twentyone herbs for fumigation arenakha, kuṣṭha, dhana, māṃsī, spṛkka, śaileyaja, jala, saffron, shellac, sandal, agallochum, nīrada, sarala, devakāṣṭha, camphor, kāntā, bāla, kunduruka, guggulu, śrīnivāsaka and sarjarasa.

sanskrit: dve dve dravye samādāya sarjabhāgair niyojayet /
english: Two of these should be taken and mixed with parts of resin from a śāla tree.

sanskrit: nakhapiṇyākamalayaiḥ saṃyojya madhunā tathā // dhūpayogā bhavantīha yathāvat svecchayā kṛtāḥ /
english: They become fit for fumigation by being mixed with nakha, piṇyāka, malaya and honey and made as desired in the proper way.

sanskrit: tvacannāḍīṃ phalantailaṃ kuṅkumaṃ granthi pravartakaṃ // śaileyantagaraṃ krāntāṃ colaṅkarpūrameva ca / māṃsīṃ surāñca kuṣṭhañca snānadravyāṇi nirdiśet //
english: The bark, tubular part, fruit, oil, saffron, granthiparvaka, śaileya, tagara, kāntā, cola, camphor, māṃsī, surā and kuṣṭha are said to be the things to be used for bathing. One should bathe with any three things from these collected as one desires after mixing with the musk.

sanskrit: etebhyastu samādāya dravyatrayamathecchayā /
english: This would increase the passion.

sanskrit: tvaṅmurānaladaistulyair vālakārdhasamāyutaiḥ / snānamutpalagandhi syāt satailaṃ kuṅkumāyate //
english: If one bathes with tvak, murā and analada in equal proportions added to half the quantity of bālaka with saffron and oil, one would have the fragrance of the lotus.

sanskrit: jātīpuṣasugandhi syāt tagarārdhena yojitaṃ /
english: By adding a half of tagara in the same, it will have the fragrance of the jātī flower.

sanskrit: saddhyāmakaṃ syādvakulaistulyagandhi manoharaṃ //
english: It gives a captivating fragrance of the bakula flowers with the dhyāmaka grass.

sanskrit: mañjiṣṭhātagaraṃ colaṃ tvacaṃ vyaghranakhaṃ nakkhaṃ / gandhapatrañca vinyasya gandhatailaṃ bhavecchubhaṃ //
english: One would get an auspicious fragrant oil by putting the mañjiṣṭhā, tagara, cola, tvak, vyāghranakha, nakha and gandhapatra.

sanskrit: tailaṃ nipīḍitaṃ rāma tilaiḥ puṣpādhivāsitaiḥ / vāsanāt puṣpasadṛśaṃ gandhena tu bhaved dhruvaṃ //
english: O Rāma! the oil extracted from the sesamum and scented with any of the flowers would certainly have the fragrance of the flower.

sanskrit: karpūraṃ kuṅkumaṃ kāntā mṛgadarpaṃ hareṇukaṃ / kakkolailālavaṅgañca jātau kośakameva ca //
english: Cardamom, clove, kakkola, nutmeg and camphor mixed with the skin of the nutmeg would be able to make the mouth fragrant.

sanskrit: tvakpatraṃ truṭimustau ca latāṃ kastūrikaṃ tathā / kaṇṭakāni lavaṅgasya phalapatre ca jātitaḥ // kaṭukañca phalaṃ rāma kārṣikāṇyupakalpayet / taccūrṇe khadiraṃ sāraṃ dadyātturyaṃ tu vāsitaṃ //
english: O Rāma! a kārṣika weight of camphor, saffron kāntā, musk, hareṇuka, kakkola, cardamom, clove, jātī, kośaka, tvakpatra, truṭi, musta, kastūrikā latā, the thorns of clove, the fruit and skin of nutmeg and kaṭuka should be powdered and a fourth part of the essence of khadira that gives fragrance should be added. Then tablets should be made of them by adding mango juice.

sanskrit: mukha nyastāḥ sugandhāstā mukharogavināśanāḥ //
english: When kept in the mouth they give fragrance and destroy the diseases of the mouth.

sanskrit: pūgaṃ prakṣālitaṃ samyak pañcapallavavāriṇā / śaktyā tu guṭikādravyair vāsitaṃ mukhavāsakaṃ //
english: Arecanut well washed with the waters of the leaves of five trees and made fragrant with the above things used for making the pills would make the mouth fragrant.

sanskrit: kaṭukaṃ dantakāṣṭhañca gomūtre vāsitaṃ tryahaṃ / kṛtañca pūgavadrāma mukhasaugandhikārakaṃ //
english: O Rāma! the herbs kaṭuka and dantakāṣṭha soaked in cow’s urine for three days and perfumed as the arecanut would make the mouth fragrant.

sanskrit: tvakpathyayoḥ samāvaṃśau śaśibhāgārdhasaṃyutau / nāgavallīsamo bhāti mukhavāso manoharaḥ //
english: Equal parts of tvak and pathya mixed with half the quantity of the camphor would give an attractive fragrance in the mouth similar to that of the nāgavallī betel.

sanskrit: evaṃ kuryāt sadā strīṇāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ /
english: The king should always protect the women thus.

sanskrit: na cāsāṃ viśvasejjātu putramāturviśeṣataḥ //
english: He should not trust them, especially, the mother of children.

sanskrit: na svapet strīgṛhe rātrau viśvāsaḥ kṛtrimo bhavet //43//
english: He should never sleep in the night in the apartment of a woman.

sanskrit: rājaputrasya rakṣā ca kartavyā pṛthivīkṣitā /
english: A king should protect the princess.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmaśāstrāṇi dhanurvedañca śikṣayet //
english: He should instruct them in the sciences of virtue, polity, erotics, archery and fine arts through reliable persons.

sanskrit: śarīrarakṣāvyājena rakṣiṇo 'sya niyojayet //
english: In the guise of protecting the body of the prince, guardians should be engaged to guard from those feigning to speak pleasant.

sanskrit: na cāsya saṅgo dātavyaḥ kruddhalubdhavimānitaiḥ /
english: He should not be given an opportunity to associate with angry, greedy and dishonoured persons.

sanskrit: aśakyantu guṇādhānaṃ kartuṃ taṃ bandhayet mukhaiḥ //
english: If not able to inculcate virtue in the prince, the king should bind him with pleasures.

sanskrit: adhikāreṣu sarveṣu vinītaṃ viniyojayet /
english: An obedient prince should be engaged in all posts of authority.

sanskrit: mṛgayāṃ pānamakṣāṃś ca rājyanāśaṃstyajennṛpaḥ //
english: The king should avoid hunting, drinking and dice playing that destroys the kingdom.

sanskrit: nindāñca daṇḍapāruṣyamarthadūṣaṇamutsṛjet // ākārāṇāṃ samuchedo durgādīnāmasatkriyā /
english: He should also avoid sleeping during the daytime, strolling about idly and scurrilous laṅguage. He should also leave off censuring, cruel infliction of punishment and extravagance.

sanskrit: arthānāṃ dūṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ viprakīrṇatvameva ca //
english: The destruction of mines, neglecting the care of the fort etc. and scattering wealth are said to be extravagance.

sanskrit: adeśakāle yaddānamapātre dānameva ca / artheṣu dūṣaṇaṃ proktamasatkarmapravartanaṃ //
english: A gift that is made to an unworthy person at an inappropriate place and time and engaging in unworthy acts are said to be extravagance.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ madaṃ mānaṃ lobhaṃ darpañca varjayet /
english: One should avoid passion, anger, haughtiness, pride, greed and arrogance.

sanskrit: tato bhṛtyajayaṅkṛtvā paurajānapadaṃ jayet //
english: Then one should win the love of citizens after having controlled the servants. Then he should subjugate his external enemies.

sanskrit: jayedvāhyānarīn paścādvāhyāś ca trividhārayaḥ / guravaste yathā pūrvaṃ kulyānantarakṛtrimāḥ //
english: The external enemies are of three kindsthose belonging to the same clan, those having enmity from the period of the ancestors and those who have enmity on account of some particular reason.

sanskrit: pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mitraṃ sāmantañca tathā ripoḥ / kṛtrimañca mahābhāga mitrantrividhamucyate //
english: Among these three each preceding one is greater than the succeeding one. O Fortunate one! Friends are of three kindsfriend of the father and grandfather, feudatory under the enemy and artificial.

sanskrit: svāmyamātyañjanapadā durgaṃ daṇdastathaiva ca / koṣo mitrañca dharmajña saptāṅgaṃ rājyamucyate //
english: O Knower of virtue! An empire is said to possess seven constituentsking, minister, subjects, fort, punishment, treasury and allies.

sanskrit: mūlaṃ svāmī sa vai rakṣyastasmādrājyaṃ viśeṣataḥ /
english: The central figure is the king. He should be protected and the kingdom is especially dependent on him.

sanskrit: rājyāṅgadrohiṇaṃ hanyātkāle tīkṣṇo mṛdurbhavet //
english: One who rebels against any of the above constituents of the kingdom should be killed. The king should be firm and liberal at the appropriate time.

sanskrit: evaṃ lokadvayaṃ rājño bhṛtyair hāsaṃ vivarjayet /
english: Thus there are two worlds to be conquered by the king. The king should not cut jokes with the servants.

sanskrit: bhṛtyāḥ paribhavantīha nṛpaṃ harṣaṇasatkathaṃ //
english: The servants soon get an upper hand of the king whom they can persuade to laugh.

sanskrit: lokasaṅgrahaṇārthāya kṛtakavyasano bhavet /
english: In order to control people he should feign grief in their misery.

sanskrit: smitapūrvābhibhāṣī syāt lokānāṃ rañjanaṃ caret //
english: He should speak preceded by a gentle smile. He should make them feel delighted.

sanskrit: dīrghasūtrasya nṛpateḥ karmahānirdhruvaṃ bhavet /
english: It would certainly be detrimental to the work if the king is procrastinating.

sanskrit: rāge darpe ca māne ca drohe pāpe ca karmaṇi // apriye caiva vaktavye dīrghasūtraḥ praśasyate /
english: Procrastination is commended in the following actspassion, arrogance, pride, quarrel, sinful acts and unpleasant things to be told.

sanskrit: suptamantro bhavedrājā nāpado guptamantrataḥ //
english: The king should hold secret counsel. There is no danger from secret counselling.

sanskrit: jñāyate hi kṛtaṃ karma nārabdhaṃ tasya rājyakaṃ /
english: The acts relating to the state done by a king holding such a counsel is known from the deeds done and begun to be done.

sanskrit: ākārair iṅgitair gatyā ceṣṭayā bhāṣitena ca //
english: One’s mind is known from the postures, gestures, gaits, action, speech and the changes in the eye and face.

sanskrit: naikastu mantrayen mantraṃ na rājā bahubhiḥ saha //
english: The king, should not keep his own counsel, nor consult a large number of his ministers.

sanskrit: bahubhirmantrayet kāmaṃ rājā mantrān pṛthak pṛthak /
english: The king may have the counsel with many ministers. But it should be had separately.

sanskrit: mantriṇāmapi no kuryān mantrī mantraprakāśanaṃ //
english: He should see that none of his ministers would disclose his secret counsels.

sanskrit: kvāpi kasyāpi viśvāso bhavatīha sadā nṛṇāṃ /
english: Men will always have trust in some one somewhere.

sanskrit: niś cayaś ca tathā mantre kārya ekena sūriṇā //
english: In counsel decision must be made by one wise man.

sanskrit: naśyedavinayādrājā rājyañca vinayāllabhet /
english: A king would perish on account of immodesty and would acquire a kingdom on account of modesty.

sanskrit: traividyebhyastrayīṃ vidyāṃ daṇḍanītiñca śāśvatīṃ // ānvīkṣikīñcārthavidyāṃ vārtārambhāṃś ca lokataḥ /
english: A king should learn the three sciences, the science of administration, metaphysics, science of wealth and business from the world.

sanskrit: jitendriyo hi śaknoti vaśe sthāpayituṃ prajāḥ //
english: Only a person that has conquered his senses would be able to keep his subjects under his control.

sanskrit: pūjyā devā dvijāḥ sarve dadyāddānāni teṣu ca /
english: The gods and all brahmins should always be worshipped and gifts should be given to them brahmins.

sanskrit: dvije dānañcākṣayo 'yaṃ nidhiḥ kaiścinna nāśyate //
english: Gift made to a brahmin would be imperishable and the treasury cannot be destroyed by any of these.

sanskrit: dānāni brāhmaṇānāñca rājño niḥśreyasamparaṃ //
english: Not retreating in the battle, protecting the subjects and giving gifts to the brahmins are the supreme good for a king.

sanskrit: kṛpaṇānāthavṛddhānāṃ vidhavānāñca yoṣitāṃ / yogakṣemañca vṛttiñca tathaiva parikalpayet //
english: The king should likewise arrange for the welfare and livelihood of the poor, destitute and old people, widows and women whose husbands have gone abroad.

sanskrit: varṇāśramavyavasthānaṃ kāryantāpasapūjanaṃ /
english: The king should arrange for the proper pursuit of the orders of the varṇa castes and āśrama stages of life.

sanskrit: na viśvasecca sarvatra tāpaseṣu ca viśvaset //
english: He should worship the ascetics. He should not trust everyone and trust only the ascetics.

sanskrit: viśvāsayeccāpi parantattvabhūtena hetunā / vakaviccintayedarthaṃ siṃhavacca parākramet //
english: He should make others trust him adducing reason to show that his words are not impeachable.

sanskrit: vṛkavaccāvalumpeta śaśavacca viniṣpatet / dṛḍhapraharī ca bhavet tathā śūkaravannṛpaḥ // citrakāraś ca śikhivad dṛḍhabhaktis tathāśvavat / bhavecca madhurābhāṣī tathā kokilavannṛpaḥ //
english: The king should think about the wealth like a crane, conquer like a lion, pounce on the enemies like a wolf, dart forth like a hare and strike firmly like a boar. The king should also be showing vanity like a peacock, faithful as a horse and be speaking pleasantly like a cuckoo.

sanskrit: kākaśaṅkī bhavennityamajñātāṃ vasatiṃ vaset /
english: A king should always be suspicious as a crow while living in the residence of a stranger.

sanskrit: nāparīkṣitapūrvañca bhojanaṃ śayanaṃ spṛśet //
english: A king should not partake of the food and touch a bed not tested before.

sanskrit: nāvijñātāṃ striyaṃ gacchennājñātāṃ nāvamārudvet /
english: He should not visit a woman whom he had not known before and not board an unfamiliar boat.

sanskrit: rāṣṭrakarṣī bhrasyate ca rājyārthāccaiva jīvitāt //
english: One who oppresses his subjects would be deprived of the position and comforts of a sovereign.

sanskrit: bhṛto vatso jātabalaḥ karmayogyo yathā bhavet / tathā rāṣṭraṃ mahābhāga bhṛtaṃ karmasahaṃ bhavet //
english: Just as a nourished bull gains strength and becomes fit for work, so also O Fortunate one! the nourished sovereignty becomes fit for work.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ karmedamāyattaṃ vidhāne daivapauruṣe / tayordaivamacintyaṃ hi pauruṣe vidyate kriyā //
english: All these works are dependent on the providence and on one’s efforts. Out of these two the providence is unthinkable and one’s accomplishments depend on his effort.

sanskrit: janānurāgaprabhavā rājño rājyamahīśriyaḥ //34//
english: The kingdom and the wealth of the earth of a king belong to him by the goodwill of the people.

sanskrit: svayameva karma daivākhyaṃ viddhi dehāntarārjitaṃ /
english: One’s own act that has been acquired from a previous existence of a person is known as the providence.

sanskrit: tasmāt pauruṣameveha śreṣṭhamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ // pratikūlaṃ tathā daivaṃ pauruṣeṇa vihanyate /
english: Hence people declare that willforce is superior. So also an adverse providence can be nullified by one’s efforts.

sanskrit: sāttvikāt karmaṇaḥ pūrvāt siddhiḥ syātpauruṣaṃ vinā // pauruṣaṃ daivasampattyā kāle phalati bhārgava /
english: One will accomplish by his previous deeds of virtue without providence. O Bhārgava son of Bhṛgu! Effort yields fruit at the proper time by the g race of providence.

sanskrit: daivaṃ puruṣakāraś ca dvayaṃ puṃsaḥ phalāvahaṃ //
english: The providence and effort are the two that yield fruit for a man.

sanskrit: kṛṣervṛṣṭisamāyogāt kāle syuḥ phalasiddhayaḥ /
english: The fruits would be accomplished at the proper time by the combination of rain and ploughing.

sanskrit: sadharmaṃ pauruṣaṃ kuryānnālaso na ca daivavān //
english: Along with virtuous deeds one should exert effort. One should neither be lazy nor be dependent on fate.

sanskrit: sāmādibhirupāyaistu sarve siddhyantyupakramāḥ /
english: All the stratagems are accomplished by means of conciliation and other things.

sanskrit: sāma copapradānañca bhedadaṇḍau tathāparau // māyopekṣendrajālañca upāyāḥ sapta tāñchṛṇu /
english: The seven means are conciliation, making gifts, creating dissent, punishment, stratagem, indifference and deceit.

sanskrit: dvividhaṃ kathitaṃ sāma tathyañcātathyameva ca //
english: Conciliation is said to be of two kindstrue and untrue.

sanskrit: tatrāpyatathyaṃ sādhūnāmākrośāyaiva jāyate /
english: Of these two the untrue reconciliation would be for the censure of the good people.

sanskrit: mahākulīnā hy ṛjavo dharmanityā jitendriyāḥ // sāmasādhyā atathyaiś ca gṛhyante rākṣasā api /
english: Those who belong to good families, upright, always virtuous and have conquered their senses are conquerable by conciliatory words. Even demons are taken by false conciliations.

sanskrit: tathā taduprakārāṇāṃ kṛtānāñcaiva varṇanaṃ //
english: The description of the good services rendered by them is conciliation.

sanskrit: parasparantu ye dviṣṭāḥ kruddhabhītāvamānitāḥ /
english: A dissension may be created between two who are inimical to each other, angry, afraid of each other and have been insulted by each other.

sanskrit: teṣānbhedaṃ prayuñjīta paramaṃ darśayedbhayaṃ //
english: He should instill fear in them. A king should give hopes to his own people relatives.

sanskrit: ātmīyān darśayedāśāṃ yena doṣeṇa bibhyati / parāstenaiva te bhedyā rakṣyo vai jñātibhedakaḥ //
english: He should cause dissent in adversaries by holding out threats about which they are afraid. One who causes such dissents among such kinsmen should be protected by the king.

sanskrit: sāmantakoṣo vāhyastu mantrāmātyātmajādikaḥ /
english: The anger of the soldiers is external and those of the ministers, counsellors and princes etc. are internal.

sanskrit: antaḥkoṣañcopaśāmya kurvan śatroś ca taṃ jayet //
english: The king should pacify the internal anger and conquer that of the enemies.

sanskrit: upāyaśreṣṭhaṃ dānaṃ syāddānādubhayalokabhāk / na so 'sti nāma dānena vaśago yo na jāyate //
english: Paying money is the excellent expedient. By giving money one would get both the worlds There is no one for instance who is not influenced by the payment of money.

sanskrit: dānavāneva śaknoti saṃhatān bhedituṃ parān /
english: Only a king who makes a gift of money would be able to cause dissent in the enemies who have become allies.

sanskrit: trayāsādhyaṃ sādhayettaṃ daṇḍena ca kṛtena ca //
english: A king should accomplish by means of punishment and service that which could not be accomplished by the other three.

sanskrit: daṇḍe sarvaṃ sthitaṃ daṇḍo nāśayedduṣpraṇīkṛtaḥ /
english: Everything rests on punishment which would destroy everything if improperly used.

sanskrit: adaṇḍyān daṇḍayannaśyeddaṇḍyānrājāpyadaṇḍayan //
english: A king would be destroyed by punishing those unpunishable and not punishing those punishable.

sanskrit: daivadaityoraganarāḥ siddhā bhūtāḥ patatriṇaḥ / utkrameyuḥ svamaryādāṃ yadi daṇḍān na pālayet //
english: In the absence of punishment, the gods, demons, serpents, men, accomplished persons, goblins and birds would transgress their limits.

sanskrit: yasmādadāntān damayatyadaṇḍyāndaṇḍayatyapi / damanāddaṇḍanāccaiva tasmāddaṇḍa vidurbudhāḥ //
english: The wisemen call ‘the punishment’ so because it controls the uncontrolled, punishes the unpunishable, controls and punishes.

sanskrit: tejasā dur nirīkṣyo hi rājā bhāskaravattataḥ /
english: The king like the sun cannot be looked at on account of his splendour.

sanskrit: lokaprasādaṃ gaccheta darśanāccandravattataḥ //
english: He should be like the moon to look at in order to please the people.

sanskrit: jagadvyāpnoti vai cārair ato rājā samīraṇaḥ /
english: The king is the windgod since he spreads himself in the world by means of his spies.

sanskrit: yadā dahati durbuddhiṃ tadā bhavati pāvakaḥ /
english: He becomes fire when he burns the wicked.

sanskrit: yadā dānaṃ dvijātibhyo dadyāt tasmāddhaneśvaraḥ // dhanadhārāpravarṣitvāddevādau varuṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
english: When he makes the gift to the brahmins he is the lord of wealth Kubera. Because he showers wealth he is known to be god Varuṇa among the celestials.

sanskrit: kṣamayā dhārayaṃllekān pārthivaḥ pārthivo bhavet //
english: The king would be the earth by supporting the universe with his forbearance.

sanskrit: utsāhamantraśaktyādyai rakṣedyasmāddharistataḥ //21//
english: incantation, strength etc.

sanskrit: daṇḍapraṇayanaṃ vakṣye yena rājñaḥ parā gatiḥ /
english: shall describe the criminal laws by enforcing which an elevated position is attained by a king.

sanskrit: triyavaṃ kṛṣṇalaṃ viddhi pāpastatpañcakaṃ bhavet //
english: You know that the weight of three barley grains is equal to one berry seed. The weight of a black gram would be that of five berries.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇalānāṃ tathā ṣaṣṭyā karṣārdhaṃ rāma kīrtitaṃ /
english: O Rāma! It is said that sixty berries make up a half of one karṣa weight.

sanskrit: suvarṇaś ca vinirdiṣṭo rāma ṣoḍaśamāpakaḥ //
english: O Rāma! A suvarṇa weight is said to be equal to sixteen blackgrams.

sanskrit: niṣkaḥ suvarṇāś catvāro dharaṇaṃ daśabhistu taiḥ /
english: Four suvarṇas make up one niṣka and ten niṣkas one dharaṇa.

sanskrit: tāmrarūpyasuvarṇānāṃ manametat prakīrtitaṃ //
english: These are the measures of weight used in weighing copper, silver and gold.

sanskrit: tāmrakaiḥ kārṣiko rāma proktaḥ kārṣāpaṇo budhaiḥ /
english: O Rāma! Kārṣika is said to be kāṛṣāpaṇa by coppersmiths wellversed with the same.

sanskrit: paṇānāṃ dve śate sārdhaṃ prathamaḥ sāhasaḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: Two hundred and fifty paṇas are remembered to be the sāhasa first.

sanskrit: madhyamaḥ pañca vijñeyaḥ sahasramapi cottamaḥ /
english: The middle one is known to be equal to five hundred paṇas and the foremost one as one thousand paṇas.

sanskrit: caurair amūṣito yastu mūṣito 'smīti bhāṣate // tatpradātari bhāpāle sa daṇḍyastāvadeva tu /
english: If a person tells ‘ have been robbed’, when he has not been robbed by the thieves and is handed over to the king, such a person should be punished by making to pay the same amount.

sanskrit: yo yāvadviparītārthaṃ mithyā vā yo vadettu taṃ // tau nṛpeṇa hy adharmajñau dāpyau taddviguṇaṃ damaṃ /
english: One who tells differently or falsely about the exact amount robbed, both these should be levied double the punishment by the king.

sanskrit: kūṭasākṣyantu kurvāṇāṃstrīn varṇāṃś ca pradāpayet //
english: The men belonging to the three castes other than brahmins who bear false witness should be levied punishment.

sanskrit: vivāsayedbrāhmaṇantu bhojyo vidhir na hīrataḥ /
english: A brahmin bearing false witness should be expelled. The above punishment has not been prescribed in that case.

sanskrit: nikṣepasya samaṃ mūlyaṃ daṇḍyo nikṣepabhuk tathā //
english: One who enjoys a property entrusted with him should be levied a fine of equal value. O Righteous one! The same fine should be levied in the case of clothes etc.

sanskrit: vastrādikasya dharmajña tathā dharmo na hīyate /
english: being used similarly. One would not swerve from righteousness by such an act.

sanskrit: yo nikṣepaṃ ghātayati yaścānikṣipya yācate // tāvubhau cauravacchāsyau daṇḍyau vā dviguṇaṃ dama /
english: One who conceals the entrusted property and one who asks for restoration of things without having entrusted the same to some one should be punished like robbers or levied double the fine.

sanskrit: ajñānādyaḥ pumān kuryāt paradravyasya vikrayaṃ // nirdoṣo jñānapūrvakantu cauravaddaṇḍamarhati /
english: One who sells away another’s property unknowingly is free of fault. But one who sells another’s property knowing that it belongs to another deserves punishment as for a robber.

sanskrit: mūlyamādāya yaḥ śilpaṃ na dadyād daṇḍya eva saḥ //
english: One who receives the price for a work and does not give goods, is indeed punishable.

sanskrit: pratiśrutyāpradātāraṃ suvarṇaṃ daṇḍayennṛpaḥ /
english: The king should levy a fine of one suvarṇa for one who promises to give something and does not give.

sanskrit: bhṛtiṃ gṛhya na kuryādyaḥ karmāṣṭau kṛṣṇalā damaḥ //
english: One who accepts payment and does not do the work should be levied a fine of eight kṛṣṇalas.

sanskrit: akāle tu tyajan bhṛtyaṃ daṇḍyaḥ syāttāvadeva tu /
english: But a master dismissing a servant before the end of the term should be punished with the same fine.

sanskrit: krītvā vikrīya vā kiñcidyasyehānuśayo bhavet // so 'ntardaśāhāttatsvāmī dadyāccaivādadīta ca /
english: One who has a remorse after buying or selling something may return to its master or take from him within ten days as the case may be.

sanskrit: pareṇa tu daśāhasya nādadyānnaiva dāpayet //
english: Neither one can receive nor return after ten days in such a deal.

sanskrit: ādadaddhi dadaccaiva rājñā daṇḍyaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ /
english: Any person receiving or returning such a property after that should be levied a fine of six hundred paṇas by the king.

sanskrit: dattāpyadattā sā tasya rājñā daṇḍyaḥ śatadvayaṃ / pradāya kanyāṃ yo 'nyasmai punastāṃ samprayacchati // daṇḍaḥ kāryo narendreṇa tasyāpyuttamasāhasaḥ /
english: One who solicits a girl for a bridegroom, should be levied a fine of two hundred paṇas by the king whether the marriage has been done or not. One who gives in marriage a girl who had already been married to another should be punished by a king.

sanskrit: satyaṅkāreṇa vācā ca yuktaṃ puṇyamasaṃśayaṃ // lubdho 'nyatra ca vikretā ṣaṭśataṃ daṇḍamarhati /
english: The fine of uttama sāhasa one thousand paṇas should be levied in that case. One who enters into a solemn agreement with a person for sale and sells it to another person out of greed deserves to be punished with six hundred paṇas.

sanskrit: dadyāddhenuṃ na yaḥ pālo gṛhītvā bhaktavetanaṃ // sa tu daṇḍyaḥ śataṃ rājñā suvarṇaṃ vāpyarakṣitā /
english: The keeper of a cowshed not restoring the cow to the owner after receiving the charges for the upkeep should be punished by the king with one hundred paṇas and a suvarṇa if not taken proper care of the entrusted animal.

sanskrit: dhanuḥśataṃ parīṇāho grāmasya tu samantataḥ // dviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ vāpi nagarasya ca kalpayet /
english: Land to the extent of one hundred dhanus one dhanu is equal to four cubits should be set apart around the village and twice or thrice as much around a city for the grazing of the cows.

sanskrit: vṛtiṃ tatra prakurvīta yāmuṣṭro nāvalokayet //
english: It should be made in such a way that a camel would not be able to look over the encircling wall.

sanskrit: tatrāparivṛte dhānye hiṃsite naiva daṇḍanaṃ /
english: When the stored grains have not been enclosed and were lost there would be no punishment.

sanskrit: gṛhantaḍāgamārāmaṃ kṣetraṃ vā bhīṣayā haran // śatāni pañca daṇḍyāḥ syādajñānād dviśato damaḥ /
english: One who frightens the owner of a house, tank, garden or land and takes the same should be punished with five hundred paṇas. If it is done inadvertently the fine would be two hundred paṇas.

sanskrit: maryādābhedakāḥ sarve daṇḍyāḥ prathamasāhasaṃ //
english: All those who break the boundaries should be punished with the first sāhasa.

sanskrit: śataṃ brāhmaṇamākruśya kṣatriyo daṇḍamarhati / vaiśyaś ca dviśataṃ rāma śūdraś ca badhamarhati //
english: O Rāma! A kṣatriya censuring a brahmin deserves to be punished with a fine of one hundred paṇas, a vaiśya, two hundred paṇas and a śūdra, a capital punishment.

sanskrit: pañcāśadbrāhmaṇo daṇḍyaḥ kṣatriyasyābhiśaṃsane / vaiśye vāpyardhapañcāśacchūdre dvādaśako damaḥ // kṣatriyasyāpnuyādvaiśyaḥ sāhasaṃ pūrvameva tu /
english: A brahmin having censured a kṣatriya should be punished with a fine of fifty paṇas, having censured a vaiśya, twentyfive paṇas and having censured a śūdra, twelve paṇas. A vaiśya having eensured a kṣatriya should get punishment to pay the first class of sāhasa.

sanskrit: śūdraḥ kṣatriyamākruśya jihvācchedanamāpnuyāt //
english: A śūdra having censured a kṣatriya should be getting the punishment of severing the tongue.

sanskrit: dharmopadeśaṃ viprāṇāṃ śūdraḥ kurvaṃś ca daṇḍabhāk / śrutadeśādivitathī dāpyo dviguṇasāhasaṃ //
english: A śūdra giving moral instruction to brahmins is liable for punishment. One who preaches falsely the doctrines of scriptures should be levied a fine of twice the sāhasa.

sanskrit: uttamaḥ sāhasastasya yaḥ pāpair uttamān kṣipet /
english: One who insults men of respect should be meted the punishment of uttama sāhasa.

sanskrit: pramādādyair mayā proktaṃ prītyā daṇḍārdhamarhati //
english: But the above described punishments should be half if the crimes have been done inadvertently or for fun.

sanskrit: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaraṃ śvaśuraṃ guruṃ / ākṣārayañcchataṃ daṇḍyaḥ panthānaṃ cādadadguroḥ //
english: One who accuses his mother or father or elder brother or fatherinlaw or the preceptor should be levied a fine of one hundred paṇas. The same punishment should be levied for obstructing the pathway of the preceptor.

sanskrit: antyajātirdvijātintu yenāṅgenāparādhnuyāt / tadeva cchedayettasya kṣipramevāvicārayan //
english: One of a lower caste should without enquiry be severed of the organ by which he had done harm to a member of the three higher castes.

sanskrit: avaniṣṭhīvato darpād dvāvoṣṭhau chedayennṛpaḥ / apamūtrayato meḍhramapaśabdayato gudaṃ //
english: The king should cause the lips to be cut off if a person spits on the ground with pride. Similarly, one passing urine or faeces on the body of a brahmin should be punished by cutting the penis and the anus respectively.

sanskrit: utkṛṣṭāsanasaṃsthasya nīcasyādhonikṛntanaṃ /
english: If a member of a low caste had occupied the seat of a member of a higher caste, his lower organ buttocks should be cut.

sanskrit: yo yadaṅgaṃ ca rujayettadaṅgantasya kartayet //
english: One who causes injury to any organ of another should be punished by cutting the same organ of the offender.

sanskrit: ardhapādakarāḥ kāryā gogajāśvoṣṭraghātakāḥ /
english: The killers of a cow, elephant, horse or camel should have their legs and hands cut off.

sanskrit: vṛkṣantu viphalaṃ kṛttvā suvarṇaṃ daṇḍamarhati //
english: One who would make a tree barren deserves the fine of a suvarṇa.

sanskrit: dviguṇaṃ dāpayecchinne pathi sīmni jalāśaye /
english: When the pathway or a boundary or the tank has been cut by a person he should be levied double the above fine.

sanskrit: dravyāṇi yo haredyasya jñānato 'jñānato 'pivā // sa tasyotpādya tuṣṭintu rājñe dadyāttato damaṃ /
english: One who either wilfully or unintentionally takes away the articles of another should restore it to him to satisfy him and pay the fine to the king.

sanskrit: yastu rajjuṃ ghaṭaṃ kūpāddharecchindyācca tāṃ prapāṃ // sa daṇḍaṃ prāpnuyān māsaṃ daṇḍyaḥ syāt prāṇitā.rane /
english: One who steals the rope or the pot from the well and damages the channel should be punished for a month with imprisonment. One should be punished similarly if he beats an animal.

sanskrit: dhānyaṃ daśabhyaḥ kumbhebhyo harato 'bhyadhikaṃ badhaḥ //
english: The punishment for stealing ten pitchers full of paddy is more than death.

sanskrit: śeṣe 'pyekādaśaguṇaṃ tasya daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet /
english: The punishment for stealing more than that quantity would be eleven times the former.

sanskrit: suvarṇarajatādīnāṃ nṛstrīṇāṃ haraṇe badhaḥ //
english: Capital punishment should be ordered for stealing gold, silver etc. and for kidnapping men and women.

sanskrit: yena yena yathāṅgena steno nṛṣu viceṣṭate / tattadeva haredasy pratyādeśāya pārthivaḥ //
english: The organ with which one would steal from others should be removed by the king for the sake of discipline.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaḥ śākadhānyādi alpaṃ gṛhṇanna doṣabhāk /
english: A brahmin taking little quantity of vegetables and grains etc. for his use without the knowledge of the owner would not be a criminal.

sanskrit: godevārthaṃ haraṃścāpi hanyādduṣṭaṃ badhīdyataṃ //
english: Similarly in the case of taking for the cows or gods one would not be a criminal.

sanskrit: gṛhakṣetrāpahartāraṃ tathā patnyabhigāminaṃ / agnidaṃ garadaṃ hanyāttathā cābhyudyatāyudhaṃ //
english: One who seizes the house or field belonging to another, one who copulates with another’s wife, one who is an incendiary and one who administers poison should be killed. So also in the case of one who attacks with a drawn weapon.

sanskrit: rājā gavābhicārādyaṃ hanyāccaivātatāyinaḥ /
english: A king should kill those who cause the death of cattle by magic spells.

sanskrit: parastriyaṃ na bhāṣeta pratiṣiddho viśenna hi // adaṇḍyā strī bhavedrājñā varayanto patiṃ svayaṃ /
english: One should not converse with another’s wife and should never copulate with a forbidden woman. A girl choosing her husband herself should not be punished by the king.

sanskrit: uttamāṃ sevamānaḥ strī jaghanyo badhamarhati // bhartāraṃ laṅghayedyā tāṃ śvabhiḥ saṅghātayet striyaṃ / savarṇadūṣitāṃ kuryāt piṇḍamātropajīvinīṃ //
english: A man of the lower caste holding incest with a woman of the higher caste deserves to be killed. The woman who breaks her faith in the husband, should be made to be bitten by dogs. A woman defiled by a man of her own caste should be made to live on a morsel of food a day.

sanskrit: jyāyasā dūṣitā nārī muṇḍanaṃ samavāpnuyāt /
english: A woman defiled by one of the superior caste should have her head shaved.

sanskrit: vaiśyāgame tu viprasya kṣatriyasyāntyajāgame // kṣatriyaḥ prathamaṃ vaiśyo daṇḍyaḥ śūdrāgame bhavet /
english: A brahmin copulating with a vaiśya woman and a kṣatriya going to a woman of the low caste should be fined with the first variety of fine. A kṣatriya and a vaiśya are punishable for going to a śūdra woman.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā vetanaṃ veśyā lobhādanyatra gacchati // vetanandviguṇaṃ dadyāddaṇdañca dviguṇaṃ tathā /
english: If a courtesan after having received a contract, goes to another on account of greed, she should pay the first one, twice the contracted amount and pay twice the amount as fine.

sanskrit: bhāryā putrāś ca dāsāś ca śiṣyo bhrātā ca sodaraḥ // kṛṭāparādhāstāḍyāḥ sūrajvā veṇudalena vā /
english: One’s wife, sons, servants, pupil and brother having done an offence should be beaten with a rope or with a piece of bamboo A thief should be struck on the back but not on the forehead.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhe na mastake hanyāccaurasyāpnoti kilviṣaṃ //
english: One would acquire sin by doing so by striking on the forehead.

sanskrit: rakṣāsvadhikṛtaiyastu prajātyarthaṃ vilupyate / teṣāṃ sarvasvamādāya rājā kuryāt pravāsanaṃ //
english: The officers in charge of protecting the people seizing very much should be banished from the kingdom after having seized all their property.

sanskrit: ye niyuktāḥ svakāryeṣu hanyuḥ kāryāṇi karmiṇāṃ / nirghṛṇāḥ krūramanasastānniḥsvān kārayennṛpaḥ //
english: Those who have been employed to do certain work if do not do the work of their employers, the king should make those shameless, cruelminded to be penniless.

sanskrit: amātyaḥ prāḍvivāko vā yaḥ kuryāt kāryamanyathā / tasya sarvasvamādāya taṃ rājā vipravāsayet //
english: Likewise the king should banish the minister or justice after having taken the entire property for doing the work of another king.

sanskrit: gurutalpe bhayaḥ kāryaḥ surāpāṇe surādhvajaḥ / steyeṣu śvapadaṃ vidyād brahmahatyāśiraḥ pumān //
english: If one violates the bed of the preceptor, mark of female generative organ should be made on the forehead, a pot of wine in case of drinking of wine, a dog in case of stealing and the head of a person in the case of killing a brahmin.

sanskrit: śūdrādīn ghātayedrājā pāpān viprān pravāsayet /
english: The king should kill criminals belonging to śūdra and other communities and banish the brahmin sinners.

sanskrit: mahāpātakināṃ vittaṃ varuṇāyopapādayet //
english: The wealth belonging to great sinners should be offered to god Varuṇa God of righteousness.

sanskrit: bhāṇḍārakoṣadāś caiva sarvāṃstānapi ghātayet // rāṣṭreṣu rāṣṭrādhikṛtān sāmantān pāpino haret /
english: A king should kill all those who offer shelter, food and wealth to thieves in the villages also. The feudatory chiefs and the governors of provinces in the kingdom who are sinful should be killed.

sanskrit: sandhiṃ kṛtvā tu ye cauryaṃ rātrau kurvanti taskarāḥ // teṣāṃ cchitvā nṛpo hastau tīkṣṇe śūle niveśayet /
english: The king should place on the pike after having cut the arms of those thieves who commit theft in the night after having agreed to show good conduct.

sanskrit: taḍāgadevatāgārabhedakān ghātayennṛpaḥ //
english: The king should kill those who break tanks and temples.

sanskrit: samutsṛjedrājamārge yastvamedhyamanāpadi / sa hi kārṣāpaṇandaṇḍyastamamedhyañca śodhayet //
english: One should be levied a fine of a kārṣāpaṇa for having committed nuisance on the thoroughfare when there was no adversity and be made to clean the impurity.

sanskrit: pratimāsaṅkramabhido dadyuḥ pañcaśatāni te / samaiś ca viṣamaṃ yo vā carate mūlyato 'pi vā // samāpnuyānnaraḥ pūrvaṃ damaṃ madhyamameva vā /
english: One who breaks his contract every month should pay a fine of five hundred paṇas to the party concerned Merchants, dealing fraudulently with honest men in respect of the price of a commodity, should be punished with the first or the middle kind of fine.

sanskrit: dravyamādāya vaṇijāmanargheṇāvarundhatāṃ // rājā pṛthak pṛthak kuryāddaṇḍamuttamasāhasaṃ /
english: The king should confiscate all goods from the obstructing merchants by paying small sum and punish them with the uttama variety of sāhasa separately.

sanskrit: dravyāṇāṃ dūṣako yaś ca praticchandakavikrayī // madhyamaṃ prāpnuyāddaṇḍaṃ kūṭakartā tathottamaṃ /
english: One who adulterates the materials and who sells imitationarticles should be given the middle kind of punishment. One who makes contraband goods should be made to pay uttama sāhasa.

sanskrit: kalahāpakṛtaṃ deyaṃ daṇḍaś ca dviguṇastataḥ //
english: One who insults in a quarrel should be given the punishment of twice that amount.

sanskrit: abhakṣyabhakṣye vipre vā śūdre vā kṛṣṇalo damaḥ /
english: A fine of kṛṣṇala should be collected from a brahmin or a śūdra who eats the forbidden food.

sanskrit: ebhiś ca vyavahartā yaḥ sa dāpyo damamuttamaṃ /
english: One who makes false balance and weight and those who make use of these should be levied the uttama kind of fine.

sanskrit: viṣāgnidāṃ patiguruviprāpatyapramāpiṇīṃ // vikarṇakaranāsauṣṭhī kṛtvā gobhiḥ pravāsayet /
english: The women who administers poison to her husband or preceptor, or a brahmin and children or sets fire to the house should be banished from the country with cows after having cut her ears, hands and nose.

sanskrit: kṣetraveśmagrāmavanavidārakās tathā narāḥ // rājapatnyabhigāmī ca dagdhavyāstu kaṭāgninā /
english: Those men who damage a land or house or village or forest and one who seduces the wife of the king should be burnt with the fire from the cremation ground.

sanskrit: ūnaṃ vāpyadhikaṃ vāpi likhedyo rājaśāsanaṃ // pārajāyikacaurau ca muñcato daṇḍa uttamaḥ /
english: One who copies the royal edict omitting or adding some sentences and one who sets free an adulterer and a thief should be punished with the uttama sāhasa fine.

sanskrit: rājayānāsanāroḍhurdaṇḍa uttamasāhasaḥ //
english: The punishment for one who ascends the vehicle or the seat of the king is the uttama sāhasa.

sanskrit: yo manyetājito 'smīti nyāyenāpi parājitaḥ / tamāyāntaṃ parājitya daṇḍayed dviguṇaṃ damaṃ //
english: If one thinks that he has not been defeated even though he has duly been defeated, the king should defeat him again and inflict doublefold punishment.

sanskrit: āhvānakārī badhyaḥ syādanāhūtamathāhvayan / dāṇḍikasya ca yo hastādabhimuktaḥ palāyate // hīnaḥ puruṣakāreṇa tad dadyāddāṇḍiko dhanaṃ //67//
english: One who summons a person that had not done any crime should be put to death. If an accused person escapes from the custody of the punisher on account of the latter’s carelessness, that punisher should pay the fine.

sanskrit: yadā manyeta nṛpatirākrandena balīyasā / pārṣṇigrāho 'bhibhūto me tadā yātrāṃ prayojayet //
english: . See the first verse, p. . When a king is attacked by a strong enemy and he thinks “ have been attacked”, he should undertake the military expedition .

sanskrit: puṣtā yodhā bhṛṭā bhṛtyāḥ prabhūtañca balaṃ mama / mūlarakṣāsamartho 'smi tair gatvā śivire vrajet //
english: If the king thinks that the warriors had been wellcared for and the servants well supported and he feels, “ have a strong army and am capable of protecting the central army”, he should go with them and move into the camp.

sanskrit: śatrorvā vyasane yāyāt daivādyaiḥ pīḍitaṃ paraṃ / bhūkampo yāndiśaṃ yāti yāñca keturvyadūṣayat // vidviṣṭanāśakaṃ sainyaṃ sambhūtāntaḥprakopanaṃ /
english: Otherwise one may invade the country of the enemy when it the latter’s country is afflicted by natural calamities such as the appearance of the earthquake in that direction or the comet afflicting it or the army of the enemy king dislikes that king and awaits his ruin.

sanskrit: śarīrasphuraṇe dhanye tathā susvapradarśane // nimitte śakune dhanye jāte śatrupuraṃ vrajet / padātināgabahulāṃ senāṃ prāvṛṣi yojayet //
english: One should enter the kingdom of the enemy when he has auspicious throbbing of the muscles of the body, has good dreams and good omens. One should employ an army consisting largely of infantry etc. and elephants in the rainy season.

sanskrit: hemante śiśire caiva rathavājisamākulāṃ / caturaṅgabalopetāṃ vasante vā śaranmmukhe //
english: In the early and advanced winter it should consist of chariots and cavalry, while it should consist of four divisions of an army cavalry, infantry etc. in the spring and autumn.

sanskrit: senā padātibahulā śatrūn jayati sarvadā /
english: An army consisting of a large number of infantry would always win the enemies.

sanskrit: aṅgasakṣiṇabhāge tu śastaṃ prasphuraṇaṃ bhavet //
english: The throbbing of the muscles on the right side of the body would be commendable.

sanskrit: na śastantu tathā vāme pṛṣṭhasya hṛdayasya ca / lāñchanaṃ piṭakañcaiva vijñeyaṃ sphuraṇaṃ tathā //
english: So also the palpitation on the left back and the heart and mark of mole on the left side should be known as not commendable.

sanskrit: viparyayeṇābhihitaṃ savye strīṇāṃ śubhaṃ bhavet /
english: While the contrary to what has been told on the left side would be auspicious for women.

sanskrit: svapnaṃ śaubhāśubhaṃ vakṣye duḥkhapraharaṇantathā /
english: shall describe the good and bad omens and the way to prevent bad dreams .

sanskrit: tantrīvādyavinodaś ca dolārohaṇameva ca // arjanaṃ padmalohānāṃ sarpāṇāmatha māraṇaṃ / raktapuṣpadrumāṇāñca caṇḍālasya tathaiva ca // varāhāśvakharoṣṭrāṇāṃ tathā cārohaṇakriyā / bhakṣaṇaṃ pakṣimāṃsānāṃ tailasya kṛśarasya ca //
english: The growth of grass and trees on one’s body except the navel, the breaking of bronze on the head, the shaving of the head, remaining nude, clad in torn dress, anointing with oil, besmearing with mud, falling from a great height, one’s marriage, music, playing on the lute or any other stringed instrument, swinging in a hammock, gathering lotus and metals, killing of serpents, seeing red flowers and trees and a cāṇḍāla, riding a pig or dog or ass or camel, eating the flesh of birds, and the oil of kṛsara ? entering the mother’s womb, getting into the funeral pyre, the fall of the flagpost etc., the fall of the moon and the sun, seeing the divine beings of the terrestrial and celestial regions as well as a calamity such as the earthquake, the wrath of the divine beings, brahmins, other beings and preceptors, dancing, laughing, marriage and singing, playing on stringed instruments other than the lute, drowning in a river, bathing in water mixed with cowdung, or muddy water or water mixed with ink, embracing the unmarried girls, sexual union of men, injury to one’s limbs, purging or vomiting, starting in the direction of the south, being afflicted by diseases, plucking of fruits, breaking of diseases, breaking of minerals, falling of buildings, sweeping the house, playing with goblins, flesheaters, monkeys and lowcaste men, insult from others and feeling grief on account of that, wearing ochre robes and playing in that dress, immersion in oil and drinks anointing with red unguent are inauspicious omens and it is better not to describe them.

sanskrit: bhūjaś ca svapanaṃ tadvat kāryāṃ snānaṃ dvijārcanaṃ / tilair homo haribrahmaśivārkagaṇapūjanaṃ //
english: After dreaming as above one should continue to sleep, bathe, worship a brahmin, do oblations with sesamum, worship gods Hari Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Śiva, Sun and Gaṇapati Vināyaka.

sanskrit: tathā stutiprapaṭhanaṃ puṃsūktādijapas tathā /
english: Then one should recite hymns on gods and repeat hymns such as the Puruṣasūkta.

sanskrit: svapnāstu prathame yāme saṃvatsaravipākinaḥ // ṣaḍbhirmāsair dvitīye tu tribhirmāsair triyāmikāḥ / caturthe tvardhamāsena daśāhādaruṇodaye //
english: The dreams dreamt in the first quarter of the night yield results within a year, the second quarter, within six months, the third quarter of the night, within three months, the fourth quarter, within a fortnight and within ten days if dreamt at the time of the sunrise.

sanskrit: ekasyāmatha cedrātrau śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubhaṃ / paścādṛṣṭastu yastatra tasya pākaṃ vinirdiśet //
english: If two dreams either auspicious or inauspicious were dreamt on the same night, one should indicate the result of the dream dreamt later.

sanskrit: tasmāttu śobhane svapne paścātsvāpo na śasyate /
english: Hence, it is not commended to sleep after a good dream has been dreamt.

sanskrit: śailaprāsādanāgāśvavṛṣabhārohaṇaṃ hitaṃ //
english: Dreaming as climbing a hill, mansion, elephant, horse or bull is beneficial.

sanskrit: drumāṇāṃ śvetapuṣpāṇāṃ gagane ca tathā dvija / drumatṛṇodbhavo nābhau tathā ca bahubāhutā // tathā ca bahuśīrṣatvaṃ palitodbhava eva ca / suśukramālyadhāritvaṃ suśuklāmbaradhāritā // candrārkatārāgrahaṇaṃ parimārjanameva ca /
english: O Brahmin! Seeing trees and white flowers in the sky seeing the navel as grown with trees, seeing oneself as having many arms and many heads, seeing the appearance of grey hair, bearing a garland of white flowers, wearing white garment, the eclipses of the moon, sun and the stars, washing oneself, embracing the flagpost and the raising of the banner are good.

sanskrit: darśanaṃ rudhirasyāpi snānaṃ vā rudhireṇa ca // sarārudhiramadyānāṃ pānaṃ kṣīrasya vāpyatha / astrair viceṣṭanaṃ bhūmau nirmalaṃ gaganaṃ tathā // mukhena dohanaṃ śastaṃ mahiṣīṇāṃ tathā gavāṃ / siṃhīnāṃ hastinīnāñca baḍavānāṃ tathaiva ca //
english: O Brahmin! Seizing of land and stream of water, victory over the enemies, success in dispute, diceplay and battle, eating of raw meat and drinking of sweet porridge, seeing blood, bathing in blood, drinking of spirituous liquor, blood and wine, drinking of milk, making marks with the weapons on the earth, seeing the clear sky, and sucking milk from cows, shebuffalos, lionesses, sheelephants and mares are commendable.

sanskrit: prasādo devaviprebhyo gurubhyaś ca tathā dvija / ambhasā cābhiṣekastu gavāṃ śṛṅgacyutena ca //
english: O Brahmin! The favour from the gods, brahmins and preceptors, the anointment with water and falling down from the horns of cow are also commendable.

sanskrit: candrād bhraṣṭena vā rāma jñeyaṃ rājyapradaṃ hi tat /
english: O Rāma! The dream as falling down from the horns of a moon is known to be capable of bestowing kingdom.

sanskrit: maraṇaṃ vahnilābhaś ca vahnidāho gṛhādiṣu / labdheś ca rājaliṅgānāṃ tantrīvādyābhivādanaṃ //
english: The installation as the sovereign, the cutting of one’s head, the death, the destruction of one’s house by fire, the gain of royal rewards and the play on stringed instruments are auspicious.

sanskrit: yastu paśyati svapnānte rājānaṃ kuñjaraṃ hayaṃ /
english: The family of a person flourishes that sees an elephant or horse or gold or bull or cow.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaṃ vṛṣabhaṅgāñca kuṭumbastasya vardhate // vṛṣebhagṛhaśailāgravṛkṣārohaṇarodanaṃ / ghṛṭaviṣṭhānulepo vā agamyāgamanaṃ tathā //
english: Dreams of riding a bull or an elephant, the climbing a peak or a tree, weeping, besmeared with ghee or excreta, copulating with a forbidden women, seeing a white cloth, clear waters, tree laden with fruits and clear sky are good augury. ṚV.

sanskrit: sitavastraṃ prasannāmbhaḥ phalī vṛkṣo nabho 'malaṃ //32//

aṅgāraṃ guḍasarjau ca muṇḍābhyaktañca nagnakaṃ / ayaḥ paṅkaṃ carmakeśau unmattañca napuṃsakaṃ // caṇḍālaśvapacādyāni narā bandhanapālakāḥ / garbhiṇī strī ca vidhavāḥ piṇyakādīni vai mṛtaṃ // tuṣabhasmakapālāsthibhinnabhāṇḍamaśastakaṃ /
english: Mixtures of herbs and black cereals are inauspicious, Cotton, grass, dried cowdung, wealth, charcoal, molasses and resin, one having a shaven head or one that has besmeared oil for bathing and one that is nude, iron, mud, hide and hair, a lunatic, an eunuch, a cāṇḍāla, a dog, an outcaste and others, men guarding the captives, a pregnant woman, widow and oilcake, etc., dead body, husk, ash, skull and bone and broken vessel are not commendable to be seen.

sanskrit: aśasto vādyaśabdaś ca bhinnabhairavajharjharaḥ // ehīti purataḥ śabdaḥ śasyate na tu pṛṣṭhataḥ / gaccheti paścācchabdo 'gryaḥ purastāttu vigarhitaḥ //
english: The sounds of musical instruments that are broken, frightening and harsh are also not commendable. The sound ‘come on’, heard in front of the person undertaking a journey is commendable, while that from behind is not commendable.

sanskrit: kva yāsi tiṣṭha mā gaccha kinte tatra gatasya ca / aniṣṭaśabdā mṛtyarthaṃ kravyādaś ca dhvajādigaḥ //
english: The undesirable sounds such as “Where do you go”, ‘stand’, ‘Do not go’, ‘What is there for you by going’ are for death.

sanskrit: skhalanaṃ vāhanānāñca śastrabhaṅgastathaiva ca / śiroghātaś ca dvārādyaiścchatravāsādipātanaṃ //
english: So also the appearance of carnivorous animals, banners etc., the fall of vehicles etc., the breaking of weapons, dashing of the head against the door etc., and the fall of umbrella, dress etc., are not commendable.

sanskrit: harimabhyarcya saṃstutya syādamaṅgalyanāśanaṃ /
english: An inauspicious augury gets destroyed by the worship and invocation of lord Hari Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: dvitīyantu tato dṛṣṭvā viruddhaṃ praviśedgṛhaṃ //
english: If a second inauspicious augury is seen while setting out then one should reenter the house.

sanskrit: śvetāḥ sumanasaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ pūrṇakumbho mahottamaḥ /
english: White flowers are excellent augury. So also a pitcher full of water is greatly meritorious.

sanskrit: dūrvārdragomayaṃ veśyā svarṇarūpyañca ratnakaṃ // vacāsiddhārthakauṣadhyo mudga āyudhakhaḍgakaṃ / chatraṃ pīṭhaṃ rājaliṅgaṃ śavaṃ ruditavarjitaṃ // phalaṃ ghṛṭaṃ dadhi payo akṣatādarśamākṣikaṃ / śaṅkhaṃ ikṣuḥ śubhaṃ vākyaṃ bhaktavāditagītakaṃ //
english: Meat, fish, a distant sound, an old man, an animal, goat, cows,horses, elephants, images of gods, glowing flame, dūrvā grass, wet cowdung, courtesan, gold, silver, gem, vacā, white mustard, herbs, beans, weapons, sword, umbrella, throne, insignia of royalty, a dead body without being followed by mourners, fruit, ghee, curd, milk, unbroken rice, mirror, honey, conch, sugarcane, auspicious sentence, the instrumental music of the devotee, the loud sound of thunder and lightning are all auspicious.

sanskrit: gambhīrameghastanitaṃ taḍittuṣṭiś ca mānasī /
english: The satisfaction in the mind of the person undertaking a journey is also auspicious.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhato gamane praśne puruṣasya śubhāśubhaṃ / nivedayanti śakunā deśasya nagarasya ca //
english: Birds let us know the good and bad indications for a man staying or leaving a country or town or putting a question.

sanskrit: sarvaḥ pāpaphalo dīpto nirdiṣṭo daivacintikaiḥ / śāntaḥ śubhaphalaś caiva daivajñaiḥ samudāhṛtaḥ //
english: All excited sounds are pointed out to indicate evil according to fortunetellers and cooing sounds are said to indicate good results by fortunetellers.

sanskrit: ṣaṭprakārā vinirdiṣṭā śakunānāñca dīptayaḥ / velādigdeśakaraṇarutajātivibhedataḥ //
english: The excitements of birds are said to be of six kinds based on the divisions of time, direction, place, karaṇa a division of the day, the sound and the species of the bird.

sanskrit: pūrvā pūrvā ca vijñeyā sā teṣāṃ balavattarā /
english: Each preceding item in the above list should be known as more powerful.

sanskrit: divācaro rātricaras tathā rātrau divācaraḥ //
english: The nocturnal bird moving in the daytime and that of the daytime moving in the night are known to be the excitement in time.

sanskrit: krūreṣu dīptā vijñeyā ṛkṣalagnagrahādiṣu /
english: One should know the malefic asterisms, ascendants and planets also as excited.

sanskrit: dhūmitā sā tu vijñeyā yāṅgamiṣyati bhāskaraḥ // yasyāṃ sthitaḥ sā jvalitā muktā cāṅgāriṇī matā /
english: It is known to be dhūmitā obscured, jvalitā burning and aṅgāritā burnt if the sun goes to or stays or leaves a particular quarter.

sanskrit: etāstisraḥ smṛtā dīptāḥ pañca śāntās tathāparāḥ //
english: These three are remembered to be the excited ones and the gentle cooings are of five kinds.

sanskrit: dīptāyāndiśi digdīptaṃ śakunaṃ parikīrtitaṃ / grāmo 'raṇyā vane grāmyās tathā ninditapādapaḥ //
english: It is said to be agitated bird if it makes an excited sound in the direction that is termed agitated. Similar appellations should be given to wild birds making sound in the village and the village birds in the forest as well as on an inauspicious tree.

sanskrit: deśe caivāśubhe jñeyo deśadīpto dvijottamaḥ /
english: O Foremost brahmin! The deśadīpta agitation in respect of a place is known to be in inauspicious place.

sanskrit: kriyādīpto vinirdiṣṭaḥ svajātyanucitakriyaḥ //
english: It is designated as kriyādīpta excitement in respect of an action if there is any action improper for one’s own species.

sanskrit: rutadīptaś ca kathito bhinnabhairavanisvanaḥ /
english: It is said to be the rutadīpta excitement in respect of sound making broken and harsh sounds.

sanskrit: jātidīptas tathā jñeyaḥ kevalaṃ māṃsabhojanaḥ //
english: It is known to be the jātidīpta excitement in respect of the species in the case of the carnivorous species alone.

sanskrit: dīptācchānto vinirdiṣṭaḥ sarvair bhedaiḥ prayatnataḥ /
english: If the excited characteristics of different categories occur together it is stated to be good.

sanskrit: miśrair miśro vinirdiṣṭastasya vācyaṃ phalāphalaṃ //
english: If they are mixed the result is said to be mixed.

sanskrit: gośvoṣṭragardabhaśvānaḥ sārikā gṛhagodhikā / caṭakā bhāsakūrmādyāḥ kathitā grāmavāsinaḥ // ajāviśukanāgendrāḥ kolo mahiṣavāyasau /
english: The cows, horses, camels, asses, dogs, birds sārikā, small houselizards, sparrows, vultures and tortoises and others are said to be living in the villages. Goats, black sheep, parrots, elephants, pig, buffalo and crow are said to be both domestic and wild.

sanskrit: grāmyāraṇyā vinirdiṣṭāḥ sarve 'nye vanagocarāḥ //
english: All other birds and animals are wild.

sanskrit: mārjārakukkuṭau grāmyau tau caiva vanagocarau /
english: The cat and the cock are both domestic and wild.

sanskrit: tayorbhavati vijñānaṃ nityaṃ vai rūpabhedataḥ //
english: We know about them from the change in their characteristics.

sanskrit: gokarṇaśikhicakrāhvakharahārītavāyasāḥ / kulāhakukkubhaśyenapherukhañjanavānarāḥ // śataghnacaṭakaśyāmacāsaśyenakaliñjalāḥ / tittiraḥ śatapatrañca kapotaś ca tathā trayaḥ // khañjarīṭakadātyūhaśukarājīvakukkuṭāḥ /
english: The snakes, peacocks, ruddy geese, mules, pigeons, cows, lightbrown horses, wild cocks, hawks, jackals, wagtails, monkeys, śataghna ?, sparrows, cuckoos, blue jays, hawks, kapiñjala the three, tittiri francoline partridge, peacocks, pigeons, wagtails, gallinules, parrots, cranes, cocks, skylarks and deer are known to be moving about during daytime.

sanskrit: vāguryulūkaśarabhakrauñcāḥ śaśakakacchapāḥ / lomāsikāḥ piṅgalikāḥ kathitā rātrigocarāḥ //
english: The fowlers, owls, śarabhas, curlews, hares, turtles, jackals and piṅgalikas a kind of owl are said to be nocturnal.

sanskrit: haṃṣāś ca mṛgamārjāranakularkṣabhujaṅgamāḥ / vṛkārisiṃhavyāghroṣṭragrāmaśūkaramānuṣāḥ // śvāvidvṛṣabhagomāyuvṛkakokilasārasāḥ /
english: Ganders, deer, cats, mongooses, bears, serpents, red dogs, lions, tigers, camels, domestic boars, men, dogs, porcupines, bulls, jackals, wolves, cuckoos, cranes, horses, men in ragged clothes and alligators wander day and night.

sanskrit: jayāvahā vinirdiṣṭāḥ paścānnidhanakāriṇaḥ //
english: The above seen in a group in front of the king making an expedition with the forces are stated to bring victory and seen on the back cause defeat.

sanskrit: gṛhādgamya yadā cāso vyāharet purutaḥ sthitaḥ / nṛpāvamānaṃ vadati vāmaḥ kalahabhojane //
english: If the blue jay comes out of the house and makes the sound remaining in front, it indicates humiliation for the king and making sound on the left indicates quarrel and gaining food.

sanskrit: yāne taddarśanaṃ śastaṃ savyamaṅgasya vāpyatha /
english: It being sighted on the vehicle or on the right side of the body are commended.

sanskrit: caurair moṣamathākhyāti mayūro bhinnanisvanaḥ //
english: The peacock making an unusual sound conveys plundering by thieves.

sanskrit: prayātasyāgrato rāma mṛgaḥ prāṇaharo bhavet /
english: O Rāma! a deer seen in front of one that has set out would be indicating danger to life.

sanskrit: ṛkṣākhujambukavyāghrasiṃhamārjāragardabhāḥ // pratilomās tathā rāma kharaś ca vikṛtrasvanaḥ /
english: O Rāma! The bears, rats, jackals, tigers, lions, cats and asses running away in the opposite direction as well as mule braying strangely would indicate the same result.

sanskrit: vāmaḥ kapiñjalaḥ śreṣṭhas tathā dakṣiṇasaṃsthitaḥ //
english: The kapiñjala bird seen on the left or right is an excellent augury.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato ninditaphalastittiristu na śasyate /
english: But it does not augur well if seen on the back. The tittiri bird in any one of the above positions is not commended.

sanskrit: eṇā varāhāḥ pṛṣatā vāmā bhūtvā tu dakṣiṇāḥ // bhavantyarthakarā nityaṃ viparītā vigarhitāḥ /
english: The black deer, boars and spotted antelopes crossing from the left to the right would always be beneficial and the contrary movements are condemned.

sanskrit: vṛṣāśvajambukavyāghrāḥ siṃhamārjāragardabhāḥ // vāñchitārthakarā jñeyā dakṣiṇādvāmato gatāḥ /
english: The bulls, horses, jackals, tigers, lions, cats and asses are known to confer the desired results if they move to the left from the right.

sanskrit: śivā śyāmānanācchūcchūḥ piṅgalā gṛhagodhikā // śūkarī parapuṣṭā ca punnāmānaś ca vāmataḥ /
english: The vixen, śyāmānana ?, chucchū a kind of animal, piṅgalā a kind of owl, house alligator, sow and a female cuckoo are said to be male omens if they are on one’s left.

sanskrit: strīsañjñā bhāsakārūṣakapiśrīkarṇaśchitkarāḥ //
english: The vulture, rūṣa ? monkey, śrīkarṇa antelope, and citkarā ? are known as feminine omens.

sanskrit: kapiśrīkarṇapipyīkā ruruśyenāś ca dakṣiṇāḥ /
english: The monkey, śrīkarṇa, pipīlikā, ruru a kind of deer, and hawks auger well seen on the right.

sanskrit: jātīkṣāhiśaśakroḍagodhānāṃ kīrtanaṃ śubhaṃ //
english: The sounds made by the bull that is born, the serpent, hare, hog and alligator are good.

sanskrit: tataḥ sandarśanaṃ neṣṭaṃ pratīpaṃ vānararkṣayoḥ /
english: Then it is not desirable to see the monkey and bear at the commencement of a work.

sanskrit: kāryakṛdbalī śakunaḥ prasthitasya hi yo 'nvahaṃ // bhavettasya phalaṃ vācyaṃ tadeva divasaṃ budhaiḥ /
english: The strong omen from a bird as one sets out on a day should be explained by wise men as bearing result on the same day.

sanskrit: matā bhakṣyārthino bālā vairasaktāstathaiva ca // sīmāntamabhyantaritā vijñeyā niṣphalā dvija /
english: O Brahmin! Mad ones, those concerned only with the prey, young ones, those mutually quarrelling and those separated by a distance should be known to bear no effect.

sanskrit: ekadvitricaturbhistu śivā dhanyā rutair bhavet //
english: The vixen howling alone or in groups of two or three or four forebode good.

sanskrit: pañcabhiś ca tathā ṣaḍbhiradhanyā parikīrtitā /
english: It is said to be not beneficial if five or six vixen howl.

sanskrit: saptabhiś ca tathā dhanyā niṣphalā parato bhavet //
english: It would be good if seven vixen howl and there would be no effect if more than that.

sanskrit: nṛṇāṃ romāñcajananī vāhanānāṃ bhayapradā / jvālānalā sūryamukhī vijñeyā bhayavardhanī //
english: The volcano facing the sun that causes the horripilation in men should be known to bring ill luck to vehicles and increase the fear.

sanskrit: prathamaṃ sāraṅge dṛṣṭe śubhe deśe śubhaṃ vadet /
english: When an antelope is seen at a good place it would give good results.

sanskrit: saṃvatsaraṃ manuṣyasya aśubhe ca śubhaṃ tathā //
english: It would give bad results for the whole year for the man if seen at a bad place.

sanskrit: tathāvidhannaraḥ paśyetsāraṅgaṃ prathame 'hani / ātmanaś ca tathātvena jñātavyaṃ vatsaraṃ phalaṃ //
english: One may know the result for himself for the whole year as he had seen the deer on the first day. The cātaka bird that is said to drink water directly from the rains.

sanskrit: viśanti yena mārgeṇa vāyasā bahavaḥ puraṃ / tena mārgeṇa ruddhasya purasya grahaṇaṃ bhavet //
english: A fabulous animal powerful than the lion. An army would take possession of a city that is under siege by that way through which many crows enter that city.

sanskrit: senāyāṃ yadi vāsārthe niviṣṭo vāyaso ruvan / vāmo bhayāturastrasto bhayaṃ vadati dustaraṃ //
english: It indicates unfordable fear if a crow taking its abode in the place of the army goes about cawing with agitation and fear.

sanskrit: chāyāṅgavāhanopānacchatravastrādikuṭṭane / mṛtyustatpūjane pūjā tadiṣṭakaraṇe śubhaṃ //
english: If the crow pecks at the shadow, body, vehicle, shoes, umbrella and clothes and other things of a person, it indicates death for that person. If it honours the person, he will be honoured.

sanskrit: proṣitāgamakṛtkākaḥ kurvan dvāri gatāgataṃ / raktaṃ dagdhaṃ gṛhe dravyaṃ kṣipanvahnivedakaḥ //
english: A crow going to and fro at the entrance to a house, indicates the return of the absentee owner of the house. It indicates destruction by fire if the crow throws a red or burnt thing inside the house.

sanskrit: nyasedraktaṃ purastācca nivedayati bandhanaṃ /
english: A red thing placed by the crow in front of a person indicates imprisonment.

sanskrit: pītaṃ dravyaṃ tathā rukma rūpyameva tu bhārgava // yaccaivopanayed dravyaṃ tasya labdhiṃ vinirdiśet /
english: O Bhārgava son of Bhṛgu, if a crow brings to the house a yellow substance, gold or silver, it would indicate the gain of that substance.

sanskrit: dravyaṃ vāpanayedyattu tasya hāniṃ vinirdiśet //
english: So also one should indicate the loss of that thing which a crow should take away.

sanskrit: purato dhanalabdhiḥ syādāmamāṃsasya chardane / bhūlabdhiḥ syān mṛdaḥ kṣepe rājyaṃ ratnārpaṇe mahat //
english: If a crow vomits raw flesh in front of a house there would be gain of wealth. There would be gain of land if a piece of earth is thrown. There would be gain of kingdom if a great gem is cast.

sanskrit: yātuḥ kāko 'nukūlastu kṣemaḥ karmakṣamo bhavet / na tvarthasādhako jñeyaḥ pratikūlo bhayāvahaḥ //
english: If the crow flies favourably to the person who undertakes a journey it bids welfare and he would be able to accomplish his task. But if it flies against him it should be known that the task would not be accomplished and would cause fear.

sanskrit: sammukhe 'bhyeti viruvan yātrāghātakaro bhavet /
english: If the crow comes cawing loudly against the person it would be an impediment to the journey.

sanskrit: vāmaḥ kākaḥ smṛto dhanyo dakṣiṇo 'rthavināśakṛt // vāmo 'nulomagaḥ śreṣṭho madhyamo dakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
english: A crow on the left is considered to be beneficial and causing destruction of the task if on the right. If the crow flies on the left in the direction of the person undertaking a journey, it is excellent and medium if on the right.

sanskrit: pratilomagatirvāmo gamanapratiṣedhakṛt //
english: If it flies against the direction of the traveller on the left, it would cause impediment to the movement.

sanskrit: nivedayati yātrārthamabhipretaṃ gṛhe gataḥ /
english: If the crow comes to the house when the traveller is beginning to move it should be known that he can set out.

sanskrit: ekākṣaracaraṇastvarkaṃ vīkṣamāṇo bhayāvahaḥ //
english: If a crow stands on one leg and looks at the sun with a single eye it causes fear.

sanskrit: koṭare vāsamānaś ca mahānarthakaro bhavet /
english: If a crow makes its habitat in a hollow of a tree there would be great misfortune.

sanskrit: na śubhastūṣare kākaḥ paṅkāṅkaḥ sa tu śasyate //
english: A crow seen in the saline soil is not for good. But the same seen as having its wings with mud is commendable.

sanskrit: amedhyapūrṇavadanaḥ kākaḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ /
english: A crow seen as having its mouth full of excreta accomplishes all things.

sanskrit: jñeyāḥ patatriṇo 'nye 'pi kākavad bhṛgunandana //
english: O Son of Bhṛgu! The other birds should also be known as indicating the same results as the crow.

sanskrit: skandhāvārāpasavyasthāḥ śvāno vipravināśakāḥ /
english: Dogs howling on the right of a royal camp indicate the destruction of the brahmins.

sanskrit: indrasthāne narendrasya pureśasya tu gopure // antargṛhe gṛheśasya maraṇāya bhavedbhaṣan /
english: If they howl at the place of Indra in the palace, at the main entrance to the royal city and inside the house, it would augur the death of the lord of the house.

sanskrit: yasya jighrati vāmāṅgaṃ tasya syādarthasiddhaye // bhayāya dakṣiṇaṃ cāṅgaṃ tathā bhujamadakṣiṇaṃ /
english: It indicates the accomplishment of the task, if a dog smells the left side of the body of a man and fear if it smells the right side of the body and the left arm.

sanskrit: yātrāghātakaro yāturbhavet pratimukhāgataḥ //
english: A dog coming against the traveller would be adverse to the journey.

sanskrit: mārgāvarodhako mārge caurān vadati bhārgava /
english: O Bhārgava son of Bhṛgu! a dog obstructing the path of a traveller indicates robbers on the way.

sanskrit: alābho 'sthimukhaḥ pāpo rajjucīramukhas tathā //
english: Similarly a dog being seen holding a rope or rag in the mouth is sinful.

sanskrit: sopānatkamukho dhanyo māṃsapūrṇamukho 'pi ca / amaṅgalyamukhadravyaṃ keśañcaivāśubhaṃ tathā //
english: A dog being seen as holding the shoes as well as full of meat in the mouth is also beneficial. A dog being seen as holding the hair or any filthy substance in the mouth is inauspicious.

sanskrit: avamūtryāgrato yāti yasya tasya bhayaṃ bhavet /
english: A dog urinating and going in front of the traveller would bring fear.

sanskrit: yasyāvamūtrya vrajati śubhaṃ deśantathā drumaṃ // maṅgalañca tathā dravyaṃ tasya syādarthasiddhaye /
english: If one sees a dog urinating and going to an auspicious place or tree or to an auspicious substance it indicates the accomplishment of the task for that person.

sanskrit: śvavacca rāma vijñeyās tathā vai jambukādayaḥ // bhayāya svāmini jñeyamanimittaṃ rutaṅgavāṃ /
english: O Rāma Paraśurāma! Jackals and other animals should also be known to indicate the same result as a dog. The lowing of the cows should be known as auguring fear for the master.

sanskrit: niśi caurabhayāya syādvikṛtaṃ mṛtyave tathā // śivāya svāmino rātrau balīvardo nadan bhavet /
english: If a cow lows in the night it would be indicating fear from thieves. If it wails it forebodes death. If a bull bellows in the night it would be for the welfare of the master.

sanskrit: utsṛṣṭavṛṣabho rājño vijayaṃ samprayacchati //
english: A bull let loose in the night would confer victory on the king.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ bhakṣayantyaś ca gāvo dattās tathā svakāḥ / tyaktasnehāḥ svavatseṣu garbhakṣayakarā matāḥ //
english: The cows belonging to a person that were given as gift indicate security if found eating as they wish. The cows that had withheld showing affection to the calves are known to be indicating miscarriage in the family.

sanskrit: bhūmiṃ pādair vinighnantyo dīnā bhītā bhayāvahāḥ /
english: The cows that pound the earth with their feet and are frightened bring fear.

sanskrit: ārdrāṅgyo hṛṣṭaromāś ca śṛgalagnamṛdaḥ śubhāḥ //
english: The cows that have wet skin, horripilation and earth stuck to the horns are auspicious.

sanskrit: mahiṣyādiṣu cāpyetat sarvaṃ vācyaṃ vijānatā /
english: It should be told in the same way in the case of the shebuffalos and others by those knowing the science.

sanskrit: ārohaṇaṃ tathānyena saparyāṇasya vājinaḥ //
english: A saddled horse being seen as ridden by another other than the appointed person forebodes evil.

sanskrit: jalopaveśanaṃ neṣṭaṃ bhūmau ca parivartanaṃ /
english: A horse being seen as plunging into the water and tumbling over the ground is not desirable.

sanskrit: vipatkaranturaṅgasya suptaṃ vāpyanimittataḥ //
english: A horse that is seen sleeping without a good cause causes misfortune.

sanskrit: yavamodakayordveṣastvakasmācca na śasyate / vadanādrudhirotpattirvepanaṃ na ca śasyate //
english: If a horse has aversion to barley and balls of grains all of a sudden it is not commended. Bleeding from the mouth and trembling of the body are also not commended.

sanskrit: krīḍan vaikaḥ kapotaiś ca sārikābhirmṛtiṃ vadet / sāśrunetro jihvayā ca pādalehī vinaṣṭaye //
english: If a horse plays with cranes, pigeons and the sārikās a species of birds, one should indicate death. A horse licking the leg with the tongue with tearfilled eyes forebodes ruin.

sanskrit: svapedvā vāmapārśvena divā vā na śubhapradaḥ //
english: If a horse scratches the earth with the left foot or sleeps during the day lying on the left side, it does not confer good.

sanskrit: bhayāya syāt sakṛnmūtrī tathā nidrāvilānanaḥ / ārohaṇaṃ na ceddadyāt pratīpaṃ vā gṛhaṃ vrajet //
english: The horse that passes urine once a day, that is looking drowsy, does not allow to be ridden and that returns home frantically if ridden upon, indicates impediment for the journey.

sanskrit: yātrāvighātamācaṣṭe vāmapārśvaṃ tathā spṛśan /
english: It indicates the same result if it touches the left side of its body.

sanskrit: heṣamāṇaḥ śatruyodhaṃ pādasparśī jayāvahaḥ //
english: The horse that neighs on seeing the enemy warrior and touching its leg brings victory.

sanskrit: grāme vrajati nāgaścen maithunaṃ deśahā bhavet /
english: If an elephant courts openly in a village it would ruin the country.

sanskrit: ārohaṇaṃ na ceddadyāt pratīpaṃ vā gṛhaṃ vrajet / madaṃ vā vāraṇo jahyādrājaghātakaro bhavet //
english: If an elephant does not allow itself to be ridden or frantically returns home after being ridden or ichor flows from the elephant, it foretells the death of the king.

sanskrit: vāmaṃ dakṣiṇapādena pādamākramate śubhaḥ /
english: An elephant crossing its left foot with its right foot and entwining its right tusk with its trunk is auspicious.

sanskrit: vṛṣo 'śvaḥ kuñjaro vāpi ripusainyagato 'śubhaḥ / khaṇḍameghātivṛṣṭyā tu senā nāśamavāpnuyāt //
english: A bull or a horse or an elephant entering the enemy forces is inauspicious. If clouds get broken suddenly and rain excessively, the king would get his army routed.

sanskrit: pratikūlagraharkṣāttu tathā sammukhamārutāt / yātrākāle raṇe vāpi chatrādipatanaṃ bhayaṃ //
english: The tumbling down of the umbrella at the time of a travel or during the war on account of adverse asterisms and planetary conditions or the wind blowing against the forces forebodes fear.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭā narāścānulomā grahā vai jayalakṣaṇaṃ /
english: Contended men and favourable planets are the characteristics for foreboding victory.

sanskrit: kākair yodhābhibhavanaṃ kravyādbhirmaṇḍalakṣayaḥ //
english: The warriors being attacked by the crows and demons forebodes the destruction of the army.

sanskrit: prācīpaścimakaiśānī śaumyā preṣṭhā śubhā ca dik //38//
english: The east, west, northeast and north are the excellent and auspicious directions.

sanskrit: sarvayātrāṃ pravakṣyāmi rājadharmasamāśrayāt /
english: shall describe all kinds of journeys relating to a sovereign.

sanskrit: astaṅgate nīcagate vikale ripurāśige // pratilome ca vidhvaste śukre yātrāṃ visarjayet /
english: A journey should be abandoned when the Venus has set or is in a weak house or debilitated or in the house of an enemy or retrograde or malefic.

sanskrit: vaidhṛtau ca vyatīpāte nāge ca śakunau tathā / catuṣpāde ca kintughne tathā yātrāṃ vivarjayet //
english: One should avoid a journey when the Mercury is retrograde, the presiding planet of the quarter or any other planet in a similar position, is under the vaidhṛti, vyatīpāta, nāga, śakuna, catuṣpada and kintughna.

sanskrit: vipattāre naidhane ca pratyarau cātha janmani / gaṇḍe vivarjayedyātrāṃ riktāyāñca tithāvapi //
english: One should avoid undertaking journey under the influence of vipat tāra, naidhana, pratyari, as well as the janma, the gaṇḍa and the void lunar day.

sanskrit: udīcī ca tathā prācī tayoraikyaṃ prakīrtitaṃ / paścimā dakṣiṇā yā dik tayoraikyaṃ tathaiva ca //
english: The north and the east are said to be having the same virtues. In the same way the west and south are of the same virtues.

sanskrit: vāyvagnidiksamudbhūtaṃ parighanna tu laṅghayet /
english: One should not cross the obstacle that has risen from the northwest to the southeast.

sanskrit: ādityacandraśaurāstu divasāś ca na śobhanāḥ //
english: Sundays, Mondays and Saturdays are not auspicious for a journey.

sanskrit: kṛttikādyāni pūrveṇa maghādyāni ca yāmyataḥ / maitrādyānyapare cātha vāsavādyāni vāpyudak // sarvadvārāṇi śastāni chāyāmānaṃ vadāmi te /
english: The asterisms kṛttikā and others for journey in the east, the asterisms maghā and others for journey in the south, the asterisms anurādhā and others for journey in the west and the asterisms jyeṣṭhā and others for journey in the north are all commendable.

sanskrit: āditye viṃśatirjñeyāś candre ṣoḍaśa kīrtitāḥ // bhaume pañcadaśaivoktāś caturdaśa tathā budhe / trayodaśa tathā jīye śukre dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ //
english: shall describe the measure of the shadows cast by the sun on different days. It is said to be twenty for the Sun, sixteen for the Moon, fifteen for the Mars, fourteen for the Mercury, thirteen for the Jupiter, twelve for the Venus and eleven for the Saturn.

sanskrit: ekādaśa tathā saure sarvakarmasu kīrtitāḥ /
english: These are said to be valid for all actions.

sanskrit: janmalagne śakracāpe sammukhe na vrajennaraḥ //
english: One should not set out on a journey under his native ascendant and in the direction of the rainbow.

sanskrit: śakunādau śubhe yāyājjayāya harimāsmaran /
english: One should march on an expedition after meditating on lord Hari for victory if the omens and other things are good.

sanskrit: vakṣye maṇḍalacintānte kartavyaṃ rājarakṣaṇaṃ //
english: shall describe the circle of twelve primary kings to be thought. about that would offer protection to the king.

sanskrit: mitrañjanapadaś caiva rājyaṃ saptāṅgamucyate //
english: A kingdom is said to consist of seven constituentsthe king, minister, fort, treasury, punishment law, allies and township.

sanskrit: saptāṅgasya tu rājyasya vighnakartṝn vināśayet / maṇḍaleṣu ca sarveṣu vṛddhiḥ kāryā mahīkṣitā //
english: One should destroy all those who obstruct the normal course of the seven constituents of a kingdom. Efforts should be made by the king to make all these circles develop.

sanskrit: ātmamaṇḍalamevātra prathamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ bhavet /
english: The kingdom over which a king exercises direct control would be the first circle.

sanskrit: sāmantāstasya vijñeyā ripavo maṇḍalasya tu //
english: The feudatories of that kingdom should be known as the enemies.

sanskrit: upetastu suhṛj jñeyaḥ śatrumitramataḥ paraṃ / mitramitraṃ tato jñeyaṃ mitramitraripustataḥ //
english: If they are attached to the paramount lord they should be known as friends. The next circle is the allies of the enemy. The next circle should be known as the ally of the ally.

sanskrit: etatpurastāt kathitaṃ paścādapi nibodha me /
english: Those in front have been described. Tell me those who are behind.

sanskrit: pārṣṇigrāhastataḥ paścāttatastvākranda ucyate // āsārastu tato 'nyaḥ syādākrandāsāra ucyate /
english: A hostile king would be the next one friend of the rear enemy. That which is adjacent to the former is said to be the next one friend of rear friend.

sanskrit: jigīṣoḥ śatruyuktasya vimuktasya tathā dvija //
english: O Brahmin! This is the way of maintaining order by an independent king that has an enemy and is desirous of conquering the same.

sanskrit: nātrāpi niś cayaḥ śakyo vaktuṃ manujapuṅgava /
english: O Excellent among men! It is not possible to declare that it is settled.

sanskrit: nigrahānugrahe śakto madhyasthaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
english: One is said to be an intermediary that is capable of punishing and favouring.

sanskrit: nigrahānugrahe śaktaḥ sarveṣāmapi yo bhavet / udāsīnaḥ sa kathito balavān pṛthivīpatiḥ //
english: A mighty king that would be able to punish and favour all is said to be neutral.

sanskrit: na kasyacidripurmitraṅkāraṇācchatrumitrake /
english: No one is really one’s enemy or ally. One is an enemy or an ally on account of some reason.

sanskrit: maṇḍalaṃ tava samproktametad dvādaśarājakaṃ //
english: have described these twelve circles relating to a king.

sanskrit: trividhā ripavo jñeyāḥ kulyānantarakṛtrimāḥ /
english: Enemies are known to be of three kindsancestral, personal and artificial.

sanskrit: pūrvapūrvo gurusteṣāṃ duścikitsyatamo mataḥ //
english: Each one of the preceding class among them are known to be stronger than the succeeding ones.

sanskrit: anantaro 'pi yaḥ śatruḥ so 'pi me kṛtrimo mataḥ /
english: One that is a personal enemy is considered by me as artificial.

sanskrit: pārṣṇigrāho bhavecchatrormitrāṇi ripavas tathā // pārṣṇigrāhamupāyaiś ca śamayecca tathā svakaṃ /
english: An enemy in the rear of an enemy and his hostiles would be one’s friends. A king should subdue his hostile king in the rear by means of strategies.

sanskrit: mitreṇa śatrorucchedaṃ praśaṃsanti purātanāḥ // mitrañca śatrutāmeti sāmantatvādanantaraṃ /
english: The ancient authorities commend the extinction of an enemy with the help of an ally. An ally may become an enemy after being a feudal.

sanskrit: śatruṃ jigoṣurucchindyāt svayaṃ śaknoti cedyadi //
english: A king wishing to vanquish an enemy should himself destroy him if it is possible for him to do.

sanskrit: pratāpavṛddhau tenāpi nāmitrājjāyate bhayaṃ /
english: There will not be any fear from an enemy when the glory is waxing.

sanskrit: yathāsya nodvijelloko viśvāsaś ca yathā bhavet // jigīṣurdharmavijayī tathā lokaṃ vaśannayet /
english: A king desiring to conquer righteously should exercise control over the world in such a way that the people do not feel griefstricken and trust him.

sanskrit: sāmabhedau mayā proktau dānadaṇḍau tathaiva ca /
english: This and the next one are among the twentyseven yogas or combinations.

sanskrit: daṇḍaḥ svadeśe kathitaḥ paradeśe vravīmi te //
english: have described the punishment to be made by the king in his own country.

sanskrit: prakāśaścāprakāśaś ca dvividho daṇḍa ucyate /
english: Punishment is said to be of two typespublic and private.

sanskrit: dūṣaṇañcaiva sādhūnāmudakānāñca dūṣaṇaṃ // daṇḍapraṇayaṇaṃ proktamupekṣāṃ śṛṇu bhārgava / yadā manyate nṛpatī raṇe na mama vigrahaḥ // anarthāyānubandhaḥ syāt sandhinā ca tathā bhavet /
english: Public punishment consists of looting and the destruction of villages of the enemy country, destruction of the food grains and setting fire. The private punishment consists of killing by poisoning or setting fire or by engaging several men, dishonouring pious men and poisoning waters.

sanskrit: sāmalabdhāspadañcātra dānañcārthakṣayaṅkaraṃ // bhedadaṇḍānubandhaḥ syāttadopekṣāṃ samāśrayet /
english: One maybe indifferent when he would find the conciliatory measures as securing the position of the enemy, paying a bribe would be squandering money and creating dissension would have punishment as the consequence.

sanskrit: na cāyaṃ mama śaknoti kiñcit kartumupadravaṃ // na cāhamasya śaknomi tatropekṣāṃ samāśrayet /
