english: One may resort to indifference if he is sure that ‘this person is not capable of doing any harm to me’ and ‘ am not capable of causing any harm to him’.

sanskrit: avajñopahatastatra rājñā kāryo ripurbhavet //
english: In that case the king should humiliate the enemy by being indifferent.

sanskrit: māyopāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi utpātair anṛtaiś carat /
english: shall describe the strategies of illusion to be practised by a king.

sanskrit: sthūlasya tasya pucchasthāṃ kṛtvolkāṃ vipulāṃ dvija / visṛjecca tataś caivamulkāpātaṃ pradarśayet //
english: The enemy should be agitated by false portents by sending extensive lighted torches tied to the tails of strong birds in the camp of the enemy. Then the fall of the meteor should be shown to them.

sanskrit: evamanye darśanīyā utpātā bahavo 'pi ca /
english: In this way many other portents also should be shown.

sanskrit: udvejanaṃ tathā kuryāt kuhakair vividhair dviṣāṃ // sāṃvatsarāstāpasāś ca nāśaṃ brūyuḥ prarasya ca /
english: The enemies should thus be agitated by different kinds of deception. The astrologers and ascetics should proclaim the fall of the enemy.

sanskrit: jigīṣuḥ pṛthivīṃ rājā tena codvejayet parān //
english: A king that desires toconquer the earth should agitate others by the above proclamation.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ prasādaś ca kīrtanīyaḥ parasya tu /
english: The favour of gods should also be proclaimed to others.

sanskrit: āgatanno 'mitrabalaṃ praharadhvamabhītavat // evaṃ brūyādraṇe prāpte bhagnāḥ sarve pare iti /
english: A king should declare to his men “We have received increased strength and you strike without fear all others have been routed”, when the battle has begun.

sanskrit: kṣveḍāḥ kilakilāḥ kāryā vācyaḥ śatrurhatas tathā //
english: Warcry and great commotion should be made saying that the enemy has been routed.

sanskrit: devājñāvṛṃhito rājā sannaddhaḥ samaraṃ prati /
english: It should also be proclaimed “The king has been blessed by the gods profusely and is ready for the battle”.

sanskrit: indrajālaṃ pravakṣyāmi indraṃ kālena darśayet //
english: shall describe Indrajāla a kind of stratagem in war.

sanskrit: caturaṅgaṃ balaṃ rājā sahāyārthaṃ divaukasāṃ / balantu darśayet prāptaṃ raktavṛṣṭiñcendrapau //
english: A king should exhibit the four divisions of the army such as the infantry, cavalry, men mounted on elephants and chariots to delude the enemy that the gods had sent them for aid.

sanskrit: chinnāni ripuśīrṣāṇi prāsādāgreṣu darśayet /
english: Severed heads of the enemy should be exhibited on the terrace of palaces.

sanskrit: sandhiś ca vigrahaś caiva yānamāsanameva ca / dvaidhībhāvaḥ saṃśayaś ca ṣaḍguṇāḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
english: shall describe six expedients , among which war and peace are most excellent. Making peace, war, expedition, halt, seeking shelter and duplicity are said to be the six expedients .

sanskrit: paṇabandhaḥ smṛtaḥ sandhirapakārastu vigrahaḥ /
english: Making peace is known to be a treaty. War is offending the enemy.

sanskrit: jigīṣoḥ śatruviṣaye yānaṃ yātrābhidhīyate // vigraheṇa svake deśe sthitirāsanamucyate /
english: Expedition is said to be the march against the enemy by the one that desires to conquer. It is said to be ‘the halt’ when a king remains in his own territory mobilising his forces for the war.

sanskrit: balārdhena prayāṇantu dvaidhībhāvaḥ sa ucyate // udāsīno madhyago vā saṃśrayātsaṃśayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
english: Mobilisation of half the army in the enemy country is said to be ‘seeking shelter. It is said to be duplicity on account of resorting to indifference or neutral position.

sanskrit: samena sandhiranveṣyo 'hīnena ca balīyasā // hīnena vigrahaḥ kāryaḥ svayaṃ rājñā balīyasā /
english: A king should seek a treaty with an equal person or not of lower strength and more powerful. A powerful king should make a war with a king of inferior strength.

sanskrit: tatrāpi śuddhapārṣṇistu balīyāṃsaṃ samāśrayet //
english: In that case he should take a stronger king as an ally when he is not having an enemy in the rear.

sanskrit: āsīnaḥ karmavicchedaṃ śaktaḥ kartuṃ riporyadā /
english: A king should mobilise his army when he could easily intercept the work of the enemy, though he is not free from an enemy in the rear.

sanskrit: aśuddhapārṣṇiścāsīta vigṛhya vasudhādhipaḥ // aśuddhapārṣṇirbalavān dvaidhībhāvaṃ samāśrayet / balinā vigṛhītastu yo 'sandehena pārthivaḥ //
english: One who is strong enough could mobilise half of his army in the territory of the enemy even though he may have an enemy in the rear. An alliance with another king is said to be the worst of all expedients a king fighting with a stronger adversary is compelled to do.

sanskrit: bahukṣayavyayāyāsaṃ teṣāṃ yānaṃ prakīrtitaṃ //
english: It is said to bring many a long and tedious marches, loss of many lives and expenditure.

sanskrit: bahulābhakaraṃ paścāttadā rājā samāśrayet /
english: A king should have an alliance only when he would have great benefits later.

sanskrit: sarvaśaktivihīnastu tadā kuryāttu saṃśrayaṃ //
english: Moreover, he should have an alliance only when he has been deprived of all his strength.

sanskrit: ajasraṃ karma vakṣyāmi dinaṃ prati yadācaret /
english: shall describe the perpetual daily duties of the king.

sanskrit: dvimuhūrtāvaśeṣāyāṃ rātrau nidrāntyajennṛpaḥ // vādyavandisvanair gītaiḥ paśyed gūḍhāṃstato narān / vijñāyate na ye lokāstadīyā iti kenacit //
english: The king should put an end to his sleep with the songs and music of the panegyrists when two muhūrtas fortyeight minutes are still left in the night. He should then see spies in such a way that they are not known as his own men by anybody.

sanskrit: āyavyayasya śravaṇaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ yathāvidhi /
english: He should then hear the report about the income and expenditure as laid down.

sanskrit: vegotsargaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā rājā snānagṛhaṃ vrajet //
english: After having eased, the king should go to the bathroom. The king should then bathe preceded by cleansing the teeth.

sanskrit: snānaṃ kuryānnṛpaḥ paścāddantadhāvanapūrvakaṃ / kṛtvā sandhyāntato japyaṃ vāsudevaṃ prapūjayet //
english: After having done the twilight worship and the repetition of the sacred syllables the king should worship lord Vāsudeva Viṣṇu’s manifestation as Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: vahnau pavitrān juhuyāt tarpayedudakaiḥ pitṝn /
english: He should then offer unto the fire holy twigs. Libations should be offered to the ancestors.

sanskrit: dadyātsakāñcīṃ dhenuṃ dvijāśīrvādasaṃyutaḥ //
english: Accompanied by the blessings of brahmins, he should then give a cow as gift together with gold.

sanskrit: anulipto 'laṅkṛtaś ca mukhaṃ paśyecca darpaṇe /
english: He should also then see his face in clarified butter kept together with gold.

sanskrit: sasuvarṇe dhṛte rājā śṛṇuyāddivasādikaṃ // auṣadhaṃ bhiṣajoktaṃ ca maṅgalālambhanañcaret /
english: The king should then hear about the nature of the day etc. He should then take medicines prescribed by the physicians. He should then touch the auspicious things.

sanskrit: paśced guruṃ tena dattāśīrvado 'tha vrajetsabhāṃ //
english: He should then see the preceptor and go to the court after having been blessed by him.

sanskrit: tatrastho brāhmaṇān paśyedamātyānmantriṇas tathā /
english: O Fortunate one! He should then see brahmins, ministers, counsellors and others presented by the doorkeeper.

sanskrit: śrutvetihāsaṃ kāryāṇi kāryāṇāṃ kāryanirṇayam /
english: After having heard the traditional history and things to be done, he should determine the business to be done.

sanskrit: vyavahārantataḥ paśyenmantraṃ kuryāttu mantribhiḥ //
english: He should then look into civil disputes and have counsel with the counsellors.

sanskrit: naikena sahitaḥ kuryānna kuryādbahubhiḥ saha / na ca mūrkhair nacānāptair guptaṃ na prakaṭaṃ caret //
english: He should not have the counsel with a single person or with many or ignorant men or untrustworthy men. He should also not make public the secret counsel.

sanskrit: mantraṃ svadhiṣṭhitaṃ kuryādyena rāṣṭraṃ na bādhate / ākāragrahaṇe rājño mantrarakṣā parā matā //
english: The counsel he had should be given effect to promptly so that the state may not get affected. The secret counsel is considered to be guarded well by a king by his postures.

sanskrit: ākārair iṅgitaiḥ prajñā mantraṃ gṛhṇanti paṇḍitāḥ /
english: Wise men gather secrets from the postures of others.

sanskrit: sāṃvatsarāṇāṃ vaidyānāṃ mantriṇāṃ vacane rataḥ // rājā vibhūtimāpnoti dhārayanti nṛpaṃ hi te /
english: A king gets prosperity by following the words of astrologers, physicians and counsellors, because they sustain the king.

sanskrit: mantraṃ kṛtvātha vyāyāmañcakre yāne ca śastrake //
english: After having had the counsel he should do physical exercises with discs, chariot and weapon.

sanskrit: niḥsattvādau nṛpaḥ snātaḥ paśyedviṣṇuṃ supūjitaṃ /
english: He should then bathe in tanks not inhabited by living creatures and see lord Viṣṇu that has already been worshipped.

sanskrit: hutañca pāvakaṃ paśyedviprān paśyetsupūjitān //
english: He should then see fire into which oblations have been made and also see brahmins that have been worshipped well.

sanskrit: bhūṣito bhojanaṅkuryād dānādyaiḥ suparīkṣitaṃ / bhuktvā gṛhītatāmbūlo vāmapārśvena saṃsthitaḥ //
english: After having adorned himself he should take food after having fed beings and after having tested the food duly. After having taken food, he should chew betels and rest lying on the left.

sanskrit: śāstrāṇi cintayed dṛṣṭvā yodhān koṣṭhāyudhaṃ gṛhaṃ / anvāsya paścimāṃ sandhyāṃ kāryāṇi ca vicintya tu // carān sampreṣya bhuktānnamantaḥpuracaro bhavet /
english: He should then have inquiry in the sacred texts. After having met the warriors and seen the granary and the armoury he should do the evening twilight worship. He should then think of the tasks to be done, send spies, eat food and spend time in the harem with instrumental music and being guarded by others.

sanskrit: yātrāvidhānapūrvantu vakṣye sāṅgrāmikaṃ vidhiṃ /
english: shall describe rites to be performed before commencing a march.

sanskrit: saptāhena yadā yātrā bhaviṣyati mahīpateḥ // pūjanīyo hariḥ śambhurmodakādyair vināyakaḥ /
english: When a march of a king has to begin after seven days, lords Hari Viṣṇu and Śambhu Śiva should be worshipped as well as lord Vināyaka the elephantfaced god, lord of impediments with sweet balls and other things on the first day.

sanskrit: dvitīye 'hani dikpālān sampūjya śayanañcaret //
english: After having worshipped the guardian deities of different directions, the priest should lie down on a bed.

sanskrit: śayyāyāṃ vā tadagre 'tha devān prārcya manuṃ smaret /
english: He should then worship gods either remaining on the bed or in front of them. He should then think of Manu.

sanskrit: namaḥ śambhoḥ trinetrāya rudrāya varadāya ca //
english: “Obeisance O Śambhu conferer of good! to the threeeyed, dreadful and conferer of boons.

sanskrit: vāmanāya virūpāya svapnādhipataye namaḥ /
english: Obeisance to the dwarf manifestation of lord Viṣṇu, the formless lord of dreams.

sanskrit: bhagavandevadeveśa śūlabhṛdvṛṣavāhana // iṣṭāniṣṭe mamācakṣva svapne suptasya śāśvata /
english: O Master! Lord of the lords! Bearer of the trident! One riding the bull! O Eternal one! Let me know in my dream while sleep, the good or evil to befall me.

sanskrit: yajjāgrato dūramiti purodhā mantramuccaret //
english: The impressions in the waking state maybe driven far away.” The priest should thus utter these sacred syllables on the second day.

sanskrit: tṛtīye 'hani dikpālān rudrāṃstān dikpatīnyajet / grahān yajeccaturthe 'hni pañcame cāśvinau yajet //
english: He should worship the guardian deities of the quarters, Rudras and the lords of directions on the third day, the planets on the fourth day and the two Aśvins divine physicians on the fifth day.

sanskrit: mārge yā devatāstāsānnadyādīnāñca pūjanaṃ / divyāntarīkṣabhaumasthadevānāñca tathā baliḥ //
english: Then the gods on the way of expedition and the sacred rivers presided over by those gods should be worshipped. Offerings should be made to gods dwelling in heavens, atmosphere and earth.

sanskrit: rātrau bhūtagaṇānāñca vāsudevādipūjanaṃ /
english: The group of goblins and gods Vāsudeva and others should be worshipped in the night.

sanskrit: bhadrakālyāḥ śriyaḥ kuryāt prārthayet sarvadevatāḥ //
english: Worship should be made to goddesses Bhadrakālī and Śrī. One should pray to all gods.

sanskrit: vāsudevaḥ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ pradyumnaścāniruddhakaḥ / nārāyaṇo 'bjajo viṣṇur nārasiṃho varāhakaḥ // śiva īśastatpuruṣo hy aghoro rāma satyajaḥ / sūryaḥ somaḥ kujaścāndrijīvaśukraśanaiś carāḥ // rāhuḥ keturgaṇapatiḥ senānī caṇḍikā hy umā /
english: “May gods Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha, Nārāyaṇa Viṣṇu, Abjaja born in the lotus, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Nārasiṃha manlion form of lord Viṣṇu, the boar manifestation of lord Viṣṇu, O Rāma! Śiva, Īśa Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Satyaja, the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rāhu, the ascending node of Moon, Ketu descending node of Moon, Gaṇapati lord of goblins, Senānī son of Śiva and Pārvatī leader of the celestials against the demon Tāraka, goddesses Caṇḍikā, Umā consort of Śiva, Lakṣmī consort of Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī goddess of speech, Durgā a form of Pārvatī, Brahmāṇī consort of Brahmā, the Rudras forms of Śiva, eleven in number, the celestials Indra and others such as the Firegod, serpents, Tārkṣya Eagle, vehicle of lord Viṣṇu and other celestials dwelling in heavens, atmosphere and earth be for my victory.

sanskrit: mardayantu raṇe śatrūn sampragṛhyopahārakaṃ /
english: Let them crush the enemies in the battle after having accepted offerings made by me.

sanskrit: saputramātṛbhṛtyo 'haṃ devā vaḥ śaraṇaṅgataḥ //
english: O Gods! have sought your refuge together with sons, mother and servants.

sanskrit: cāmūnāṃ pṛṣṭhato gatvā ripunāśā namo 'stu vaḥ /
english: Obeisance to you! After going to the rear of the enemies destroy them.

sanskrit: vinivṛttaḥ pradāsyāmi dattādabhyadhikaṃ baliṃ //
english: will offer more than that have given after returning from the battle”.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭhe 'hni vijayasnānaṃ kartavyaṃ cābhiṣekavat /
english: On the sixth day, the king should bathe for victory just as the bath at the coronation.

sanskrit: yātrādine saptame ca pūjayecca trivikramaṃ //
english: Lord Trivikrama manifestation of lord Viṣṇu as a dwarf and taking three strides humiliating king Bali should be worshipped on the seventh day, the day of expedition.

sanskrit: nīrājanoktamantraiś ca āyudhaṃ vāhanaṃ yajet / puṇyāhajayaśabdena mantrametanniśāmayet //
english: The weapons and vehicles should be worshipped with the sacred syllables prescribed for nirājana rite of purification. The following sacred syllable should be uttered in the ear of the king with the sounds of auspiciousness and victory.

sanskrit: divyāntarīkṣabhūmiṣṭhāḥ santvāyurdāḥ surāś ca te /
english: “May the celestials dwelling in heaven, atmosphere and earth be bestowers of longevity on you.

sanskrit: devasiddhiṃ prāpnuhi tvaṃ devayātrāstu sā tava //
english: May the success of gods be attained by you. Let your expedition be the expedition of gods.

sanskrit: rakṣantu devatāḥ sarvā iti śrutvā nṛpo vrajet /
english: May all gods protect you”. After having heard this, the king should proceed.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā saśarañcāpaṃ dhanurnāgeti mantrata // tadviṣṇoriti japtvātha dadyādripumukhe padaṃ /
english: After having taken the bow together with the arrow with the recitation of the sacred syllable dhanurnāga, the king should place his foot in the direction of his enemy after having repeated the sacred syllable tad viṣṇoḥ.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaṃ padaṃ dvātriṃśaddikṣu prācyādiṣu kramāt //
english: After having set his right foot, he should place thirty steps in different directions such as the east in due order.

sanskrit: nāgaṃ rathaṃ hayañcaiva dhuryāṃś caivāruhet kramāt /
english: He should duly climb the elephant, chariot, horse and the animal carrying the burden.

sanskrit: āruhya vādyair gacchet pṛṣthato nāvalokayet //
english: After having climbed he should move on along with the sounds of musical instruments without looking back.

sanskrit: krośamātraṃ gatastiṣṭhet pūjayeddevatā dvijān /
english: After having gone a distance of a krośa two or two and a half miles he should halt and worship gods and brahmins.

sanskrit: paradeśaṃ vrajet paścādātmasainyaṃ hi pālayan // rājā prāpya deveśantu deśapālantu pālayet /
english: He should move to the foreign country protecting his own army. After having reached the alien country enemy’s domain the king should protect the guardian deity of the country.

sanskrit: devānāṃ pūjanaṃ kuryānna chindyādāyamatra tu //
english: He should worship deities and should not destroy their properties.

sanskrit: nāvamānayettaddeśyānāgatya svapuraṃ punaḥ / jayaṃ prāpyārcayeddevān dadyāddānāni pārthivaḥ //
english: He should not humiliate the natives of that country. After having returned to his metropolis again after having gained victory, the king should worship gods and make gifts.

sanskrit: dvitīye ahani saṅgrāmo bhaviṣyati yadā tadā /
english: If there is a battle on the second day, the elephant, horse etc.

sanskrit: snapayedgajamaśvādi yajeddevaṃ nṛpasiṃhakaṃ //
english: should be bathed and lord Nrsiṃha manlion manifestation of lord Viṣṇu should be worshipped.

sanskrit: chatrādirājaliṅgāni śastrāṇi niśi vai gaṇān /
english: The royal insignia such as the umbrella etc., weapons and the goblins should be worshipped in the night.

sanskrit: prātarnṛsiṃhakaṃ pūjya vāhanādyamaśeṣataḥ // purodhasā hutaṃ paśyedvahniṃ hutvā dvijānyajet /
english: After having worshipped lord Nṛsiṃha and all vehicles in the morning, the king should see the sacrificial fire kindled by the priest. After having made oblations into the fire, the king should worship brahmins.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā saśarañcāpaṃ gajādyāruhya vai vrajet //
english: After having taken the bow and arrow he should mount the elephant and move.

sanskrit: deśe tvadṛśyaḥ śatrūṇāṃ kuryāt prakṛtikalpanāṃ / saṃhatān yodhayedalpān kāmaṃ vistārayedbahūn //
english: He should walk in the country of the enemy without being noticed by anybody and find the nature of the enemy. He should cause a small army of men spread extensively.

sanskrit: sūcīmukhamanīkaṃ syādalpānāṃ bahubhiḥ saha /
english: A small army as the mouth of a needle can stand against many.

sanskrit: vyūhāḥ prāṇyaṅgarūpāś ca dravyarūpāś ca kīrtitāḥ // garuḍo makaravyūhaś cakraḥ śyenastathaiva ca / ardhacandraś ca vajraś ca śakaṭavyūha eva ca //
english: The arrangement of the army is of the form of animals and things such as the garuḍa the king of birds, crocodile, circle, vulture, semicircle, vajravyūha a strong impenetrable array, cart shaped, the sarvatobhadra circular array and sūcīvyūha as a needle.

sanskrit: vyūhānāmatha sarveṣāṃ pañcadhā sainyakalpanā // dvau pakṣāvanupakṣau dvāvaśyaṃ pañcamaṃ bhavet /
english: An army in one of the above arrays should be arranged in five partsthe two composing its two principal wings, the two forming its sides to protect the wings and the fifth one would be the main body.

sanskrit: ekena yadi vā dvābhyāṃ bhāgābhyāṃ yuddhamācaret //
english: A battle should be fought with one or two of the above parts.

sanskrit: bhāgatrayaṃ sthāpayettu teṣāṃ rakṣārthameva ca /
english: The remaining three parts should be stationed only for their protection.

sanskrit: na vyūhakalpanā kāryā rājño bhavati karhicit //
english: A king should never be in arrays.

sanskrit: mūlacchede vināśaḥ syānna yudhyecca svayannṛpaḥ / sainyasya paścāttiṣṭhettu krośamātre mahīpatiḥ //
english: If the main force is destroyed, the whole army will be routed. A king should not himself fight. A king should remain at a krośa about two or two and a quarter miles, behind the army.

sanskrit: bhagnasandhāraṇaṃ tatra yodhānāṃ parikīrtitaṃ /
english: It is said that a broken army could be resustained by that.

sanskrit: pradhānabhaṅge sainyasya nāśasthānaṃ vidhīyate // na saṃhatānna viralānyodhān vyūhe prakalpayet / āyudhānāntu sammardo yathā na syāt parasparaṃ //
english: One’s stay is not laid down if the main army has suffered a defeat. The soldiers in the array should not be set up too close or too wide apart, so that there may not be any clash of their weapons mutually.

sanskrit: bhettukāmaḥ parānīkaṃ saṃhatair eva bhedayet / bhedarakṣyāḥ pareṇāpi kartavyāḥ saṃhatās tathā // vyūhaṃ bhedāvahaṃ kuryāt paravyūheṣu cecchayā /
english: One who wants to break the hostile army should do so only with collective strength. So also the enemy should protect it from being broken with the collective strength. That division of a hostile army among many divisions, should be first attacked and broken through by the commander as he desires.

sanskrit: gajasya pādarakṣārthāś catvārastu tathā dvija //
english: O Brahmin! There should be four soldiers to guard each foot of an elephant.

sanskrit: rathasya cāśvāś catvāraḥ samāstasya ca carmiṇaḥ /
english: There should be four cavalry and an equal number of armoured soldiers for guarding a chariot.

sanskrit: dhanvinaś carmibhistulyāḥ purastāccarmiṇo raṇe //
english: There should be an equal number of bowmen as the armoured soldiers in front of the armoured soldiers in the battle.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato dhanvinaḥ praścāddhanvinānturagā rathāḥ / rathānāṃ kuñjarāḥ paścāddātavyāḥ pṛthivīkṣitā //
english: Behind bowmen, the cavalry and the chariotfighters and then the soldiers mounted on elephants should be set up by a king. He should look after the duties of the infantry, elephants and horses with effort.

sanskrit: śūrāḥ pramukhato deyāḥ skandhamātrapradarśanaṃ //
english: Bold men should be placed in front. Only a division of the army should be shown.

sanskrit: dārayanti purastāttu na deyā bhīravaḥ puraḥ // protsāhantyeva raṇe bhīrūn śūrāḥ purasthitāḥ /
english: Cowards should not be placed in front because that would break the work of driving away the enemy. The bold men remaining in the front would enthuse cowards in the battle.

sanskrit: saṃhatabhrūyugāś caiva krodhanā kalahapriyāḥ / nityahṛṣṭāḥ prahṛṣṭāś ca śūrā jñeyāś ca kāminaḥ //
english: Men of tall stature with acquiline noses, not having squint eyes, with wellblended eyebrows, irascible, fond of quarrels, contented, happy and lustful are known to be bold.

sanskrit: saṃhatānāṃ hatānāṃ ca raṇāpanayanakriyā / pratiyuddhaṃ gajānāñca toyadānādikañca yat //
english: Carrying the wounded and the dead from the battlefield, offering water to the elephants in each war, bringing weapons to the soldiers are said to be the work of the soldiers.

sanskrit: ripūṇāṃ bhettukāmānāṃ svasainyasya tu rakṣaṇaṃ // bhedanaṃ saṃhatānāñca carmiṇāṃ karma kīrtitaṃ /
english: Protecting their own army from the enemies desiring to break, breaking the collected force of the enemies are the works of armoured men. Making the enemies turn away from battle is the task of bowmen.

sanskrit: dūrāpasaraṇaṃ yānaṃ suhatasya tathocyate /
english: It is said that the chariot of a wounded person should be led away to a distant place.

sanskrit: trāsanaṃ ripusainyānāṃ rathakarma tathocyate //
english: It is stated that the work of the chariotwarriors is to frighten the enemy army.

sanskrit: bhedanaṃ saṃhatānāñca bhedānāmapi saṃhatiḥ / prākāratoraṇāṭṭāladrumabhaṅgaś ca saṅgate //
english: The duties of men mounted on elephants are to break through the collected force of the enemy, to gather soldiers got split in the army of the self and the destruction of walls, arches, battlements and trees.

sanskrit: pattibhūrviṣamā jñeyā rathāśvasya tathā samā /
english: The ground for the infantry to fight is known to be uneven and that for the cavalry and chariot as even.

sanskrit: sakardamā ca nāgānāṃ yuddhabhūmirudāhṛtā //
english: The battlefields for the elephants are pointed out as wet.

sanskrit: evaṃ viracitavyūhaḥ kṛtapṛṣṭhadivākaraḥ / tathānulomaśukrārkidikpālamṛdumārutāḥ // yodhānuttejayetsarvānnāmagotrāvadānataḥ / bhogaprāptyā ca vijaye svargaprāptyā mṛtasya ca //
english: After having arranged the arrays thus and having the Sun behind and the Venus, Saturn, guardian deities of the quarters and the gentle breeze being favourable, all the warriors should be encouraged by repeating their names and the achievement of their clans and pointing out gain of prosperity on success and gain of heaven for the dead.

sanskrit: jitvārīn bhogasamprāptiḥ mṛtasya ca parā gatiḥ /
english: After conquest over the enemies one gets pleasures. There would be supreme position for the dead.

sanskrit: niṣkṛtiḥ svāmipiṇḍasya nāsti yuddhasamā gatiḥ //
english: There is no way of requital for the food taken from the master equal to sacrificing in the battle.

sanskrit: śūrāṇāṃ raktamāyāti tena pāpantyajanti te /
english: They would be washed of their sins as blood flows from the bold warriors.

sanskrit: dhātādiduḥkhasahanaṃ raṇe tat paramantapaḥ //
english: The endurance of pain due to wounds is the excellent penance.

sanskrit: varāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi yānti śūraṃ raṇe mṛtaṃ / svāmī sukṛtamādatte bhagnānāṃ vinivartināṃ //
english: Thousands of celestial women attend on a man killed in the battle. One’s master gets the result of the deeds done by those who run away after being defeated in battle.

sanskrit: brahmahatyāphalaṃ teṣāṃ tathā proktaṃ pade pade /
english: It is said that such people get the fruits of killing a brahmin at each one of their step.

sanskrit: tyaktvā sahāyān yo gaccheddevāstasya vinaṣṭaye //
english: The gods would be lost for one who deserts his companions in the battlefield.

sanskrit: aśvamedhaphalaṃ proktaṃ śūrāṇāmanirvartināṃ /
english: It is said that the brave who do not retreat in battle would get the benefit of performing the sacrifice of aśvamedha.

sanskrit: dharmaniṣṭhe jayo rājñi yoddhavyāś ca samāḥ samaiḥ //
english: If the king is righteous he would be victorious. He should fight with men of equal valour.

sanskrit: gajādyaiś ca gajādyāś ca na hantavyāḥ palāyinaḥ /
english: Men mounted on elephants should be fought by men mounted on elephants.

sanskrit: na prekṣakāḥ praviṣṭāś ca aśastrāḥ pratitādayaḥ //
english: Retreating men, spectators, those not having weapons and those that have fallen should not be killed.

sanskrit: śānte nidrābhibhūte ca ardhottīrṇe nadīvane / durdine kūṭayuddhāni śatrunāśārthamācaret //
english: One should do treacherous warfare when one is fatigued, sleeping, is crossing half the river or forest and on bad days. Raising up arms one should cry that the enemies have been defeated.

sanskrit: prāptaṃ mitraṃ balaṃ bhūri nāyako 'tra nipātitaḥ // senānīrnihatāścāyaṃ bhūpatiścāpi viplutaḥ /
english: “We have got the ally with abundant strength. The king of the enemy forces and the commander have been slain or the hostile king had retreated.” One may kill easily the retreating warriors.

sanskrit: vidrutānāntu yodhānāṃ mukhaṃ ghāto vidhīyate // dhūpāś ca deyā dharmajña tathā ca paramohanāḥ / patākāś caiva sambhāro vāditrāṇām bhayāvahaḥ //
english: O One wellversed in righteousness! incense that stupefies the enemies should be burnt. The banners and other paraphernalia and the musical instruments making frightening sounds should be made use of.

sanskrit: samprāpya vijayaṃ yuddhe devānviprāṃś ca saṃyajet / ratnāni rājagāmīni amātyena kṛte raṇe //
english: After having gained victory in the battle, one should worship gods and brahmins. In a battle won by the minister, the gems acquired by the minister should be made over to the king.

sanskrit: tasya striyo na kasyāpi rakṣyāstāś ca parasya ca /
english: The wives of a defeated king would not belong to anyone else but to that defeated king.

sanskrit: śatruṃ prāpya raṇe muktaṃ putravat paripālayet //
english: A king should honour a hostile king defeated in the battle and treat him as his own son.

sanskrit: punastena na yoddhavyaṃ deśācārādi pālayet /
english: He should not fight with him again.

sanskrit: tataś ca svapuraṃ prāpya dhruve bhe praviśed gṛhaṃ //
english: Then after having entered his native country, he should enter the palace when a fixed star is ruling.

sanskrit: devādipūjanaṃ kuryādrakṣedyodhakuṭumbakaṃ /
english: He should worship the deities etc. and protect the families of warriors.

sanskrit: saṃvibhāgaṃ prāvāptaiḥ kuryād bhṛtyajanasya ca // raṇādīkṣā mayoktā te jayāya nṛpaterdhruvā /
english: He should divide the booty got from the battle among his servants. The procedure for commencing a military expedition has thus been described to you. It gives sure success for the king.

sanskrit: rājyalakṣmīsthiratvāya yathendreṇa purā śriyaḥ /
english: ṚV. ..0. Indra made the prayer to the goddess Śrī Lakṣmī in days of yore for securing the kingdom.

sanskrit: stutiḥ kṛtā tathā rājā jayārthaṃ stutimācaret //
english: A king should similarly do that prayer for the sake of victory.

sanskrit: namasye sarvalokānāṃ jananīmabdhisambhavāṃ / śriyamunnindrapadmākṣīṃ viṣṇuvakṣaḥsthalasthitāṃ //
english: make obeisance to the mother of all worlds, that is born of the ocean, the Goddess Śrī Fortune, that has eyes like the lotus that is waking up after sleep and that person dwelling on the chest of lord Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tvaṃ siddhistvaṃ svadhā svāhā sudhā tvaṃ lokapāvani /
english: O Goddess! You are the success. You are the Svadhā food offered to the manes, the Svāhā oblations.

sanskrit: sandhayā rātriḥ prabhā bhūtirmedhā śraddhā sarasvatī //
english: You are the twilights, night, lustre, wealth, memory, faith and Sarasvatī the Goddess of speech.

sanskrit: yajñavidyā mahāvidyā guhyavidyā ca śobhane /
english: You are the sacrificial knowledge, supreme knowledge and secret knowledge.

sanskrit: ātmavidyā ca devi tvaṃ vimuktiphaladāyinī //
english: O Auspicious one! O Goddess! You are the knowledge of the soul and the conferer of the benefit of emancipation.

sanskrit: ānvīkṣikī trayī vārtā daṇḍanītistvameva ca /
english: You are the metaphysics, the three Vedas and the science of administration.

sanskrit: saumyā saumyair jagadrūpaistvayaitaddevi pūritaṃ //
english: O Goddess! The Beautiful! This has been filled by your beautiful worldly forms.

sanskrit: kā tvanyā tvāmṛte devi sarvayajñamayaṃ vapuḥ / adhyāste deva devasya yogicintyaṃ gadābhṛtaḥ //
english: O Godess! Who else other than you would rest in the body composed of all sacrifices of the macewielding Lord Nārāyaṇa, the god of gods whom the yogins contemplate.

sanskrit: tvayā devi parityaktaṃ sakalaṃ bhuvanatrayaṃ / vinaṣṭaprāyamabhavat tvayedānīṃ samedhitaṃ //
english: O Goddess! All the three worlds were forsaken by you and the Earth was almost lost and resuscitated by you now.

sanskrit: dārāḥ putrās tathāgāraṃ suhṛddhānyadhanādikaṃ / bhavatyetanmahābhāge nityaṃ tvadvīkṣaṇān nṛṇāṃ //
english: O Most Fortunate One! Men would always get wives, sons, house, friends, grains, wealth etc. on account of your glances.

sanskrit: śarīrārogyamaiśvaryamaripakṣakṣayaḥ sukhaṃ / devi tvaddṛṣṭidṛṣṭānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ na durlabhaṃ //
english: O Goddess! It is not impossible for men seen by your glances to get beauty, health, fortune, destruction of the enemy beside happiness.

sanskrit: tvamambā sarvabhūtānāṃ devadevo hariḥ pitā /
english: You are the mother of all beings and Lord Hari Viṣṇu, the god of gods, is the father.

sanskrit: tvayaitadvoiṣṇunā cāmba jagadvyāptaṃ carācaraṃ //
english: O Mother! This world of movable and immovable beings is pervaded by you and lord Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: mā śarīraṃ kalatrañca tyajethāḥ sarvapāvani //
english: O Purifier of all! Do not forsake honour, treasury, granary, house, attendants, body and wife.

sanskrit: tyajethā mama devasya viṣṇorvakṣaḥsthalālaye //
english: One resting on the chest of lord Viṣṇu! Do not desert children, circle of friends, cows and ornaments.

sanskrit: sattvena satyaśaucābhyāṃ tathā śīlādibhirguṇaiḥ / tyajante te narā sadyaḥ santyaktā ye tvayāmale // tvayāvalokitāḥ sadyaḥ śīlādyair akhilair guṇaiḥ /
english: O Spotless one! Those men forsaken by you would be forsaken at once by nobility, truth, purity and other qualities such as good conduct. Men seen by you would at once be endowed with all qualities such as good conduct, the fortune of good family etc. even though they be without good qualities.

sanskrit: sa ślāghyaḥ sa guṇī dhanyaḥ sa kulīnaḥ sa buddhimān / sa śūraḥ sa ca vikrānto yastvayā devi vīkṣitaḥ //
english: O Goddess! Whoever is seen by you would be praiseworthy, possessing good qualities, fortunate, belonging to a good family, wise, valiant and victorious.

sanskrit: sadyo vaiguṇyamāyānti śīlādyāḥ sakalā guṇāḥ / parāṅmukhī jagaddhātrī yasya tvaṃ viṣṇuvallabhe //
english: O Consort of lord Viṣṇu! The Sustainer of the universe! All qualities such as good conduct shed their excellence at once in men from whom you have turned your face.

sanskrit: na te varṇayituṃ śaktā guṇān jihvāpi vedhasaḥ /
english: Even the tongue of Brahmā is not capable of describing your qualities.

sanskrit: prasīda devi padmākṣi nāsmāṃstyākṣīḥ kadācana //
english: O Goddess Lotuseyed! Be gracious. Never forsake us.

sanskrit: evaṃ stutā dadau śrīś ca varamindrāya cepsitaṃ / susthiratvaṃ ca rājyasya saṅgrāmavijayādikaṃ //
english: Being thus adored, goddess Śrī Lakṣmī conferred on Indra the desired boon such as firmness of sovereignty and success in the battle etc.

sanskrit: svastotrapāṭhaśravaṇakartṝṇāṃ bhuktimuktidaṃ /
english: It confers enjoyment and emancipation on those reciting or hearing the hymn.

sanskrit: śrīstotraṃ satataṃ tasmāt paṭhecca śṛṇuyānnaraḥ //
english: Hence one should always read and listen to the hymn on goddess Śrī Lakṣmī.

sanskrit: nītiste puṣkaroktā tu rāmoktā lakṣmaṇāya yā / jayāya tāṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu dharmādivardhanīṃ //
english: Listen. shall now narrate the ethics narrated by Rāma to Lakṣmaṇa for victory and that would increase piety etc. Wealth should be acquired by rightful means.

sanskrit: nyānenārjanamarthasya vardhanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ caret /
english: It should be developed and guarded. It should be given to a deserving person.

sanskrit: satpātrapratipattiś ca rājavṛttaṃ caturvidhaṃ // nayasya vinayo mūlaṃ vinayaḥ śāstraniś cayāt /
english: These are the four obligatory acts of a king. Humility is the cause of statesmanship. Humility is the resultant of determination from scriptures as well as the control of senses.

sanskrit: vinayo hīndriyajayastair yuktaḥ pālayenmahīṃ //
english: The king should guard the earth endowed with these.

sanskrit: śāstraṃ prajñā dhṛtirdākṣyaṃ prāgalbhyaṃ dhārayiṣṇutā / utsāho vāgmitaudāryamāpatkālasahiṣṇutā // prabhāvaḥ śucitā maitrī tyāgaḥ satyaṃ kṛtajñatā /
english: Scriptures, knowledge, fortitude, dexterity, proficiency, reticence, energy, eloquence, generosity, endurance at the time of distress, greatness, purity, amity, renunciation, truthfulness gratitude, good family, good conduct, selfcontrol are the qualities for gaining fortune.

sanskrit: prakīrṇaviṣayāraṇye dhāvantaṃ vipramāthinaṃ / jñānāṅkuśena kurvīta vaśyamindriyadantinaṃ //
english: The elephant in the form of senses running uncontrolled in the forest of diverse pleasures should be controlled with the goad of knowledge.

sanskrit: kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobho harṣo māno madas tathā / ṣaḍvargamutsṛjedenamasmiṃstyakte sukhī nṛpaḥ //
english: A king should give up the aggregate of six things, namely, lust, anger, greed, delight, pride and arrogance. The king who rejects these would be happy.

sanskrit: ānvīkṣikīṃ trayīṃ vārtāṃ daṇḍanītiṃ ca pārthivaḥ / tadvaidyaistatkriyopaitaiścintatayedvinayānvitaḥ //
english: A king being endowed with modesty should contemplate on metaphysics, the three Vedas, emissary and polity with those wellversed in these and those practising them.

sanskrit: ānvīkṣikyārthavijñānaṃ dharmādharmau trayīsthitau / arthānarthau tu vārtāyāṃ daṇḍanītyāṃ nayānayau //
english: The knowledge about true nature of things is got through metaphysics. Virtue and vice rest on the three Vedas. Material prosperity and misfortune depend on emissary and justice and injustice on polity.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā sūnṛtā vāṇī satyaṃ śaucaṃ dayā kṣamā / varṇināṃ liṅgināṃ caiva sāmānyo dharma ucyate //
english: Abstaining from killing or causing injury to beings, courteous laṅguage, truthfulness, purity, kindness, and forbearance are the general virtues of the religious students.

sanskrit: prajāḥ samanugṛhṇīyāt kuryādācārasaṃsthitiṃ /
english: One should show compassion to all beings and practise codes of conduct.

sanskrit: vāk sūnṛtā dayā dānaṃ hīnopagatarakṣaṇaṃ // iti vṛttaṃ satāṃ sādhuhitaṃ satpuruṣavrataṃ /
english: Courteous words, compassion, charity and protection of one that has sought refuge are the acts of good people agreeable to pious men.

sanskrit: ādhivyādhiparītāya adya śvo vā vināśine // ko hi rājā śarīrāya dharmāpetaṃ samācaret / na hi svamukhamanvicchan pīḍayet kṛpaṇaṃ janaṃ //
english: Which king would do impious acts for the sake of the body that is encompassed by misery and disease and that is liable to get destroyed today or tomorrow? One should not oppress the poor people desiring his own happiness.

sanskrit: kṛpaṇaḥ pīḍyamāno hi manyunā hanti pārthivaṃ /
english: A poor man being oppressed kills the king by means of his anger.

sanskrit: kriyate 'bhyarhaṇīyāya svajanāya yathāñjaliḥ // tataḥ sādhutaraḥ kāryo durjanāya śivarthinā /
english: A king desiring his own good should conduct with more humility than that shown to a respectful kinsman with folded palms.

sanskrit: priyamevābhidhātavyaṃ satsu nityaṃ dviṣatsu ca //
english: One should always speak only in a pleasing manner to friends and foes.

sanskrit: devāste priyavaktāraḥ paśavaḥ krūravādinaḥ /
english: Those who speak pleasingly are gods and those who speak harsh are animals.

sanskrit: śucirāstikyapūtātmā pūjayeddevatāḥ sadā //
english: One should always worship gods with cleanliness and get purified with piety.

sanskrit: devatāvat gurujanamātmavacca suhṛjjanaṃ /
english: The preceptors should be respected as gods and friends as one’s own selves.

sanskrit: praṇipātena hi guruṃ sato 'mṛṣānuceṣṭitaiḥ //
english: The preceptor should be pleased by bowing down.

sanskrit: kurvītābhimukhān bhṛtyair devān sukṛtakarmaṇā /
english: The favourable pious men should be pleased by doing true gestures and services. The gods should be pleased by good deeds.

sanskrit: sadbhāvena harenmitraṃ sambhrameṇa ca bāndhavān // strībhṛtyān premadānābhyāṃ dākṣiṇyetaraṃ janaṃ /
english: A friend should be attracted by courteousness and kinsmen by showing respect. The wife and servants should be pleased respectively by showing affection and making gifts.

sanskrit: kṛpaṇeṣu dayālutvaṃ sarvatra madhurā giraḥ /
english: The rest of the people should be won by showing compassion.

sanskrit: prāṇair apyupakāritvaṃ mitrāyāvyabhicāriṇe // gṛhāgate pariṣvaṅgaḥ śaktyā dānaṃ sahiṣṇutā / svasamṛddhiṣvanutsekaḥ paravṛddhiṣvamatsaraḥ // aparopatāpi vacanaṃ maunavratacariṣṇutā / bandhabhirbaddhasaṃyogaḥ svajane caturaśratā //
english: Not reviling the acts of others, maintaining to do one’s duties, kindness to wards the poor, sweet words towards all, helping a true friend even by sacrificing one’s life, receiving warmly the person that has come to the house, making a gift according to one’s ability, forbearance, absence of pride in prosperity, not jealous at other’s prosperity, not speaking words hurting the feelings of others, practising the vow of silence, maintaining the bondage with kinsmen, keeping even attitude towards one’s own men and taking actions conducive to welfare are the acts of greatmen.

sanskrit: svāmyamātyañca rāṣṭrañca durgaṃ koṣo balaṃ suhṛt / parasparopakārīdaṃ saptāṅgaṃ rājyamucyate //
english: The king, ministry, kingdom, fort, treasury, army and allies helpful to one another are said to be the seven constituents of a kingdom.

sanskrit: rājyāṅgānāṃ varaṃ rāṣṭraṃ sādhanaṃ pālayet sadā /
english: The sovereignty is the most important means of a kingdom. It should hence always be protected.

sanskrit: kulaṃ śīlaṃ vayaḥ sattvaṃ dākṣiṇyaṃ kṣiprakāritā // avisaṃvāditā satyaṃ vṛddhasevā kṛtajñatā / daivasampannatā buddhirakṣudraparivāratā // śakyasāmantatā caiva tathā ca dṛḍhabhaktitā /
english: Good descent, good conduct, young in years, good quality, compassion, quick action, consistency, truthfulness, service to the aged, gratefulness, being fortunate, intellect, possessing an unwicked retinue, able to exhibit his valour, faithfulness, foresightedness zeal, purity, generosity, modesty and virtuousness are the qualities of a pious man and a king.

sanskrit: vinītatvaṃ dhārmikatā sādhoś ca nṛpaterguṇāḥ / prakhyātavaṃśamakrūraṃ lokasaṅgrāhiṇaṃ śuciṃ //
english: A king, seeking his own good, should make those belonging to a good family his attendants, be not cruel, but capable of winning the people and pure.

sanskrit: kurvītātsahitāṅkṣī paricāraṃ mahīpatiḥ / vāgmī pragalbhaḥ smṛtimānudagro balavān vaśī // netā daṇḍasya nipuṇaḥ kṛtaśilpaparigrahaḥ / parābhiyogaprasahaḥ sarvaduṣṭapratikriyā // pravṛttānvavekṣī ca sandhivigrahatattvavit /
english: A king should be eloquent, confident, possessing good memory, distinguished, strong, selfcontrolled, a leader, wellversed in polity and the different branches of fine arts, capable of facing an attack, capable of remedying all evils, one who knows the movements of hostiles, one who knows the principles of peaces making and war capable of knowing the secret counsels of the hostiles, knower of opportune time and place, one that takes goods in the proper way and distributes to the proper person, free from wrath, greed, fear, doing evil, haughtiness and fickleness, free from harassing others, calumny, jealousy, envy and untruth, fortunate in getting the counsel of the aged, able, showing his amiable manners and one that is fond of good qualities which are known to confer prosperity.

sanskrit: kulīnāḥ śucayaḥ śūrāḥ śrutavanto 'nurāgiṇaḥ // daṇḍanīteḥ prayoktāraḥ sacivāḥ syurmahīpateḥ /
english: Men of noble descent, virtuous, brave, learned, attached, those who would implement the rules of punishment should be the ministers of the king.

sanskrit: suvigraho jānapadaḥ kulaśīkakalānvitaḥ // vāgmī pragalbhaś cakṣuṣmānutsāhī pratipattimān / stambhacāpalahīnaś ca maitraḥ kleśasahaḥ śuciḥ // satyasattvadhṛtisthairyaprabhāvārogyasaṃyutaḥ / kṛtaśilpaś ca dakṣaś ca prajñāvān dhāraṇānvitaḥ //
english: The minister should moreover be havṃg good physique, a native of the country, belonging to a good family, endowed with good conduct and knowledge in arts, eloquent, courageous, possessing good eyesight, enthusiasm, discrimination, devoid of rigidity and ficklemindedness, friendly, capable of enduring hardship, virtuous, possessing the qualities, of truthfulness, good nature, firmness, perseverence, dignity, good health, able, having retentive memory, firm devotion to the king and not creating enmity with other kings.

sanskrit: smṛtistatparatārtheṣu cittajño jñānaniś cayaḥ // dṛḍhatā mantraguptiś ca mantrisampat prakīrtitā /
english: memory, good application of the mind conducive to gain, decisive knowledge, firmness and guarding the secret counsels are the virtues of a minister.

sanskrit: atharvadevavihitaṃ kuryācchāntikapauṣṭikaṃ /
english: The priest should do the expiatory and welfareyielding rites as laid down in Atharvaveda.

sanskrit: sādhutaiṣāmamātyānāṃ tadvidyaiḥ saha buddhimān //
english: The wise king should examine the fitness of these ministers with the help of experts.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣmattāṃ ca śilpañca parīkṣeta guṇadvayaṃ /
english: The two qualities of having a clear sight and skill should be examined.

sanskrit: svajanebhyo vijānīyāt kulaṃ sthānamavagrahaṃ //
english: He should know about the family and the integrity from his own people.

sanskrit: parikarmasu dakṣañca vijñānaṃ dhārayiṣṇutāṃ / guṇatrayaṃ parīkṣeta prāgalabhyaṃ prītitāṃ tathā //
english: The three qualitiesability in service, knowledge and endurance should be examined. So also the boldness, and their pleasure in conversation should be known.

sanskrit: kathāyogeṣu buddhyeta vāgmitvaṃ satyavāditāṃ / utasāhaṃ ca prabhāvaṃ ca tathā kleśasahiṣṇutāṃ //
english: Their eloquence, truthfulness, enthusiasm, greatness, endurance for hardship, firmness, loyalty and steadiness in distress should be noted.

sanskrit: bhaktiṃ maitrīṃ ca śaucaṃ ca jānīyādvyavahārataḥ //
english: The king should know their devotion, friendship and honesty from their conduct.

sanskrit: saṃvāsibhyo balaṃ sattvamārogyaṃ śīlameva ca / astabdhatāmacāpalyaṃ vairāṇāṃ cāpyakīrtanaṃ //
english: Likewise their strength, good nature, health, good conduct, not being fickleminded and not exhibiting their enmity should be known from their companions.

sanskrit: pratyakṣato vijānīyād bhadratāṃ kṣudratāmapi /
english: Their gentleness and meanness should be known from their acts in his presence.

sanskrit: phalānumeyāḥ sarvatra parokṣaguṇavṛttayaḥ //
english: Everywhere the virtues of them practised not in his presence should be gauged from results.

sanskrit: śasyākaravatī puṇyā khanidravyasamanvitā / gohitā bhūrisalilā puṇyair janapadair yutā // ramyā sakuñjarabalā vāristhalapathānvitā /
english: A region having good crops, meritorious, endowed with minerals, beneficial for cows, having plenty of water having holy cities, enchanting, abounding in elephants, having water courses and not depending on rains is commended for abundant prosperity.

sanskrit: śūdrakāruvaṇikprāyo mahārambhaḥ kṛṣī balaḥ / sānurāgo ripudveṣī pīḍāsahakaraḥ pṛthuḥ //
english: It should abound with śūdras, artisans and merchants and have great enterprises and agriculturers. It should abound with men fondly attached to the king, hating the hostile king, capable of enduring hardship.

sanskrit: nānādeśyaiḥ samākīrṇo dhārmikaḥ paśumān balī /
english: It should contain people who have come from different countries and who are pious, possessing cattle and strength.

sanskrit: īdṛkjanapadaḥ śasto 'mūrkhavyasanināyakaḥ //
english: The head should be wise and not addicted to any vice.

sanskrit: pṛthusīmaṃ mahākhātamuccaprākāratoraṇaṃ / puraṃ samāvasecchailasarinmaruvanāśrayaṃ // jalavaddhānyadhanavaddurgaṃ kālasahaṃ mahat /
english: The fortress should be built on hills having a river or desert or forest as a boundary covering a large area and having a deep moat, high walls and gateways. The fort should contain water, grains and treasures to stand a long siege.

sanskrit: audakaṃ pārvataṃ vārkṣamairiṇaṃ dhanvinaṃ ca ṣaṭ //
english: Those surrounded by water, mountain, forest, desert and archers are six kinds of forts.

sanskrit: īpsitadravyasampūrṇaḥ pitṛpaitāmahocitaḥ / dharmārjito vyayasahaḥ koṣo dharmādivṛddhaye //
english: The forts should be replete with choice things, righteously acquired since the time of forefathers that would stand a heavy drain for the furtherance of righteousness etc.

sanskrit: pitṛpaitāmaho vaśyaḥ saṃhato dattavetanaḥ / vikhyātapauruṣo janyaḥ kuśulaḥ śakunair vṛtaḥ //
english: The servants should be descendants of their forefathers’ servants, subservient, salaried, known for their valour, belonging to a good family, able, possessing knowledge about omens.

sanskrit: nānāprahaṇopeto nānāyuddhaviśāradaḥ / nānāyodhasamākīrṇau nīrājitahayadvipaḥ // pravāsāyāsaduḥkheṣu yuddheṣu ca kṛtaśramaḥ /
english: The army of the king should be armed with different kinds of weapons, conversant with different types of warfare, possessing varied kinds of warriors, having horses and elephants duly sanctified, which i^s endured hardships in battle and sufferings in expeditions etc.

sanskrit: advaidhakṣatriyaprāyo daṇḍo daṇḍavatāṃ mataḥ //
english: Those who administer justice should be undivided and mostly drawn from the kṣatriya community.

sanskrit: yogavijñānasattvārūḍhyaṃ mahāpakṣaṃ priyamvadaṃ / āyātikṣamamadvaidhaṃ mitraṃ kurvīta satkulaṃ //
english: One that is proficient in yoga, goodnatured, possessing a strong army, conversing affectionately, able to wait patiently for the outcome, not divided and belonging to a good family should be befriended.

sanskrit: dūrādevābhigamanaṃ spaṣṭārthahṛdayānugā / vāk satkṛtya pradānañca trividho mitrasaṅgrahaḥ //
english: Approaching from a distance, uttering words having clear meaning and agreeable to the heart and doing good deeds are the three ways of acquiring friendship.

sanskrit: dharmakāmārthasaṃyogo mitrāttu trividhaṃ phalaṃ /
english: One gets three kinds of fruits such as piety, enjoyment and prosperity through the friend.

sanskrit: rakṣitaṃ vyasanebhyaś ca mitraṃ jñeyaṃ caturvidhaṃ /
english: The son of a friend, a newly acquired friend, an ancestral friend and one protected from distress are known to be the four kinds of friends.

sanskrit: mitre guṇāḥ satyatādyāḥ samānasukhadukhatā //
english: Truthfulness and other things and similar pleasure and pain are the qualities in the friend.

sanskrit: vakṣye 'nujīvināṃ vṛtte sevī seveta bhūpatiṃ /
english: shall describe the conduct of those who serve the king. A servant should serve the king to the best of his ability.

sanskrit: dakṣatā bhadratā dārḍhyaṃ kṣāntiḥ kleśasahiṣṇutā // santoṣaḥ śīlamutsāho maṇḍayatyanujīvinaṃ /
english: Ability, good disposition, firmness, forbearance, ability to endure hardship, happiness, good conduct, enthusiasm are ornaments for the servants.

sanskrit: yathākālamupāsīta rājānaṃ sevako nayāt //
english: A servant should serve the king to the best of his ability for the agreed period.

sanskrit: parasthānagamaṃ krauryamauddhatyaṃ matsarantyajet / vigṛhya kathanaṃ bhṛtyo na kuryāj jyāyasā saha //
english: He should give up visiting the place of enemies, doing cruel acts, haughtiness and jealousy. A servant should not exchange harsh words with his superiors.

sanskrit: guhyaṃ marma ca mantrañca na ca bhartuḥ prakāśayet /
english: He should not publicise the confidential matters and the secret councils of his master.

sanskrit: raktād vṛttiṃ samīheta viraktaṃ santyajennṛpaṃ //
english: He should desire the prosperity of the affectionate king.

sanskrit: akārye pratiṣedhaś ca kārye cāpi pravartanaṃ / saṅkṣepāditi sadvṛttaṃ bandhumitrānujīvināṃ //
english: Dissuading the king from doing evil deeds and persuading him to do good deeds are said to be the good conduct in brief for the relatives, friends and servants.

sanskrit: ājīvyaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ rājā parjanyavadbhavet /
english: The king, like the god of rain, should be sustainer of all good.

sanskrit: āyadvāreṣu cāptyarthaṃ dhanaṃ cādadatīti ca //
english: He would take a part of the earnings from the sources of one’s earning.

sanskrit: kuryādudyogasampannānadhyakṣān sarvakarmasu /
english: He should employ efficient men to be in charge of all deeds.

sanskrit: khanyākarabalādānaṃ śūnyānāṃ ca niveśanaṃ / aṣṭavargamimaṃ rājā sādhuvṛtto 'nupālayet //
english: A good king should protect eight things such as agriculture, trade, fort, bridge, elephant stable, mines, ocean the source of gems and the abodes of the downcast and thus follow a good code of conduct.

sanskrit: āmuktikebhyaś caurebhyaḥ paurebhyo rājavallabhāt / pṛthivīpatilobhācca prajānāṃ pañcadhā bhayaṃ //
english: There is danger for the subjects from the following five sources such as the soldiers, thieves, subjects, king’s officers and the greed of the king.

sanskrit: avekṣyaitadbhayaṃ kāle ādadīta karaṃ nṛpaḥ /
english: The king should take tax after having taken note of this danger at the proper time.

sanskrit: abhyantaraṃ śarīraṃ svaṃ vāhyaṃ rāṣṭrañca rakṣayet //
english: He has to protect his own body and the external body, the kingdom.

sanskrit: daṇḍāṃsta daṇḍayedrājā svaṃ rakṣecca viṣāditaḥ / striyaḥ putrāṃś ca śatrubhyo viśvasenna kadācana //
english: He should punish those deserving punishment and protect himself from poison as well as his wives and sons from the enemies. He should never trust them.

sanskrit: maṇḍalaṃ cintayet mukhyaṃ rājā dvādaśarājakaṃ /
english: It mentions only five names. A king should think mainly about the circle of twelve kings.

sanskrit: arirmitramarermitraṃ mitramitramataḥ paraṃ // tathārimitramitrañca vijigīṣoḥ puraḥ smṛtāḥ / pārṣṇigrāhaḥ smṛtaḥ paścādākrandastadanantaraṃ //
english: The enemy, friend, ally of an enemy, ally of an ally, ally of an ally of the enemy are known to be at the front of the conqueror. An enemy in the rear, a king whose kingdom lies next but one, the allies of these two is the circle of kings of a king desiring to conquer.

sanskrit: areś ca vijigīṣoś ca madhyamo bhūmyanantaraḥ // anugrahe saṃhatayor nigrahe vyastayoḥ prabhuḥ /
english: One who is beyond the enemy and the invader is the neutral. One is a master in favouring the united and the suppression of the divided.

sanskrit: maṇḍalādvahireteṣāmudāsīno balādhikaḥ //
english: One who is beyond this circle of kings and possessing a greater strength is known to be a neutral.

sanskrit: anugrahe saṃhatānāṃ vyastānāṃ ca budhe prabhuḥ /
english: One is a lord in favouring the allies and the annihilalation of the divided.

sanskrit: sandhiñca vigrahaṃ yānamāsānadi vadāmi te // balavadvigrahītena sandhiṃ kuryācchivāya ca /
english: shall describe the treaty, battle, vehicle, seat etc. One should make a treaty with the strongly opposed for one’s welfare.

sanskrit: parikramas tathā chinnas tathā ca paradūṣaṇaṃ / skandhopayeyaḥ sandhiś ca sandhayaḥ ṣoḍaśeritāḥ //
english: Treaties are said to be sixteenkapāla, upahāra, santāna, saṅgata, upanyāsa, pratīkāra, saṃyoga, puruṣāntara, adṛṣṭanara, ādiṣṭa, ātman, upagraha, parikrama, chinna, paradūṣaṇa and skandhopaneya.

sanskrit: parasparopakāraś ca maitraḥ sambandhakas tathā / upahārāś ca catvārasteṣu mukhyāś ca sandhayaḥ //
english: Reciprocally beneficial, mutual amity, being related to each other and making presents as token of friendship are the four principal treaties.

sanskrit: anekacittamantraś ca devabrāhmaṇanindakaḥ // daivopahatakaś caiva daivanindaka eva ca / durbhikṣavyasanopeto balavyasanasaṅkulaḥ // svadeśastho bahuripurmuktaḥ kālena yaś ca ha / satyadharmavyapetaś ca viṃśatiḥ puruṣā amī //
english: One should not make treaties with the twenty people such as a child, an old man, one ill since a long time, an excommunicated relative, a coward, cowardly people, greedy people, one who has renounced the world, one excessively fond of worldly things, one devising many schemes, a despiser of gods and brahmins, an illfated one, one who speaks ill of fate, one suffering from famine, one having a discontented army, one having many enemies within the country and one who had become free in course of time and one swerved from adhering to truth and virtuous life.

sanskrit: ertaiḥ sandhiṃ na kurvīta vigṛhṇīyāttu kebalaṃ /
english: They should always be fought.

sanskrit: parasparāpakāreṇa puṃsāṃ bhavati vigrahaḥ //
english: A war is the result of mutual offence of men hostile kings.

sanskrit: ātmano 'bhyudayākāṅkṣī pīḍyamānaḥ pareṇa vā / deśakālabalopetaḥ prārabheteha vigrahaṃ //
english: One aspiring the prosperity for himself, one being oppressed by another and one having favourable position, time and strength should begin war.

sanskrit: rājyastrīsthānadeśānāṃ jñānasya ca balasya ca / apahārī mado mānaḥ pīḍā vaiṣayikī tathā // jñānātmaśaktidharmāṇāṃ vighāto daivameva ca / mitrārthañcāpamānaś ca tathā bandhuvināśanaṃ //
english: Taking possession of kingdom, women, suzerainty, knowledge and strength, pride, honour, loss of fortune, destruction of knowledge, one’s soul force and the virtue, that is due fate, dishonour on account of a friend, the destruction of a relative, cessation of the favour of natural elements, disturbance among the circle of monarchs, intense attachment for the sake of one are the causes for hostility.

sanskrit: sāpatnyaṃ vāstujaṃ strījaṃ vāgjātamaparādhajaṃ / vairaṃ pañcavidhaṃ proktaṃ sādhanaiḥ praśamannayet //
english: Enmity is said to be of five kindsthrough the cowife, on account of one’s abode, on account of wife, that arising from one’s expression and that due to an offence.

sanskrit: āyatyāñca tadātve ca doṣasañjananaṃ tathā /
english: It should be amended by suitable expedients.

sanskrit: parārthaṃ strīnimittañca dīrghakālaṃ dvijaiḥ saha / akāladaivayuktena baloddhatasakhena ca // tadātve phalasaṃyuktamāyatyāṃ phalavarjitaṃ / āyatyāṃ phalasaṃyuktaṃ tadātve niṣphalaṃ tathā // itīmaṃ ṣoḍaśavidhannakuryādeva vigrahaṃ /
english: A king should not engage in any of the following sixteen kinds of war, such as giving meagre result, yielding absolutely nil result, of uncertain result, that vitiating the existing order, proving fruitless in the long run that which affects in the long run and the existing order, with an army mobilised by enemy whose strength is not known, being undertaken for the sake of an ally or for the recovery of a woman or that lasting for a long time, or with brahmins, with one equipped with an untimely providence, with an enemy supported by a mighty friend, when it yields some result only at that moment but with no fruit in the long run and that which bears fruit in the long run but no benefit at that very moment.

sanskrit: tadātvāyatisaṃśuddhaṃ karma rājā sadācaret //
english: A king should undertake a task that would bear fruit at that moment and also in the long run.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭaṃ puṣṭaṃ balaṃ matvā gṛhṇīyādviparītakaṃ /
english: One should wage war when one’s forces are happy and strong and the enemy forces are of contrary nature.

sanskrit: mitramākranda āsāro yadā syurdṛḍhabhaktayaḥ // parasya viparītañca tadā vigrahamācaret /
english: One should commence a battle when the friend, an ally and a neighbouring king are firmly attached to him and that of the enemy is the contrary.

sanskrit: upekṣayā ca nipuṇair yānaṃ pañcavidhaṃ smṛtaṃ / parasparasya sāmarthyavighātādāsanaṃ smṛtaṃ // areś ca vijagīṣoś ca yānavat pañcadhā smṛtam /
english: A military expedition is said to be of five kinds by experts such as an open foe, as an ally If one of the combatants, as united force, as occasional and remaining neutral. Like the expedition, halt is also of five kinds according to the ability of mutually combating forces of the enemy and the invader.

sanskrit: balinīrdviṣatormadhye vācātmānaṃ samarpayan // dvaidhībhāvena tiṣṭheta kākākṣivadalakṣitaḥ /
english: One should inform his arrival to the commander of the stronger of the two opposing forces remaining without taking the side of either of them and like the eye of the crow remain unnoticed.

sanskrit: ubhayorapi sampāte seveta balavattaraṃ //
english: One should join the stronger one when the hostilities begin.

sanskrit: yadā dvāvapi necchetāṃ saṃśleṣaṃ jātasaṃvidau / tadopasarpettacchatrumadhikaṃ vā svayaṃ vrajet //
english: When both of them suspect his feigned neutrality and would dislike the engagement, one should himself attack the enemy that is more antagonistic.

sanskrit: ucchidyamāno balinā nirupāyapratikriyaḥ / kuloddhataṃ satyamāryamāseveta balotkaṭaṃ // taddarśanopāstikatā nityantadbhāvabhāvitā /
english: When a king with his army is routed by the powerful enemy and does not find a strategy, he should practise truthfulness and noble virtues of the ancestors. He should visit the powerful ally frequently, stay by his side, view things as he does and show gratitude for the support extended.

sanskrit: tatkāritapraśriyatā vṛttaṃ saṃśrayiṇaḥ śrutaṃ //
english: The code of conduct for those seeking refuge has been heard.

sanskrit: prabhavotsāhaśaktibhyāṃ mantraśaktiḥ praśasyate /
english: l. The power of counsel is commended than the power of greatness and enthusiasm.

sanskrit: prabhāvotsāhavān kāvyo jito devapurodhasā //
english: Kāvya Śukra, the preceptor of demons, possessing greatness and enthusiasm was conquered by the priest of the celestials Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: mantrayeteha kāryāṇi nānāptair nāvipaścitā /
english: One should not have a counsel with untrustworthy and foolish persons.

sanskrit: aśakyārambhavṛttīnāṃ kutaḥ kleśādṛte phalaṃ //
english: How can a scheme that is impossible to begin be made to bear the fruit without toil.

sanskrit: avijñātasya vijñānaṃ vijñātasya ca niś cayaḥ / arthadvaidhasya sandehacchedanaṃ śeṣadarśanaṃ // sahāyāḥ sādhanopāyā vibhāgo deśakālayoḥ / vipatteś ca pratīkāraḥ pañcāṅgo mantra iṣyate //
english: A counsel is laid down as of five kindsknowledge of the unknown, ascertainment of that known already, removal of doubt relating to an ambiguous matter in politics, determination of the right time and place of action and helpful means, and remedial measures against misfortunes.

sanskrit: manaḥprasādaḥ śraddhā ca tathā karaṇapāṭavaṃ /
english: The marks of success in the acts are the cheerfulness of the mind, faith, efficiency of the means, aid and effort.

sanskrit: madaḥ pramādaḥ kāmaś ca suptapralapitāni ca / bhindanti mantraṃ pracchannāḥ kāminyo ramatāntathā //
english: Pride, negligence, lust, prattling in sleep and enjoying pleasures with the beloved women break the secret counsel.

sanskrit: pragalbhaḥ smṛtimānvāgmīśastre śāstre ca niṣṭhitaḥ / abhyastakarmā nṛpaterdūto bhaviturmarhati //
english: A person who is bold, having good memory, eloquent wellversed in the wielding of weapons and in the sciences, and one accustomed with the work deserves to become a messenger of the king.

sanskrit: nisṛṣṭārtho mitārthaś ca tathā śāsanahārakaḥ / sāmarthyāt pādato hīno dūtastu trividhaḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: A messenger is said to be of three types such as one that discharges duty efficiently, one that does moderately and one who just conveys the message. Each one of the succeeding one is inferior by a quarter based on the ability of the respective ones.

sanskrit: nāvijñātaṃ puraṃ śatroḥ praviśecca na śaṃsadaṃ /
english: One should not enter the city of the enemy and his assembly without having previous acquaintance.

sanskrit: kālamīkṣeta kāryārthamanujñātaś ca niṣpatet //
english: One should abide the right time and should fall upon the enemy after knowing the opportune moment.

sanskrit: chidrañca śatrorjānīyāt koṣamitrabalāni ca /
english: One should know the weakness of the enemy as well as his treasury, friends and strength.

sanskrit: rāgāparāgau jānīyād dṛṣṭigātraviceṣṭitaiḥ //
english: He should also know the likes and dislikes from the looks and gestures of the enemy.

sanskrit: kuryāccaturvidhaṃ stortraṃ pakṣayorubhayorapi /
english: An enemy should make fourfold eulogies of both the sides i.e. the master and the enemy.

sanskrit: tapasvivyañjanopetaiḥ sucaraiḥ saha saṃvaset //
english: He should live with good spies having the guise of ascetics.

sanskrit: caraḥ prakāśo dūtaḥ syādaprakāśaś caro dvidhā /
english: An ambassador would be an open spy. A spy in disguise is of two kinds.

sanskrit: baṇik kṛṣībalo liṅgī bhikṣukādyātmakāś carāḥ //
english: Spies would be in the guise of a merchant, agriculturer or mendicant and the like.

sanskrit: yāyādariṃ vyasaninaṃ niṣphale dūtaceṣṭite / prakṛtavyasanaṃ yatsyāttat samīkṣya samutpatet //
english: When the effort of the messenger has become fruitless, the king should attack the distressed enemy. One should take into account the natural calamity that has befallen the enemy and fall upon him.

sanskrit: anayādvyasyati śreyastasmāttadvyasanaṃ smṛtaṃ /
english: Because it destroys the good fortune on account of bad policy it is said to be misfortune.

sanskrit: hutāśano jalaṃ vyādhirdurbhikṣaṃ marakaṃ tathā // iti pañcavidhaṃ daivaṃ vyasanaṃ mānuṣaṃ paraṃ /
english: Conflagration, water, diseases epidemics, famine and hell are the five calamities due to divine agency. The rest are due to human agency.

sanskrit: daivaṃ puruṣakāreṇa śāntyā ca praśamannayet //
english: The misfortune due to divine agency should be subdued by means of human effort and appeasing rites.

sanskrit: utthāpitena nītyā ca mānuṣaṃ vyasanaṃ haret /
english: The misfortune due to human agency should be removed by means of expedients based on the rightful living.

sanskrit: mantro mantraphalāvāptiḥ kāryānuṣṭhānamāyatiḥ // āyavyayau daṇḍanītiramitrapratiṣedhanaṃ / vyasanasya pratīkāro rājyarājābhirakṣaṇaṃ // ityamātyasya karmedaṃ hanti savyasanānvitaḥ /
english: Deliberation, the reaping of the fruits of deliberation, following a course of action for future contingencies, the income and expenditure of the state, enforcing laws, the prevention of the encroachment by the enemy, takingremedial steps for the calamity and the protection of kingdom and the king are the duties of a minister. Hence one beset with misfortune would ruin kingdom.

sanskrit: hiraṇyadhānyavastrāṇi vāhanaṃ prajayā bhavet //
english: Gold, grain, clothes and vehicle would be through the subjects.

sanskrit: tathānye dravyanicayā danti savyasanā prajā /
english: In the same way other things are got through the subjects.

sanskrit: prajānāmāpadisthānāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ koṣadaṇḍayoḥ // paurādyāścopakurvanti saṃśrayādiha durdinaṃ / tūṣṇīṃ yuddhaṃ janatrāṇaṃ mitrāmitraparigrahaḥ //
english: Citizens of the city etc. help to protect subjects having misfortune as well as the treasury and law if it is sought. The duties of feudatory chiefs are to put down disturbance, help the sovereign in war, protection of people and taking note of the allies and foes.

sanskrit: sāmantādi kṛte doṣe naśyettadvyasanācca tat /
english: A king would perish on account of the fault of the vassals and suffer misfortune.

sanskrit: bhṛtyānāṃ bharaṇaṃ dānaṃ prajāmitraparigrahaḥ // dharmakāmādibhedaś ca durgasaṃskārabhūṣaṇaṃ /
english: Treasure enables a king to pay his servants, to win him friends and subjects, to aid the purposes of virtue and desire, to attend to the renovation of forts.

sanskrit: koṣāttadvyasanāddhanti koṣamūlo hi bhūpatiḥ //
english: If that is having misfortune, it would ruin the king. The king is dependent on the treasury.

sanskrit: mitrāmitrāvanīhemasādhanaṃ ripumardanaṃ / dūrakāryāśukāritvaṃ daṇḍāttadvyasanāddharet //
english: The enforcement of law is a means to create friends and foes, to acquire land and gold, to conquer enemies, to accomplish a work quickly that would take long time.

sanskrit: sastambhayati mitrāṇi amitraṃ nāśayatyapi /
english: If that is affected it would ruin the king.

sanskrit: dhanādyair upakāritvaṃ mitrāttadvyasanāddharet //
english: An ally would collect together allies, destroy the enemy and help him with money etc.

sanskrit: rājā savyasanī hanyādrājakāryāṇi yāni ca /
english: The king having a vice would destroy the affairs of the state.

sanskrit: vāgdaṇḍayoś ca pāruṣyamarthadūṣaṇameva ca // pānaṃ strī mṛgayā dyūtaṃ vyasanāni mahīpateḥ /
english: The vices of a king are the use of harsh words, inflicting cruel punishment, wasteful spending of revenue, drinking, excessive enjoyment of the company of women, hunting and gambling.

sanskrit: ālasyaṃ stabdhatā darpaḥ pramādo dvaidhakāritā // iti pūrvopadiṣṭañca sacivavyasanaṃ smṛtaṃ /
english: Idleness, obstinacy, pride, intelligence and duplicity are the defects of a minister as already pointed out.

sanskrit: anāvṛṣṭiś ca pīḍādau rāṣṭravyasanamucyate // viśīrṇayantraprākāraparikhātvamaśastratā / kṣīṇayā senayā naddhaṃ durgavyasanamucyate //
english: Drought and epidemics etc. are the misfortunes of a country. Shattered machines, walls and ditches not equipped with weapons and possessing a depleted army are the defects of a fort.

sanskrit: vyayīkṛtaḥ parikṣipto 'prajito 'sañcitas tathā / daṣito darasaṃsthaś ca koṣavyasanamucyate //
english: One nearly drained, not filled regularly, not being accounted, not accumulated, made waste and situated at a far off place are the defects in treasury.

sanskrit: uparuddhaṃ parikṣiptamamānitavimānitaṃ / abhūtaṃ vyādhitaṃ śrāntaṃ dūrāyātannavāgataṃ // parikṣīṇaṃ pratihataṃ prahatāgratarantathā / āśānirvedabhūyiṣṭhamanṛtaprāptameva ca // kalatragarbhannikṣiptamantaḥśalpaṃ tathaiva ca /
english: Being obstructed, scattered, not honoured, disrespected, not existing, afflicted with disease, tired, arrived from a distant place, newly recruited, much reduced, disappointed, repulsed much, abound with hopes and disgust, deceived, having wives, having grievance within, break in the supply of provisions of different kinds, the base being made void, divided by the hostile king, deprived of a leader and bribed by the hostile king at the rear are said to be the defects of an army.

sanskrit: asvāmyasaṃhataṃ vāpi bhinnakūṭaṃ tathaiva ca / duṣpārṣṇigrāhamarthañca balavyasanamucyate //
english: An ally suffering adverse fate, attacked by the enemy forces, having lust, rage etc. and energy would be considered as an enemy.

sanskrit: arthasya dūṣaṇaṃ krodhāt pāruṣyaṃ vākyadaṇḍayoḥ / kāmajaṃ mṛgayā dyūtaṃ vyasanaṃ pānakaṃ striyaḥ //
english: Lavish spending of money, inflicting harsh words and punishment on account of anger, due to lust, hunting, gambling, drinking and women are the vices of a king.

sanskrit: vākpāruṣyaṃ paraṃ loke udvejanamanarthakaṃ /
english: Harsh words create the estrangement in the world and havoc.

sanskrit: asiddhasādhanaṃ daṇḍastaṃ yuktyānayennṛpaḥ //
english: Punishment is a means to achieve things difficult to accomplish.

sanskrit: udvejayati bhūtāni daṇḍapāruṣyavān nṛpaḥ / bhūtānyudvejyamānāni dviṣatāṃ yānti saṃśrayaṃ //
english: A king should remove it with care. A king that inflicts punishment and harsh words would agitate the subjects. The agitated subjects resort to the enemy.

sanskrit: vivṛddhāḥ śatravaś caiva vināśāya bhavanti te /
english: Multiplication of enemies would be for your destruction.

sanskrit: dūṣyasya dūṣaṇārthañca parityāgo mahīyasaḥ // arthasya nītitattvajñair arthadūṣaṇamucyate /
english: A wasteful expenditure of wealth to a greater extent in order to defile one is said to be extravagance in spending by the learned in political science.

sanskrit: pānāt kāryādino jñānaṃ mṛgayāto 'ritaḥ kṣayaḥ // jitaśramārthaṃ mṛgayāṃ vicaredrakṣite vane /
english: By drinking one becomes ignorant, by hunting one gets destroyed by the enemy. One should wander in the forest that is guarded doing hunting in order to remove hardships due to victory.

sanskrit: dharmārthaprāṇamāśādi dyūte syāt kalahādikaṃ // kālātipāto dharmārthapī.rā strīvyasanādbhavet /
english: The destruction of virtues, wealth, life and quarrels etc. would be on account of gambling. Delay and affliction to virtue and wealth would result from the defect of association with women.

sanskrit: pānadoṣāt prāṇanāśaḥ kāryākāryāviniś cayaḥ // skandhāvāraniveśajño nimittajño ripuṃ jayet /
english: On account of the vice of drinking there would be destruction of life, indecision relating to things to be done and not to be done. One who knows the mode of laying the capital and the opportune moments would conquer the enemy.

sanskrit: skandhāvārasya madhye tu sakoṣaṃ nṛpatergṛhaṃ //
english: The dwelling of the king along with the treasury should be in the midst of the royal capital.

sanskrit: rājaharmyaṃ samāvṛtya krameṇa viniveśayet // sainyaikadeśaḥ sannaddhaḥ senāpatipuraḥsaraḥ / paribhrameccatvarāṃś ca maṇḍalena vahir niśi //
english: The artisans, friends, unhostile foresters and the main division of the army should be placed surrounding the royal dwelling. The army should be placed ready at a corner under the lead of the commander. They should roam about the quadrangular points in a circle during the nights.

sanskrit: vārtāḥ svakā vijānīyāddarasīmāntacāriṇaḥ /
english: Information relating to one’s self should be known through spies moving about the borders of the country.

sanskrit: nirgacchet praviśeccaiva sarva evopalakṣitaḥ // sāmadānaṃ ca bhedaś ca daṇḍopekṣendrajālakaṃ / māyopāyāḥ sapta pare nikṣipetsādhanāya tān //
english: All should leave and enter the city being noticed, The seven political expedients such as conciliation, gift, dissension, punishment indifference, conjuring and deceit should be instituted for accomplishing them.

sanskrit: caturvidhaṃ smṛtaṃ sāma upakārānukīrtanāt / mithaḥsambanhdakathanaṃ mṛdupūrvaṃ ca bhāṣaṇaṃ // āyāte darśanaṃ vācā tavāhamiti cārpaṇaṃ /
english: Conciliation is of four kinds such as the expression of gratitude, recollection of the relationship between one another, use of soft words and seeing and submission of the self with the words “ yours”, when the other person had come.

sanskrit: yaḥ samprāptadhanotsarga uttamādhamamadhyamaḥ //
english: The making of a gift of wealth to one that has come is of three kinds such as excellent, medium and inferior.

sanskrit: dravyadānamapūrvaṃ ca svayaṅgrāhapravartanaṃ // deyaś ca pratimokṣaś ca dānaṃ pañcavidhaṃ smṛtaṃ /
english: The making of a gift is of five kinds such as giving back the gift, accepting the gift received, making a novel gift, accepting a gift by his own choice, giving and returning.

sanskrit: sneharāgāpanayanasaṃharṣotpādanaṃ tathā // mitho bhedaś ca bhedajñair bhedaś ca trividhaḥ smṛtaḥ / badho 'rthaharaṇaṃ caiva parikleśastridhā damaḥ //
english: Dissension is of three kinds by experts knowing dissension such as destroying amity, creating a thrill of fear, inducing dissension between the two. Punishment is of three kinds such as killing, confiscating the property, and imposing hardship.

sanskrit: prakāśaścāprakāśaś ca lokadviṣṭān prakāśataḥ /
english: Punishment is also of two other kinds such as public and secret. The public enemies should be punished in public.

sanskrit: udvijeta hatair lokasteṣu piṇḍaḥ praśasyate // viśeṣeṇopaniṣidyogair hanyācchastrādinā dviṣaḥ /
english: In cases in which the people would get agitated by killing in public, killing by poisoning the food is commended. The enemies of the public should be killed by employing special black rites or with weapons etc.

sanskrit: jātimātraṃ dvijaṃ naiva hanyāt sāmottaraṃ vaśe //
english: A member of the brahmin community alone should not be killed even after being under control after conciliation.

sanskrit: pralimpanniva cetāṃsi dṛṣṭvāsādhu pibanniva / grasannivāmṛtaṃ sāma prayuñjīta priyaṃ vacaḥ //
english: A good person should do conciliation speaking sweet words as if besmearing the heart, looking at the person as if feasting and taking in his form as if ambrosia.

sanskrit: mithyābhiśastaḥ śrīkāma āhūyāpratimānitaḥ / rājadveṣī cātikara ātmasambhāvitas tathā // vicchinnadharmakāmārthaḥ kruddho mānī vimānitaḥ /
english: One duped with false hopes, desirous of getting wealth, one being invited and insulted, one having contempt for the king, one superseded in honour, one thinking much about his virtue, one whose virtue, desire and riches have been cut off, one that is angry, one having.

sanskrit: akāraṇāt parityaktaḥ kṛtavairo 'pi sāntvitaḥ // hṛtadravyakalatraś ca pūjārho 'pratipūjitaḥ / etāṃstu bhedayecchatrau sthitānnityān suśaṅkitān //
english: selfrespect, insulted, one rejected without any cause, appeased even though had enmity, one whose wealth and wife have been taken, one deserving to be honoured but not honoured and such men permanently remaining in the enemy camp and are to be suspected should be divided.

sanskrit: āgatān pūjayet kāmair nijāṃś ca praśamannayet /
english: A king should honour those that have come from the enemy side with presents and pacify those on his own side.

sanskrit: sāmadṛṣṭānusandhānamatyugrabhayadarśanaṃ // pradhānadānamānaṃ ca bhedopāyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
english: Winning affection by conciliatory measures, showing threats, and honouring and buying the allegiance of principal men are stated to be the means for dissension.

sanskrit: mitraṃ hataṃ kāṣṭhamiva ghuṇajagdhaṃ viśīryate //
english: One having a frustrated ally is ruined like the timber eaten by an insect.

sanskrit: triśaktirdeśakālajño daṇḍenāstaṃ nayedarīn /
english: A king possessing the three kinds of regal power and one who knows the proper place and time should subjugate his enemies by means of force.

sanskrit: maitrīpradhānaṃ kalyāṇabuddhiṃ sāntvena sādhayet // lubdhaṃ kṣīṇañca dānena mitrānanyonyaśaṅkayā /
english: The ruler of a neighbouring country who is favourably disposed should be pacified in the event of his being befriended by mighty allies. The greedy and poor should be won by making a gift.

sanskrit: daṇḍasya darśanādduṣṭān putrabhrātādi sāmataḥ //
english: The wicked should be won by threats of punishment and the sons, brothers and others by conciliatory measures.

sanskrit: dānabhedaiś camūmukhyān yodhān janapadadikān / sāmāntāṭavikān bhedadaṇḍābhyāmaparāddhakān //
english: The chieftains of the army, the warriors and the heads of provinces should be controlled, the vassals and foresters by making gifts and causing dissension among themselves.

sanskrit: devatāpratimānantu pūjayāntargatair naraiḥ / pumān strīvastrasaṃvīto niśi cādbhutadarśanaḥ // vetālolkāpiśācānāṃ śivānāṃ ca svarūpakī / kāmato rūpadhāritvaṃ śastrāgnyaśmāmbuvarṣaṇaṃ //
english: After having propitiated the images of gods the male should dress as the female and illusions should be made by men such as the forms of goblins, meteors, monsters and vixens, assuming the desired form, showering of weapons, fire, stones and water, and showing the divine phenomena such as darkness, wind, fire, and cloud.

sanskrit: jaghāna kīcakaṃ bhīma āsthitaḥ strīrūpatāṃ //
english: Bhīma one of the Pāṇḍavas killed Kīcaka son of king of Virāṭa assuming the form of a woman.

sanskrit: anyāye vyasane yuddhe pravṛttasyānivāraṇaṃ / upekṣeyaṃ smṛtā bhrātopekṣitaś ca hiḍimbayā //
english: It is said to be indifference when one does not dissuade another from unfair battle or plight just as Hiḍimbā the demoness that married Bhīma remained indifferent towards his brother when he was fighting with Bhīma.

sanskrit: meghāndhakāravṛṣṭyagniparvatādbhutadarśanaṃ / darasthānaṃ ca sainyānāṃ darśanaṃ dhvajaśālināṃ //
english: Indrajāla stratagem such as clouds, darkness, rain, fire, mountain, wonders, the banners of a large army causing fright and miragelike picture of being tom and spread should be shown in order to frighten the enemies.

sanskrit: itīndrajālaṃ dviṣatāmbhotyarthamupakalpayet //
english: These are the supreme position of the king, the strength of a good council and energy.

sanskrit: ṣaḍvidhantu balaṃ vyūhya devān prārcya ripuṃ vrajet /
english: After having worshipped gods and arranging six divisions of the army the king should march against the enemy.

sanskrit: maulaṃ bhūtaṃ śroṇisuhṛddviṣadāṭavikaṃ balaṃ //
english: The six divisions of the army are the central force, the front, the rear, the auxiliary, hostile and the pioneer.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ garīyastu balānāṃ vyasanaṃ tathā /
english: Each division of the above forces are more important than the succeeding ones. The same holds good in the case of reverses also.

sanskrit: ṣaḍaṅgaṃ mantrakoṣābhyāṃ padātyaśvarathadvipaiḥ // nadyadravanadurgeṣu yatra yatra bhayaṃ bhavet / senāpatistatra tatra gacchedvyūhīkṛtair balaiḥ //
english: The commanderinchief should go to such places as the rivers, mountains, forests and forts wherever there may be danger, with the a^y in array consisting of six divisions, machines, treasury, footsoldiers, cavalry, chariots and elephants.

sanskrit: nāyakaḥ purato yāyāt pravīrapuruṣāvṛtaḥ /
english: The leader of the forces should march at its head being surrounded by best warriors.

sanskrit: madhye kalatraṃ svāmī ca koṣaḥ phalgu ca yadbalaṃ //
english: The queen, king, treasury and the excellent warriors of the army should be placed in the middle.

sanskrit: pārśvayorubhayoraśvā vājināṃ pārśvayo rathāḥ / rathānāṃ pārśvayornāgā nāgānāṃ cāṭavībalaṃ //
english: The cavalrymen should be on the two sides, the chariots by the side of the cavalry and the elephants by the side of the chariots. The pioneer forces should be by the side of the elephants.

sanskrit: paścāt senāpatiḥ sarvaṃ puraskṛtya kṛtī svayaṃ / yāyātsannaddhasainyaughaḥ khinnānāśvāsayañcchanaiḥ //
english: Then the commanderinchief should go slowly behind all with a fully equipped army encouraging the dejected.

sanskrit: yāyādvyūhena mahatā makareṇa purobhaye / śyenenoddhṛtapakṣeṇa sūcyā vā vīravaktrayā //
english: A marching army should be set in the array of a crocodile and in the array of a hawk with raised wings or a sūcī or Vīravaktra in case of danger in the front.

sanskrit: paścādbhaye tu śakaṭaṃ pārśvayorvajrasañjñitaṃ /
