english: In case of fear behind, an array in the form of the cart should be made.

sanskrit: sarvataḥ sarvatobhadraṃ bhaye vyūhaṃ prakalpayet //
english: If there is danger on all sides one should set up the array known as sarvatobhadra.

sanskrit: kandare śailagahane nimnagāvanasaṅkaṭe /
english: A commander should guard his army while passing through a cave, mountain forest, river and dense forest.

sanskrit: dīrghādhvani pariśrāntaṃ kṣutpipāsāhitaklamaṃ // vyādhidurbhikṣamarakapīḍitaṃ dasyuvidrutaṃ /
english: He should also guard when the army has to go a long way, when it is tired, when it suffers hunger, thirst or adversity, when it is affected by illhealth, famine and epidemics, when attacked by robbers.

sanskrit: paṅkāṃśujalaskandhaṃ vyastaṃ puñjīkṛtaṃ pathi //
english: He should see that they are neither scattered nor gathered together on the way.

sanskrit: prasuptaṃ bhojanavyagramabhūmiṣṭhamasusthitaṃ / caurāgnibhayavitrastaṃ vṛṣṭivātasamāhataṃ // ityādau svacamūṃ rakṣet prasainyaṃ ca ghatayet /
english: He should also guard them while sleeping, eating their food, while staying at an unfit place, when they are not wellplaced, when they have been scared by robbers, fire and fear and when they have been struck by rains and wind.

sanskrit: viśiṣṭo deśakālābhyāṃ bhinnaviprakṛtirbalī //
english: When the army of the enemy is in a similar position it should be struck.

sanskrit: kuryāt prakāśayuddhaṃ hi kūṭayuddhaṃ viparyaye / teṣvavaskandakāleṣu paraṃ hanyātsamākulaṃ //
english: One should have an open encounter with an enemy only when the grounds and time are favourable and one is strong. On the contrary one should do treacherous warfare.

sanskrit: abhūmiṣṭhaṃ svabhūmiṣṭhaṃ svabhūmau copajāyataḥ /
english: An enemy on another’s soil could be won from staying in one’s own soil. An enemy in one’s own soil could be won by means of sowing seeds of dissension.

sanskrit: prakṛtipragrahākṛṣṭaṃ pāśair vanacarādibhiḥ // hanyāt pravīrapuruṣair bhaṅgadānāpakarṣaṇaiḥ /
english: An enemy subject to the wrath of his people should be made captive by employing the foresters and others and killed. They can also be conquered by employing extremely brave warriors.

sanskrit: purastāddarśanaṃ datvā tallakṣakṛtaniś cayāt // hanyātpaścāt pravīreṇa balenopetya veginā / paścādvā saṅkulīkṛtya hanyācchūreṇa pūrvataḥ //
english: By appearing in front of the enemy the king would become a sure object of their aim. Then the enemy should be killed by extremely brave warriors by striking swiftly with a strong force. Brave warriors could be set in an array in front or at the back and the enemy could be killed.

sanskrit: ābhyāṃ pārśvābhighātau tu vyākhyātau kūṭayodhane /
english: It has been explained by these two methods as to how to attack the two enemies on the adjacent sides in a treacherous warfare.

sanskrit: purastādviṣame deśe paścāddhanyāttu vegavān // puraḥ paścāttu viṣame evameva tu pārśvayoḥ /
english: If the front part of the hostile army is in an unfavourable land, the rear portion should be attacked swiftly. If the front and rear are both unfavourable one should strike on the sides in the same way.

sanskrit: prathamaṃ yodhayitvā tu dūṣyāmitrāṭavībalau // śrāntaṃ mandannirākrandaṃ hanyādaśrāntavāhanaṃ /
english: After having fought with the vanguards, allies of the enemy and the pioneers, one should attack the fatigued, slow and the one whose aid has been cut off without causing fatigue for his force.

sanskrit: dūṣyāmitrabalair vāpi bhaṅgandatvā prayatnavān //
english: In the alternative, one should defeat by employing the pioneer force or the allies.

sanskrit: jitamityeva viśvastaṃ hanyānmantravyapāśrayaḥ /
english: Or, one should feign defeat and attack the enemy that is complacent that he has won by resorting to good counsel.

sanskrit: skandhāvārapuragrāmaśasyasvāmiprajādiṣu // viśrabhyantaṃ parānīkamapramatto vināśayet /
english: One should destroy the enemy force when it is resting in the camps, barracks, villages, fields and among subjects without protection.

sanskrit: athavā gograhākṛṣṭaṃ tallakṣyaṃ mārgabandhanāt //
english: Otherwise the cattle of the enemy should be seized and then the army on their way to reach the goal.

sanskrit: avaskandabhayādrātripūjāgarakṛtaśramaḥ / divāsuptaṃ samāhanyānnidrāvyākulasainikaṃ //
english: Or the hostile army fatigued on account of overnight vigil fearing an attack and sleeping during the day overcome by sleep should be attacked to gain victory.

sanskrit: niśi viśrabdhasaṃsuptaṃ nāgair vā khaḍgapāṇibhiḥ /
english: In the alternative a hostile army sleeping during the night without any fear should be attacked by employing elephants or with men armed with swords.

sanskrit: prayāne pūrvayāyitvaṃ vanadurgapraveśanaṃ // abhinnānāmanīkānāṃ bhedanaṃ bhinnasaṅgrahaḥ / vibhīṣakādvāraghātaṃ koṣarakṣebhakarma ca //
english: The functions of men on elephants are proceeding in front of the marching army, entry into forest fortification, division of the united hostile army, collecting together a divided army, causing right, breaking the doors of the fort and the protection of the treasury.

sanskrit: abhinnabhedanaṃ mitrasandhānaṃ rathakarma ca /
english: Division of an undivided army and effecting the union of friendly forces are the task of the men on chariots.

sanskrit: vanadiṅmārgavicaye vīvadhāsāralakṣaṇaṃ // anuyānāpasaraṇe śīghrakāryopapādanaṃ / dīnānusaraṇaṃ ghātaḥ koṭīnāṃ jaghanasya ca //
english: The functions of cavalry are to reconnoitre the forests, different directions and the highway, guard the transport of provisions, follow the retreating army, attend to tasks requiring quick action, follow the weak and attack the last columns and rear of the hostile army.

sanskrit: aśvakarmātha patteś ca sarvadā śastradhāraṇaṃ /
english: The functions of infantry are to bear always the weapons, inspecting the camps and the highways and to remove obstructions.

sanskrit: saṃsthūlasthāṇuvalmīkavṛkṣagulmāpakaṇṭakaṃ / sāpasārā padātīnāṃ bhūrnātiviṣamā matā // svalpavṛkṣopalā kṣipralaṅghanīyanagā sthirā / niḥśarkarā vipaṅkā ca sāpasārā ca vājibhūḥ //
english: The ground suitable for infantry should not be very uneven or abound with thick rows of trees, ant hills, bushes and thorns and should have provision for escape. The ground suitable for cavalry should have scanty trees, should be quickly traversible, firm, without sand and not be marshy and have provision for escape.

sanskrit: nisthāṇuvṛkṣakedārā rathabhūmirakardamā / mardanīyatarucchedyavratatīpaṅkavarjitā //
english: The ground suitable for the chariot should not have trees, fields, mire, trees causing obstruction, creepers and mire.

sanskrit: urasyādīni bhinnāni pratigṛhṇan balāni hi //
english: The ground for the elephant are hills difficult to cross having streams.

sanskrit: pratigraha iti khyāto rājakāryāntarakṣamaḥ /
english: It is known as the rear of the army. It is capable of serving the needs of the king.

sanskrit: tena śūnyastu yo vyūhaḥ sa bhinna iva lakṣyate //
english: An array not having this the division would appear as if it has been segmented.

sanskrit: jayārthī na ca yuddhyeta matimānapratigrahaḥ /
english: A wise king desiring to conquer should not fight without having the array with the divisions.

sanskrit: yatra rājā tatra koṣaḥ koṣādhīnā hi rājatā //
english: The treasury would remain with the king. A kingship would be suzerainty over the treasure.

sanskrit: yodhebhyastu tato dadyāt kiñciddātuṃ na yujyate /
english: The soldiers should be paid rewards on gaining victory. It is not proper to give only a little.

sanskrit: dravyalakṣaṃ rājaghāte tadardhaṃ tatsutārdane //
english: A lakh should be given on the death of the enemy king and half that when the son of that king is killed.

sanskrit: senāpatibadhe tadvaddadyāddhastyādimardane / athavā khalu yudhyeran pratyaśvarathadantinaḥ // yathā bhavedasaṃbādho vyāyāmavinivartane /
english: Similarly the soldiers should be paid when the enemy commanderinchief is killed or at the killing of the elephant etc. Otherwise the soldiers should fight in such a way that the infantry, cavalry, men on chariots and elephants do not get affected when the battle has been completed.

sanskrit: asaṅkareṇa yuddheran saṅkaraḥ saṅkulāvahaḥ //
english: The soldiers should fight without confusion. Confusion causes melee.

sanskrit: mahāsaṅkulayuddheṣu saṃśrayeranmataṅgajaṃ /
english: One should employ an elephant in battles causing great confusion.

sanskrit: aśvasya pratiyoddhāro bhaveyuḥ puruṣāstrayaḥ // iti kalpyāstrayaścāśvā vidheyāḥ kuñjarasya tu /
english: Three infantry soldiers would be equal to fight a cavalryman. Three such cavalrymen should be employed to combat a single elephant man.

sanskrit: pādagopā bhaveyuś ca puruṣā daśa pañca ca //
english: Fifteen infantry men would guard each foot of the elephant.

sanskrit: vidhānamiti nāgasya vihitaṃ syandanasya ca / anīkamiti vijñeyamiti kalpyā nava dvipāḥ //
english: It is laid down that an arrangement known as an anika a unit of the elephants should be made for guarding the chariot. There should be nine elephant men.

sanskrit: tathānīkasya randhrantu pañcadhā ca pracakṣate /
english: The vulnerable point of such an army is said to be of five kinds.

sanskrit: ityanīkavibhagena sthāpayed vyūhasampadaḥ //
english: An array should be set by this division of the army.

sanskrit: uraḥkakṣau ca pakṣau ca madhyaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ pratigrahaḥ // koṭī ca vyūhaśāstrajñaiḥ saptāṅgo vyūha ucyate /
english: The chest, sides and wings are said to be three divisions. An array is said to have seven parts such as the chest, sides, wings, centre, back hip, rear and the edge by those well acquainted with the arrangement of arrays.

sanskrit: urasyakakṣapakṣāstu vyūho 'yaṃ sapratigrahaḥ // guroreṣa ca śukrasya kakṣābhyāṃ parivarjitaḥ /
english: The array called guru consists of chest, sides and wings together with the rear. That of śukra is devoid of two sides.

sanskrit: tiṣṭheyuḥ senāpatayaḥ pravīraiḥ puruṣair vṛtāḥ //
english: The commanders should remain being surrounded by excellent warriors.

sanskrit: abhedena ca yudhyeran rakṣeyuś ca parasparaṃ /
english: They should fight without any faction defending one another.

sanskrit: madhyavyūhe phalgu sainyaṃ yuddhavastu jaghanyataḥ //
english: Excellent warriors of the army should be at the centre.

sanskrit: yuddhaṃ hi nāyakaprāṇaṃ hanyate tadanāyakaṃ /
english: A commander of an army is the life of a battle. It would be destroyed if it is without a commander.

sanskrit: urasi sthāpayennāgān pracaṇḍān kakṣayo rathān //
english: The powerful elephants should be placed at the chest of an array, the chariots on the sides and horses on the wings.

sanskrit: hayāṃś ca pakṣayorvyūho madhyabhedī prakīrtitaḥ /
english: This array is said to be breaking the central force.

sanskrit: madhyadeśe hayānīkaṃ rathānīkañca kakṣayoḥ // pakṣayoś ca gajānīkaṃ vyūhontarbhedyayaṃ smṛtaḥ /
english: An army of horses at the centre, an army of chariots on the sides and an army of elephants on the wings is known to be an array of breaking the inner force.

sanskrit: rathasthāne hayān dadyāt padātīṃś ca hayaśrāye // rathābhāve tu dviradān vyūhe sarvatra dāpayet /
english: Station the cavalry in the place of chariots, the infantry in the place of cavalry in the above order or place elephants everywhere in the array in the absence of chariots.

sanskrit: yadi syāddaṇḍabāhulyamābādhaḥ samprakīrtitaḥ // maṇḍalāṃsaṃhato bhogo daṇḍāste bahudhā śṛṇu /
english: If there is more than the required army it is said to be ābādha. An array called bhoga consists of arranging the army in concentric circles. An array called daṇḍa is of many kinds.

sanskrit: tiryagvṛttistu daṇḍaḥ syād bhogo 'nyāvṛttireva ca //
english: An array spread horizontally would be called daṇḍa. The array called bhoga is in the form of a wave.

sanskrit: maṇḍalaḥ sarvatovṛttiḥ pṛthagvṛttirasaṃhataḥ /
english: The array called maṇḍala would be in perfect circle. The asaṃhata class would be in concentric circles.

sanskrit: pradaro dṛḍhako 'sahyaḥ cāpo vai kukṣireva ca // pratiṣṭhaḥ supratiṣṭhaś ca śyeno vijayasañjayau / viśālo vijayaḥ śūcī sthūṇākarṇacamūmukhau //
english: The other arrays such as the pradara, dṛḍhaka, asahya, cāpa, kukṣi, pratiṣṭha, supratiṣṭha, śyena, vijaya, sañjaya, viśāla, vijaya, sūcī, sthūṇākarṇa, camūmukha, sarpāsya and valaya are all invincible and modifications of the array called daṇḍa.

sanskrit: atikrāntaḥ pratikrāntaḥ kakṣābhyāñcaikakṣapakṣataḥ // atikrāntastu pakṣābhyāṃ trayo 'nye tadviparyaye /
english: They have the following characteristicsextending on both sides, extending on one side, extending in one wing, extending on both wings, three others of the contrary nature.

sanskrit: pakṣorasyair atikrāntaḥ pratiṣṭho 'nyo viparyayaḥ //
english: The array pratiṣṭha extends on the wing and chest and the other supratiṣṭha is the contrary.

sanskrit: sthūṇāpakṣo dhanuḥpakṣo dvisthūṇo daṇḍa ūrdhvagaḥ / dviguṇontastvatikrāntapakṣo 'nyasya viparyayaḥ //
english: The arrays called sthūṇāpakṣa and dhanuḥ pakṣa, dvisthūṇa and daṇḍa after that are of doubled units at the end or an additional wing or of the reverse of another.

sanskrit: dvicaturdaṇḍa ity ete jñeyā lakṣaṇataḥ kramāt /
english: They should be known to have the characteristics of two or four columns of soldiers in order.

sanskrit: gomūtrikāhisañcārīśakaṭo makaras tathā // bhogabhedāḥ samākhyātās tathā pariplavaṅgakaḥ /
english: The arrays known as gomūtrikā, ahisañcārī, śakaṭa and makara are said to be variations of the array bhoga. So also the array called pāriplavaṅgaka.

sanskrit: daṇḍapakṣau yugārasyaḥ śakaṭastadviparyaye //
english: The array called yugorasya consists of two wings in the array daṇḍa.

sanskrit: makaro vyatikīrṇaś ca śeṣaḥ kuñjararājibhiḥ /
english: The array of the name crocodile is of mixed nature. The array śeṣa is marked by the rows of elephants.

sanskrit: maṇḍalavyūhabhedau tu sarvatobhadradurjayau //
english: The arrays sarvatobhadra and duryaya are the modifications of the array called maṇḍala.

sanskrit: aṣṭānīko dvitīyastu prathamaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ /
english: That which has openings on all sides is the first one and that having the eight army units is the second one.

sanskrit: ardhacandraka ūrdhvāṅgo vajrabhedāstu saṃhateḥ //
english: The arrays known as ardhacandraka of the shape of half the moon and ūrdhvāṅga elevated parts are formed by the combinations of different divisions of the class known as the vajra.

sanskrit: tathā karkaṭaśṛṅgī ca kākapādau ca godhikā / tricatuḥsainyānāṃ jñeyā ākārabhedataḥ //
english: In the same way the arrays known as karkaśṛṅgī the pincers of a crab, kākapāda the feet of a crow and godhikā lizard are known from their difference in shape consisting of three, four and five units of army.

sanskrit: daṇḍasya syuḥ saptadaśa vyūhā dvau maṇḍalasya ca / asaṅghātasya ṣaṭ pañca bhogasyaiva tu saṅgare //
english: Seventeen kinds of arrays could be formed from the array called daṇḍa. Two from the maṇḍala class, six from the asaṅghāta and five from the bhoga are combined in a battle.

sanskrit: pakṣādīnāmathaikena hatvā śeṣaiḥ parikṣipet / urasā vā samāhatya koṭibhyāṃ pariveṣṭayet //
english: The structures of the abovesaid battle arrays may be modified by omitting a wing or two wings. Otherwise a squadron may be taken from the chest of the army and placed around the edges.

sanskrit: pare koṭī samākramya pakṣābhyāmapratigrahāt / koṭibhyāñjaghanaṃ hanyādurasā ca prapīḍayet //
english: After having attacked the boundary army in the front with the army forming the wings, one should strike the army at the hip with the army at the boundaries and attack with that comprising the chest.

sanskrit: tataścāribalaṃ hanyādātmanaścopavṛṃhayet //
english: The routed soldiers of a hostile army as well as the reserves should be completely destroyed and one’s own should be expanded.

sanskrit: sāraṃ dviguṇasāreṇa phalgusāreṇa pīḍayet /
english: The main part of the hostile army should be attacked with double that of the main and the reserve force of the hostile army with the main.

sanskrit: saṃhatañca gajānīkaiḥ pracaṇḍair dārayedbalaṃ //
english: A compact hostile army should be scattered with a strong contingent of elephants.

sanskrit: syāt kakṣapakṣorasyaś ca vartamānastu daṇḍakaḥ / tatra prayogo ḍaṇḍasya sthānanturyeṇa darśayet //
english: If the hostile army is in the array daṇḍaka with the flanks, wings and chest drawn up then a general should employ the array daṇḍa and quickly show the position.

sanskrit: syāddaṇḍasamapakṣābhyāmatikrānto dṛḍhaḥ smṛtaḥ / bhavetsa pakṣakakṣābhyāmatikrāntaḥ pradārakaḥ //
english: The array called pradāraka would be by the addition of two wings to the daṇḍa. If it is added with wings and flanks it is known as dṛḍha. The array that is increased by adding two flanks is known to be asahya.

sanskrit: kakṣapakṣāvadhaḥ sthapyorasyaiḥ kāntaś ca khātakaḥ //
english: The array khātaka consists of keeping the flanks and wings down and attacking with the troops at the chest.

sanskrit: dvau daṇḍau balayaḥ prokto kāntaś ca khātakaḥ /
english: The array valaya is said to be the union of two daṇḍas capable of breaking the enemy.

sanskrit: durjayaś caturvalayaḥ śatrorbalavimardanaḥ //
english: The array durjaya consists of four valayas that is capable of routing the enemy forces.

sanskrit: kakṣapakṣaurasyair bhogo viṣayaṃ parivartayan / sarpacārī gomūtrikā śarkaṭaḥ śakaṭākṛtiḥ //
english: By changing the arrangement of elements troops on the flanks, wings and chest of the array bhoga we get the arrays sarpacārī and gomūtrikā. The array śakaṭa is of the shape of a cart.

sanskrit: viparyayo 'maraḥ proktaḥ sarvaśatruvimardakaḥ /
english: The reverse is said to be the array amara capable of destroying the enemies.

sanskrit: syāt kakṣapakṣorasyānāmekībhāvastu maṇḍalaḥ //
english: The arrangement of troops on the sides, wings and chest would be in the same way as the array maṇḍala.

sanskrit: cakrapadmādayo bhedā maṇḍalasya prabhedakāḥ /
english: The divisions called cakra, padma and others are variations of the maṇḍala.

sanskrit: evañca sarvatobhadro vajrākṣavarakākavat // ardhacandraś ca śṛṅgāṭo hy acalo nāmarūpataḥ / vyūhā yathāsukhaṃ karyāḥ śatrūṇāṃ balavāraṇāḥ //
english: In the same way the arrays sarvatobhadra, the excellent vajrākṣa, the crowshaped one, the half moon, śṛṅgāṭaka resembling the junction of four roads and .acala of the forms corresponding to their names should be formed according to one’s convenience that would prevent the enemy forces.

sanskrit: rāmastu rāvaṇaṃ hatvā ayodhyāṃ prāptavān dvija / rāmoktanītyendrajitaṃ hatavāṃllakṣmaṇaḥ purā //
english: O Brahmin! Rāma reached Ayodhyā after killing the demon Rāvaṇa. Lakṣmaṇa brother of Rāma killed Indrajit son of Rāvaṇa in days of yore by means of statesmanship narrated by Rāma.

sanskrit: rāmoktoktā mayā nītiḥ strīṇāṃ rājan nṛṇāṃ vade /
english: O King! Ethics were described by me to Rāma.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇaṃ yadsamudreṇa gargāyoktaṃ yathā purā //
english: shall now describe the characteristics of men and women as described by Samudra to sage Garga formerly.

sanskrit: puṃsāñca lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye strīṇāñcaiva śubhāśubhaṃ /
english: shall describe the good and bad characteristics of men and women.

sanskrit: ekādhiko dviśukraś ca triganbhīrastathaiva ca // tritrikastripralambaś ca tribhirvyāpnoti yas tathā / tribalīmāṃstrivinatastrikālajñaś ca suvrata // puruṣaḥ syātsulakṣaṇyo vipulaś ca tathā triṣu /
english: O Virtuous one! A man having the signs and features symbolised by the terms ekādhika, dviśukla two whites, trigambhīra three depths, tritrika three triads or nine virtues, tripralamba three elongated organs, a spreading in three, threefolds of skins, trivinata having bends at three places, trikālajña knowing the three periods of time and trivipula broad organs at three places would be possessing good characteristics.

sanskrit: caturlekhas tathā yaś ca tathaiva ca catuḥsamaḥ // catuṣkiṣkuś caturdaṃṣṭraḥ śuklakṛṣṇastathaiva ca / caturgandhaś caturhrasvaḥ sūkṣmadīrghaś ca pañcasu // ṣaḍunnato 'ṣṭavaṃśaś ca saptasneho navāmalaḥ / daśapadmo daśavyūho nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalaḥ //
english: Similarly, one possessing four marks on four different parts of the body, or four equal parts of the body, or cubits four frontal teeth of commendable size, dark complexion of four, in four parts of the body, sweet smells at the four joints of the body and four specific organs of short stature, five parts of the body small and long, six parts raised, eight bones strong, seven parts glossy, nine parts clean, nine parts like the lotus, ten parts like an array and of the form of the fig tree, fourteen pairs of parts equal and sixteen eyes is commended.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmasaṃyukto dharmo hy ekādhiko mataḥ //
english: The term ekādhika stands for virtue together with the goals of life righteousness, attainment of riches and pleasures.

sanskrit: tārakābhyāṃ vinā netre śukradanto dviśuklakaḥ /
english: The term dviśukla signifies the whiteness of teeth and the eyes except the two pupils.

sanskrit: gambhīrastriśravo nābhiḥ sattvañcaikaṃ trikaṃ smṛtaṃ // anasūyā dayā kṣāntirmaṅgalācārayuktatā / śaucaṃ spṛhā tvakārpaṇyamanāyāsaś ca śauryatā //
english: The term trigambhīra denotes depth in the ear and navel and the term tritrika the virtues of absence of envy, compassion, forbearance, endowed with auspicious deeds, purity, desire, liberality, ease and valour known as one triad of virtue.

sanskrit: citrikastripralambaḥ syādvṛṣaṇe bhujayornaraḥ /
english: The term tripralamba denotes a person that would have the testicles and arms long.

sanskrit: digdeśajātivargāṃś ca tejasā yaśasā śriyā // vyāpnoti yastrikavyāpī tribalīmānnarastvasau /
english: One who has spread by his radiance, fame and fortune on the quarters, country and his own class is said to be trikavyāpī. A person that has three folds on the belly is said to be trivalimān.

sanskrit: udare balayastisro narantrivinataṃ śṛṇu //
english: Listen to me. shall describe the man having three bends.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ dvijānāñca gurūṇāṃ praṇatastu yaḥ / dharmārthakāmakālajñastrikālajño 'bhidhīyate //
english: He is the person that bows to the gods, brahmins and preceptors. One who knows the suitable time for the practice of virtues, attainment of riches and pleasure is said to be the knower of three periods.

sanskrit: uro lalāṭaṃ vaktrañca trivistīrṇo vilekhavān /
english: One who has a broad chest, forehead and face is said to be trivistīrṇa.

sanskrit: dvau pāṇī dvau tathā pādau dhvajacchatrādibhiryutau //
english: The two hands and two feet bearing the marks of banners, umbrellas etc.

sanskrit: aṅgulyo hṛdayaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ kaṭiḥ śastaṃ catuḥsamaṃ / ṣaṇṇavatyaṅgulotsedhaś catuṣkiṣkupramāṇataḥ //
english: The fingers, chest, back and hip that are equal are commendable. The commendable height of the human figure is four cubits. Four frontal teeth having moonlike lustre is meant by caturdaṃṣṭraḥ .

sanskrit: draṃṣṭrāś catasraś candrābhāś catuḥkṛṣṇaṃ vadāmi te / netratārau bhruvau śmaśruḥ kṛṣṇāḥ keśāstathaiva ca //
english: shall describe the four black things. The two pupils of the eyes, the two eyebrows, the beard and hair are the four black things.

sanskrit: nāsāyāṃ vadane svede kakṣayorviḍagandhakaḥ /
english: The absence of bad smell in the nostril, mouth, perspiration and armpits is caturgandha.

sanskrit: hrasvaṃ liṅgaṃ tathā grīvā jaṅghe syādvedahrasvakaṃ // sūkṣmāṇyaṅguliparvāṇi nakhakeśadvijatvacaḥ / hanū netre lalāṭe ca nāsā dīrghā stanāntaraṃ //
english: The four short things are short penis, neck and the two shanks. The fingerjoints nails, hair on the head, teeth and skin are the five minute, parts. The two cheeks, two eyes, forehead, nose and the space between the breasts are the five long parts.

sanskrit: vakṣaḥ kakṣau nakhā nāsonnataṃ vaktraṃ kṛkāṭikā /
english: The chest, shoulders, nails, nose, face and the back of neck are the six parts.

sanskrit: snigdhāstvakkeśadantāś ca loma dṛṣṭirnakhāś ca vāk //
english: The seven parts that are glossy are the skin, hair on the head, teeth, hair on the body, one’s sight nails and speech.

sanskrit: jānvorurvoś ca pṛṣṭhastha vaṃśau dvau karanāsayoḥ / netre nāsāpuṭau karṇau meḍhraṃ pāyumukhe 'malaṃ //
english: The eight bones that are strong are those in the two knees, two thighs, back, bones of the hand and nose. The nine parts that are clean are the two eyes, two nostrils, two ears, penis, anus and face.

sanskrit: śiśnāgravaktraṃ śasyante padmābhā daśa dehināṃ // pāṇipādaṃ mukhaṃ grīvā śravaṇe hṛdayaṃ śiraḥ / lalāṭamudaraṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ vṛhantaḥ pūjitā daśa //
english: The ten parts of the body of men of the lustre of a lotus that are commended are the tongue, two lips, palate, eyes, hands, feet, nails, tip of the penis and face. The hand, foot, face, neck, two ears, heart, head, forehead, belly and back, the ten that are broad like an array are praiseworthy.

sanskrit: prasāritabhujasyeha madhyamāgradvayāntaraṃ / ucchrāyeṇa samaṃ yasya nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalaḥ //
english: One is said to be of the form of a fig tree if the interspace between the two middle and index fingers of the extended arms is equal to the height.

sanskrit: pādau gulphau sphicau pārśvau vaṅkṣaṇau vṛṣaṇau kucau / karṇauṣṭhe sakthinī jaṅghe hastau bāhū tathākṣiṇī //
english: The two feet, ankles, buttocks, sides, groins, testicles, breasts,ears, lips, thighs, shanks, hands, forearms and eyes are the pairs of fourteen organs that are equal in general for a man.

sanskrit: vidyāś caturdaśa dvyakṣaiḥ paśyedyaḥ ṣoḍaśākṣakaḥ //
english: One that sees with the fourteen branches of learning and the two eyes is said to be having sixteen eyes.

sanskrit: rūkṣaṃ śirātataṃ gātramaśubhaṃ māṃsavarjitaṃ / durgandhiviparītaṃ yacchastandṛṣṭyā prasannayā //
english: One with extremely dry body with exposed veins and emaciated, smelling badly is deemed to be unfortunate. The person with contrary characteristics and pleasing look is commendable.

sanskrit: dhanyasya madhurā vāṇī gatirmattebhasannibhā / ekakūpabhavaṃ roma bhaye rakṣā sakṛt sakṛt //
english: The voice of a lucky man is sweet. His gait resembles that of an elephant in rut. He has two hairs from the same root. It gives protection from fear at once.

sanskrit: śastā strī cārusarvāṅgī mattamātaṅgagāminī / gurūrujaghanā yā ca mattapārāvatekṣaṇā // sunīlakeśī tanvaṅgī vilomāṅgī manoharā / samabhūmispṛśau pādau saṃhatau ca tathā stanau //
english: A woman that is beautiful in all her limbs, having the gait of an elephant in rut, having heavy thighs and hips and possessing a look like that of a longing pigeon is commendable. One that is having luxurious dark hair, slim, not having hairs on the body, beautiful, feet touching the ground evenly, and having a pair of breasts closely pressing each other is also deemed to be lucky.

sanskrit: nābhiḥ pradakṣiṇāvartā guhyamaśvatthapatravat / gulphau nigūḍhau madhyena nābhiraṅguṣṭhamānikā //
english: The navel spiralling right to left, the private organ resembling the leaf of the fig tree, ankles having a dip in the middle and the dip in the navel is of the measure of the head of a thumb are also commendable.

sanskrit: jaṭharanna pralambañca romarūkṣā na śobhanā /
english: One that is not having an elongated abdomen is also praiseworthy. One whose hairs are not soft is not good.

sanskrit: narkṣavṛkṣanadīnāmnī na sadā kalahapriyā // na lolupā na durbhāṣā śubhā devādipūjitā /
english: One that is not having the name of an asterism, tree and river, one that is not fond of quarrels, one that is not greedy and one that does not speak harsh is auspicious and is honoured by the celestials.

sanskrit: gaṇḍair madhūkapuṣpābhair na śirālā na lomaśā // na saṃhatabhrūkuṭilā patiprāṇā patipriyā /
english: One that is having her cheeks of the colour of the madhūka flower, one that is not having the body as sinewy and abound with hairs, not having the eyebrows dose to one another is also commended.

sanskrit: alakṣaṇāpi lakṣaṇyā yatrākārāstato guṇāḥ //
english: If the quality of attraction is present other qualities would also be present.

sanskrit: bhuvaṅkaniṣṭhikā yasyā na spṛśenmṛtyureva sā //7//
english: One whose little toe does not touch the earth is verily the death itself.

sanskrit: cāmaro rukmādaṇḍo 'gryaḥ chatraṃ rājñaḥ praśasyate / haṃsapakṣair viracitaṃ mayūrasya śukasya ca //
english: The handle of the royal fan should be of gold. The royal umbrella made of the feathers of haṃsa, peacock, parrot or the feathers of crane is praised.

sanskrit: pakṣair vātha balākāyā na kāryaṃ miśrapakṣakaiḥ /
english: It should not be made with mixed feathers,.

sanskrit: caturasyaṃ brāhmaṇasya vṛttaṃ rājñaś ca śuklakaṃ //
english: An umbrella of a brahmin should be of square shape and that of a king should be circular and white.

sanskrit: tricatuḥpañcaṣaṭsaptāṣṭaparvaś ca daṇḍakaḥ /
english: There should be three, four, five, six, seven or eight joints on the handle of umbrella.

sanskrit: bhadrāsanaṃ kṣīravṛkṣaiḥ pañcāśadaṅgulocchrayaiḥ //
english: The auspicious seat of the king should be made with the wood of the kṣīra trees of fifty inches long.

sanskrit: vistāreṇa trihastaṃ syāt suvarṇādyaiś ca citritaṃ / dhanurdravyatrayaṃ lohaṃ śṛṅgaṃ dāru dvijottama //
english: Its breadth should be three cubits and decorated with gold and other things. O Excellent brahmin! The bow is made of three materials iron, horn or wood. The three materials for the bowstring are the bamboo fibre, hide and wood.

sanskrit: dārucāpapramāṇantu śreṣṭhaṃ hastacatuṣṭayaṃ //
english: Four cubits would be the excellent measure of a bow.

sanskrit: tadeva samahīnantu proktaṃ madhyakanīyasi /
english: It is said to be mediocre if equal and inferior if less than that.

sanskrit: muṣṭigrāhanimittāni madhye dravyāṇi kārayet // svalpakoṭistvacā śṛṅgaṃ śārṅgalohamaye dvija /
english: Materials should be added at the middle part for the sake of the grip of the fist. O Brahmin! the tip of the bow made of horns or iron should be having minute edge covered by hides.

sanskrit: kāminībhrūlatākārā koṭiḥ kāryā susaṃyutā //
english: The edge should be like the creeper, like the eyebrow of a beautiful damsel and should be fastened well.

sanskrit: pṛthagvā vipra miśraṃ vā lauhaṃ śārṅgantu kārayet /
english: O Brahmin! One should make the bow separately made of the horn or iron or the two mixed.

sanskrit: śārṅgaṃ samucitaṃ kāryaṃ rukmavinduvibhūṣitaṃ //
english: A good bow should suitably be decorated with particles of gold.

sanskrit: kuṭilaṃ sphuṭitañcāpaṃ sacchidrañca na śasyate /
english: A bow that is crooked, broken and with incisions is not commended.

sanskrit: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ kṛṣṇāyo dhanuṣi smṛtaṃ //
english: Gold, silver, copper and black iron are remembered to be the materials in making a bow.

sanskrit: māhiṣaṃ śārabhaṃ śārṅgaṃ rauhiṣaṃ vā dhanuḥ śubhaṃ /
english: A bow made of horns of a buffalo, a śarabha a fabulous animal or rohiṣa a kind of deer are auspicious.

sanskrit: candanaṃ vetasaṃ sālaṃ dhāvalaṅkakubhantaruḥ //
english: A bow made of sandal, cane, sāla, dhavala and kakubha trees are good.

sanskrit: sarvaśreṣṭhaṃ dhanurvaṃśair gṛhītaiḥ śaradi śritaiḥ / pūjayettu dhanuḥ khaḍgamantraistrailokyamohanaiḥ //
english: The most excellent bow is that made of bamboos cut and collected in the autumn. The bow should be worshipped with the sacred syllables called trailokyamohana captivating the three worlds used for the swords.

sanskrit: ayasaścātha vaṃśasya śarasyāpyaśarasya ca /
english: The arrows may be made of iron, bamboo or reeds.

sanskrit: ṛtvijo hemavārṇābhāḥ snāyuśliṣṭāḥ supatrakāḥ // rukmapuṅkhāḥ supaṅkāste tailadhautāḥ suvarṇakāḥ /
english: They should be straight and goldcoloured and bound by sinews. They should have good feathers. They should have gold feathers that are good. They should be cleaned with oil and be of good colour.

sanskrit: yātrāyāmabhiṣekādau yajedvāṇadhanurmukhān // sapatākāstrasaṅgrāhasāṃvatsarakarānnṛpaḥ /
english: One should worship weapons, bows and other things before starting an expedition or the royal consecration. The king should also worship those carrying banners and weapons and the astrologers.

sanskrit: brahmā vai meruśikhare svargagaṅgātaṭe 'yajat //
english: Lord Brahmā performed a sacrifice on the banks of celestial Ganges on the peaks of the Meru mountain.

sanskrit: lauhadaityaṃ sa dadṛśe vidhnaṃ yajñe tu cintayan /
english: When he was contemplating at the sacrifice he saw the demon Loha that causes obstruction.

sanskrit: tasya cintayato vahneḥ puruṣo 'bhūdvalī mahān //
english: As he was thinking about that, a great mighty form appeared from the fire in front of him.

sanskrit: vavande 'jañca tandevā abhyanandanta harṣitāḥ /
english: He bowed down to the lord Brahmā and the celestials greeted him with joy.

sanskrit: tasmātsa nandakaḥ kaḍgo devokto hariragrahīt // taṃ jagrāha śanair devo vikoṣaḥ so 'bhyapadyata /
english: Lord Hari took the sword called Nandaka from the demon as requested by the celestials. The lord seized it slowly and it became unsheathed.

sanskrit: khaḍgo nīlo ratnamuṣṭistato 'bhūcchatabāhukaḥ //
english: The sword was blue in colour with gem studded handle.

sanskrit: daityaḥ sa gadayā devān drāvayāmāsa vai raṇe /
english: That demon made the celestials run away in the battlefield by means of the mace.

sanskrit: viṣṇunā khaḍgacchinnāni daityagātrāṇi bhūtale // patitāni tu saṃsparśānnandakasya ca tāni hi / lohabhūtāni sarvāṇi hatvā tasmai harirvaraṃ //
english: The body of the demon was cut by lord Hari with the sword and the parts of the body fell on the earth and all of them became pieces of iron on account of their contact with the sword Nandaka.

sanskrit: dadau pavitramaṅgante āyudhāya bhavedbhuvi /
english: After having killed him lord Hari gave him a boon saying “Your holy body would become the material for weapons on the earth”.

sanskrit: hariprasādād brahmāpi vinā vighnaṃ hariṃ prabhuṃ //
english: On account of the grace of lord Hari, Brahmā also worshipped lord Hari with the sacrifice without obstruction.

sanskrit: pūjayāmāsa yajñena vakṣye 'tho khaḍgalakṣaṇaṃ /
english: Then shall describe the characteristics of a sword.

sanskrit: khaṭīkhaṭṭarajātā ye daśanīyāstute smṛtāḥ //
english: Swords that are produced at the places Khaṭī and Khaṭṭara are known to be worthy of being seen.

sanskrit: kāyacchidastvāṣikāḥ syurdṛḍhāḥ sūrpārakodbhavāḥ /
english: Those belonging to the region called ‘Ṛṣi’ would be capable of cutting the body. Those produced from Sūrpāraka would be strong.

sanskrit: tīkṣṇāśchedasahā vaṅgāstīkṣṇāḥ syuścāṅgadeśajāḥ //
english: Those got from Vaṅga are sharp and capable of cutting. Those produced from the country Aṅga are sharp.

sanskrit: śatārdhamaṅgulānāñca śreṣṭhaṃ khadgaṃ prakīrtitaṃ /
english: Sword of the length of fifty inches is said to be excellent.

sanskrit: tadardhaṃ madhyamaṃ jñeyaṃ tato hīnaṃ na dhārayet //
english: Half of that measure is known to be medium. One should not bear a sword shorter than that length.

sanskrit: dīrghaṃ sumadhuraṃ śabdaṃ yusya khaḍgasya sattama / kiṅkiṇīsadṛśantasya dhāraṇaṃ śreṣṭhamucyate //
english: O Noblest one! It is said to be extremely worthy to wear a sword that is long and that which makes a sweet sound like that of a bell.

sanskrit: khaḍgaḥ padmapalāśāgro maṇḍalāgraś ca śasyate / karavīradalāgrābho ghṛtagandho viyatprabhaḥ //
english: A sword having the tip resembling the lotus flower or round is commended. Swords having the colour of the tip of a karavīra leaf, the smell of ghee and the lustre of the sky are also good.

sanskrit: samāṅgulasthāḥ śasyante vraṇāḥ khadgeṣu liṅgavat /
english: Spots at equal intervals of an inch on the swords are commendable as on the liṅga.

sanskrit: kākolūkasavarṇābhā viṣamāste na śobhanāḥ //
english: Those resembling the colour of a crow or owl and of an uneven shape are not auspicious.

sanskrit: khaḍge na paśyedvadanamucchiṣṭo na spṛśedasiṃ / mūlyaṃ jātiṃ na kathayenniśi kuryānna śīrṣake //
english: One should not see his face reflected in the sword. One should not touch the sword after eating without washing the mouth. One should not disclose the value and quality of a sword. One should not place the sword under the head in the night.

sanskrit: ratnānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye ratnaṃ dhāryamidaṃ nṛpaiḥ /
english: shall describe the characteristics of gems .

sanskrit: vajraṃ marakataṃ ratnaṃ padmarāgañca mauktikaṃ // indranīlaṃ mahānīlaṃ vaidūryaṃ gandhaśasyakaṃ / candrakāntaṃ sūryakāntaṃ sphaṭikaṃ pulakaṃ tathā //
english: The gems that are to be worn by the kings are diamond, emerald, ruby, pearl, sapphire, mahānīla a kind of sapphire, lapis lazuli, gandhaśasyaka ?, moonstone, sunstone, crystal, pulaka, karketana, topaz and the jyotirasa.

sanskrit: spaṭikaṃ rājapaṭṭañca tathā rājamayaṃ śubhaṃ //
english: Crystal, rājapaṭṭa an inferior kind of diamond and rājamaya are auspicious.

sanskrit: saugandhikaṃ tathā gañjaṃ śaṅkhabrahmamayaṃ tathā / gomedaṃ rudhirākṣañca tathā bhallātakaṃ dvija //
english: O Brahmin! Ruby, gañjā, conchshell of a variety, gomeda, rudhirākṣa holy beads and the marking nut are auspicious.

sanskrit: pīluṃ pravālakañcaiva girivajraṃ dvijottama // bhujaṅgamamaṇiñcaiva tathā vajramaṇiṃ śubhaṃ / ṭiṭṭibhañca tathā piṇḍaṃ bhrāmarañca tathotpalaṃ // suvarṇapratibaddhāni ratnāni śrījayādike /
english: O Excellent brahmin! Dhūli emerald, blue vitriol, lead, pīlu, coral girivajra ? the gem found in the serpents, auspicious diamond, ṭiṭṭibha ?, piṇḍa ?, bhrāmara a kind of stone? and utpalathese gems set in gold and worn would confer prosperity and success.

sanskrit: antaḥprabhatvaṃ vaimalyaṃ susaṃsthānatvameva ca //
english: Inward lustre, free from impurities and good formation of the shape are the characteristics of good gems.

sanskrit: sudhāryā naiva dhāryāstu niṣprabhā malinās tathā / khaṇḍāḥ saśarkarā ye ca praśastaṃ vajradharaṇam //
english: Such gems could be worn. Those not having lustre, impure, cracked and containing pebbles inside should not at all be worn. It is commendable to wear the diamond.

sanskrit: ambhastarati yadvajramabhedyaṃ vimalaṃ ca yat / ṣaṭkoṇaṃ śakracāpābhaṃ laghu cārkanibhaṃ śubham // śukapakṣanibhaḥ snigdhaḥ kāntimānvimalas tathā / svarṇacūrṇanibhaiḥ sūkṣmair marakataś ca vindubhiḥ //
english: The diamond that could be carried away by water, that is unbreakable, without impurity, of hexagonal shape, has the lustre of the rainbow, light and brilliant like the sun is auspicious to wear. Similarly an emerald possessing the hues of the plumes of a parrot, glossy, radiant, without impurity and containing minute particles resembling powdered gold is auspicious.

sanskrit: sphaṭikajāḥ padmarāgāḥ syū rāgavanto 'tinirmalāḥ /
english: The rubies got from crystal mines would be extremely red and spotless.

sanskrit: jātavaṅgā bhavantīha kuruvindasamudbhavāḥ //
english: Those got from the place Kuruvinda are naturally red.

sanskrit: saugandhikotthā kāṣāyā muktāphalāstu śuktijāḥ / vimalāstebhya utkṛṣṭā ye ca śaṅkhodbhavā mune //
english: and those got from sulphur mines are of dark brown colour. The pearls got from oysters are free from impurities. O Sage! Those got from the conchshells are superior to them.

sanskrit: nāgadantabhavāścāgryāḥ kumbhaśūkaramatsyajāḥ / veṇunāgabhavāḥ śreṣṭhā mauktikaṃ meghajaṃ varaṃ //
english: The pearls obtained from the tusks and temples of the elephants, those got from the boars and fish and those found in the bamboos and clouds are excellent.

sanskrit: vṛttatvaṃ śukratā svācchyaṃmahattvaṃ mauktike guṇāḥ / indranīlaṃ śubhaṃ kṣīre rājate bhrājate 'dhikaṃ //
english: Rotundity, whiteness, transparency and heaviness are the good qualities in a pearl. A good sapphire shines in the milk, spreads more lustre and tinge of its own colour.

sanskrit: rañjayet svaprabhāveṇa tamamūlyaṃ vinirdiśet /
english: It should be declared as invaluable.

sanskrit: nīlaraktantu vaidūryaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ hārādikaṃ bhajet //
english: The lapis lazuli of redblue colour is excellent and should be used in a necklace and other ornaments.

sanskrit: vāstulakṣma pravakṣyāmi viprādīnāṃ ca bhūriha /
english: shall describe the characteristics of a building site for the brahmins and others.

sanskrit: śvetā raktā tathā pītā kṛṣṇā caiva yathākramam // ghṛtaraktānnamadyānāṃ gandhāḍhyā vasataś ca bhūḥ /
english: They are white, red, yellow and black soil in order for the four castes. A building site should have the smell of ghee, blood, cooked rice and wine in order for the four castes.

sanskrit: madhurā ca kaṣāyā ca amlādyuparasā kramāt // kuśaiḥ śarais tathākāśair dūrvābhiryā ca saṃśritā / prārcya viprāṃś ca śiḥśalpāṃ khātapūrvantu kalpayet //
english: They should also taste sweet, pungent and acid and other secondary tastes in order. The ground should be cleared of kuśa, reeds, kāśa a kind of grass and dūrvā a kind of grass having razorlike edges after having dug out pieces of iron etc.

sanskrit: catuḥṣaṣṭipadaṃ kṛtvā madhye brahmā catuṣpadaḥ /
english: and worshipped the brahmins. Sixtyfour squares should be made. Lord Brahmā occupies the four central squares.

sanskrit: prāk teṣāṃ vai gṛhasvāmī kathitastu tathāryamā //
english: The presiding deity of the two squares on the east of those squares is said to be lord Aryamā.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇena vivasvāṃś ca mitraḥ paścimatas tathā /
english: God Vivasvān is on the two squares on the south. God Mitra is on the two squares on the west.

sanskrit: udaṅmahīdharaś caiva āpavatsau ca vahnige //
english: Āpas and Āpa Vatsa are on the southeast.

sanskrit: sāvitraś caiva savitā jayendrau nairṛte 'mbudhau /
english: God Sāvitra, Savitā, Jaya and Indra are respectively on the southwest and west.

sanskrit: rudravyādhī ca vāyavye pūrvādau koṇagādvahiḥ //
english: God Rudra and personification of disease are on the northwest.

sanskrit: mahendraś ca raviḥ satyo bhṛśaḥ pūrve 'tha dakṣiṇe /
english: The gods worshipped outside on the east and other directions from the angular squares are Mahendra, Satya and Śeṣa on the east.

sanskrit: puṣpadanto 'surāś caiva varuṇo yakṣa eva ca / saumye bhallāṭasomau ca aditirdhanadas tathā //
english: Gṛhakṣata, Aryaman, Dhṛti and Gandharva on the south, Puṣpadanta, Asura Varuṇa and Yajña on the west and Bhallāṭa Soma, Aditi and Dhanada on the north.

sanskrit: nāgaḥ karagrahaś caiśe aṣṭau diśi diśi smṛtāḥ /
english: Nāga is the lord on northeast. Similarly, the first and the last are said to be the lords in each one of the eight directions.

sanskrit: parjanyaḥ prathamo devo dvitīyaś ca karagrahaḥ /
english: Parjanya is the first god. The second one is Karagraha.

sanskrit: mahendraravisatyāś ca bhṛśo 'tha gaganantathā //
english: The other gods are Mahendra, Ravi, Satya, Bhṛśa and Gagana.

sanskrit: pavanaḥ pūrvataś caiva antarīkṣadhaneśvarau / āgneye cātha nairṛtye mṛgasugrīvakau surau //
english: Pavana should be worshipped in the east, gods Antarīkṣa and Dhaneśvara in the southeast and the celestials Mṛga and Sugrīvaka in the southwest.

sanskrit: rogo mukhyaś ca vāyavye dakṣiṇe puṣpavittadau / gṛhakṣato yamabhṛśau gandharvo nāgapaitṛkaḥ // āpye dauvārikasugrīvau puṣpadanto 'suro jalaṃ /
english: Roga and Mukhya should be worshipped in the northwest, Puṣpa, Kubera as well as Gṛhakṣata, Varna, Bhṛśa, Gandharva and Nāgapaitṛka on the south, Dauvārika, Sugrīva, Puṣpadanta, the demon, the presiding deity of water should be worshipped in the west.

sanskrit: yakṣmā rogaś ca śoṣaś ca uttare nāgarājakaḥ //
english: The pulmonary disease that emaciates men and Nāgarāja the king of the serpents should be worshipped in the north.

sanskrit: mukhyo bhallāṭaśaśinau aditiś ca kuverakaḥ / nāgo hutāśaḥ śreṣṭho vai śakrasūryau ca pūrvataḥ //
english: The gods Mukhya, Bhallāṭa, Moon, Aditi, Kubera, Nāga, Fire god, the excellent Indra and Sun god should be worshipped in the east.

sanskrit: dakṣe gṛhakṣataḥ puṣpa āpye sugrīva uttamaḥ / puṣpadanto hy udagdvāri bhallāṭaḥ puṣpadantakaḥ //
english: Gṛhakṣata and Puṣpa are worshipped in the south, the outstanding Sugrīva in the west and Puṣpadanta and Bhallāṭa at the northern door.

sanskrit: śileṣṭakādivinyāsaṃ mantraiḥ prārcya surāṃś caret / nande nandaya vāsiṣṭhe vasubhiḥ prajayā saha //
english: A stoneslab or a brick should be laid on the ground and worshipped with the mystic syllables as follows and the celestials should be worshipped. O Daughter of the sage Vasiṣṭha! Gladden us with wealth and progeny.

sanskrit: jaye bhārgavavadāyāde prajānāñjayamāhave / pūrṇe 'ṅgirasadāyāde pūrṇakāmaṃ kurudhva māṃ //
english: O Victorious one! Heir of sage Bhargava Paraśurāma! Bring victory to the progeny. O Heir of sage Aṅgirasa! The Satisfied one! Fulfil my desires.

sanskrit: bhadre kāśyapadāyāde kuru bhadrāṃ matiṃ mama /
english: O Auspicious one! Heir of sage Kāśyapa! Make my mind good.

sanskrit: sarvavījasamāyukte sarvaratnauṣadhair vṛte // rucire nandane nande vāsiṣṭhe ramyatāmiha /
english: O One endowed with all seeds! One surrounded by all gems and herbs! O Bright one! Rejoicing one! Daughter of sage Vasiṣṭha! Be pleased here.

sanskrit: prajāpatisute devi caturasre mahīmaye //
english: O Daughter of Prajāpati! Goddess on the quadrangle on the earth.

sanskrit: subhage suvrate bhadre gṛhe kaśyapi ramyatāṃ /
english: O Goddess of Good fortune and Good demeanour! Auspicious one! Daughter of sage Kāśyapa! Be pleased in this house.

sanskrit: pūjite paramācāryair gandhamālyair alaṅkṛte // bhavabhūtikare devi gṛhe bhārgavi ramyatāṃ /
english: O One worshipped by great masters and adorned with incense and flowers! O Goddess that makes one get prosperous! O Daughter of sage Bhārgava! May you be pleased in this house.

sanskrit: avyaṅgye cākṣate pūrṇe muneraṅgirasaḥ sute //
english: One not mutilated! Unbroken one! Complete one! Daughter of the sage Aṅgirasa! establish you on this brick.

sanskrit: iṣṭake tvaṃ prayaccheṣṭaṃ pratiṣṭāṅkārayamyahaṃ /
english: Confer on me the desired things.

sanskrit: deśasvāmipurasvāmigṛhasvāmiparigrahe // manuṣyadhanahastyaśvapaśuvṛddhikarī bhava /
english: One that is held by sovereigns, chieftains and owners of houses! May you be one that increases the progeny, wealth, elephants, horses and cows.

sanskrit: gṛhapraveśe 'pi tathā śilānyāsaṃ samācaret //
english: A brick or stone should similarly be laid at the entrance to the house for the first time.

sanskrit: uttareṇa śubhaḥ plakṣo vaṭaḥ prāk syād gṛhāditaḥ / udumvaraś ca yāmyena paścime 'śvattha uttamaḥ //
english: A plakṣa tree would be auspicious on the north and the vaṭa tree on the east of the house. Udumbara on the south and the aśvattha on the west are excellent.

sanskrit: vāmabhāge tathodyānaṃ kuryādvāsaṃ gṛhe śubhaṃ /
english: A garden should be laid on the left of the house. Dwelling in such a house is good.

sanskrit: sāyaṃ prātastu gharmāptau śītakāle dināntare // varṣārātre bhuyaḥ śoṣe sektavyā ropitadrumāḥ /
english: The trees planted and grown should be watered morning and evening in the summer, alternate days in the winter and each night in the rainy season if the ground gets dried.

sanskrit: viḍaṅgaghṛṭasaṃyuktān secayecchītavāriṇā //
english: They should be sprinkled with cold water mixed with the paste of vidaṅga a medicinal herb used as a vermifuge.

sanskrit: phalanāśe kulatthaiś ca māṣair mudgaistilair yavaiḥ / ghṛtaśītapayaḥsekaḥ phalapuṣpāya darvadā //
english: If the fruits get destroyed, the trees should be sprinkled with water mixed with the paste of horsebeans, blackgram, green gram, sesamum and barley. Sprinkling of cold water together with ghee is always beneficial for the trees bearing fruits and flowers.

sanskrit: matsyāmbhasā tu sekena vṛddhirbhavati śākhinaḥ /
english: Sprinkling with the washings of the fish would also increase the growth of the trees.

sanskrit: āvikājasakṛccūrṇaṃ yavacūrṇaṃ tilāni ca // gomāṃsamudakañceti saptarātraṃ nidhāpayet / utsekaṃ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ phalapuṣpādivṛddhidaṃ //
english: The powdered excrement of the sheep and goat mixed with the powdered barley and sesamum, beef and water should be buried in the ground for seven nights and then sprinkling that would make all the trees bear fruits and flowers abundantly.

sanskrit: matsyodakena śītena āmrāṇāṃ seka iṣyate /
english: Sprinkling mango trees with cold water mixed with fish is commended.

sanskrit: praśastaṃ cāpyaśokānāṃ kāminīpādatāḍanaṃ //
english: The gentle kick of the aśoka tree by women with their feet is also commended.

sanskrit: kharjūranārikelāderlavaṇādbhirvivardhanaṃ / viḍaṅgamatsyamāṃsādbhiḥ sarveṣu dohadaṃ śubhaṃ //
english: Date palms, coconut and other trees grow well by adding salt. Sprinkling with water mixed with vidaṅga herb and fish would be beneficial for all trees. Yama and Bhṛṅgarāja in other texts.

sanskrit: puṣpaistu pūjanādviṣṇuḥ sarvakāryeṣu siddhidaḥ /
english: Lord Viṣṇu would confer success in all ventures by worshipping him with flowers .

sanskrit: mālatī mallikā yūthī pāṭalā karavīrakaṃ // pāvāntiratimuktaś ca karṇikāraḥ kurāṇṭakaḥ / kubjakastagaro nīpo vāṇo varvaramallikā //
english: The flowers for worship are mālatī, mallikā, yūthī, pāṭalā, karavīraka, pāvanti, atimukta, karṇikāra, kuraṇṭaka, kubjaka, tagara, nīpa, vāṇa, barbara, mallikā, aśoka, tilaka, kunda and tamālaka would be good for worship.

sanskrit: bilvapatraṃ śamīpatraṃ patraṃ bhṛṅgarajasya tu // tulasīkālatulasīpatraṃ vāsakamarcane /
english: The leaves of bilva, śamī, bhṛṅgarāja, tulasī, and vāsaka are deemed good for worship.

sanskrit: ketakīpatrapuṣpaṃ ca padmaṃ raktotpalādikaṃ //
english: The ketakī leaf and flower, lotus and red lotus and others are also good.

sanskrit: nārkannonmattakaṅkāñcī pūjane girimallikā / kauṭajaṃ śālmalīpuṣpaṃ kaṇṭakārībhavannahi //
english: But the arka, unmattaka, kāñcī, girimallikā, kauṭaja, śālmali and kaṇṭakārī flowers are not at all good for the worship.

sanskrit: ghṛtaprasthena viṣṇoś ca snānaṅgokoṭisatphalaṃ /
english: The bathing of lord Viṣṇu with a prastha measure of ghee would be equal to the benefit of making a gift of a crore of cows.

sanskrit: āḍhakena tu rājā syāt ghṛtakṣīrair divaṃ vrajet //
english: By doing so with āḍhaka one would become a king. One would ascend heavens by bathing with ghee and milk.

sanskrit: catuṣpādaṃ dhanurvedaṃ vede pañcavidhaṃ dvija / rathanāgāśvapattīnāṃ yodhāṃścāśritya kīrtitaṃ //
english: O Brahmin! shall describe the science of archery in four sections. It is said to be of five kinds resting on the warriors on chariots, elephant, cavalry and infantry.

sanskrit: yanmuktaṃ pāṇimuktaṃ muktasandhāritaṃ tathā / amuktaṃ bāhuyuddhañca pañcadhā tyat prakīrtitaṃ //
english: It is said to be of five kinds such as those projected by a machine, thrown by the hand, those cast by hands and retained, those permanently retained in the hand and boxing.

sanskrit: tatra śastrāstrasampattyā dvividhaṃ parikīrtitaṃ /
english: The weapons are said to be of two kindsordinary weapons and missiles.

sanskrit: ṛjumāyāvibhedena bhūyo dvividhamucyate //
english: They are again stated to be of two kinds by the divisions such as curved and conceit.

sanskrit: kṣepiṇī cāpayantrādyair yantramuktaṃ prakīrtitaṃ / śilātomarayantrādyaṃ pāṇimuktaṃ prakīrtitaṃ //
english: The weapons projected by means of a sling or bow or other such contrivances are said to be projected by a machine. Stones and weapons such as the iron clubs are stated to be weapons thrown by the hand.

sanskrit: muktasandhāritaṃ jñeyaṃ prāsādyamapi yadbhavet / khaḍgādikamamuktañca niyuddhaṃ vigatāyudhaṃ //
english: Weapons such as the prāsa dart would be known as the weapons cast and retained. Swords and other weapons are those permanently retained. Personal combat without weapons is the last one.

sanskrit: kuryādyogyāni prātrāṇi yoddhumicchurjitaśramaḥ /
english: After surmounting the difficulties, the king desiring to fight should engage fit men for the purpose.

sanskrit: dhanuḥśreṣṭhāni yuddhāni prāsamadhyāni tāni ca // tāni khaḍgajaghanyāni bāhupratyavarāṇi ca /
english: Battles fought with the bows and arrows are excellent, those with darts are mediocre, those with swords are inferior and those fought with hands are still inferior to them.

sanskrit: dhanurvede gururvipraḥ prokto varṇadvayasya ca //
english: A brahmin is said to be the preceptor in archery for two castes.

sanskrit: yuddhādhikāraḥ śūdrasya svayaṃ vyāpādi śikṣayā /
english: A śūdra has the right to fight in case of an emergency if he had undergone training.

sanskrit: deśasthaiḥ śaṅkarai rājñaḥ kāryā yuddhe sahāyatā //
english: The people of mixed castes belonging to that country should render assistance to the king in the battle.

sanskrit: aṅguṣṭhagulphapāṇyaṅghyaḥ śliṣṭāḥ syuḥ sahitā yadi / dṛṣṭaṃ samapadaṃ sthānametallakṣaṇatas tathā //
english: If the thumbs, calves, palms and feet are kept closely pressed against each other, the position is said to be samapada from its characteristic feature.

sanskrit: vāhyāṅgulisthitau pādau stabdhajānubalāvubhau / trivitastyantarāsthānametadvaiśākhamucyate //
english: It is said to be vaiśākha if one stands on the outer toes and the two knees are held in a straight and motionless posture and the distance between the two soles is three vitastis twelve aṅgulas.

sanskrit: caturvitastivicchinne tadetanmaṇḍalaṃ smṛtaṃ //
english: It is known as maṇḍala if the two knees look like a row of haṃsas and the feet are four vitastis apart.

sanskrit: halākṛtimayaṃ yacca stabdhajānūrudakṣiṇaṃ / vitastyaḥ pañca vistāre tadālīḍhaṃ prakīrtitaṃ //
english: It is stated to be ālīḍha when the right thigh and knee are held motionless and appear like the plough and are five vitastis apart.

sanskrit: etadeva viparyastaṃ pratyālīḍhamiti smṛtaṃ /
english: If the same is changed to the left it is known to be pratyālīḍha.

sanskrit: gulphau pārṣṇigrahau caiva sthitau pañcāṅgulāntarau / sthānaṃ jātaṃ bhavedetad dvādaśāṅgulamāyataṃ //
english: If the left leg would be curved and the right would be straight and the two calves and the legs remain fifteen aṅgulas apart, the posture would be known as jāta on the whole extending to twelve aṅgulas.

sanskrit: athavā dakṣiṇañjānu kubjaṃ bhavati niś calaṃ // daṇḍāyato bhavedeṣa caraṇaḥ saha jānunā / evaṃ vikaṭamuddiṣṭaṃ dvihastāntaramāyataṃ // jānunī dviguṇe syātāmuttānau caraṇāvubhau /
english: If the left knee would be straight and the right knee extended well or the right knee is curved and motionless and the feet together with the knee are four cubits apart, it is said to be vikaṭa extending to two cubits. If the knees are kept down twice as much and the two legs are raised, that posture is said to be vikaṭa.

sanskrit: kiñcidvivartitau pādau samadaṇḍāyatau sthirau /
english: The feet are a little turned round, firm and equal to four cubits.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭameva yathānyāyaṃ ṣoḍaśāṅgulamāyataṃ //
english: It is properly seen to extend to sixteen aṅgulas.

sanskrit: svastikenātra kurvīta praṇāmaṃ prathamaṃ dvija / kāmukaṃ gṛhya vāmena vāṇaṃ dakṣiṇakena tu //
english: O Brahmin! With this posture known as svastika one should first bow down holding the bow by the left hand and the arrow by the right hand.

sanskrit: vaiśākhe yadi vā jāte sthitau vāpyathavāyatau / guṇāntantu tataḥ kṛtvā kārmuke priyakārmukaḥ //
english: One that loves his bow should remain in the postures vaiśākha or jāta or firm or extended and put the string on the bow.

sanskrit: dharaṇyāṃ sthāpayitvā tu tolayitvā tathaiva ca //
english: The lower tip of the bow and the striking part of the arrow should be fixed on the ground.

sanskrit: bhujābhyāmatra kuñjābhyāṃ prakoṣṭhābhyāṃ śubhavrata / yasya vāṇaṃ dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ puṅgadeśe ca patriṇaḥ // vinyāso dhanuś caiva dvādaśāṅgulamantaraṃ /
english: O One practising good austerities! it should be raised with the hands by means of the curved forearms. That bow and arrow of a person is excellent which a space of twelve inches between the bow and the feathered part of the arrow.

sanskrit: jyayā viśiṣṭaḥ kartavyo nātihīno na cādhikaḥ //
english: The string should be made neither too long nor too short.

sanskrit: utkṣipedutthitaṃ hastamantareṇākṣikarṇayoḥ // pūrveṇa muṣṭinā grāhyastanāgre dakṣiṇe śaraḥ / haraṇantu tataḥ kṛtvā śīghraṃ pūrvaṃ prasārayet //
english: Holding the bow in line with the navel and the quiver on the back, the bow should be raised with the left hand between the eye and the ear. The arrow should be taken with the right fist to the edge of the breast. Then the string should be put on and quickly drawn to its full capacity.

sanskrit: nābhyantarā naiva vāhyā nordhvakā nādharā tathā / na ca kubjā na cottānā na calā nātiveṣṭitā //
english: It should not be stretched so much as to be within or beyond or above or below or curbed or raised or shaking or extremely obstructed.

sanskrit: samā sthairyaguṇopetā pūrvadaṇḍamiva sthitā /
english: It should be parallel, firm and straight like a rod.

sanskrit: chādayitvā tato lakṣyaṃ pūrveṇānena muṣṭinā // urasā tūtthito yantā trikoṇavinatasthitaḥ / srastāṃśe niś calagrīvo mayūrāñcitamastakaḥ //
english: After having covered the mark with the right fist, the archer should stand with his chest raised and bent in the shape of a triangle, the shoulders stooping, the neck without motion, and the head poised erect as a peacock.

sanskrit: lalāṭanāsāvaktrāṃsāḥ kuryuraśvasamambhavet /
english: The space between the fore head,_nose, face, shoulder and the elbow should be equal.

sanskrit: antaraṃ tryaṅgulaṃ jñeyaṃ civukasyāṃsakasya ca //
english: The space between the chin and shoulder is known to be three aṅgulas.

sanskrit: prathamantryaṅgulaṃ jñeyaṃ dvitīye dvyaṅgulaṃ smṛtaṃ / tṛtīye 'ṅgulamudiṣṭamāyatañcivukāṃsayoḥ // gṛhītvā sāyakaṃ puṅkhāttarjanyāṅguṣṭhakena tu / anāmayā punargṛhya tathā madhyamayāpi ca //
english: The interval between the chin and shoulder is said to be three aṅgulas in the first, two aṅgulas in the second and one aṅgulas in the third kind ofbowl After having taken the feathered end of an arrow with the thumb and the index finger and then with the ring and middle finger of the right hand, it should be drawn fully such that the arrow gets completely stretched.

sanskrit: evaṃ vidhamupakramya moktavyaṃ vidhivat khagaṃ //
english: After having begun in this way, the arrow should be released in the proper manner.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭimuṣṭihataṃ lakṣyaṃ bhindyādvāṇena suvrataḥ / muktvā tu paścimaṃ hastaṃ kṣipedvegena pṛṣṭhataḥ //
english: O Man of good conduct! The target that has been seen by the eyes and covered by the fist should be split with the arrow. After releasing the arrow the left hand should be thrown back quickly.

sanskrit: etaducchedamicchanti jñātavyaṃ hi tvayā dvija /
english: O Brahmin! It is known as excision. It should be known by you.

sanskrit: kūrparantadadhaḥ kāryamākṛṣya tu dhanuṣmatā // ūrdhvaṃ vimuktake kārye lakṣaśliṣṭantu madhyamaṃ /
english: An expert in the archery should keep the elbow down while drawing an arrow, above while releasing and be in line with the target in the middle state.

sanskrit: śreṣṭhaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ vijñeyaṃ dhanuḥśāstraviśāradaiḥ //
english: Those who are wellversed in the science of archery know it as the excellent.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhastu sāyako jñeyo bhaveddvādaśamuṣṭayaḥ / ekādaśa tathā kanīyāndaśamuṣṭayaḥ //
english: The superior kind of arrow is known to be twelve muṣṭis, the mediocre of eleven muṣṭis and the inferior one of ten muṣṭis.

sanskrit: caturhastaṃ dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ trayaḥ sārdhantu madhyamaṃ / kanīyastu trayaḥ proktaṃ nityameva padātinaḥ //
english: A bow of four cubits is excellent, that of three and a half cubits is mediocre and that of three cubits is said to be inferior always by the infantry men.

sanskrit: aśve rathe gaje śreṣṭhe tadeva parikīrtitaṃ //38//
english: The same is said to be excellent in the case of cavalry, chariot and elephant.

sanskrit: pūrṇāyataṃ dvijaḥ kṛtvā tato māṃsair gadāyudhān / sunirdhautaṃ dhanuḥ kṛtvā yajñabhūmau vidhāpayet //
english: The breadth of the clenched fist. Then a brahmin should get ready the weapons such as the mace, bow etc., wash them well free from flesh and place them on the sacrificial ground.

sanskrit: tato vāṇaṃ samāgṛhya daṃśitaḥ susamāhitaḥ / tūrṇamāsādya badhnīyādṛḍhāṃ kakṣāñca dakṣiṇām //
english: Then after having collected the arrow, furnishing himself with an armour and remaining composed he should get the quiver and bind it firmly on the right shoulder.

sanskrit: vilakṣyamapi tadvāṇaṃ tatra caiva susaṃsthitaṃ /
english: Even though there may not be any definite aim, that arrow that has been placed in it in th at position should be lifted from the quiver with the right hand.

sanskrit: tataḥ samuddharedvāṇaṃ tūṇāddakṣiṇapāṇinā // tenaiva sahitaṃ madhye śaraṃ saṅgṛhya dhārayet / vāmahastena vai kakṣāṃ dhanustasmātsamuddharet //
english: Then the arrow together with the hand that be lifted should be placed on the bow and held. The middlepart of the bow should be held with the left hand. After having made his mind diverted of all anxieties, the feathered end of the arrow should be placed on the string.

sanskrit: sampīḍya siṃhakarṇena puṅkhenāpi same dṛḍhaṃ // vāmakarṇopaviṣtañca phalaṃ vāmasya dhārayet / varṇān madhyamayā tatra vāmāṅgulyā ca dhārayet //
english: After holding firmly in the position known as siṃhakarṇa evenly with the feathered end, the fruit of the left that rested on the left ear should be borne ? The covers should be borne with the left middle finger.

sanskrit: mano lakṣyagataṃ kṛtvā muṣṭinā ca vidhānavit / dakṣiṇe gātrabhāge tu kṛtvā varṇaṃ vimokṣayet //
english: One who knows the procedure should fix his mind on the target and hold the arrow with the right fist on the right side of the body and discharge covers.

sanskrit: lalāṭapuṭasaṃsthānaṃ daṇḍaṃ lakṣye niveśayet / ākṛṣya tāḍayettatra candrakaṃ ṣoḍaśāṅgulam //
english: One that practises to shoot an arrow should place a pole as the target in line with the fold on the forehead. The circular mark of the extent of sixteen aṅgulas should be struck after pulling the arrow.

sanskrit: muktvā vāṇaṃ tataḥ paścādulkāśikṣastadā tayā /
english: After having discharged such an arrow, one should then practise discharging firebrands with that.

sanskrit: nigṛhṇīyān madhyamayā tato 'ṅgulyā punaḥ punaḥ //
english: One should place the arrow again and again with the middle finger.

sanskrit: akṣilakṣyaṃ kṣipettūṇāccaturasrañca dakṣiṇam / caturasragataṃ vedhyamabhyaseccāditaḥ sthitaḥ //
english: One should strike from the quiver at the target perceived by the eye imagining as a square on the right. One that is in the first stage should practise to pierce the target in a square.

sanskrit: tasmādanantaraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ parāvṛttaṃ gatañca yat /
english: Then he should practise to aim quickly, turning round and to pierce that below or above.

sanskrit: nimnamunnatavedhañca abhyaset kṣiprakantataḥ // vedhyasthāneṣvathaiteṣu sattvasya puṭakāddhanuḥ /
english: When the targets are at the position of being pierced the bow should be lifted from its position and the hands should threaten with varied sounds of invincible nature ?

sanskrit: tasmin vedhyagate vipra dve vedhye dṛḍhasañjñake / dve vedhye duṣkare vedhye dve tathā citraduṣkare //
english: O Brahmin! Among those objects to be struck by a bowman, two kinds are known to be dṛḍha requiring firm hand, two are known as Duṣkara difficult to hit and two as citraduṣkara extremely difficult to hit.

sanskrit: na tu nimnañca tīkṣṇañca dṛḍhavedhye prakīrtite /
english: That which is not below and hard is stated to be requiring firm hand.

sanskrit: nimnaṃ duṣkaramuddiṣṭaṃ vedhyamūrdhvagatañca yat //
english: That which is below as well as that which is above is said to be duṣkara.

sanskrit: mastakāyanamadhye tu citraduṣkarasañjñake /
english: That which is between the head and the zenith is known as citraduṣkara.

sanskrit: evaṃ vedhyagaṇaṅkṛtvā dakṣiṇenetareṇa ca // ārohet prathamaṃ vīro jitalakṣastato naraḥ /
english: Thus after having known the position of the objects to be hit with the right and left, a hero archer should first make progress. Then one would be the conqueror of the target.

sanskrit: eṣa eva vidhiḥ proktastatra dṛṣṭaḥ prayoktṛbhiḥ // adhikaṃ bhramaṇaṃ tasya tasmādvedhyāt prakīrtitam /
english: This is said to be the rule that has been laid by those wellversed in that. It is said that one would have more mobility from that practice. The target that comes within the purview of the arrow should be aimed at firmly.

sanskrit: bhrāntaṃ pracalitañcaiva sthiraṃ yacca bhavediti / samantāttāḍayed bhindyācchedayedvyathayedapi //
english: One should strike at once, break, pierce and cause distress to that which is whirling round, that which is moving and that which is extremely steady.

sanskrit: karmayogavidhānajño jñātvaivaṃ vidhimācaret /
english: One who is wellversed in the performance of actions should practise this way after knowing that.

sanskrit: manasā cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭyā yogaśikṣuryamaṃ jayet // jitahasto jitamatirjitadṛglakṣyasādhakaḥ / niyatāṃ siddhimāsādya tato vāhanamāruhet //
english: One that has learnt the application would conquer the lord of death by means of his mind, eyes and look. One that has controlled the hand, conquered the mind and obtained proficiency in hitting the target perceived should board the chariot after getting the specified perfection.

sanskrit: daśahasto bhavet pāśo vṛttaḥ karamukhas tathā /
english: A noose should be ten cubits long, round and such as to be held in the hand.

sanskrit: anyeṣāṃ sudṛḍhānāñca sukṛtaṃ pariveṣṭitam / tathā triṃśatsamaṃ pāśaṃ budhaḥ kuryāt suvartitam //
english: It may be made of any other strong material well twined with thirty pieces. A wiseman should make the noose wellrounded.

sanskrit: kartavyaṃ śikṣakaistasya sthānaṃ kakṣāsu vai tadā /
english: The instructors should always provide a place for that on the sides.

sanskrit: vāmahastena saṅgṛhya dakṣiṇenoddharettataḥ // kuṇḍalasyākṛtiṃ kṛtvā bhrāmyakaṃ mastakopari / kṣipet tūrṇamaye tūrṇaṃ puruṣe carmaveṣṭite //
english: Having gathered it with the left hand it should be lifted with the righthand. After having made the noose into a loop, it should be whirled round the head and thrown quickly on a person covered by the armour and quiver.

sanskrit: valgite ca plute caiva tathā pravrajiteṣu ca / samayogavidhiṃ kṛtvā prayuñjīta suśikṣitam // vijitvā tu yathānyāyaṃ tato bandhaṃ samācaret /
english: One that is welltrained should be employed after having made him proficient to use the noose on the horsemen galloping, capering and running away. After having conquered the enemy, he should be made a captive in the proper manner.

sanskrit: kaṭyāmbaddhvā tataḥ khaḍgaṃ vāmapārśvāvalambitam // dṛḍhaṃ vigṛhya vāmena niṣkarṣeddakṣiṇena tu /
english: The sword should be hanging on the left side on the waist. The sheath should be held firmly by the left hand and the sword should be drawn out from the scabbard with the right hand.

sanskrit: ṣaḍaṅgulaparīṇāhaṃ saptahastasamucchritaṃ //
english: The circumference of a dart should be six aṅgulas, its height seven hastas and it be made of iron.

sanskrit: ayomayyaḥ śalākāś ca varmāṇi vividhāni ca /
english: Armours are of different kinds.

sanskrit: ardhahaste same caiva tiryagūrdhvagataṃ tathā //
english: It should be half the hasta, equal, spreading across and upwards.

sanskrit: yojayedvidhinā yena tathātvaṅgadataḥ śṛṇu /
english: It should be fitted in the proper manner. Listen to me as describe.

sanskrit: tūṇacarmāvanaddhāṅgaṃ sthāpayitvā navaṃ dṛḍhaṃ // kareṇādāya lagūḍaṃ dakṣiṇāṅgulakaṃ navaṃ /
english: After having made the person stand with the quiver and armour on his body, one should take the new, strong club in the right hand, move nine aṅgulas and strike.

sanskrit: udyamya ghātayedyasya nāśastena śiśordṛḍhaṃ //
english: By this blow the head of the enemy would certainly be destroyed.

sanskrit: ubhābhyāmatha hastābhyāṃ kuryāttasya nipātanaṃ /
english: Otherwise he may be struck down with both hands.

sanskrit: akleśena tataḥ kurvan badhe siddhiḥ prakīrtitā //
english: After having done thus without strain, one is said to accomplish the death of the person.

sanskrit: vāhānāṃ śramakaraṇaṃ pracārārthaṃ purā tava //13//
english: have already described how to cause the distress of the arms for the sake of the movement.

sanskrit: bhrāntamudbhrāntamāviddhamāplutaṃ viplutaṃ sṛtaṃ / sampātaṃ samudīśañca śyenapātamathākulaṃ // uddhūtamavadhūtañca savyaṃ dakṣiṇameva ca / anālakṣitavisphoṭau karālendramahāsakhau // vikarālanipātau ca vibhīṣaṇabhayānakau /
english: Bhrānta, udbhrānta, āviddha, āpluta, vipluta, sṛta, saṃpāta, samudīrṇa, śyenapāta, ākula, uddhūta, avadhūta, savya, dakṣiṇa, anālakṣita, visphoṭa, karāla, indramahāsakha, vikarāla, nipāta, vibhīṣaṇa, bhayānaka, samagra the entire, ardha half, tṛtīyāṃśa onethird, pāda, pādārdha, vārija, pratyālīḍha, ālīḍha, varāha and lulita are known to be the thirtytwo kinds of employment of the sword and armour in a battle.

sanskrit: parāvṛttamapāvṛttaṃ gṛhītaṃ laghusañjñitaṃ / ūrdhvāt kṣiptamadhaḥ kṣiptaṃ sandhāritavidhāritaṃ // śyenapātaṃ gajapātaṃ grāhagrāhyantathaiva ca /
english: Parāvṛtta, apāvṛtta, gṛhīta, that known as laghu, ūrdhvakṣipta, adhaḥkṣipta, sandhārita, vidhārita, śyenapāta, gajāpāta and grāhagrāhya are the eleven ways of manipulating a noose.

sanskrit: ṛjvāyataṃ viśālañca tiryagbhrāmitameva ca / pañcakarma vinirdiṣṭaṃ vyaste pāśe mahātmabhiḥ //
english: Great men hold that the five ways of casting a noose are extending in a straight line, long, broad, horizontal and whirling.

sanskrit: chedanaṃ bhedanaṃ pāto bhramaṇaṃ śayanaṃ tathā /
english: The uses of a disc are cutting, piercing, felling, whirling and severing.

sanskrit: āsphoṭaḥ kṣeḍanaṃ bhedastrāsāndolitakau tathā / śūlakarmāṇi jānīhi ṣaṣṭhamāghātasañjñitaṃ //
english: May you know that the uses of a spear are slapping, thrashing, cleaving, frightening, incarcerating and, the sixth, striking down.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭighātaṃ bhujāghātaṃ pārśvaghātaṃ dvijottama / ṛjupakṣeṣuṇā pātaṃ tomarasya prakīrtitaṃ //
english: O Excellent Brahmin! It has been declared that an iron club TOMARA is used in striking the eyes, the arms and sides of the enemy and should be countered with an arrow of the defendent.

sanskrit: āhataṃ vipra gomūtraprabhūtaṅkamalāsanaṃ / tatordhvagātraṃ namitaṃ vāmadakṣiṇameva ca // āvṛttañca parāvṛttaṃ pādoddhūtamaplutaṃ / haṃsamardaṃ vimardañca gadākarma prakīrtitaṃ //
english: O Brahmin! It has been declared that a mace GADĀ is used for the acts such as āhata, gomūtra, prabhūta, kamalāsana, ūrdhvagātra, vāmanamita, dakṣiṇanamita, āvṛtta, parāvṛtta, pādodbhūta, avapluta, haṃsamardda and vimarda.

sanskrit: karālamavaghātañca daśopaplutameva ca / kṣiptahastaṃ sthitaṃ śūnyaṃ parāśostu vinirdiśet // tāḍanaṃ chedanaṃ vipra tathā cūrṇanameva ca /
english: The use of a battleaxe is said to be karāla dreadful, avaghāta sharp blow, daṃśa cutting, upapluta leaping, kṣiptahasta that has been released from the hand, sthita remaining in the original position and śūnya void.

sanskrit: mudgarasya tu karmāṇi tathā plavanaghātanaṃ //
english: O Brahmin! The use of a mudgara mace is for striking, cutting, pounding, causing deluge and killing.

sanskrit: saṃśrāntamatha viśrāntaṃ govisargaṃ sudurdharaṃ / bhindipālasya karmāṇi laguḍasya ca tānyapi //
english: The uses of a bhindipāla sling are for saṃśrānta, viśrānta and govisarga and sudurdhara that is extremely unbearable. The same are the uses of a laguḍa club.

sanskrit: antyaṃ madhyaṃ parāvṛttaṃ nideśāntaṃ dvijottama /
english: O Excellent Brahmin! The uses of a mace VAJRA are for striking with the end, with the middle, turning back and commanding.

sanskrit: vajrasyetāni karmāṇi paṭṭiśasya ca tānyapi //
english: The same are the uses of a paṭṭiśa a kind of spear with sharp edge.

sanskrit: haraṇaṃ chedanaṃ ghāto baloddhāraṇamāyataṃ / kṛpāṇakarma nirdiṣṭaṃ pātanaṃ sphoṭanaṃ tathā // trāsanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ ghāto baloddharaṇamāyatam /
english: Taking away, cutting, killing, piercing, anointing, felling and snapping are indicated as the uses of a sword. The functions of a sling are indicated to be frightening, protecting, killing and helping a big fighting column.

sanskrit: gātrasaṃśleṣaṇaṃ śāntaṃ tathā gātraviparyayaḥ //
english: The same are the functions of a machine also.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaprahāraṃ ghātañca gomūtraṃ savyadakṣiṇe / pārantārakaṃ daṇḍaṃ karavīrandhamākulaṃ // tiryagbandhamapāmārgaṃ bhīmavegaṃ sudarśanaṃ / siṃhākrāntaṃ gajākrāntaṃ gardabhākrāntameva ca // gadākarmāṇi jānīyānniyuddhasyātha karma ca /
english: The methods of using the mace GADĀ should be known as total discharge, stimulating, throwing upwards in the posture of a boar, using the hand and the back of the hand, standing with the right knee being advanced and the left leg retracted, holding with one hand, holding by the back of the hand, holding with two hands, with the arms thrown round as in embracing, discharging from the hip, raising upwards, striking on the chest, striking on the forehead, bhujāvidhamana ?, raising with the hand, lifting skywards, striking at the feet, injuring the feet, pressing the body together, putting an end, total destruction of the body, striking after raising up, blowing, intermittently striking, wielding in the left or right hand, enabling to cross, enabling to protect, like a stick, fettered like the braid of hair, agitating, transversely locked up, removal, frightening speed, good looking, attacking like lion or elephant or an ass.

sanskrit: pādaprahāramāsphoṭaṃ kaṭirecitakantathā / gātrāśleṣaṃ skandhagataṃ mahīvyājanameva ca // urolalāṭaghātañca vispaṣṭakaraṇantathā / uddhūtamavadhūtañca tiryaṅmārgagataṃ tathā // gajaskandhamavakṣepamaparāṅmukhameva ca /
english: The modes of wrestling are drawing the enemy, drawing apart the base of the hands, the turning about of the neck, the breaking of the back, the terrible one, revolution, reversion, the manner of slaughtering animals, ajāvika ?, hitting the feet, slapping as done with the arms, discharging from the hip, resting on the shoulder, using the earth as a contrivance, striking at the chest and forehead, open conquest, raised one, as a wave, moving transverse, riding an elephant, casting down, not having the face turned aside, the path of the celestials, downward path, moving haphazardly, consistent, striking with a club, casting down, tearing the earth, locking up in the knees, locking up by the arms, embracing by the body, the terrific one, backwards, together with water, shining one and enclosed with the arms.

sanskrit: sannaddhaiḥ saṃyuge bhāvyaṃ saśastraistair gajādibhiḥ //
english: At the time of the battle, the warriors should be ready with the weapons, elephants and other divisions.

sanskrit: varāṅkuśadharau cobhau eko grīvāgato 'paraḥ / skandhau dvau ca dhānuṣkau dvau ca khaḍgadharau gaje //
english: Two soldiers should be bearing excellent goads, one of them on the neck of the elephant and the other on the shoulder and two archers and two soldiers carrying the sword on the elephant.

sanskrit: rathe raṇe gaje caiva turagāṇāṃ trayaṃ bhavet /
english: Three cavalry men should be there to defend a chariot or the battlefront or the elephant man.

sanskrit: dhānuṣkāṇāntrayaṃ proktaṃ rakṣārthe turagasya ca //
english: It is said that there should be three archers to guard the cavalry.

sanskrit: dhanvino rakṣaṇārthāya carmiṇantu niyojayet /
english: Armoured men should be employed for the protection of the archers.

sanskrit: svamantraiḥ śastramabhyarcya śāstrantrailokyamohanaṃ // yo yuddhe yāti ca jayedarīn sampālayedbhuvaṃ //34//
english: Whoever goes for a war after having worshipped the weapon with the respective sacred formula or the sacred formula known as the one captivating the three worlds, would conquer the enemies and would govern the earth well.

sanskrit: vyavahāraṃ pravakṣyāmi nayānayavivekadaṃ /
english: shall describe the administration of justice that gives the discriminative knowledge of justice and injustice.

sanskrit: catuṣpācca catuḥsthānaś catuḥsādhana ucyate // caturhitaś caturvyāpī catuṣkārī ca kīrtyate /
english: It is said to comprise four feet, four places and four means. That which is beneficial to four classes of men, extends to four different parties and benefits fourfold.

sanskrit: aṣṭāṅgo 'ṣṭādaśapadaḥ śataśākhastathaiva ca //
english: In the same way it is said to comprise eight parts and hundred divisions.

sanskrit: triyonirdvyabhiyogaś ca dvidvāro dvigatis tathā /
english: It has three sources, two sorts of statements, two parties and two kinds of issues.

sanskrit: dharmaś ca vyavahāraś ca caritraṃ rājaśāsanaṃ //
english: The codes of law, justice, conduct and the command of the king are the four feet in the administration of the justice .

sanskrit: catuṣpādvyavahārāṇāmuttaraḥ pūrvasādhakaḥ /
english: Among these each subsequent one is the means for the previous one.

sanskrit: tatra satye sthito dharmo vyavahārastu sākṣiṣu //
english: Therein righteousness rests on truth. A law suit rests on the witnesses.

sanskrit: caritraṃ saṅgrahe puṃsāṃ rājājñāyāntu śāsanaṃ /
english: The conduct of a person rests on the opinion of the people. The decree depends on the command of the king.

sanskrit: sāmābhyupāyasādhyatvāccatuḥsādhana ucyate // caturṇāmāśramāṇāñca rakṣaṇātsa caturhitaḥ / kartāraṃ sākṣiṇaś caiva satyānrājānameva ca //
english: Since a legal case could be decided by the means such as the conciliation and the like, they are said to be the four means. Since it is protecting the four institutions such as the student life, it is said to be beneficial in four ways.

sanskrit: dharmasyārthasya yaśaso lokapaṅktestathaiva ca // caturṇāṅkaraṇādeṣa catuṣkārī prakīrtitaḥ /
english: It is said to be the instruments of four kinds, because it accomplishes the fourrighteousness, material prosperity, fame and esteem of mankind.

sanskrit: rājā sapuruṣaḥ sabhyāḥ śāstraṃ gaṇakalekhakau // hiraṇyamagnirudakamaṣṭāṅgaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ /
english: The king with the attendant, courtiers, scripture, astrologer, scribe, gold, fire and water are stated to be the eight accessories in a lawsuit.

sanskrit: kāmāt krodhācca lobhācca tribhyo yasmāt pravartate // triyoniḥ kīrtyate tena trayametadvivādakṛt /
english: It is said to be having three sources because it results from the three such as lust, anger and greed. Hence these three are the cause of a lawsuit.

sanskrit: dvyabhiyogastu vijñeyaḥ śaṅkātattvābhiyogataḥ // śaṅkāṣaḍbhistu saṃsargāttattvaṣoḍhādidarśaṇāt / pakṣadvayābhisambandhāddvidvāraḥ samudāhṛtaḥ //
english: The cause of the lawsuit are two such as apprehension and firm disquisition. Among these, apprehension is known from association with six things and the genuine fault from the preceding events of six kinds. Because the suit has two sides it is said to be having two openings.

sanskrit: pūrvavādastayoḥ pakṣaḥ pratipakṣastvanantaraḥ /
english: Among these two, the first one is the plaintiff and the other one is the defendant.

sanskrit: ṛṇandeyamadeyañca yena yatra yathā ca yat / dānagrahaṇadharmaś ca ṛṇādānamiti smṛtam //
english: The term debt denotes that admitted by a person as payable or that denied by him as not payable or that which is given as gift to another.

sanskrit: svadravyaṃ yatra viśrambhānnikṣipatyaviśaṅkitaḥ / nikṣepannāma tat proktaṃ vyavahārapadambudhaiḥ //
english: One’s own property placed out of trust with another without any doubt is said by wise men to be a trust that is a matter of dispute.

sanskrit: vaṇikprabhṛtayo yatra karma sambhūya kurvate / tatsambhūyasamuptyānaṃ vyavahārapadaṃ viduḥ //
english: The place where the merchants and others collectively transact business called the active occupation is known to be a matter of dispute.

sanskrit: dattvā dravyañca samyagyaḥ punarādātumicchati / dattvāpradānikaṃ nāma tadvivādapadaṃ smṛtaṃ //
english: If one wants to take back that he has paid to another, that is called the withdrawer of a gift and is known to be the matter of dispute.

sanskrit: aśuśrūṣābhyupetyaitadvivādapadamucyate // bhṛtyānāṃ vetanasyoktādānādānavidhikriyā / vetanasyānapākarma tadvivādapadaṃ smṛtam //
