english: Having agreed to do service to another, if one refuses to do so, it is known as refusal to do service and is said to be a matter for dispute. The wage of a servant is said to be coming under the head of debts and the nonpayment of the same is deemed to be a matter of dispute.

sanskrit: nikṣiptaṃ vā paradravyaṃ naṣṭaṃ labdhvā prahṛtya vā / kikrīyate parokṣaṃ yat sa jñeyo 'svāmivikrayaḥ //
english: If one sells the entrusted property of another or the lost property of another after having got it or having stolen it without the knowledge of the owner, it is known to be selling of another’s property.

sanskrit: vikrīya paṇyaṃ mūlyena kretre yacca na dīyate / vikrīyāsampradānantadvivādapadamucyate //
english: After having sold the goods for money if the goods are not made over to the buyer, it is nondelivery of sold articles and is a matter for dispute.

sanskrit: krītvā mūlyena yat paṇyaṃ duṣkrītaṃ manyate krayī // pāṣaṇḍanaigamādīnāṃ sthitiḥ samaya ucyate /
english: If a purchaser opines that the articles bought are not good after having bought it is also a disputable thing. That condition of a wicked assuring good conduct is said to be conventional practice.

sanskrit: samayasyānapākarma tadvivādapadaṃ smṛtaṃ //
english: The transgression of the conventional practice is said to be a matter for dispute.

sanskrit: setukedāramaryādāvikṛṣṭākṛṣṭaniś cayāḥ / kṣetrādhikāre yatra syurvivādaḥ kṣetrajastu saḥ //
english: The dispute that arises in respect of the right over the land that has been determined by a bridge or a field or drawn boundaries is said to be that dispute arising from the land.

sanskrit: vaivāhiko vidhiḥ strīnāṃ yatra puṃsāñca kīrtyate / strīpuṃsayogasaṃjñantu tadvivādapadaṃ smṛtam // vibhāgorthasya paitrasya putrair yastu prakalpyate /
english: Where the marriage rite of men and women is declared that is named as the union of women and men and is a matter for dispute. That which is termed the division of the ancestral property by the sons is said to be the partition of the property and a matter of dispute by the wise men.

sanskrit: sahasā kriyate karma yat kiñcit baladarpitaiḥ / tat sāhasamiti proktaṃ vivādapadamucyate //
english: A rash act done by those haughty of their strength is said to be a crime and is declared as a matter for dispute.

sanskrit: deśajātikulādīnāmākrośatyaṅgasaṃyutam / yadvacaḥ pratikūlārthaṃ vākpāruṣyaṃ taducyate //
english: It is said to be an abusive laṅguage that is spoken out of hostility with reference to the country, caste and family and the like with gestures.

sanskrit: paragātreṣvabhidrehī hastapādāyudhādibhiḥ / agnyādibhiś copaghātair daṇḍapāruṣyamucyate //
english: It is said to be an assault if injury is inflicted on other’s bodies with hands, feet, weapons and destructive materials such as the fire.

sanskrit: akṣavajjaśalākādyair daivataṃ dyūtamucyate /
english: It is said to be divine gambling when it is played with dice, vajra diamond and rod etc.

sanskrit: pañcakriḍāvayobhiś ca prāṇidyutasamāhvayaḥ //
english: It is termed as animal gambling if it is played with animals, and birds kept for pleasure.

sanskrit: prakīrṇakaḥ punarjñeyo vyavahāro nirāśrayaḥ /
english: That dispute is again known to be a miscellaneous one if it does not rest on anything.

sanskrit: rājñāmājñāpratoghātastatkarmākaraṇantathā //
english: The violation of the command of the king as well as not carrying out that command also constitute an offence.

sanskrit: vyavahāro 'ṣṭādaśapadasteṣāṃ bhedo 'tha vai śatam /
english: Thus disputes are of eighteen kinds and there are one hundred divisions of these.

sanskrit: kriyābhedānmanuṣyānāṃ śataśākho nigadyate //
english: These hundred divisions of disputes are stated to be due to difference in the acts of men.

sanskrit: vyavahārānnṛpaḥ paśyej jñāniviprair akopanaḥ /
english: A king should examine the disputes with the help of learned brahmins without becoming angry.

sanskrit: śatrumitrasamāḥ sabhyā alobhāḥ śrutivedinaḥ //
english: They should not be greedy and they should be proficient in the scriptures.

sanskrit: apaśyatā kāryavaśāt sabhyair vipraṃ niyojayet /
english: When such men cannot be found, a brahmin should be engaged with the help of the courtiers.

sanskrit: rāgāllobhādbhayādvāpi smṛtyapetādikāriṇaḥ // sabhyāḥ pṛthak pṛthag daṇḍyā vivādādvdiguṇo damaḥ /
english: Judges swerving from the codes of law and the like out of attachment, greed or fear should be punished separately. The fine is double as that for a quarrel.

sanskrit: smṛtyācāraeṣvyapetena mārgeṇa dharṣitaḥ paraiḥ // āvedayati yadrājñe vyavahārapadaṃ hi tat /
english: If a person that has been annoyed by others by following a method that is contrary to the codes of law and practice, informs the king, that is known to be a matter for dispute.

sanskrit: pratyarthino 'grato lekhyaṃ yathā veditamarthinā // samāmāsatadardhāharnāmajātyādicihnitam /
english: The year, month, fortnight, day, name, caste and the marks on the body should be recorded by the complainant as known to him in the presence of the defendant.

sanskrit: śrutārthasyottaraṃ lekhyaṃ pūrvāvedakasannidhau // tapto 'rthī lekhayetsadyaḥ pratijñātārthasādhanam /
english: The reply of the defendant after having heard that of the complainant should be recorded in the presence of the complainant. Then the complainant should record the arguments that would accomplish his statement.

sanskrit: tatsiddhau siddhamāpnoti viparītamato 'nyathā //
english: He would get success if it is established or the contrary if otherwise.

sanskrit: catuṣpādvyavahāroyaṃ vivādeṣūpadarśitaḥ /
english: These are the four steps indicated by experts in disputes.

sanskrit: abhiyogamanistīrya nainaṃ pratyabhiyojayet // abhiyuktañca nānyena tyaktaṃ viprakṛtiṃ nayet /
english: Without having settled a plaint, the court should not accept a crosssuit. One should not take up a case rejected by another tribunal.

sanskrit: kuryāt pratyabhiyogantu kalahe sāhaseṣu ca // ubhayoḥ pratibhūrgrāhyaḥ samarthaḥ kāmyanirṇaye /
english: A countersuit could be made only in the case of a quarrel or violence. An appropriate bail should be collected from both the parties in deciding optional cases.

sanskrit: nihnave bhāvito dadyāddhanaṃ rājñe tu tatsamam //
english: One should pay a fine of equal amount to the king for the denial of an established matter.

sanskrit: mithyābhiyogād dviguṇamabhiyogāddhanaṃ haret / sāhasasteyapāruṣyeṣvabhiśāpātyaye striyāḥ //
english: Double the fine has to be collected for a false plaint from the plaintiff. Cases of rash acts, theft, abusive laṅguage, pronouncing a curse and disappearance of women should be examined at once.

sanskrit: vicārayetsadyaḥ eva kālo 'nyatrecchayā smṛtaḥ /
english: It has been said that in other cases, they may be put off to a different time optionally.

sanskrit: deśāddeśāntaraṃ yāti sṛkkaṇī parileḍhi ca // lalāṭaṃ svidyate cāsya mukhavaivarṇyameva ca / svabhāvādvikṛtaṃ gacchenmanovākkāyakarmabhiḥ //
english: One that wanders from one place to another, one that licks the corners of the mouth, one whose forehead perspires, one whose face gets discoloured and one who by his nature gets changed in his thought, speech and physical actions is said to be a defamer for a plaint and witness.

sanskrit: sandigdhārthaṃ svatantro yaḥ sādhayedyaś ca niṣpatet // na cāhūto vadet kiñciddhanī daṇḍyaś ca sa smṛtaḥ /
english: A witness uttering words of ambiguous import, uttering voluntarily something not being summoned, falling down when questioned, not telling something when summoned is known to be punishable if he is rich.

sanskrit: sākṣiṣūbhayataḥ satsu sākṣiṇaḥ pūrvavādinaḥ // pūrvapakṣe 'dharībhūte bhavantyuttaravādinaḥ /
english: Among the witnesses of both the sides, the witness of the plaintiff should be heard first. When the examination of the plaintiff is completed, the examination of the defendant would be done.

sanskrit: sagaṇaścedvivādaḥ syāttatra hīnantu dāpayet // dattaṃ paṇaṃ vasañcaiva dhanino dhanameva ca / chalannirasya dūtena vyavahārānnayennṛpaḥ //
english: If the dispute is between members of the same clan, the younger should be punished. The king should conduct the proceedings with respect to money paid or property or riches of a rich man after removing the fraud by employing the messenger.

sanskrit: nihnute nikhilānekamekadeśavibhāvitam //
english: The king should confiscate all treasures, if it is concealed wholly or partly.

sanskrit: dāpyaḥ sarvānnṛpeṇārthānna grāhyastvaniveditaḥ /
english: All such properties should not pass over to the sovereign unless voluntarily offered by the parties.

sanskrit: arthaśāstrāddhi balavaddharmaśāstramiti sthitiḥ / pramāṇaṃ likhitaṃ bhuktiḥ sākṣiṇaśceti kirtitam //
english: The codes of law are deemed to be stronger than the science of wealth. The documents, actual enjoyment and the witnesses are said to be evidences in a law suit.

sanskrit: eṣāmanyatamābhāve divyānyatamamucyate /
english: An oath is prescribed in the absence of one of these.

sanskrit: sarveṣveva vivādeṣu balavatyuttarā kriyā //
english: The later incidents are stronger in all the law suits.

sanskrit: ādhau pratigrahe krīte pūrvā tu balavattarā /
english: The preliminary events are stronger in the case of a mortgage, gift or purchase.

sanskrit: pareṇa bhujyamānā yā dhanasya daśavārṣikī / ādhisaumopaniḥkṣepajaḍabāladhanair vinā // tathopanidhirājastrīśrotriyāṇāṃ dhanair api /
english: The wealth enjoyed by another could be disputed by the legitimate owner only within ten years, except in the case of a mortage, an encroachment, a property held in trust, wealth belonging to an idiot or an infant, or treasures or wealth belonging to the sovereign, to a woman or a brahmin.

sanskrit: ādhyādīnāṃ vihartāraṃ dhanine dāpayeddhanaṃ // daṇḍyaṃ ca tatsamaṃ rājñe śaktyapekṣyamathāpi vā /
english: One who sells away a mortgaged property should pay the value to the owner of the property and pay an equal amount of fine or that befitting his ability to the king.

sanskrit: āgamopyadhiko bhuktiṃ vinā pūrvakramāgatāṃ // āgamopi balannaiva bhuktiḥ stokāpi yatra na /
english: Possession is title, even in the absence of proof of continuous enjoyment. But possession without proof of even a little enjoyment has no strength for the title.

sanskrit: āgamena viśuddhena bhogo yāti pramāṇatām //
english: An enjoyment with good possession of a property becomes valid.

sanskrit: aviśuddhāgamo bhogaḥ prāmāṇyaṃ nādhigacchati /
english: An enjoyment without proper possession could not be valid.

sanskrit: āgamastu kṛto yena so 'bhiyuktastamuddharet //
english: The possession made by the trespasser should be recovered by a suit.

sanskrit: na tatsutastatsuto vā bhuktistatra garīyasī /
english: It would be of no avail that the present possessor had got it from the son or the son’s son of the original trespasser.

sanskrit: yobhiyuktaḥ paretaḥ syāt tasya ṛkthāttamuddharet //
english: In the case of the death of the possessor, the value of the property should be recovered from the property left by him.

sanskrit: na tatra kāraṇaṃ bhuktirāgamena vinākṛtā /
english: An enjoyment without a sound possession could not be a valid reason against that.

sanskrit: balopādhivinirvṛttān vyavahārānnivartayet //
english: The king should prevent the encroachment by force or deceit.

sanskrit: strīnaktamantarāgāravahiḥśatrukṛtas tathā / mattonmattārtavyasanibālabhītaprayojitaḥ // asambaddhakṛtaś caiva vyavahāro na siddhyati /
english: A transaction done by a woman or in the night or inside a room or outside or made by an enemy as well as that done by a drunkard, lunatic or one addicted to evil, an infant or a frightened one or one that is defective is not valid.

sanskrit: pranaṣṭādhiśataṃ deyaṃ nṛpeṇa dhanine dhanaṃ //
english: The king should cause the mortgager to return to the mortgagee the property mortgaged.

sanskrit: deyañcaurahṛtaṃ dravyaṃ rājñā janapadāya tu //
english: The king should pay to the village headman the property stolen by a thief.

sanskrit: aśītibhāgo vṛddhiḥ syānmāsi māsi sabandhake /
english: The interest relating to a loan for which interest accrues every month is one eightieth of the amount lent.

sanskrit: varṇakramācchataṃ dvitricatuṣpañcakamanyathā //
english: Otherwise the interest should be two, three, four or five per cent in the order of the castes to which they belonged.

sanskrit: saptatistu paśustrīṇāṃ rasasyāṣṭaguṇā parā / vastradhānyahiraṇyānāṃ catustridviguṇā tathā //
english: It is seventieth part in the case of animals and women, eight times in the case of food, four or three or two times in the case of dress, food grains, gold and other things.

sanskrit: grāmāntarāttu daśakaṃ sāmudrādapi viṃśatiṃ /
english: If the money is lent to a person of a different village, it should be ten per cent and if beyond the ocean, it should be twenty per cent.

sanskrit: dadyurvā svakṛtāṃ vṛddhiṃ sarve sarvāsu jātiṣu //
english: Members of all castes may pay rates of interest of their choice.

sanskrit: prapanna sādhayannarthaṃ na vācyā nṛpatirbhavet /
english: A king would not be censurable by paying money to those in need.

sanskrit: sādhyamāno nṛpaṃ gaccheddaṇḍyo dāpyaś ca taddhanaṃ // gṛhītārthaḥ kramāddāpyo dhanināmadhamarṇikaḥ /
english: One that would go to the king after having obtained a loan would be liable for punishment and that money should be confiscated. A debtor may pay the borrowed money to a creditor in instalments.

sanskrit: datvā tu brāhmaṇāyādau nṛpatestadanantaram //
english: One has to pay to the king after paying to a brahmin first.

sanskrit: rājñādhamarṇiko dāpyaḥ sādhitāddaśakaṃ smṛtam / pañcakantu śataṃ dāpyaḥ prāptārtho hy uttamarṇakaḥ //
english: It is said that the debtor should be made to pay ten per cent of the loan by the king as fine. In case the debtor had realised his money back, five per cent of the amount should be made payable to the king.

sanskrit: hīnajātiṃ parikṣīṇamṛṇārthaṃ karma kārayet /
english: A debtor belonging to the low caste and impoverished should be made to work in lieu of the debt.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇastu parikṣīṇaḥ śanair dāpyo yathodayam //
english: A brahmin debtor who is impoverished should be made to pay leisurely after the betterment.

sanskrit: dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇāti prayuktaṃ yaḥ svakandhanam / madhyasthasthāpitaṃ tatsyādvardhate na tataḥ paraṃ //
english: The money that the creditor does not accept when offered, should be deposited with an arbitrator and it would cease to bear any interest.

sanskrit: ṛkthagrāha ṛṇaṃ dāpyo yoṣidgrāhastathaiva ca / putro 'nanyāśritadravyaḥ putrahīnasya ṛkthinaḥ // avibhuktaiḥ kuṭumbārthaṃ yadṛṇantu kṛtambhavet /
english: One that inherits a property, as well as the wife of a deceased person that inherits the property should be made to pay the incurred debt. The debt of a sonless owner of a property should be paid by the person that inherits the property. The debt that is incurred on an undivided family for the sake of the family should also be paid similarly by the person that inherited that property.

sanskrit: dadyustadṛkthinaḥ prete proṣite vā kuṭumbini //
english: When the head of a family is dead or had gone abroad, it should be done similarly.

sanskrit: na yoṣit patiputrābhyāṃ na putreṇa kṛtaṃ pitā /
english: The wife is not bound to repay the loan incurred by the husband or the sons and the father is not bound to repay the loan incurred by the son.

sanskrit: dadyādṛte kuṭumbārthānna patiḥ strīkṛtaṃ tathā //
english: The husband need not repay the loan incurred by the wife unless it has been taken for the sake of the family.

sanskrit: gopaśauṇḍikaśainūṣarajakavyādhayoṣitāṃ / ṛṇaṃ dadyātpatistvāsāṃ yasmādvṛttistadāśrayā //
english: The husbands of the women of the gopa a guard, śauṇḍika a distiller and seller of spirituous liquors, śailūṣa an actor or dancer, rajaka a washerman or vyādha a hunter castes should repay the loan incurred by them because their livelihood is dependent on them those women.

sanskrit: pratipannaṃ striyā deyaṃ patyā vā saha yat kṛtaṃ / svayaṃ kṛtaṃ vā yadṛṇaṃ nānyastrī dātumarhati // pitari proṣite prete vyasābhiplute 'tha vā /
english: The wife need not repay any other loan except that incurred by her husband with her consent, or that incurred jointly with her husband or that incurred by herself. When the father has gone abroad, is dead, overpowered by misfortune, the loan incurred by him should be paid by

sanskrit: putrapautrair ṛṇandeyaṃ nihnave sākṣibhāvitam //
english: the sons and grandsons. If the loan incurred by the father is not known to the son, it should be paid on being established by the witness.

sanskrit: vṛthā dānaṃ tathaiveha putro dadyānna paitṛkam // bhrātṝṇāmatha dampatyoḥ pituḥ putrasya caiva hi / pratibhāvyamṛṇaṃ grāhyamavibhaktena ca smṛtam //
english: The son need not repay the debt incurred by the father by drinking or wenching or by way of the balance of fine inflicted by the court or by making improper gifts. A loan should be got by a member of the undivided family against the surety of the brothers, the husband and wife, the father or the son.

sanskrit: darśane pratyaye dāne pratibhāvyaṃ vidhīyate / ādhau tu vitathe dāpyā vitathasya sutā api //
english: A surety consists in being a witness, or in giving a guarantee for the repayment of a debt. When a property is pledged by a person that has no right of possession, the sons of that mortgager should be liable to repay the incurred loan.

sanskrit: darśanapratibhūryatra mṛtaḥ prātyayiko 'pi vā / na tatputrā dhanaṃ dadyurdadyurdānāya ye sthitāḥ //
english: The sons of the deceased persons who had been sureties as witnesses or as guarantors, need not pay that money. But those who had induced to make the payment should pay in similar cases.

sanskrit: bahavaḥ syuryadi svāṃśair dadyuḥ pratibhuvo dhanam /
english: In case if there were many guarantors to an advance made, the guarantors should be made to pay their respective shares.

sanskrit: ekacchāyāśriteṣveṣu dhanikasya yathā ruci //
english: A creditor will have the choice of realising his dues from any one of the sureties of the joint bond.

sanskrit: pratibhūrdāpito yatra prakāśaṃ dhanine dhanam / dviguṇaṃ pratidātavyamṛṇikaistasya tadbhavet // svasantatistrīpaśavyaṃ dhānyaṃ dviguṇameva ca /
english: A debtor should pay double the amount to his surety, in case if the latter pays the loan with the knowledge of the debtor. If the hypothecated thing is one’s own progeny or the wife or cattle or grains, double the amount has to be paid to redeem.

sanskrit: vastraṃ caturguṇaṃ proktaṃ rasaścāṣṭaguṇas tathā //
english: It is said that four times that in the case of dressing material and eight times that in the case of condiments has to be paid to redeem.

sanskrit: ādhiḥ praṇaśyet dviguṇe dhane yadi na mokṣyate /
english: A mortgage shall be forfeited if that is not redeemed by paying double the amount.

sanskrit: kāle kālakṛtaṃ naśyet phalabhogyo na naśyati // gopyādhibhogyo nāvṛddhiḥ sopakāre 'tha bhāvite /
english: But it would not cease if enjoyments of the proceeds have been ageed upon. Interest need not be paid on a thing left as a deposit or in a deposit that has been left for enjoyment.

sanskrit: naṣṭo deyo vinaṣṭaś ca daivarājakṛtādṛte // ādheḥ svīkaraṇātsiddhaurakṣamāṇopyasāratām /
english: If the mortgaged property is lost on account of any reason other than fate or the king, it should be restored to its original state. On the acceptance of the hypothecated property by the mortgagee, it becomes valid.

sanskrit: yātaścedanya ādheyo dhanabhāg vā dhanī bhavet //
english: Otherwise the creditor should be paid money in lieu of it.

sanskrit: caritraṃ bandhakakṛtaṃ savṛddhaṃ dāpayedvanaṃ / satyaṅkārakṛtaṃ dravyaṃ dviguṇaṃ pratidāpayet //
english: Money borrowed by pledging one’s character, should be repaid together with interest. Money borrowed on a solemn affirmation should be returned double that. A mortgaged property should be released by the mortgagee, when it is sought for.

sanskrit: upasthitasya moktavya ādhirdaṇḍo 'nyathā bhavet /
english: Otherwise he would be liable for punishment.

sanskrit: prayojake sati dhanaṃ kulenyasyādhimāpnuyāt // tatkālakṛtamūlyo vā tatra tiṣṭhedavṛddhikaḥ / vinā dhāraṇakādvāpi vikrīṇīte sasākṣikam //
english: If the moneylender belongs to one’s own family and advances money on the security of one of his coparceners, he should be looked upon as a mortgagee. The value of that property should be determined according to the market at that time and it should remain without any interest.

sanskrit: yadā tu dviguṇībhūtamṛṇamādhau tadā khalu / mocyaścādhistadutpādya praviṣṭe dviguṇe dhane //
english: The property may be sold without the consent of the debtor in his very presence, if the debt on the mortgage gets doubled. The mortgaged property should be released if double the amount is produced by the debtor.

sanskrit: vyasanasthamanākhyāya haste 'nyasya yadarpayet / dravyaṃ tadaupanidhikaṃ pratideyaṃ tathaiva tat //
english: A packet that has been entrusted with another without disclosing its contents is said to be a deposit and it should be returned in the same condition.

sanskrit: na dāpyo 'pahṛtaṃ tattu rājadaivakataskaraiḥ /
english: If it the contents of that packet has been destroyed by the acts of the king, fate or the robbers, it need not be restored.

sanskrit: preṣaścenmārgite datte dāpyo daṇḍaś ca tatsamam // ājīvan svecchayā daṇḍyo dāpyastaccāpi sodayaṃ / yācitāvāhitanyāse nikṣepeṣvapyayaṃ vidhiḥ //
english: If that is found after search and the custodian returns it after being urged to do so, the custodian should be punished to pay an amount equal to that. If the custodian wilfully derives benefit from that, he is punishable and should pay together with the benefit.

sanskrit: tapasvino dānaśīlāḥ kulīnāḥ satyavādinaḥ / dharmapradhānā ṛjavaḥ putravanto dhanānvitāḥ // pañcayajñakriyāyuktāḥ sākṣiṇaḥ pañca vā trayaḥ /
english: The same rule holds good in the case of deposits such as yācita, āhita and nyāsa. There should be five or three witnesses such as those who are ascetics, munificent, born in noble families, truthful, virtuous, honest, having progeny, wealthy and regular in performing the pañcayajña.

sanskrit: yathājāti yathāvarṇa sarve sarveṣu vā smṛtāḥ //
english: They may all belong to the same jāti or varṇa or from all the castes.

sanskrit: strīvṛddhabālakitavamattonmattābhiśastakāḥ / raṅgāvatāripāṣaṇḍikūṭakṛdvikalendriyāḥ // patitāptānnasambandhisahāyariputaskarāḥ /
english: Those who are not suitable to be witnesses are women, old men, children, cheats, intoxicated, lunatics, injured, actors, heretics, men of the writer caste, those having defective sense organs, those that take food from degraded persons, relatives or friends or enemies of the persons contesting the dispute and thieves.

sanskrit: amākṣiṇaḥ sarvasākṣī cauryapāruṣyasāhase //
english: All people are deemed to be witnesses in cases of thefts, violence and rashness.

sanskrit: ubhayānumataḥ sākṣī bhavatyekopi dharmavit /
english: A virtuous man accepted by both the parties may be a witness.

sanskrit: abruvan hi naraḥ sākṣyamṛṇaṃ sadaśabandhakam // rājñā sarvaṃ pradāpyaḥ syāt ṣaṭcatvāriṃśake 'hnani /
english: A person that refuses to answer the questions relating to a loan in which interest at the rate of ten per cent has been allowed should be made by the king to pay the full amount together with interest within fortysix days.

sanskrit: na dadāti hi yaḥ sākṣyaṃ jānannapi narādhamaḥ // sa kūṭasākṣiṇāṃ pāpaistulyo daṇḍena caiva hi /
english: The vilest person that does not depose the facts even though he is aware of them, is considered as equivalent to the sins of false witnesses and is also liable for similar punishment.

sanskrit: sākṣiṇaḥ śrāvayedvādiprativādisamīpagān // ye pātakakṛtāṃ lokā mahāpātakināṃ tathā / agnidānāñca ye lokā ye ca strībālaghātināṃ // tān sarvān samavāpnoti yaḥ sākṣyamanṛtaṃ vadet /
english: The witnesses of the plaintiff as well as the defendant should be questioned in the presence of the parties as follows “A person making a false statement would incur all the sins that would accrue to the sinners, deadly sinners, incendiaries and the murderers of women and children.

sanskrit: sukṛtaṃ yattvayā kiñcijjanmāntaraśataiḥ kṛtam // tatsarvaṃ tasya jānīhi yaṃ parājayase mṛṣā /
english: You also know that the few good deeds that you had done in hundreds of your previous births, would befall that person whom you defeat by fraud.”

sanskrit: dvaidhe bahūnāṃ vacanaṃ sameṣu guṇināntathā // guṇidvaidhe tu vacanaṃ grāhyaṃ ye guṇavattarāḥ /
english: If the statements of the witnesses of both the sides are equal, then that of the virtuous should be accepted. In the case of conflict among the views of the virtuous, the statement of more virtuous should be accepted.

sanskrit: yasyocuḥ sākṣiṇaḥ satyāṃ pratijñāṃ sa jayī bhavet //
english: That person whose witnesses make the truthful declaration, would become the winner.

sanskrit: anyathā vādino yasya dhrūvastasya parājayaḥ /
english: That plaintiff whose witnesses are different from the above, his defeat is certain.

sanskrit: ukte 'pi sākṣibhiḥ sākṣye yadyanye guṇavattarāḥ // dviguṇā vānyathā brūyuḥ kūṭāḥ syuḥ pūrvasākṣiṇaḥ /
english: When a set of witnesses have deposed, if more virtuous men or double the previous number make statements against that, the previous witnesses become false witnesses.

sanskrit: pṛthak pṛthagdaṇḍanīyāḥ kūṭakṛtsākṣiṇas tathā //
english: Then the forgers and false witnesses should be punished separately.

sanskrit: vivādāddviguṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ vivāsyo brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
english: The punishment would be double that of the fee for litigation. A brahmin witness in similar circumstances should be banished from the country.

sanskrit: yaḥ sākṣyaṃ śrāvito 'nyebhyo nihnute tattamovṛtaḥ // sa dāpyo 'ṣṭaguṇam daṇḍaṃ brāhmaṇantu vivāsayet /
english: A person that conceals, on account of his ignorance, the statements of evidences heard from others, should be fined eight times. A brahmin in similar circumstances should be banished from the country.

sanskrit: varṇināṃ hi badho yatra tatra sākṣya.anṛtaṃ vadet //
english: A false statement may be made only when a brahmin stands to be capitally punished.

sanskrit: yaḥ kaścidartho 'bhimataḥ svarucyā tu parasparaṃ / lekhyaṃ tu sākṣimat kāryaṃ tasmin dhanikapūrvakam //
english: If a property has been accepted after mutual consent of two parties, the loanbond should be endorsed by the witness in the presence of the creditor.

sanskrit: samāmāsatadarhāhar nāmajātisvagotrajaiḥ / sabrahmacārikātmīyapitṛnāmādicihnitam //
english: That bond should bear the details such as the year, month, fortnight, date, name, caste, one’s own clan, and the name of one’s fellowstudent, one’s own name and that of the father etc.

sanskrit: samāpte 'rthe ṛṇī nāma svahastena niveśayet / mataṃ me 'mukaputrasya yadatroparilekhitaṃ // sākṣiṇaś ca svahastena pitṛnāmakapūrvakam / atrāhamamukaḥ sākṣī likheyuriti te samāḥ //
english: When the bond has been completed, the debtor should enter his name in his own handwriting and also write, “, so and so, son of so and so, fully agree to the statements made above.” Then the witnesses also should write their names after having written the names of their fathers and write “, so and so, son of so and so, put my name as a witness”.

sanskrit: alipijña ṛṇī yaḥ syālekayet svamatantu saḥ /
english: An unlettered debtor should cause the writer of the deed to write his assent.

sanskrit: sākṣī vā sākṣiṇānyena sarvasākṣisamīpataḥ // ubhayābhyarthitenaitanmayā hy amukasūnunā /
english: Then the scribe of the deed should write “ so and so, son of so and so, being requested by both the parties have written this deed” and then write the deed.

sanskrit: likhitaṃ hy amukeneti lekhako 'thāntato likhet // vināpi sākṣibhir lekhyaṃ svahastalikhitañca yat /
english: A deed that has been written in the handwriting of the mortgager is valid even without the attestation by the witnesses, except in cases where undue compulsion had been made.

sanskrit: ṛṇaṃ lekhyakṛtaṃ deyaṃ puruṣaistribhireva tu /
english: The debt mentioned in a deed has to be discharged by the three men the debtor, the son or grandson.

sanskrit: ādhistu bhujyate tāvadyāvattanna pradīyate //
english: A mortgage remains in force until the pledge is not redeemed.

sanskrit: deśāntarasthe durlekhye naṣṭonmṛṣṭe hṛte tathā / bhinne cchinne tathā dagdhe lekhyamanyattu kārayet //
english: A new deed has to be written when the old one has been taken abroad or the original writing has been forged or lost or erased or seized or torn or mutilated or burnt.

sanskrit: yuktiprāptikriyācihnasambandhāgamahetubhiḥ // lekhyasya pṛṣṭhe 'bhilikhet praviṣṭamadhamarṇinaḥ /
english: One should record in his own hand, things that are explanatory of ambiguous terms, on the back of the deed, such as total, receipt, investigation, indication, relation, addition and means.

sanskrit: dhanī copagataṃ dadyāt svahastaparicihnitam // datvarṇaṃ pāṭayellekhyaṃ śuddhyai cānyattu kārayet /
english: The creditor should endorse all that he has received from the debtor with his own mark. A deed should be destroyed after paying the debts and another deed of release should be executed.

sanskrit: sākṣimacca bhavedyattu taddātavyaṃ sasākṣikaṃ //
english: It should duly be attested by the witnesses, if the original one was also made in the presence of witnesses.

sanskrit: tulāgnyāpo viṣaṃ koṣo divyānīha viśuddhaye /
english: The balance, fire, water, poison and holy water are the divine ordeals to test one’s innocence.

sanskrit: mahābhiyogeṣvetāni śīrṣakasthe 'bhiyoktari //
english: These ordeals should be instituted in cases of great offences when the accuser agrees to undergo punishment.

sanskrit: rucyā vānyataraḥ kuryāditaro vartayecchiraḥ /
english: Or one may be made to undergo the ordeal, and the other to undertake the agreement to undergo punishment.

sanskrit: vināpi śīrṣakāt kuryānnṛpadrohe 'tha pātake //
english: They may be made to undergo an ordeal even without the agreement in cases of treason and sin.

sanskrit: nāsahasrāddharet phālaṃ na tulānna viṣantathā /
english: One should not carry the ploughshare, the balance, or the poison for matters of less than a thousand coins.

sanskrit: nṛpārtheṣvabhiyogeṣu vaheyuḥ śucayaḥ sadā //
english: In the case of treasons one should always agree to carry these ordeals to show their innocence.

sanskrit: sahasrārthe tulādīni koṣamalpe 'pi dāpayet / śatārdhaṃ dāpayecchuddhamaśuddho daṇḍabhāg bhavet //
english: The balance and other ordeals are instituted in the case of matters exceeding one thousand and the holy water is instituted even for minor offences. If it is lesser than that and the innocence has been established in the ordeal, one should pay fifty coins.

sanskrit: sacelasnātamāhūya sūryodaya upoṣitam / kārayetdarvadivyāni nṛpabrāhmaṇasannidhau //
english: The accused that has bathed together with the dress and observed fast should be called up and made to carry all the ordeals in the presence of the king and brahmins.

sanskrit: tulā strībālavṛddhāndhapaṅgubrāhmaṇarogiṇāṃ /
english: The balance is for women, boys, the aged, the blind, the lame, brahmins and the sick.

sanskrit: agnirjvalaṃ vā śūdrasya yavāḥ sapta viṣasya vā //
english: The ordeals of fire, water and seven yava weights of poison are for the śūdra.

sanskrit: tulādhāraṇavidvadbhirabhiyuktastulāśritaḥ /
english: The accused that is resorting to the balance is weighed by those conversant with balances.

sanskrit: pratimānasamībhūto rekhāṃ kṛtvāvatāritaḥ //
english: After the balance comes to rest, line is drawn and the accused is taken off.

sanskrit: ādityacandrāvanilo 'nalaś ca dyaurbhūmirāpohṛdayaṃ yamaś ca / ahaś ca rātriś ca ubhe ca sandhye dharmaś ca jānāti narasya vṛttam //
english: The accused should begin the ordeal thus “The Sun, the Moon, the Wind, the Fire, the Sky, the Earth, the Waters, the Heart, the god of Death, the Day, the Night, the two Twilights, as well as the god of Virtue know the acts of man! O Balance! You are the abode of truth.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tule satyadhāmāsi purā devair vinirmitā /
english: You were created by the gods in olden days.

sanskrit: satyaṃ vadasva kalyāṇi saṃśayānmāṃ vimocaya //
english: Speak the truth. O Auspicious one! Deliver me from suspicion.

sanskrit: yadyasmi pāpakṛnmātastato māṃ tvamadho naya /
english: If am a sinner, O mother! Then lead me downwards.

sanskrit: śuddhaścedgamayordhvammāṃ tulāmityabhimantrayet //
english: If am pure then take me upwards.” Thus one should address the balance.

sanskrit: karau vimṛditavrīherlakṣayitvā tato nyaset / saptāśvaptyasya patrāṇi tāvat sūtreṇa veṣṭayet //
english: One should mark the hands of a person that has rubbed rice, and then place seven leaves of the holy fig tree on those hands and fix them with a string wrapped as many times.

sanskrit: tvameva sarvabhūtānāmantaś carasi pāvaka /
english: Then he should be made to utter as follows “O Agni! O Purifier! You reside in all beings.

sanskrit: sākṣivat puṇyapāpebhyo brūhi satyaṅgare mama // tasyetyuktavato lauhaṃ pañcāśatpalikaṃ samam /
english: O Truthful one! speak the truth like a witness about my good deeds and sins.” After he has said this, the judge should place a redhot, round ball of iron weighing fifty palas on both his hands.

sanskrit: sa tamādāya saptaiva maṇḍalāni śatair vrajet /
english: After he has taken that, he should walk slowly through the seven circles.

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśāṅgulakaṃ jñeyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tāvadantaram //
english: The inner space of the circle is known as sixteen aṅgulas four finger breadth.

sanskrit: muktvāgniṃ mṛditavrīhiradagdhaḥ śuddhimāpnuyāt /
english: After he has released the fire and rubbed rice between his hand, the one that is not burnt gets freed as innocent.

sanskrit: antarā patite piṇḍe sandehe vā punarharet //
english: If the ball falls in between or if there is doubt, he should carry it again.

sanskrit: pavitrāṇāṃ pavitra tvaṃ śodhyaṃ śodhaya pāvana /
english: O Purifier! You purify the accused.

sanskrit: satyena mābhirakṣasva varuṇetyabhiśastakam // nābhidaghnodakasthasya gṛhītvorū jalaṃ viśet /
english: O Varuṇa! You protect me with the truth.” Having addressed the water thus, one should enter the water holding onto the thighs of a man standing in water upto his navel.

sanskrit: samakālamiṣuṃ muktamānīyānyo javo naraḥ // yadi tasminnimagnāṅgaṃ paśyecca śuddhimāpnuyāt /
english: His innocence would be established, if one bringing back an arrow simultaneously discharged, finds him fully dived into the water.

sanskrit: tvaṃ viṣa brahmaṇaḥ putra satyadharme vyavasthita // trāyasvāsmādabhīśāpāt satyena bhava me 'mṛtam /
english: In the case of the ordeal of poison one should address the poison as follows “O Poison! the son of Brahmā One established in truth and Virtue! Deliver me with your truth from this curse.

sanskrit: evamuktvā viṣaṃ sārṅgaṃ bhakṣayeddhimaśailajaṃ //
english: You become ambrosia for me.” After having said thus, he should take the śārṅga poison that is got from the Himalaya mountain.

sanskrit: yasya vegair vinā jīrṇaṃ śuddhiṃ tasya vinirdiśet /
english: His purity should be declared if he could assimilate the poison without vomitting.

sanskrit: devānugrān samabhyarcya tatsnānodakamāharet //
english: Alternatively, one should collect the waters for bathing dreadful gods after having worshipped them.

sanskrit: saṃśrāvya pāpayettasmājjalāttu prasṛtitrayam /
english: He should proclaim that he has not done the crime and drink three handfuls of that water.

sanskrit: ācaturdaśamādahno yasya no rājadaivikam // vyasanaṃ jāyate ghoraṃ sa śuddhaḥ syādasaṃśayam /
english: He should be deemed undoubtedly pure if no dreadful malady afflicts him within fourteen days.

sanskrit: satyavāhanaśastrāṇi govījakanakāni ca // devatāgurupādāś ca iṣṭāpūrtakṛtāni ca /
english: Truth, vehicles, weapons, cattle, grain and gold, the feet of the gods and preceptors and the consecrated tanks are the easy oaths proclaimed for minor matters.

sanskrit: ityete sukarāḥ proktāḥ śapathāḥ svalpasaṃśaye //
english: The word jāti denotes the castes in general and the word varṇa denotes the four principal castes. A kind of grain.

sanskrit: vibhāgañcet pitā kuryādicchayā vibhajet sutān / jyeṣṭhaṃ vā śreṣṭhabhāgena sarve vā syuḥ samāṃśinaḥ //
english: In the morning and in the evening. The poison got from the śṛṅga plant. A father that desires to partition his properties, should divide them either equally among his sons, or set apart a greater portion for the eldest son.

sanskrit: yadi dadyāt samānaṃśān kāryāḥ patnyaḥ samāṃśikāḥ / na dattaṃ strīdhanaṃ yāsāṃ bhartrā vā śvaśurena vā // śaktasthānīhamānasya kiñciddatvā pṛthak kriyā /
english: The wives that had not been given private property by their husbands or fathersinlaw, should be given a share in the division, if equal divisions are made for the sons. After having given a little of the share to the wealthy that does not wish to have the share then, the division should be made afterwards.

sanskrit: nyūnādhikavibhaktānāṃ dharmyaś ca pitṛnā kṛtaḥ //
english: Unequal divisions made by the father should be held as legal.

sanskrit: vibhajeyuḥ sutāḥ pitrorūrdhvamṛkthamṛṇaṃ samam / māturduhitaraḥ śeṣamṛṇāttābhya ṛte 'nnayaḥ //
english: The sons should equally divide among themselves the liabilities of their father afterwards. The outstanding debts of the mother should be borne by the daughters, if they had no progeny.

sanskrit: pitṛdravyāvināśena yadanyat svayamarjayet / maitramaudvāhikañcaiva dāyādānānna tadbhavet //
english: That which one has earned by his effort without the destruction of the paternal property, that acquired from friends as a gift and through marriage, cannot be claimed by the coparteners for a share.

sanskrit: sāmānyārthasamutthāne vibhāgastu samaḥ smṛtaḥ /
english: The benefits of a common property should be divided equally.

sanskrit: anekapitṛkāṇāntu pitṛto bhāgakalpanā //
english: The sons of different fathers forming an undivided family should take their shares according to the shares of their fathers.

sanskrit: bhūryāpitā mahopāttā nibandho dravyameva vā / tatra syāt sadṛśaṃ svāmyaṃ pituḥ putrasya cobhayoḥ //
english: Both the father and the son would be entitled to equal shares in the property or wealth of the land acquired by the grandfather.

sanskrit: vibhakteṣu suto jātaḥ savarṇāyāṃ vibhāgabhāk / dṛśyādvā tadvibhāgaḥ syādāyavyayaviśodhitāt //
english: If a son is born to a man through his wife of his own caste after the division of the property, a share should be set apart, even after the settlement of the accounts after it is seen.

sanskrit: kramādabhyāgataṃ dravyaṃ hṛtamabhyuddharecca yaḥ / dāyādebhyo na taddadyādvidyayā labdhameva ca //
english: One should not give to the coparceners an ancestral property that was lost and recovered by him, as well as that acquired by his own skill.

sanskrit: pitṛbhyāṃ yasya yaddattaṃ tattasyaiva dhanaṃ bhavet / piturūrdhvaṃ vibhajatāṃ mātāpyaṃśaṃ samaṃ haret //
english: The property that has been given to one by his parents would be his own. But the mother also would have an equal share in the property that has been divided by the grandfather.

sanskrit: asaṃskṛtāstu saṃskāryā bhrātṛbhiḥ pūrvasaṃskṛtaiḥ / bhāginyaś ca nijādaṃśāddatvāṃśantu turīyakaṃ //
english: Marriage of the unmarried sisters should be done by the brothers already married in the event of the death of the father by giving a fourth part of their share.

sanskrit: catuḥstridvyekabhāgāḥ syurvarṇaśo brāhmaṇātmajāḥ / kṣatrajāstridvyekabhāgā viḍjāstu dvyekabhāginaḥ //
english: The sons of a brahmin father would be eligible for four, three, two or one share respectively according to the caste of their mothers. Similarly the sons of a warrior caste would be eligible for three, two or one shares and that of a tradesman for two or one shares.

sanskrit: anyonyāpahṛtaṃ dravyaṃ vibhakte yattu dṛśyate /
english: The property that has been wrongly taken possession of by somebody and divided should again be equally divided.

sanskrit: tat punaste samair aṃśair vibhajeranniti sthitiḥ //
english: That is the practice.

sanskrit: aputreṇa parakṣetre niyogotpāditaḥ sutaḥ / ubhayorapyasāvṛkthī piṇḍadātā ca dharmataḥ //
english: A son got by one not having a son by niyoga through another’s wife inherits the properties of both the parents. He is allowed by the codes of law to do the obsequies of his father.

sanskrit: auraso dharmapatnījastatsamaḥ putrikāsutaḥ /
english: A son born to one through his lawful wife is called aurasa legitimate.

sanskrit: kṣetrajaḥ kṣetrajātastu sagotreṇetareṇa vā // gṛhe pracchanna utpanno gūḍhajastu sutaḥ smṛtaḥ /
english: A son begotten through the wife of a man by one belonging to his own gotra clan, or by anyone else, is known as kṣetraja a legitimate son. A son clandestinely begotten in the paternal house of a woman is known to be born in secret.

sanskrit: kānīnaḥ kanyakājāto mātāmahasuto mataḥ //
english: A son born to a virgin is known as kānīna and is held to be the son of the maternal grandfather girl’s father.

sanskrit: kṣatāyāmakṣatāyāṃ vā jātaḥ paunarbhavaḥ sutaḥ /
english: A son born of a married woman by another, whether she had menstruated or not, is known as paunarbhava.

sanskrit: dadyānmātā pitā vā yaṃ sa putrī dattako bhavet //
english: A son given as adoption by his mother or father would be a dattaka an adopted son.

sanskrit: krītaś ca tābhyāṃ vikrītaḥ kṛtrimaḥ syāt svyaṃ kṛtaḥ /
english: A son sold by them his original parents is known as krīta bought. A son adopted without the consent of his parents would be known as artificial.

sanskrit: dattātmā tu svayaṃ datto garbhe vittaḥ sahoḍhajaḥ //
english: A son offering himself as a sonto another is known as dattātman one that offers himself.

sanskrit: utsṛṣṭo gṛhyate yastu sopaviddho bhavet sutaḥ / piṇḍado 'ṃśaharaś caiṣāṃ pūrvābhāve paraḥ paraḥ //
english: A son deserted by his father and becoming a filial of another is known as apaviddha abandoned. All these are eligible to offer cakes at the obsequies and to inherit their shares. Among these, the subsequent ones are eligible if the preceding ones do not exist.

sanskrit: sajātīyeṣvayaṃ proktastanayeṣu mayā vidhiḥ /
english: have described to you the injunctions in the case of sons born of the parents of the same castes.

sanskrit: jāto 'pi dāsyāṃ śūdrasya kāmato 'ṃśaharo bhavet // mṛte pitari kuryustaṃ bhrātarastvardhabhāgikaṃ /
english: A son got by a śūdra out of lust through a slave girl would be entitled to have a share in the property of his deceased father. On the decease of his father, his brothers should give him half a share.

sanskrit: abhrātṛko haret sarvaṃ duhitṝṇāṃ sutādṛte // patnī duhitaraś caiva pitaro bhrātaras tathā / tatsuto gotrajo bandhuḥ śiṣyaḥ sabrahmacāriṇaḥ // eṣāmabhāve pūvasya dhanabhāguttarottaraḥ /
english: Such a person should take the entire property after the death of the father in the absence of any brothers or son of sisters. The wife, daughters, parents, brothers, their sons, one born in the same gotra, a relative, a disciple and costudents are deemed as heirs to a sonless man, each one of the latter being eligible in the absence of the former.

sanskrit: svaryātsya hy aputrasya sarvavarṇeṣvayaṃ vidhiḥ //
english: This rule holds good in the case of those diea without progeny belonging to all the castes.

sanskrit: vānaprasthayatibrahmacāriṇāmṛkthabhāginaḥ / krameṇācāryasacchiṣyadharmabhrātrekatīrthinaḥ //
english: The preceptor, the good disciple, the fellow religious student of the same religious order are duly the heirs to the properties of a vānaprastha forester, ascetic and a religious student.

sanskrit: saṃsṛṣṭinastu saṃsṛṣṭī sodarasya tu sodaraḥ / dadyāccāpahereccāṃśaṃ jātasya ca mṛtasya ca //
english: A coparcener and a brother may give to a coparcener or a brother that is born or may take away from a coparcener or a brother that is dead.

sanskrit: anyodaryastu saṃsṛṣṭī nānyodaryadhanaṃ haret /
english: The coparcener not born of the same womb should not inherit the property of one not born of the same womb.

sanskrit: asaṃsṛṣtyapi cādadyātsodaryo nānyamānṛjaḥ // patitastatsutaḥ klīvaḥ paṅgurunmattako jaḍaḥ / andho 'cikitsyarogādyā bhartavyāstu niraṃśakāḥ //
english: A coparcener not born of the same womb should not inherit the property of one born of different mother. A degraded person, his son, a eunuch, a lame person, a mad man, a dull person, one suffering from incurable diseases should be entitled for maintenance but not a share in the ancestral property.

sanskrit: aurasāḥ kṣetrajāstveṣāṃ nirdoṣā bhāgahāriṇaḥ / sutāś caiṣāṃ prabhartavyā yāvadvai bhartṛsātkṛtāḥ // aputrā yoṣitaś caiṣāṃ bhartavyāḥ sādhuvṛttayaḥ /
english: The sons of these persons, those born of the same womb and those born to a different mother not having any of the above defects are permitted to get their share. The daughters of such persons are to be maintained until they are got married. The wives of men not having sons should be maintained if they follow pious paths.

sanskrit: nirvāsyā vyabhicāriṇyaḥ pratikūlāstathaiva ca //
english: But those wives that are unchaste and infidels should be banished.

sanskrit: pitṛmātṛpatibhrātṛdattamadhyagnyupāgataṃ / ādhivedanikuñcaiva strīdhanaṃ parikīrtitaṃ //
english: The wealth of women is said to be that given by the father, mother, husband, brother and that presented to her near the fire and the ādhivedanika.

sanskrit: aprajāyāmatītāyāṃ bāndhavāstadavāpnuyuḥ // aprajāstrīdhanaṃ bhratturbrāhmyādiṣu caturṣvapi /
english: The wealth of a woman not having progeny would belong to the husband after her death applicable to all the four castes such as the brahmins etc.

sanskrit: duhitṛṇāṃ prasūtā cecchreṣe tu pitṛgāmi tat //
english: The daughters would be the legal heirs if they had delivered a child. Otherwise it would go to the father.

sanskrit: datvā kanyāṃ haran daṇḍyo vyayaṃ dadyācca sodayam /
english: One who takes away the property given to his daughter is liable to punishment.

sanskrit: mṛtāyāṃ dattamādadyāt pariśodhyobhayavyayam //
english: In the event of her death, he may take away that given to her after checking the two expenses mentioned above.

sanskrit: durbhikṣe dharmakārye ca vyādhau saṃpratirodhake / gṛhītaṃ strīdhanaṃ bhartā na striye dātumarhati //
english: A husband need not return the wealth of his wife in the event of it being spent to meet a famine, religious observance, illness or on account of imprisonment.

sanskrit: adhivittastriyai dadyādadhivedanikaṃ samam /
english: One should pay an amount of wealth to his second wife equal with what he has done to his first wife.

sanskrit: na dattaṃ srīdhanaṃ yasyai datte tvardhaṃ prakīrtitam //
english: If he has not given to the first wife already, he should pay a half now.

sanskrit: vibhāganihnave jñātibandhusākṣyabhilekhitaiḥ / vibhāgabhāvanā jñeyā gṛhakṣetraiś ca yautikaiḥ // sīmno vivāde kṣetrasya sāmantāḥ sthavirā gaṇāḥ /
english: In case that share has been kept as a secret, the division has to be ^^de on being attested by his own people and relatives as witnesses. This should be known as the method by which the division of the house and property and that relating to the dowry is made. A practice prevalent in ancient times which permitted a childless widow to cohabit the brother or any near kinsman of her deceased husband to raise up issue to him.

sanskrit: gopāḥ sīmākṛṣāṇā ye sarve ca vanagocarāḥ // nayeyurete sīmānaṃ sthalāṅgāratuṣadrumaiḥ / setuvalmīkanimnāsthicaityādyair upalakṣitām //
english: In the event of a dispute relating to the boundary of a field, the guards, the assembly of elders, cowherds, the tillers of the bordering lands and all the foresters should lay down the boundaries demarcated by coal, husks, trees, mounds, anthills, slopes, bones, and pile of stones.

sanskrit: sāmantā vā samaṃgrāmāś catvāro 'ṣṭau daśāpi vā /
english: Four or eight or ten guards wearing garland of red flowers and red dress should be there in each village for laying the boundaries.

sanskrit: raktasragvasanāḥ sīmānnayeyuḥ kṣitidhāriṇaḥ // anṛte tu pṛthagdaṇḍyā rājñā madhyamasāhasam / abhāve jñātṛcihnānāṃ rājā sīmnaḥ pravattakaḥ //
english: Those that make a false statement relating to the boundaries of a field should be punished with the madhyamasāhasa. In the absence of men familiar with the fields or the marks of identification, the king himself should demarcate.

sanskrit: ārāmāyatanagrāmanipānodyānaveśmasu / eṣa eva vidhirjñeyo varṣāmvupravaheṣu ca //
english: The same procedure is known to be applicable in the case of groves, temples, villages, reservoirs, gardens, houses and channels of rain water.

sanskrit: maryādāyāḥ prabhedeṣu kṣetrasya haraṇe tathā / maryādāyāś ca daṇḍyāḥ syuradhamottamamadhyamāḥ //
english: If one transgresses the boundary or encroaches into another’s field or removes the boundary, that person is to be punished with the adhama or uttama or madhyama sāhasa.

sanskrit: na niṣedhyo 'lpabādhastu setuḥ kalyāṇakārakaḥ /
english: A minor encroachment should not be obstructed if it is for the sake of a bridge that benefits all.

sanskrit: parabhūmiṃ haran kūpaḥ svalpakṣetro bahūdakaḥ //
english: Similarly one that encroaches another’s field for a well occupying a little space and providing copious water should not be obstructed.

sanskrit: svāmine yo 'nivedyaiva kṣetre setuṃ prakalpayet /
english: If a bridge is built in a field without informing its owner, the owner will have the right to its use after it is completed.

sanskrit: utpanne svāmino bhogastadabhāve mahīpateḥ //
english: The king would have the right to its use in the absence of an owner.

sanskrit: phālāhatamapi kṣetraṃ yo na kuryānna kārayet / sa pradāpyo 'kṛṣṭaphalaṃ kṣetramanyena kārayet //
english: One who does not cultivate or employ someone to cultivate in a field that has been tilled should not be given the fruits of the cultivation and the field should be made over to another for cultivation.

sanskrit: māsānaṣṭau tu mahiṣī satyaghātasya kāriṇī / daṇḍanīyā tadardhantu gaustadardhamajāvikaṃ //
english: The owner of a shebuffalo that trespasses on another’s field and causes destruction of the grains, should be fined eight māṣas a particular weight of gold.

sanskrit: bhakṣayitvopaviṣṭānāṃ yathoktād dviguṇo damaḥ / samameṣāṃ vivītepi svarāṣṭraṃ mahiṣīsamam //
english: The owner of a cow should be fined four māṣas, of a shegoat two māṣas for the same offence. They should be levied twice that told above, if they sit and watch them grazing in the pasture land.

sanskrit: yāvat satyaṃ vinaṣṭantu tāvat kṣetrī phalaṃ labhet / pālastāḍyo 'tha gosvāmī pūrvoktaṃ daṇḍamarhati //
english: The owner of the field would get the same quantity of grains that has been destroyed as above. The keeper of the animal should be beaten and the owner of the cow should get the punishment already described.

sanskrit: pathi grāmavivītānte kṣetre doṣo na vidyate /
english: But it is not objectionable if the grazing is done on a field laying along the roadside, or at the end of the grazing grounds of a village if done unintentionally.

sanskrit: akāmataḥ kāmacāre cauravaddaṇḍamarhati //
english: But if it is done wantonly, the concerned person deserves to be finished like a thief.

sanskrit: mahotkṣotsṛṣṭapaśavaḥ sūtikāgantukā ca gauḥ / pālo yeṣāntu mocyā daivarājapariplutāḥ //
english: The cows let loose by strong bulls, the cow that has delivered a calf, the cow that has strayed and those that have the keeper should be freed i.e.

sanskrit: yathārpitān paśūn gopoḥ sāyaṃ pratyarpayettathā / pramādamṛtanaṣṭāṃś ca pradāpyaḥ kṛtavetanaḥ //
english: The cowherd should return the cows in the evening as entrusted to him in the morning. A paid servant is bound to pay the price of the animals that were killed or lost in his custody by his negligence.

sanskrit: pāladoṣavināśe tu pāle daṇḍo vidhīyate /
english: A cowherd is to be punished in the event of a cow being killed on account of his negligence.

sanskrit: ardhatrayodaśapaṇaḥ svāmino dravyameva ca // grāmecchayā gopracāro bhūmirājavaśena vā /
english: The pasture land should be set apart at a place according to the wish of the people of the village or being beneficial to the land and the king.

sanskrit: dvijastṛṇaidhaḥpuṣpāṇi sarvataḥ svavadāharet //
english: A brahmin may collect grass, fuel and flowers from any land as if it were his own.

sanskrit: dhanuḥśataṃ parīṇāho grāmakṣetrāntaraṃ bhavet / dve śate kharvaṭasya syānnagarasya catuḥśatam //
english: The extent of the interspace between the village and the field should be one hundred dhanus, while that between the markettown and the field should be two hundred dhanus and that between the city and the field should be four hundred dhanus.

sanskrit: svaṃ labhetānyavikrītaṃ kreturdoṣo 'prakāśite /
english: If a property is sold to another without disclosing its defects, then the purchaser has the right to take it at a lower price.

sanskrit: hīnādraho hīnamūlye velāhīne ca taskaraḥ // naṣṭāpahṛtamāsādya hartāraṃ grāhayennaram / deśakālātipattau vā gṛhītvā svayamarpayet //
english: A man who has found out a lost and stolen article should cause the thief to be apprehended. But if there was a lapse of time and was found at a distant place, the owner should himself apprehend the thief and hand him over to the authorities.

sanskrit: vikreturdarśanācchuddhiḥ svāmī dravyaṃ nṛpo damam / kretā mūlyaṃ samāpnoti tasmādyastatra vikrayī //
english: The purchaser gets free after showing the seller of a stolen property. The owner would get the property. The king would get the fine. The purchaser would get his money back from the seller.

sanskrit: āgamenopabhogena naṣṭaṃ bhāvyamato 'nyathā /
english: Allowance should be made for wear and tear by way of addition or enjoyment for an article.

sanskrit: pañcabandho damastasya rājñe tenāpyabhāvite //
english: If it exceeds the limit, a fivefold fine should be paid to the king.

sanskrit: hṛtaṃ pranaṣṭaṃ yo dravyaṃ parahastādavāpnuyāt / anivedya nṛpe daṇḍyaḥ sa tu ṣannayatiṃ paṇān //
english: A man who recovers or takes back a stolen or lost article from another, without intimating the king should be fined to pay ninetysix paṇas.

sanskrit: śaulkikaiḥ sthānapālair vā naṣṭāpahṛtamāhṛtaṃ / arvāk saṃvatsarāt svāmī labhate parato nṛpaḥ //
english: A lost or stolen article recovered by the customs officers or sentinels should be given to the owner if it is less than a year after its loss and thereafter it should be with the king.

sanskrit: paṇānekaśaphe dadyāccaturaḥ pañca mānuṣe / mahiṣoṣṭragavāṃ dvau dvau pādaṃ pādamajāvike //
english: One should pay as interest four paṇas for a single hoofed animal, five for a slave, two for a buffalo, camel and cow and one fourth of that for a goat and sheep.

sanskrit: svakuṭumbāvirodhena deyaṃ dārasutādṛte / nānvaye sati sarvasvaṃ deyaṃ yaccānyasaṃśrutam //
english: One may give away his possessions, except his wife and son, for interest, without causing hardship to his own family members, if not objected to by any of them. If he does not have the progeny, he may give all his possessions.

sanskrit: pratigrahaḥ prakāśaḥ syāt sthāvarasya viśeṣataḥ /
english: The acceptance of a property should be made public, especially of an immovable property.

sanskrit: deyaṃ pratiśrutañcaiva datvā nāpaharet punaḥ //
english: After having given the promised thing that is payable to one, one should not take it back.

sanskrit: daśaikapañcasaptāhamāsatryahārdhamāsikaṃ / vījāyovāhyaratnastrīdohyapuṃsāṃ pratīkṣaṇam //
english: A person who gives the seed, iron, vehicle, gem, woman, milch animal and a man should wait for ten, one, five, seven days, a month, three days and a fortnight respectively for interest.

sanskrit: agnau suvarṇamakṣīṇaṃ dvipalaṃ rajate śate / aṣṭau trapuṇi sīse ca tāmre pañcadaśāyasi //
english: In the case of gold that does not get reduced in fire as well as silver, interest would be two palas for every hundred palas, eight palas in the case of tin and lead, five in the case of copper and ten for iron.

sanskrit: śate daśapalāvṛddhiraurṇe kārpāsike tathā /
english: Interest would be ten palas for hundred for wool and cotton.

sanskrit: madhye pañcapalā jñeyā sūkṣme tu tripalā matā //
english: For mediocre quality it is known to be five palas and in extremely thin varieties it is three palas.

sanskrit: kārmike romabaddhe ca triṃśadbhāgaḥ kṣayo mataḥ /
english: The wastage is known to be a thirtieth part of the original weight in the case of embroidered and woollen mixed material.

sanskrit: na kṣayo na ca vṛddhistu kauśeye valkaleṣu ca //
english: No allowance for decay or interest in the case of silk and bark garments.

sanskrit: deśaṃ kālañca bhogañca jñātvā naṣṭe balābalam / dravyāṇāṃ kuśalā brūyuryattaddāpyamasaṃśayam //
english: The experts should declare with certainty the allowance to be made on things after knowing the place of origin of the things, the season, the wear and tear and the strength of the materials.

sanskrit: balāddāsīkṛtaś caurair vikrītaścāpi mucyate / svāmiprāṇaprado bhaktatyāgāttanniṣkrayādapi // pravrajyāvasito rājño dāsa āmaraṇāntikaḥ /
english: One who has saved the life of his master and has been forcibly made a slave by thieves and sold should be made free by the king even by paying a ransom. A religious mendicant who has renounced his order is a slave of the king until his death.

sanskrit: varṇānāmānulomyena dāsyaṃ na pratilomataḥ //
english: For the four castes, men of the next natural order of castes alone could be a slave, but not of the reverse order.

sanskrit: kṛtaśilpopi nivaset kṛtakālaṃ gurorgṛhe / antevāsī guruprāptabhojanastratphalaptadaḥ //
english: A pupil who has completed his studies should stay for the stipulated period at the house of his preceptor and has to serve him for the food got from him.

sanskrit: rājā kṛtvā pure sthānaṃ brāhmaṇānnyasya tatra tu / traividyaṃ vṛttimadbrūyāt svadharmaḥ pālyatāmiti //
english: The king should allot a frontal place to the brahmins in his city, provide for their livelihood by means of the three Vedas and tell them, “May you adhere to your own duty”.

sanskrit: so 'pi yatnena saṃrakṣyo dharmo rājakṛtaś ca yaḥ //
english: One who adheres to the work agreed upon without conflicting with one’s own duties should also be protected by the king with care.

sanskrit: gaṇadravyaṃ haredyastu saṃvidaṃ laṅghayecca yaḥ / sarvasvaharaṇaṃ kṛtvā taṃ rāṣṭrādvipravāsayet //
english: One who transgresses the discipline laid down by the king, who swindles the property of the society and who breaks an agreement should be deprived of all his possessions and banished from the country.

sanskrit: kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ sarvaiḥ samūhahitavādibhiḥ /
english: Everyone should follow the words of those who preach for the welfare of the society.

sanskrit: yastatra viparītaḥ syātsa dāpyaḥ prathamaṃ damam // samūhakāryaprahito yallabhettattadarpayet /
english: One who does the contrary should be made to pay the first sāhasa fine. One who is entrusted with a task relating to the society should offer to the king all that he gets.

sanskrit: ekādaśaguṇaṃ dāpyo yadyasau nārpayet svayam //
english: If he himself does not offer, he should be made to pay a fine eleven times that collected by him.

sanskrit: vedajñāḥ śucayo 'lubdhā bhaveyuḥ kāryacintakāḥ /
english: Those who think of public service should be learned in the scriptures and not greedy.

sanskrit: kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ teṣāṃ samūhahitavādināṃ //
english: All should follow the words of those who speak for the welfare of the society.

sanskrit: śreṇinaigamapākhaṇḍigaṇānāmapyayaṃ vidhiḥ /
english: The same rule holds good in the case of guild of traders, assembly of interpreters of the scriptures and those professing other religions.

sanskrit: bhedañcaiṣāṃ nṛpo rakṣet pūrvavṛttiñca pālayet //
english: The king has to maintain the separate entities of these and govern the former profession.

sanskrit: gṛhītavetanaḥ karma tyajan dviguṇamāvahet / agṛhīte samaṃ dāpyo bhṛtyai rakṣya upaskaraḥ //
english: One who does not do a work after having received the wages for the same should pay double the amount as fine. If the amount has not been taken, one has to pay an equal amount as fine.

sanskrit: dāpyastu daśamaṃ bhāgaṃ bāṇijyapaśusasyataḥ / aniścitya bhṛtiṃ yastu kārayetsa mahīkṣitā //
english: The supplementary grants given to the servants should be retained by them. One who gains by trade, cattle or grains without obtaining the previous permission should be made to pay one tenth of the gain as fine by the king.

sanskrit: deśaṃ kālañca yo 'tīyāt karma kuryācca yo 'nyathā / tatra tu svāminaśchando 'dhikaṃ deyaṃ kṛte 'dhike //
english: It is the discretion of the employer to pay an employee if one does work for more than the stipulated period and does work beyond the country that was stipulated. More money should be paid if more work has been done.

sanskrit: yo yāvat kurute karma tāvattasya tu vetanam /
english: One’s wages would be commensurate with the work done by him.

sanskrit: ubhayorapyasādhyañcet sādhye kuryādyathāśrutam //
english: If both the parties find it untenable, it should be done as laid down in the scriptures.

sanskrit: prasthānavighnakṛccaiva pradāpyo dviguṇāṃ bhṛtim //
english: One who causes obstruction to a public carrier should pay double the amount of the wages.

sanskrit: prakrānte saptamaṃ bhāgaṃ caturthaṃ pathi saṃtyajan / bhṛtimardhapathe sarvāṃ pradāpyastyājakoapi ca //
english: If the carrier abandons the goods at the start, or on the way or on half the way, he would be required to pay one seventh or one fourth or the entire wages respectively.

sanskrit: glahe śatikavṛddhestu sabhikaḥ pañcakaṃ gataṃ / gṛhṇīyāddhūrtakitavāditarāddaśakaṃ śataṃ //
english: If the stake at gambling is in the multiples of hundreds, then the king’s share would be five hundred paṇas. If they are cheats and swindlers, then the king should take one thousand paṇas.

sanskrit: sa samyakpālito dadyādrājñe bhāgaṃ yathākṛtaṃ / jitamudgrāhayejjetre dadyātsatyaṃ vacaḥ kṣamī //
english: The manager at the gambling house should run it properly and pay the king’s share as laid down. The defeated person should be made to deposit the amount that is payable to the victor.

sanskrit: prāpte nṛpatinā bhāge prasiddhe dhūrtamaṇḍale / jitaṃ saśabhike sthāne dāpayedanyathā na tu //
english: When the king has obtained his share in the reputed society of the gamblers, he should put the defeated in the midst of the gamblers to pay the fine. If not, he should not.

sanskrit: draṣṭāro vyavahārāṇāṃ sākṣiṇaś ca ta eva hi /
english: They are who see and the witnesses in such transactions.

sanskrit: rājñā sacihnā nirvāsyāḥ kūṭākṣopadhidevinaḥ //
english: Those who indulge in false die and fraudulent ways should be banished by the king along with the marks on their person.

sanskrit: dyūtamekamukhaṃ kāryaṃ taskarajñānakāraṇāt /
english: There should be only one leader of the gambling house in order to know the cheats in gambling.

sanskrit: eṣa eva vidhirjñeyaḥ prāṇidyūte samāhvaye //
english: The same is the procedure in gambling with fighting animals and betting after setting animals to fight.

sanskrit: satyāsatyānyathā stotrair nyūnāṅgendriyarogiṇāṃ / kṣepaṃ karoti ceddaṇḍyaḥ paṇānardhatrayodaśa //
english: One dhanus is equal to four times the length of the forearm. If a person abuses the sick and men having defective organs, by means of lampoons, whether true or untrue or otherwise, he should be fined thirteen and a half paṇas.

sanskrit: abhigantāsmi bhaginīmmātaraṃ vā taveti ca / śapantaṃ dāpayedrājā pañcaviṃśatikaṃ damaṃ //
english: The king should levy a fine of twentyfive paṇas on one that abuses another with the words “ copulate with your sister or copulate with your mother”.

sanskrit: ardho 'dhameṣu dviguṇaḥ parastrīṣūttameṣu ca / daṇḍapraṇayanaṃ kāryaṃ varṇajātyuttarādharaiḥ // prātilomyāpavādeṣu dviguṇatriguṇā damāḥ /
english: A man of the higher caste committing adultery on women of the lower caste should be levied half the fine and a man of the lower caste committing adultery on women of the higher caste should be levied double the fine. The men of lower orders of castes censuring the men of the next higher order should be levied double or three times the fine.

sanskrit: varṇānāmānulomyena tasmādevārdhahānitaḥ //
english: But in the case of censures made by men of the higher orders on those of lower orders, half the fine should be levied.

sanskrit: vāhugrīvānetrasakthivināśe vācike damaḥ / śatyastato 'rdhikaḥ pādanāsākarṇikarādiṣu //
english: The fine that should be levied on a capable person uttering words threatening the injury of the hands, neck, eyes and thighs of another should be levied the sāhasa fine.

sanskrit: aśaktastu vadannevandaṇḍanīyaḥ paṇān daśa /
english: An incapable person who says as above should be levied a fine of ten paṇas.

sanskrit: tathā śaktaḥ pratibhuvaṃ dadyāt kṣemāya tasya tu //
english: So also a capable person should give surety for the safety of that person.

sanskrit: patanīyakṛte kṣepe daṇḍī madhyamasāhasaḥ / upapātakayukte tu dāpyaḥ prathamasāhasaṃ //
english: The middle sāhasa fine should be levied on that person who abuses one ascribing degrading sin to him. The first kind of sāhasa should be levied on one who ascribes another with minor sin of second degree.

sanskrit: traividyanṛpadevānāṃ kṣepa uttamasāhasaḥ /
english: The highest sāhasa should be levied for offences villifying the brahmins, kings and gods.

sanskrit: madhyamo jñātipūgānāṃ prathamo grāmadeśayoḥ //
english: Middle sāhasa should be levided for offences villifying one’s own relatives and the members of the village assembly and the first sāhasa for speaking ill of one’s own village or country.

sanskrit: asākṣikahate cihnair yuktibhinnāgamena ca / draṣṭavyo vyavahārastu kūṭacihnakṛtādbhayāt //
english: In the case of charge of murder without witness, the judge should pronounce the judgement after considering the marks, reasoning and written testimony, in order to safeguard himself from being misled by false marks.

sanskrit: bhasmapaṅkarajaḥsparśe daṇḍo daśapaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
english: The fine for touching another with ashes, mud or dust is said to be ten paṇas and for touching with filth or the heels or spitting, double that.

sanskrit: amedhyapārṣṇiniṣṭhyūtasparśane dviguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // sameṣvevaṃ parastrīṣu dviguṇastūttameṣu ca /
english: For offences against women of one’s own caste single fine should be levied and twice that in the case of other women as well as of higher castes. The fine is half in the case of offences against those belonging to lower castes.

sanskrit: hīneṣvardhaṃ damo mohamadādibhiradaṇḍanam //
english: For offences done under delusion or the influence of liquor, there is no punishment.

sanskrit: viprapīḍākaraṃ cchedyamaṅgamabrāhmaṇasya tu / udgūrṇe prathamo daṇḍaḥ saṃsparśe tu tadardhikaḥ //
english: The organ of a nonbrahmin that inflicts pain on a brahmin should be cut off. First sāhasa punishment should be preseribed for one who raises one’s arms and strikes a brahmin and half that fine if one touches.

sanskrit: udgūrṇe hastapāde tu daśaviṃśatikau damau /
english: If the hand and the leg are held and pulled, the fine is ten and twenty paṇas respectively.

sanskrit: parasparantu sarveṣāṃ śāstre madhyamasāhasaḥ //
english: If several men one by one hold and pull, the scriptures prescribe the middle sāhasa for all of them.

sanskrit: pādakeśāṃśukakarolluñcaneṣu paṇān daśa /
english: The fine for pulling the feet or hair or the garment or hand is ten paṇas.

sanskrit: pīḍākarṣāṃ śukāveṣṭapādādhyāse śatandamaḥ // śoṇitena vinā duḥsvaṅkurvan kāṣṭhādibhirnaraḥ /
english: The fine for causing affliction or pulling or dragging after putting cloth around or placing foot on a person is one hundered paṇas. One who causes misery by means of a log of wood etc.

sanskrit: dvātriṃśataṃ paṇān dāpyo dviguṇaṃ darśane 'sṛjaḥ //
english: and if there be no blood injury, should be fined thirtytwo paṇas. Double that is the fine, if blood is seen.

sanskrit: karapādadato bhaṅge cchedane karṇanāsayoḥ / madhyo daṇḍo vraṇodbhede mṛtakalpahate tathā // ceṣṭābhojanavāgrodhe netrādipratibhedane / kandharābāhusakthyāñca bhaṅge madhyamasāhasaḥ //
english: The middle sāhasa fine is levied for breaking hand, foot and teeth and cutting ear and nose. Similarly one causing injurious wounds, one who strikes fatally, one who impairs organs of movement, eating and speaking, one who pierces eyes etc., and one who breaks neck, arm and thigh should be punished with middle sāhasa.

sanskrit: ekaṃ ghnatāṃ bahūnāñca yathoktāddviguṇā damāḥ /
english: If many persons jointly assault a man, each one of them should be levied double the amount of fine laid down before.

sanskrit: kalahāpahṛtaṃ deyaṃ daṇḍastu dviguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: Articles forcibly taken away after a quarrel should be returned and the fine is said to be double.

sanskrit: duḥkhamutpādayedyastu sa samutthānajaṃ vyayam / dāpyo daṇḍañca yo yasmin kalahe samudāhṛtaḥ //
english: A person who causes grief should pay the cost of recovery of the article and the fine is said to be the same as laid down in the case of a quarrel.

sanskrit: tarikaḥ sthalajaṃ śulkaṃ gṛhnan daṇḍyaḥ paṇāndaśa /
english: A ferryman collecting a landtoll should be punished to pay ten paṇas.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaprātiveśyānāmetadevānimantraṇe //
english: A brahmin going to dine at the neighbour’s house uninvited, shall be liable for the same punishment.

sanskrit: paṇāndāpyaḥ pañcadaśaviṃśatiṃ tattrayantathā //
english: One has to be fined five, ten, twenty and sixty paṇas respectively for assaulting, piercing, cutting and breaking the house of another person.

sanskrit: duḥsvotpādigṛhe dravyaṃ kṣipan prāṇaharaṃ tathā / ṣāḍaśādyaṃ paṇāt dāpyo dvitīyo madhyamandamam // duḥkhe ca śoṇitotpāde śākhāṅgacchedane tathā /
english: One should be fined sixteen paṇas for having thrown into another’s house, an object, that would cause misery or death to another. The abettor should be fined the middle sāhasa. One should duly be fined two paṇas onwards for having caused misery or bleeding injury or breaking the limbs of the body of a small animal.

sanskrit: daṇḍaḥ kṣudrapaśūnāṃ syāddvipaṇaprabhṛtiḥ kramāt // liṅgasya cchedane mṛttau madhyamo mūlyameva ca /
english: One should be fined the middle sāhasa and should pay the price for having cut off the genital organ of an animal or having killed it.

sanskrit: mahāpaśūnāmeteṣu sthāneṣu dviguṇā damāḥ //
english: In the case of bigger animals, in these instances, the fine would be double the above.

sanskrit: prarohiśākhināṃ śākhāskandhasarvavidāraṇe / upajīvyadrumāṇāntu viṃśaterdviguṇā damāḥ //
english: The fine is forty paṇas for lopping the branches, trunk of the tree or the whole tree that is growing and providing sustenance.

sanskrit: yaḥ sāhasaṅkārayati sa dāpyo dviguṇandamam / yastvevamuktvāhaṃ dātā kārayet sa caturguṇam // āryākrośātikramakṛdbhrātṛjāyāprahāradaḥ /
english: One who causes another to indulge in a violent act shall have to pay double the fine and one who says that he would pay if fine is imposed and causes another to do a violent act shall be required to pay four times that fine.

sanskrit: pañcāśatpaṇiko daṇḍa eṣāmiti viniś cayaḥ // svacchandavidhavāgāmī vikruṣṭe nābhidhāvakaḥ / akāraṇe ca vikroṣṭā caṇḍālaścottamān spṛśan //
english: It has been fixed that, a person who reviles or shows disrespect to a respectable person, one who beats the wife of his brother, one who does not give the promised gift, one who breaks the summerhouse built in the midst of water and one who injures the neighbours, shall be fined fifty paṇas.

sanskrit: śūdraḥ pravrajitānāñca daive paitrye ca bhojakaḥ / ayuktaṃ śapathaṃ kurvannayogyo yogyakarmakṛt // vṛṣakṣudrapaśūnāñca pūṃstvasya pratighātakṛt / sādhāraṇasyāpalopī dāsīgarbhavināśakṛt // pitāputrasvasṛbhrātṛdampatyācāryaśiṣyakāḥ /
english: One who copulates with a licentious widow, one who assaults another uttering abuses, one who abuses another without any reason, a man of the low caste touching the men of higher castes, a śūdra a man of the fourth caste eating the meal at the time of the ceremony of a mendicant and in the divine and ancestral ceremonies, one who makes an improper oath, an incompetent person who does the act of a competent person, one who castrates the bulls or small animals, one who hides a wellknown matter, one who destroys the foetus of a servant woman, one who disregards any one of the followingfather, son, sister, brother, husband or wife, preceptor and pupil, that has not been degraded, shall be fined a hundred paṇas.

sanskrit: vasānastrīn paṇān daṇḍyo nejakastu parāṃśukam /
english: A washerman who wears the dress of others given to him for washing should be fined three paṇas.

sanskrit: vikrayāvakrayādhānayāciteṣu paṇān daśa // tulāśāsanamānānāṃ kūṭakṛnnāṇakasya ca / ebhiś ca vyavahartā yaḥ sa dāpyo daṇḍamuttamam //
english: It is ten paṇas if he sells them or requests others to take them without any charges. One who deals with those who make false marks on weights and measures and make counterfeit coins should be fined the highest sāhasa.

sanskrit: akūṭaṃ kūṭakaṃ brūte kūṭaṃ yaścāpyakūṭakam /
english: The cointester who declares the genuine as counterfeit and the counterfeit as genuine should be fined the first sāhasa.

sanskrit: bhiṣaṅmithyācaran dāpyastiryakṣu prathamaṃ damam / mānuṣe madhyamaṃ rājamānuṣeṣūttamantathā //
english: A physician who gives wrong medical treatment to birds and animals, men in general and men of royal household, should be punished with the first, middle and the highest fine respectively.

sanskrit: abadhyaṃ yaś ca badhnāti badhyaṃ yaś ca pramuñcati / aprāptavyavahārañca sa dāpyo damamuttamam //
english: An officer who keeps in custody a man that should not be kept incarcerated and allows an untried criminal to escape, should be fined the highest sāhasa.

sanskrit: mānena tulayā vāpi yo 'ṃśamaṣṭamakaṃ haret / dvāviṃśatipaṇān dāpyo vṛddhau hānau ca kalpitam //
english: One who steals an eighth part of the real weight of an article, by means of false scale or fraudulent measurement, should be fined twentytwo paṇas, no matter, whether the real weight has been increased.

sanskrit: bheṣajasnehalavaṇagandhānyaguḍādiṣu /
english: One who mixes lowstandard material in medicines, oils, salts, perfumes, grains and molasses etc.

sanskrit: paṇyeṣu prakṣipan hīnaṃ paṇāndāpyastu ṣoḍaśa //
english: should be fined sixteen paṇas.

sanskrit: sambhūya kurvatāmarghaṃ sabādhaṃ kāruśilpināṃ / arthasya hrāsaḥ vṛddhiṃ vā sahasro daṇḍa ucyate //
english: A thousand paṇas is said to be the fine to be imposed on the artisans who collectively indulge in affecting the value of the goods or cause the decrease or the increase of the wealth.

sanskrit: rājāni sthāpyate yo 'rthaḥ pratyahaṃ tena vikrayaḥ / krayo vā nisravastasmādbaṇijāṃ lābhakṛt smṛtaḥ //
english: It is considered to be profitable for the traders to sell or purchase everyday, goods that are dependent on the king.

sanskrit: svadeśapaṇye tu śataṃ baṇij gṛhṇīta pañcakaṃ / daśakaṃ pāradeśye tu yaḥ sadyaḥ krayavikrayau // paṇyasyopari saṃsthāpya vyayaṃ paṇyasamudbhavaṃ /
english: A trader should take five per cent profit on indigenous goods and ten percent profit on foreign goods that are bought and sold immediately. A trader, after having added the incidental expenses relating to the goods, to the price of the goods, should settle its price with the seller or purchaser.

sanskrit: artho 'nugrahakṛt kāryaḥ kreturvikretureva ca // gṛhītamūlyaṃ yaḥ paṇyaṃ kreturnaiva prayacchati / sodayantasya dāpyo 'sau diglābhaṃ vā digāgate //
english: A trader not delivering the goods to the purchaser from whom the cost has been collected, should be made to pay the amount along with the profit or the profit allowed on the foreign goods if the goods have come from the foreign country.

sanskrit: vikrītamapi vikreyaṃ pūrve kretaryagṛhṇati /
english: Goods that are sold already could again be sold, if the previous purchaser has not taken delivery of the goods.

sanskrit: hāniścet kretṛdoṣeṇa kretureva hi sā bhavet //
english: The defects in the goods due to the purchaser’s fault should be borne only by the purchaser.

sanskrit: rājadaivopaghātena paṇye doṣamupāgate / hānirvikreturevāsau yācitasyāprayacchataḥ // anyahaste ca vikrītaṃ duṣṭaṃ vā duṣṭavadyadi / vikrīnīte damastatra tanmūlyādadviguṇo bhavet //
english: In the case of any damage to the goods caused by political disturbances or natural calamities, or due to nondelivery at the desired time, the consequences have to be borne only by the seller. The fine payable by a seller for the damage or the apparent damage to goods sold through his agent would be double the value of the cost of the goods.

sanskrit: kṣayaṃ vṛddhiñca baṇijā paṇyānāmavijānatā / krītvā nānuśayaḥ kāryaḥ kurvan ṣaḍ bhāgadaṇḍabhāk //
english: A trader who has purchased the goods without the knowledge of the decrease or increase in their prices should not reopen the negotiation. In case he does so, he should be punished to pay one sixth of the value of the whole stock.

sanskrit: samavāyena baṇijāṃ lābhārthaṃ karma kurvatāṃ / labhālābhau yathā dravyaṃ yathā vā saṃvidā kṛtau // pratiṣiddhamanādiṣṭaṃ pramādādyacca nāśitaṃ /
english: The profits and losses of traders trading as partners for the sake of profit, should be divided proportionately to their shares in the capital, or according to agreement made at the commencement of the business. A partner should make good the loss sustained by him on account of doing the prohibited thing or doing a thing that he has not been asked to do or on account of folly.

sanskrit: sa taddayādvipravācca rakṣitāddaśamāṃśabhāk // arthaprekṣapaṇādviṃśaṃ bhāgaṃ śulkaṃ nṛpā haret /
english: A partner who has saved the goods from destruction is eligible to get one tenth of the value of the goods. The king shall take a twentieth part of the value of the abandoned goods as tax.

sanskrit: vyāsiddhaṃ rājayogyañca vikrītaṃ rājagāmi tat //
english: The contraband goods fit for royal use and sold to someone should go to the king.

sanskrit: mithyā vadan parīmāṇaṃ śulkasthānādapakraman / dāpyastvaṣṭaguṇaṃ yaś ca savyājakrayavikrayau //
english: A deceitful purchaser or seller giving out false measures and going away from the toll office should be fined eight times the value of the goods.

sanskrit: deśantaragate prete dravyaṃ dāyādabāndhavāḥ / jñātayo vā hareyustadāgatāstair vinā nṛpaḥ //
english: Relatives and rightful heirs who have come should get the properties of a person on his death or his settlement abroad and the king should get in the absence of them the legal heirs.

sanskrit: anena vidhirākhyāta ṛtvikkarṣakarmiṇāṃ //
english: The following injunctions have been laid down for the officiating priest and ploughman They should eschew dishonesty.

sanskrit: grāhakair gṛhyate cauro loptreṇātha padena vā / pūrvakarmāparādhī vā tathaivāśuddhavāsakaḥ //
english: They should get the task done by employing another in the case of personal incapacity. A thief is apprehended by constables on finding the stolen property in his possession, by his footprint, his past crime and dirty clothes.

sanskrit: anye 'pi śaṅkayā grāhyā jātināmādinihnavaiḥ /
english: Others that hide their caste, name etc. should also be held on account of suspicion.

sanskrit: dyūtastrīpānaśaktāś ca śuṣkabhinnamukhasvarāḥ //
english: Persons addicted to gambling, wenching and drinking and those who turn pale and speak in a dry and broken voice should also be held.

sanskrit: paradravyagṛhāṇāñca pṛcchakā gūḍhacāriṇaḥ / nirāyā vyayavantaś ca vinaṣṭa dravyavikrayāḥ //
english: Those who enquire about the properties and houses of others, those who wander in disguise, those who spend much without income, those who sell lost goods should also be held.

sanskrit: gṛhītaḥ śaṅkayā cauryenātmānañcedviśodhayet / dāpayitvā hṛtaṃ dravyaṃ cauradaṇḍena daṇḍayet //
