english: If wild animals and birds enter village and those of village enter forest land animals enter water and water animals enter land, vixens howl at the threshold of a palace, cocks crow at pradoṣa the time preceding the night fall vixens howl at the residence or at the rising Sun dove enters the house, carnivorous birds stoop down on the head bees make sweet sound crows mate in sight strong arches of palace, garden, doorways, corridor and mansions fall without an obvious cause, it forebodes evil.

sanskrit: animittantu patanaṃ dṛḍhānāṃ rājamṛtyave /
english: It forebodes the death of the king.

sanskrit: rajasā vātha dhūmena diśo yatra samākulāḥ // ketūdayoparāgau ca chidratā śaśisūryayoḥ / graharkṣavikṛtiryatra tatrāpi bhayamādiśet //
english: If the quarters are filled by dust or smoke, if the country is under the influence of the descending node, if spots in the moon and sun are visible, or if the stars and planets are not to be seen, it also indicates fear.

sanskrit: agniryatra ma dīpyeta sravante codakambhakāḥ / mṛtirbhayaṃ śūnyatādirutpātānāṃ phalambhavet //
english: Where the fire does not glow, the waterpots ooze, there is the fear of death and witchcraft as the result of the portents.

sanskrit: dvijadevādipūjābhyaḥ śāntirjapyaistu homataḥ //33//
english: The portent is appeased by the worship of brahmins and gods, recitation of hymns and offer of oblations. ṚV.

sanskrit: devapūjādikaṃ karma vakṣye cotpātamardanam /
english: shall describe the mode of worshipping the gods and other rites that destroy the effects of portents.

sanskrit: āpohiṣṭeti tisṛbhiḥ snāto 'rghyaṃ vioṣṇaverpayet //
english: One should offer respectful water of libation to Lord Viṣṇu with the three hymns beginning with āpo hi ṣṭhā after having bathed.

sanskrit: hiraṇyavarṇā iti ca pādyañca tisṛbhirdvija /
english: O Brahmin! Water for washing the feet should be offered with the three hymns beginning with hiraṇyavarṇa.

sanskrit: śanna āpo hy ācamanamidamāpo 'bhiṣecanaṃ //
english: Water for sipping is offered with the recitation of the hymn śanna āpo and for bathing with the hymn idamāpaḥ.

sanskrit: rathe akṣe ca tisṛbhirgandhaṃ yuveti vastrakaṃ /
english: Perfumes are offered with the three hymns rathe akṣe and dress with the hymn yuva.

sanskrit: puṣpaṃ puṣpavatītyevaṃ dhūpandhūposi cāpyatha //
english: Flowers are given with the recitation of the hymn puṣpavatīḥ and incense with the hymn dhūposi.

sanskrit: tejosi śukraṃ dīpaṃ syānmadhuparkaṃ dadhīti ca /
english: The hymn for offering the lamp is tejo’si and for the madhuparka, dadhi.

sanskrit: hiraṇyagarbha ity aṣṭāvṛcaḥ proktā nivedane // annasya manujaśreṣṭha pānasya ca sugandhinaḥ / cāmaravyajanopānacchatraṃ yānāsane tathā //
english: O Foremost among men! The eight hymns beginning with hiraṇyagarbhaḥ are said to be used in offering eatables to gods, cooked rice, drinks, perfume, chowrie, fan, shoe, umbrella, chariot and seat.

sanskrit: yat kiñcidevamādi syātsāvitreṇa nivedayet /
english: Whatever other thing has to be offered should be accompanied by the recitation of the hymn of god Savitṛ.

sanskrit: pauruṣantu japet sūktaṃ tadeva juhuyāttathā //
english: The puruṣasūkta should be repeated and oblations should be offered with the same hymn.

sanskrit: arcābhave tathā vedyāñjale pūrṇaghate tathā / nadītīre 'tha kamale śāntiḥ syādviṣṇupūjanāt //
english: In the absence of an image of Lord Viṣṇu the deity should be invoked on the altar or in water or in a pot full with water or on the banks of a river or in a lotus.

sanskrit: tato homaḥ prakartavyo dīpyamāne vibhāvasau /
english: One would thus accomplish the propitiation by worshipping lord Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: parisammṛjya paryukṣya paristīrya paristaraiḥ // sarvānnāgraṃ samuddhṛtya juhuyāt prayatastataḥ /
english: Then the oblations should be offered to the glowing fire with the entire food being collected and offered with earnestness after cleaning the ground, sprinkling water and spreading sand and kuśa grass.

sanskrit: vāsudevāya devāya prabhave cāvyayāya ca // agnaye caiva somāya mitrāya varuṇāya ca /
english: One should say obeisance to Vāsudeva, to the lord, to the master, to the immutable, to the Fire god, to Soma, to Mitra, to Varuṇa and to Indra.

sanskrit: viśvebhyaś caiva devebhyaḥ prajānāṃ pataye namaḥ /
english: O Fortunate one Obeisance to Indra and Fire god, the Viśvedevas and to the lord of the beings.

sanskrit: anumatyai tathā rāma dhanvantaraya eva ca // vāstoṣpatyai tato devyai tataḥ sviṣṭikṛte 'gnaye /
english: Oh! Rāma! Then one should say obeisance to Anumati, to Dhanvantari, to Vāstoṣpati, to the goddess, to the Fire that accomplishes the sacrificial rite.

sanskrit: sacaturthyantanāmnā tu hutvaitebhyo baliṃ haret //
english: After having made the oblations thus with the names ending in the dative case, a part of the offering is given away as gift.

sanskrit: takṣopatakṣamabhitaḥ pūrveṇāgnimataḥ param / aśvānāmapi dharmajña ūrṇānāmāni cāpyatha // nirundhī dhūmriṇīkā ca asvapantī tathaiva ca /
english: O Son of Bhṛgu! Knower of righteousness! Takṣa and Upatakṣa towards the east, then the horses and the hairs on the south, Nirundhī and Dhūmriṇīkā on the west and Asvapantī and Meghapatnī on the north are the names of all those to be worshipped all around in a circle.

sanskrit: meghapatnī ca nāmāni sarveṣāmeva bhārgava //
english: The Firegod and other gods should be located in the places of the goddesses.

sanskrit: nandinyai ca subhāgyai ca sumaṅgalyai ca bhārgava // bhadrakālyai tato datvā sthūṇāyāñca tathā śriye / hiraṇyakeśyai ca tathā vanaspataya eva ca //
english: O Son of Bhṛgu! goddesses Nandinī, Subhāgyā, Sumaṅgalī, Bhadrakālī, Sthūṇā, Śrī, Hiraṇyakeśī and Vanaspati are worshipped.

sanskrit: dharmādharmamayau dvāre gṛhamadhye dhruvāya ca / mṛtyave ca vahirdadyādvaruṇāyodakāśaye // bhūtebhyaś ca bahirdadyāccharaṇe dhanadāya ca / indrāyendrapuruṣebhyo dadyāt pūrveṇa mānavaḥ //
english: Offering is made to Dharma and Adharma at the door, Dhruva at the centre of the house, Mṛtyu outside, Varuṇa at a reservoir, the goblins outside the house, the god of wealth at the house, Indra and companions on the east, Yama and his attendants on the south, Varuṇa and his companions on the west and Soma and his attendants on the north.

sanskrit: brahmaṇe brahmapuruṣebhyo madhye dadyāttathaiva ca //
english: Offering is made to Brahmā and his attendants at the centre.

sanskrit: divā divācarebhyaś ca rātrau rātricareṣu ca // baliṃ vahis tathā dadyātsāyaṃ prātastu pratyahaṃ /
english: Offerings should be made in the sky, above, on the floor and on the earth during the day for the spirits that wander during the day and in the night for those that wander during the night.

sanskrit: piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ kuryāt prātaḥ sāyanna kārayet //
english: Then offering of balls of rice is made for the manes. It should not be done in the evening.

sanskrit: pitre tu prathamaṃ dadyāttatpitre tadanantaram / prapitāmahāya tanmātre pitṛmātre tato 'rpayet //
english: Offering is first made to the dead father, then to the grandfather and greatgradfather, then to one’s mother, paternal grandmother and paternal greatgrandmother.

sanskrit: tanmātre dakṣiṇāgreṣu kuśeṣvevaṃ yajet pitṝn /
english: The manes should thus be worshipped on the kuśa grass having their tips facing the south.

sanskrit: te kākāḥ pitṛgṛhantu imaṃ piṇḍaṃ mayodvṛtam / kākapiṇḍantu mantreṇa śunaḥ piṇḍaṃ pradāpayet //
english: Similarly the ball of rice to the dogs is offered with the repetition of the sacred formula, ‘ am offering the ball of rice to the dogs in the family of Sun that are black and of variegated colours.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ piṇḍaṃ pradāsyāmi pathi rakṣantu me sadā //
english: May it protect me always on the path to the next world’.

sanskrit: saurabheyyaḥ sarvahitāḥ pavitrāḥ pāpanāśanāḥ / pratigṛhṇantu me grāsaṃ gāvastrailokyamātaraḥ //
english: Then offerings are made to the cows with the following words ‘Accept this oblation of mine, O cows, the daughters of the celestial cow, that are good for all, holy, destroyer of sins and the mothers of the three worlds’.

sanskrit: grogrāsañca svastyayanaṃ kṛtvā bhikṣāṃ pradāpayet / atithīndīnān pūjayitvā gṛhī bhuñjīta ca svayaṃ //
english: After having offered the food to the cows and bidding adieu, one should offer the alms. After having worshipped the guests and the poor, the householder should himself eat.

sanskrit: viṣṇupūjāvaiśvadevabaliste kīrtito mayā //29//
english: Oṃ bhuvaḥ oblations. Oṃ svaḥ oblations. Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ oblations.

sanskrit: devālaye jvarārtyādau vināyakagrahārdite /
english: Oṃ oblations, you are the atonement for sins done by the gods.

sanskrit: padminyāṃ snāpayennārīṃ garbho yasyāḥ sravettathā / aśokasannidhau snāyājjāto yasyā vinaśyati //
english: Oṃ oblations, you are the atonement for sins done by men. Oblations, you are the atonement for all sins done by the learned men and the ignorant men.

sanskrit: puṣpārthināñca puṣpāḍhye putrārthināñca sāgare /
english: Oblations, to Fire god that accomplishes the desires. Oṃ oblations to Prajāpati lord of beings.

sanskrit: gṛhasaubhāgyakāmānāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣṇusannidhau //
english: have described to you the mode of worship of Lord Viṣṇu and the offering made to all gods. ṚV.

sanskrit: vaiṣṇave revatīpuṣye sarveṣāṃ snānamuttamaṃ /
english: ṚV. ..a. Rathe akṣeṣu, AV. ..a. Cf.

sanskrit: snānakāmasya saptāhampūrvamutsādanaṃ smṛtaṃ //
english: Sam. ..0. Consisting of curd, clarified butter, water, honey and candied sugar. Cf.

sanskrit: madhūkaṃ rajanī dve ca tagarannāgakeśaram //
english: AV. ..b and TB. .... ṚV.

sanskrit: ambarīñcaiva mañjiṣṭhāṃ māṃsīyāsakamardanaiḥ /
english: ..a. ṚV. .0.a. This and the following three are different celestial gods.

sanskrit: maṇḍale karṇikāyāñca viṣṇuṃ brāhmaṇamarcayet //
english: A particular group of deities ten in number and supposed to be sons of Viśvā. A female deity.

sanskrit: dakṣe vāme haraṃ pūrvaṃ patre pūrvādike kramāt /
english: The deity that presides over the foundation of a house.

sanskrit: likhedindrādikāndevān sāyudhān sahabāndhavān //
english: shall describe the bathing that accomplishes all objects and that is propitiatory.

sanskrit: snānamaṇḍalakān dikṣu kuryāccaiva vidikṣu ca / viṣṇubrahmeśaśakrādīṃstadastrāṇyarcya homayet //
english: A wise man should bathe the planets and Lord Viṣṇu on the banks of a river. One who is afflicted by fever as well as one who is afflicted by planets causing obstacles should bathe it in a temple.

sanskrit: ekaikasya tvaṣṭaśataṃ samidhastu tilān dhṛtaṃ /
english: One hundred and eight twigs, sesamum and ghee are offered to each one of the gods.

sanskrit: bhadraḥ subhadraḥ siddhārthaḥ kalasāḥ puṣṭivardhanāḥ //
english: The pitchers bhadra, subhadra, siddhartha, amogha, citrabhānu, parjanya and sudarśana that give prosperity should be placed on the ground.

sanskrit: viśve devas tathā daityā vasavo munayas tathā / āveśayantu suprītās tathānyā api devatāḥ //
english: The gods should be invoked in them as follows “May the Aśvins, Rudras, Maruts, Viśvedevas, Demons, Vasus and Munis and other gods get pleased and enter these pitchers.”

sanskrit: śatāvarīṃ śatapuṣpāṃ viṣṇukrāntāparājitām // jyotiṣmatīmatibalāñcandanośīrakeśaraṃ / kastūrikāñca karpūraṃ bālakaṃ patrakaṃ tvacaṃ // jātīphalaṃ lavaṅgañca mṛttikāṃ pañcagavyakaṃ /
english: The herbs jayantī, vijayā, jayā, śatāvarī, śatapuṣpā, viṣṇukrāntā, aparājitā, jyotiṣmatī, atibalā, sandal, uśīra, keśara, musk, camphor, bālaka, patraka, tvak, jātīphala nutmeg, clove, earth and the five things got from a cow should be put into the pitcher.

sanskrit: bhadrapīṭhe sthitaṃ sādhyaṃ snāpayeyurdvijā balāt //
english: Then the person who desires to have the ceremonial bath should be made to sit on the auspicious seat and bathed by brahmins.

sanskrit: rājābhiṣekamantroktadevānāṃ homakāḥ pṛthak / pūrṇāhutintato datvā gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dadet //
english: Then oblations should separately be offered to the gods with the sacred formulas used in the anointing of kings. Then the final oblation should be made and the fee paid to the preceptor.

sanskrit: indro 'bhiṣikto guruṇā purā daityān jaghāna ha /
english: In olden times Lord Indra was able to kill the demons being thus bathed by the preceptor.

sanskrit: dikpālasnānaṅkathitaṃ saṃgrāmādau jayādikaṃ //
english: have described to you the bathing of the guardians of the directions that give victory in the battle and other things.

sanskrit: vināyakopasṛṣṭānāṃ snānaṃ sarvakaraṃ vade /
english: shall describe the bathing that would be beneficial for those afflicted by the evil spirit called Vināyaka.

sanskrit: vināyakaḥ karmavighnasiddhyarthaṃ viniyojitaḥ // gaṇānāmādhipatye ca keśaveśapitāmahaiḥ /
english: The spirit Vināyaka was commissioned by Lords Keśava Viṣṇu, Īśa Śiva and Pitāmaha Brahmā as the leader of the attendants in order to frustrate the work of men.

sanskrit: svapnevagāhate 'tyarthaṃ jalaṃ muṇḍāṃś ca paśyati // vināyakopasṛṣṭastu kravyādānadhirohati / vrajamānas tathātmānaṃ manyate 'nugatamparaiḥ //
english: One who is possessed by Vināyaka dreams as if he is bathing in water excessively, sees shaven heads, rides the demons in a dream and as he goes thinks that he is being followed by others.

sanskrit: vimanā viphalārambhaḥ saṃsīdatyanimittataḥ /
english: The fruitless beginning of a task leads to frustration and the body emaciates without any reason.

sanskrit: kanyā varaṃ na cāpnoti na cāpatyaṃ varāṅganā // ācāryatvaṃ śrotriyaś ca na śiṣyo 'dhyayanaṃ labhet /
english: A girl does not get a suitable bridegroom, a married woman does not get progeny, a brahmin does not become a preceptor and a pupil does not get instruction.

sanskrit: dhanī na lābhamāpnoti na kṛṣiñca kṛṣībalaḥ //
english: A trader does not get profit and a cultivator, the produce.

sanskrit: rājā rājyaṃ na cāpnoti snapanantasya kārayet /
english: A king does not get a kingdom. In such cases a ceremonial bath has to be done.

sanskrit: hastapuṣyāśvayuksaumye vaiṣṇave bhadrapīṭhake // gaurasarṣapakalkena sājyenotsāditasya ca / sarvauṣadhaiḥ sarvagandhaiḥ praliptaśirasas tathā //
english: It should be done on an auspicious seat in the asterisms hasta, puṣya, aśvinī, mṛgaśīrṣa and śravaṇa. Levigated powders of white mustard mixed with clarified butter, all herbs and perfumes should be besmeared on the head of the person concerned.

sanskrit: caturbhiḥ kalasaiḥ snānanteṣu sarvauṣādhau kṣipet /
english: He should be bathed with the waters in four pitchers into which all herbs have been put.

sanskrit: aśvasthānādgajasthānādvalmīkāt saṅgamāddhradāt // mṛttikāṃ rocanāṅgandhaṅguggulunteṣu nikṣipet /
english: Earth brought from stables of horses and elephants, anthill and confluence of rivers as well as resin got from a cow, perfumes and guggulu should be put into the pitchers.

sanskrit: sahasrākṣaṃ śatadhāramṛṣibhiḥ pāvanaṃ kṛtam //
english: The bathing is done with the repetition of the following sacred formulas “Sahasrākṣam śatadhāram ṛṣibhiḥ pāvanaṃ kṛtaṃ.

sanskrit: tena tvāmabhiṣiñcāmi pāvamānyaḥ punantu te /
english: bathe you with the waters that have been made holy by the sages.

sanskrit: bhagavante varuṇo rājā bhagaṃ sūryo vṛhaspatiḥ // bhagamindraś ca vāyuś ca bhagaṃ saptarṣayo daduḥ /
english: May the removers of sins protect you.” Bhagaṃ te varuṇo rājā bhagaṃ sūryo bṛhaspatiḥ bhagamindraśca vāyuśca bhagaṃ saptarṣayo daduḥ.

sanskrit: lalāṭe karṇayorakṣṇorāpastadghnantu sarvadā / darbhapiñjalimādāya vāmahaste tato guruḥ // snātasya sārṣapantailaṃ śruveṇauḍumbareṇa ca / juhuyānmūrdhani kuśān savyena parigṛhya ca //
english: “May Varuṇa, the Sun, Bṛhaspati, Indra, Vāyu and the seven sages give you wealth.” “May the misfortune that sticks to your hair, the parting line of the hair, head, forehead, ears and eyes always be removed by the water.” Then the preceptor should hold the leaf of the darbha grass on the left hand and pour the mustard oil on the head of the person that has bathed with a ladle made of udumbara tree.

sanskrit: mitaś ca sammitaś caiva tathā śālakakaṇṭakau / kuṣmāṇḍo rājaputraś ca etaiḥ svāhāsamanvitaiḥ // nāmabhirbalimantraiś ca namaskārasamanvitaiḥ /
english: Then oblation should be made holding the kuśa grass on the head with the left hand repeating the names Mita, Sammita, Śālaka, Kaṇṭhaka, Kūṣmāṇḍa and Rājaputra together with the word oblation, the sacred formulas for oblation and obeisance.

sanskrit: dadyāccatuṣpathe śūrpe kuśānāstīrya sarvataḥ // kṛtākṛtāṃstaṇḍulāṃś ca palalaudanameva ca / matsyānpaṅkāṃstathaivāmān puṣpaṃ citraṃ surāṃ tridhā // mūlakaṃ pūrikāṃ pūpāṃstathaivaiṇḍavikāsrajaḥ / dadhyannaṃ pāyasaṃ piṣṭaṃ modakaṃ guḍamarpayet //
english: Then after having spread the kuśa grass everywhere at the crossroads, one should offer cooked and uncooked rice, meat, food, large quantities of raw fish, coloured flower, wine, mūlaka, cake, sweet cake of flour, garland of eṇḍavikā ?, curd rice, sweet porridge pīyasa, piṣṭaka a cake made of any grain, modaka a kind of sweetmeat in the form of balls and treacle on a winnowing basket.

sanskrit: vināyakasya jananīmupatiṣṭhettato 'mbikāṃ / dūrvāsarṣapapuṣpāṇāṃ datvārghyaṃ pūrṇamañjaliṃ //
english: Then Ambikā mother goddess consort of Śiva, the mother of Vināyaka, should be worshipped after having offered dūrvā grass, mustard and flowers and the final oblation is made.

sanskrit: rūpaṃ dehi yaśo dehi saubhāgyaṃ subhage mama / putraṃ dehi dhanaṃ dehi sarvān kāmāṃś ca dehi me //
english: The following request is made O Fortunate one! You give me beauty, fame, good fortune, progeny, wealth and all desired things.

sanskrit: bhojayedbrāhmaṇāndadyādvastrayugmaṃ gurorapi /
english: The brahmins should be fed and a pair of clothes should be given to the preceptor also.

sanskrit: vināyakaṃ grahānprārcya śriyaṃ karmaphalaṃ labhet //
english: One would get the fruit of his action and wealth after worshipping the spirit Vināyaka and the planets.

sanskrit: snānaṃ māheśvaraṃ vakṣye rājāderjayavardhanam / dānavendrāya balaye yajjagādośanāḥ purā //
english: shall describe the bathing known as Māheśvara that has been described by Uśanas preceptor of demons to Bali, the king of demons, in olden days and that would promote the victory of a king and others.

sanskrit: bhāskare 'nudite pīṭhe prātaḥ saṃsnāpayed ghaṭaiḥ / evaṃ snatastu mantreṇa juhuyāttilataṇḍulam //
english: When the sun has not risen the votary should be bathed on a seat with the waters of pitchers with the repetition of the following words Oṃ obeisance to Lord Rudra and to Bala besmeared with ashes of grey colour.

sanskrit: pañcāmṛtaistu saṃsnāpya pūjayecchūlapāṇinaṃ /
english: After having bathed with the pañcāmṛta, the trident bearing lord should be worshipped.

sanskrit: snānānyanyāni vakṣyāmi sarvadā vijayāya te //
english: shall describe to you the other kinds of ablutions that would always be for your victory.

sanskrit: snānaṃ ghṛtena kathitamāyuṣyavardhanaṃ param / gomayena ca lakṣmīḥ syādgomūtreṇāghamardanam //
english: Bathing with ghee is said to be excellent for the lengthening of life. Bathing with cowdung would be conferring fortune. Bathing with cow’s urine would destroy the sins.

sanskrit: kṣīreṇa balabuddhiḥ syāddadhnā lakṣmīvivardhanaṃ /
english: Bathing with milk would be giving strong intellect and with curd, would further fortune.

sanskrit: kuśodakena pāpāntaḥ pañcagavyena sarvabhāk //
english: One would be destroying the sins by bathing with kuśa grass and would get all the things by bathing with the five things got from a cow.

sanskrit: śatamūlena sarvāptirgośṛṅgodakato 'ghajit /
english: One would get everything by bathing with śatamūla.

sanskrit: palāśabilvakamalakuśasnānantu sarvadaṃ //
english: One would get everything by bathing with palāśa, bilva, lotus and kuśa grass.

sanskrit: vacā haridre dve mustaṃ snānaṃ rakṣohaṇaṃ paraṃ /
english: Bathing with vacā, two varieties of haridrā and musta is spoken as excellent for killing the demons.

sanskrit: āyuṣyañca yaśasyañca dharmamedhāvivardhanam //
english: One would gain long life, fame, righteousness and intellect by ablution with washings of gold.

sanskrit: haimādbhiś caiva māṅgalyaṃ rūpyatāmrodakais tathā / ratnodakaistu vijayaḥ saubhāgyaṃ sarvagandhakaiḥ //
english: It would be auspicious to bathe with the washings of silver and copper. One would gain victory and fortune respectively by bathing with the washings of gems and all perfumes.

sanskrit: phalādbhiś ca tathārogyaṃ dhātryadbhiḥ paramāṃ śriyam /
english: One would gain health and excellent fortune respectively by bathing with water containing fruits and water with dhātrī.

sanskrit: tilasiddhārthakair lakṣmīḥ saubhāgyañca priyaṅguṇā // padmotpalakadambaiś ca śrīrbalaṃ balādrumodakaiḥ /
english: One would get wealth and fortune respectively by bathing with sesamum and white mustard and priyaṅgu. One would gain wealth by bathing with water containing lotus, blue lotus and kadamba. One would gain strength by bathing with the water containing the twigs of the balā tree.

sanskrit: viṣṇupādodakasnānaṃ sarvasnānebhya uttamam //
english: Bathing with the water that has washed the feet of Lord Viṣṇu is the best among all kinds of ablutions.

sanskrit: ekākī ekakāmāyetyekorkaṃ vidhivaccaret /
english: At the time of bathing one should repeat the hymn ekakāmāya alone duly.

sanskrit: kuṣṭhapāṭhā vācā śuṇṭhī śaṅkhalohādiko maṇiḥ /
english: A band made of the herbs kuṣṭha, pāṭhā, vacā, śuṇṭhi, conch and iron etc.

sanskrit: sarveṣāmevakāmānāmīśvaro bhagavān hariḥ //
english: should be tied round the wrist with the repetition of the hymn ākrandayati. Lord Hari Viṣṇu is the master of all desires.

sanskrit: tasya saṃpūjanādeva sarvānkāmānsamaśnute /
english: One would enjoy all the pleasures by worshipping Him. lb.

sanskrit: snāpayitvā ghṛtakṣīraiḥ pūjayitvā ca pittahā // pañcamudgabalindatvā atisārāt pramucyate / pañcagavyena saṃsnāpya vātavyādhiṃ vināśayet //
english: By bathing the image of Lord Viṣṇu with ghee and milk and worshipping Him, one would get rid of biliousness. By offering an oblation of five kinds of pulses one would get free from dysentry. By bathing the image with the five things got from a cow, one would get rid of rheumatism.

sanskrit: dvisnehasnapanāt śleṣmarogahā cātipūjayā /
english: Bathing with dvisneha ghee and water with intense devotion would remove derangement of phlegm.

sanskrit: ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ tathā kṣaudraṃ snānantu trirasaṃ paraṃ //
english: Ghee, oil and honey is said to be the trirasa three fluids mixed together that is excellent for bathing.

sanskrit: snānaṃ ghṛtāmbu dvisnehaṃ samalaṃ ghṛtatailakam /
english: Ghee and water mixed for bathing is said to be dvisneha, Ghee and oil mixed for bathing is said to be samala.

sanskrit: kṣaudramikṣurasaṃ kṣīraṃ snānaṃ trimadhuraṃ smṛtam // ghṛtamiśurasaṃ tailaṃ kṣaudrañca trirasaṃ śriye / anulepastriśukrastu karpūrośīracandanaiḥ //
english: Bath water with honey, the juice of sugarcane and milk is known to be trimadhura three sweet things. Bath water with ghee, juice of sugarcane, oil and honey is known to be trirasa three fluids good for wealth. An unguent of the three white thingscamphor, uśīra a fragrant thing and sandal should be used for bath.

sanskrit: candanāgurukarpūramṛgadarpaiḥ sakuṅkumaiḥ / pañcānulepanaṃ viṣṇoḥ sarvakāmaphalapradaṃ //
english: Sandal, agallochuṃ, camphor, musk and saffron are the five unguents for Lord Viṣṇu that yield all the pleasures.

sanskrit: trisugandhañca karpūraṃ tathā candanakuṅkumaiḥ /
english: The three fragrant things are camphor, sandal and saffron.

sanskrit: mṛgadarpaṃ sakarpūraṃ malayaṃ sarvakāmadam //
english: Musk, camphor and sandal used as an unguent yield all the pleasures.

sanskrit: jātīphalaṃ sakarpūraṃ candanañca triśītakam /
english: Nutmeg, camphor and sandal are said to be the three cooling things.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāni caiva raktāni pañcavarṇāni nirdiśet /
english: O son of Bhṛgu! The five co lours are indicated as yellow, blue, white, black and red.

sanskrit: utpalaṃ padmajātī ca triśītaṃ haripūjane //
english: Blue lotus, lotus and jātī flowers are spoken to be the three cool things that are commended for the worship of Lord Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: kuṅkumaṃ raktapadmāni triraktamutpalaṃ /
english: Saffron, red lotuses and red lilies are the three red things.

sanskrit: dhūpadīpādibhiḥ prārcya viṣṇuṃ śāntirbhavennṛṇāṃ //
english: Men would get peace by worshipping Lord Viṣṇu well by showing incense, lamp, etc.

sanskrit: caturasrakare kuṇḍe brāhmaṇāścāṣṭa śoḍaśa / lakṣahomaṅkoṭihomantilājyayavadhānyakaiḥ // grahānabhyarcya gāyatryā sarvaśāntiḥ kramādbhavet //24//
english: One would duly get all peace by worshipping the planets with the gāyatrī hymn after offering a lakh or crore oblations of sesamum, clarified butter, barley and other grains in a square sacrificial pit done by eight or sixteen brahmins. The three cities of the demons Tārakākṣa.

sanskrit: karma sāṃvatsaraṃ rājñāṃ janmarkṣe pūjayecca taṃ /
english: ṚV. ..0. shall describe the rites to be performed by the kings in the course of a year.

sanskrit: māsi māsi ca saṃkrāntau sūryasomādidevatāḥ //
english: The Sun, Moon and other gods should be worshipped every month at the time of sun’s entry into one of the signs of the zodiac.

sanskrit: agastyasyodaye 'gastyañcāturmāsyaṃ hariṃ yajet /
english: Agastya should be worshipped at the time of the rise of Agastya Canopus.

sanskrit: śayanotthāpane pañcadinaṃ kuryātsamutsavam // proṣṭhapāde site pakṣe pratipatprabhṛtikramāt / śivirāt pūrvadigbhāge śakrārthaṃ bhavanañcaret //
english: Festivities should be had for fifteen days in connection with the lying down to sleep and waking up from sleep of Lord Viṣṇu. A mansion should be made ready by the king on the east of his army camp in the bright fortnight of the month ruled by the asterism Proṣṭhapāda i.e.

sanskrit: tatra śakradhvajaṃ sthāpya śacī śakrañca pūjayet /
english: The banner of Indra should be raised therein. Lord Indra and his consort Śacī should be worshipped therein.

sanskrit: aṣṭamyāṃ vādyaghoṣeṇa tāntu yaṣṭiṃ praveśayet //
english: Those two and the flagstaff should be led to the proper place accompanied by the sounding of musical instruments on the eighth day.

sanskrit: ekādaśyāṃ sopavāso dvādaśyāṃ ketumutthitam / yajedvastrādisaṃvītaṃ ghaṭasthaṃ surapaṃ śacīṃ //
english: He should fast on the eleventh day, raise the flag staff on the twelfth day and worship the flagstaff, as well as the Lord of celestials Indra and Śacī in a pitcher covered by a cloth etc.

sanskrit: vardhasvendra jitāmitra vṛtrahan pākaśāsana / deva deva mahābhāga tvaṃ hi bhūmiṣṭhatāṃ gataḥ //
english: “O Indra! You flourish! Conqueror of the enemies! Killer of the demon Vṛtra! Punisher of the demon Pāka! Lord of lords! Most fortunate one! You have come to the earth.

sanskrit: tvaṃ prabhuḥ śāśvataś caiva sarvabhūtahite rataḥ /
english: You are the master, the eternal one and one who is bent on the welfare of all the beings.

sanskrit: anantatejā vai rājo yaśojayavivardhanaḥ //
english: You are a person who has endless lustre and splendour.

sanskrit: tejaste vardhayantvete devāḥ śakraḥ suvṛṣṭikṛt /
english: You are the one who increases fame and victory. May these gods increase your lustre.

sanskrit: brahmaviṣṇumaheśāś ca kārttikeyo vināyakaḥ // ādityā vasavo rudrāḥ sādhyāś ca bhṛgavo diśaḥ / marudguṇā lokapālā grahā yakṣādrinimnagāḥ // samudrā śrīrmahī gaurī caṇḍikā ca sarasvatī /
english: O Śakra Indra! One who causes good rain! May the Lords Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa Śiva, Kārtikeya son of Śiva, Vināyaka son of Śivā, the twelve Suns, the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the Sādhyas, the Bhṛgus, the different quarters, group of Maruts, the protectors of the world, planets, the Yakṣas a kind of semidivine beings, the rivers, the oceans, goddesses Śrī the consort ofViṣṇu, Earth, Gaurī consort of Śiva, Caṇḍikā a form of the consort of Śiva and Sarasvatī goddess of speech consort of Brahmā increase your radiance.

sanskrit: pravartayantu te tejo jaya śakra śacīpate // tava cāpi jayānnityaṃ mama sampaṭhyatāṃ śubhaṃ /
english: Hail O Indra! Consort of Śacī! May auspicious things accrue to me daily by your victory.

sanskrit: prasīda rājñāṃ viprāṇāṃ prajānāmapi sarvaśaḥ //
english: Always extend thy grace to the kings, brahmins and people.

sanskrit: bhavatprasādāt pṛthivī nityaṃ śasyavatī bhavet / śivaṃ bhavatu nirvighnaṃ śāmyantāmītayo bhṛśaṃ //
english: May the earth abound in grains by your grace. May there be prosperity without any obstacle. May calamities come to an end.”

sanskrit: mantreṇendraṃ samabhyarcya jitabhūḥ svargamāpnuyāt /
english: After having worshipped Indra with the above sacred formulas, one will conquer the earth and reach the heaven.

sanskrit: bhadrakālīṃ paṭe likhya pūjayedāśvine jaye // śuklapakṣe tathāṣṭamyāmāyudhaṃ kārmukaṃ dhvajam / chatrañca rājaliṅgāni śastrādyaṃ kusumādibhiḥ //
english: The picture of Bhadrakālī a benevolent form of the consort of Śiva should be drawn on a cloth on the eighth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Āśvina OctoberNovember for victory. In the same way, the weapon, bow, banner, umbrella, the insignia of the king such as the arms should be worshipped with flowers.

sanskrit: jāgranniśi balindadyāddvitīye 'hni punaryajet /
english: After remaining awake in the night, the offering should be made. She is again worshipped on the second day.

sanskrit: bhadrakāli mahākāli durge durgārtihāriṇi // trailokyavijaye caṇḍi mama śāntau jaye bhava /
english: O Bhadrakāli! Mahākālī! Durgā! Remover of all difficulties! Conqueror of the three worlds! Caṇḍī! Be successful in conferring peace on me!

sanskrit: nīrājanavidhiṃ vakṣye aiśānyānmandiraṃ caret //
english: shall describe the mode of performing the nīrājanā rite. A chamber should be got ready in the northeastern direction.

sanskrit: toraṇatritayaṃ tatra gṛhe devānyajet sadā /
english: Three arches should be erected therein and the gods should be worshipped daily.

sanskrit: citrāntyaktvā yadā svātiṃ savitā pratipadyate // tataḥ prabhṛti kartavyaṃ yāvat svātau raviḥ sthitaḥ /
english: The worship should be done from the moment Sun leaves the asterism Citrā and enters the asterism Svāti and stays therein.

sanskrit: brahmā viṣṇuś ca śambhuś ca śakraś caivānalānilau // vināyakaḥ kumāraś ca varuṇo dhanado yamaḥ / viśvedevā vaiśravaso gajāścāṣṭau ca tānyajet // kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadantaś ca vāmanaḥ /
english: The gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śambhu Śiva, Śakra Indra, Firegod, Windgod, Vināyaka and Kumāra the two sons of Śiva, Varuṇa, Dhanada god of wealth, Yama god of death, Viśvedevas a group of gods and the eight elephants of Vaiśravasa son of Viśravas such as Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, Vāmana, Supratīka, Añjana and Nīla, should be worshipped in the chamber.

sanskrit: supratīko 'ñjano nīlaḥ pūjā kāryā gṛhādike //
english: The priest should offer as oblation clarified butter, twigs, white mustard and sesamum.

sanskrit: kumbhā aṣṭau pūjitāś ca taiḥ snāpyāśvagajottamāḥ //
english: After worshipping eight pitchers, the excellent horses and elephants should be bathed with them.

sanskrit: aśvāḥ snāpyā dadet piṇḍān tato hi prathamaṃ gajān / niṣkrāmayettoraṇaistu gopurādi na laṅghayet //
english: The horses should be bathed first and the balls of rice offered. Then the elephants should be led out first through the arches but should not be made to cross the principal gateways etc.

sanskrit: vikrameyustataḥ sarve rājaliṅgaṃ gṛhe yajet /
english: Then all should set out. The insignia of the king should be worshipped in the chamber.

sanskrit: vāruṇe varuṇaṃ prārcya rātrau bhūtabaliṃ dadet //
english: After having worshipped Lord Varuṇa on the west, the offering to the spirits should be made in the night.

sanskrit: viśākhāyāṃ gate sūrye āśrame nivasennṛpaḥ /
english: When the Sun has entered the asterism Viśākhā, the king should stay in the hermitage.

sanskrit: alaṅkuryāddine tasmin vāhanantu viśeṣataḥ //
english: The chariot should be specially decorated on that day.

sanskrit: pūjitā rājaliṅgāś ca kartavyā narahastagāḥ /
english: The royal insignia that has been worshipped should be placed in the hands of the respective men.

sanskrit: hastinanturagaṃ chatraṃ khaḍgaṃ cāpañca dundubhim // dhvajaṃ patākāṃ dharmajña kālajñastvabhimantrayet /
english: O Knower of righteousness! An astrologer should then consecrate the elephant, horse, umbrella, sword, bow, wardrum, flag staff and flag of the king.

sanskrit: abhimantrya tataḥ sarvān kuryāt kuñjaradhūrgatān //
english: After consecration they should be made to be carried on the elephant.

sanskrit: kuñjaroparigau syātāṃ sāṃvatsarapurohitau / mantritāṃś ca samāruhya toraṇena vinirgamet //
english: The astrologer and priest should then ride the elephant. The king should ride the consecrated horses and set out through the arch.

sanskrit: niṣkramya nāgamāruhya toraṇenātha nirgamet /
english: After setting out he should ride the elephant and go out through the arch.

sanskrit: baliṃ vibhajya vidhivadrājā kuñjaradhūrgataḥ // unmūkānāntu nicayamādīpitadigantaraṃ / rājā pradakṣiṇaṃ kuryāttrīn vārān susamāhitaḥ // caturaṅgabalopetaḥ sarvasainyena nādayan /
english: After having offered the oblation, the king riding the elephant and remaining calm should circumambulate the city thrice as the collection of firebrands illuminate the different quarters of space, the fourfold army keep company and the entire army shout victory.

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtvā gṛhaṃ gacchedvisarjitajalāñjaliḥ //
english: After doing this, the king having offered water with the palms should go back to the palace.

sanskrit: śāntir nīrājanākhyeyaṃ vṛddhaye ripumardanī //31//
english: This is the appeasing rite called ṃīrājanā that would make a king prosper and kill the enemy.

sanskrit: chatrādimantrānvakṣyāmi yaistat pūjya jayādikam /
english: shall describe the sacred formulas for the consecration of the umbrella and other things, the worship of which would confer victory and other things.

sanskrit: brahmaṇaḥ satyavākyena somasya varuṇasya ca // sūryasya ca prabhāvena vardhasva tvaṃ mahāmate /
english: “O One with great intellect! One having the splendour of jasmine! One having the lustre of snow, jasmine and moon! You be glorious by the true words of Brahmā, Soma, and Varuṇa and the power of the Sun.

sanskrit: yathāmbudaśchādayate śivāyaināṃ vasundharāṃ / tathācchādaya rājānaṃ vijayārogyavṛddhaye //
english: May you shield the king for the achievement of success and promotion of health in the same way as the cloud covers the earth for its welfare.

sanskrit: gandharvakulajātastvaṃ mābhūyāḥ kuladūṣakaḥ /
english: O Horse! You were born in the race of the Gandharvas a kind of semidivine beings.

sanskrit: brahmaṇaḥ satyavākyena somasya varuṇasya ca // prabhāvācca hutāśasya vardhasva tvaṃ turaṅgama / tejasā caiva sūryasya munīnāṃ tapasā tathā // rudrasya brahmacaryeṇa pavanasya balena ca /
english: May you not become a defiler of the race. You be glorious by the true words of Brahmā, Soma and Varuṇa and the power of Fire god as well as the splendour of the Sun, the penance of the sages, the continence of Rudra Śiva and the strength of the Wind god.

sanskrit: smara tvaṃ rājaputro 'si kaustubhantu maṇiṃ smara //
english: You remember that you are of royal birth. You remember the kaustubha gem.

sanskrit: yāṃ gatiṃ brahmahā gacchet pitṛhā mātṛhā tathā / bhūmyarthe 'nṛtavādī ca kṣatriyaś ca parāṅmukhaḥ // vrajestvantāṃ gatiṃ kṣipraṃ mā tat pāpaṃ bhavettava / vikṛtiṃ māpagacchestvaṃ yuddhe 'dhvani turaṅgama //
english: May you not incur the sin that would accrue to the killer of a brahmin, or to a patricide or to a matricide or to a person who utters a lie for the sake of gaining a land or to a man of the warriorclass who turns his back upon the battle, although you may swiftly move that way. O Horse! May you not meet with adversity in the battle or on the road.

sanskrit: ripūn vinighnansamare saha bhartrā sukhī bhava /
english: May you be happy together with your master after killing the enemies in the battle.

sanskrit: śakraketo mahāvīryaḥ suvarṇastvāmupāśritaḥ //
english: O Banner of Indra! Suparṇa of great valour has taken his position on you.

sanskrit: patatrirāḍvainateyas tathā nārāyaṇadhvajaḥ / kāśyapeyo 'mṛtāhartā nāgārirviṣṇuvāhanaḥ // aprameyo durādharṣo raṇe devārisūdanaḥ / mahābalo māvego mahākāyo 'mṛtāśanaḥ // garutmānmārutagatistvayi sannihitaḥ sthitaḥ /
english: The lord of birds, Son of Vinatā, One seated on the banner of Nārāyaṇa Viṣṇu, A progeny of sage Kaśyapa, One that carried away the nectar, The Enemy of the serpents, the Vehicle of Lord Viṣṇu, Immeasurable one, Unassailable in the battle, Destroyer of the enemies of the celestials, One having great strength, One having swift speed, One possessing a huge body, One who drinks the nectar, The winged one, One who has the swiftness of Māruti son of Wind, Hanumat is always present in you.

sanskrit: viṣṇunā devadevena śakrārthaṃ sthāpito hy asi //
english: You have been fixed by Lord Viṣṇu, the lord of lords, for the sake of Indra.

sanskrit: jayāya bhava me nityaṃ vṛddhaye 'tha balasya ca / sāśvavarmāyudhānyodhānrakṣāsmākaṃ ripūndaha //
english: May you always give me victory, prosperity and strength. You protect the warriors together with their horses, armours and weapons. You burn our enemies.

sanskrit: kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadanto 'tha vāmanaḥ / supratīko 'ñjano nīla ete 'ṣṭau devayonayaḥ //
english: Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, Vāmana, Supratīka, Añjana and Nīla are the eight elephants of divine origin.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ putrāś ca pautrāś ca balānyaṣṭau samāśritāḥ /
english: Their sons and grandsons constitute eight forces.

sanskrit: bhadro mando mṛgaś caiva gajaḥ saṃkīrṇa eva ca // vane vane prasūtāste smarayoniṃ mahāgajāḥ /
english: You remember Bhadra, Manda, Mṛga and Saṅkīrṇa that have been born in the different forests and have become great elephants.

sanskrit: pāntu tvāṃ vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ //
english: May the eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, twelve Ādityas, the group of Maruts protect you.

sanskrit: bhartāraṃ rakṣa nāgendra samayaḥ paripālyatāṃ / airāvatādhirūḍhastu vajrahastaḥ śatakratuḥ // pṛṣṭhato 'nugatastveṣa rakṣatu tvāṃ sa devarāṭ /
english: O King of elephants! Protect the master! May the obligation be discharged! Lord Indra, the lord of the celestials, riding the Airāvata the elephant of Indra and wielding the weapon thunderbolt following you, protect you.

sanskrit: avāpnuhi jayaṃ yuddhe susthaś caiva sadā vraja //
english: May you gain victory in the battle and march always in good state.

sanskrit: avāpnuhi balañcaiva airāvatasamaṃ yudhi /
english: May you get the strength of Airāvata elephant of Indra in the battle.

sanskrit: śrīste somādbalaṃ viṣṇostejaḥ sūryājjavo 'nilāt // sthairyaṃ girerjayaṃ rudrādyaśo devāt purandarāt /
english: May you get wealth from Soma, strength from Viṣṇu, splendour from Sun, speed from wind, firmness from mountain, victory from Rudra and fame from Lord Purandara Indra.

sanskrit: yuddhe rakṣantu nāgāstvāṃ diśaś ca saha daivataiḥ // aśvinau saha gandharvaiḥ pāntu tvāṃ sarvato diśaḥ /
english: May the elephants protect you in the battle. May the quarters in the company of Aśvins the two physicians of the gods and Gandharvas semidivine beings protect you in all the directions.

sanskrit: manvo vasavo rudrā vāyuḥ somo maharṣayaḥ // nāgakinnaragandharvayakṣabhūtagaṇā grahāḥ / pramathāstu sahādityair bhūteśo mātṛbhiḥ saha // śakraḥ senāpatiḥ skando varuṇaścāśritastvayi /
english: May the Manus the first representative of mankind, Rudras, Vāyu, Soma, the great sages, Nāgas serpents, Kinnaras semidivine beings, Gandharvas semidivine beings, Yakṣas semidivine beings, the hosts of spirits, planets, goblins with Ādityas, the Lord of the goblins with the divine mothers, Indra, Skanda son of Śiva the commanderinchief of the celestials and Varuṇa resting in you burn all the enemies.

sanskrit: pradahantu ripūn sarvān rājā vijayamṛcchatu // yāni prayuktānyaribhirbhūṣaṇāni samantataḥ /
english: May the king gain victory. May the festoons used by the enemy for decoration everywhere, fall down being struck by your splendour.

sanskrit: patantu tava śatrūṇāṃ hatāni tava tejasā // kālanemibadhe yadvat yuddhe tripuraghātane / hiraṇyakaśiporyuddhe badhe sarvāsureṣu ca //
english: In the same way as you have shone at the time of killing the demon Kālanemi, the destruction of Tripura, the battle with Hiraṇyakaśipu and the killing of all the demons, may you shine now.

sanskrit: śobhitāsi tathaivādya śobhasva samayaṃ smara /
english: You remember the opportune moment.

sanskrit: vyādhibhirvividhair ghoraiḥ śastraiś ca yudhi nirjitāḥ /
english: May the enemies of the king be destroyed quickly. May the enemies be conquered by different kinds of terrible diseases and weapons.

sanskrit: pūtanā revatī lekhā kālarātrīti paṭhyate // dahantvāśu ripūn sarvānpatāke tvāmupāśritāḥ /
english: May the names Pūtanā, Revatī, Lekhā and Kālarātrī that we have read as terrible forces burn all the enemies quickly with your help.

sanskrit: sarvamedhe mahāyajñe devadevena śūlinā // śarveṇa jagataś caiva sāreṇa tvaṃ vinirmitaḥ /
english: O sword! You have been created by the god of gods, the tridentbearer, Lord Śarva Śiva out of the essence of the world at the great sacrifice in which everything was offered.

sanskrit: nandakasyāparāṃ mūrtiṃ smara śatrunivarhaṇa // nīlotpaladalaśyāma kṛṣṇa duḥsvapnanāśana / asirviśasanaḥ khaḍgastīkṣṇadhāro durāsadaḥ //
english: The destroyer of the enemies! Remember the foremost form of Nandaka the sword of Lord Kṛṣṇa. One having a dark complexion like the petals of blue lotus! Dark one! Destroyer of bad dreams! Lord Brahmā has declared the following as your eight names asiḥ, viśasanaḥ, khaḍgaḥ, tīkṣṇadhāraḥ, durāsadaḥ, śrīgarbhaḥ, vijayaḥ.

sanskrit: augarbho vijayaś caiva dharmapālastathaiva ca /
english: and dharmapālaḥ.

sanskrit: nakṣatraṃ kṛttikā tubhyaṃ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ /
english: Kṛttikā is your asterism. Lord Maheśvara Śiva is your preceptor.

sanskrit: hiraṇyañca śarīrante daivatante janārdanaḥ //
english: Gold is your body. Janārdana Viṣṇu is your lord.

sanskrit: śarmapradastvaṃ samare varman sainye yaśo 'dya me / rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo 'hantavānagha namo 'stu te //
english: O Armour! You cause the enemy forces to feel ashamed in the battle. will have fame in the army today. O Sinless one! Protect me, worthy of being protected by you! Obeisance to you.

sanskrit: dundubhe tvaṃ sapatnānāṃ ghoṣāddhṛdayakampanaḥ /
english: O War drum! You cause the hearts of enemies to tremble by your sound.

sanskrit: bhava bhūmisainyānāṃ yathā vijayavardhanaḥ //
english: You act in such a way that you may achieve victory for the king’s army.

sanskrit: yathā jīmūtaghoṣeṇa hṛṣyanti varavāraṇāḥ / tathāstu tava śabdena harṣo 'smākaṃ mudāvaha //
english: Just as the excellent elephants get delighted on hearing the sound of the colliding clouds, in the same way let us rejoice on hearing your sound.

sanskrit: yathā jīmūtaśabdena strīṇāṃ trāso 'bhijāyate / tathā tu tava śabdena trasyantvasmaddviṣo raṇe //
english: Just as the rumbling clouds cause fright in women, so also let our enemies get frightened by your sound in the battle.

sanskrit: mantraiḥ sadārcanīyāste yojanīyā jayādiṣu /
english: These should always be worshipped with sacred formulas. They should be employed for victory etc.

sanskrit: ghṛtakambalaviṣṇādestvabhiṣekañca vatsare //
english: Every year Lord Viṣṇu should be anointed with ghee and water.

sanskrit: rājño 'bhiṣekaḥ kartavyo daivajñena purodhasā //39//
english: The king should be given the ablution by an astrologer and priest. Supposed to guard the quarters.

sanskrit: tripurañjaghnuṣaḥ pūrvaṃ brahmaṇā viṣṇupañjaraṃ / śaṅkarasya dvijaśreṣtha rakṣaṇāya nirūpitaṃ //
english: A demon killed by Viṣṇu. O Foremost among brahmins! This hymn Viṣṇupañjara was prescribed by Brahmā for the protection of Śiva, who was desirous of destroying Tripura in olden days.

sanskrit: vāgīśena ca śakrasya balaṃ hantuṃ prayāsyataḥ /
english: It was told by Vāgīśa Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the celestials to Indra, who was making efforts to kill the demon Bala.

sanskrit: tasya svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi tattvaṃ śṛṇu jayādimat //
english: shall describe its form. You listen to that which will give you victory.

sanskrit: viṣṇuḥ prācyāṃ sthitaś cakrī harirdakṣinaṇato gadī / pratīcyāṃ śārṅgadhṛgviṣṇurjiṣṇuḥ khaḍgī mamottare //
english: Lord Viṣṇu is stationed in the east bearing the disc. Lord Hari is stationed in the south bearing the mace. Lord Viṣṇu remains in the west bearing the bow. Lord Viṣṇu is stationed to my north bearing the sword.

sanskrit: hṛṣīkeśo vikoṇeṣu tacchidreṣu janārdanaḥ /
english: Lord Hṛṣīkeśa is in the angular points and Lord Janārdana in the interspaces.

sanskrit: kroḍarūpī harirbhūmau narasiṃho 'mbare mama //
english: Lord Hari is stationed on the earth in the form of a tortoise and Lord Narasiṃha manlion form of Viṣṇu in the sky above me.

sanskrit: kṣurāntamamalañcakraṃ bhramatyetat sudarśanaṃ /
english: This sharpedged and stainless Sudarśana disc of Viṣṇu revolves. His garland of rays is imperceivable.

sanskrit: asyāṃśumālā duṣprekṣyā hantuṃ pretaniśācarān //
english: “May you kill the evil spirits and those who wander in the night.”

sanskrit: gadā ceyaṃ sahasrārciḥpradīptapāvakojjvalā /
english: This mace has the lustre of the flames given out by the Sun.

sanskrit: rakṣobhūtapiśācānāṃ ḍākinīnāñca nāśanī //
english: It is capable of destroying the demons, goblins, spirits and female spirits..

sanskrit: śārṅgavisphūrjitañcaiva vāsudevasya madripūn / tiryaṅmanuṣyakuṣmāṇḍapretādīn hantvaśeṣataḥ //
english: May the bow of Vāsudeva Viṣṇu, that is striking suddenly, kill all my enemies, such as birds, men, kūṣmāṇḍa and the spirits of the dead.

sanskrit: khaḍgadhārojjvalajjo 'tsnānirdhūtā ye samāhitāḥ / te yāntu śāmyatāṃ sadyo garuḍeneva pannagāḥ //
english: Those who have been shaken by the shining lustre of the stroke of the sword, let those assembed enemies be subdued at once, like serpents by Garuḍa vehicle of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: pretā vināyakāḥ krūrā manuṣyā jambhagāḥ khagāḥ // siṃhādayaś ca paśavo dandaśūkāś ca pannagāḥ / sarve bhavantu te saumyāḥ kṛṣṇaśaṅkharavāhatāḥ //
english: May the kūṣmāṇḍas, yakṣas, demons, the night wanderers, spirits of the dead, Vināyakas, cruel men, jambhagas jackals?, birds, lions and other animals, serpents and others become good being struck by the sound of the conch of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: cittavṛttiharā ye me ye janāḥ smṛtihārakāḥ / balaujasañca hartāraśchāyāvibhraṃśakāś ca ye // ye copabhogahartāro ye ca lakṣaṇanāśakāḥ / kuṣmāṇḍāste praṇaśyantu viṣṇucakraravāhatāḥ //
english: Those that take away my thinking faculty, those men who affect my memory, those who affect my strength and splendour, those who cast their shadow, those who affect my pleasures, those who destroy my traits, may those kūṣmāṇḍas get destroyed by the sound of the disc of Lord Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: mamāstu devadevasya vāsudevasya kīrtanāt //
english: May my intellect, mind and senseorgans be healthy by the singing of the glory of lord of lords, Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhe purastānmama dakṣiṇottare vikoṇataścāstu janārdano hariḥ /
english: May Lord Janārdana, Hari, be behind me, in my front, on the south and north and at the angular points.

sanskrit: tamīḍyamīśānamanantamacyutaṃ janārdanaṃ praṇipatito na sīdati //
english: One that makes obeisance to the Lord Janārdana, one worthy of worship, Īsāna, endless and undecaying will not have grief.

sanskrit: yathā paraṃ brahma haris tathā paraḥ jagatsvarūpaś ca sa eva keśavaḥ /
english: Just as Lord Hari is the Supreme Brahman, that Keśava is above the form of the universe.

sanskrit: satyena tenācyutanāmakīrtanāt praṇāśayettu trividhaṃ mamāśubhaṃ //
english: May my three kinds of inauspiciousness get destroyed by the truth of singing the name Acyuta undecaying.

sanskrit: sarvānugrāhakā mantrāś caturvargaprasādhakāḥ / ṛgatharva tathā sāma yajuḥ saṃkhyā tu lakṣakaṃ //
english: The number of hymns of the Ṛg veda, Yajur veda, Sāma veda and Atharva veda that yield all the desires and confer the four ends of the human life is one lakh.

sanskrit: bhedaḥ sāṅkhyāyanaś caika āśvalāyano dvitīyakaḥ /
english: The Ṛgveda is divided into two branches, Sāṅkhyāyana and Āśvalāyana.

sanskrit: śatāni daśa mantrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇā dvisahasrakaṃ //
english: The brāhmaṇas of this Veda contain two thousand one hundred and ten hymns.

sanskrit: ṛgvedo hi pramāṇena smṛto dvaipāyanādibhiḥ /
english: The Ṛgveda is considered as the authority by the Dvaipāyanas and others.

sanskrit: ekonidvisahasrantu mantrāṇāṃ yajuṣas tathā //
english: The hymns of the Yajurveda number one thousand nine hundred and ninetynine.

sanskrit: śatāni daśa viprāṇāṃ ṣaḍaśītiś ca śākhikāḥ /
english: Their branches are one thousand eightysix.

sanskrit: kāṇvamādhyandinī saṃjñā kaṭhī mādhyakaṭhī tathā // maitrāyaṇī ca saṃjñā ca taittirīyābhidhānikā /
english: The branches of the Yajur veda are known as Kāṇvī, Mādhyandinī, Kaṭhī, Mādhyakaṭhī, Maitrāyaṇī, Taittirīya and Vaiśampāyana.

sanskrit: sāmnaḥ kauthumasaṃjñaikā dvitīyātharvaṇāyanī /
english: Sa. The first branch of the Sāmaveda is known as Kauthuma and the second as Atharvaṇāyanī.
